### Overview of the Accounts Payable Application
*Source: `RP Accounting AP Daily Tasks User Guide.pdf`, Page 22*

Accounts Payable 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Daily Tasks User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Overview of the Accounts Payable Application 

Accounts Payable (A/P) enables you to keep track of your vendor accounts and A/P invoices. 

Basically, you enter and edit your vendor transactions, and then pay them. 

Before you first use A/P, you or your system administrator must subscribe to and configure A/P 

for your company. Configuration involves selecting the features you want to appear in the A/P 

menus and pages as well as assigning permissions to those who need to access those features. 

For step-by-step instructions on how to configure A/P for your company, go to the Configure 

Accounts Payable page in the online help system or download the RealPage Accounting Accounts 

With Accounts Payable, you can:  

• 
Set up Accounts Payable to emulate your payment process. An optional approval cycle 

includes different levels authorization for approvers. For example, checks less than $500 may 

not need approval, but ones over $5,000 may need additional approval by staff authorized 

for that amount. You can require two check signatures that can be signed or digital, where 

the second is required at a preset amount. You can add digital files or attachments to 

transactions, providing permanent and secure access to underlying documentation. 

• 
Pay vendors in numerous ways. Payment types include full or partial payments against 

vendor A/P invoices, recurring and future payments, and advances. Payment methods 

include printed checks, online check delivery, cash, credit cards, funds transfer, and manual 

payments. You can apply overpayments and other amounts that vendors owe you to the 

next A/P invoice you pay. 

• 
Categorize vendors into different types, so you can run reports and other processes on an 

entire class of vendors. 

• 
Create custom terms. In addition to the default Accounts Payable terms and aging periods, 

you can create custom terms as you need them. 

• 
Use quick check entry to write checks manually – a fast way to enter up to 100 checks per 

page. You can also enter large numbers of A/P invoices in a similar fashion. In addition, you 

can create vendors on the fly. You cannot delete the A/P invoices or significantly edit them 

after they are paid, which allows for a high degree of accounting control. 

• 
Close Accounts Payable periods while keeping the General Ledger open; financial data is 

retained indefinitely. You can easily adjust accounts with debit or credit memos. 

• 
Create and print reports. To aid in cash management, the application generates a wide 

variety of easily customizable aging and payables reports and graphs. 

The Accounts Payable application is fully integrated with other accounting applications for 

real-time posting. You can also seamlessly integrate your external applications with our XML 

gateway. 

---


<!-- Page 23 -->
Chapter 1: Accounts Payable 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Daily Tasks User Guide 

• 
The Spend management application synchronizes with Accounts Payable to provide 

purchasing staff with procurement tools such as POs, with PO application transactions 

posting automatically to both Accounts Payable and the General Ledger. 

• 
The Facilities application integrates with RealPage Accounting’s asset records so that you 

can find in Fixed Assets and Accounts Payable. Changes that you make in one application 

change the asset records in the other application. When you import asset records, the 

system creates new asset records in both RealPage Accounting and Facilities. 

The Accounts Payable application comes with many standard reports that you can run 

immediately. To learn more, see the summary of standard Accounts Payable reports in the online 

help system or download the RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Reports User Guide.

These are the Accounts Payable menu options on the All tab. 

Approval workbench: Approve and decline transactions such as A/P invoices, payments, and

Search & Find Section 

•

• 
A/P invoices (on page 262): Opens the list of A/P invoices. 

• 
Invoice research (on page 430): Search for invoices. This list does not preload invoices, 

resulting in faster searches. 

• 
Payments (on page 514): Opens the list of posted payments. 

Daily Tasks Section 

Enter A/P Invoices Section 

• 
Create an A/P invoice: Create a new A/P invoice. 

• 
Quick A/P invoice entry: Enter multiple A/P invoices. 

• 
Approve vendors: Approve vendor records that have been created or updated. 

• 
Document dashboard: Review your invoice processing workflow. 

• 
AI-Invoice queue: Add and manage invoices by importing or scanning and have AI create 

the invoice records. 

• 
AI-Invoice upload audit: View the list of AI-added invoices and view details of failures. 

• 
View vendor requests: Opens the list of new and updated vendors waiting for approval. 

• 
View payment requests: Opens the list of payments waiting for approval. 

• 
Third party payments queue: View the list of payments made through a third party. 

• 
Paymode-X payments queue: View payment requests that are in queue for Paymode-X 

processing. 

• 
Paymode-X payments file: View the payments that have been sent to Paymode-X for 

processing. 

Pay A/P Invoices Section 

• 
Pay A/P Invoices: Pay A/P invoices. 

• 
Pay by entity: Pay A/P invoices based on the owing entity. 

• 
Select AP invoices to pay: Select A/P invoices that you want to pay, and then pay the 

invoices. 

• 
Adjustments: Create and manage adjustments. 

• 
Advances: Create and manage advances. 

• 
Release A/P invoices to pay: Release invoices so that they can be paid.

### About the Approval Workbench
*Source: `RP Accounting AP Daily Tasks User Guide.pdf`, Page 32*

Approval Workbench

About the Approval Workbench 

See the How to Get Here (on page 17) topic for a list of ways to access this area. 

Use the Approval workbench page to view the transactions waiting for approval. This page has 

two sections: 

• 
A filters section to control which transactions appear in the workbench. 

• 
A transactions list to approve, close, decline, view, or edit pending transactions. You can also 

add another approver or export the transaction to Excel. 

You can switch between two workbench views using the following buttons: 

• 
My approvals: Displays the transactions assigned to you for approval. 

AI Approvals in RealPage Accounting streamlines the A/P invoice approval process using AI 
Match percentage. 

• 
View all: Displays all transactions pending approval or partially approved. 

You cannot approve or decline transactions in the View all workbench view. However, you 
can click the link in the Status column to review the transaction’s approval history.

Before You Begin 

Access can vary depending on your organization’s subscriptions and your permissions. If you do 

not see the option in the menu, then ask your System Administrator to check your permissions. 

Subscriptions 

Your company must subscribe to the Company application and at least one of the following 

applications. Choose the appropriate application for the type of approval workflow that you need. 

• 
Accounts Payable: Subscribe to the Accounts Payable application to use the approval 

process with A/P invoices, A/P payments, and expense reports. Approvals of new and 

changed vendors also requires you to subscribe to the Accounts Payable application. 

• 
Spend Management: Subscribe to the Spend Management application to use the approval 

process with purchase orders, service contracts, and subcontracts. 

• 
General Ledger: Subscribe to the General Ledger application to use the approval process 

with journal entries. 

• 
Job Cost & Reserves: Subscribe to the Job Cost & Reserves application to use the approval 

process with job cost change orders.

#### Filtering Transactions in the Approval Workbench
*Source: `RP Accounting AP Daily Tasks User Guide.pdf`, Page 36*

Approval Workbench 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Daily Tasks User Guide

Filtering Transactions in the Approval Workbench 

See the How to Get Here topic (on page 17) for a list of ways to access the Approval workbench. 

The filter options on the Approval workbench page change depending on the transaction type 

you select. 

To filter the approval queue: 

1. 
Select the transaction type: 

• 
A/P invoice 

• 
Purchase order 

• 
Service contract 

• 
Subcontract 

• 
Job cost change order 

• 
Journal entry 

• 
A/P payment 

• 
Expense report 

2. 
Select additional filter criteria as needed. See the section below that corresponds with your 

transaction type for a list of available filter options. 

3. 
If you want to hide declined transactions from the list so you can edit and resubmit them, 

select the Included declined check box.  

By default, declined transactions are not included in the workbench. If you want to include 
them by default, then create a custom workbench view with the Include declined option 
selected and save it as the Default view. 

4. 
Click the Apply button. 

The approval queue refreshes with a list of transactions that meet the selected criteria. 

The system retains your filter selections even if you switch to a different transaction type 
in the workbench. To clear and reset filters, click the Clear button.

#### Approving and Declining Transactions
*Source: `RP Accounting AP Daily Tasks User Guide.pdf`, Page 41*

Chapter 2: Approval Workbench

Approving and Declining Transactions 

See the How to Get Here (on page 17) topic for a list of ways to access the Approval workbench.  

This page has two views, View All and My Approvals. You must be in the Approval Workbench - 

My Approvals view to approve and decline transactions. If you are on the Approvals Workbench 

- View All view, click the My Approvals button to change to the My Approvals view.  

From the My Approvals view, you can approve or decline transactions individually or in bulk. If 

you are reviewing A/P invoices, then you can use the Review and approve button to quickly 

approve or decline invoices back-to-back (on page 59). 

When you approve a transaction, the system looks up the next approver. If the next approver 
previously approved the transaction, then the system sets the status of the transaction to 
Approved. 

Approving One Transaction 

To approve one transaction: 

1. 
Click the Approve link. 

The Approve [transaction type] box opens. 

2. 
Optionally, in the Comments box, type a comment. 

3. 
Click the Approve button. 

---


<!-- Page 42 -->
Approval Workbench 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Daily Tasks User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Approving Multiple Transactions 

This method does not allow you to enter a comment about why you are approving these 
transactions. 

To approve multiple transactions: 

• 
From the Approval Workbench - My Approvals page, select the check box for each 

transaction that you want to approve, and then click the Approve button. 

Declining One Transaction 

To decline one transaction: 

1. 
Click the Decline link. 

The Decline [transaction name] box opens. 

2. 
In the Reason box, type an explanation for why you declined the transaction. 

3. 
Click the Decline button. 

---


<!-- Page 43 -->
Chapter 2: Approval Workbench 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Daily Tasks User Guide 

Declining Multiple Transactions 

This method does not allow you to enter a comment about why you are declining the 
transactions. 

To decline multiple transactions: 

• 
Click the check box for each transaction you want to decline, and then click the Decline 

button. 

You also have the option to close and delete declined purchase orders to remove them from your 

Approval Workbench list page. You must have Delete permissions.

Viewing and Editing Transactions in the Approval Workbench 

See the How to Get Here (on page 17) topic for a list of ways to access the Approval workbench. 

To view and evaluate transactions for approval: 

1. 
Select the desired transaction type. 

The system filters the list so that it shows only the type of transaction that you selected. The top 

section of the list contains controls that you can use to filter the list. 

1. 
Find the transaction that you want to review, and then click the View or Edit link. 

When the A/P invoice transaction is first opened, the system automatically opens the 
attachment to view. You can choose to not show attachments automatically on the My 

Preferences page by selecting the Do not show attachments automatically within invoices 
check box. 

2. 
Review the transaction, make changes as needed if you selected Edit, and then click Save. 

When Gasoline is selected in the Expense category field and the tax rate is enabled in 


> **Navigation Path:** `Accounts Payable > Setup > Expense Report Configuration, and when you click the`


Amount field, a box opens that allows you to enter the number of miles. When you click 

Save, the system recalculates the amount with the tax rate included. 

3. 
Continue by approving or declining the transaction.  

After the journal entry has gone through the approval process and been approved, it cannot 

be edited.

Exporting Transactions to Excel 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > Approvals > Approval Workbench`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Spend Management > All > Workbench`


You can export transaction data from the Approval workbench or Spend management 

workbench to an Excel file. The data included in the file depends on the columns that you have 

enabled in the workbench. 

To export data using the Export to Excel button: 

1. 
Click the Export to Excel button in the upper-right corner of the approval queue. 

The Excel file downloads with any column data configured in the workbench. 

2. 
In the Save as box, name the Excel file, and determine a file location for the exported file. 

3. 
Click Save. 

Adding an Approver to a Transaction 

See the How to Get Here (on page 17) topic for a list of ways to access the Approval workbench. 

As an approver, you can add another approver to a transaction in the Approval workbench. 

To add an approver to a transaction: 

1. 
Click the Add approver link next to the transaction. 

The Add approver box opens. 

2. 
Type any comments explaining why you are adding the approver. 

You can drag the lower-right corner of the Comments text box to resize it as needed. 

3. 
In the Additional approver drop-down list, select the user that you want to add to the 

transaction, and then click the Done button. 

All users in the drop-down list have access to the transaction ’s location.

#### Sending a Transaction Back to the Previous Approver
*Source: `RP Accounting AP Daily Tasks User Guide.pdf`, Page 46*



#### Viewing an Attachment for a Transaction
*Source: `RP Accounting AP Daily Tasks User Guide.pdf`, Page 46*

Approval Workbench 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Daily Tasks User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Sending a Transaction Back to the Previous Approver 

See the How to Get Here (on page 17) topic for a list of ways to access the Approval workbench. 

Some transactions require approvals from multiple levels. If a transaction pending your approval 

was approved by someone else, you can send the transaction back to that approver instead of 

declining the transaction outright. 

To send a transaction back to the previous approver: 

1. 
On the Approval workbench - My approvals page, click the Send back link in the Send 

back column next to the transaction. 

The Send back box opens. 

2. 
Type your reason for sending back the transaction in the Comments field. 

3. 
Click the Send back button. 

The system loads the Approval workbench - My approvals page, and the transaction no 

longer appears in your queue. 

Sending Back Multiple Transactions 

To send back multiple transactions to the previous approver: 

1. 
From the Approval workbench - My approvals page, select the check box next to each 

transaction that you want to send back to the previous approver. 

2. 
Click the Send back link in the Send back column next to any of the transactions that you 

selected. 

The Send back box opens. 

3. 
Type your reason for sending back the transaction in the Comments field. 

4. 
Select the additional approver from the Additional approver drop-down list. 

5. 
Click the Send back button. 

The system loads the Approval workbench - My approvals page, and the transactions no 

longer appear in your queue. 

Viewing an Attachment for a Transaction 

See the How to Get Here (on page 17) topic for a list of ways to access this area. 

To view an attachment for a transaction in the approval queue: 

1. 
Click the 
 icon in the Actions column next to the transaction. 

2. 
Click the Open button to open the file. You may have to open the file in a separate program 

to view its contents. 

---

Viewing the Approval History of a Transaction

Approval Workbench

Available Budget Page 

See How to Get Here (on page 408) for a list of ways to access this page. 

This page opens when you click the Spend control button on an A/P invoice, purchase order, or 

subcontract. 

The tabs on the Available budget page change depending on the Line entry type that you 

selected in the transaction:  

• 
Standard 

• 
Job Cost 

• 
Both 

Standard Line Items 

If you selected Standard as the Line entry type of an A/P invoice or purchase order, then the 

Available budget page includes three tabs, (Month, Year to date, and Current Year), that show 

the monthly, year-to-date, and current-year spending for a property and account. 

Use the Current year tab to view the full-year budget and current activity and compare it to the 

planned activity for the remainder of the year.

Job Cost Line Items 

If you selected Include Job cost as the Line entry type on an A/P invoice or purchase order—or if 

the transaction is a subcontract—then the Available budget page shows only job cost budget 

amounts. You can view the amount budgeted, the actual amount spent, and the budget 

remaining for the job cost code. 

Standard and Job Cost Line Items

amount spent, and the budget remaining for the job cost code.

### Approval History List
*Source: `RP Accounting AP Daily Tasks User Guide.pdf`, Page 53*

Chapter 2: Approval Workbench 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Daily Tasks User Guide 

Approval History List 

See the How to Get Here topic for a list of ways to access this area. 

Use this page to review a transaction’s approval history. This page displays when you click a status 

in the Approval workbench. 

When you enable approvals for a transaction type, RealPage Accounting auto-generates a 
default policy and a default workflow for routing transactions of this type to the user (or role) 
you have set as the default approver. Default policies and workflows are visible only to admin 
users, including any events or actions logged in the approval history. 

Columns 

• 
Policy type: This column shows the policy type that the system used to approve the item. 

• 
Policy name: This column shows the policy name that the system used to approve the item. 

Click the link to view policy details. 

• 
Workflow name: This column shows the name of the workflow that the system used in the 

transaction. Click the link to view workflow details. 

• 
Approver role/user: This column contains a link to information about the person who 

decided on the approval. Click to view the role assignment details. You can find out who is 

assigned to a particular role with this link. 

• 
Approved/Declined by: This column contains the user name of the person who made the 

approval decisions. 

• 
Event date: This column contains the date that the transaction last underwent an approval 

event. (It was submitted for approval or partially approved.) 

• 
Comments: This column contains the comments the approver made along with his decision. 

• 
State: This column contains the status of the approval. 

• 
Action type: This column contains the approval status of the transaction. 

• 
Action comments: This column contains the comments associated with the action in the 

state. 

• 
Submitted by: This column contains the name of the user who submitted the transaction. 

“Console member” appears when the user accesses RealPage Accounting through the 
console rather than by logging in directly.

#### Viewing Approval Policy Details from Approval History
*Source: `RP Accounting AP Daily Tasks User Guide.pdf`, Page 54*



#### Viewing Workflow Details from Approval History
*Source: `RP Accounting AP Daily Tasks User Guide.pdf`, Page 54*

Approval Workbench 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Daily Tasks User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Viewing Approval Policy Details from Approval History 

See the How to Get Here topic for a list of ways to access this area. 

You can view the details of an approval policy that was used to decide on a transaction. 

1. 
Apply filters (on page 18) to the workbench so that the desired transaction appears in the 

list. 

2. 
If needed, click the View all button to show all transactions (not just the transactions in your 

approval queue). 

3. 
Find the desired transaction in the approval queue. 

4. 
Click the link in the Status column. 

The Approval history list opens. See Approval History List (on page 35) for more 

information. 

5. 
Click the text in the Policy name column to open the Approval policy manager, allowing 

you to review the policy details. 

6. 
Click the Close button to return to the Approval history box. You can also click Print to 

print the approval policy details. 

Viewing Workflow Details from Approval History 

See the How to Get Here topic for a list of ways to access this area. 

You can view the details of an approval workflow that was used to route a transaction. 

1. 
Apply filters (on page 18) to the workbench so that the desired transaction appears in the 

list. 

2. 
If needed, click the View all button to show all transactions (not just the transactions in your 

approval queue). 

3. 
Find the desired transaction in the approval queue. 

4. 
Click the link in the Status column. 

The Approval history list opens. See Approval history list (on page 35) for more information. 

5. 
Click the link in the Workflow name column to display the Approval workflow details. 

6. 
Click Close to return to the Approval history box. You can also click Print to print the 

approval workflow details.

### Review and Approve Process for A/P Invoices

#### Enabling the Image Viewer

Review and Approve Process for A/P Invoices 

The Review and approve process allows you to evaluate A/P invoices quickly. Instead of opening 

each A/P invoice individually, the Review and approve process moves to the next A/P invoice in 

queue instead of returning you to the workbench to select the next item to evaluate.  

The Review and approve process is available only for A/P invoices. Before you can use this 
process, you must configure the system. 

Configuration Process 

1. 
Add an approval policy that uses the accounting reviewer policy type. See Creating a 

Reviewer Policy Type (on page 58). 

2. 
Apply the policy to a workflow, and then assign a property to the workflow. See Adding a 

Reviewer Policy to a Workflow (on page 59). 

This feature works well with the image viewer. When you open an A/P invoice with an 
attachment, the attached document opens in a separate window. You can enable the image 
viewer in your preferences. See Enabling the Image Viewer (on page 57 ). 

Reviewing and Approving Process 

• 
Someone creates A/P invoices for the property to which the reviewer policy is assigned. 

When the user submits the A/P invoice for approval, it appears in the Approval workbench. 

• 
The approver opens the Approval workbench and clicks the Review & approve button to 

begin reviewing A/P invoices. See Reviewing and Approving A/P Invoices (on page 59). 

Enabling the Image Viewer 

[login name] > My Preferences 

The image viewer opens attachments in a separate window. 

To enable the image viewer: 

1. 
Click your login name in the upper-right corner of the browser window. A shortcut menu 

appears. 

2. 
Select the My preferences option. 

3. 
In the Display section, find the Personalize interactive behavior section.

Adding a Reviewer Policy to a Workflow 

To add a reviewer policy to a workflow: 

1. 
From the Applications menu, select Company, and then select the All tab. 

2. 
Select Approval Workflow. The Approval workflows list is displayed. 

3. 
Find the approval workflow to which you want to add a policy, and then select the Edit link. 

4. 
In the Policies list, click the next blank row in the Policy name column, and then select the 

new policy from the list that displays. 

5. 
Click the Override check box if you want the policy to be an override.  

6. 
Click the Save button. 

Reviewing and Approving A/P Invoices 

See the How to Get Here (on page 17) topic for a list of ways to access this area. 

When the Approval workbench is filtered by A/P invoices, an additional button appears in the 

upper-right corner labeled Review & approve. This button allows you to quickly open and review 

invoices in the order they appear in the approval queue.  

To review and approve A/P invoices: 

1. 
From the Applications menu, select Company, and then select the All tab. 

2. 
Select Approval workbench. 

3. 
Select the A/P invoice option. Set any other filters as needed. 

4. 
Click the Apply button. The system filters the list so that it shows only A/P invoices. 

5. 
Click the Review & approve button. The A/P invoice page opens. If the A/P invoice has an 

attachment and you have enabled the image viewer, the attachment displays in a separate 

window. If not, the invoice image will show on the same page as the invoice. 

If the Review & approve button does not appear, there are no A/P invoices in queue to 
approve. 

6. 
Review the A/P invoice. You can also edit the invoice at the same time. 

7. 
Click one of the buttons: 

• 
Approve & next: Approve the current A/P invoice, and then have the system display 

the next A/P invoice to evaluate. If you made any changes to the invoice, your changes 

are saved and the invoice is routed to the next person for approval. 

• 
Approve & next > Next: Skip the current A/P invoice and display the next A/P invoice 

in your queue. Any changes you made to the invoice will not be saved. 

---

8. 
Click the Done button to exit the review and approval process. 

When an eInvoice is created in Accounting, goes through approvals, and then gets posted, 
RealPage Accounting sends an update to OpsMerchant to change the partner status from 

Pending to Approved. This ensures that the vendor is aware of the current status of the 
invoice. We also send updates to OpsMerchant when the eInvoice is paid or voided, along 
with the payment details.

### Vendors (Suppliers) Overview
*Source: `RP Accounting AP Daily Tasks User Guide.pdf`, Page 80*

Vendors (Suppliers) 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Daily Tasks User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Vendors (Suppliers) Overview 

A vendor (supplier) is a person or business that supplies goods or services to your company. 

In many situations, a company presents the vendor with a purchase order stating the goods or 

services needed, the price, the delivery date, and other terms. 

Generally, when the vendor delivers the goods or services it also sends an invoice to the company. 

The company should then match the vendor’s invoice with its purchase order and receiving 

report. If the three documents agree, the company can than arrange for payment to the vendor. 

Every vendor must have a vendor record in the system. An optional vendor record approval exists 

to ensure that your company has appropriate transparency into the vendors being used for goods 

and services. 

When you add a vendor, you can enter key descriptive information about that vendor and 

establish how you want to pay them, such as by check, credit card, or electronic payment.

Example of Vendors List 

This is an example of a simple Vendors list and its filters: 

a) Include One-time: When you create or select a vendor that you will use only once or rarely, 

you can flag that vendor so that the vendor doesn’t appear on the vendor list unless you 

filter for it. 

b) Include Inactive: A list can contain items that are inactive but still present because they link 

to transaction data. For example, you may have a vendor who no longer carries items you 

need to purchase. In the vendor record, you flag the vendor as Inactive. Inactive vendors 

aren’t included in the list unless you specify their display. 

Select the Include Inactive check box to include items set to a status of Inactive in the 

search. The system refreshes the list and adds a Status column to indicate which items are 

active and which are inactive.  

Clear the Include Inactive check box to prevent inactive items from appearing in the list. 

c) Group Filters: Dimensions such as vendors and customers also have dimension groups. 

After creating dimension groups, you can use them to filter a dimension’s list. To create a 

dimension group, see Setting up dimension groups. 

d) Display Hierarchy: By default, the Vendors list uses icons and indentation to show how 

parent and child vendors are related. This hierarchical view is helpful when you have 

vendors that are related, such as when you are doing business with subsidiaries or divisions 

of the same company and need to separately track their contact and payment information. 

• 
Groups 

• 
Types 

• 
Visibility 

Click the Display Hierarchy check box to show the vendor relationships.

Importing Vendors 

Workflow for importing vendor and vendor-related data: 

1. 
Download the vendors template. 

2. 
Fill the template file with vendor data. 

3. 
Save the file in CSV format (on page 257). 

4. 
Import the vendor file. 

• 
If you plan on importing vendor 1099 transactions, follow the instructions in Importing 

Vendor 1099 Transactions. 

• 
If you plan to import vendor ACH information, follow the instructions in Importing 

Vendor Electronic Payment Information. 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > Import Data > Set Up AP Master List, Open Invoices 
and Adjustments > Vendor > Template`

Open the Company menu. 

2. 
Select the Import data option.

Do not use leading zeros in ID fields. If you MUST use leading zeros in IDs, convert the column of 

ID numbers to text format in Excel before importing the file content. Excel does not remove the 

leading zeros when you save the file. Remember to do this every time you use a template to 

import information that requires IDs.

template file. Take care to exactly match the template’s data structure as you do this.

the latest vendor template to add preferred payment method to vendor records when you 
import vendors.

Adding Vendor (Supplier) Records 

See the How to Get Here (on page 64) topic for a list of ways to access the Vendors list. 

Adding Vendor Records 

Add vendor records when you want to pay A/P invoices.  

When you add a vendor, you can type key descriptive information about that vendor and select 

the payment method that the vendor prefers, such as by check, credit card, or ACH (electronic 

payment). 

If you enabled the Single Scan Upload feature in your preferences and have previously 
downloaded the Dynamsoft scanning software, you may be prompted to update the software 
when you add a new scannable record such as an A/P invoice, vendor, purchase order, service 
contract, or document. When this occurs, download the new software; there is no need to 
uninstall the previous version. 

To add a basic vendor record: 

1. 
In the ID field, type a unique identifier for the vendor record. 

Use a character as a prefix to your ID; for example, V0001 for a vendor ID. 

When you save the record, the system converts the vendor ID to all uppercase to prevent 

duplication. You can prevent this conversion by clearing the Set IDs to uppercase check 

box. For information, see Disabling Vendor ID Capitalization. 

After creating a vendor ID, you can only change it with the Customer Utility Tool. Most users 

do not have access to the tool as it requires administrator privileges. Contact your system 

administrator if you need to change a vendor ID. 

2. 
In the Name field, type the vendor’s name. The system completes the Print as field in the 

Primary Contact section. 

3. 
Select the One-time use check box to designate the vendor as a one-time or occasional use 

vendor that you don’t want to include in your standard vendor lists. An example of a 

one-time use of a vendor record is when you issue a customer’s deposit refund. 

These vendors won’t appear in the Vendors (Suppliers) list unless you select the Include 

one-time option at the top of the list. 

4. 
Select the Corporate vendor check box as needed. When you add an invoice for a corporate 

vendor, the system marks the invoice as a corporate invoice and prevents it from appearing 

in Site Experience. Also, corporate vendors do not appear in Site Experience. 

5. 
Select the This vendor is an owner check box when the vendor is also the owner of the 

company. 

---


<!-- Page 89 -->
Chapter 3: Vendors (Suppliers) 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Daily Tasks User Guide 

6. 
In the Status list, select the Active option if you want vendors to have A/P invoices entered 

and payments issued. You can also select the Inactive option to prevent A/P invoices from 

being entered and payment issued. 

You can inactivate multiple vendors at a time using the Customer Utility Tool’s Inactivate 

Vendors option. 

7. 
Select the appropriate Storefront supplier code. This code is the vendor’s code for use with 

the Storefront application associated with Spend Management.  

If your company does not use Spend Management, then this option does not appear. 

8. 
Select the Require PO – Spend check box option when your company requires that you 

create a manual or online purchase order before creating an online A/P invoice on behalf of 

the vendor. If a purchase order is not available to match with the A/P invoice, then the user 

cannot submit the A/P invoice for the vendor. 

The Require PO – Spend check box appears only when your company has purchased and 
installed Spend Management. 

9. 
Select the Send Offline Purchase Orders to Vendor check box. When enabled, when the 

user adds or edits a purchase order in the Submitted or Partially Approved state, the option 

Send purchase order to vendor appears.  

To use this feature, the vendor’s subscription type must also be set to Invoice Submission 

Service, and a Storefront Supplier Code must be defined for the vendor. 

If this option is ever disabled, the system continues to show the Send purchase order to 

vendor option on historical purchase orders.  

10. 
Select Keep active to prevent the vendor from being automatically changed to Inactive.  

Use this option for vendors that should remain available, even if they meet conditions that 

would normally make them inactive. For example, companies that use the AI Finance Agent 

may have rules that automatically inactivate vendor records based on configured criteria. 

When Keep active is selected, the vendor stays active and can continue to be used. 

11. 
Select the Exclude from Full Service check box to prevent the vendor from syncing with 

Invoice processing full service. You can enable syncing again at any time. 

12. 
Select the Exclude from Auto Request Storefront Account check box to prevent the system 

from sending an automatic request for the vendor for a Storefront account.  

13. 
Select the Preferred vendor check box to identify this vendor as one your company prefers 

or recommends using. This setting helps users distinguish preferred vendors from other 

vendors in the vendor list. 

---

14. 
Select the Do not itemize invoices check box if you do not want the AI Agent to itemize this 

vendor’s invoices when its invoices are scanned. The system will define only one line item 

for the total amount of each invoice when the AI Agent scans this vendor’s invoices. This 

setting is useful when, after scanning in an invoice, you find that you have to delete line 

items after the AI Agent has broken out charge details into multiple line items.  

If you do not select this check box, the AI Agent creates a line item for each charge it finds 

in invoices when it scans invoices.  

15. 
Select the OneSite resident check box if the vendor is a resident in a OneSite-managed 

property. 

16. 
Select the Sync to external systems check box to allow RealPage Accounting to sync the 

vendor record with Procore or other external systems. 

This field appears only if you have configured the Procore integration in Job Cost & 
Reserves. 

17. 
Select the RequirePO check box when the vendor requires a purchase order. The A/P 

invoice must be matched to a purchase order before you save and post it. 

This field does not apply to actions performed in the RealPage Financial Suite system. The 

RequirePO check box appears only when your system is integrated with OPSTechnology. 
When the RequirePO check box is selected, it causes the OPS system to validate the 
purchase order record in OPS.

3. 
In the VAT reg no field, type the vendor’s VAT registration number.  

4.

validated.

Vendors (Suppliers): Additional Information Tab 

The Additional Information tab has up to six sections: 

• 
Vendor Details 

• 
Documents: This section appears when you have single scan enabled in your preferences. 

The section replaces the Attachments field, allowing you to upload documents by scanning 

or attaching them from your computer.  

• 
Billing Details 

• 
Special Designation: Fill in this section when the vendor qualifies for a special designation. 

• 
Vendor Merge: Fill in this section when you want to pay all open invoices with this vendor 

with one check. 

• 
CA DE 542: Fill in this section when the vendor is located in California. 

Filling In the Vendor Details Section 

1. 
In the Type ID field, select or add a vendor type ID. Type IDs are used to group vendors so 

that you can run a report on them. 

2. 
In the Parent field, find or add a parent vendor. The parent vendor must have a record in 

the system before you can add it to the new vendor record. 

3. 
In the G/L group or Account label field, select the G/L group or account label to associate 

with this vendor. 

You can use the field level controls to add a new G/L account, view a G/L account’s record, 

or find a G/L account’s record. To add or import G/L accounts, you must be at the top level. 

4. 
In the Tax ID field, type the employer identification number (EIN) for the vendor. An EIN is a 

federal tax identification number used to identify a business entity. 

5. 
If the vendor is eligible for 1099 taxing, select the 1099 eligible check box.

the Form 1099 Information with Default Box box (on page 198 ) appears, allowing you to

Adding Attachments to the Vendor Record 

When you have scanning disabled in your preferences, use the Attachments field to add 

documents to a record. 

When the Attachments field appears, you can attach a file to the record. You can attach a file that 

has already been added to the system, or you can upload a file from your computer. You can also 

drag your files from the file explorer into the Attachments box if you are using Firefox, Chrome, 

or Edge web browsers. 

• 
To select a file that is already stored in the system, select the document that you want to 

attach from the Attachments drop-down list. 

• 
To upload a document from your computer, click the Add link in the Attachments 

drop-down list, and then click the Choose Files button. 

• 
Click the Show All/Show unattached link to change the contents of the drop-down list 

between showing all files to showing unattached files. Unattached files are files that are not 

yet attached to any other record in the system. 

• 
To view a document before attaching it, click the document that you want to review, and 

then click the View link. 

• 
To find a document in the system, click the Find link. 

• 
If you are using Firefox, Chrome, or Edge, you can drop your file on the Attachments box to 

attach the file to this record.  

If you have enabled the single scan feature in your preferences, then the Attachments field 
does not appear. Instead, the record has a Documents section where you can attach files.

Filling In the Billing Details Section 

1. 
Select the appropriate A/P account for this vendor. When you select an A/P account in the 

vendor record, the system completes the A/P account field in every A/P invoice or 

adjustment that includes this vendor. You can override the A/P account by selecting a 

different A/P account when needed. 

This drop-down list appears only when you’ve enabled the feature. The system fills in the 

A/P account that you select here in every A/P invoice or adjustment that includes this 

vendor.  

In Accounts Payable, this feature applies to A/P invoices and adjustments only. It does not 
apply to recurring A/P invoices, manual payments, quick A/P invoice entry, or advances. 

2. 
In the Default expense account drop-down list, select the desired default G/L account for 

this vendor’s A/P invoices. You can type the G/L code, and the system will complete the 

code. 

 You can override the account later on the A/P invoices page. 

3. 
Select the Taxable check box if regular purchases from this vendor are taxable. When you 

select the Taxable check box, you must select a tax group. 

• 
In the Contact tax group drop-down list, select a contact tax group. Assigning a 

vendor to a contact tax group instructs the system to apply a specific tax schedule to 

this vendor for applicable documents in accounts payable. 

The contact tax group must exist before being added to this vendor. 

4. 
In the Credit limit field, type the amount of credit extended to you by the vendor. 

5. 
To put a vendor on credit hold, select the On hold check box. This status prevents users 

from entering A/P invoices into the system for the vendor. 

6. 
Select the Don’t pay check box to stop payments to the vendor from the system. Users can 

add A/P invoices with the vendor, but the system prevents payment until someone clears 

this check box.  

The Don’t pay check box can be used as a temporary measure when your company is 

waiting for supporting documentation from the vendor such as proof of insurance or 

licenses. 

The Don’t pay check box is also useful when your company determines that it will no longer 

do business with a particular vendor and does not intend to make any further payments to 

that vendor. This decision could be due to various reasons such as poor quality of goods or 

services, unresolved disputes, or the vendor going out of business. 

7. 
In the Comments field, type any comments about the vendor. Be mindful of what you enter 

in this field, as other users can see these comments.

Filling In the Special Designation Section 

Use this section to mark the vendor’s business with a special designation. 

The US government offers set-asides for businesses with special designations. The designations 

include women-owned businesses, veteran-owned businesses, HUBZone businesses (businesses 

that are located in a traditionally underutilized business area), and 8(a) businesses owned by 

socially and economically disadvantaged people. You can flag a vendor’s business with one of 

these special designations.  

1. 
In the Special Designation section, select the check box that applies to the vendor’s business. 

Select all check boxes that apply. 

2. 
In the Expiration date column, type or select the date that the designation expires.  

The special designation status expires after nine years of holding the designation. 

About the Vendor Merge Section 

When a vendor has been merged with another vendor, this section shows the vendor merge 

history. When the vendor record has not been merged with another vendor record, the list is 

empty. 

Filling In the CA DE 542 Section 

Follow the instructions in this section when the vendor is located in California. 

1. 
Select the CA DE 542 Required check box when you are required by California state law to 

fill in Form CA DE 542. 

2. 
In the Date sent field, select or type the date that the company completed the Form CA DE 

542 for this vendor. 

What’s Next? 

Continue filling out the vendor record by clicking the Contact List (on page 80) tab.

Vendors (Suppliers): Contact List Tab 

Use this tab to record additional contact names associated with the vendor. 

The Contact List tab has two sections: 

• 
Pay to/Return to 

• 
Contact List 

You can use this tab in two ways: 

• 
You can select existing contacts for the Pay to/Return to contacts.  

• 
Or, you can add new contacts in the lower section, and then select the new contacts in the 

Pay to/Return to section in the upper part of the tab. 

Filling In the Pay to/Return to Section 

1. 
In the Primary contact list, you can select Same as vendor to use the same contact that 

appears in the Primary contact section on the first page of the vendor record. If you need to 

specify a different contact, then select the appropriate name from the drop-down list. If you 

do not see the desired name in the drop-down list, then you can add it in the next section, 

Contact list. 

2. 
In the Pay to contact list, select the appropriate contact from the drop-down list. The 

system uses this contact as the default vendor contact for paying checks and creating A/P 

invoices. If you do not see the desired name in the drop-down list, then you can add a 

contact to the Contact List section.  

3. 
In the Return to contact list, if you need to specify a return-to contact, then select the 

appropriate contact from the drop-down list. If you do not see the correct name in the 

drop-down list, then add it to the Contact List tab. The system uses the return-to contact in 

several accounts payable activities. 

4. 
In the 1099 contact list, if you need to specify a dedicated 1099 contact for printing 

purposes, then select the appropriate contact from the drop-down list. If you do not see the 

correct name in the drop-down list, then add it in the Contact List section. 

Filling In the Contact List Section 

Use this section when the contact that you want to specify in one of the upper fields does not yet 

exist in the system. You can also use this section to associate a category with an existing contact. 

1. 
In the Category column, type a word that categorizes the vendor contact. For example, the 

category might represent a location (home, office) or a position (CEO, or Returns). 

2. 
In the Contact list, select a contact that falls into the category. You can also click the Add 

link in the drop-down list to add a new contact record. 

3. 
Optionally, assign the new contact to one of the contacts in the Pay to/Return to section.

Configuring Vendor Records for Joint Checks 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > All > Vendors > Edit > Primary Contact`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > All > Vendors > Edit > Contact List > Pay To 
Contact`


Before you can issue joint checks to two parties, update the vendor records of both signers.  

Updating Vendor Records Pay to Contact 

To update a vendor record so that the system issues joint checks:  

1. 
Create a new vendor record or open the vendor record of one of the vendors that you want 

to pay with a joint check.  

When creating checks, the system addresses the check to the same contact that appears on 

the invoice and uses the text in the Print as field of the contact record to fill in the Pay to 

the order of field on the check. The Pay to contact field often defaults to the vendor’s 

primary contact. When this is the case, you can change the Print as field of the primary 

contact on the vendor record. The primary contact’s information appears on the Vendor tab 

(the first page) of the vendor record. 

2. 
In the Primary contact section, type the names of both parties that must sign the joint check 

in the Print as field. 

3. 
Save the vendor record.

Vendors (Suppliers): Payment Information Tab 

Use this tab to set up payment priorities and the terms of payment. 

The Payment Information tab has three sections:

Payment details 

• 
Payment services 

• 
Vendor account number 

Although you’re not required to enter payment information for a vendor, you can use the options 

on the Payment information tab to:

Track basic information about your account with the vendor, such as your account number 

and how the vendor prefers to be paid. 

• 
Set a default for the payment request method. You can merge A/P invoices into one 

payment request for this vendor, or you can set one request per invoice. 

• 
Set up electronic payments for this vendor. 

• 
Set up automatic payment notifications for the vendor.

After you have selected payments for a vendor on the Pay A/P invoices page, you can merge the

all payment requests to be merged into one A/P invoice. 

• 
Generate one request per AP invoice: The system generates one payment request per 

A/P invoice. 

• 
Merge requests into one per vendor: Merge selected payments into one draft 

payment request in the outbox. This option prints the Pay to Contact of the vendor, 

not the A/P invoice, on the check.

one draft payment request in the outbox. The A/P invoice’s Pay to Contact will appear 

on the check.

request page appears.

Vendor name 
Payment date 
Payment method 
Bank 
Currency

Click Merge to merge the selected payment or payments into an existing draft payment 

request in the outbox. If multiple A/P invoices match, then the system lets you choose the 

A/P invoice to merge with you selected A/P invoices. 

If you change your mind, you can choose not to merge payments. On the
 Merge payment 

request page, click Don’t Merge to add it to the outbox as a separate draft payment

link.

Click the Restrictions tab.

Choose how you want to restrict the vendor:

Unrestricted: Select this option if you want the vendor to be used in any transaction,

Click Save.

Marking a Vendor as Don’t Pay 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > All > Search & Find > Vendors > Edit > Additional 
Information > Billing Details > Don’t Pay`


You might mark a vendor as “Don’t Pay” when your company determines that it will no longer do 

business with a particular vendor and does not intend to make any further payments to that 

vendor. This decision could be due to various reasons such as poor quality of goods or services, 

unresolved disputes, or the vendor going out of business. 

Let’s say Company A decides to mark Vendor X as “Don’t Pay” because of consistent delivery 

delays and quality issues with the products received. Company A has decided to terminate its 

relationship with Vendor X and will not be making any future purchases or payments to them. 

After marking the vendor as “Don’t Pay,” no further payments are processed for the vendor. 

To mark the vendor as “Don’t Pay”: 

1. 
Open the Accounts payable menu. 

2. 
In the Search & Find section, click Vendors. 

3. 
Click the Edit link of the vendor that you want to mark as “Don’t pay.” 

4. 
Click the Additional Information tab. 

5. 
Find the Billing details section. 

6. 
Select the Don’t pay check box. 

7. 
Click Save.

#### About Vendor Contact Information
*Source: `RP Accounting AP Daily Tasks User Guide.pdf`, Page 120*

Vendors (Suppliers) 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Daily Tasks User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

About Vendor Contact Information 

When you set up a vendor, the system uses the information in the Primary contact section on the 

Vendor tab as the default contact information for the vendor unless otherwise specified. On the 

Contact list tab, you can set up and attach contacts that have different locations or contact 

information from the initial default vendor information.  

Assigning a contact to one of the contact types (Primary, Pay to, Return to, or 1099) sets that 

contact as the new default vendor contact for specific areas. The following list describes which 

contact type is used as the default for which transactions and activities:  

• 
Primary contact: Default contact for all transactions if no other vendor contacts are defined.  

• 
Pay to contact: Default contact when paying by checks or creating A/P invoices. 

• 
Return to contact: Contact for A/P and purchasing transactions.  

• 
1099 contact: Default contact for all 1099 tax transactions and documents. Learn more 

about 1099 vendor information (on page 157).  

Contact Names: On-screen and Printed 

When you set up your contacts, there are two fields you should pay special attention to: 

Suggested contact name and Print as.  

Suggested contact name is a unique ID used across your company in common areas such as 

vendors, employees, customers, users, projects, dimensions, and recurring transactions. This field 

isn’t printed on your documents or used in your transactions; rather, the Suggested contact name 

is how the contact record is stored in the system. This name is that you use to search through 

contacts in the system, whether through the Contact list or when selecting a different contact 

during the creation of a transaction. After the Suggested contact name is created, it cannot be 

changed.  

In contrast, the Print as field defines how the contact name appears on printed documents, such 

as A/P invoices and checks. The Print as field doesn’t have to match the Suggested contact name. 

Furthermore, because the Print as field is not unique, you can make changes to it at any time.  

Because of how the system uses these fields in your company, you don’t need to create a new 

contact record when your vendor’s name or mailing information changes. Moreover, you can 

create separate contact records for different vendor locations using unique Suggested contact 

names, but still retain the same Print as name across all records as it should appear.  

For example, say you need to add contacts for the vendor AM Supplies. AM Supplies has 
locations in both California and North Carolina. In this case, you would create two contact 
records - one for California and one for North Carolina. For the California contact record, you’d 
set the Suggested contact name to something like “AM Supplies vendor California” so that the 
record is easy to identify when setting up your vendor contact list or manually choosing 
different contacts on transactions. However, you ’d set the Print as field to “AM Supplies” as it

#### Guidelines for Updating Vendors
*Source: `RP Accounting AP Daily Tasks User Guide.pdf`, Page 123*

Chapter 3: Vendors (Suppliers) 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Daily Tasks User Guide 

Guidelines for Updating Vendors 

These guidelines pertain to updating vendor records using the CSV import method. 

The most important thing to remember when updating vendor records is that any change you 

make in the spreadsheet will affect your vendor records. For example: 

• 
If you update spreadsheet data for a vendor, the information you specify will overwrite the 

data in the existing vendor record. 

• 
If you remove data from the spreadsheet, the corresponding information will be removed 

from the vendor record. 

Do not overwrite existing data with blank data unless you intend to remove that data from 
your Vendors list. For example, if you export the Email Address field and then clear the 
data in the Email Address column of your spreadsheet, existing vendor email addresses will 
be deleted when you import the file. 

Recommended Precautions 

• 
Make a backup of your vendor information before you make changes. Export the vendors 

list using the “CSV for Import” format and save it as a backup so that you have a record of 

the Vendors list before the update process. 

When you export the “CSV for Import ” file, be sure to include the Vendor ID column. This 
identifies the vendor record that you are updating. 

• 
Before making large-scale changes, test your update process. For example, create a few test 

vendors and then update just those vendor records. 

Column order isn’t important; for example, the Vendor ID doesn’t need to be first. The 
header row identifies the contents of each column. 

When you’re updating the “CSV for Import” file, keep in mind that different types of fields 
require different information. For check box options, enter TRUE to select the option and 
enter FALSE to clear the option.

#### Troubleshooting Vendor Restrictions
*Source: `RP Accounting AP Daily Tasks User Guide.pdf`, Page 130*

Vendors (Suppliers) 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Daily Tasks User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Troubleshooting Vendor Restrictions 

A location can use a vendor if the location is included in vendor restrictions. When a location is 

excluded from vendor restrictions while the vendor account is active, problems may arise as A/P 

invoices are submitted for the vendor. For example, if you restrict a vendor of a location in which 

the vendor has an active account with pending transactions, the pending transactions will receive 

this error: 

“Location is invalid, enter valid location.” 

If you try to restrict a vendor from a location that has an active account, this message is displayed: 

“Vendor has active storefront accounts for locations outside of locations restricted,  

 please correct and try again.” 

This means that the vendor has an active account number for an excluded location. 

To remedy these problems, do one of the following: 

• 
Remove the vendor account from the location where you do not want the vendor to be 

used, and then exclude the location (on page 95) from the vendor restriction list. You can 

continue to pay invoices. 

• 
Change the vendor restrictions to include the location that has an active vendor account. 

Invoices will no longer cause an error. See Setting Up Vendor Restrictions (on page 95). 

• 
Generate a vendor account request for the excluded location in the entity’s record. Invoices 

will no longer cause an error. See Requesting a Vendor Account Number for a Property for 

Online Shopping (on page 114). 

You can generate an account number for a vendor if the vendor that you want to use is 

excluded from the location restrictions. To generate the account number, the vendor must 

be listed in the Entity record on the Spend Management tab of the excluded location.

### Vendor Record Approval Process
*Source: `RP Accounting AP Daily Tasks User Guide.pdf`, Page 136*

Vendors (Suppliers) 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Daily Tasks User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Vendor Record Approval Process 

This section describes how to participate in the vendor record approval process. 

1. 
A user (“the requester”) creates a new vendor record (on page 70). 

2. 
The system checks the vendor record approval policy to see if it requires approval for new 

and updated vendor records.  

• 
If it does, the system adds the vendor record to the approval queue.  

• 
If it does not, the system adds the vendor record to the Vendors list, and this is the 

end of the process. 

The user who adds or edits the vendor record cannot be the person who approves the 
vendor request. If no one else has permission to approve vendors, then an administrator 
will need to assign that permission (on page 120 ) to at least one other user. Otherwise, 
the vendor request will be stuck in the approval queue. 

3. 
The requester can view the status of the vendor record he created or updated (the “vendor 

request”) using the View vendor requests (on page 585) option. 

4. 
The system notifies approvers that a record is pending approval. 

5. 
Approvers can click a link in the email notification (on page 588) to open the system to 

where the vendor record is waiting for approval. 

6. 
The approver reviews the vendor record in the Approve vendors list (on page 586). 

7. 
The approver approves or declines the vendor record (on page 586). 

• 
If approved, the system moves approved vendor records to the vendors list.  

• 
If declined, the system deactivates declined vendor records.  

8. 
The requester checks with the approver to find out why the vendor was declined and then 

resolves the problem. 

---


<!-- Page 137 -->
Chapter 3: Vendors (Suppliers) 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Daily Tasks User Guide 

9. 
The requester recreates the vendor record, and the approval process begins from step 1.  

---



#### Configuring Permissions for Vendor Approvers
*Source: `RP Accounting AP Daily Tasks User Guide.pdf`, Page 138*

Configuring Permissions for Vendor Approvers 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > Setup > Roles > Subscriptions`


As a best practice, create a new role for each level of vendor approver and then assign the role to 

the appropriate users. 

Make sure each role is assigned to more than one user. Approvers cannot approve their own 
vendor requests, so if an approver adds or edits a vendor and they are the only person with 
permission to approve that vendor, the vendor request will get stuck in the approval queue. 

Creating Vendor Approver Roles 

To create a vendor approver role: 

1. 
Open the Company menu, and then select the Setup tab. 

2. 
Click Roles and then click the Add button. 

3. 
In Name, type an appropriate name to reflect the purpose of the role, such as Vendor 

approvers 1. 

If you name all vendor approver roles consistently, it will pay off when you assign the roles 
later. 

4. 
In the Description, describe the purpose of level one approvers: First level approves all 

vendors and then click the Save button.  

The Vendor approvers 1 - Roles subscriptions page is displayed.  

5. 
Select Accounts payable, and then click the Permissions link. 

6. 
Click 
 Expand to expand the permissions box. 

7. 
Find Approve vendors, and then select the List check box and the Level1 check box. 

8. 
Click the Save button. 

9. 
Repeat the process by creating new roles for Level2 and Level3 vendor approvals. 

We recommend setting up approval levels separately because the system sends one email 
for each level of approval. If you assign multiple levels to a single user or role, the approver 
will receive multiple emails for each vendor record in the approval workflow.

In the Require approvers drop-down list, select the levels of approval that the vendor must 

go through (1-4).

Click Save.

vendor records. 

2. 
In the Vendor type drop-down list, select the type of vendor that should always go through 

approval. 

3. 
In the Require approvers drop-down list, select the levels of approval that the vendor must 

go through (1-4).

Click Save.

Searching for a Storefront Supplier Code 

A Storefront Supplier Code is associated with each vendor in the Storefront. The system offers 

two methods for finding the vendor’s code. 

Use the search-ahead feature: 

• 
Type the first few letters of a vendor’s name to have the system search ahead to find the 

vendor’s Storefront supplier code.  

Using the Find option: 

1. 
Click Find in the Storefront Supplier Code drop-down list to have the system display a list 

of the suppliers that are already in the Storefront list of vendors. 

The Select Storefront Suppliers list includes Supplier Name, Supplier Code, Tax ID, and 

Address to help you find a supplier code for the desired vendor. These details can help you 

spot the same vendor listed in multiple locations. 

2. 
Select the vendor in the Storefront Supplier Code drop-down to link the supplier from RPA 

to the merchant. 

After you select the supplier code, the system links the vendor record to a supplier code. 
The customer must request account numbers for each vendor location for the property. For 
example, the system assigns: 
- One account number for the vendor Real Supplier located in Cooper Station. 
- One account number for the vendor Real Supplier located in Cassidy South. 

Learn about Requesting a Vendor Account for a Property for Online Shopping (on page 114).

Using Wildcards 

Use the % character as a wildcard to match zero or more characters in text columns. 

Examples: 

bank% will display all vendors that have “bank” at the beginning of the name, like Bank of 

Metropolis. 

%bank or %bank% will display all vendors that have “bank” anywhere in the name, like Bank 

of Metropolis, Metropolis Bank, and MetroBank. 

%bank will display all vendors that end with the word “bank,” like Metropolis Bank. 

Filter Example 

To find an office property with an ID that begins with the letter M, break the search into two 

conditions. 

1. 
Enter the first search condition: Find all property IDs that begin with the letter M. 

• 
Select the Property name column for the first search condition. 

• 
Select the Starts with operator. 

• 
Type the letter “M” in the third field. 

2. 
Enter the second search condition: Find all office properties. 

• 
Select the Property type column for the second search condition. 

• 
Select the Equals operator. 

• 
Type the word “Office” in the third field. 

When you apply the filter, the system displays a list of all items that meet both criteria.

Filtering for Recent Records 

The system provides a set of standard views for quickly displaying list items that you recently 

modified or viewed.

modified, or All recently modified. The system displays only those records that you’ve

records.

Vendor (Supplier) Information Page 

See the How to Get Here (on page 64) topic for a list of ways to access the Vendors (Suppliers) 

list. 

Use this page to add and edit vendor records. A vendor record has six tabs: 

• 
Vendor (Supplier): This tab has two sections, the Summary section, and the Primary contact 

section. Use the Summary section to determine how the vendor is handled in the system, 

and the Primary contact section to record all of the contact details for the primary contact of 

the vendor. 

• 
Additional information: This tab has five sections: Vendor details, Billing details, Email 

template options, Vendor merge, and CA DE 542. Use this tab to record details about the 

vendor and billing, select email templates to associate with a transaction type, view details 

about vendor merges, and indicate when a California form DE 542 is required and note the 

date the form was sent. 

• 
Contact list: This tab has two sections, Pay to/Return to and Contact list. Use this tab to 

define the contact to whom to direct payments and to list all contacts associated with this 

vendor. 

• 
Payment information: This tab has three sections: Payment details, Payment services, and 

Vendor account number. Use this tab to define how and when to pay this vendor. 

• 
Restrictions: This tab has one section. Use this tab to restrict access to this vendor. This tab 

appears only when your system has multiple entities. 

• 
Insurance/License: This tab has three sections for three insurance policies and licenses. Use 

this tab to maintain details about insurance and licenses that cover this vendor.

information page opens. See field-by-field descriptions (on page 140).

Vendor Information Page 

Fields 

ID 
The system provides two mutually exclusive ways to add vendor IDs. You 

can type your own unique ID, or you can have the system automatically 

add them from a present numbering scheme. Set up automatic 

numbering for vendors, 

This ID can’t be overwritten after the vendor is created. 

Best practices for creating identifiers 

An ID enables your company to keep track of a specific type of 

information, such as G/L account, department, location, transaction, 

vendor, and customer. You can create IDs by adding them on the fly or 

by having the system automatically add them from a preset numbering 

scheme. 

Whichever method you choose, we recommend against using leading 

zeros as part of an ID. IDs with leading zeros can cause errors when you 

import information into your company from Excel because Excel 

removes the leading zeros. 

Best practice: Use a character as a prefix to your ID; for example, C0001 

for a customer ID. 

Workaround: If you must use leading zeros in IDs, then convert the 

column of ID numbers to text format in Excel before importing the file 

content. Excel won’t remove the leading zeros when you save the file. 

Remember to do this every time you use a template to import 

information that requires IDs. 

Name 
The name of the vendor as it will appear on lists and menus across your 

company.

box)

don’t want to include in your standard vendor lists.
