### 1099 Vendor Information
*Source: `RP Accounting AP Daily Tasks User Guide.pdf`, Page 175*

Chapter 3: Vendors (Suppliers) 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Daily Tasks User Guide 

1099 Vendor Information 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > All > Vendors > Edit > Additional Information > 
Form1099`


This section describes how to set up vendors for 1099 and have the system track 1099 totals. 

You can tag any vendor as a 1099 vendor and have the system track 1099 totals for printing on 

your 1099 form. In addition, if you are setting up this vendor mid-year, or for prior years, you can 

enter historical YTD amounts.  

After you tag a vendor with 1099 status, each transaction that you create against that vendor 

displays the selected 1099 form type and 1099 box per line item. You can configure Accounts 

Payable so you can override the form type and box at the line level of the transaction as needed. 

---



### Guide to Vendor 1099s
*Source: `RP Accounting AP Daily Tasks User Guide.pdf`, Page 176*

Vendors (Suppliers) 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Daily Tasks User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Guide to Vendor 1099s 

RealPage Accounting automates the process of generating and printing 1099s based on your 

vendor and transaction setup. You connect vendors to bills, generate a report to verify the results, 

and then print your forms. 

This topic contains an overview of the steps involved in the 1099 process. 

1099 Process Overview 

This is the basic workflow for working with 1099 vendor and transaction records: 

Configuring Accounts Payable to Tag Transactions as 1099 Eligible 

Depending on your requirements and processes, you can configure two options for 1099 

transaction tagging in your company: 

• 
Enable 1099 flag override for line items: Users can include or exclude specific transaction 

line-item totals in any 1099 calculations. The system automatically includes or excludes the 

line-item totals at 1099 generation time. When the vendor is set as a 1099 vendor and 

---


<!-- Page 177 -->
Chapter 3: Vendors (Suppliers) 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Daily Tasks User Guide 

transactions are created, the system automatically marks that transaction as 1099. Enabling 

this option provides the ability to remove the 1099 flag on the transaction. 

For vendors not set as 1099, when transactions are created, the system does not mark the 

transactions as 1099.  

• 
Enable 1099 form and box override: Users can select the 1099 form or box for use at the 

line-item level of transactions. The system automatically allocates those line-item amounts 

to the selected form and box at 1099 generation time. 

Learn more about 1099 configuration overrides. 

Setting up vendors for 1099 tracking 

You can tag any vendor as a 1099 vendor and have the system track 1099 totals for printing on 

your 1099 form. In addition, if you are setting up a vendor mid-year, or for prior years, you can 

enter historical YTD amounts. After you tag a vendor with 1099 status, each transaction that you 

create against that vendor displays the selected 1099 form type and 1099 box per line item. Learn 

more about setting up vendors for 1099s (on page 163). 

If you need to remove a vendor’s 1099 status, you can learn how to do that here (on page 200 ). 

If you accidentally created two duplicate vendors and both have 1099 information tied to their 

records, you can inactivate one vendor and add any 1099 transaction amounts to the open 

balance of your target vendor. Learn how to inactivate a vendor (on page 129). Alternatively, you 

may want to merge vendor records. See Merging Duplicate Vendors (on page 236). 

Tagging Transactions for 1099 Tracking 

The system generates 1099 information for vendor invoices that are tagged as 1099-eligible, were 

paid in the same year covered by the 1099, and exceed a prescribed vendor payment amount. 

To tag transactions as 1099 eligible: 

1. 
Open the Accounts Payable menu. 

2. 
Click A/P invoices. 

3. 
Edit each transaction that should be included in the 1099 coverages. 

4. 
Review the Form 1099 check box, and select it’s not selected. 

5. 
Make sure that the payment date occurs in the same year that you selected for 1099 

coverage. 

6. 
Confirm that the total amount paid to the vendor requires a 1099 form. 

For certain types of 1099
-MISC payments, amounts below a certain threshold don’t 
require a printed 1099 form. When determining whether to print a 1099 form, RealPage 
Accounting follows the latest government guidelines. 

---


<!-- Page 178 -->
Vendors (Suppliers) 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Daily Tasks User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Ordering 1099 Forms 

The tax forms you’ll find on the Forms for RealPage page are perfectly aligned for printing and 

the only ones that we support. 

Tax forms are updated each year. Be sure to purchase the latest forms for the upcoming tax 

season. 

To order 1099 forms, visit https://www.specialtychecksandforms.com/ 

https://www.specialtychecksandforms.com/ 

You also can find a link to this vendor from the Home page. Click the Checks & supplies link in 

the Resources box. 

Running the 1099 Report 

Run the 1099 report to preview your 1099 information before you print the forms. Using the 1099 

report, you can uncover any 1099 issues you may need to correct before you print. 

Generate the 1099 report to: 

• 
Verify that you set up your vendors or employees with the correct 1099 form. 

• 
Review the amounts paid to 1099 vendors or employees for a specific year. 

The 1099 report includes only payments classified as 1099 income paid to vendors or employees. 

You can create the report to include either all 1099 categories or a specific 1099 category. You 

can sort the results by vendor or employee name or by 1099 category. 

Prepare for Accurate 1099 Report Generation 

Before generating your 1099 report, we recommend that you create a custom 1099 vendor or 

employee list to be sure that you haven’t left an eligible vendor or employee out or tagged one as 

eligible who shouldn’t be. 

Solving 1099 Reporting Issues 

After you generate your 1099 report, if you discover issues with your transactions, you can 

reclassify any transactions that are incorrect (some transactions can’t be reclassified, such as in 

Global Consolidation), or you can import transactions to mass update them. See Reclassifying an 

Invoice (on page 416). 

You can also change the status of a vendor from ineligible to eligible, and vice versa, and then 

have the system automatically update all of the associated transactions. 

As you review the report, if you discover other issues, such as missing information or incorrect 

totals, check out these Troubleshooting Vendor 1099s (on page 189). 

---


<!-- Page 179 -->
Chapter 3: Vendors (Suppliers) 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Daily Tasks User Guide 

Printing Your 1099s and 1096s 

When you are confident that your 1099 report is accurate, you’re ready to print your 1099 forms, 

and print your 1096 cover form, both of which you submit to the government. For more 

information, see: 

• 
Printing 1099 forms 

• 
Printing 1096 forms 

About Form 1096 

Form 1096 is the cover sheet for the 1099 forms submitted by your company. Use one 1096 for all 

1099s you submit that are of a specific type. For example, if you file ten 1099-MISC forms, you fill 

out just one 1096 form as the cover sheet for those ten forms. If you also plan to submit a group 

of 1099-DIV forms, you must print another 1096 to submit with those forms. 

Find tips on printer alignment: 

• 
Printer alignment form 1099 

• 
Form 1096 

Filing Your 1099s 

You can export your 1099 file in CSV, Excel, XML, or XSD file format. 

If you are filing 1099s for more than 250 records, tax law requires you to use 1099 Electronic 

Filing. 

---



#### 1099 Information for the Vendor
*Source: `RP Accounting AP Daily Tasks User Guide.pdf`, Page 180*

Vendors (Suppliers) 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Daily Tasks User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

1099 Information for the Vendor 

Form Name 

Choose a form from the Form 1099 drop-down list. After you select the form, the area below is 

populated with line items and initial entry fields applicable to that form. When a vendor is defined 

as receiving 1099s, a Form 1099 section is added to the A/P invoice page so you can allocate 

amounts to different 1099 accounts. 

Keep the None default if you do not want the vendor to receive a 1099. 

Default 1099 Box 

Unless you make a more specific choice when you pay vendor A/P invoices, the default here is the 

category to which payments are otherwise assigned. The content of the Default 1099 Box field 

changes to the appropriate selections, based on the choice you make in the Form 1099 field. 

Entity 

This field is displayed only for users in a top-level multi-entity company that has selected Issue a 

separate 1099 per entity in the Configure multi entity page so you can select the appropriate 

entity for entering initial YTD amounts. 

Initial Values for Years 

If you are setting up your books with a start date after January 1st, you probably need to set up 

starting YTD balances for each 1099 eligible vendor. You may also want to enter values for prior 

years. You obtain these balances from your old accounting system. 

• 
If you want to enter YTD balances for this year, accept the default date of this year found in 

the Initial Values for Year drop-down list. 

• 
If you want to enter values for a prior year, select one of the prior years available in the 

drop-down list. Then, enter the starting YTD balances in the blank fields. 

Future amounts you pay the vendor are added to the amounts, if any, you enter here. 

Remember to only enter the calendar year-to-date 1099 balance for each vendor (which can be 
different from the entire amount paid to that vendor year to date). In addition, if your company 
is on a fiscal year that does not correspond with the calendar year, you need to back out 
payments made to that vendor during the prior calendar year. 

For multi-entity shared companies, the process varies depending on whether Issue a separate 

1099 per entity option is selected or not. When Issue a separate 1099 per entity check box is 

selected, initial YTD amounts are entered at the top level or entity level for the entity. In this 

mode, vendors in subordinate entities are assigned entity-specific initial amounts, even if they use 

the same vendor. If not selected, initial amounts for all vendors and all entities are entered at the 

top-level entity. 

---

#### Entering Historical YTD Amounts
*Source: `RP Accounting AP Daily Tasks User Guide.pdf`, Page 203*

Chapter 3: Vendors (Suppliers) 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Daily Tasks User Guide 

Entering Historical YTD Amounts 

Historical YTD amounts are the amounts you had before you started tracking in this system. If 

you’re setting up your books with a start date after January 1st, you probably need to set up 

starting YTD balances for each 1099 eligible vendor. You may also want to enter values for prior 

years. You obtain these balances from your old accounting system. The vendor total amount is 

the historical amount added to the transactions flagged in the system as 1099 eligible. 

To enter historical YTD amounts: 

1. 
Open the Accounts payable menu. 

2. 
Select the Vendors option. 

3. 
Click the Edit link next to the desired vendor. 

4. 
In the Vendor information page, go to the Additional information tab. 

5. 
Click the Form 1099 link. The Form 1099 Information with default box page appears. 

6. 
In Initial Values for Year, select the year you want to enter information for. 

7. 
Enter the beginning balance or any adjustment you need to make, then click Save. 

8. 
When you return to the Vendor information page, click Save. 

Future amounts you pay the vendor are added to the amounts, if any, you enter here. 

Only enter the calendar year-to-date 1099 balance for each vendor (which can be different from 
the entire amount paid to that vendor year to date). If your company is on a fiscal year that does 
not correspond with the calendar year, you need to back out payments made to that vendor 
during the prior calendar year. 

For multi-entity shared companies: This process varies depending on whether the Issue a 
separate 1099 per entity option is selected or not. If the option is selected, initial YTD 
amounts are entered at the top level or entity level for the entity. In this mode, vendors in 
subordinate entities are assigned entity -specific initial amounts, even if they use the same 
vendor. If not selected, initial amounts for all vendors and all entities are entered at the top-level 
entity. 

If you need to update historical YTD information for multiple vendors, you can import your 
changes as a CSV.

Entering Information for Other Form 1099 Boxes 

After you set up a vendor as 1099 eligible and then make payments to that vendor, the system 

keeps track of that information and automatically prints it on 1099 forms. However, some 

information required for a 1099 form may not be available in the system. For example, say you 

chose the Miscellaneous Income (Form 1099-MISC) form in the Form name drop-down list. If you 

examine an actual 1099-MISC form, you will notice that box 9 contains information that is not 

available in the system. 

Consequently, blank fields are provided for you to enter this information. If you had selected this 

form in the drop-down list, you could add an “X” in Box 9 (if applicable). 

Assign Line Items on an A/P Invoice to a Different 1099 Form 

You can assign each line of an A/P invoice to a different 1099 form and box. The form and box 

you select overrides the setting you made in the vendor record as well as the default box in that 

payment process. 

To assign line items on an A/P invoice to a different 1099 form: 

• 
Select the Enable 1099 flag override check box in the Configure accounts payable page in 

the 1099’s section. This setting allows you to include or exclude specific transaction 

line-item totals in any 1099 calculations. The system automatically includes or excludes the 

line-item totals at 1099 generation time. 

• 
Select the Enable 1099 form and box override in the Configure accounts payable page in 

the 1099’s section. Users can select the 1099 form or box for use at the line-item level of 

transactions. The system automatically allocates those line-item amounts to the selected 

form and box at 1099 generation time. 

To override the 1099 form on a line item: 

1. 
In the appropriate A/P invoice, click the line item, then click Show details. The line-item 

details area appears. 

2. 
In Form 1099 type, select the appropriate form from the drop-down list.

#### Setting Up 1099 Reporting for Duplicate Vendor Records
*Source: `RP Accounting AP Daily Tasks User Guide.pdf`, Page 206*

Vendors (Suppliers) 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Daily Tasks User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Setting Up 1099 Reporting for Duplicate Vendor Records 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > Setup > Subscriptions > Multi Entity Console > Configure > 
Validate and Issue 1099 by Tax ID and Legal Contact Information`


In a multi-entity system, sometimes two vendor records are needed for business purposes. 

Because the vendor records have the same tax ID, it causes problems when it is time to report 

1099 taxes. When reporting 1099 taxes, the two records 1099 amounts must be combined and 

reported as one vendor, and then the system needs to determine which address and 1099 name 

to use on the 1099 form.  

To set up the system to multiple vendor records at tax reporting time: 

1. 
Open the Company menu, and then select the Setup tab. 

2. 
Click Subscriptions. 

3. 
In the Multi Entity Console row, click Configure. 

4. 
In the 1099 section, select the Validate and issue 1099 by Tax ID and Legal Contact 

Information check box to have the system check for duplicate vendor tax IDs. When it finds 

duplicates, the system combines the 1099 amounts for the two vendor records. 

5. 
Click Save. 

6. 
Open the Accounts Payable menu, and then select Vendors. 

7. 
Determine which vendor record has the address and 1099 name that you want to use on the 

1099 form, and then open the vendor record with the Edit link. 

When the Validate and issue 1099 by Tax ID and Legal Contact Information check box is 
enabled in the Multi Entity configuration section, the Preferred 1099 vendor check box 
appears on Vendor records. 

8. 
Select the Preferred 1099 check box to mark the vendor record. 

9. 
Click Save.

#### Troubleshooting Vendor 1099s
*Source: `RP Accounting AP Daily Tasks User Guide.pdf`, Page 207*

Chapter 3: Vendors (Suppliers) 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Daily Tasks User Guide 

Troubleshooting Vendor 1099s 

If some crucial information is missing from your 1099, such as a vendor or A/P invoices, 

oftentimes, the cause can be tracked to one of the following:  

• 
The vendor isn’t set up as 1099 eligible 

• 
The vendor A/P invoices aren’t flagged for 1099 treatment 

• 
The 1099 total payment amount to the vendor is in a different year or the amount is under 

the threshold for required reporting. 

The following troubleshooting instructions can help you discover and resolve the causes of 

missing information on your 1099s. 

Ensure that the Vendor Is Set Up as 1099 Eligible 

The system can only generate and print 1099 forms for vendors who’ve been set up as eligible for 

1099s. 

To check vendor 1099 eligibility: 

1. 
Open the Accounts payable menu. 

2. 
Select Vendors. 

3. 
Click Edit beside the required vendor. 

4. 
In the Additional Information tab, is the required 1099 form listed beside the Form 1099 

link? 

If so, this is an indicator that the vendor is at least partly set up for 1099 eligibility. 

If not, the vendor isn’t eligible, and you can now resolve the issue by making the vendor 

eligible. 

5. 
Click the Form 1099 link. 

6. 
In the Form 1099 information page, makes sure the following fields have values: 

• 
Form Name: The 1099 form that you want to send to the vendor. This is the form 

name that appears on the Additional Information tab after you save. 

• 
Default 1099 Box: The form box where the vendor payments should be tracked. 

• 
Initial Values for Year: The year that you want the 1099 to cover. 

7. 
If you want historical values included in the vendor payment total, make sure they are 

added. 

8. 
After you save, the Additional information tab lists the selected 1099 form beside the Form 

1099 link. 

For detailed information on adding 1099 status to a vendor (on page 198) or removing a vendor’s 

1099 status. 

---


<!-- Page 208 -->
Vendors (Suppliers) 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Daily Tasks User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Are the vendor A/P invoices correctly set up for the 1099? 

The system generates 1099 information for vendor A/P invoices that are flagged for 1099 

treatment, were paid in the same year covered by the 1099, and exceed a prescribed vendor 

payment amount. 

To review your A/P invoices for 1099 setup: 

1. 
Open the Accounts payable menu. 

2. 
Select A/P invoices. 

3. 
Click Edit for each A/P invoice that should be included in 1099 coverage. 

• 
Determine if the 1099 check box is selected. If not, select it. 

• 
Make sure that the A/P invoice payment date occurs in the same year that you 

selected for 1099 coverage. 

• 
Confirm that the total amount paid to the vendor requires a 1099 form. 

• 
For certain types of 1099-MISC payments, amounts below a certain threshold don’t 

require a printed 1099 form. When determining whether to print a 1099 form, 

RealPage Accounting follows the latest government guidelines. 

Can I generate a 1099 form for a vendor that does not meet the $600 threshold? 

Because the IRS mandates the $600 threshold, the system does not allow 1099 forms to generate 

if the vendor was entitled to less than $600 in payments. The user must manually create a 1099 

form for the vendor for lesser amounts.

Vendors That Do Not Appear on 1099 Report 

When vendors do not appear on the 1099 report, you can update vendor records in bulk using 

the Vendor 1099 Transaction Update template. 

Downloading the Vendor Template 

1. 
Open the Company menu, and then select the Setup tab. 

2. 
Select Import data. 

3. 
Find Vendor 1099 transaction update and then click Template. The system downloads the 

file. 

4. 
Open the file in Excel. 

5. 
Fill in the spreadsheet with Vendor ID and Vendor Name for all vendors that need to be 

updated.  

The Vendor ID and Vendor Name must mirror the formatting used for the vendors, 
including capitalization, spaces, and use of special characters. 

6. 
Fill in the Vendor Transaction Update Template with the vendors that need to be updated to 

receive and/or not receive a 1099. 

7. 
In NAME1099, fill in the name of the appropriate 1099 form. 

8. 
In DEFAULT1099TYPE, enter a value if you want to change the default form type for vendor 

and form type for the specified transactions.  

9. 
In DEFAULT1099BOX: 

• 
Changes default box for vendor and box for the specified transactions.  

• 
This field is updated if a value is present.  

• 
If the field is blank, the system leaves the existing value in the system.  

• 
To remove the existing value, enter the value NULL. 

10. 
In UPDATETRANS, enter Y to mark the vendors’ transactions as 1099 taxable based on date 

range and Form 1099 type and box. 

11. 
In FROMDATE, enter the starting date of the date range for transactions to be updated. Use 

the format MM/DD/YYYY. 

12. 
In TODATE, enter the ending date of the date range. 

13. 
Save the template as a CSV (Comma delimited) file.

Type the 1099 name, as needed.

*Source: `RP Accounting AP Daily Tasks User Guide.pdf`, Page 211*

Correcting a Mistake on a 1099 Form 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > All > Reports > Vendor Reports > 1099/1096 > 
1099 Electronic Filing`


You can create a correction file for 1099 electronic filings. There are two types of correction files 

that you can submit to the IRS. You can only submit one type of correction at a time.  

• 
The first type of correction file corresponds to the first two check boxes. For these 

corrections, the IRS allows you to send just the corrected information. When you submit 

these corrections, the system generates the correction file with the corrected amount(s).  

• 
The second type of correction requires that you send the originally reported data. This type 

of correction corresponds to the last three check boxes. When you submit these corrections, 

the system generates the correction file with the originally reported data and the updated 

data. 

To create a correction file: 

1. 
Open the Accounts Payable menu. 

2. 
In the Reports column of the menu, in the Vendor reports section, click 1099/1096, and then 

select the 1099 Electronic filing option. 

3. 
In the Year ending drop-down list, select the filing year that you want to correct. 

4. 
In the From vendor drop-down list, select the vendor that needs a correction. 

5. 
Select the Correction file check box. 

Submitting Simple Corrections 

1. 
Select the check boxes of either or both of the first two issues that you want to correct: 

• 
Incorrect amount was reported for a vendor 

• 
Amount was reported in the incorrect box 

When you select either of the first two check boxes, the last three options become 
unavailable because you can only submit one correction file type at a time. 

2. 
Skip to the Filling In the Format section.

Removing a Vendor’s 1099 Status 

Best Practice: Before you actually add or remove the 1099 status for a vendor and update the 

associated transactions, it’s a good idea to run a 1099 report to get an idea of just how many 

transactions will be affected. After you add or remove the 1099 status, you can then run the 

report again to verify that the change has taken place. After you remove the 1099 status from a 

vendor, the system offers you the option of updating the 1099 status for line items in A/P invoices 

linked to that vendor. 

Running a Report to View Affected A/P Invoices 

1. 
Open the Accounts payable menu. 

2. 
In the Reports section, pause on 1099/1096, and select 1099 reports. The 1099 reports 

parameters page opens. 

3. 
In From vendor, select or type the vendor. 

4. 
Click the 1099 form type Select button, and then select the relevant form type.  

5. 
In Summary/Detail, select Detail. 

6. 
In Entity/Entity group, select an entity. 

7. 
Click View. The report appears with a list of transactions for the selected vendor. 

Notice that the report displays the Tax ID and the 1099 Category for the vendor 
transactions. More on running a 1099 report . 

Removing a Vendor’s 1099 Status 

To edit the vendor information to remove the 1099 status: 

1. 
On the Accounts Payable menu, select Vendors. 

2. 
Click Edit beside the relevant vendor. 

3. 
In the Additional Information tab, click the Form 1099 link. The Form 1099 Information 

with Default Box page appears. 

---


<!-- Page 219 -->
Chapter 3: Vendors (Suppliers) 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Daily Tasks User Guide 

4. 
Set Form Name to None. 

If you don’t clear the Form Name field, and then save, the form won’t be cleared and will 
reappear the next time you click the Form 1099 link. 

5. 
Save the Form 1099 Information with Default Box page, then save the Vendor Information 

page. 

6. 
In the message box, select Yes to automatically update the line items in A/P invoices and 

adjustments for the vendor for the current and prior year based on your 1099 changes, or 

select No to leave as is. 

7. 
Click the Save button. 

The system offers you the option of updating the 1099 status of line items in A/P invoices 
linked to that vendor. 

Removing the 1099 Status from Multiple Vendors 

If you have multiple vendors with transactions that require a status change, you can generate a 

1099 report for those vendors, export the resulting transactions, change the status, then import 

them again using the Vendor 1099 Transaction Update template. Go to Company > All > Import 

data to access the template. 

1. 
Generate a 1099 report of vendors.  

2. 
Export the resulting list of vendors. 

3. 
In the exported file, change the status of the vendors from which to remove the 1099 status. 

4. 
Save the file in CSV format.  

5. 
From the Company menu, select the Setup tab. 

6. 
Select Import Data and find the Vendor 1099 Transaction Update row located under the 

Set Up A/P Master List, Open Invoices and Adjustments section. 

7. 
Select Import.

Form 1099 Information Page 

Use the Form 1099 information page to add the following 1099 information to a vendor record: 

• 
Form Name (and 1099 line items) 

To define this vendor as being eligible for a 1099 at the end of the year, choose a form from 

the Form 1099 drop-down list. After you select the form, the area below is populated with 

line items and initial entry fields appropriate for that form. When a vendor is defined as 

receiving 1099s, a Form 1099 section is added to the A/P invoice page so you can allocate 

amounts to different 1099 accounts. 

Keep the None default if you do not want the vendor to receive a 1099. 

 Learn how to remove a vendor’s 1099 status (on page 200).  

• 
Default 1099 Box 

Unless you make a more specific choice when you pay vendor A/P invoices, the default here 

is the category to which payments are otherwise assigned. The content of the Default 1099 

Box field changes to the appropriate selections, based on the choice you make in the Form 

1099 field. 

• 
Entity 

This field appears only for users in a top-level multi-entity company that has selected Issue a 

separate 1099 per entity in the Configure Multi Entity page so you can select the 

appropriate entity for entering initial YTD amounts. 

• 
Initial Values for Year 

Choose the year for which you are entering YTD amounts. 

If you are setting up your books with a start date after January 1st, you probably need to set up 

starting YTD balances for each 1099 eligible vendor. You may also want to enter values for prior 

years. You obtain these balances from your old accounting system. 

• 
If you want to enter YTD balances for this year, accept the default date of this year found in 

the Initial values for year drop-down list. 

• 
If you want to enter values for a prior year, select one of the prior years available in the 

drop-down list. Then, enter the starting YTD balances in the blank fields. 

• 
Enter any amounts that you plan to pay the vendor in the future, if any. 

Remember to enter only the calendar year-to-date 1099 balance for each vendor (which can be 
different from the entire amount paid to that vendor year to date). In addition, if your company 
is on a fiscal year that does not correspond with the calendar year, you need to back out 
payments made to that vendor during the prior calendar year.

Section 897 gain: If a RIC described in section 897(h)(4) (A)(ii) or a REIT disposes of a USRPI at

Dividend Income (Form 1099-DIV) 

Before You Begin 

This form has changed for 2024. If you have vendors or transactions assigned to the DIV form box 

1a, you must update vendor records. You can update the records manually or use the import 

feature in Company > Import Data menu option to update vendor and transaction records.  

If you choose to use the Import Data option, use the following import templates: 

• 
Vendor: Use this template to update vendor information, including the 1099 form type and 

box. 

• 
Vendor 1099 Transaction Update: Use this template to update transactions with vendors 

that have transactions assigned to the DIV for box.  

• 
Vendor 1099 Opening Balance: Use this template to import 1099 importing balances for 

vendors that have transactions assigned to the DIV for box. (This import is optional.) 

Filling In the Dividend Income Form 

1. 
Choose Dividend Income (Form 1099-DIV). 

When you choose Dividend income from the Form name box, the Default 1099 box 

drop-down list includes these options: 

• 
1a - Total ordinary dividends 

• 
1b - Qualified dividends  

• 
2a - Total capital gain distribution 

• 
2b - Unrecap, sec. 1250 gain  

• 
2c - Section 1202 gain  

• 
2d - Collectibles (28%) gain 

• 
2e - Section 897 ordinary dividends 

• 
2f - Section 897 capital gain 

• 
3 - Non-dividend distributions 

• 
4 - Federal income tax withheld 

• 
5 - Investment expenses 

• 
6 - Foreign tax paid 

• 
8 - Cash liquidation distributions 

• 
9 - Non-cash liquidation distributions 

• 
10 - Exempt-interest dividends 

• 
11 - Specified private activity bond interest dividends 

• 
14 - State tax withheld

The system sums the amounts in boxes 1b, 2e, and 6 and adds the amount to box 1a.  

2. 
In Default 1099 box, select the desired default 1099 box. 

3. 
In Entity, select the entity that is to generate the 1099 form. 

4. 
In Initial values for year, select a year to associate the values with a tax year.  

5. 
In 1a - Total Ordinary dividends, enter the amount of total ordinary dividends, including 

those from money market funds and net short-term capital gains from mutual funds, and 

other distributions on stock. Include reinvested dividends and section 404(k) dividends.  

6. 
In 1b - Qualified dividends, enter the amount of dividends taxed at a lower rate than 

ordinary dividends. 

7. 
In 2a - Total capital gain distribution, enter the amount of total capital gain distributions 

(long-term). This includes all amounts shown in boxes 2b, 2c, and 2d. 

8. 
In 2b - Unrecap, sec. 1250 gain: Enter any amount included in box 2a that is 28% rate gain. 

9. 
In 2c - Section 1202 gain, enter any amount included in box 2a that is unrecaptured section 

1250 gain from certain depreciable real property. 

10. 
In 2d - Collectibles (28%) gain, enter any amount included in box 2a that is section 1202 

gain from certain qualified small business stock.  

11. 
In 2e - Section 897 ordinary dividends, enter any amount included in box 1a that is section 

897 gain from dispositions of USRPI 

12. 
In 2f - Section 897 capital gain, enter any amount included in box 2a that is section 897 

gain from dispositions of USRPI. 

Only RICs and REITs should complete boxes 2e and 2f. Boxes 2e and 2f do not need to be 
completed for recipients that are US individuals. 

13. 
In 3 - Non-dividend distributions, enter the amount of nontaxable distributions, if 

determinable.  

File Form 5452, Corporate Report of Non -dividend Distributions, if you pay non-taxable 
distributions to shareholders. 

14. 
In 4 - Federal income tax withheld, enter any backup withholding. For example, persons 

who have not furnished their TIN to you in the manner required are subject to withholding 

at a 31% rate on certain dividend payments reported on this form. 

15. 
In 5 - Investment expenses, select when you have the stockholder’s pro rata share of certain 

amounts deductible by a non-publicly offered regulated investment company in computing 

its taxable income. You can include this amount in the stockholder’s gross income under 

section 67(c); it must also be included in box 1.

• 
1 - Rents 

•

• 
3 - Other income 

• 
4 - Federal income tax withheld 

• 
5 - Fishing boat proceeds 

•

•

(recipient) for resale 

•

• 
9 - Crop insurance proceeds 

• 
10 - Gross proceeds paid to an attorney  

• 
11 - Fish purchased for resale 

•

•

• 
15 - Nonqualified deferred compensation 

• 
16 - State tax withheld  

• 
17 - State/Payer’s state number 

• 
18 - State income 

2. 
Select the desired Default 1099 box. 

3. 
In Entity, select the entity that is to generate the 1099 form. 

4. 
In Initial values for year, select a year to associate the values with a tax year.  

5. 
In 1 - Rents, enter amounts of $600 or more for all types of rents. 

6. 
In 2 - Royalties, enter gross royalty payments (or similar amounts) of $10 or more. Report 

royalties from oil, gas, or other mineral properties before reduction for severance and other 

taxes that may have been withheld and paid.  

7. 
In 3 - Other income, enter other income of $600 or more required to be reported on Form 

1099-MISC that is not reportable in one of the other boxes on the form. 

---


<!-- Page 230 -->
Vendors (Suppliers) 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Daily Tasks User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Also enter in box 3 prizes and awards that are not for services performed. Include the fair 

market value (FMV) of merchandise won on game shows. Also include amounts paid to a 

winner of a sweepstakes not involving a wager. 

8. 
In 4 - Federal income tax withheld, enter backup withholding. For example, persons who 

have not furnished their TINs to you are subject to withholding on payments required to be 

reported in boxes 1, 2 (net of severance taxes), 3, 5 (to the extent paid in cash), 6, 7 (except 

fish purchases for cash), 8, 10, and 14. For more information on backup withholding, 

including the rate, see part N in the 2019 General Instructions for Certain Information 

Returns. 

Also enter any income tax withheld from payments to members of Indian tribes from the 

net revenues of class II or class III gaming activities conducted or licensed by the tribes. 

9. 
In 5 - Fishing boat proceeds, enter the individual’s share of all proceeds from the sale of a 

catch or the FMV of a distribution in kind to each crew member of fishing boats with 

normally fewer than 10 crew members. A fishing boat has normally fewer than 10 crew 

members if the average size of the operating crew was fewer than 10 on trips during the 

preceding 4 calendar quarters. 

In addition, report cash payments of up to $100 per trip that are contingent on a minimum 

catch and are paid solely for additional duties (such as mate, engineer, or cook) for which 

additional cash payments are traditional in the industry. However, do not report on Form 

1099-MISC, Miscellaneous Information, any wages reportable on Form W-2. 

10. 
In 6 - Medical and health care payments, enter payments of $600 or more made in the 

course of your trade or business to each physician or other supplier or provider of medical 

or health care services. Include payments made by medical and health care insurers under 

health, accident, and sickness insurance programs. If payment is made to a corporation, list 

the corporation as the recipient rather than the individual providing the services. Payments 

to persons providing health care services often include charges for injections, drugs, 

dentures, and similar items. In these cases, the entire payment is subject to information 

reporting. You are not required to report payments to pharmacies for prescription drugs. 

The exemption from issuing Form 1099-MISC, Miscellaneous Information, to a corporation 

does not apply to payments for medical or health care services provided by corporations, 

including professional corporations. However, you are not required to report payments 

made to a tax-exempt hospital or extended care facility or to a hospital or extended care 

facility owned and operated by the United States (or its possessions), a state, the District of 

Columbia, or any of their political subdivisions, agencies, or instrumentalities. 

11. 
In 7 - Payer made direct sales of $5,000 or more of consumer products to a buyer 

(recipient) for resale, select the check box for sales by you of $5,000 or more of consumer 

products to a person on a buy–sell, deposit–commission, or other commission basis for 

resale (by the buyer or any other person) anywhere other than in a permanent retail 

establishment. Do not enter a dollar amount in this box.

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Daily Tasks User Guide 

12. 
In 8 - Substitute payments in lieu of dividends or interest, enter aggregate payments of at 

least $10 of substitute payments received by a broker for a customer in lieu of dividends or 

tax-exempt interest as a result of a loan of a customer’s securities. Substitute payment 

means a payment in lieu of (a) a dividend, or (b) tax-exempt interest to the extent that 

interest (including original issue discount) has accrued while the securities were on loan. For 

this purpose, a customer includes an individual, trust, estate, partnership, association, 

company, or corporation. 

13. 
In 9 - Crop insurance proceeds, enter crop insurance proceeds of $600 or more paid to 

farmers by insurance companies unless the farmer has informed the insurance company that 

expenses have been capitalized under section 278, 263A, or 447. 

14. 
In 10 - Gross proceeds paid to an attorney, enter gross proceeds of $600 or more paid to 

an attorney in connection with legal services (regardless of whether the services are

15. 
In 11 - Fish purchased for resale, report total cash payments of $600 or more paid during 

the year to any person who is engaged in the trade or business of catching fish. You are 

required to keep records showing the date and amount of each cash payment made during 

the year, but you must report only the total amount paid for the year on this form. 

“Fish” means all fish and other forms of aquatic life. “Cash” means US and foreign coin and 

currency and a cashier’s check, bank draft, traveler’s check, or money order. Cash does not 

include a check drawn on your personal or business account. 

16. 
In 12 - Section 409A deferrals, you do not have to complete this box. If you complete this 

box, enter the total amount deferred during the year of at least $600 for the non-employee 

under all non-qualified plans. The deferrals during the year include earnings on the current 

year and prior year deferrals. 

17. 
In 15 - Nonqualified deferred compensation, enter income as a nonemployee under an 

NQDC plan that does not meet the requirements of section 409A. This amount is also 

included in box 1, Form 1099-NEC as nonemployee compensation. Any amount included in 

box 12 that is currently taxable is also included in this box. This income is also subject to a 

substantial additional tax to be reported on Form 1040, 1040-SR, or 1040-NR.  

18. 
In 16 - State tax withheld, enter to report that you withheld state income tax from payments 

made to contractors/vendors who performed services for you. 

19. 
In 17 - State/Payer’s state no, enter the abbreviated name of the state and the payer’s state 

identification number. The state number is the payer’s identification number assigned by the 

individual state. In box 18, you may enter the amount of the state payment.  

20. 
In 18 - State income, enter to report the amount of the state income payment.

Distributions From Pensions, Annuities, Retirement or Profit-Sharing Plans, IRAs, 
Insurance Contracts, etc. (Form 1099-R) 

File Form 1099-R for each person to whom you have made a designated distribution or are 

treated as having made a distribution of $10.00 or more from: 

• 
Profit-sharing or retirement plans. 

• 
Any individual retirement arrangements (IRAs). 

• 
Annuities, pensions, insurance contracts, survivor income benefit plans. 

• 
Permanent and total disability payments under life insurance contracts. 

• 
Charitable gift annuities, etc. 

To file form 1099-R: 

1. 
Choose Distributions from pensions, annuities (Form 1099-R). 

When you choose Distributions from pensions, annuities from the Form name box, the 

Default 1099 box drop-down list includes these options: 

• 
1 - Gross distribution 

• 
2a - Taxable amount 

• 
3 - Capital gain (included in box 2a) 

• 
4 - Federal income tax withheld 

• 
5 - Employee Contributions/Designated Roth contributions or insurance premiums 

• 
6 - Net unrealized appreciation in employer’s securities 

• 
8 - Other 

• 
9b - Total employee contributions  

• 
10 - Amount allocable to IRR within 5 years  

• 
12 - FATCA filing requirement 

• 
13 - Date of payment 

• 
14 - State tax withheld 

• 
15 - State/Payer’s state no 

• 
16 - State distribution 

• 
17 - Local tax withheld 

• 
18 - Name of locality 

• 
19 - Local distribution 

2. 
Select the desired default 1099 box. 

3. 
In Entity, select the entity that is to generate the 1099 form. 

4. 
In Initial values for year, select a year to associate the values with a tax year.  

---


<!-- Page 234 -->
Vendors (Suppliers) 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Daily Tasks User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

5. 
In 1 - Gross distribution, enter the total amount of the distribution before income tax or 

other deductions were withheld. Include direct rollovers, IRA direct payments to accepting 

employer plans, recharacterized IRA contributions, Roth IRA conversions, and premiums 

paid by a trustee or custodian for the cost of current life or other insurance protection. Also 

include in this box distributions to plan participants from governmental section 457(b) 

plans. 

6. 
In 2a - Taxable amount, enter the taxable amount. When determining the taxable amount 

to be entered in box 2a, do not reduce the taxable amount by any portion of the $3,000 

exclusion for which the participant may be eligible as a payment of qualified health and 

long-term care insurance premiums for retired public safety officers under section 402(l). 

7. 
In 3- Capital gain (included in box 2a), if any amount is taxable as a capital gain, report it in 

box 3. 

8. 
In 4- Federal income tax withheld, enter any federal income tax withheld. This withholding 

under section 3405 is subject to deposit rules and the withholding tax return is Form 945. 

Backup withholding does not apply. 

9. 
In 5- Employee Contributions/Designated Roth contributions or insurance premiums, 

enter the employee’s contributions, designated Roth contributions, or insurance premiums 

that the employee may recover tax free this year (even if they exceed the box 1 amount). 

The entry in box 5 may include any of the following: (a) designated Roth contributions or 

contributions actually made on behalf of the employee over the years under the plan that 

were required to be included in the income of the employee when contributed (after-tax 

contributions), (b) contributions made by the employer but considered to have been 

contributed by the employee under section 72(f), (c) the accumulated cost of premiums paid 

for life insurance protection taxable to the employee in previous years and in the current 

year under Regulations section 1.72-16 (cost of current life insurance protection) (only if the 

life insurance contract itself is distributed), and (d) premiums paid on commercial annuities. 

Do not include any DVECs, elective deferrals, or any contribution to a retirement plan that 

was not an after-tax contribution. 

Generally, for qualified plans, section 403(b) plans, and non-qualified commercial annuities, 

enter in box 5 the employee contributions or insurance premiums recovered tax free during 

the year based on the method you used to determine the taxable amount to be entered in 

box 2a. On a separate Form 1099-R, include the portion of the employee’s basis that has 

been distributed from a designated Roth account. 

10. 
In 6- Net unrealized appreciation in employer’s securities, use this box if a distribution 

from a qualified plan (except a qualified distribution from a designated Roth account) 

includes securities of the employer corporation (or a subsidiary or parent corporation) and 

you can compute the NUA in the employer’s securities. Enter all the NUA in employer 

securities if this is a lump-sum distribution. If this is not a lump-sum distribution, enter only 

the NUA in employer securities attributable to employee contributions.

only, enter the patron’s share of the amount of section 199A(g) deduction claimed by the 

cooperative under section 199A(g) and passed through to the patron. This amount must 

have been designated in a written notice sent to the patron from the cooperative within the 

payment period under section 1382(d). The deduction allocated to each patron cannot 

exceed 9% of the qualified payments reported in box 7 and cannot be passed through to 

patrons that are C corporations. Do not reduce the amounts reported in box 1 or box 3 by 

the amount reported in box 6. 

11. 
In 7-Qualified payments (Section 199A (b) (7)), enter the qualified payments paid to the 

patron. You are required to provide this information whether or not you pass any of the 

DPAD through to the patrons. 

If your distributions to patrons relate to more than one trade or business for purposes of 

your section 199A reporting, you must provide a statement to the patron reporting the 

qualified payments for each trade or business separately, so the total from all trades and 

businesses equals the amount reported in box 7. See the instructions for box 13. 

12. 
In 8- Section 199 (A) qualified items, enter amounts reported to the patrons that are 

qualified items of income, gain, deduction, or loss from qualified trades or businesses that 

are not a specified service trade or business (SSTB) for purposes of section 199A. Examples 

of income that are not qualified items include tax-exempt income, capital gains, and income 

that isn’t effectively connected with the conduct of a trade or business within the United 

States.  

13. 
In 9 - Section 199 (A) SSTB, enter amounts reported to the patrons that are qualified items 

from otherwise qualified trades or businesses that are an SSTB for purposes of section 199A. 

Examples of SSTBs include the provision of services in the fields of health, law, accounting, 

etc.  

14. 
In 10- Investment credit, for specified agricultural and horticultural cooperatives only, enter 

the qualified payments paid to the patron. You are required to provide this information 

whether or not you pass any of the DPAD through to the patrons. 

15. 
In 11 - Work opportunity credit, enter the patron’s share of total work opportunity credit.

Certain Government Payments (Form 1099-G) 

1. 
Select the Certain Government Payments (Form 1099-G) form. 

When you choose Certain Government Payments from the Form name box, the Default 

1099 box drop-down list includes these options: 

• 
1 - Unemployment compensation 

• 
2 - State or local income tax refunds, credits, or offsets 

• 
4 - Federal income tax withheld 

• 
5 - RTAA payments 

• 
6 - Taxable grants 

• 
7 - Agriculture payments  

• 
9 - Market Gain 

2. 
Select the desired Default 1099 box. 

3. 
In the Entity drop-down list, select the entity that is to generate the 1099 form. 

4. 
In the Initial values for year drop-down list, select a year to associate the values with a tax 

year.  

5. 
In 1 - Unemployment compensation, enter to report payments of $10 or more in 

unemployment compensation, including Railroad Retirement Board payments for 

unemployment. 

If you make payments from a contributory program that has been deemed to be in the 

nature of unemployment compensation, such as California’s Family Temporary Disability 

Insurance payments or governmental paid family leave program payments, file a separate 

Form 1099-G for payments from each contributory program. Enter the total amount before 

any income tax was withheld. If you withhold federal income tax at the request of the 

recipient, enter it in box 4. 

6. 
In 2 - State or local income tax refunds, credits or offsets, enter select to report refunds, 

credits, or offsets of state or local income tax of $10 or more you made to recipients. These 

include refunds or carry-forward credits of overpayments of tax due to refundable state tax 

credits and incentive payments that are paid under an existing state tax law and 

administered by the state taxing agency. Filmmaker incentive credits, home improvement 

credits paid in low-income areas, and solar panel installation credits are some types of state 

programs which are generally reportable in box 2, to the extent a refund is paid by the state 

taxing agency or amount allowed as carry-forward credit to the next taxable year. 

7. 
In 4 - Federal income tax withheld, enter backup withholding on payments required to be 

reported in box 6 or 7. You must backup withhold on such payments at a rate of 24% if a 

recipient does not furnish its TIN to you or if you are notified by the IRS that the TIN is 

incorrect.

conserve or produce energy, but only with respect to energy property or a dwelling unit 

located in the United States. Also, enter any amount of a taxable grant administered by an 

Indian tribal government. Report amounts of other taxable grants of $600 or more. State

calendar years that the taxpayer provided an incorrect TIN. If you select this check box, the 

IRS will not send you any further notices about this account. 

However, if you received both IRS notices in the same year, or if you received them in 

different years but they both related to information returns filed for the same year, do not 

check the box at this time. For purposes of the two-notices-in-three-years rule, you are 

considered to have received one notice, and you are not required to send a second “B” 

notice to the taxpayer on receipt of the second notice.

*Source: `RP Accounting AP Daily Tasks User Guide.pdf`, Page 248*

Vendors (Suppliers) 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Daily Tasks User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Printing the CA 542 Data as a Report or Form 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > All > 1099/1096 > DE542 Form`


To print the CA DE 542 information: 

1. 
Open the Accounts payable menu. 

2. 
In the Vendor Reports section, pause on 1099/1096 and then select DE542 form. 

3. 
In the Time period section, select or type the Reporting date. 

4. 
Use the From vendor and To vendor fields to filter by a vendor, a range of vendors, or all 

vendors. 

How to use the From/To fields: 

All From/To field pairs work the same way. Use them to get search results in as broad or as 

fine a range as you need—from everything in the system down to a single specific object. 

To run this report for a single object: 

• 
Click the down arrow next to the From box, and from the menu that appears, click the 

object you want. 

• 
Click the down arrow next to the To box, and from the menu that appears, click the 

same object. 

To run this report for a specific range of objects: 

• 
Click the down arrow next to the From box, and from the menu that appears, click the 

object you want at the beginning of the range. 

• 
Click the down arrow next to the To box, and from the menu that appears, click the 

object you want at the end of the range. 

To run this report for all objects: 

Leave both boxes blank. 

If you have a large number of objects, or if this report takes too long to process, use the 

From and To boxes to run a series of smaller reports. For example, you can run five reports, 

one each for objects whose names begin with A–E, then F-J, K-O, P-T, and U–Z. 

An object is a catch -all term that refers to any specific data item in the system. 
Customers, vendors, items, and accounts are all examples of objects. 

5. 
In Entity, select the paying entity. 

Filling In the Activity Section 

1. 
In the Mode drop-down list, select Report Only to generate a report or select Update 

vendors & generate forms to select the CA DE 542 required check boxes in the vendor 

records.

### Merging Vendors
*Source: `RP Accounting AP Daily Tasks User Guide.pdf`, Page 250*

Vendors (Suppliers) 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Daily Tasks User Guide

Merging Vendors 

When you find duplicate vendor records in the system, you can merge them. 

This feature allows you to: 

• 
Compare two vendor records side-by-side, enabling you to confirm that they are duplicates. 

• 
Update the vendor records. 

• 
Update transactions that link to the vendors so that they all use the same record. 

As a result of the merge, only one vendor record will remain. The second vendor record becomes 

inactive. 

If you forget to include invoices linked to the vendor record that was inactivated, you must 
re-activate the inactive vendor record and repeat the merge of the two vendor records.

Merging Duplicate Vendors 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > All > Periodic Tasks > Account Maintenance > 
Merge Vendors`


If either vendor has a parent-child relationship, you must break this relationship before you can 

merge the vendor records. 

To merge duplicate vendor records: 

1. 
Open the Accounts payable menu. 

2. 
In the Account Maintenance section, select Merge vendors. 

3. 
On the Merge vendor page, in the left column, in the Active vendor ID drop-down list, 

select the vendor you want to remain active. This is the vendor you want your A/P invoices 

to show. 

4. 
In the Record Update section, select the type of vendor merge that you want to perform: 

All: Select to merge all A/P invoices, for both historical and active vendors. 

Update historical A/P invoices only: Select this option to merge all historical payments. 

New vendor information appears in the system, but the checks have already been printed 

with the original vendor information. 

Update active A/P invoices only: This option updates open items with active vendor 

information only and the historical A/P invoices appear on the available, side but are not 

updated. 

Update A/P invoice range: If you have a specific A/P invoice range that you want to update, 

this option will pull over just that range. On the A/P invoice range, you are required to move 

the available A/P invoices to the selected column. 

Update date range: Select this option when you have a specific date range that you want to 

update. 

• 
In From date and To date, enter the starting date and ending date of the date 

range.  

• 
Click the Get AP invoices button. The system selects the available A/P invoices to 

the selected column. 

None: If you do not merge A/P invoices, but you want to merge a vendor, then select this 

option.

Exporting Lists 

You can export most lists to several available file formats and then import the data into an 

external application, such as Microsoft Word or Microsoft Excel. 

Although you can export up to 25,000 rows, if you want to save time and effort, we recommend 

that you filter your list to pinpoint only the information you need to export by creating a custom 

view. That way, when you export the list, you’ll have a spreadsheet tailored to the information you 

need. You can export any view of this list for use on your local computer. 

Use column filters, advanced filters, and views to filter the data. For instructions, refer to 

Managing Lists. 

If you have a sorted and filtered list that you use consistently, you can create and save it as a 

custom report for convenience. With a custom report, you need to set the filtering and 

parameters only once to enable you to generate the report as needed after that. 

1. 
Click the Export button. 

2. 
Select the format to which you want to export the list. 

• 
CSV: Select this format if you plan to move the data from one program to another. 

You can use files that you save in CSV format with any spreadsheet program. 

• 
Word: When you select this option, the system exports the list in Word format. If a list 

of conversion formats displays, select HTML document. 

• 
Excel: When you select this option, the system exports the list in XLS format. If you see 

an error message about file type and extension type incompatibility, you can disregard 

the message and select Yes. 

• 
PDF: Select this option if you plan to print or share the list. When you select this 

option, the system exports the list and tries to open the file in the browser. If 

prompted, select Yes to allow the PDF to open. 

• 
CSV for import: Select this option if you want to export data, change it, or add to it, 

and then import it into the system again. 

Some lists in RealPage Accounting do not have the CSV for import option.

### A/P Invoice Overview
*Source: `RP Accounting AP Daily Tasks User Guide.pdf`, Page 266*

A/P Invoice Overview 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > All > A/P Invoices`


Managing A/P invoices includes adding, editing, and deleting A/P invoices received from vendors. 

The most important information appears at the top of the A/P invoice page for quick and easy 

access. For example, you can quickly scan to find the A/P invoice date, A/P invoice total, amount 

paid, and amount due. These fields change depending on the status of your A/P invoice. For 

example, if your payment is overdue then the banner includes the Overdue field that shows 

number of days that it is overdue in red text. 

You can pay an A/P invoice directly from the page when you are editing or viewing a posted A/P 

invoice. When the A/P invoice is partially or fully paid, you can click the link to view payment 

details. 

You can use the Ledger Sentry to set up a past due threshold. When an A/P invoice reaches the 

threshold, the system can send the user an email. Set up the threshold in the Ledger Sentry 

(Company > Ledger Sentry). 

Not ready to post or pay an A/P invoice? You can save it in draft format and post or pay it later. 

---



### Standard Invoices, eInvoices, and oInvoices
*Source: `RP Accounting AP Daily Tasks User Guide.pdf`, Page 267*

Chapter 4: A/P Invoices 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Daily Tasks User Guide 

Standard Invoices, eInvoices, and oInvoices 

Standard A/P invoices are invoices that you create in RealPage Accounting.  

Your system may be configured to accept invoices from outside of the RealPage Accounting 

system. These are called eInvoices, oInvoices, and UM invoices. 

All types of A/P invoices appear in the A/P invoices list. The invoice type appears in the 

Transaction type column. 

---


<!-- Page 268 -->
A/P Invoices 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Daily Tasks User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

eInvoices  

An eInvoice is an A/P invoice created when someone uses the Spend Management Storefront to 

create an order for a hosted catalog or punchout vendor, or is set up to receive invoices from an 

online vendor. The system generates a PDF of the invoice to match the order. 

• 
Click the URL in the OPs Attachments section to view attachments and the invoice. 

An eInvoice can include attachments when the attachment was made in Ops Technology. 

Information about the eInvoice includes Description, QTY, SKU, and Unit. Additional information 

appears in the Invoice Entries section so that you can tell which unit or SKU is tied to each line 

item in the invoice.  

Posting Date 

When invoices originate in Ops Merchant and are imported into RealPage Accounting, the 

posting date is set to the date that the record arrives in the RealPage Accounting system. You can 

manually change invoice posting dates as needed. 

Filtering the A/P Invoices list to show eInvoices 

To filter the list so that only eInvoices are included in the list, type an “e” in the Transaction type 

filter field, and then press ENTER. 

If you do not see a Storefront supplier code, you can invite the vendor to the marketplace (on 

page 103) to become an online vendor.  

If you do see that the vendor has a Storefront supplier code for the vendor, but you are not 

receiving eInvoices, it is likely that you need to send account requests to the vendor (on page 

114) for each property. After the vendor approves the request and assigns an account number, 

you can begin receiving eInvoices.  

---


<!-- Page 269 -->
Chapter 4: A/P Invoices 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Daily Tasks User Guide 

oInvoices 

An oInvoice is an A/P invoice created when you upload invoices using the Full Service menu 

option, Invoice Processing Upload.  

GL accounts and oInvoices 

When the G/L account is supplied on an oInvoice, and the account matches a G/L account in 

RealPage Accounting, RealPage Accounting accepts the account and codes the line item of the 

invoice. When the G/L account does not match exactly, the system codes the line to the default 

G/L account that is set up for Full Service.  

Posting oInvoices 

Normally, oInvoices post to the default G/L account that are defined for oInvoices.  

You can configure the system to prevent oInvoices from posting to the default G/L account. When 

enabled, after you save, submit and approve, or post the transaction, the system displays an error 

message to let you know that you cannot post to the default G/L. After receiving this message, 

you must select a different expense account. 

This list is filtered to show oInvoices. 

---



### Importing A/P Invoices
*Source: `RP Accounting AP Daily Tasks User Guide.pdf`, Page 270*

A/P Invoices

Importing A/P Invoices 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > Import Data > Set Up AP Master List, Open Invoices 
and Adjustments > Accounts Payable Invoices > Template/Import`


You can import A/P invoice data by filling in an A/P invoice template with data, saving the file in 

CSV format, and uploading the CSV file into the system. The actual import process occurs offline.  

• 
Each CSV file can contain up to 5,000 transactions. 

• 
The A/P invoice transactions should be open transactions only. Do not include paid or 

partially paid transactions. 

If an error occurs, the system rolls back the transaction. 

To upload historical invoices, be sure to select the Historical option. 

To import A/P invoices: 

1. 
Download the template. 

2. 
Fill in the template. 

3. 
Save the template as a CSV file (on page 257). 

4. 
Importing the A/P invoice data.  

You can upload A/P invoices using the Import data option. You can also upload the A/P 
invoices in the A/P invoices list. 

Downloading the Template 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > Import Data`


We recommend downloading a new blank template from the Import data page whenever you 

import information into the system. This is important because:  

• 
Templates are automatically customized based on your company configuration, including 

dimensions and custom fields you created.  

• 
Templates can be updated at any time, especially when a new version of RealPage 

Accounting is released. This means that an older template might not work.  

Templates 

As long as you have appropriate permissions, you can download any template, fill it with data, 

and then import the data. 

Follow these steps to prepare the data. Alternatively, give these instructions to your database 

administrator, who can help you with this step. 

---


<!-- Page 271 -->
Chapter 4: A/P Invoices 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Daily Tasks User Guide 

Each template has detailed information about one type of data. An item can be a thing, such as 

an entity, location, vendor, or contact; or a transaction type, such as invoices, fees, or adjustments. 

When you fill a template, make sure the data matches the template. For example, do not fill a Unit 

template with Location data. 

You can download the templates and import the data from the Import data page. 

To download a template:  

1. 
Open the Company menu. 

2. 
Select Import data. The Import data page lists the information that you can import.  

3. 
In the Set Up AP Master List, Open Invoices and Adjustments section, find the Accounts 

Payable Invoices option. 

4. 
Click the Template link to download the A/P invoices import template. You can find the file 

in your browser’s default download location.  

Filling In the Template 

Perform the following steps for each item that you want to import: 

1. 
Open the template in Excel and review the data structure. The information in the template 

file can help you formulate extraction queries. 

2. 
Export the data from your other source. 

3. 
Copy the exported data into the template file for the same kind of object. Take care to 

exactly match the template’s data structure as you do this. 

Avoid using leading zeros in ID fields. If you must use leading zeros in IDs, convert the 
column of ID numbers to text format in Excel before importing the file content. Excel does 
not remove the leading zeros when you save the file. Remember to do this every time you 
use a template to import information that requires IDs. 

4. 
Fill in the required columns: 

• 
VENDOR_ID: Type the unique identifier of the vendor associated with the invoice. 

• 
CREATED_DATE: Type the date of the invoice. 

• 
DUE_DATE: Type the date that the payment is due. 

• 
BASECURR: Type the three-letter ISO-4127 currency code such as USD or EUR for the 

base currency. The currency and its format must be defined in the system. This field is 

required for shared multi-entity companies with multiple base currencies. Locations in 

line items must use the same base currency. 

• 
CURRENCY: Type the three-letter ISO-4127 currency code for the currency used for 

this transaction.  

• 
INVOICE_NO: Type the unique invoice number.  

---

### A/P Invoice Workflow Overview
*Source: `RP Accounting AP Daily Tasks User Guide.pdf`, Page 276*



#### A/P Invoice Workflow (Approvals Disabled)
*Source: `RP Accounting AP Daily Tasks User Guide.pdf`, Page 276*

A/P Invoices 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Daily Tasks User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

A/P Invoice Workflow Overview 

As an A/P invoice travels through the system, it changes status. 

• 
When you create an A/P invoice, it is an A/P draft invoice. 

• 
After you post the A/P invoice, it is waiting to be approved (if you are using the A/P invoice 

approval workflow) and its status is Submitted. If the A/P invoice does not require approval, 

its status is Posted. 

• 
If the invoice is not approved, its status is Declined, and the invoice can be deleted. 

• 
If the invoice is eligible to be paid, the Pay link appears in the A/P invoices list. 

• 
If the Reverse link appears, the invoice can be reversed (but not deleted). 

• 
If the Delete link appears, the invoice can be deleted (but not reversed). 

• 
When an invoice has been paid but resides in the payment Outbox, its status is Selected. 

A/P Invoice Workflow (Approvals Disabled) 

The state of the invoice changes as it works its way through the workflow: 

• 
Draft: The invoice is saved but not yet posted or submitted for approval. 

• 
Posted: The invoice is posted to the General Ledger. (If approvals are enabled, the invoice is 

not posted until the transaction is approved.) 

• 
Selected: The invoice is selected for payment but not yet paid. 

• 
Partially paid: Only part of the invoice is paid. 

• 
Paid: The invoice is paid in full. 

• 
Reversed: The invoice has been reversed. 

• 
Reversal: The listed transaction is the reversal created from the reversed invoice. 

---


<!-- Page 277 -->
Chapter 4: A/P Invoices 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Daily Tasks User Guide 

---



#### A/P Invoice Workflow (Approvals Enabled)
*Source: `RP Accounting AP Daily Tasks User Guide.pdf`, Page 278*

A/P Invoices 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Daily Tasks User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

A/P Invoice Workflow (Approvals Enabled) 

When the A/P invoice approval feature is enabled: 

• 
Submitted: The invoice is saved and submitted to the approval workflow. 

• 
Partially approved: A transaction can have more than one approver. The invoice is approved 

by at least one approver in the workflow, but more approvals are required. 

• 
Declined: Approver or approvers declined the invoice. 

---

list enters packaging mode. Select the invoices to include in the package, and then 

click the Generate Package button. 

h) 
Pay: When an unpaid A/P invoice is in a state that allows you to pay it, the Pay link 

appears. Click the Pay link to open the Pay A/P invoices box where you can pay the 

invoice. 

i) 
Print: Click to print the invoice. 

j) 
Reverse: Click the Reverse link in the Delete column to reverse the invoice. When an 

invoice is in draft state, the system replaces the Reverse link with a check box. To 

delete invoices, select the check boxes of the invoices that you want to delete, and 

then click the Delete button. If the column does not have a Reverse link or a Delete 

check box, then you cannot delete or reverse the invoice. 

Select the Show future draft invoices check box to filter the list so that future draft 
invoices are included in the list.  

Customizing the List 

You can add more columns to the list, like Payment method and Payment number, by creating a 

custom view. Use the list controls to create custom views and filter and sort the list. See 

Managing the List for details.

<!-- Page 282 -->
A/P Invoices 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Daily Tasks User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Additional Options 

Some additional options are available in this list that may or may not appear in the example. 

• 
After selecting the invoice or invoices to include in a package, click one of the following 

buttons: Generate Package or Show Only Selected Invoices. The Generate Package button 

will generate an invoice package containing the invoices that are selected from the A/P 

Invoices list. The Show Only Selected Invoices button lists only the A/P invoices that are 

selected. Click the Cancel Package button to clear all selections. 

• 
Transaction types: Invoices that appear in this list can come from RealPage Accounting or 

from other sources. When invoices are generated in other parts of the system, they are 

called eInvoices, or oInvoices. eInvoices come from Storefront, and oInvoices come from Full 

Service. When Full Service’s Invoice Processing process creates an A/P invoice record, the 

process inserts the account number in the oInvoice’s Reference number field. 

Management Fees 

Management fees are billed with recurring invoices. To create a fee, create a recurring A/P invoice 

and then create an A/R invoice to bill the site back for the fee. Fees work differently than 

intercompany billing. For fees, the A/R liability isn’t relieved. Instead, the A/R invoice stays open 

until you apply a payment against the fee’s invoice.  

Utility Invoices 

When your company subscribes to the RealPage Utility Management (UM) application, RealPage 

offers a feature that prevents customers from paying UM invoices, as the UM application makes 

the utility payments on customers’ behalf. These invoices are only hidden for customers for whom 

RUM makes payments. 

When the feature is enabled, the UM invoices do not appear on the Pay A/P invoices page, and 

the UM invoices do not have a Pay option when they appear in the A/P invoices list.  

Contact RealPage Support to enable this feature. 

Distributions 

Investor distributions appear in the A/P invoices list with a Transaction Type of “Distribution.” 

Invoices List in a Multi-entity Company 

In multi-entity companies, transaction lists at the entity level include transactions created at the 

top level that have been tagged to your entity. However, if no transactions have been posted in 

the last six months that fit the criteria, then entity-level transaction lists only include entity-level 

transactions. 

If you want to see older transactions created at the top level for your entity, then select the 

Include top level transactions check box at the top of your list.

Excel

This topic describes how to create an A/P invoice as if every possible feature is enabled. Your 

experience of this page will differ depending on the features that your system has enabled. 

Variations occur due to system configuration, your permissions, and your company’s installation 

of other RealPage Financial Suite applications. For instructions on importing A/P invoices, see 

Importing A/P Invoices (on page 252). 

Applications that Affect the Fields on A/P Invoice Records 

• 
Spend Management 

• 
Job Cost  

Configuration Differences that Affect the Fields on A/P Invoice Records 

• 
When your system is configured to use multiple currencies, additional currency fields appear 

in this record. See the multi-currency systems section on the General Ledger configuration 

page. 

• 
When the Intercompany billing option is enabled (Accounts Receivable configuration), the 

A/R Invoice Dimensions section appears. 

• 
When your system is integrated with OpsTechnology, it allows RealPage Accounting to 

receive eInvoices. 

• 
Accounts Payable configuration:  

---


<!-- Page 291 -->

• 
When the Enable bank account selection in A/P invoice option is selected (Accounts 

Payable configuration), it causes the Bank account field to appear on the A/P invoice 

record. 

• 
When the Enable invoice entry control validation option is selected (Accounts 

Payable configuration), it causes the Total invoice amount field to appear on the A/P 

invoice record. 

• 
When Spend management is enabled, then the Match Order button appears, allowing you 

to match a purchase order to the A/P invoice. Additional fields appear on the record such as 

QTY, Price, Extended Price, UOM, and Account code description. 

• 
When Job Cost is enabled, the Line Entry Type section appears. When you select Include Job 

cost, the system adds Job cost-specific columns in the Invoice Entries list such as Job name, 

Cost code, and Job unit.  

• 
When scanning is enabled, the Attachments field is replaced with the Documents section, 

affecting the way that you attach documents.  

• 
If the Please complete one-time setup scanner prompt appears, follow the 

instructions in Downloading the Scanning Software. If you do not plan to scan 

supporting documents at this time, you can skip the download by clicking the X in 

upper-right corner of the box.  

• 
If you enabled the Single scan upload feature in your preferences and have previously 

downloaded the Dynamsoft scanning software, you may be prompted to update the 

software when you add a new scannable record such as an A/P invoice, vendor, 

purchase order, or service contract, or scan a document into the document dashboard. 

When this occurs, download the new software. There is no need to uninstall the 

previous version. 

• 
Clicking the Scan button in the Documents section redisplays the scanner prompt.

• 
Permissions for attachments 

• 
Permissions for adding assets

To create an A/P invoice: 

1. 
In the Date field, type the date of the invoice, or leave it set to today’s date.  

Any date entered here is automatically filled in the G/L posting date field (and to the 

Exchange rate date field if you’re a multi-currency company). You can change either date as 

needed; for example, if you want to create the adjustment today, but post it on a different 

date. 

2. 
In the G/L posting date field, type the date that you want the A/P invoice to post on the 

general ledger.  

3. 
In the Total invoice amount field, type the amount of the invoice.  

This field appears only when the Enable invoice entry control validation check box is 

selected on the configuration page of Accounts Payable. When enabled, this is a required 

field.  

4. 
In the Vendor drop-down list, select an existing vendor or add a new vendor, as required. 

The system completes the Pay to and Return to fields automatically based on the vendor 

record that you select. This is a required field. 

To add a new vendor, you must be at the top level. You can use the field-level controls to 

add a new vendor, view a vendor’s record, or find a vendor’s record. 

The system fills in the Pay to field automatically. If you need to change the Pay to contact, 

you can do that here. In the Pay to drop-down list, select the name of the person to whom 

the payment should be sent. 

The system fills in the Return to field automatically. If you need to change the Return to 

contact, you can do that here. In the Return to drop-down list, select the name of the 

person to whom returns should be addressed.  

5. 
To fill in the A/P invoice form with data from the last A/P invoice from this vendor, click the 

Populate from last A/P invoice button.  

6. 
In the Invoice number field, type the invoice number. This is a required field. 

7. 
Type a Reference number. Reference numbers can be a vendor’s number that they use to 

track the payment.  

8. 
Type a Description of the transaction.  

You can also use the Reference number and Description fields to enter specific 
information that a vendor requires. Sometimes, a vendor requires a specific piece of 
information to reconcile your payments, such as a customer account number or a pin 
number. 

9. 
Select the Corporate invoice check box if you want to prevent this invoice from appearing 

in Spend Management’s Site Experience. 

---

10.

Click the Match order button.
