In the Match orders box, click the View details link. 

• 
In the Contract details section that appears below, select the service order for which 

you want to create an A/P invoice. 

• 
Click Apply. 

Make the Invoice Recurring 

1. 
Select the Make recurring check box to turn this invoice into a recurring invoice. When you 

submit the A/P invoice, the system creates a recurring A/P invoice based on the current 

invoice. When you select this check box, the Schedules section appears.  

2. 
In the Schedules section, fill in the A/P invoice start date field with the date that you want 

the system to start creating the recurring A/P invoices. 

3. 
Select the sequence number scheme from the AP invoice sequence number drop-down list. 

4. 
In the Ending on drop-down list, select: 

• 
Never: To keep the invoice perpetually running, select Never. This is common for A/P 

invoices for ongoing services that have a set price. 

• 
Number of occurrences: The End after field appears. To have the invoice run for a 

limited number of times, type the number of times you want the invoice to recur in the 

End after field. This setting is often used for debts that are being paid over time. 

Setting the number of occurrences eliminates the possibility of making payments after 

the debt is paid off. 

• 
End date: To have the invoice recur until a specific date, select End date and then, in 

the End on field, type the date on which the last invoice is to recur.

None

Months

Years

In the Every field, type the number of time frames to repeat by. For example, if you selected

When you submit the A/P invoice, the system creates a draft invoice with a posting date set 

for the future date and containing the details of the source A/P invoice.  

The system sends you an email as a reminder on the day before the future draft invoice 
date is to be automatically posted.

Select the terms of payment in the Term drop-down list. If you selected the Make recurring 

check box, the Term field is required.

 Calendar button and then select the

Saving the A/P Invoice 

When entering the transaction information, save it as a draft or post it. The system validates 

transactions only when they are posted. For example, required departments or locations are not 

validated until posting. 

• 
Click Draft or Draft & new to save your progress on the transaction without affecting the 

subledger or G/L. Later, you or another user can review and post it. 

• 
Click Post or Post & new to post the transaction. 

System Checks for Budget Exceeded  

If you try to post an A/P invoice that exceeds the default budget, and your company uses the A/P 

invoice approval process with the budget exceeded feature, the system displays a warning. The 

system may also prevent you from posting the A/P invoice. If you want to be able to bypass this 

budget check, ask your system administrator to grant you the desired bypass permission. Bypass 

permissions are available for A/P invoices and purchase orders. 

---


<!-- Page 307 -->
Chapter 4: A/P Invoices 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Daily Tasks User Guide 

When the budget exceeded feature is enabled, the system checks the A/P invoice amount against 

the budgeted number for the G/L account. When the amount exceeds the budget, then the 

system either displays a warning or prevents you from saving the A/P invoice, depending on how 

your company configured the feature. When preventing an A/P invoice from being posted, the 

system also displays a warning to let you know why you cannot post. 

To enable or disable the budget exceeded feature, see Setting a system action when an A/P 

invoice or purchase order exceeds the budget (on page 568).  

System Checks for Attachments 

Your company may require that you attach a document to support the A/P invoice before you can 

save it as a draft, post, or submit it. If you need to save an A/P invoice without an attachment, 

contact your system administrator and ask them to remove the Require attachment permission 

(on page 266) from your role or account. 

What’s Next? 

When your company uses approvals, A/P invoices first go through the payment approval 

workflow. After payments are approved, you can make the payments.  

Go to the Pay A/P invoices page to select the invoice for payment. When you select Add to 

outbox or Pay now: 

• 
The invoice becomes a payment request. 

• 
The system notifies approvers that a payment is waiting for their approval. 

• 
You can view the status of the payment request in the Payment request list. 

• 
When an approver approves the invoice, the system pays the invoice. 

• 
If the payment method is Check, the system allows the payment to be included in a check 

run.

Using an Invoice as a Model for Similar Invoices 

If your goal is to create one invoice and reuse it as the starting point for additional invoices, use 

the Duplicate function. You can use the same invoice to make duplicate records, or duplicate 

invoices as needed.  

You can also create a future draft of an invoice as you add the invoice, and then set the date to 
create the future draft. See Adding an A/P Invoice Manually (on page 272 ) and look for the 
section called “Creating a Future Draft Invoice.” 

You cannot download a duplicated record to save and reuse it, but you can print it.

1. 
Open the Accounts Payable menu.

Click the A/P Invoices option. 

3. 
Use the View or Edit link of an A/P invoice to open it.

Click the Duplicate button. A copy of the record opens, including its data.

Fill in the new record with its unique details, and then click Save.

#### Duplicating Records
*Source: `RP Accounting AP Daily Tasks User Guide.pdf`, Page 312*

A/P Invoices

Duplicating Records 

If your goal is to create one record and reuse it as the starting point for additional records, use 

the Duplicate function. Most types of records can be duplicated—including A/P invoices, A/R 

invoices, recurring invoices, adjustments, entities, vendors, contacts, journals, G/L accounts, 

user-defined books, document numbering sequences, contracts, service tickets, email templates, 

and reporting account sets. When you open a record and it includes a Duplicate button, you can 

use it as a template to quickly create a new record.  

For invoices, you can also create a future draft of an invoice as you add it, and set the date to 

create the future draft. See Adding an A/P Invoice Manually (on page 272) and look for the 

section called “Creating a Future Draft Invoice.” 

To duplicate recurring invoices, look for the Duplicate option that is located in the More actions 
button menu. 

To duplicate a record: 

1. 
Open the record that you want to duplicate by clicking View or Edit.  

2. 
Click the Duplicate button. The system creates a new record that is identical to the original. 

After you duplicate a record, the copy of the record stays open so that you can change its 

details.  

3. 
Fill in the fields.  

4. 
The system sets the status to Active. You can leave the status set to Active or select Inactive 

to prevent the item from appearing in lists. 

5. 
Click the Save button. You can also click the More actions button, and then select Save & 

New. The system saves the record and then opens a new blank record. 

---

#### Editing A/P Invoices
*Source: `RP Accounting AP Daily Tasks User Guide.pdf`, Page 321*

Chapter 4: A/P Invoices 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Daily Tasks User Guide 

Editing A/P Invoices 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > All > A/P Invoices > Edit`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > All > Invoice Research > (search) > Edit`


The most important elements of the A/P invoice appear at the top of the page in the banner, 

including the vendor ID balance, invoice date, due date, invoice total, overdue, amount paid, and 

amount due. 

When you open an invoice in edit mode, the invoice image automatically opens. You can control 

how the invoice appears, either next to the invoice record or in a separate window. To change 

how the invoice appears, open the My Preferences > Personalize Interactive Behavior section, 

and then select or clear the Open Image Review in Separate Window check box. 

Invoices That You Can Edit 

You can edit unposted A/P invoices, eInvoices, and oInvoices. You can also edit posted A/P 

invoices if you have the Edit When Posted permission. 

A/P invoices can be associated with multiple locations. Only unrestricted users and users who 

have access to all of an A/P invoice’s associated locations can edit the invoice.  

Editing Invoices Submitted for Approval 

When your system has approvals enabled for A/P invoices, after you create an A/P invoice, the 

system submits the invoice for approval and changes its state to Submitted. You can edit 

submitted A/P invoices until they are approved.  

If you do not want the system to send edited A/P invoices through the approval process again 

when there is no change to the Location, G/L Account, or Total Amount fields, it is configurable. 

Ask your system administrator to configure it by going to Company > All > Approvals > 

Approval Configuration and selecting the Do not retrigger approvals check box in the A/P 

invoices section of the Approval Configuration page. 

Invoices That You Cannot Edit 

You can only edit invoices when you open them with the Edit link. In some cases, an Edit link is 

not available, such as when you do not have access to an invoice’s associated locations. If you do 

not have access to all of the locations associated with an A/P invoice, then the system does not 

display an Edit link for the invoice. 

Invoices created using the intercompany billing or management fee features cannot be edited. If 

your company wants the ability to edit these invoices, you can contact RealPage Customer 

Support to have RealPage enable additional permissions that permit the editing of these types of 

invoices. When enabled, two additional permissions appear in the permissions list for A/P 

invoices, Edit MF and Edit ICB. These permissions apply to both A/P and A/R invoices.  

---


<!-- Page 322 -->
A/P Invoices 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Daily Tasks User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

A/P Invoices with an Intercompany Billing Invoice 

When you edit the A/P invoice that is the result of an intercompany billing (ICB) invoice, the 

changes that you make do not affect the original intercompany billing invoice. You must make 

changes to the intercompany billing invoice directly. Open Accounts Receivable, select 

Intercompany Billing, and then find the original invoice and make your changes there. The 

invoice must be in the Submitted state but not be posted.  

Users can view the A/R invoice that is created after the A/P invoice is posted. The A/R invoice 

does not appear in the Intercompany Billing list until the A/P invoice is posted. 

Editing Invoices 

To edit an invoice: 

1. 
Open the Accounts payable menu. 

2. 
Select A/P invoices. The A/P invoices list opens. 

You can also edit invoices from the Invoice Research list. 

3. 
Find the A/P invoice you want to change, and then click Edit. The system opens the A/P 

invoice page with information about the A/P invoice. 

4. 
To match the A/P invoice with orders, click the Match Order button. The Match Orders 

page opens and lists all open purchase orders for that vendor and location. Use the Match 

Orders page to match the A/P invoice, eInvoice, or oInvoice to purchase orders, subcontract 

orders, and service orders that were created from service contracts.  

5. 
Add, modify, or delete information as needed. You can change any field without having to 

repost the A/P invoice except for the G/L account field. If you change the G/L account field, 

then you must post the A/P invoice again. 

The system displays a warning and can prevent you from posting the invoice if you increase 
the amount on the invoice and your company has enabled the warning for when the budget is 
exceeded. 

The system actions that occur when the budget is exceeded depends on your company 

configuration. You can enable or disable the system warning or change the system action 

from a warning to preventing the invoice from posting. You must have system 

administration privileges to make this change. 

• 
To change the system action, go to Company > All > Approval Configuration.  

• 
To enable or disable the feature, select or clear the Enable preventing or warning a 

user when adding an A/P Invoice that exceeds the budget check box. 

• 
You can also change the system action to Prevent or Warn.  

6. 
To change the G/L account, the 1099 status, or any dimensions, click Reclassify.

7. 
Click Save to save the changes. The system sends the invoice through the approval

The accounting reviewer is typically the final approver in an approval workflow. When an 

accounting reviewer makes changes to an invoice, the system does not send the invoice 

through the approval workflow.  

What’s Next? 

After the invoice is approved, the A/P invoice becomes a payment request. The next step in the 

process is to pay the invoice. 

Adding a Note to an A/P Invoice 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > All > A/P Invoices > Edit`


This topic describes how to add a note to an A/P invoice. The note will appear on the A/P invoice 

when you print or email it. 

To add a note to an A/P invoice: 

1. 
Open the Accounts payable menu. 

2. 
Select A/P invoices. The A/P invoices list opens. 

3. 
Find the A/P invoice you want to change, and then click Edit. The system displays the A/P 

invoice page with information about the A/P invoice. 

4. 
Scroll to the bottom of the page.  

5. 
Type the desired message in the Notes field. 

6. 
Click the Post or Submit button to save the note. 

Removing a Note from the A/P Invoice 

When you add a note to an A/P invoice, the system includes the note on the printed or emailed 

version of the A/P invoice.  

To prevent the note from appearing on the A/P invoice: 

1. 
Edit the A/P invoice. 

2. 
Delete the text in the Note field. 

3. 
Click the Post or Submit button to save the A/P invoice.

#### What You Can Edit on an A/P Invoice
*Source: `RP Accounting AP Daily Tasks User Guide.pdf`, Page 324*

A/P Invoices 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Daily Tasks User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

What You Can Edit on an A/P Invoice 

Depending on its state, you can edit all aspects of an A/P invoice, or you can partially edit it. 

• 
Full edit: You can change any aspect of the A/P invoice including those that affect the G/L, 

such as the amount or the associated account. 

• 
Partial edit: You can change aspects that don’t affect the G/L, such as the invoice number, 

term, or memo. 

This is a list of edit capabilities on an A/P invoice based on its state. 

• 
Draft: Fully Edit 

• 
Posted: Fully Edit* 

• 
Posted from another application: Fully edit and partially edit; Edit the invoice from the 

application where it was created and posted. 

• 
Selected: Partially edit; If you want to have full edit capability, cancel the payment request, 

then edit the A/P invoice. 

• 
Selected (partially paid): Partially edit 

• 
Paid: Partially edit 

• 
No Value: Fully edit and partially edit 

* You can edit unposted A/P invoices, eInvoices, and oInvoices. You can also edit posted A/P 
invoices if you have the Edit When Posted permission. You cannot edit invoices that result from 
intercompany bills (ICBs) or management fees.

Paid: The invoice has been fully paid.

invoice’s approval history. 

• 
Partially paid: The invoice has been partially paid. 

• 
Posted: The invoice has been posted to the general ledger.

Selected: The invoice has been selected for payment, but has not yet been submitted.

Submitted (link): The invoice has been created and submitted for approval. Click the 

link to review the invoice’s approval history.

Matching Invoices to Purchase Orders 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > All > A/P Invoices > Edit > Match Order`


To match invoices with purchase orders, the invoice type must be eInvoice or oInvoice. Spend 

Management Storefront creates eInvoices. Spend Management Full Service creates oInvoices. 

When Storefront or Full Service Invoice Processing exchanges invoices with RealPage Accounting, 

the system automatically matches the imported invoices with the purchase orders. 

When the PO number is on the invoice attachment, the system automatically matches the PO with 

the invoice.  

• 
When a match occurs, the button name on the invoice changes to View Matched Order. 

Click the View Matched Order button to view the match details.  

• 
If the invoice is not matched, then the button is called Match Order.  

When the system is unable to match any of the purchase orders, you can match them manually by 

matching line items in the invoices to items in purchase orders using the Match Order button. 

When an eInvoice comes into the system and a user selects the Match order option, the system 

displays all orders for the vendor and the parent and child vendors of that vendor.  

Matching Errors 

When eInvoices and oInvoices are received by the system, they undergo the auto-matching 

process. When the system detects errors during auto-matching, it disables auto-matching for the 

invoice to allow you to fix the error. After fixing the invoice, you submit the fixed invoice so that it 

goes through the approval process. See Troubleshooting PO Matching (on page 319). 

Matching One to Many 

When you try to match a purchase order to an invoice that has Spend Management fields, you 

can select one line to match many purchase order lines on different purchase orders as long as 

the match does not exceed the total quantity (the number in the Qty field of the A/P invoice). 

You can also match one line of a purchase order to many lines of an invoice as long as the match 

does not exceed the quantity. 

By default, the quantity is 1 on invoices that were created before the Spend Management fields 

were added to the system. If you know that the quantity is more, then edit the invoice to change 

the quantity, and then submit it for approval as needed.

1. 
Open the Accounts Payable menu. 

2. 
Select A/P Invoices. 

3. 
Find the eInvoice or oInvoice that you want to match, and then click the Edit link.

Matching a New A/P Invoice to an Order

To use this feature for purchase orders, your company must use the Spend Management 

application to create purchase orders (POs) so that the invoice will match the PO exactly.  

You can create a matching A/P invoice for a purchase order, service order, or subcontract order.  

eInvoices and oInvoices 

EInvoices and oInvoices come from the vendor’s system. RealPage Accounting prevents changing 

the amounts on eInvoices and oInvoices so that the invoices sync properly between the two 

systems, and therefore, they will match appropriately.  

If the system detects errors during auto-matching, it disables auto-matching for the invoice to 

allow you to fix the error. After fixing the invoice, you submit the fixed invoice so that it goes 

through the approval process.  

Thresholds 

Spend Management allows you to set thresholds on invoice amounts.  

• 
When thresholds are enabled, the invoice total can be higher than or less than the allowed 

variance between the PO and the invoice. 

• 
When thresholds are not enabled, the total of the PO and the total of the invoice must be 

the same. If they are not, you must update the PO so that they are.

Troubleshooting PO Matching 

Automatic purchase order (PO) matching fails when the system does not find an exact PO number 

on the eInvoice. 

If it is a standard invoice (and not an eInvoice): 

• 
Make sure that the purchase order was created by looking for it in the Purchase Orders list 

or the Spend Management workbench. 

• 
Ensure that the purchase order is in the Approved or Partial Invoice Match state. 

If the invoice is an eInvoice, these things are essential for the PO matching feature to work: 

• 
The PO number must appear on the eInvoice.  

Click the URL link on the attachment to find the PO number. 

• 
You must place the orders online using the Storefront.  

Manually created purchase orders can be automatically matched to the invoice as long as 

the vendor sets the exact same PO number on the vendor invoice. 

• 
The vendor must have defined the PO number on the eInvoice. 

If the vendor does not add the PO number to their paperwork, then the PO matching 

feature does not work. 

• 
The PO number on the eInvoice must match exactly the PO number in the RealPage 

Accounting system.  

The PO number is created when you place the order in Storefront. 

If the PO number does not appear, check that the PO has been approved. If it has not been 
approved, the PO number will not appear.

To match an invoice when adding a transaction:

orders not matched from the previous month display as well. Match the A/P invoices with

match line items, the G/L account on the purchase order overrides the invoice’s G/L 
account. This is true for all three types of invoices: A/P Invoices, oInvoices, and eInvoices.

•

appear in the invoice’s line item. 

Multiple transaction line items can be added to an order and vice versa to improve 
matching functionality. Two frequent scenarios are an invoice with one line item that can be 
matched to multiple lines of a purchase or service orders and an invoice with multiple line 
items that can be matched to a single line of a purchase or service order. The selected 
quantity on both the invoice and the order should match.

#### Matching External Invoices
*Source: `RP Accounting AP Daily Tasks User Guide.pdf`, Page 344*

A/P Invoices 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Daily Tasks User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

To match a partial quantity of a transaction: 

If the Receipt of Goods function is not enabled in Spend Management, then when an invoice 

contains and matches a partial quantity, the transaction partially matches the quantity and 

remains open to match the remaining quantity. This changes the transaction’s status to Partial 

Invoice Match. Then if an online invoice is created for only the amount received, the automatic 

matching function will take into consideration that the quantity of the invoice matches the 

quantity of the transaction. 

Matching External Invoices 

eInvoices and oInvoices arrive at the RealPage Accounting system through different processes 

and thus are treated differently. 

eInvoices 

When the vendor sends you an eInvoice, the vendor includes a purchase order (PO) number on 

the eInvoice. The RealPage Accounting system compares the PO number on incoming eInvoices 

to the data in the system. 

When an eInvoice arrives and the system can match the PO on the eInvoice with a PO number in 

the RealPage Accounting system, then the system records the match and fills in the line items of 

the eInvoice. In this case, the PO already has the correct G/L account, so it flows into the invoice. 

When the eInvoice is not automatically matched to a PO, the system codes the invoice to the 

default expense account set up on the vendor record. If there is no default expense account, then 

the system codes the eInvoice to the default G/L account. 

oInvoices 

oInvoices are created in the Spend Management Full Service module, and come through OPS 

Invoice processing. The RealPage Accounting system does not attempt to match an incoming 

oInvoice even when it has a PO number. oInvoices must be matched manually.

Total Price 
This is the total price for all items on this line. 

Memo 
This is a note that the person who submitted the order added to the line 

item. 

Qty received 
This is the number of items received from the vendor. 

Prior invoice qty 
This is the number of items received prior to the purchase order. 

Invoice qty 
This is the number of items of this type on the invoice. 

Invoice price 
This is the amount of the invoice of the transaction. The Invoice Price field is 

highlighted in red to remind you to update the invoice price.

Tracking Transactions Using Segments 

The system offers the use of segments to track the following transaction types: 

• 
Manual deposits 

• 
A/R advances 

• 
Recurring A/R invoices 

• 
A/R adjustments 

• 
A/R invoices 

• 
A/P invoices 

• 
A/P advances 

• 
Recurring A/P invoices 

• 
Manual payments 

• 
A/P adjustments 

• 
Journal entries 

When creating a transaction, assign at least one segment type and value to it. 

When you post the transaction, the system can report on the transaction by its defined segment.  

For example, a property manager of a mall, can create a custom segment for retail categories. By 

assigning a retail category to each A/R invoice, you would be able to run a report to track the rent 

by retail segment. Segments are available in the General Ledger report and the Trial Balance 

report. In addition, a segment activity report allows you to filter by segment.

#### Reversing Versus Deleting A/P Invoices
*Source: `RP Accounting AP Daily Tasks User Guide.pdf`, Page 355*

Chapter 4: A/P Invoices 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Daily Tasks User Guide 

Reversing Versus Deleting A/P Invoices 

You can either reverse or delete an A/P invoice as needed. Which action you take is dependent on 

your configuration and the state of the A/P invoice. 

Draft A/P Invoices: A partially created A/P invoice, perhaps waiting for additional input. 

• 
When reversal is disabled: Delete the A/P invoice (on page 339). 

• 
When reversal is enabled: Reverse the A/P invoice (on page 340). 

Posted A/P Invoices: Created and posted from the A/P invoices page. 

• 
When reversal is disabled: Delete the A/P Invoice. 

• 
When reversal is enabled: You can reverse an unpaid A/P invoice that was entered 

directly in Accounts Payable. To make sure that the system is enabled for reversing an 

unpaid A/P invoice, see Enabling A/P Functionality. 

A/P invoices and approvals in the Approval workbench.  

A/P invoices are submitted and then: 

• 
Approved: You can reverse an approved A/P invoice when reversal is enabled. 

• 
Declined: You must enable a setting before you can reverse a declined invoice. To 

enable the setting, open the Approval Configuration page, and then select the Ability 

to delete declined approvals check box.  

Selected A/P invoices: Associated with a payment request but has no payment against it. 

When reversal is disabled:  

• 
Cancel the payment request (on page 498) or 

• 
Delete the A/P Invoice. 

When reversal is enabled: 

• 
Cancel the payment request or 

• 
Reverse the A/P invoice. 

Selected (partially paid): The A/P invoice has a payment request and already has a partial 

payment against it. 

When reversal is disabled: 

• 
Cancel the payment request or 

• 
Void the payment (on page 529), and then delete the A/P invoice. 

When reversal is enabled: 

• 
Cancel the payment request or  

• 
Void the payment and then reverse the A/P invoice.

#### Configuring Reversals for Unpaid A/P Invoices
*Source: `RP Accounting AP Daily Tasks User Guide.pdf`, Page 358*

A/P Invoices 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Daily Tasks User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Reversing A/P Invoices 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > All > A/P Invoices > Reverse`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > All > Invoice Research > Reverse`


Before You Begin  

The Reverse option appears only at the level where the invoice was created. If the invoice was 

created at the top level, then navigate to the top level. If the invoice was created at the entity 

level, then navigate to the entity’s level.  

To reverse A/P invoices: 

1. 
Open the Accounts payable menu. 

2. 
In the Search & Find section, select A/P invoices. The A/P invoices list opens. 

3. 
Click the Reverse link beside the A/P invoice record you want to reverse.  

If a Reverse link does not appear on the A/P invoice line, you cannot reverse the invoice. 

Instead, you can click the Delete link to delete the invoice. 

If an asset is associated with an A/P invoice, the reversal does not delete the asset. If you 

want to delete the asset record, you must do so manually. 

Configuring Reversals for Unpaid A/P Invoices 

To track changes and maintain an audit trail, you can reverse unpaid A/P invoices instead of 

deleting them. Your company can be configured to enable reversal of unpaid A/P invoices, which 

means that a transaction can only be reversed, not deleted, unless it is in Draft or Posted state. 

When you reverse an A/P invoice, the system automatically creates the required adjustment to the 

A/P account targeted in the transaction. If you want to target a different A/P account, you can 

leave the transaction as is and create a manual adjustment. For example, if you create an invoice 

and then learn that you’re never going to receive payment on it, you might want to create a 

manual adjustment that targets a bad-debt A/R Account. 

To enable reversal: 

1. 
Edit your A/P configuration. 

2. 
In the Enable functionality section, select Enable reversal of unpaid A/P invoices. 

Selecting Enable reversal of unpaid A/P invoices changes these pages: 

• 
Accounts Payable: A/P invoices - replaces Delete with Reverse 

• 
Permissions: For A/P invoices, makes Delete a read-only selection

To locate and reverse an unpaid A/P invoice:

Voiding and Reversing a Paid A/P Invoice Simultaneously 

To void and reverse at the same time, start by displaying a register report for the account from 

which the payment was made. Then, you void the payment and reverse the A/P invoice from the 

register report. 

You can wait to reverse the A/P invoice at a later time. To access the A/P invoice to void it later 
on, go to the A/P invoices page and click the Reverse link.

The Reverse option appears only at the level where the invoice was created. If the invoice 

was created at the top level, then navigate to the top level. If the invoice was created at the

depending on the payment type you want to void and reverse.

Select the type of account from which the payment was made.

#### Troubleshooting a Missing Reverse Link for a Transaction (Property Management)
*Source: `RP Accounting AP Daily Tasks User Guide.pdf`, Page 362*

A/P Invoices 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Daily Tasks User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Troubleshooting a Missing Reverse Link for a Transaction (Property Management) 

If you don’t see a Reverse link for a transaction, then it may be that your user account is not 

granted permission for reversals, or you are trying to reverse a transaction that can’t be reversed. 

Check the following: 

• 
Permissions: Make sure that you have the user permissions to reverse this type of 

transaction. Contact your administrator if you are not sure. 

• 
Transaction was already reversed: View the status of the transaction to make sure that it is 

not already reversed.  

• 
Transaction type: Make sure that you are trying to reverse a transaction type that is allowed 

to be reversed. The following are transactions that can be reversed. If you don’t see your 

transaction type in this list, then it can’t be reversed. 

• 
Accounts Payable: A/P invoices and adjustments. 

• 
Accounts Receivable: A/R invoices, adjustments, posted payments, and advances 

(prepayments). 

• 
Cash Management: Charge card transactions (not relating to A/P invoice payments), 

charge payoffs, fund transfers. 

• 
General Ledger: Journal entries. 

• 
Subledger period is closed: Make sure that the subledger period is open for the reversal 

transaction. If the period in which the transaction was created is closed, then you can: 

• 
Open the closed period to reverse the transaction with the original date. 

• 
Reverse the transaction in the current open period. 

• 
Paid transaction: The transaction must be partially or fully paid to reverse it, unless you 

specifically configured your application for reversal of unpaid transactions (on page 340), 

such as A/P invoices, A/R invoices, expenses, or adjustments.  

• 
If the transaction state is Selected, then you need to remove it from the selected state, and 

then reverse the transaction.  

• 
If the transaction state is Partially paid or Paid, then you need to reverse the payment first, 

and then reverse the transaction.

Find the invoice, and then click number in the Paid by column.

Click the Void link. The Void Payment Date box opens. 

7. 
Type the date for the void to be effective. 

8. 
If the Reverse section appears, select the check box of the invoice to reverse, and then enter 

a date in the Reverse as of field.

Click Submit.

#### Creating a Journal Entry to Make an Adjustment to the General Ledger
*Source: `RP Accounting AP Daily Tasks User Guide.pdf`, Page 367*

Chapter 4: A/P Invoices 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Daily Tasks User Guide 

Creating a Journal Entry to Make an Adjustment to the General Ledger 

To create a journal entry to make an adjustment: 

1. 
Open the General Ledger menu. 

2. 
In the Search & Find section of the menu, click 
 next to Journal Entry. 

3. 
In the Posting date field, type the same date as the date of the original G/L record that you 

are fixing. 

4. 
Make the adjusting entries. 

• 
In the Entries section, type the credit amount on the first line to reverse the original 

transaction. 

• 
Type the debit amount in the second line with the correct G/L account to post to the 

correct account.  

Example: 

The original transaction in error is a DEBIT to account 5555 for $100, which should have been a 

DEBIT to account 4444 for $100. 

• 
First line is a CREDIT to account 5555 for $100; this reverses the original transaction. 

• 
Second line is a DEBIT to account 4444 for $100; this posts to the correct account. 

All journal entries must have matching credit/debit amounts before they can be posted.

Reversing a Paid Invoice 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Receivable > All > Payments`


An invoice with a state of Partially paid or Paid has an associated payment. To reverse a paid 

invoice, locate and reverse the payment, and then reverse the invoice. This method works for a 

payment regardless of type, whether it is a cash payment, credit card payment, Paymode-X 

payment, RealPage payment, ACH/EFT/BACS payment, Third Party payment, payment with a 

printed check, payment with a manual check, or a Petty cash reimbursement. 

Alternatively, you can also reverse the invoice during the process of reversing the payment. Learn 

more about reversing a posted payment.  

To reverse a paid invoice requires two steps.  

1. 
Reverse the payment on the invoice. 

2. 
Reverse the invoice. 

Step 1: Reverse the payment on the invoice 

1. 
Open the Accounts receivable menu. 

2. 
Select Payments. The system opens the list of posted payments. 

3. 
In the list of Posted Payments, click Reverse beside the appropriate row. The Transaction 

Reversal Date box opens.  

4. 
Review the reversal date and memo, making any changes you might need.  

• 
Reverse the transaction on date: Select the date for reversing the transaction. This is 

usually the original transaction date or a later date.  

• 
Memo: We recommend that you enter the reason for the reversal.  

5. 
Click Submit.  

The system retains the original payment transaction and creates a new transaction that 

essentially zeros out the payment, which provides an audit trail. Now the invoice has no 

payment associated with it. You can reverse it.

### Packaging Invoices
*Source: `RP Accounting AP Daily Tasks User Guide.pdf`, Page 370*

A/P Invoices 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Daily Tasks User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Packaging Invoices 

This section describes how to create a package of invoices. You can create a package of A/P or 

A/R invoices. 

Use this feature when you need to provide a set of invoices to another party. Many customers use 

this feature to create a package of invoices for stakeholders. Customers who do not own the Job 

Cost and Reserves application can use the packaging feature to collect a set of invoices for the 

draw request document bundle, which they then submit to the lender as a request to release 

funds. 

When you generate the package, you can specify the components that you want to include in the 

package: 

• 
Cover page: Include a cover page and either use the system default cover page or import a 

custom cover page. 

• 
Summary: This is a list of the invoices in the package. 

• 
Attachments: Include the attachments of the invoices in the package. 

• 
Printed invoice: For A/R invoice packages, you can include the A/R invoices in printable 

format. 

• 
Printed AP invoice: For A/P invoice packages, you can include the A/P invoices in printable 

format. 

• 
Payment information: For A/P invoice packages, you can include additional payment 

information. 

• 
Proof of payment: For A/P invoice packages, you can include the proof of payment 

information when it is available. 

• 
Include separator pages: You can choose to include or exclude pages between the invoices. 

The separator page contains this text “The following invoices are included in this package:” 

and it lists the invoices in the package with these details: vendor name, invoice number, 

invoice date, amount of the payment, payment method, payment number, and the number 

of documents associated with the invoice.  

Packaging the invoices does not change the status of the invoices or their presence in the 
invoices list. 

If you are packaging A/P invoices, you have the choice of saving the package of invoices in a ZIP 

file or a printable PDF file.  

A/R invoice packages are saved as PDF files and open in Adobe Acrobat after the system creates 

the package.  

Regardless of file format, the system saves the package in your browser’s default download 

location.  

---



#### Creating A/P Invoice Packages

Creating A/P Invoice Packages

Invoices`

Use the Package invoices button when you want to bundle a set of invoices. You can package 

invoices from the A/P invoices list or from the Spend Management workbench. 

To create an invoice package: 

1. 
Click the Package invoices button. The page name changes to reflect that it has entered 

packaging mode. 

2. 
Filter the list so that the invoices that you want to package are displayed in the list. 

For example, you can use the A/P invoice list’s filters to help you find the invoices to include 

in the package. Each box above the column is a filter. Enter the text that you want to find in 

a column to find matching A/P invoices. You can also apply a custom view that you 

previously saved to get a list of A/P invoices that you want to package.  

Likewise, on the workbench, you can use the workbench controls to filter the list of invoices. 

For example, the column control lets you filter the data in the column. Click the Clear button 

to reset filters, including the column filters. 

3. 
Select the invoices to include in the package. 

After you select at least one invoice, check boxes appear to the left of the Edit links in the 

list, and three buttons appear: 

• 
Show Only Selected Invoices 

• 
Generate Package 

• 
Cancel Package 

While in packaging mode, you can also create new A/P invoices. If your company uses the 
approval workflow, then the system sends the new A/P invoice through the approval 
process before you can include it in the package. You must also go through the process of 
posting and paying the invoice before it can be included in an A/P invoice package.

Showing Only Selected Invoices 

• 
Click the Show Only Selected Invoices button to remove unselected A/P invoices from the 

list so that you see only the invoices that will be included in the package. This action cannot 

be undone. If you accidentally exclude an A/P invoice, you must cancel the package and 

start over. 

Generating the Package 

1. 
Click the Generate Package button to open the Generate Invoice Package box. 

2. 
In the Package Option drop-down list, select the type of package that you want to create, 

Document (PDF) or Compressed (Zip). 

3. 
Finalize the package by selecting what to include in the package in addition to the invoices. 

You can choose to include: 

• 
Cover page: Select this check box, and then click the Browse button to find and select 

the cover page that you want to use. 

• 
Summary: Select this check box to include a summarized list of invoices in the 

package. 

• 
Attachments: Select this check box to include any attachments that the invoice records 

might have in the package. 

• 
Printed A/P invoice: Select this check box to include a printable version of the invoice. 

• 
Payment information: Select this check box to include additional payment information 

in the package. 

• 
Proof of payment: Select this check box to include proofs of payment when they are 

available. 

• 
Include separator pages: Select this check box if you want the system to include a 

separator page between each invoice. The separator page contains this text “The 

document(s) that follow are for:” and then lists the details about the invoice that 

follows, including Vendor ID, Vendor Name, Invoice Number, Invoice Date, and Invoice 

Amount.  

4. 
Click the Build package button to create the package. The system downloads the file to 

your browser’s default download location. If you selected PDF, the system opens the file in 

Adobe Acrobat. 

Canceling the Package 

• 
Click the Cancel package button to discard the package and return to the A/P invoices list 

or Spend Management workbench.

Downloading the A/P Invoice Template 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > Import data`


Templates are used for importing data into the system. Each type of data has a unique template 

designed for that data object. When your system was set up, RealPage worked with your 

company to design each template so that the import of data includes all of the fields that your 

company wants uploaded when importing. 

The purpose of downloading a template is so that you can fill the template with the data that you 

want to import into the system. For example, if you want to import A/P invoice data, then you 

download the A/P invoice template, fill it with data, and them import the A/P invoice template. 

If your goal is to create one invoice and reuse it as the starting point for additional invoices, use 
the Duplicate function instead of a template. 

To find and download the template for A/P invoice data: 

1. 
Open the Company menu. 

2. 
Click Import data. 

3. 
Find the Set Up AP Master List, Open Invoices and Adjustments section. 

4. 
Find the Accounts Payable Invoices row, and then select the Template link. A prompt opens 

at the bottom of the browser page asking if you want to Open, Save, or Cancel. 

• 
Open: Opens the file in Excel. 

• 
Save: Saves the file to your local computer. 

• 
Save as: Saves the file under a new name and in a different location. 

• 
Save and Open: Saves the file to your local computer, and then opens the file in Excel. 

5. 
Click Save.

*Source: `RP Accounting AP Daily Tasks User Guide.pdf`, Page 375*

Filling In the Template with Data and Saving as CSV 

Filling In the Template 

To fill in the A/P invoice template: 

1. 
Open the template in Excel and review the data structure. This information can help you 

formulate extraction queries from your data source. 

2. 
Export the data from your other system. 

3. 
Paste the exported data into the template file for the object. Take care to match the 

template’s data structure exactly as you do this. 

Avoid using leading zeros in ID fields. If you must use leading zeros in IDs, convert the 
column of ID numbers to text format in Excel before importing the file content. Excel does 
not remove the leading zeros when you save the file. Remember to do this every time you 
use a template to import information that requires IDs. 

Saving the File 

In Excel: 

1. 
Click File and then select Save As. 

2. 
Click Browse and select where you want to save the file. 

3. 
In File name, type a name that represents the data that the template contains. 

4. 
In Save as type, select CSV (Comma delimited) (*.csv). 

5. 
Click the Save button.

When you click the Package Invoices button, you enter into Packaging mode. If you choose 

another option from the menu and then return to invoices, the system displays the Package 

Invoices list, not the Invoices list. In other words, the invoices list will still be in Packaging mode. 

To return to the invoices list from the Package Invoices list, you can either generate the package 

or cancel the package. 

• 
When you generate a package, the system builds the package and saves it where your 

browser saves downloaded files, and then returns to the Invoices list. 

• 
You can cancel the current package, which leaves Packaging mode and returns to the 

invoice. 

Troubleshooting PDFs 

When you have trouble opening a PDF file, try the following: 

• 
Make sure that you are running the latest version of Adobe Reader or Adobe Acrobat. 

• 
Repair program installation. 

• 
Disable the Protected mode at startup. 

• 
Revert to an earlier version for non-compliant PDFs.

A/P Invoice Page 


> **Navigation Path:** `Accounts Payable > All > Search & Find > A/P Invoices`


Use the A/P invoice page to add a new A/P invoice and view and edit an existing A/P invoice. 

After creating the invoice, you can: 

• 
Duplicate the invoice. Click the Duplicate button. 

• 
Print the invoice. Click the Print button. 

• 
Pay the invoice. Click the Pay button. 

• 
Reclassify the invoice. Click the Reclassify button.  

If the button does not appear at the top left, then you cannot reclassify this transaction. 

• 
Post the invoice to the General ledger. Click the Post button. 

• 
Create a recurring transaction based on the invoice. Click the More actions button and then 

select Create recurring transaction. 

• 
View the invoice’s audit trail. Click the More actions button and then select View audit trail. 

• 
View a breakdown of the total balance due to the vendor. Click the Vendor ID balance link 

at the top of the page. 

• 
Associate documents with this invoice and view the attached documents. 

• 
In the OPS section, you can view the approval workflow of an invoice when your system is 

integrated with OPSTechnology. 

• 
In the OPS Attachments section, you can click the URL to view the eInvoice and any 

attachments associated with the eInvoice. This section appears when the invoice type is 

eInvoice or oInvoice. 

In the Invoice Entries section, you can: 

• 
View the available budget (on page 409) for the property. Click the Spend control button. 

• 
Add default values for the invoice entries list. Click the Show defaults link. 

• 
Apply A/P allocations to the invoice. Click the Apply A/P allocation button.  

• 
Save the A/P allocations. Click the Save A/P allocation button. 

• 
Define an allocation split. Click Show details. 

• 
Customize the allocation. Click Show details and then click the Customize allocation 

button. 

• 
Select one or more segment type and segment values to associate with the A/P invoice. 

• 
Use fields shared by Spend Management to help you match the A/P invoice to a purchase 

order. The shared fields include Account code description, Qty, UOM, Price, and Extended 

price.

The A/P Invoice page can have up to eight sections: 

• 
At the top is the vendor name, vendor ID in parentheses, and the vendor’s balance, the total 

amount that you owe to the vendor. This section appears only after you have saved the 

invoice. 

• 
The banner section shows basic information about the A/P invoice so that you can find it 

quickly. This section appears only after you have saved the invoice. 

• 
The Date section (so-called because the first field in the section is the Date field) contains 

most of the important information about the A/P invoice.  

• 
The Term section contains further details about the invoice. 

• 
The next section can contain custom fields requested by your company. Consult your 

System Administrator for details. 

• 
The Documents section contains documents related to this A/P invoice. Use this section to 

attach documents, scan documents and to view the attached documents. 

• 
The Currency section appears if your system is multi-currency enabled.  

• 
The Invoice entries section contains the line items that are covered by this A/P invoice.  

The A/P Invoice record can have up to three tabs: 

• 
A/P invoice: This tab contains the essential components of the invoice,  

• 
Messaging: This tab allows you to send a message (on page 374) about this invoice to 

another system user, to an external email address, or to the vendor associated with the A/P 

invoice. 

• 
Header: This tab contains any custom fields that the property management company wants 

to track.

*Source: `RP Accounting AP Daily Tasks User Guide.pdf`, Page 386*

A/P Invoices 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Daily Tasks User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Duplicating an A/P Invoice 

Sometimes it is easier and faster to add a record by duplicating an existing one, and editing the 

duplicate than creating a new record from scratch. You can view and access a list of invoices from 

the A/P Invoices list. 

To duplicate an A/P invoice: 

1. 
Open the Accounts Payable menu. 

2. 
In the Search & Find section, select A/P Invoices. The list of A/P invoices opens. 

3. 
On the A/P invoices list, find the invoice that you want to copy, and then click Edit. The 

system displays the A/P invoice page with its invoice details. 

4. 
Click the Duplicate button. The system opens the copy of the invoice. 

5. 
Change the date in the invoice and change other data as needed. 

6. 
Save the invoice as a draft or post it. 

Saving a Transaction in Draft Format 

You can save a transaction as a draft when you are not ready to post it. 

You can save it as a draft without affecting the G/L or any subledger. With the ability to save A/P 

invoices, A/R invoices, and adjustments in draft state, you can save your progress so far. You or 

another user can come back later and post the transaction.  

Prerequisite: Your ability to add a transaction in draft state or post a transaction depends on your 

permissions: 

• 
Add permission enables you to add, edit, delete, and save a transaction as a draft. 

• 
Edit permission enables you to edit, delete, and save a transaction as draft. 

• 
Post permission enables you to post the transaction when you’re ready. 

To save a transaction in draft format: 

1. 
Add a transaction (an A/P invoice, A/R invoice, or adjustment). 

2. 
Click the Draft button. A drop-down list displays with these options.  

3. 
Select one of the options:  

• 
Draft & New: Select this option to have the system save the transaction but not post it, 

and then open a new blank transaction.  

• 
Draft: Select this option to have the system save the transaction but not post it, and 

then close the page. 

• 
Draft & Continue: Select this option to save the transaction and continue working on 

it.

Setting Default Line-Item Values 

Setting default values is a time-saver when you need to fill in a long list of line items. 

To set a default value for a line-item field: 

1. 
In the Entries section of a transaction’s page, click the Show defaults link. 

The area expands to display all fields for which you can set defaults. The type of fields that 

appear here depend on your company setup. For example, if you’ve enabled standard 

dimensions, or created and deployed user-defined dimensions, multi-currency processing 

fields, or revenue-recognition fields, then you can set default values for them here. 

2. 
Click the drop-down arrow for any field that frequently uses the same value, and then select 

that value. 

3. 
Click the Apply defaults button above the first line item. 

The value that you selected appears on every line or in the line-item detail of every line, 

depending on where the field is located. 

You can override the default value by selecting a different value or typing over the text. 

4. 
Optionally, click the Hide defaults link to hide the defaults section after you have applied 

them to the list. 

Example 

In this example, the user chooses to set up a default value for the Location column in the Entries 

list. 

a) Select the location that you want the system to complete for you. 

b) Click the Apply defaults button. 

c) The system completes the Location column with your selected location.

Click the Draft button to save the A/P invoice without posting it. 

Adding a Recurring A/P Invoice Based on an Existing Invoice 

To use an existing A/P invoice as the basis for a recurring A/P invoice: 

1. 
Open the Accounts payable menu. 

2. 
In the Search & Find section, select A/P invoices.  

3. 
Find the A/P invoice you want to use as the basis for a recurring A/P invoice, and then click 

Edit. 

4. 
Click the More Actions button, and then select Create recurring transaction. 

5. 
If the Leave site? message appears, click Leave. The Recurring invoice page opens. 

Filling In the A/P Invoice Details 

1. 
Enter details about the A/P invoice. Required fields include: 

• 
Vendor: Choose the vendor you’re paying. 

• 
A/P invoice sequence number: If your Accounts Payable preferences have been set up 

to require A/P invoice numbers, choose a numbering sequence that the system can 

use to automatically generate invoice numbers for recurring A/P invoices. 

• 
Term: Choose the A/P terms that the vendor extends to you. If you chose a default A/P 

term on the vendor’s record, this will be completed by the system. You can also add a 

new A/P term. 

• 
Line item details: For each line item on the A/P invoice, select the G/L account and 

enter the amount. You may also want to pick the department, location, and segment 

or specify other dimensional information. 

2. 
Add or edit any other information as needed, just as you would for a regular A/P invoice. 

Information such as the reference number, description, or contract ID can be used for 

searching and reporting on the A/P invoice later on. 

3. 
(Optional) If you need to specify different Ship To or Return To information for the vendor, 

you can do so on the Additional Information tab. 

4. 
The Vendor and Term on the Additional Information and Schedule tabs are for reference 

only. You can edit them only from the A/P invoice tab. 

5. 
On the Schedule tab, indicate when the first A/P invoice should be created, how often it 

should be repeated, and when it should expire.

Placing A/P Invoices On Hold 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > All > A/P invoices > Edit > Place This Invoice On 
Hold`


When an A/P invoice is on hold, the system does not display the A/P invoice in the Approve 

Payments list or Pay A/P invoices page. However, the system does display the A/P invoice in 

reports such as the A/P invoice register. 

To place an A/P invoice on hold: 

1. 
Open the Accounts payable menu. 

2. 
Select A/P invoices. The A/P invoices list opens. 

3. 
In the A/P invoices list, find the A/P invoice you want to place on hold, and click Edit. 

4. 
In the Term section, select the Place this invoice on hold check box. 

5. 
Click the Submit button. 

The check box is unavailable when you open the invoice with the 
View link instead of the Edit 
link. This option is also unavailable when the invoice has already been paid. 

Removing an A/P Invoice from Being On Hold 

Before you begin, if the A/P invoice is from a prior period, make sure to open the books for the 

invoice period. 

To take an invoice off hold: 

1. 
Open the invoice using the Edit link. 

2. 
Clear the Place invoice on hold check box. 

3. 
Save the invoice.  

Now you can pay the invoice.  

If you are having trouble editing an invoice, see Editing A/P Invoices (on page 303).

Sending a Message Regarding an A/P Invoice

> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > All > Invoice Research > (search) > Edit > Messaging`


You can send a message about an A/P invoice to other system users, to external users, and to 

vendors. To send the message to the vendor, the vendor’s email address must be defined in the 

Vendor record.

5. 
Choose who will receive the message: 

• 
To send the message to someone who has an account in the system, click the To 

drop-down list, and then select the desired user.

not send the email. You can either edit the vendor record, add an email address to it, 
and then try again, or type the vendor’s email address in the External user email field. 

• 
To send the message to someone who does not have an account in the system, type 

the person’s email address in the External user email field.  

• 
To send emails to multiple addresses, type the addresses in the External user email 

field and separate email addresses with a comma. Do not add spaces between email 

addresses.

table.

Fields

List Controls

A/P Invoices List

view of the list, you can add a custom view using the Manage views > Create new view. 

Columns 

Select (check box) 
Use these check boxes to select invoices that you want to include in an 

invoice package. When you select a check box, the package invoice 

mode begins.  

Edit (link) 
Opens the A/P invoice so that you can change it. 

The Edit option is not available when you do not have access to all 
locations in the invoice. This means that your company has multiple 
entities, and you are not allowed to view activities between entities to 
which you do not have access.  

View (link) 
Opens the A/P invoice so that you can review the details. 

Vendor name 
This column contains the name of the vendor who is the source of the

Invoice number 
This column contains the record number assigned to the A/P invoice by

the check itself. 

Date

Hold 
This column contains a check mark when someone has placed the A/P 

invoice on hold.

Amount 

Base Amount 

Transaction amount 

This column contains the actual amount of the transaction for this item 

in a single-currency company. 

If you’ve enabled multi-currency, the system displays Base Amount and 

Transaction Amount in place of Amount. 

Base Amount is the amount of the item in the base currency of your 

company. 

Transaction amount is the amount of the item in the currency you set 

for the A/P invoice. 

For example, if your base currency is USD and you create a 100 Euro A/P 

invoice, for the A/P invoice Line Item, you see the A/P invoice with 100 

Euro as the Transaction amount and 110 USD as the Base Amount 

(assuming a 1.1 exchange rate from Euro to USD). 

Transaction type 
This column contains the type of invoice: 

• 
A/P invoice: Regular A/P invoices 

• 
eInvoice: A system-generated A/P invoice created by Spend 

Management Storefront. 

• 
oInvoice: A system-generated A/P invoice created by Full 

Service.  

Base currency 
This column indicates what the base currency is for this entity. 

This field appears only when your company is a multi-currency company. 

State 
This column contains the current part of the processing cycle for the A/P 

invoice. How much you can edit an A/P invoice, or delete or reverse it, 

depends on its state. 

• 
Draft: The A/P invoice is created, but not posted. It can be 

changed without consequence. 

• 
Posted: The A/P invoice was posted to the G/L. 

• 
Selected: The A/P invoice is now selected for payment. 

• 
Paid: Vendor payment was made. 

• 
Partially Paid: Only a partial payment was made. There is a 

remaining amount to be paid. 

• 
Reversed: The A/P invoice was reversed by a second transaction, 

which essentially zeroed out the balance in the GL. Your 

company retains a record of the reversed A/P invoice and the 

reversal transaction for audit trail purposes. 

• 
Reversal: This transaction is created when you reverse a 

transaction and causes the balance to zero out.

• 
No value: This transaction is posted but has not affected the 

General ledger.  

Summary title 
This column contains the name of the summary that include this A/P 

invoice. A summary is a collection of same type transactions, grouped 

together for same-time processing.  

Payment method 
This column contains the payment method used to pay this A/P invoice.  

Payment number

The presence and order of fields can differ based on how you open a record (Add, Edit, or View)

### Using Discounts
*Source: `RP Accounting AP Daily Tasks User Guide.pdf`, Page 421*



#### Applying a Discount to One Line Item
*Source: `RP Accounting AP Daily Tasks User Guide.pdf`, Page 421*

Chapter 4: A/P Invoices 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Daily Tasks User Guide 

Using Discounts 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > All > A/P invoices > Add/Edit`


Use the Discount Amount field on the A/P Invoice page to apply a discount. 

You can distribute a discount across a transaction, or apply a discount to a specific line item in a 

transaction.  

You can also set up a discount for a particular customer or vendor by building the discount into 

the term. For example, set up a term that specifies when a customer pays the invoice within ten 

days of receiving it, then they will get a 10% discount. These discounts apply when paying the 

invoice, causing the price to change. 

Applying a Discount to One Line Item 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > All > A/P Invoice > Edit`


To apply a discount to a line item: 

1. 
Open the Accounts Payable menu. 

2. 
Select the A/P invoices option. 

3. 
Click the Edit link of the invoice that you want to open. 

4. 
In the Invoice entries section of an A/P invoice, find the item to which you want to add a 

discount. 

5. 
Click the row. The Show details tab opens. 

6. 
Click the Show details tab. The Details section opens. 

7. 
In the TAX/SHIPPING section, type the discount amount in the Discount field. The amount 

must be a positive number. The amount that you enter reduces the total amount due. 

---


<!-- Page 422 -->
A/P Invoices 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Daily Tasks User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

After applying the discount to the line item, you can: 

• 
Continue to edit the line item’s details. 

• 
Click the Hide details tab to close the Details section. 

• 
Click the Post button to post the A/P invoice to the General Ledger. 

• 
Click the Draft button to save the A/P invoice without posting it. 

---



#### Applying a Discount Across a Transaction
*Source: `RP Accounting AP Daily Tasks User Guide.pdf`, Page 423*

Chapter 4: A/P Invoices 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Daily Tasks User Guide 

Applying a Discount Across a Transaction 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > All > A/P Invoice > Edit`


To apply a discount to the entire transaction: 

1. 
Open the Accounts Payable menu. 

2. 
Select the A/P invoices option. 

3. 
Open the A/P invoice to which you want to apply a discount. 

4. 
In the Discount amount field located below the Invoice entries section, type the discount 

amount. 

5. 
Click the Distribute button. The system equally distributes the discount across all of line 

items in the A/P invoice. 

After applying the discount to the transaction, you can: 

• 
Click the Post button to post the A/P invoice to the General Ledger. 

• 
Click the Draft button to save the A/P invoice without posting it.

#### Reclassifying Invoices
*Source: `RP Accounting AP Daily Tasks User Guide.pdf`, Page 432*

A/P Invoices 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Daily Tasks User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Reclassifying Invoices 

Reclassification typically happens when an invoice was coded to a valid but incorrect G/L account 

— meaning the expense or revenue was recorded in the wrong category. The goal is to move it to 

the right account without changing the total amount or vendor record. 

Typical examples of reclassification include: 

• 
Reclassify a Utilities Expense to Repairs & Maintenance when the charge was for equipment 

servicing rather than usage. 

• 
Reclassify Rental income to Other income for non-rent charges such as late fees. 

• 
Reclassify Security Deposits Payable to Tenant Refunds Payable when the deposit was 

returned. 

What You Can Reclassify 

You can reclassify A/R and A/P invoices and adjustments. 

• 
Reclassifying an A/R invoice enables you to change how revenues are assigned for an 

invoice that was paid or partially paid.  

• 
Reclassifying an A/P invoice enables you to change how expenses are assigned for an A/P 

invoice that was paid or partially paid.  

For example, when you reclassify an A/P invoice, you could assign line items to different G/L 

accounts, or change the department, location, or other dimensions. 

When to Reclassify 

Consider reclassifying a transaction:  

• 
When the transaction is initially recorded in the wrong account. 

• 
When there’s a change in the accounting period. 

• 
When adjustments are needed to reflect the proper allocation of revenue or expenses. This 

ensures that financial statements accurately represent the company’s financial position and 

comply with accounting standards.  

Who Can Reclassify 

Only users who have special permission can reclassify invoices. They can edit accounting 

information on both partially and fully paid invoices. You can update almost anything on the A/P 

invoice except for the amount and the payment date. For example, if the A/P invoice was assigned 

to the wrong department, you can choose a different department from the drop-down menu. 

---

Accessing the Reclassify Function 

In the Financial Suite, you can reclassify a single invoice or adjustment, or you can reclassify 

several invoices or adjustments at the same time 

You can reclassify a single invoice or adjustment from the A/R Invoices or A/P invoices lists. Edit 

the invoice that you want to reclassify and click the Reclassify button. See Reclassifying an Invoice 

(on page 416). 

You can reclassify multiple transactions at the same time using the Invoice Reclassification menu 

option. See Reclassifying Multiple Invoices. 

Things to Keep in Mind When Reclassifying Transactions 

• 
Do not change the transaction total or vendor. 

• 
Always add a memo that explains why you reclassified the transaction. 

Before You Begin

not see the option in the menu, then ask your System Administrator to check your permissions.

2. 
Select the Setup tab. 

3. 
Select Configuration. 

4. 
In the Enable functionality section, select the Enable reclassification for invoices and 

adjustments check box.

#### Saving a Transaction in Draft Format
*Source: `RP Accounting AP Daily Tasks User Guide.pdf`, Page 441*

Chapter 4: A/P Invoices

RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Daily Tasks User Guide 

Saving a Transaction in Draft Format 

You can save a transaction as a draft when you are not ready to post it. 

You can save it as a draft without affecting the G/L or any subledger. With the ability to save A/P 

invoices, A/R invoices, and adjustments in draft state, you can save your progress so far. You or 

another user can come back later and post the transaction.  

Prerequisite: Your ability to add a transaction in draft state or post a transaction depends on your 

permissions: 

• 
Add permission enables you to add, edit, delete, and save a transaction as a draft. 

• 
Edit permission enables you to edit, delete, and save a transaction as draft. 

• 
Post permission enables you to post the transaction when you’re ready. 

To save a transaction in draft format: 

1. 
Add a transaction (an A/P invoice, A/R invoice, or adjustment). 

2. 
Click the Draft button. A drop-down list displays with these options.  

3. 
Select one of the options:  

• 
Draft & New: Select this option to have the system save the transaction but not post it, 

and then open a new blank transaction.  

• 
Draft: Select this option to have the system save the transaction but not post it, and 

then close the page. 

• 
Draft & Continue: Select this option to save the transaction and continue working on 

it.

#### Voiding a Payment from the Invoice
*Source: `RP Accounting AP Daily Tasks User Guide.pdf`, Page 443*

Chapter 4: A/P Invoices 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Daily Tasks User Guide 

Voiding a Payment from the Invoice 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > All > A/P Invoices > Edit/View > Void Payment`


You can void a payment from the invoice.  

For the Void Payment button to appear, the payment must have been made for the single invoice 

rather than a payment that covers multiple invoices.  

You cannot void payments when the payment method is RealPage Payment. 

To void a payment from an invoice: 

1. 
Go to the level where the payment was made. If it was paid at the entity level, go to the 

entity level.  

2. 
Open the desired A/P invoice. You can only void the payment if the A/P invoice has a status 

of Paid. 

3. 
Click the Void payment button. The Void payment date box opens. 

4. 
Type the date that you want to void the payment in the Void the payment on date field. 

5. 
Type the reason for voiding the payment in the Memo field.  

6. 
Click Submit.  

What’s next? 

• 
Create an adjustment (on page 829) to accommodate the voided payment.

This topic describes how to create an A/P invoice as if every possible feature is enabled. Your 

experience of this page will differ depending on the features that your system has enabled. 

Variations occur due to system configuration, your permissions, and your company’s installation 

of other RealPage Financial Suite applications. For instructions on importing A/P invoices, see 

Importing A/P Invoices (on page 252). 

Applications that Affect the Fields on A/P Invoice Records 

• 
Spend Management 

• 
Job Cost  

Configuration Differences that Affect the Fields on A/P Invoice Records 

• 
When your system is configured to use multiple currencies, additional currency fields appear 

in this record. See the multi-currency systems section on the General Ledger configuration 

page. 

• 
When the Intercompany billing option is enabled (Accounts Receivable configuration), the 

A/R Invoice Dimensions section appears. 

• 
When your system is integrated with OpsTechnology, it allows RealPage Accounting to 

receive eInvoices. 

• 
Accounts Payable configuration:  

• 
When the Enable bank account selection in A/P invoice option is selected (Accounts 

Payable configuration), it causes the Bank account field to appear on the A/P invoice 

record. 

• 
When the Enable invoice entry control validation option is selected (Accounts 

Payable configuration), it causes the Total invoice amount field to appear on the A/P 

invoice record. 

• 
When Spend management is enabled, then the Match Order button appears, allowing you 

to match a purchase order to the A/P invoice. Additional fields appear on the record such as 

QTY, Price, Extended Price, UOM, and Account code description. 

---

• 
When Job Cost is enabled, the Line Entry Type section appears. When you select Include Job 

cost, the system adds Job cost-specific columns in the Invoice Entries list such as Job name, 

Cost code, and Job unit.  

• 
When scanning is enabled, the Attachments field is replaced with the Documents section, 

affecting the way that you attach documents.  

• 
If the Please complete one-time setup scanner prompt appears, follow the 

instructions in Downloading the Scanning Software. If you do not plan to scan 

supporting documents at this time, you can skip the download by clicking the X in 

upper-right corner of the box.  

• 
If you enabled the Single scan upload feature in your preferences and have previously 

downloaded the Dynamsoft scanning software, you may be prompted to update the 

software when you add a new scannable record such as an A/P invoice, vendor, 

purchase order, or service contract, or scan a document into the document dashboard. 

When this occurs, download the new software. There is no need to uninstall the 

previous version. 

•

To create an A/P invoice: 

1. 
In the Date field, type the date of the invoice, or leave it set to today’s date.  

Any date entered here is automatically filled in the G/L posting date field (and to the 

Exchange rate date field if you’re a multi-currency company). You can change either date as 

needed; for example, if you want to create the adjustment today, but post it on a different 

date. 

2. 
In the G/L posting date field, type the date that you want the A/P invoice to post on the 

general ledger.  

3. 
In the Total invoice amount field, type the amount of the invoice.  

This field appears only when the Enable invoice entry control validation check box is 

selected on the configuration page of Accounts Payable. When enabled, this is a required 

field.  

4. 
In the Vendor drop-down list, select an existing vendor or add a new vendor, as required. 

The system completes the Pay to and Return to fields automatically based on the vendor 

record that you select. This is a required field. 

To add a new vendor, you must be at the top level. You can use the field-level controls to 

add a new vendor, view a vendor’s record, or find a vendor’s record. 

The system fills in the Pay to field automatically. If you need to change the Pay to contact, 

you can do that here. In the Pay to drop-down list, select the name of the person to whom 

the payment should be sent. 

The system fills in the Return to field automatically. If you need to change the Return to 

contact, you can do that here. In the Return to drop-down list, select the name of the 

person to whom returns should be addressed.  

5. 
To fill in the A/P invoice form with data from the last A/P invoice from this vendor, click the 

Populate from last A/P invoice button.  

6. 
In the Invoice number field, type the invoice number. This is a required field. 

7. 
Type a Reference number. Reference numbers can be a vendor’s number that they use to 

track the payment.  

8. 
Type a Description of the transaction.  

You can also use the Reference number and Description fields to enter specific 
information that a vendor requires. Sometimes, a vendor requires a specific piece of 
information to reconcile your payments, such as a customer account number or a pin 
number. 

---


<!-- Page 452 -->

RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Daily Tasks User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

9. 
Select the Corporate invoice check box if you want to prevent this invoice from appearing 

in Spend Management’s Site Experience. 

10. 
If your company uses the Spend Management application for purchase orders: 

• 
Click the Match order button. 

• 
In the Match orders box, click the View details link. 

• 
In the Contract details section that appears below, select the service order for which 

you want to create an A/P invoice. 

• 
Click Apply. 

Make the Invoice Recurring 

1. 
Select the Make recurring check box to turn this invoice into a recurring invoice. When you 

submit the A/P invoice, the system creates a recurring A/P invoice based on the current 

invoice. When you select this check box, the Schedules section appears.  

2. 
In the Schedules section, fill in the A/P invoice start date field with the date that you want 

the system to start creating the recurring A/P invoices. 

3. 
Select the sequence number scheme from the AP invoice sequence number drop-down list. 

4. 
In the Ending on drop-down list, select: 

• 
Never: To keep the invoice perpetually running, select Never. This is common for A/P 

invoices for ongoing services that have a set price. 

• 
Number of occurrences: The End after field appears. To have the invoice run for a 

limited number of times, type the number of times you want the invoice to recur in the 

End after field. This setting is often used for debts that are being paid over time. 

Setting the number of occurrences eliminates the possibility of making payments after 

the debt is paid off. 

• 
End date: To have the invoice recur until a specific date, select End date and then, in 

the End on field, type the date on which the last invoice is to recur.  

---

5. 
In the Posting repeat by drop-down list, select the frequency that you want the system to 

generate the recurring A/P invoices. The options are: 

• 
None 

• 
Days 

• 
Weeks 

• 
Months 

• 
Years 

6. 
In the Every field, type the number of time frames to repeat by. For example, if you selected 

Months, then type the number of months to repeat by, such as 6 to have the system bill 

every 6 months. 

7. 
If you selected Months, then you can select the End of month check box to have the invoice 

created at the end of the month. 

8. 
Type the email address of the person to whom to send notifications about the recurring 

invoice in the Email field. 

Creating a Future Draft Invoice 

1. 
Select the Create future draft invoice on check box. A date field appears below the check 

box. 

2. 
Type the date that you want the system to create the future draft invoice.  

When you submit the A/P invoice, the system creates a draft invoice with a posting date set 

for the future date and containing the details of the source A/P invoice.  

The system sends you an email as a reminder on the day before the future draft invoice 
date is to be automatically posted.

1. 
Select the terms of payment in the Term drop-down list. If you selected the Make recurring 

check box, the Term field is required. 

2. 
In the Recommended to pay on field, click the 
 Calendar button and then select the 

date by which to pay the invoice. 

3. 
In the Attachments field, you can attach any documents related to the invoice. The system

If you have enabled the single scan feature in your preferences, then the Attachments field 
does not appear. See the Documents section for instructions on attaching documents to 
the A/P invoice. 

• 
You can also click the Add option to create a new folder. Type a name and description 

for the folder, and then select its Parent folder.

Filling In the A/P Invoice Entries 

The Invoice entries list varies depending on your selection of Line entry type: Standard or

• 
When you select Standard, you can fill in the standard fields in the Invoice entries list.

Selecting default values is one method of speeding up data entry. Use this section to choose the 

values that you want the system to complete for you in the Entries list. (optional)

Click the Show defaults link to expand the area.

2.
