Entering the Line-Item Details 

The order in which the line-item columns appear varies from system to system. Some columns 

can be missing when your company chooses not to enable features such as allocations, segments, 

and assets. 

1. 
Select the Location (Location area). The location determines the accounts that appear in the 

Accounts drop-down list. The chart type associated with the property determines the 

accounts in the list. For the A/P invoice to be posted, you must specify at least the account 

and an amount for each line item. For more information see Chart types in the online help 

system or download the RealPage Accounting General Ledger Setup User Guide.  

2. 
In the Account column (or Account label column if you enabled A/P account labels), select 

an account to categorize the expense. Type any part of the G/L account name or number to 

have the system find it. 

If this account is flagged as 1099, or is set up as a 1099 account, you can select the 1099 

check box for individual line items. At the year’s end, the system sums up all of the Form 

1099 items for inclusion in the Form 1099. 

You can use the field-level controls to add a new G/L account, view a G/L account’s record, 
or find a G/L account’s record. To add or import G/L accounts, you must be at the top level. 

3. 
Select the No tax check box when the item is not taxable. 

4. 
In the QTY field, type the quantity of this item that you purchased. This field appears only 

when your system is enabled with Spend management. 

5. 
In the Price field, type the price of one item. This field appears only when your system is 

enabled with Spend management. 

6. 
In the Extended price field, the system fills in the field by calculating the quantity by the 

price. This field appears only when your system is enabled with Spend management. 

7. 
In the Amount field, type the cost of the item. The system requires this field to be 

populated, even if the amount is zero (0). If your system is enabled with Spend 

management, then this field is filled in automatically. 

If your system is enabled for multiple currencies, type the Transaction amount, which is the 
cost of the item expressed in the currency used in the transaction. The system calculates 
the Base amount in your company’s base currency using the exchange rate listed in the 
header. 

8. 
In the Customer column, select a customer to associate with the line item. 

9. 
In the Project column, select the project to associate with the line item. 

10. 
In the Allocation column, select an allocation template for the line item. The system 

automatically distributes the amount of the A/P invoice across the specified dimensions. 

---

Click the Show details tab and then click the Customize allocation button to set their

11. 
In the Discount field, if the item is discounted, type the discount amount.

System Checks for Budget Exceeded  

If you try to post an A/P invoice that exceeds the default budget, and your company uses the A/P 

invoice approval process with the budget exceeded feature, the system displays a warning. The 

system may also prevent you from posting the A/P invoice. If you want to be able to bypass this 

budget check, ask your system administrator to grant you the desired bypass permission. Bypass 

permissions are available for A/P invoices and purchase orders. 

When the budget exceeded feature is enabled, the system checks the A/P invoice amount against 

the budgeted number for the G/L account. When the amount exceeds the budget, then the 

system either displays a warning or prevents you from saving the A/P invoice, depending on how 

your company configured the feature. When preventing an A/P invoice from being posted, the 

system also displays a warning to let you know why you cannot post. 

To enable or disable the budget exceeded feature, see Setting a system action when an A/P 

invoice or purchase order exceeds the budget (on page 568).  

System Checks for Attachments 

Your company may require that you attach a document to support the A/P invoice before you can 

save it as a draft, post, or submit it. If you need to save an A/P invoice without an attachment, 

contact your system administrator and ask them to remove the Require attachment permission 

(on page 266) from your role or account. 

What’s Next? 

When your company uses approvals, A/P invoices first go through the payment approval 

workflow. After payments are approved, you can make the payments.  

Go to the Pay A/P invoices page to select the invoice for payment. When you select Add to 

outbox or Pay now: 

• 
The invoice becomes a payment request. 

• 
The system notifies approvers that a payment is waiting for their approval. 

• 
You can view the status of the payment request in the Payment request list. 

• 
When an approver approves the invoice, the system pays the invoice. 

• 
If the payment method is Check, the system allows the payment to be included in a check 

run.

#### Editing A/P Invoices
*Source: `RP Accounting AP Daily Tasks User Guide.pdf`, Page 469*

Editing A/P Invoices 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > All > A/P Invoices > Edit`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > All > Invoice Research > (search) > Edit`


The most important elements of the A/P invoice appear at the top of the page in the banner, 

including the vendor ID balance, invoice date, due date, invoice total, overdue, amount paid, and 

amount due. 

When you open an invoice in edit mode, the invoice image automatically opens. You can control 

how the invoice appears, either next to the invoice record or in a separate window. To change 

how the invoice appears, open the My Preferences > Personalize Interactive Behavior section, 

and then select or clear the Open Image Review in Separate Window check box. 

Invoices That You Can Edit 

You can edit unposted A/P invoices, eInvoices, and oInvoices. You can also edit posted A/P 

invoices if you have the Edit When Posted permission. 

A/P invoices can be associated with multiple locations. Only unrestricted users and users who 

have access to all of an A/P invoice’s associated locations can edit the invoice.  

Editing Invoices Submitted for Approval 

When your system has approvals enabled for A/P invoices, after you create an A/P invoice, the 

system submits the invoice for approval and changes its state to Submitted. You can edit 

submitted A/P invoices until they are approved.  

If you do not want the system to send edited A/P invoices through the approval process again 

when there is no change to the Location, G/L Account, or Total Amount fields, it is configurable. 

Ask your system administrator to configure it by going to Company > All > Approvals > 

Approval Configuration and selecting the Do not retrigger approvals check box in the A/P 

invoices section of the Approval Configuration page. 

Invoices That You Cannot Edit 

You can only edit invoices when you open them with the Edit link. In some cases, an Edit link is 

not available, such as when you do not have access to an invoice’s associated locations. If you do 

not have access to all of the locations associated with an A/P invoice, then the system does not 

display an Edit link for the invoice. 

Invoices created using the intercompany billing or management fee features cannot be edited. If 

your company wants the ability to edit these invoices, you can contact RealPage Customer 

Support to have RealPage enable additional permissions that permit the editing of these types of 

invoices. When enabled, two additional permissions appear in the permissions list for A/P 

invoices, Edit MF and Edit ICB. These permissions apply to both A/P and A/R invoices.

A/P Invoices with an Intercompany Billing Invoice 

When you edit the A/P invoice that is the result of an intercompany billing (ICB) invoice, the 

changes that you make do not affect the original intercompany billing invoice. You must make 

changes to the intercompany billing invoice directly. Open Accounts Receivable, select 

Intercompany Billing, and then find the original invoice and make your changes there. The 

invoice must be in the Submitted state but not be posted.  

Users can view the A/R invoice that is created after the A/P invoice is posted. The A/R invoice 

does not appear in the Intercompany Billing list until the A/P invoice is posted. 

Editing Invoices 

To edit an invoice: 

1. 
Open the Accounts payable menu. 

2. 
Select A/P invoices. The A/P invoices list opens. 

You can also edit invoices from the Invoice Research list. 

3. 
Find the A/P invoice you want to change, and then click Edit. The system opens the A/P 

invoice page with information about the A/P invoice. 

4. 
To match the A/P invoice with orders, click the Match Order button. The Match Orders 

page opens and lists all open purchase orders for that vendor and location. Use the Match 

Orders page to match the A/P invoice, eInvoice, or oInvoice to purchase orders, subcontract 

orders, and service orders that were created from service contracts.  

5. 
Add, modify, or delete information as needed. You can change any field without having to 

repost the A/P invoice except for the G/L account field. If you change the G/L account field, 

then you must post the A/P invoice again. 

The system displays a warning and can prevent you from posting the invoice if you increase 
the amount on the invoice and your company has enabled the warning for when the budget is 
exceeded. 

The system actions that occur when the budget is exceeded depends on your company 

configuration. You can enable or disable the system warning or change the system action 

from a warning to preventing the invoice from posting. You must have system 

administration privileges to make this change. 

• 
To change the system action, go to Company > All > Approval Configuration.  

• 
To enable or disable the feature, select or clear the Enable preventing or warning a 

user when adding an A/P Invoice that exceeds the budget check box. 

• 
You can also change the system action to Prevent or Warn.

Reversing Versus Deleting A/P Invoices 

You can either reverse or delete an A/P invoice as needed. Which action you take is dependent on 

your configuration and the state of the A/P invoice. 

Draft A/P Invoices: A partially created A/P invoice, perhaps waiting for additional input. 

• 
When reversal is disabled: Delete the A/P invoice (on page 339). 

• 
When reversal is enabled: Reverse the A/P invoice (on page 340). 

Posted A/P Invoices: Created and posted from the A/P invoices page. 

• 
When reversal is disabled: Delete the A/P Invoice. 

• 
When reversal is enabled: You can reverse an unpaid A/P invoice that was entered 

directly in Accounts Payable. To make sure that the system is enabled for reversing an 

unpaid A/P invoice, see Enabling A/P Functionality. 

A/P invoices and approvals in the Approval workbench.  

A/P invoices are submitted and then: 

• 
Approved: You can reverse an approved A/P invoice when reversal is enabled. 

• 
Declined: You must enable a setting before you can reverse a declined invoice. To 

enable the setting, open the Approval Configuration page, and then select the Ability 

to delete declined approvals check box.  

Selected A/P invoices: Associated with a payment request but has no payment against it. 

When reversal is disabled:  

• 
Cancel the payment request (on page 498) or 

• 
Delete the A/P Invoice. 

When reversal is enabled: 

• 
Cancel the payment request or 

• 
Reverse the A/P invoice. 

---


<!-- Page 477 -->

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Daily Tasks User Guide 

Selected (partially paid): The A/P invoice has a payment request and already has a partial 

payment against it. 

When reversal is disabled: 

• 
Cancel the payment request or 

• 
Void the payment (on page 529), and then delete the A/P invoice. 

When reversal is enabled: 

• 
Cancel the payment request or  

• 
Void the payment and then reverse the A/P invoice. 

Paid: The A/P invoice was paid. 

• 
When reversal is disabled: Void the payment and then delete the A/P invoice. 

Exception: If the A/P invoice and the payment were recorded simultaneously via the 
manual payment process, voiding the payment automatically reverses the A/P 
invoice. 

• 
When reversal is enabled: Void the payment and then reverse the A/P invoice. 

Exception: If the A/P invoice and the payment were recorded simultaneously via the 
manual payment process, voiding the payment automatically reverses the A/P 
invoice.  

No Value: The transaction is posted, but doesn’t affect the G/L. 

• 
When reversal is disabled: Delete the A/P invoice. 

• 
When reversal is enabled: Reverse the A/P invoice.  

Posted from Spend Management: Created and posted from Spend Management 

• 
When reversal is disabled: Delete the A/P invoice from Spend Management. 

• 
When reversal is enabled: Reverse the A/P invoice from Spend Management.

2. 
In the Search & Find section, select A/P invoices. The A/P invoices list opens. 

You can also delete invoices from the Invoice Research page after performing a search for 
invoices.  

3. 
Select the Delete check box beside the A/P invoices that you want to delete, and then click 

the Delete button.  

If a Delete link or check box does not appear in the A/P invoice line, you cannot delete the 

invoice. Instead, you may be able to reverse the invoice. Click the Reverse link to reverse the 

invoice.  

If an asset is associated with an A/P invoice, the deletion does not delete the asset. If you 
want to delete the asset record, you must do so manually.  

Troubleshooting Deletion 

• 
The system uses the check boxes on the left side of the A/P invoices list to help you build an 

invoice package. Do not select the check box to the left of the A/P invoice for deletions. 

• 
The Reverse option appears only at the level where the invoice was created. If the invoice 

was created at the top level, then navigate to the top level. If the invoice was created at the 

entity level, then navigate to the entity’s level.

<!-- Page 481 -->
Chapter 5: Invoice Research 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Daily Tasks User Guide 

State 
This column contains the current part of the processing cycle for the A/P 

invoice. How much you can edit an A/P invoice, or delete or reverse it, 

depends on its state. 

• 
Draft: The A/P invoice is created but not posted. It can be 

changed without consequence. 

• 
Posted: The A/P invoice was posted to the G/L. 

• 
Selected: The A/P invoice is now selected for payment. 

• 
Paid: Vendor payment was made. 

• 
Partially Paid: Only a partial payment was made. There is a 

remaining amount to be paid. 

• 
Reversed: The A/P invoice was reversed by a second transaction, 

which essentially zeroed out the balance in the G/L. Your 

company retains a record of the reversed A/P invoice and the 

reversal transaction for audit trail purposes. 

• 
Reversal: This transaction is created when you reverse a 

transaction and causes the balance to zero out. 

• 
No value: This transaction is posted but has not affected the 

general ledger.  

Payment Method 
This column contains the payment method used to pay this A/P invoice. 

Payment Number 
This column contains the payment number. When there are multiple 

payments, open the A/P invoice and click the Multiple payments link to 

see the list of payments. 

Property 
This is the location associated with the invoice.

### Payment Requests
*Source: `RP Accounting AP Daily Tasks User Guide.pdf`, Page 486*

Payments 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Daily Tasks User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Payment Requests 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > All > View Payment Requests`


Payment requests are A/P invoices that have been submitted to be paid and are queued for 

review and approval. 

If you’ve added payment requests to your A/P outbox, those requests are in a draft state and 

ready for you to view, edit, or remove them as needed, or move them forward into the next phase 

of the workflow.  

If you’ve clicked Pay now from Pay A/P invoices, or Pay from the outbox, the A/P invoices in the 

payment request can move to the next step in the flow. That step depends on the payment 

method and whether approval is required. For example, if the payment method is by check, then 

you can print the check. If approval is required, then you can go to the Approvals page to move 

the payment process along. If the payment is through the RealPage Payments service, then the 

system creates a payment request that you can access in the Third-Party Payment Queue page.  

If you’ve clicked Pay from the outbox, a confirmation page appears, which displays the next step 

in the process, such as electronic payment processing (on page 902). If the payment method used 

is Check, then the confirmation page displays a direct link to the Print checks (on page 986) page. 

When you follow the link, the Print Checks page defaults to displaying just the checks that you 

are responsible for printing. 

For other tasks related to the payment request, click More Actions at the top of the 
confirmation page, and select the next task in the process, such as Go to approval. 

---

After you have selected payments for a vendor on the Pay A/P invoices page, you can merge the

all payment requests to be merged into one A/P invoice. 

•

A/P invoice. 

• 
Merge requests into one per vendor: Merge selected payments into one draft 

payment request in the outbox. This option prints the Pay to Contact of the vendor, 

not the A/P invoice, on the check. 

•

one draft payment request in the outbox. The A/P invoice’s Pay to Contact will appear 

on the check.

request page appears.

### Pay A/P Invoices Outbox
*Source: `RP Accounting AP Daily Tasks User Guide.pdf`, Page 490*

Payments 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Daily Tasks User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Pay A/P Invoices Outbox 

The outbox is a holding area for draft payment requests that you’re not quite ready to process. 

For example, using the outbox can be highly efficient if you create multiple types of payment 

requests, such as requests that use different banks or currencies. If you have an aging report that 

you want to tie to, then adding requests to the outbox can make that task a no-brainer because 

you can view the total amount to be paid for all the requests. The outbox holds and stores 

requests until you are ready to move them on for payment. 

A company generally has one outbox per user who pays bills. Admins can access all outboxes. 

Outbox does not support Wells Fargo Payment Manager payments. To make Wells Fargo 
Payment Manager payments, select your payments and click Pay now.  

When you pay bills from the Pay A/P Invoices page, you create payment requests that can then 

be approved or processed for payment. The Pay A/P Invoices page provides a couple of options 

for generating payment requests based on your needs: Pay now or add A/P invoices to the 

outbox. If you want to use the outbox, you can select A/P invoices, or filter A/P invoices from the 

Pay A/P invoices list and add the resulting payment requests to your outbox as drafts. The 

outbox can hold multiple draft payment requests that differ from each other in their payment 

methods, currencies, and banks. 

About Your Outbox Draft Payment Request List 

Draft payment requests can have one or more associated A/P invoices with one or more credits 

that are applied or can be applied. 

Your outbox provides a summary of the number of A/P invoices and, of those A/P invoices the 

number that are currently selected for next-step processing based on the Outbox and Bank 

selection. 

If there are multiple outboxes or banks that you use, you can select any combination of outboxes 

(based on permissions) and banks to filter the payment request list: 

• 
Your outbox and one bank 

• 
Your outbox and all banks 

• 
Another user’s outbox or all outboxes, and one bank (Requires admin permissions for 

viewing all outboxes) 

• 
Another user’s outbox or all outboxes and all banks (Required admin permissions for 

viewing all outboxes) 

To view all payment requests for a specific bank or all banks, leave the outbox empty and 
select All for all banks or the name of a specific bank. 

The page refreshes to display the resulting payment request list. 

---

Processing Draft Payment Requests 

To move draft payment requests from the outbox to the next step: 

• 
Click the Pay button. A payment confirmation page appears which lists the request, the 

payment method, the amount, and the next step in the process. The request moves from 

the outbox to the next part of the process, such as Printing checks (on page 986) or ACH 

Generation (on page 902). 

• 
If the check is ready to print, a Print check link appears. You can click the link, or you can 

click the More actions button, and then select the Go to print check page option.  

• 
If a payment needs an approval, the last column contains “Waiting approval.” The check 

cannot be printed until the payment is approved. 

If the system does not display a Print check link, then you can try to fix it by starting over. 
Cancel the payment, and then reselect the invoice to pay, and then pay it.

Merging Payment Requests 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > All > Pay A/P Invoices`


You can merge multiple draft payment requests of multiple users for a vendor. When you select 

multiple payments for the same vendor on the Pay A/P invoices page, you have the option to 

merge your payments with draft payments that are stored in your outbox.  

When this feature is enabled, the system checks for payment requests in the Outbox that are for 

the same vendor as the payment requests that you select, and gives you the option to merge the 

payment requests so that you only need to generate one check to the vendor. 

To be eligible to be merged, your selections must match several attributes of payment requests in 

the outbox: 

• 
Vendor name 

• 
Payment date 

• 
Payment method 

• 
Bank 

• 
Currency 

Before You Begin 

Access can vary depending on your organization’s subscriptions and your permissions. If you do 

not see the option in the menu, then ask your System Administrator to check your permissions. 

Permissions 

These permissions are required to merge payment requests: 

Application 
Activity 
Permissions 

Accounts payable 
Select to Pay 
Run 

If your user account doesn’t have the permissions shown above, then ask your System 

Administrator for assistance. If you have administrator privileges, you can assign permissions for a 

new feature to a user or to a role. See Roles and Permissions for a description of how to review a 

user’s permissions. 

Requirements 

You can only merge payment requests if the payments you selected on the Pay A/P Invoices 

page: 

• 
Are all for the same vendor. 

• 
Have the same vendor, payment method, bank, and currency as an existing draft payment 

request in your outbox.

Adding an A/P Invoice to an Existing Draft Payment Request 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > All > Pay A/P Invoices`


You may have already created a draft payment request but received an additional A/P invoice that 

needs to be included. You can add payments to draft payment requests by merging them 

together. Do this by selecting and merging payments for one vendor at a time. 

To merge draft payment requests, payments must match in vendor name, payment date, payment 

method, bank, and currency. Learn more about how to merge draft payment requests (on page 

481). 

Merging Draft Payment Requests 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > All > Pay A/P Invoices > Outbox Payments > Return 
to Pay A/P Invoices`


When you make payments to the same vendor as a payment in the Outbox, the system offers to 

merge the payments for you. 

If your system does not offer to merge payment requests for the same vendor, then ask your 
system administrator to enable the feature. To enable this feature, go to the Accounts Payable 

Configuration page, and then select the Enable Merge Payments added to the outbox across all 

users check box. 

Before You Begin 

• 
You must have the Merge Payment Drafts - Create permission to use this procedure. 

To merge draft payment requests: 

1. 
Open the Accounts payable menu. 

2. 
Select Pay A/P invoices. The Pay A/P invoices page opens. 

3. 
Click Outbox payments to review the payment requests that are in your outbox. Decide 

which A/P invoice and vendor you can merge with the A/P invoices on the Pay A/P invoices 

page. 

4. 
Click the Return to Pay A/P Invoices button to return to the list. 

5. 
In the list of invoices in the bottom half of the page, select payments for the vendor that 

already has a draft payment request in the outbox.

What to Do if You Make a Mistake 
If you selected Don’t Merge, the payment is added to the outbox without merging it with 
other payments. If you didn’t mean to do that, you can remove the payment from the 
outbox and start the process anew. You must have the Merge Payment Drafts - Delete 
permission to remove the merged payment request. 
 - Select the check box of the payment and click the Remove from Outbox button. 
 - Click the Return to Pay A/P Invoices button to return to the list of invoices.  
You will find the removed payment there, where you can start the merge process again. 
You can also select Pay now if you need to pay it immediately while you continue to merge 
other draft payments. 

Merging Payment Requests as You Add Them to the Outbox 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > All > Pay A/P invoices`


After you have selected payments for a vendor on the Pay A/P invoices page, you can merge the 

payments into an existing draft payment request as you add them to the outbox. 

1. 
Open the Accounts payable menu. 

2. 
Select Pay A/P invoices. The Pay A/P invoices page opens. 

3. 
In Bank, select the bank from which funds will be used for these payments. 

4. 
From the list of invoices in the bottom half of the page, select payments for the vendor that 

you want to merge. 

5. 
In the Payment request method drop-down list, select one of the following: 

• 
Use vendor preference: Select this option only when you know that the vendor prefers 

all payment requests to be merged into one A/P invoice. 

• 
Generate one request per AP invoice: The system generates one payment request per 

A/P invoice. 

• 
Merge requests into one per vendor: Merge selected payments into one draft 

payment request in the outbox. This option prints the Pay to Contact of the vendor, 

not the A/P invoice, on the check. 

• 
Merge request into one per vendor pay to contact: Merge selected payments into 

one draft payment request in the outbox. The A/P invoice’s Pay to Contact will appear 

on the check. 

6. 
Click Add to outbox. If your payments match the required attributes*, the Merge payment 

request page appears.

Stopping Payments 

This section describes the methods by which you can stop a payment. 

• 
Stopping Payments (on page 492) 

• 
Stopping an AvidXchange Payment (on page 493) 

• 
Reversing A/P Invoices (on page 340) 

• 
Removing an Outbox Draft Payment Request (on page 474) 

• 
Removing an A/P Invoice from a Draft Payment Request (on page 473) 

•

• 
Placing A/P Invoices On Hold (on page 373) 

• 
Declining Payments (on page 499) 

• 
Voiding and Reversing a Paid A/P Invoice Simultaneously (on page 341) 

Stopping a Payment 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > All > Daily Tasks > View Payment Requests`


If you selected an A/P invoice to pay that you don’t want to pay for the foreseeable future, you 

can delete the payment request for that A/P invoice: 

1. 
Open the Accounts payable menu. 

2. 
Select View payment requests. 

3. 
On the Payment requests page, locate the payment request, and then delete it from the list. 

When a Payment Status Is “Success” And You Want to Stop the Payment 

If a payment has already been successfully processed through AvidXchange, you cannot cancel it 

from the RealPage Financial Suite. At that point, the payment has left the system and is now fully 

controlled by AvidXchange’s payment network. At this point, RealPage no longer has control over 

the payment’s lifecycle, so cancelation must be handled by AvidXchange. 

Step 1: Contact AvidXchange Support Immediately. 

AvidXchange may be able to stop or reverse the payment depending on: 

• 
The payment method (ACH, virtual card, check) 

• 
Whether the payment has already settled. 

• 
Whether the vendor has already claimed the funds. 

Click the Avid Community button on the Third Party Payments Queue page or use your 

organization’s AvidXchange support channel or portal to request a cancelation. 

---



#### Stopping an AvidXchange Payment
*Source: `RP Accounting AP Daily Tasks User Guide.pdf`, Page 511*

Chapter 6: Payments 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Daily Tasks User Guide 

Step 2: Notify the vendor (if needed) 

For some payment types—especially virtual cards or checks—AvidXchange may instruct you to 

notify the vendor not to deposit or use the payment while the cancelation request is in progress. 

Step 3: Record the outcome in the RealPage Financial Suite 

After AvidXchange confirms the cancelation or reversal: 

• 
Reverse the payment in the RealPage Financial Suite. 

• 
Reopen or reissue the invoice if necessary. 

• 
Document the cancelation for audit purposes. 

This keeps your ledger aligned with the actual payment status. 

Stopping an AvidXchange Payment 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > All > Third Party Payments Queue > Stop Payment`


 To stop a payment that has been sent to AvidXchange for processing: 

1. 
Open the Accounts Payable menu. 

2. 
Find the payment that you want to stop. 

3. 
Click the Stop payment link at the end of the row. If you don’t see a Stop payment link, 

then you can use the Cancel payment link. If neither link appears, then the payment may 

have been completed successfully. If so, see When a Payment Status Is “Success” And You 

Want to Stop the Payment (on page 492).

Voiding and Reversing a Paid A/P Invoice Simultaneously 

To void and reverse at the same time, start by displaying a register report for the account from 

which the payment was made. Then, you void the payment and reverse the A/P invoice from the 

register report. 

You can wait to reverse the A/P invoice at a later time. To access the A/P invoice to void it later 
on, go to the A/P invoices page and click the Reverse link. 

Before You Begin 

• 
The Reverse option appears only at the level where the invoice was created. If the invoice 

was created at the top level, then navigate to the top level. If the invoice was created at the 

entity level, then navigate to the entity’s level.  

Step 1. Locate the payment in the account register report 

1. 
Open the Accounts Payable menu.  

2. 
In the Reports section of the menu, select A/P Invoice Register or Check register, 

depending on the payment type you want to void and reverse. 

3. 
Select the type of account from which the payment was made. 

You can generate register reports for banking and credit card accounts. 

4. 
Optionally, in the Filter section, select options to narrow the transactions that you’ll see in 

the register report. 

5. 
Click View to display the register report. 

6. 
Locate the payment in the register report. 

7. 
Payments that can be voided and reversed appear with a Void link. 

If the Void link isn’t active, that means that the payment has already been voided. 

---


<!-- Page 519 -->
Chapter 6: Payments 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Daily Tasks User Guide 

Step 2. Void the payment and reverse the A/P invoice 

When you void the payment from the register report, you automatically reverse the A/P invoice. 

1. 
In the register report, click the Void link next to the payment. 

2. 
In the Void Payment Date page, scroll down and select the Reverse check box next to any 

payments that you’re reversing. 

3. 
Review the void and reversal dates, and then add a memo. 

• 
Void date: Select the date for voiding the payment. This is usually the original 

transaction date or a later date. 

• 
Reversal date: Select the date for reversing the transaction. This is usually the original 

transaction date or a later date. 

• 
Memo: We recommend that you enter the reason for the reversal. 

4. 
Click Submit.

Payment Notifications 

Payment notifications are particularly valuable for vendors that are paid through ACH, but 

notifications can be automatically sent to any vendor, regardless of how they are paid. 

By enabling notifications for a vendor, you are indicating that you want the vendor to be notified 

by email whenever the system confirms a payment to them. 

Before You Begin 

Access can vary depending on your organization’s subscriptions and your permissions. If you do 

not see the option in the menu, then ask your System Administrator to check your permissions. 

Permissions 

These permissions are required to change vendor records. 

Application 
Activities/Lists 
Permissions 

Accounts payable 
Vendors 
List, View, Add, Edit, Delete 

If your user account doesn’t have the permissions shown above, then ask your System 

Administrator for assistance. If you have administrator privileges, you can assign permissions for a 

new feature to a user or to a role. See Roles and Permissions for a description of how to review a 

user’s permissions. 

Vendor Configuration 

Decide which vendors should be notified of payments and verify that they have an email address 

on record. By enabling notifications for a vendor, you are indicating that you want the vendor to 

be notified by email whenever a payment to them is confirmed in the system. 

Add vendor types to help you group vendors by type of service or product.  

Level 

You must be at the top level to add and import vendors.

automatic payment notification.  

5. 
On the Contacts tab for the vendor, verify the vendor’s name and email address.  

• 
The payment notification will be sent to the email address listed in the “Pay to” contact 

for the vendor, and the vendor’s “Print as” name will be used in the email greeting line.  

• 
If the vendor’s “Pay to” contact is the “same as vendor,” the “Print as” name and email 

address will come from the first tab of the Vendor record. 

Setting Up Automatic Payment Notifications 

When you set up automatic notification for a vendor, the system automatically notifies the vendor 

every time anyone sends them a payment. 

To set up automatic notification: 

1. 
Decide which vendors should be notified after you have paid them. 

2. 
Open the Accounts payable menu. 

3. 
Select Vendors. 

4. 
Identify a vendor that you want to notify automatically and click the Edit link. 

5. 
Select the Payment Information tab. 

6. 
Select the Send automatic payment notification check box. 

7. 
Select the Contacts tab. 

8. 
Verify the vendor’s name and email address. 

The payment notification will be sent to the email address listed in the Pay to contact for 

the vendor, and the vendor’s Print as name will be used in the email greeting line. 

If the vendor’s Pay to contact is the same as vendor, the Print as name and email address 

will come from the first tab of the Vendor record. 

9. 
Click the Save button. 

10. 
Repeat steps four through nine for each vendor.

Determining the “From” Contact 

At the time you are paying A/P invoices, you can select the “from” contact that will be used in 

payment notification emails. Select the contact in the Send payment notifications from 

drop-down list. By default, the contact is set to the user who is paying the A/P invoices. 

Contact information for this user will be used for two purposes: 

• 
Payment notification emails will be sent “from” this contact’s email address. 

• 
The name and email address from this contact will be included in the email body in case the 

vendor has questions about the payment. 

If you don’t want to use a specific user ’s contact information, consider creating a generic user 
such as “Accounts Payable. ” The contact information for this user can have a generic name and 
email address that you want to use for payment inquiries.

### Email Delivery Log
*Source: `RP Accounting AP Daily Tasks User Guide.pdf`, Page 523*

Chapter 6: Payments 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Daily Tasks User Guide 

Email Delivery Log 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > Setup > History and Reports > Email Delivery History`


Use the Email delivery log to check whether any emails that were sent encountered errors. The 

log displays a list of emails that failed to be sent to one or more recipients. Click View to view the 

details of an error. 

For example, suppose that you email invoices to multiple customers. By checking the Email 

delivery log, you can see whether any invoices encountered errors. By viewing the details of a 

particular error, you can see which recipients couldn’t be reached, giving you the opportunity to 

go back and correct the errors. 

The Email delivery log captures only errors that are encountered at the time the emails are 
sent. Sometimes, email errors are returned some period of time after the email is sent. For 
example, a particular email domain might return an error several hours after the original email 
was sent. These errors are not captured in the log.

Administrator for assistance. If you have administrator privileges, you can assign permissions for a

user’s permissions. 

Viewing the Log of Email Delivery Errors 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > Setup > History and Reports > Email Delivery History`


When you view the Email delivery log, you see a list of emails that failed to be sent to one or 

more recipients. 

By default, administrators automatically have access to the 
Email delivery log, but access can 
be granted to other users by changing their permissions to the Company application. 

1. 
Open the Company menu, and then select the Setup tab. 

2. 
In the History and reports section, select the Email delivery history menu option. 

The Email delivery log opens. 

3. 
Review the list of errors in the log: 

• 
Error: Emails with this status weren’t delivered to any recipients. 

• 
Warning: Emails with this status were sent to at least one recipient, but other 

recipients couldn’t be reached. 

Each record in the log represents one email, each of which may have had multiple recipients.

4. 
Click the View link next to an item to examine a particular error. 

A separate Email delivery log page opens. The left side of the record displays the email 

errors that were encountered. The Result details field lists each email address that was 

rejected. The right side of the record displays a copy of the email that was sent.

#### Resending Failed Emails
*Source: `RP Accounting AP Daily Tasks User Guide.pdf`, Page 525*

Chapter 6: Payments 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Daily Tasks User Guide 

Viewing All Emails 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > Setup > History and Reports > Email Delivery History > 
Show All Emails`


By default, the Email delivery log displays only failed emails. However, you can use the Show all 

emails button to display all sent emails. 

To view all emails sent within the company: 

1. 
Open the Company menu, and then select the Setup tab. 

2. 
In the History and reports section, select the Email delivery history menu option. 

3. 
Click the Show all emails button located in the upper-right corner of the page. This button 

acts as a toggle between displaying all errors and showing all emails. Click the Show errors 

only button to return to the original view. 

Troubleshooting Incorrect Email Addresses 

The majority of emails are sent to either customers, vendors, or employees. When you send an 

email, the email address is typically pulled from the contact record for that customer, vendor, or 

employee. You also have the option to manually enter one or more email addresses at the time 

that you send the email. 

If the email address for a customer, vendor, or employee is incorrect, then it’s best to correct the 

error in their contact record.  

Resending Failed Emails 

After correcting any incorrect email addresses, try resending the failed documents. To do this, 

return to the page where you originally sent the email. The Accounts Receivable, Accounts 

Payable, and Spend Management applications have email functions where you can send invoices, 

statements, payment notifications, and other documents. 

For automatic payment notifications to vendors or employees, you can resend a payment 

notification that failed by emailing a copy of the payment. 

1. 
Open the Accounts payable menu. 

2. 
In the Account maintenance section, select Print payment copies. 

3. 
Use the filters to narrow your search. You can filter for a specific range of dates, or for a 

particular customer, vendor, or employee. 

4. 
Resend the email.

new feature to a user or to a role. See Roles and Permissions for a description of how to review a 

user’s permissions. 

The items you can see on the Posted payments page vary slightly depending on whether your

Voiding Payments 

There are several ways to void payments.  

• 
Payments made by check: You can void payments made by check (on page 530) from the 

Check Register report. 

• 
Manual payments: You can void a manual payment (on page 533) from the Manual 

Payments list.  

• 
RealPage debit card payment: You can void this type of payment through the Bank Register 

report. 

• 
Credit card payments: You can void credit card payments through the Credit Card Register 

or Bank Register  

• 
Record Transfers: You can void record transfers through the Check Register (on page 530) or 

Bank Register report. 

• 
Voiding a payment from its A/P invoice (on page 425): The invoice must have a status of 

Paid. 

• 
Voiding a payment that was made with credit (on page 536).  

• 
Voiding multiple payments (on page 534): You can void payments in bulk. 

Voiding Electronic Payments 

• 
Voiding pending electronic payments (on page 934) 

• 
Voiding a confirmed electronic payment (on page 936) 

Voiding payments made through third party payment services: 

• 
Paymode-X payments: You can void Paymode-X payments in the Bank Register report. 

• 
RealPage payments: Contact Avid to void a payment. For details, see Voiding RealPage 

payment service payments (on page 530).

#### Voiding a Manual Payment
*Source: `RP Accounting AP Daily Tasks User Guide.pdf`, Page 551*

Chapter 6: Payments 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Daily Tasks User Guide 

Voiding a Manual Payment 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > All > Daily Tasks > Banking > Manual Payment > 
Void`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Cash Management > All > Periodic Tasks > Manual Payment > Void`


You cannot edit or delete manual payments after they are saved and confirmed. However, you 

can void the payment, which automatically reverses the A/P invoice. Voiding a payment reverses 

its effect on the General Ledger (G/L) and leaves a record of both the original and voided 

payment. 

When you void a payment: 

• 
The system creates a new transaction that is the reverse of the transaction you are voiding. 

In other words, the transaction is not zeroed out, resulting in an audit trail. This produces a 

net effect of zero for that transaction. 

• 
The system treats the reversed entry as a new payment and places the reversed manual 

payment into its payment summary based on the auto-summary frequency. 

• 
Both transactions are labeled as Voided. However, there are now two: the original positive 

one and the new negative reversing one. The title of the summary contains wording similar 

to “Reversed Quick Payments.” 

• 
The system also reverses the A/P invoice that is associated with the voided payment in a 

similar manner, leaving two A/P invoices: the original positive one and a new negative 

reversing one. Both are labeled as Reversed. 

If a manual payment is in a summary, you must open the summary before you can void the 
payment. You cannot void a reconciled payment or a payment in a closed period. 

To void a manual payment: 

1. 
In the Manual payments list, locate the payment that you want to void, and then click the 

corresponding Void link. The Void payment date box opens. 

2. 
In the Void the payment on date field, type or select a date on or after the transaction date. 

3. 
In the Memo field, type an optional note to store with the G/L entry. 

4. 
Click the Submit button. 

---

Can’t Find A/P Invoices 

When you are selecting A/P invoices to pay, you might receive a message that no A/P invoices 

were found, or you might not see the A/P invoices you expected. There are several reasons why 

A/P invoices might not show up on the Pay A/P invoices page. 

By default, A/P invoices won’t load until you apply a filter. Filters must result in less than 1000 
A/P invoices. Learn tips on creating filters. 

Reasons you might not be able to find A/P invoices 

The following list describes possible reasons for A/P invoices not showing up on the Pay A/P 

invoices page. 

Reason: Multi-entity only — The A/P invoice was created at the top level and you’re at the entity 

level. 

Solution: When viewing the Pay A/P invoices page from the entity level, the list only displays A/P 

invoices created at the entity level. To include A/P invoices created at the top level that are 

tagged to your entity, create a Filter set that includes the Show top level transactions option. 

1. 
Open the Accounts payable menu. 

2. 
Select Pay A/P invoices. 

3. 
Edit or add a filter set in the Filter by drop-down. 

4. 
Select the Show top level transactions check box. 

5. 
Click Save. 

---

Solution: Review and change any fields on the Pay A/P Invoices page: 

1. 
Open the Accounts payable menu. 

2. 
Select Pay A/P invoices.

Check fields for blank spaces, change values that may be excluding A/P invoices from being 

found (such as vendor or date ranges), and click View. Learn more about selecting A/P 

invoices to pay (on page 760).

Reason: A large number of A/P invoices exist, and the Pay A/P invoices page is not configured to 

display all of them. 

Solution: By default, the Pay A/P invoices page selects a maximum of 50 A/P invoices to display 

on the Pay A/P invoices page. Increase the number of A/P invoices that the system displays: 

1. 
Open the Accounts payable menu. 

2. 
Select Pay A/P invoices. 

3. 
Select a larger value in the Maximum Number Of Records To Select drop-down.

Click View.

Deposit and Record a Refund from a Vendor 

Learn how to record a vendor refund for the following supported use cases. 

Scenario 1 

The vendor sent you a cash or check refund, and you need to record the amount. 

• 
You haven’t created an adjustment (credit memo) to account for the refund. You don’t need 

to balance anything on the Accounts Payable side. 

• 
You want to deposit the amount in your bank and are not planning on using the refund as a 

credit on a future A/P invoice. 

Do this: 

• 
Create an Other receipt to record the refund.  

Scenario 2 

The vendor sent you a credit to use on a future A/P invoice. 

Do this: 

1. 
Create an A/P adjustment (on page 837) (debit memo) to decrease the amount that you 

owe the vendor. 

2. 
Apply the adjustment (debit memo) to the next A/P invoice that you receive from the 

vendor on the Pay A/P invoices page. 

Debit memos decrease the overall amount that you owe a vendor.

The vendor sent you a cash or check refund, and you need to record the amount. 

•

Accounts Payable side. 

• 
You want to deposit the amount in your bank and are not planning on using the refund as a 

credit on a future A/P invoice. 

Do this: 

1. 
Create an AP Adjustment to clear the vendor balance. 

• 
Credit memo increases the overall amount that you owe a vendor. 

• 
Debit memo decreases the overall amount that you owe a vendor. 

2. 
Apply the adjustment to the vendor balance. 

3. 
Create an Other receipt to record the refund. 

No Available Bank Accounts 

You’re all set to pay A/P invoices and receive an error message that no bank accounts exist to 

make the payment. To avoid these types of error messages, ensure that bank accounts have been 

properly set up for the default payment method or appropriate options have been selected for 

A/P invoices in other currencies. 

Reasons for a message about no bank accounts 

The following list describes possible reasons for error messages about no bank accounts and 

provides solutions for each reason. 

Reason: No accounts have been set up for the default payment method. 

Solution: Verify the default payment method for paying A/P invoices and ensure that the 

payment method has been fully configured. For example: 

• 
If Check is the default payment method, ensure that at least one checking account has been 

set up. 

• 
If ACH is the default payment method, ensure that you’ve set up your bank as an ACH bank 

and have associated one or more checking accounts with the ACH bank. 

To determine the default payment method:  

1. 
Click the Applications menu, select Accounts payable, and then select the Setup tab. 

2. 
Select Configuration. 

3. 
In the Defaults section, review the Payment method value. 

---

Unselect an A/P Invoice to Be Paid 

If you made a mistake when you selected A/P invoices to be paid, you can undo the payment and 

start over. 

• 
If the payment has already been recorded, you can void the payment. This will return the 

A/P invoice to the list of A/P invoices that can be paid. 

• 
If the payment was never recorded--for example, if the check hasn’t yet been printed or if 

the payment requires approval--you can start over by canceling the payment request. This 

makes the related A/P invoices available to be paid again in the Pay A/P invoices page (on 

page 734).

Enter A/P Invoices Section 

This section lists the different methods for creating and managing A/P invoices. 

• 
Creating an A/P invoice lets you create a single A/P invoice by manually entering all of the 

data. 

• 
Quick A/P invoice entry allows you to enter multiple A/P invoices one after the other. 

• 
Document dashboard lets you monitor the scanned invoices uploaded from invoice 

processing. You can create an A/P invoice while you review the image of the scanned 

invoice. 

These options appear in the Daily tasks section. Use these options to help you ensure that your 

processes are moving smoothly. 

• 
Approve vendors: This option lets you approve new vendor records and updated vendor 

records. 

• 
View vendor requests: This option lets you review the status of vendor approvals. 

• 
View payment requests: This option lets you review the status of payment requests. 

Adding an A/P Invoice Manually 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > All > 
 A/P Invoices`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > All > Invoice Research > Add`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > Setup > Import Data > Set Up AP Master List, Open 
Invoices and Adjustments > Accounts Payable Invoices > Create`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Spend Management > Search & Find > 
 AP Invoice`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Job Cost > Daily Tasks > Create an AP Invoice`


This topic describes how to create an A/P invoice as if every possible feature is enabled. Your 

experience of this page will differ depending on the features that your system has enabled. 

Variations occur due to system configuration, your permissions, and your company’s installation 

of other RealPage Financial Suite applications. For instructions on importing A/P invoices, see 

Importing A/P Invoices (on page 252). 

Applications that Affect the Fields on A/P Invoice Records 

• 
Spend Management 

• 
Job Cost

Configuration Differences that Affect the Fields on A/P Invoice Records 

• 
When your system is configured to use multiple currencies, additional currency fields appear 

in this record. See the multi-currency systems section on the General Ledger configuration 

page. 

• 
When the Intercompany billing option is enabled (Accounts Receivable configuration), the 

A/R Invoice Dimensions section appears. 

• 
When your system is integrated with OpsTechnology, it allows RealPage Accounting to 

receive eInvoices. 

• 
Accounts Payable configuration:  

• 
When the Enable bank account selection in A/P invoice option is selected (Accounts 

Payable configuration), it causes the Bank account field to appear on the A/P invoice 

record. 

• 
When the Enable invoice entry control validation option is selected (Accounts 

Payable configuration), it causes the Total invoice amount field to appear on the A/P 

invoice record. 

• 
When Spend management is enabled, then the Match Order button appears, allowing you 

to match a purchase order to the A/P invoice. Additional fields appear on the record such as 

QTY, Price, Extended Price, UOM, and Account code description. 

• 
When Job Cost is enabled, the Line Entry Type section appears. When you select Include Job 

cost, the system adds Job cost-specific columns in the Invoice Entries list such as Job name, 

Cost code, and Job unit.  

• 
When scanning is enabled, the Attachments field is replaced with the Documents section, 

affecting the way that you attach documents.  

• 
If the Please complete one-time setup scanner prompt appears, follow the 

instructions in Downloading the Scanning Software. If you do not plan to scan 

supporting documents at this time, you can skip the download by clicking the X in 

upper-right corner of the box.  

• 
If you enabled the Single scan upload feature in your preferences and have previously 

downloaded the Dynamsoft scanning software, you may be prompted to update the 

software when you add a new scannable record such as an A/P invoice, vendor, 

purchase order, or service contract, or scan a document into the document dashboard. 

When this occurs, download the new software. There is no need to uninstall the 

previous version.

To create an A/P invoice: 

1. 
In the Date field, type the date of the invoice, or leave it set to today’s date.  

Any date entered here is automatically filled in the G/L posting date field (and to the 

Exchange rate date field if you’re a multi-currency company). You can change either date as 

needed; for example, if you want to create the adjustment today, but post it on a different 

date. 

2. 
In the G/L posting date field, type the date that you want the A/P invoice to post on the 

general ledger.  

3. 
In the Total invoice amount field, type the amount of the invoice.  

This field appears only when the Enable invoice entry control validation check box is 

selected on the configuration page of Accounts Payable. When enabled, this is a required 

field.  

4. 
In the Vendor drop-down list, select an existing vendor or add a new vendor, as required. 

The system completes the Pay to and Return to fields automatically based on the vendor 

record that you select. This is a required field. 

To add a new vendor, you must be at the top level. You can use the field-level controls to 

add a new vendor, view a vendor’s record, or find a vendor’s record. 

The system fills in the Pay to field automatically. If you need to change the Pay to contact, 

you can do that here. In the Pay to drop-down list, select the name of the person to whom 

the payment should be sent. 

The system fills in the Return to field automatically. If you need to change the Return to 

contact, you can do that here. In the Return to drop-down list, select the name of the 

person to whom returns should be addressed.  

5. 
To fill in the A/P invoice form with data from the last A/P invoice from this vendor, click the 

Populate from last A/P invoice button.  

6. 
In the Invoice number field, type the invoice number. This is a required field. 

7. 
Type a Reference number. Reference numbers can be a vendor’s number that they use to 

track the payment.  

8. 
Type a Description of the transaction.  

---


<!-- Page 571 -->

You can also use the Reference number and Description fields to enter specific 
information that a vendor requires. Sometimes, a vendor requires a specific piece of 
information to reconcile your payments, such as a customer account number or a pin 
number. 

9. 
Select the Corporate invoice check box if you want to prevent this invoice from appearing 

in Spend Management’s Site Experience. 

10. 
If your company uses the Spend Management application for purchase orders: 

• 
Click the Match order button. 

• 
In the Match orders box, click the View details link. 

• 
In the Contract details section that appears below, select the service order for which 

you want to create an A/P invoice. 

• 
Click Apply. 

Make the Invoice Recurring 

1. 
Select the Make recurring check box to turn this invoice into a recurring invoice. When you 

submit the A/P invoice, the system creates a recurring A/P invoice based on the current 

invoice. When you select this check box, the Schedules section appears.  

2. 
In the Schedules section, fill in the A/P invoice start date field with the date that you want 

the system to start creating the recurring A/P invoices. 

3. 
Select the sequence number scheme from the AP invoice sequence number drop-down list. 

4. 
In the Ending on drop-down list, select: 

• 
Never: To keep the invoice perpetually running, select Never. This is common for A/P 

invoices for ongoing services that have a set price. 

• 
Number of occurrences: The End after field appears. To have the invoice run for a 

limited number of times, type the number of times you want the invoice to recur in the 

End after field. This setting is often used for debts that are being paid over time. 

Setting the number of occurrences eliminates the possibility of making payments after 

the debt is paid off. 

---


<!-- Page 572 -->

© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

• 
End date: To have the invoice recur until a specific date, select End date and then, in 

the End on field, type the date on which the last invoice is to recur.  

5. 
In the Posting repeat by drop-down list, select the frequency that you want the system to 

generate the recurring A/P invoices. The options are: 

• 
None 

• 
Days 

• 
Weeks 

• 
Months 

• 
Years 

6. 
In the Every field, type the number of time frames to repeat by. For example, if you selected 

Months, then type the number of months to repeat by, such as 6 to have the system bill 

every 6 months. 

7. 
If you selected Months, then you can select the End of month check box to have the invoice 

created at the end of the month. 

8. 
Type the email address of the person to whom to send notifications about the recurring 

invoice in the Email field. 

Creating a Future Draft Invoice 

1. 
Select the Create future draft invoice on check box. A date field appears below the check 

box. 

2. 
Type the date that you want the system to create the future draft invoice.  

When you submit the A/P invoice, the system creates a draft invoice with a posting date set 

for the future date and containing the details of the source A/P invoice.  

The system sends you an email as a reminder on the day before the future draft invoice 
date is to be automatically posted. 

Filling In the Term Section 

1. 
Select the terms of payment in the Term drop-down list. If you selected the Make recurring 

check box, the Term field is required. 

2. 
In the Recommended to pay on field, click the 
 Calendar button and then select the 

date by which to pay the invoice. 

3. 
In the Attachments field, you can attach any documents related to the invoice. The system 

stores the attachment in the folder that you select. 

If you have enabled the single scan feature in your preferences, then the Attachments field 
does not appear. See the Documents section for instructions on attaching documents to 
the A/P invoice.

The system calculates the default Due date based on the A/P invoice date and terms.  

4. 
In the Due date field, enter a new date to override the due date. This field is required. 

5. 
Select the desired priority to assign to the payment in the Payment priority drop-down list. 

Priorities allow you to sort A/P invoices according to their importance. 

6.

Selecting the Line Entry Type 

The Line entry type section appears only when your company has installed the Job Cost 

application. 

In the Term section, in the Line entry type section, select: 

• 
Standard: Select this option to add standard line entries to the A/P invoice. 

• 
Include job cost: Select this option to add line entries associated with a project. The system 

displays a list with columns for both standard and job cost types of entries in the same list. 

Invoices from OpsTechnology, Full Service, and oInvoices also appear in the combined list.

Selecting the Workflow Type 

This section appears when your company has enabled A/P invoice approvals. 

Leave the workflow set to Default. You can also use a specific approval workflow for this invoice. 

Click the Select workflow option, and then select the desired workflow in the Workflow 

drop-down list. 

About the OPS Section 

When your system is integrated with OpsTechnology, the OPS section appears after the Term 

section, and contains two required fields, OPS and IRN.  

• 
The OPS field contains the location of the scanned image of the invoice (OPS URL). 

• 
The IRN field contains the invoice routing number (IRN) which is assigned to all invoices 

submitted electronically or entered manually in OpsTechnology. 

Additional custom fields may also appear based on how your system is integrated with other 

applications. 

Filling In the Currency Section 

This section appears when your company has multi-currency enabled. If you’re a multi-currency 

company, type the currency details in the Currency section. 

1. 
In the Transaction currency drop-down list, select the currency being used for this 

transaction. 

2. 
In the Base currency drop-down list, select the base currency of your company. 

If the currency is not your company’s base currency, continue with the next steps. Otherwise, 

move to the next section. 

3. 
Type a date in the Exchange rate date field. You can also click the 
 Calendar button and 

select the desired date to have the system fill in the date. The default value is the current 

date, but you can override it. 

For example, you may want to change it to the date that the transaction was issued, or the 

date that you intend to pay if it is an A/P invoice.

If you override the date of the transaction, the system automatically updates the exchange 

rate date. 

4. 
In the Exchange rate type drop-down list, select an exchange rate type. The Daily rate is the 

system-supplied default exchange rate type unless you’ve defined a different one. 

5. 
If you know the exchange rate for this transaction or have contracted on a set exchange rate

Filling In the Documents Section 

The Documents section appears in place of the Attachments field when you have enabled the 

single scan feature in your Preferences settings. 

Use the Documents section to store a digital version of a supporting document in this record. You 

can either upload a document from your computer or scan a document if you have a scanner 

attached to your computer. You must have permissions for attachments.  

If you are using Firefox, Chrome, or Edge, you can drop your file on the Attachments box to 

attach the file to this record.  

To upload a document: 

1. 
Click the Choose file button. 

2. 
Locate the document that you want to associate with this record. 

3. 
Select the document and click the Open button. 

4. 
Click the Attach button. 

To scan a document: 

1. 
In the File name field, type a name for the document that you are about to scan.  

2. 
Click the Scan button. 

3. 
In the Select Source box, select the scanner that is attached to your computer. 

4. 
Click the Select button. 

Follow the on-screen instructions to scan the document.

Filling In the A/P Invoice Entries 

The Invoice entries list varies depending on your selection of Line entry type: Standard or 

Include Job Cost. 

• 
When you select Standard, you can fill in the standard fields in the Invoice entries list.  

• 
When you select the Include Job Cost option, fields for both standard and job cost line 

items are available in the Invoice Entries list. 

Selecting default values is one method of speeding up data entry. Use this section to choose the 

values that you want the system to complete for you in the Entries list. (optional)  

After choosing the values and applying them, the system completes the fields in the Entries list 

with the values that you selected. After the system completes the fields, you can change any of 

the values, such as when one row requires a different value than the others. 

To set up default values: 

1. 
Click the Show defaults link to expand the area. 

You can specify a default value for one field, or for as many fields as are offered in the 
Defaults section.  

2. 
For each field that you want to prefill, choose the value that you enter most frequently or 

choose a value that is a standard value for the list of line items in this invoice. 

3. 
Click the Apply defaults button. The system completes the column or columns with your 

default values. Learn more about Setting default line items (on page 369). 

Entering the Line-Item Details 

The order in which the line-item columns appear varies from system to system. Some columns 

can be missing when your company chooses not to enable features such as allocations, segments, 

and assets. 

1. 
Select the Location (Location area). The location determines the accounts that appear in the 

Accounts drop-down list. The chart type associated with the property determines the 

---


<!-- Page 577 -->

accounts in the list. For the A/P invoice to be posted, you must specify at least the account 

and an amount for each line item. For more information see Chart types in the online help 

system or download the RealPage Accounting General Ledger Setup User Guide.  

2. 
In the Account column (or Account label column if you enabled A/P account labels), select 

an account to categorize the expense. Type any part of the G/L account name or number to 

have the system find it. 

If this account is flagged as 1099, or is set up as a 1099 account, you can select the 1099 

check box for individual line items. At the year’s end, the system sums up all of the Form 

1099 items for inclusion in the Form 1099. 

You can use the field-level controls to add a new G/L account, view a G/L account’s record, 
or find a G/L account’s record. To add or import G/L accounts, you must be at the top level. 

3. 
Select the No tax check box when the item is not taxable. 

4. 
In the QTY field, type the quantity of this item that you purchased. This field appears only 

when your system is enabled with Spend management. 

5. 
In the Price field, type the price of one item. This field appears only when your system is 

enabled with Spend management. 

6. 
In the Extended price field, the system fills in the field by calculating the quantity by the 

price. This field appears only when your system is enabled with Spend management. 

7. 
In the Amount field, type the cost of the item. The system requires this field to be 

populated, even if the amount is zero (0). If your system is enabled with Spend 

management, then this field is filled in automatically. 

If your system is enabled for multiple currencies, type the Transaction amount, which is the 
cost of the item expressed in the currency used in the transaction. The system calculates 
the Base amount in your company’s base currency using the exchange rate listed in the 
header. 

8. 
In the Customer column, select a customer to associate with the line item. 

9. 
In the Project column, select the project to associate with the line item. 

10. 
In the Allocation column, select an allocation template for the line item. The system 

automatically distributes the amount of the A/P invoice across the specified dimensions. 

Selecting a line item allocation template overrides the allocation template in the Entries 

defaults section. This column appears when your company has allocations enabled. 

If you use allocation for your line items, any default dimensions that you selected for those 
line items don’t flow through to the allocations table. 

Click the Show details tab and then click the Customize allocation button to set their 
values.

Allocation Splits 

Use the Allocation Splits section to override the allocation template distribution by customizing 

allocation amounts across locations, departments, customers, vendors, employees, or other 

dimensions that your system offers. 

1. 
Click the Customize Allocation button to open the Custom Allocation box. 

2. 
Type the amount of the allocation in the Amount field. 

3. 
In the dimension drop-down list or lists, select the location, department, or other dimension 

to customize. 

4. 
Click the Yes button. The system inserts the word “Custom” in the Allocation column. 

Even when an allocation with a predetermined distribution of amounts is assigned to a line 

item, you can still override these amounts. You can also override aspects of the allocation at 

the line-item level of the relevant transaction page (A/R invoices, A/P invoices, or journal 

entries).  

If you change the amounts such that the total is different from what you entered in the 
transaction page, the system updates the total when you save and return to the 
transaction page.

Using the Release to Pay Function 

Use the Release to pay function to select and authorize payment for specific line items in the 

same A/P invoice. When your system has the Release to pay setting enabled, a Release to pay 

check box appears at the end of each A/P invoice line item. 

• 
To release every line item for payment, select the check box next to the Release to pay 

option. Each item that you select will display on the Release to pay list, which you use to 

record the payments you actually make. 

You can change your mind and clear the release to pay from a line item if that item hasn’t 
been paid. 
Clear the item’s Release check box. 
Click Save. The system removes that item from the Release to pay list. 


> **Navigation Path:** `• 
To record payment for released to pay items, go to Accounts Payable > All > Payments >`


Release A/P Invoices to Pay. 

If the Release to pay check box displays but is unavailable, that means that the line item has 

already been paid. 

Distributing Costs and Discounts Across All Transactions 

Use these steps to apply costs and discounts and distribute them equally across all transactions in 

the A/P invoice. 

1. 
In the Tax amount field at the bottom of the page, type the tax on the transactions in this 

A/P invoice.  

2. 
In the Shipping amount field, type the shipping cost associated with this A/P invoice. 

3. 
In the Discount amount field, type the dollar value of the discount on this A/P invoice. 

4. 
Click the Distribute button to distribute the costs or discounts evenly across the transaction.

Entering a Note about the Transaction 

• 
Below the Discount amount field, in the Notes field, type an optional note pertaining to the 

transaction. This note appears on the customer’s version of the invoice. 

• 
To prevent this note from appearing on the invoice, delete the text in the Notes field. 

Filling In the ICB - Entries List 

This section appears when you selected the Create intercompany billing check box.  

Fill in the Entries - ICB list with the relevant ICB line items. 

1. 
In the Location drop-down list, select the entity to invoice. The location that you select must 

have a customer record associated with its entity record. 

2. 
In the Amount field, type the amount of the expense. 

3. 
In the Expense account drop-down list, select the G/L debit account. 

4. 
In the Accounts payable account drop-down list, select the Accounts payable credit 

account (if it is different from the default A/P account in your configuration). 

5. 
In the Department drop-down list, select the department related to this line item if any. 

6. 
In the Memo field, enter a note or a description of the item. You can enter up to 100 

characters in this field. 

7. 
In the Revenue account drop-down list, select the revenue account. 

8. 
In the Accounts receivable account, select the A/R account for this transaction.  

This option appears when you’ve enabled the default G/L account to be overridden. You can 

select a G/L alternative account here to override the default G/L account for all line items, or 

you can override the designated account individually per line item. 

• 
For A/P transactions, this drop-down list contains one or more alternative A/P G/L 

accounts. 

• 
For A/R transactions, this drop-down list contains one or more alternative A/R G/L 

accounts.

type and Segment value drop-down lists do not appear, then your system does not have

Saving the A/P Invoice 

When entering the transaction information, save it as a draft or post it. The system validates

validated until posting.

System Checks for Budget Exceeded  

If you try to post an A/P invoice that exceeds the default budget, and your company uses the A/P 

invoice approval process with the budget exceeded feature, the system displays a warning. The 

system may also prevent you from posting the A/P invoice. If you want to be able to bypass this 

budget check, ask your system administrator to grant you the desired bypass permission. Bypass 

permissions are available for A/P invoices and purchase orders. 

When the budget exceeded feature is enabled, the system checks the A/P invoice amount against 

the budgeted number for the G/L account. When the amount exceeds the budget, then the 

system either displays a warning or prevents you from saving the A/P invoice, depending on how 

your company configured the feature. When preventing an A/P invoice from being posted, the 

system also displays a warning to let you know why you cannot post. 

To enable or disable the budget exceeded feature, see Setting a system action when an A/P 

invoice or purchase order exceeds the budget (on page 568).  

System Checks for Attachments 

Your company may require that you attach a document to support the A/P invoice before you can 

save it as a draft, post, or submit it. If you need to save an A/P invoice without an attachment, 

contact your system administrator and ask them to remove the Require attachment permission 

(on page 266) from your role or account. 

What’s Next? 

When your company uses approvals, A/P invoices first go through the payment approval 

workflow. After payments are approved, you can make the payments.  

Go to the Pay A/P invoices page to select the invoice for payment. When you select Add to 

outbox or Pay now: 

• 
The invoice becomes a payment request. 

• 
The system notifies approvers that a payment is waiting for their approval. 

• 
You can view the status of the payment request in the Payment request list. 

• 
When an approver approves the invoice, the system pays the invoice. 

• 
If the payment method is Check, the system allows the payment to be included in a check 

run.

Setting a System Action When a Transaction Exceeds the Budget 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > Approvals > Approval Configuration`


Use this procedure to determine what happens when an A/P invoice or purchase order exceeds 

the budgeted amount.  

To set up the system action: 

1. 
Open the Company menu. 

2. 
In the Approvals section, select the Approval Configuration menu option. 

The Approval configuration page opens. 

3. 
To enable the budget warning or prevention for A/P invoices:

Find the A/P Invoice Approvals section.

Select the Enable preventing or warning a user when adding a Purchase Order that 

exceeds the budget check box.

budgeted amount by the purchase order, select Warn. 

• 
To have the system prevent the user from posting the purchase order, select Prevent.

message.

### Vendor Record Approval Process
*Source: `RP Accounting AP Daily Tasks User Guide.pdf`, Page 600*

Enter AP Invoices Section 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Daily Tasks User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Vendor Record Approval Process 

This section describes how to participate in the vendor record approval process. 

1. 
A user (“the requester”) creates a new vendor record (on page 70). 

2. 
The system checks the vendor record approval policy to see if it requires approval for new 

and updated vendor records.  

• 
If it does, the system adds the vendor record to the approval queue.  

• 
If it does not, the system adds the vendor record to the Vendors list, and this is the 

end of the process. 

The user who adds or edits the vendor record cannot be the person who approves the 
vendor request. If no one else has permission to approve vendors, then an administrator 
will need to assign that permission (on page 120 ) to at least one other user. Otherwise, 
the vendor request will be stuck in the approval queue. 

3. 
The requester can view the status of the vendor record he created or updated (the “vendor 

request”) using the View vendor requests (on page 585) option. 

4. 
The system notifies approvers that a record is pending approval. 

5. 
Approvers can click a link in the email notification (on page 588) to open the system to 

where the vendor record is waiting for approval. 

6. 
The approver reviews the vendor record in the Approve vendors list (on page 586). 

7. 
The approver approves or declines the vendor record (on page 586). 

• 
If approved, the system moves approved vendor records to the vendors list.  

• 
If declined, the system deactivates declined vendor records.  

8. 
The requester checks with the approver to find out why the vendor was declined and then 

resolves the problem. 

---


<!-- Page 601 -->
Chapter 7: Enter AP Invoices Section 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Daily Tasks User Guide 

9. 
The requester recreates the vendor record, and the approval process begins from step 1.  

---
