Approve Vendors List 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > All > Daily Tasks > Approve Vendors`


Use the Approve vendors list to review new and updated vendor records. From the list, you can: 

• 
View a vendor record’s details. If it is an updated record, the edits are noted in the record. 

• 
Approve or decline one vendor record. 

• 
Select and then approve or decline multiple vendor records. 

• 
Export the list of vendor records that are pending approval. 

Use the list controls to create custom views and filter and sort the list. See Managing the List for 

details. 

Approving Vendors 

When the vendor record approval feature is enabled, you can evaluate and approve new vendor 

records and updated vendor records. 

The user who adds or edits the vendor record cannot be the person who approves the vendor 
request. If no one else has permission to approve vendors, then an administrator will need to 
assign that permission (on page 120 ) to at least one other user. Otherwise, the vendor request 
will be stuck in the approval queue. 

Approving New Vendors 

To assess new vendor records and approve or decline them: 

1. 
Open the Accounts payable menu. 

2. 
Select Approve vendors. 

3. 
Find the new vendor record, indicated in the Type column. 

4. 
Click the View link to open the vendor record to review it.  

5. 
Click the Approve or Decline button. Alternatively, click the Done button to return to the 

Approve vendors list so that you can view the next vendor record in your approval queue.  

6. 
After reviewing all queued vendor records, you can select the vendor records that you want 

to approve or decline and then select the Approve or Decline button to approve or decline 

them in bulk.

### AI-Invoice Scanning
*Source: `RP Accounting AP Daily Tasks User Guide.pdf`, Page 609*

Chapter 7: Enter AP Invoices Section 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Daily Tasks User Guide 

AI-Invoice Scanning 

The AI-Invoice feature automates the process of bringing A/P invoices into the system, creating 

A/P invoice records by reading and extracting key information from the invoice document.  

How It Works 

The AI agent receives invoices when you scan, upload, or email invoices to the system. You can 

scan or upload invoices directly into the Financial Suite or set up an email address for vendors 

and employees to send invoices for AI processing. 

The AI agent scans the document and extracts all relevant information, including the invoice 

number, date, amount, vendor, property, and line-item descriptions.  

To find a vendor in the system that matches the vendor on the invoice, the agent first looks for a 

vendor record with a matching Vendor name. If it doesn’t find a match, then it will look for a 

matching Print as name instead. If it still doesn’t find a match, it will check for a matching vendor 

address. 

After the AI agent processes an invoice, the result is an A/P invoice record. You can view the 

invoice records that the agent created in the AI-invoice queue list. 

Configuration 

Before you can use the AI-Invoice Scanning agent, you must enable the AI-Invoice Scanning 

function and configure its settings. See Configuring AI-Invoice Scanning (on page 595) for more 

information. 

Agent Processing Results 

After configuring AI-invoice scanning, use the following pages to track the progress of invoices 

that have been processed by the AI-Invoice scanning agent: 

• 
AI-Invoice Queue: (on page 604) This page displays a list of all invoices successfully 

processed by the AI-Invoice feature.  

• 
AI-Invoice Upload Audit (on page 631): This page provides an additional view for 

administrators to monitor which email addresses the invoices are submitted from, what time 

they’re submitted, and who submitted them. 

To monitor the scanned invoice progress, you can add an action card to your Home page for AI 

invoice queue count. To add an action card, see Adding a Finance Agent Action Card to the 

Home Page. 

---


<!-- Page 610 -->

When the AI Agent Fails to Match an Invoice to a Property 

When an invoice is sent into the AI-Invoice queue and the AI Finance Agent cannot identify the 

property, the AI agent creates invoice but does not assign a property to it. The AI agent places the 

invoice in the AI-Invoice Queue list where the submitter can access it.  

For other users to access these property-less invoices, they must have a special permission. To 

grant a user access to these invoices, assign the user the View Invoices with No Property Defined 

permission.

### AI-Invoice Intake
*Source: `RP Accounting AP Daily Tasks User Guide.pdf`, Page 615*

Chapter 7: Enter AP Invoices Section 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Daily Tasks User Guide 

AI-Invoice Intake 

You can load a file containing invoice data to have the system use AI to analyze the file and turn it 

into an invoice record.  

Loading the Invoice Data 

When you load a file with invoice information, the system uses AI to analyze the file and create a 

new invoice using the data from the uploaded file. When the file has multiple pages with separate 

invoices on each page, the pages are separated and an invoice is created for each page.  

You can load the invoice file using three methods: 

• 
Scanning: Scan an invoice with a scanning device to add it to the queue. 

• 
Emailing: Send invoice files to the email address that your company defined during 

configuration (on page 595). It is the address that ends with @ap.realpage.com. 

• 
Importing: Import an invoice file from your computer. 

Required Data 

The A/P invoices that you add to the system using AI must contain the following data: 

• 
Date 

• 
Vendor 

• 
Invoice number 

• 
Total invoice amount 

• 
Due date 

Line items must contain: 

• 
Location 

• 
Either Price or Amount must be included.  

---


<!-- Page 616 -->
Enter AP Invoices Section 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Daily Tasks User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

How AI Matches Invoices to Properties 

As the system creates an invoice record, it tries to match the property name on the invoice with 

the entity name in the system. If it does not match the entity name, it checks the Property name 

field of the entity record. This is the field where the property’s alias is stored. If it does not match 

the entity name or the property name, the system checks the address. 

It will also search on likeness. If the entity in the system is “Glenview Living Apartments” and 

“Glenview Living” is shown on the invoice, the system will match the two because they are similar. 

This method is also used when matching vendor records.  

The AI agent removes special characters from names and addresses before the matching process 

and ignores case sensitivity in names and addresses. 

How the AI Agent Matches Entity Name and Addresses 

When the AI agent receives an invoice, it scans the information and compares the invoice details 

to the corresponding entity name, property name, and the Ship to property address. 

If the invoice has only one address, the AI agent compares the address on the invoice to the Ship 

to address in the entity record in the system. 

If the invoice has two addresses, the AI agent: 

a) First checks the name and address in the Ship to area on the invoice to find a match with an 

entity record in the system.  

b) If it does not find a match, the AI agent checks if the other name on the invoice matches an 

entity in the system.  

---


<!-- Page 617 -->
Chapter 7: Enter AP Invoices Section 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Daily Tasks User Guide 

How the AI Agent Matches the Vendor 

When the AI agent receives an invoice, it compares the vendor name on the invoice and tries to 

get a 90% match with the vendor name in the system. It does not require an exact match to 

identify the vendor name. The AI agent also tries to match the vendor’s address. 

Utility and Telecommunications Invoices 

The system can recognize an invoice for utility or telecommunication services when the vendor’s 

Vendor type field is set to “utility” or “Utility type.” 

When you email, upload, or scan invoices into the system, and it detects an invoice for utility or 

telecommunication services, the system processes them differently.  

• 
For utility vendors, the system sets the Do not itemize option automatically so that only the 

total amount is coded.  

• 
If the system finds an account number on the invoice, it sets the Invoice number field to the 

account number. 

• 
If the system finds service dates, it sets the Invoice number field to the account number 

plus service date range.  

Attachments 

When a document includes multiple invoices, the system automatically separates the PDF into 

individual invoice documents. Each extracted invoice is attached only to its corresponding invoice 

record. 

• 
Multi-invoice PDFs are automatically split into individual invoice files. 

• 
Each invoice record receives only the attachment that belongs to it. 

---


<!-- Page 618 -->
Enter AP Invoices Section 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Daily Tasks User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

G/L Accounts 

The system uses historical data to code the items with a G/L account.  

When the system processes a new A/P invoice, it reviews previously entered invoices for the same 

vendor and item descriptions, and identifies patterns in how the invoices have been coded for the 

vendor. Using this historical data, the system suggests the most frequently used G/L accounts, 

and automatically pre-sets the GL account to the most likely account. 

The system presents a list of suggested G/L accounts for each line item. 

The system runs this same process on eInvoices. 

Line Items 

The system creates a line item for each charge. The system identifies a credit when it detects 

“Credit memo” in the invoice data. When the system identifies a credit, it creates a line item with a 

negative amount. 

If you prefer, you can enable the Do not itemize invoice option to have the system create one 

line item per invoice. You can turn on this option for all invoices, or by vendor only.  

• 
To turn on the feature system wide, see Scanning Invoices Without Itemization (on page 

609).  

• 
To control the option not to itemize for one vendor, see Adding Vendor Records (on page 

70). 

---


<!-- Page 619 -->
Chapter 7: Enter AP Invoices Section 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Daily Tasks User Guide 

Submitting or Posting 

When the auto post option is enabled and the loaded invoice contains all of the required data, 

the system automatically submits the invoices for review and approval. If approvals are not 

enabled, then the system posts the invoices. 

If the required fields are incomplete, then the system creates the invoice records and saves them 

as drafts. 

You can change this setting in Company > AI Configuration. Find the AI Invoice Scanning section, 

and then select or clear the Automatically submit or post AI Invoices if all required information 

is defined check box.

#### Setting Up a Property Alias
*Source: `RP Accounting AP Daily Tasks User Guide.pdf`, Page 621*

Setting Up a Property Alias 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > Entities > Edit > Property Name`


You can create an alias for a property name to help the system’s AI recognize the property on 

scanned invoices—even if the name differs slightly from the official record. This improves invoice 

automation and reduces manual review. 

Creating a Property Name Alias 

An alias can be a nickname, a commonly used abbreviation, or an alternate spelling of the 

property. 

To create an alias for a property: 

1. 
Open the Company menu. 

2. 
Click Entities. 

3. 
Find the entity record associated with the property, and then click the Edit link. 

4. 
Type the alias (such as the commonly used name or abbreviation) in the Property Name 

field. 

Tip: Use consistent naming conventions and include a common variation that vendors 
might use. If no alias is created and the invoice name doesn’t match, the system may not 
recognize the property, leading to processing delays. 

5. 
Click Save. 

During AI invoice processing, the system checks the name on the invoice to see if it matches 

either the entity name or the property name (alias).

Predefining Invoice Data

Uploading the Invoice Files 

1. 
Click the Upload button. The AI agent scans the information in the invoice file and creates 

an invoice record with information that it can read from the file.  

The system displays the message “Attachment uploaded successfully. AI scanning will 

happen offline.”  

2. 
Click OK. 

You can continue uploading additional invoices, or click Cancel to close the AI-Invoice 

Scanning box. 

How the AI Agent Fills In Missing Information 

If you do not predefine a G/L account, and the AI agent does not find one on the invoice, then the 

AI agent checks if there are any previous invoices for the same vendor with the same items, and 

with a similar memo. If the AI agent finds a matching invoice, then the system automatically codes 

the new invoice based on the historical invoice. 

On the invoice, the system creates a Suggested G/L section that contains a list of G/L accounts that 

have been used previously on invoices for this vendor. The section includes suggested G/L 

accounts for each line item. 

If the AI agent doesn’t find any prior invoices with G/L accounts, then the system uses the default 

expense account from the vendor. If the vendor does not have a default expense account, then 

the system sets the default expense account for online shopping, if enabled.

Click the Scan button. The system scans in the invoice, reads the information, creates a new 

A/P invoice record, fills in the invoice record with information read from the image, and then 

adds the invoice to the AI-Invoice Queue list. 

Scanning Invoices Without Itemization 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Finance Agent > Setup > AI Configuration > AI-Invoice Scanning > Do 
Not Itemize Invoices`


You can control how the system treats line items as it scans invoices.  

To change the setting: 

1. 
Click AI Configuration. 

2. 
In the AI-Invoice Scanning section, select the Do not itemize invoices check box. When this 

check box is selected, all invoices that you scan in through AI will have a single line item for 

the total invoice amount. When this check box is cleared, the system creates line items for 

each item that it identifies in a scanned invoice.  

3. 
Click Save.

#### Reviewing AI-Invoices
*Source: `RP Accounting AP Daily Tasks User Guide.pdf`, Page 628*

Enter AP Invoices Section 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Daily Tasks User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Reviewing AI-Invoices 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > All > Daily Tasks > AI-Invoice Queue > Review`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Finance Agent > All > AI Invoicing > AI Invoice Queue > Review`


To review AI-scanned invoices: 

1. 
Open the Accounts Payable menu. 

2. 
In the Daily Tasks section, click the AI-Invoice queue option. 

3. 
Click the Review button. The AI-Invoice Scanning page opens, displaying the invoice record 

on one side, and the scanned (or imported) image on the other side.  

4. 
Make any needed corrections and additions. 

You can archive the invoice, post the invoice, save the invoice, or if approvals are enabled, 

submit the invoice for approval. 

Finishing the Review 

To finish a review, you can either archive the invoice, post or submit the invoice, or save the 

invoice. 

• 
Click the Archive button to archive the invoice. 

• 
To post the invoice, select Post & Next. To skip this invoice and display the next invoice in 

the queue, click the Post & Next down arrow, and then click Next. This button appears only 

if the approval workflow is disabled for A/P invoices. 

• 
To submit the invoice for approval, select Submit & Next. To skip this invoice and display 

the next invoice in the queue, click the Submit & Next down arrow, and then click Next.  

This option appears only when the approval workflow is enabled for A/P invoices. If your 
account has been granted the Bypass Transaction Approval - A/P Invoice permission, then 
the Post & Next button appears instead of the Submit & Next button. 

• 
To save the invoice, select Save & Next. You can skip this invoice by clicking the Save & 

Next down arrow and then clicking Next.

Editing AI-Invoices

To edit an AI scanned-in invoice: 

1. 
Open the Accounts Payable menu. 

2. 
In the Daily Tasks section, click the AI-Invoice queue option. 

3. 
Find the invoice that you want to change, and then click the Edit link. 

4. 
Make the desired changes. 

Finalizing the Edited Invoice 

• 
To post the invoice, select Post & Next. You can also click the Post & Next down arrow, and 

then click Next.  

• 
To submit the invoice for approval, click the Submit & Next button. You can also click the 

Submit & Next down arrow, and then click Next.  

This option appears only when the approval workflow is enabled for A/P invoices. If your 
account has been granted the Bypass Transaction Approval - A/P Invoice permission, then 
the Post & Next button appears instead of the Submit & Next button. 

• 
To save the invoice, select Save & Next. You can also click the Save & Next down arrow, and 

then click Next. Use this option when you want to submit the invoice later.  

• 
To archive the changed invoice, click the Archive button. This option hides the invoice from 

view in the queue, letting you focus on invoices that need to be reviewed now. You can 

include archived invoices in the list by selecting the Show archived check box above the list.

You can delete invoices to remove them from the queue permanently.  

To delete invoices from the queue: 

1. 
Open the Accounts Payable menu.  

2.

3.

the number of days until the payment is due. 

Overdue: When an invoice passes the due date, this field contains the 

number of days that the payment is past due. 

Invoice total 
This is the amount that is due on the due date.

invoice.

DRAFT

as a draft instead of posting it. 

% 
This is the confidence barometer. The system determines how 

confident you can be that the A/P invoice is valid and should be paid. 

Colors help to show the confidence level. Green indicates that 

confidence is high. 

You can configure the system to approve A/P invoices based on 

confidence level automatically.

Date

 Calendar button to select the date of the 

invoice.

invoice. This field is required. 

G/L posting date 

Type the date or click the 
 Calendar button to select the date to post 

the A/P invoice to the General Ledger. 

The G/L posting date appears on this page only if enabled on the 

Configure Accounts Payable page. This is the date on which the 

transaction actually posts to the general ledger. Unless you change it, 

this date defaults to the transaction date. 

Total invoice amount Type the total amount, the sum of all line items, in this field. This field is 

required. 

This field is controlled by the Enable invoice entry control validation 

check box. When selected, the system validates that the total invoice 

amount equals the total amount defined in the line items and the Total 

invoice amount field appears on the A/P invoice page.  

Vendor (Supplier) 
Select the vendor (supplier) that is the source of the A/P invoice. You can 

either select a vendor from the drop-down list or type the name of the 

vendor for the A/P invoice. For vendors that you use often, it’s best to 

create vendor records for them in the system. This field is required. 

You can use the field controls to add a new vendor, view a vendor’s 

record, or find a vendor’s record.  

To add or import vendors, you must be at the top level. 

Pay to 
Select the vendor contact to whom you want to send the payment.  

The system automatically completes this field from the Pay to contact 

field in the Vendor record. If the Pay to contact is empty, then the 

system uses the contact associated with the vendor record. You can 

override the contact by selecting a different one on this page. As an 

example, a vendor that has multiple offices may request that you send 

the check to an office other than the one on record.

Return to 
Select the vendor contact to whom you want to send a return of the 

purchase. By default, this is the Return to contact on the Vendor record.  

If it is not filled in, then the system uses the contact associated with the 

vendor that you selected on this page. In most cases, you won’t need to 

override the default, but you can override it as needed. As an example, 

when returning a defective product, the vendor may request that you 

return it to a location other than the one on record. 

State 
The state of the invoice: 

• 
Submitted: The invoice is saved and submitted to the approval 

workflow. 

• 
Declined: Approvers declined the invoice. 

• 
Selected: The invoice is selected for payment but not yet paid. 

• 
Draft: The invoice is saved but not yet posted or submitted for 

approval. 

• 
Posted: The invoice is posted to the General Ledger. 

• 
Partially paid: Only part of the invoice is paid. 

• 
Partially approved: A transaction can have more than one 

approver. The invoice is approved by at least one approver in 

the workflow, but more approvals are required. 

• 
Paid: The invoice is paid in full. 

• 
Reversed: The invoice has been reversed. 

• 
Reversal: The listed transaction is the reversal created from the 

reversed invoice. 

This field appears only after you save the invoice. 

Invoice number 
Type a unique number to assign to the invoice. 

To set an alarm for duplicate numbers, or to disallow duplicate numbers 

for this vendor, see Configure Accounts Payable. This number prints on 

the check remittance stub, but not on the check itself. 

This field is required.

### AI-Invoice Upload Audit
*Source: `RP Accounting AP Daily Tasks User Guide.pdf`, Page 649*



### AI-Invoice Upload Audit List
*Source: `RP Accounting AP Daily Tasks User Guide.pdf`, Page 649*

Chapter 7: Enter AP Invoices Section 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Daily Tasks User Guide 

AI-Invoice Upload Audit 

Use the AI-Invoice Upload Audit menu option to view the AI-Invoice Audit list which contains a 

list of invoices processed by the AI-Invoice feature.  

AI-Invoice Upload Audit List 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > All > Daily Tasks > AI-Invoice Upload Audit`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Finance Agent > All > AI Invoicing > AI Invoice Upload Audit`


Use this list to monitor and troubleshoot AI-Invoice processing issues. From this list, you can 

monitor the sources of invoices being submitted, the time that the invoices were submitted, and 

who submitted them.  

You must be an administrator to view this list. The AI-Invoice Upload Audit list is also available to 

administrators in Site View. 

 In this list, you can: 

• 
Click the 
 Attachment button to open the processed invoice image. 

• 
Find out more information about processing failures by clicking the Failed link in the Result 

column. 

Possible results include: 

• 
Success: The invoice image is successfully added to the system.  

• 
Failed: The invoice was not added to the system. Click the Failed link to find out why. Click 

the 
 Attachment button so that you can display and download the invoice. 

• 
Submitted: The invoice is being uploaded and is pending processing by the AI agent. 

What to Do When an Invoice Fails 

The Result column shows Failed when an invoice fails to upload. 

When an invoice fails, you can: 

• 
Click the Retry upload link to have the AI agent try to process the invoice again. 

• 
Click the Failed link to review the reason for the failure. If the invoice failed due to missing 

required information, contact the vendor to get an updated invoice. 

• 
Contact RealPage support with the downloaded failed invoice and the error message. Click 

the Failed link to get the error message. Click the 
 Attachment button to display and 

download the invoice so that you can give it to the support representative. 

---

a) 
When the system fails to upload an invoice, it has a Retry Upload link. Click the link to 

try to upload the invoice again. 

b) 
Click the Failed link to show the error that describes why the upload failed. 

c) 
Click the 
 Attachment button to display the image of the invoice. 

Troubleshooting AI-Processed Invoices 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > All > Daily Tasks > AI-Invoice Upload Audit`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Finance Agent > All > AI Invoicing > AI Invoice Upload Audit`


When you scan or upload an invoice and it does not appear in the queue, you can check the 

AI-Invoice Upload Audit list to gather information about why the invoice processing failed.  

Only administrators can access the AI-Invoice Upload Audit list. 

To use the audit list for troubleshooting: 

1. 
Open the Accounts Payable menu. 

2. 
In the Daily Tasks section, click the AI-Invoice Upload Audit option. 

3. 
Review the list for pertinent details: 

• 
Check the Result column to see if the invoice processing failed.  

• 
If an invoice failed, click the Failed link to view the system message about the failure. 

The message often provides the reason for the failure. 

• 
In the Uploaded by column, find out who uploaded the invoice. You can use the email 

address to contact the user to get more information about the invoice as needed. 

• 
Collect details about the failed invoices, such as invoice number, amount, and the date 

it was scanned.

Document Dashboard

Use the Document dashboard to queue and monitor commercial invoices being processed. From 

the Document dashboards page, you can monitor the progress of all of your queued documents 

and access individual queues. 

Using Document Dashboards 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > All > Document Dashboard`


From the Document dashboards list, you can click a queue name to view the list of documents in 

the queue. The queue shows the document’s index ID, how it was added to the system, the 

reason that the document cannot be processed, the date that the document was added, and who 

added it.

Document Dashboards List 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > All > Document Dashboard`


The Document dashboard offers insight into your company’s invoice processing workflow. The 

dashboard shows the various document queues that have been set up in your system, and how 

many documents are in each queue. 

If your company subscribes to Spend Management and Site Experience, the documents that users 

upload through Site Experience also appear in this list in the Site View queue. 

Use the Document Dashboard option to view the number of document images queued for action 

in each queue. You can also add a document image to a queue by uploading a PDF file, or by 

scanning a document directly into a queue. 

• 
Click a queue name to see the list of documents in a specific queue.  

• 
Click the Site View queue to view a list of documents that users have uploaded using the 

Site Experience. 

• 
Click the Add images button to scan documents into a queue. 

• 
Click the Upload images button to add an external file to a queue. Files must be in PDF 

format.  

• 
Click the Export button to export the data in this list to a file. 

Queues are created in the Accounts payable application’s Setup tab. If you have appropriate 
permissions, you can create and rename queues as needed. Configure document dashboard 
queues to use document dashboards. 

Use the list controls to create custom views and filter and sort the list. See Managing the List for 

details.

Preparing for Scanning 

Insert a blank page between invoices as you scan to have the system divide your scanned image 

into separate files so that it will store one invoice per file. As the system uploads a scanned image, 

it starts a new file every time it detects a blank page. 

Scanning Document Images into a Queue 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > All > Document Dashboard > Add Images`


If you enabled the Single Scan Upload feature in your preferences and have previously 
downloaded the Dynamsoft scanning software, you may be prompted to update the software 
when you add a new scannable record such as an A/P invoice, vendor, purchase order, service 
contract, or an image in the document dashboard. When this occurs, download the new software; 
there is no need to uninstall the previous version. 

To scan a document into a queue: 

1. 
Open the Accounts payable menu. 

2. 
Select Document dashboard. 

3. 
Click the Add images button. The Add images box opens. 

4. 
In the Assign to queue drop-down list, select the queue to which to assign the document. 

The Site View queue does not appear in the drop-down list. You can only add documents to 
the Site View queue by uploading images from Spend Management’s Site Experience. 

5. 
Click the Scan button. The system displays the Select source box. 

6. 
Select your scanner from the list, and then click the Select button. The scanner’s box opens.  

---


<!-- Page 657 -->
Chapter 7: Enter AP Invoices Section 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Daily Tasks User Guide 

7. 
Using your scanner’s controls, scan the document. Upon success, the scanned document 

appears in the queue.  

You can see the documents that you scanned in from Site Experience in the Site View 

queue. 

---

#### Dividing a Document Image into Separate Invoice Files
*Source: `RP Accounting AP Daily Tasks User Guide.pdf`, Page 660*

Enter AP Invoices Section 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Daily Tasks User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Dividing a Document Image into Separate Invoice Files 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > All > Document Dashboard`


To separate a document image into separate files: 

1. 
In the Document Dashboard, click the queue with the document that you want to separate. 

2. 
Find the document that you want to separate, and then click the number in the Index ID 

column. 

The Invoice Processing page opens. 

3. 
Examine the file and determine how you want to separate the file.  

4. 
Enter a page range for the first file to create.  

Example: 

---


<!-- Page 661 -->
Chapter 7: Enter AP Invoices Section 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Daily Tasks User Guide 

If the first invoice is on pages 1 and 2 of the scanned images, then type “1-2.” 

5. 
Click the Create New button. The system creates a new file for the invoice, deletes the 

pages from the original file, and renumbers the pages of the original file. 

6. 
Repeat the process by typing a page number range for the next invoice, and clicking Create 

New. 

7. 
When you have finished separating the invoices in the image file, click Save. You can also 

click Save & Next to open the next scanned image. 

8. 
Click the Done button to leave the Invoice Processing page and return to the list of 

document queues.

#### Removing Pages from a Document Image
*Source: `RP Accounting AP Daily Tasks User Guide.pdf`, Page 662*

Enter AP Invoices Section 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Daily Tasks User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Removing Pages from a Document Image 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > All > Document Dashboard`


To remove pages from a scanned image: 

1. 
In the Document Dashboard, click the queue with the document that has pages that you 

want to remove. 

2. 
Find the document with the pages that you want to remove, and then click the number in 

the Index ID column. 

The Invoice Processing page opens. 

3. 
Examine the file and note the page number of the first page that you want to remove. 

4. 
Type the page number in the field next to the Remove Pages button. 

5. 
Click the Remove Pages button. 

When you remove a page in the middle of the file, the system renumbers the pages.  

6. 
Check the page number of the next page that you want to remove, and then repeat steps 4 

- 5.  

7. 
Click Save when you have finished removing the desired pages. You can also click the Save 

& Next button to open the next file in the queue. 

8. 
Click Done to close the Invoice Processing page and return to the list of document queues.

When you’re reviewing the document queue and processing invoices, you may need to create a

1. 
Open the Accounts payable menu. 

2. 
Select Document dashboard. 

3. 
Click the Queue name of the queue to review. The Document Queues list opens. 

4. 
Click the Index ID of the queue to review. The system displays the Invoice Processing page. 

Navigate the invoices in the queue using the Previous and Next buttons.  

5. 
When you need to create a new A/P invoice, select the Standard A/P Entry check box, and 

then click the Create A/P Invoice button. The system opens the standard A/P invoice page. 

When the Standard A/P Entry check box is not selected, the system opens a condensed 

form for entering the invoice details instead of the full A/P invoice page.

page 379) for help in filling in the A/P invoice information. 

7. 
When you finish entering the transaction information, save it as a draft or post it.  

Click the Draft button and select: 

• 
Draft & Continue to save the transaction and continue working on it. 

• 
Draft to save your progress on the transaction without posting it to the system. Later, 

you or another user can review and post it.  

• 
Draft & New to save the transaction and create a new transaction of the same type. 

The system saves your progress on the transaction without posting it. 

Click Post and select: 

• 
Post to post the transaction. 

• 
Post & New to post the transaction and create a new transaction of the same type.

Putting a Hold on a Queued Document 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > All > Document Dashboard > (queue name) > (index 
ID)`


To put a hold on a document: 

1. 
Open the Accounts payable menu. 

2. 
Select Document dashboard, and then click the queue name. The system displays the 

Document Queues list. 

3. 
Click the index ID of a queued invoice. The system displays the Invoice Processing page. 

4. 
In the Reason drop-down list, select the reason that you are putting a document on hold. 

5. 
Click the Save button. The system changes the document’s status to Saved. 

Removing Pages from a Document in the Queue 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > All > Document Dashboard > [queue name] > 
[Index ID]`


When you are reviewing the document queue and processing invoices, you may need to remove 

pages from a document. 

1. 
Open the Accounts payable menu. 

2. 
Select Document dashboard. 

3. 
Click the Queue name of the queue to review. The Document Queues list opens. 

4. 
Click the Index ID of the queue to review. The system opens the Invoice Processing page. 

The name of the queue displays in the Queue drop-down list. 

5. 
In the Reason drop-down list, select the reason that you are removing pages from the 

document. 

6. 
In the field next to the Remove Pages button, type the page numbers that you want to 

remove. 

7. 
Click the Remove Pages button. 

8. 
Click Save. You can also click the Save and Next button to save the change, and then open 

the next document. Click Done to return to the Document Queues list.

A/P Invoice Short Form  

Fields 

Date 
Select or type the transaction date. When entering a new A/P invoice, 

the date defaults to the current date. You can choose to enter a different 

date such as the date on the A/P invoice. 

This field is required. 

G/L posting date

Accounts Payable page. This is the date on which the transaction

RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Daily Tasks User Guide 

Total invoice amount Enter the total amount, the sum of all line items, in this field. 

This field is required. 

Vendor  
Select the vendor that is the source of the A/P invoice. You can either 

select a vendor from the drop-down list or type the name of the vendor 

for the A/P invoice. For vendors you use repeatedly, it’s best to enter 

them into the system. This field is required. 

You can use the field level controls to Add a new vendor, View a 

vendor’s record, or Find a vendor’s record.  

To add or import vendors, you must be at the top level. 

Invoice number 
The record number assigned to the A/P invoice by the vendor.  

To set an alarm for duplicate numbers, or to disallow duplicate numbers 

for this vendor, see Configure Accounts Payable. This number prints on 

the check remittance stub, but not on the check itself. 

This field is required. 

Reference number 
This is a number, such as a purchase order or account number, which 

may be useful in searches or reports on this A/P invoice. This number 

shows on the G/L Details report but does not print on the check or 

check remittance stub. 

When Invoice Processing creates an A/P invoice, the process inserts the 

account number in this field. 

Description  
Enter information that you want stored with this A/P invoice. This 

information prints on the Vendor Ledger report but does not print on 

the check or remittance stub. 

Term 
The system uses terms selected here to calculate due date, discounts, 

and penalties associated with this A/P invoice.  

Due date 
The system calculates the due date based on the A/P invoice date and 

terms. Changes in either are reflected in the due date. You can type or 

select a due date that overrides the calculated date. This field is 

required. 

Place this invoice on 

hold (check box) 

When an A/P invoice is on hold, the system does not display the A/P 

invoice in the Approve Payments list or Pay A/P invoices page. However, 

the system does display the A/P invoice in reports such as the A/P 

Invoices Register. 

You can place the vendor on hold, if needed.

### Create Payment Requests Page
*Source: `RP Accounting AP Daily Tasks User Guide.pdf`, Page 678*

Enter AP Invoices Section 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Daily Tasks User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Create Payment Requests Page 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > All > Daily Tasks > Create Payment Requests`


The Create Payment Requests menu option appears on the Accounts Payable menu only upon 

request. Contact RealPage Support to request this menu option. 

• 
When this option is enabled, you can create payment requests directly from this menu 

option. 

• 
When not enabled, you create payment requests by paying an A/P invoice.  

After enabling payment approvals, pay some A/P invoices. After payment, the system 

creates a payment request. Payments that are waiting for approval are called payment 

requests. After a payment request is paid, it becomes a posted payment.  

Before You Begin 

• 
Enable approvals for payments. This means that your company must enable the approvals 

workflow for your system and configure the approval workflow for payments.  

Create Payment Requests Page 

Use this page to create payment requests manually. From this page, you can also: 

• 
Refresh the list. 

• 
Delete draft payment requests. 

• 
Export the list of draft payment requests. 

• 
View the list of A/P invoices in a vendor’s draft payment request. 

This page is divided into three parts: 

• 
Filters 

• 
Payment options 

• 
Payment request drafts 

Filters 

Use the filters to narrow the payment request drafts by: 

• 
Vendors. 

• 
Vendor type. 

• 
The person who submitted the payment request. 

• 
Location. 

Select the desired filters, and then click the Apply filters button. 

---

*Source: `RP Accounting AP Daily Tasks User Guide.pdf`, Page 679*

Chapter 7: Enter AP Invoices Section

RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Daily Tasks User Guide 

Payment Options

•

•

Payment Request Drafts 

Select the payment requests from the resulting list, and then click the button corresponding to 

the desired action: 

• 
Create 

•

•

•

Creating a Payment Request from a Draft 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > All > Daily Tasks > Create Payment Requests`


To create a payment request from a draft payment request: 

1. 
Open the Accounts Payable menu. 

2. 
In the Daily Tasks section, click the Create Payment Requests option. 

3. 
On the Create Payment Requests page, set up the filters that will retrieve the payment 

requests you want to work on. 

4. 
Click the Apply filters button.  

5. 
In the Payment options section, select a checking account to use for the payments.  

6. 
Set the payment date. 

7. 
In the Payment request drafts section, select the payment requests that you want to pay.  

The system monitors the checking account’s available balance against the payment request 

total and displays a message if the payment requests exceed the amount that you have 

available in the checking account. 

8. 
Click the Create button. The confirmation box opens.  

9. 
Type your email address in the field, and then click the Confirm button. The system 

processes your payment requests. 

---

Payment Requests List 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > All > View Payment Requests`


Use the Payment requests list to review, change, and cancel payments that have been submitted 

for approval. You can check the status of an A/P invoice payment that you submitted for payment. 

The Payment request list enables you to: 

• 
View the A/P invoices and credits included in the payment request. 

• 
Remove an A/P invoice from a request. 

• 
Navigate to the detail of an A/P invoice or credit where you can even edit it or reclassify it. 

• 
Track an A/P invoice payment. 

• 
Edit: Click to open the payment request and change it as needed. 

• 
View: Click to review the details of a payment request. 

• 
Cancel request: Select the Cancel Request check box of payment requests that you want to 

cancel. By canceling a payment request, you can address a problem with a payment, and 

then resubmit it. 

• 
Export: Click the Export button and select the format in which to export the list of payment 

requests. 

If you’ve added payment requests to your A/P outbox, those requests are in a draft state and 

ready for you to view, edit, or cancel them as needed, or move them forward into the next phase 

of the workflow.  

The Payment request list enables you to view the A/P invoices and credits included in the request, 

remove an A/P invoice from a request, navigate to the detail of an A/P invoice or credit, or even 

navigate to an A/P invoice or credit to edit or reclassify it. 

The items you can see on this page vary slightly depending on whether your company is an 
enterprise, or a multi-entity shared company. If your company is a multi-entity shared company 
at the top level, you initially see only the items that were created at the top level. To see items 
created in the entities, select the Include private check box. Also, when you edit an item that 
was created in an entity, your changes apply to that entity. After you save your changes, you are 
returned to the top level.  

You can add a custom view to add more columns to your view of the list using Manage views > 

Create new view.

#### Payment Statuses
*Source: `RP Accounting AP Daily Tasks User Guide.pdf`, Page 694*

Enter AP Invoices Section 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Daily Tasks User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Payment Statuses 

This is a list of the possible payment statuses: 

• 
(blank):  

• 
For Petty Cash Reimbursement, Utility Reimbursement, and Virtual Refunds: The 

payment request has not yet been sent. 

• 
For other payment methods, when the Payment Status column is blank, it means that 

the system has not processed the payment. 

• 
ACH Credit Issued: The payment has been included in transactions sent to the bank to debit 

and deposit to the supplier’s bank account. (AvidPay direct payments) 

• 
Approved: The payment is selected and approved, but not yet confirmed. This status 

appears only when approvals are enabled. When approvals are not enabled, see the 

Delivered status. 

• 
Authorized: The bank has approved the payment, but it hasn’t yet been sent to the 

processor. 

• 
AvidPay Check Issued to Supplier: When AvidXchange receives payment details for a 

supplier (vendor), they print and mail a check to the supplier. This happens on the first 

business day after the supplier’s invoice is approved for payment. 

• 
Bad Request: The system ran into an issue processing the payment request. Click the View 

details link and then download the response to see what the error was. 

• 
Cleared: The money has fully transferred from one account to the other. 

• 
Cleared - With Exception(s): The money has fully transferred from one account to the other, 

but there are issues with the transfer. 

• 
Conflict: The payment request was in the Bad Request state, and you sent it again. 

• 
Created: (Third Party Payment) – This status is only used for Nexus payments, and means 

that the payment has been sent to Nexus.  

• 
Customer Funds Received: The organization received the payment from the customer to 

cover a debit return. (deprecated) 

• 
Debit Requested: AvidPay has sent information to the bank to request the debit. Depending 

on your bank, the funds could appear on hold in your bank account either that night, or the 

next day. 

• 
Declined: A payment has been declined by the system. The transaction will not be 

processed. This can happen when the customer’s bank rejected the payment due to 

insufficient funds or limits. 

• 
Delivered: This status applies to checks and ACH payments. For checks, this status means 

that the check has been printed but not yet confirmed. For ACH payments, it means that the 

payment file has been created, but not yet confirmed. 

• 
Error: The system has encountered an error when trying to process the payment and cannot 

process it. 

---


<!-- Page 695 -->
Chapter 7: Enter AP Invoices Section 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Daily Tasks User Guide 

• 
Funds Received: The debit initiated and the payment is ready to be issued to supplier. 

• 
Issued to Supplier: The payment details have been received by the check printing partner, 

and the check(s) will be printed and mailed to your supplier(s). (AvidPay check payments) 

• 
Held: The payment is on hold pending resolution of an issue with the bank account or other 

reasons. This status is buyer generated if the client has pay workflows set in AvidPay. 

• 
Multiple: The original payment is being processed with multiple payment methods.  

• 
Partially Posted: A partial amount of the payment is posted to the bank account. 

• 
Partially Authorized: The bank has only partially approved the payment, and the payment 

has not yet been sent to the processor. 

• 
PayNow Complete: RealPage Payments has received a payment from the PayNow payment 

service. (deprecated) 

• 
Pending Approval: The payment must be approved by a user at your company who did not 

initiate the payment before processing can begin. After being approved, check the payment 

status to ensure that it changes from “Pending approval” to “Released” and then 

“Confirmed” before the cut-off time. 

• 
Processing: The payment is in the initial post-approval state. Depending on your financial 

institution, it takes 1–2 days to post to your bank. 

• 
Refund - Approved: The payment refund has been approved. 

• 
Refund Issued: Money has been transferred back to the customer. 

• 
Refund ACH Cleared: The payment refund has been cleared through ACH (Automated 

Clearing House). 

• 
Refund Processing: A refund of the payment is being processed. 

• 
Refund Requested: The customer has requested a refund.  

• 
Re-Issue Treasury Hold: The refunded payment is currently in the stop payment process 

and will be held for 24 hours to ensure the original check has not been deposited by the 

supplier. This status denotes the time that treasury needs to ensure the first attempted 

payment has not cleared before formally reissuing the payment again.  

• 
Request Sent: For Petty Cash Reimbursements, Utility Reimbursements, and Virtual Refunds 

– The payment request is processing. 

• 
Sent to Check Printer: The payment details have been sent to a third-party check printing 

partner to print and mail the check(s). (AvidPay check payments) 

• 
Stop Payment - Treasury Review: Treasury or a certifying agency has indicated that a 

Treasury check should not be paid and instead should be canceled. 

• 
Success: For Petty Cash Reimbursements, Utility Reimbursements, and Virtual Refunds – The 

payment has been successfully processed. 

• 
VCC Processing: The payment information is being delivered via the method the supplier 

requested (phone, email, portal, or fax).  (Mastercard payments) 

• 
Vendor Processed: The vendor has processed the payment.

the system sends you an email notification.

Third-Party Payment Configuration 

Whether you choose a third-party payment service such as RealPage Payments, Paymode-X, or 

RealPage Virtual Refunds, the system must be configured to use the desired payment service 

before use. Follow these steps to configure the desired third-party payment service: 

1. 
Enable the third-party payment feature (on page 680). 

2. 
Configure a bank account for making third-party payments (on page 684) 

3. 
Configure the vendor’s preferred payment method (on page 685).  

Enabling Third Party Payments 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Cash Management > Setup > Configuration`


To enable third-party payments: 

1. 
In the Cash Management menu, select the Setup tab. 

2. 
Select the Configuration menu option. 

The Configure Cash Management page opens. 

Third Party Payments Section 

Use this section to configure a third-party payment method for vendor payments. If this section 

does not display, click the Request information button to have a sales representative contact you 

about this additional feature. 

To configure third party payments: 

• 
Select the Enable third party payments check box to display the third-party payment 

configuration options.  

Configuring the RealPage Payments Service 

1. 
Select the RealPage payments check box if you want to use the RealPage Payments 

third-party payment service. 

2. 
Click the Select button under Notify user when invoice is put on hold to send an email 

notification to users when an invoice is put on hold. 

The system opens an Available items selection box. For more information, see Using the 

Multi-Select Box. 

3. 
In the RealPage Payments credentials subsection, type your Username and Password for the 

RealPage Payments third-party payment service. By providing the credentials, you are 

authorizing your company to send payment details to the service. 

4. 
In the Payment processing subsection, select the time interval to send the payment to the 

third-party service provider.

Configuring Debit Cards for Petty Cash 

The Debit cards for petty cash feature allows you to track and replace your cash on hand at the 

property or staff with a Prepaid MasterCard. You can issue cards to a property or to individual 

users with a set limit. As they make purchases, purchase information is loaded into RealPage 

Accounting to submit as an expense. You can view and submit expenses in core Accounting, 

Spend Management Site View for properties, or the RealPage Accounting Mobile App. 

To configure petty cash (PC) cards: 

1. 
Select the Enable debit cards for petty cash check box. 

2. 
In the Payment processing subsection, select the time interval to send the payment to the 

third-party service provider. 

• 
Immediately: Select this option to immediately process the payment requests and 

complete the payment. 

• 
Process end of each day: Select this option to include the payment requests when the 

system processes all requests at the end of each day. 

• 
Manual: Select this option to manually process the payment requests through the 

Third party payments queue. 

3. 
In the Unrestricted users for submitting the expenses multi-select box, add one or more 

unrestricted users or user roles. Unrestricted users can submit expenses for cards even if 

they are not issued to them. These are typically administrators. 

4. 
In the Reimbursement categories section, define the expense categories that will be available 

when users are submitting their debit card transactions. The system predefines a number of 

expense categories, but you can add, edit, or remove categories based on your business 

needs. 

• 
Expense category: Type the name of the expense category or rename an existing 

category. 

• 
G/L account: Select the G/L account to map the expense category to. 

• 
Attachment required: Select this check box to require users to include an attachment 

when submitting the expense category. 

If you have configured expense reports in Accounts Payable, then these are the same categories 
that are set up for expenses.

RealPage Payments 

The RealPage Payments service is a third-party payment service that allows you to pay A/P 

invoices online.  

Before you can use this payment service, you must configure the system to use it.  

RealPage Third-Party Payment Workflow 

Use this workflow to pay A/P invoices using the RealPage Payments payment service. 

1. 
Pay A/P invoices (on page 687). 

2. 
If the Payment processing option is set to manual, send payment requests to RealPage 

payments (on page 694). 

3. 
Monitor the payment processing status (on page 697). The system confirms payments 

offline, and sends you an email notification when it confirms a payment. 

4. 
Run the RealPage payments report to view RealPage Payments. The system creates 

individual payment requests being submitted from Pay A/P invoice pages.

Paying A/P Invoices Using RealPage Payments 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > All > Paying A/P Invoices`


Before you begin, determine whether you need to make the payments using an entity-level bank 

account or a top-level bank account. If the answer is an entity-level bank account, change to the 

entity level before beginning to make payments. 

To pay an A/P invoice using RealPage Payments: 

1. 
Open the Accounts payable menu. 

2. 
Select the Pay A/P invoices option. 

3. 
In the Payment method drop-down list, select RealPage Payments. 

The RealPage Payments option appears in the list when your company has enabled the 
third-party payments feature in the Cash Management application’s configuration. 

The system displays only the vendor invoices with preferred payment method set to 

RealPage Payments. 

4.

made. 


> **Navigation Path:** `To view the payments and monitor payment status, go to Accounts Payable > All > Third`


Party Payments Queue. 

RealPage Payments Critical-to-Pay Data 

Some vendors need specific data to reconcile your payments. In addition to the invoice number 

and amount, the vendor sometimes requires a customer account number or a pin number. Use 

the Description and Reference Number fields of an A/P invoice to add information that a vendor 

must have in order to reconcile your account. This is called critical-to-pay data.  

The data that you add to these two fields will appear on your check stub. The data is also sent to 

AvidXchange to help their payment specialists apply payments with your vendor.

Handling Partial Refunds When the Payment Method Is RealPage Payments 

When you pay a vendor with a single-use card and you have a credit with the vendor that has not 

been applied to an invoice, the vendor will either refund part of the payment or will not process 

your entire payment.  

When this happens, AvidXchange refunds the money to your bank account and sends you a 

notification. You will need to correct the General Ledger in RealPage Accounting. 

Create a Journal for Tracking Vendor Payment Refunds

reporting on these types of transactions. This is an example of a journal for vendor payment 

refunds.

You can create a journal entry for each payment. If the refund is for the same expense account, 

you can create one journal entry per month.

Open the General ledger menu.

Click 
 Journal Entry.

Handling Full Refunds When RealPage Payments Is Used 

When a vendor issues a full refund, the system does the following: 

1. 
Voids the payment.  

2. 
Changes the status of invoices associated with that payment to Posted and marks them as 

On hold. 

3. 
Sends an email notification to alert you that an invoice was put on hold due to a Vendor 

Payment refund. It sends notifications to any user who has been selected on the Cash 

Management Configuration page with the Notify user when invoice is put on hold option.

You can send third party payments to the processing center only when payment processing is set

Payment Statuses

• 
(blank): A blank payment status means that you have not yet sent this payment, and you 

will be using the manual payment processing option, as when the payment is a petty cash 

reimbursement.  

• 
Processing: This payment status means that the request is being sent to the third-party to 

process the payment. 

• 
Bad Request: This payment status occurs when there is incorrect address information in the 

vendor record, or No MID/LID configured for the Site ID that is involved in the payment.

Payment Statuses 

This is a list of the possible payment statuses when using RealPage Payments as a third-party 

payment processor: 

• 
(blank):  

• 
For Petty Cash Reimbursement, Utility Reimbursement, and Virtual Refunds: The 

payment request has not yet been sent. 

• 
For other payment methods, when the Payment Status column is blank, it means that 

the system has not processed the payment. 

• 
ACH Credit Issued: The payment has been included in transactions sent to the bank to debit 

and deposit to the supplier’s bank account. (AvidPay direct payments) 

• 
Approved: The payment is selected and approved, but not yet confirmed. This status 

appears only when approvals are enabled. When approvals are not enabled, see the 

Delivered status. 

• 
Authorized: The bank has approved the payment, but it hasn’t yet been sent to the 

processor. 

• 
AvidPay Check Issued to Supplier: When AvidXchange receives payment details for a 

supplier (vendor), they print and mail a check to the supplier. This happens on the first 

business day after the supplier’s invoice is approved for payment. 

• 
Bad Request: The system ran into an issue processing the payment request. Click the View 

details link and then download the response to see what the error was. 

• 
Cleared: The money has fully transferred from one account to the other. 

• 
Cleared - With Exception(s): The money has fully transferred from one account to the other, 

but there are issues with the transfer. 

• 
Conflict: The payment request was in the Bad Request state, and you sent it again. 

• 
Created: (Third Party Payment) – This status is only used for Nexus payments, and means 

that the payment has been sent to Nexus.  

• 
Customer Funds Received: The organization received the payment from the customer to 

cover a debit return. (deprecated) 

• 
Debit Requested: AvidPay has sent information to the bank to request the debit. Depending 

on your bank, the funds could appear on hold in your bank account either that night, or the 

next day. 

• 
Declined: A payment has been declined by the system. The transaction will not be 

processed. This can happen when the customer’s bank rejected the payment due to 

insufficient funds or limits. 

• 
Delivered: This status applies to checks and ACH payments. For checks, this status means 

that the check has been printed but not yet confirmed. For ACH payments, it means that the 

payment file has been created, but not yet confirmed. 

---


<!-- Page 717 -->
Chapter 7: Enter AP Invoices Section 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Daily Tasks User Guide 

• 
Error: The system has encountered an error when trying to process the payment and cannot 

process it. 

• 
Funds Received: The debit initiated and the payment is ready to be issued to supplier. 

• 
Issued to Supplier: The payment details have been received by the check printing partner, 

and the check(s) will be printed and mailed to your supplier(s). (AvidPay check payments) 

• 
Held: The payment is on hold pending resolution of an issue with the bank account or other 

reasons. This status is buyer generated if the client has pay workflows set in AvidPay. 

• 
Multiple: The original payment is being processed with multiple payment methods.  

• 
Partially Posted: A partial amount of the payment is posted to the bank account. 

• 
Partially Authorized: The bank has only partially approved the payment, and the payment 

has not yet been sent to the processor. 

• 
PayNow Complete: RealPage Payments has received a payment from the PayNow payment 

service. (deprecated) 

• 
Pending Approval: The payment must be approved by a user at your company who did not 

initiate the payment before processing can begin. After being approved, check the payment 

status to ensure that it changes from “Pending approval” to “Released” and then 

“Confirmed” before the cut-off time. 

• 
Processing: The payment is in the initial post-approval state. Depending on your financial 

institution, it takes 1–2 days to post to your bank. 

• 
Refund - Approved: The payment refund has been approved. 

• 
Refund Issued: Money has been transferred back to the customer. 

• 
Refund ACH Cleared: The payment refund has been cleared through ACH (Automated 

Clearing House). 

• 
Refund Processing: A refund of the payment is being processed. 

• 
Refund Requested: The customer has requested a refund.  

• 
Re-Issue Treasury Hold: The refunded payment is currently in the stop payment process 

and will be held for 24 hours to ensure the original check has not been deposited by the 

supplier. This status denotes the time that treasury needs to ensure the first attempted 

payment has not cleared before formally reissuing the payment again.  

• 
Request Sent: For Petty Cash Reimbursements, Utility Reimbursements, and Virtual Refunds 

– The payment request is processing. 

• 
Sent to Check Printer: The payment details have been sent to a third-party check printing 

partner to print and mail the check(s). (AvidPay check payments) 

• 
Stop Payment - Treasury Review: Treasury or a certifying agency has indicated that a 

Treasury check should not be paid and instead should be canceled. 

• 
Success: For Petty Cash Reimbursements, Utility Reimbursements, and Virtual Refunds – The 

payment has been successfully processed. 

• 
VCC Processing: The payment information is being delivered via the method the supplier 

requested (phone, email, portal, or fax).  (Mastercard payments)

• 
Vendor Processed: The vendor has processed the payment. 

• 
Void - After Issued: An individual in your organization has marked an item as void after the

Void: The payment has been marked as void, which cancels the payment transaction before

#### Stopping a Payment to a RealPage Payment Vendor
*Source: `RP Accounting AP Daily Tasks User Guide.pdf`, Page 719*

Chapter 7: Enter AP Invoices Section 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Daily Tasks User Guide 

Stopping a Payment to a RealPage Payment Vendor 

A RealPage payment is a third-party payment to a vendor.  

The Stop Payment feature may not appear in your version of the Financial Suite as it is available 

only upon request. Contact your RealPage Support Representative for more information. 

To stop a third-party RealPage payment: 

1. 
Open the Accounts Payable menu. 

2. 
In the Daily Tasks section, click Third party payments queue. 

3. 
Find the payment that you want to stop, and then click the Stop Payment link. 

The Stop Payment link appears only when the system has sent the payment to the 

processing center, and it does not offer the option to cancel the payment.  

When the processing center sends the response that the payment has been stopped, 

RealPage voids the payment in RealPage Accounting, and the status of the invoice changes 

to Posted. The system also puts the invoice on hold.

Paymode-X Payments 

RealPage Accounting allows you to pay vendors using the Paymode-X payment service. 

Paymode-X is a third-party payment network that helps businesses pay vendors using electronic 

payments, thereby maximizing cost-savings, efficiency, and security. Paymode-X offers 100% 

payment automation. 

Paymode-X Third Party Payment Workflow 

Use this three-step process to pay A/P invoices using the Paymode-X third-party payment service. 

1. 
When paying an A/P invoice, select Paymode-X for the payment method (on page 711). 

2. 
If the Payment processing option is set to manual, send the payment request to Paymode-X 

(on page 713). 

3. 
The system confirms payments offline, and sends you an email notification when it confirms 

a payment. 

4. 
Monitor the payment processing status (on page 715).

### Resident Virtual Refunds
*Source: `RP Accounting AP Daily Tasks User Guide.pdf`, Page 739*

Chapter 7: Enter AP Invoices Section

RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Daily Tasks User Guide 

Resident Virtual Refunds 

Refunds are an important part of property management and community accounting. They may 

result from overpayments, deposit returns, or adjustments to resident accounts. Processing 

refunds correctly ensures financial accuracy, builds resident trust, and supports compliance with 

accounting standards. 

Refunds are an important part of property management and community accounting. They may 

result from overpayments, deposit returns, or adjustments to resident accounts. Processing 

refunds correctly ensures financial accuracy, builds resident trust, and supports compliance with 

accounting standards. 

You can issue refunds to residents by selecting RealPage Virtual Refunds as the payment method. 

• 
Eligibility: Residents are eligible for refunds only when their name includes the “TEMP” 

prefix. 

• 
Availability: This feature is offered at an additional charge. Contact your RealPage 

Representative for details on purchasing. 

Where to Use RealPage Virtual Refunds 

The RealPage Virtual Refund payment method can be applied in the following areas: 

• 
Pay A/P Invoices page: Set the Payment method to RealPage Virtual Refunds to create a 

refund payment to a resident. 

• 
Pay by Entity (Group by Entity) page: Set the Payment method to RealPage Virtual Refunds 

to issue refunds from a specific entity. 

• 
Vendor record: Every resident who is issued a refund must have a vendor record to facilitate 

the payment. Configure the vendor record’s preferred payment method as RealPage Virtual 

Refunds. 

Approval Workflows for RealPage Virtual Refunds 

You can configure approval workflows for RealPage virtual refund payments in the following ways: 

• 
Configure approvals of A/P payments and use RealPage Virtual Refunds as the payment 

method. 

• 
Create an approval policy for the RealPage Virtual Refunds payment method. 

• 
Create an approval workflow for payments and then select the policy that you set up for 

RealPage Virtual Refunds payment method. 

• 
Set up an approval workflow for another policy type and then set up a condition for policy 

type where payment method equals RealPage Virtual Refunds. For example, you can set up 

a User policy type that sends transactions to a specific person or role for approval, and then 

set up a condition where the transaction to be approved must be a RealPage Virtual Refund 

payment method. For an example of this method, see Adding an Approval Workflow for 

Virtual Refunds. 

---

Enabling the RealPage Virtual Refund Payment Method

Refunds`


To enable the virtual payment method: 

1. 
Open the Cash management menu. 

2. 
Click the Setup tab. 

3. 
Click the Configuration menu option. 

4. 
In the Third party payments section of the Configure Cash Management page, select the 

Enable RealPage Virtual Refunds check box. 

5.

• 
Immediately: Select this option to immediately process the payment requests and 

complete the payment. 

• 
Process end of each day: Select this option to include the payment requests when the 

system processes all requests at the end of each day. 

• 
Manual: Select this option to manually process the payment requests.

Issuing Virtual Refunds 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > All > Pay AP Invoices > RealPage Virtual Refunds`


You can issue refunds such as security deposits or overpayments directly through the system 

without relying on manual checks. Use the RealPage Virtual Refunds payment method to issue a 

refund. 

Prerequisites 

• 
Your company must have purchased the RealPage Virtual Refund feature.  

• 
The virtual refund payment method must be enabled in Cash Management (on page 722). 

• 
You can refund residents only when they have names that begin with TEMP. These denote 

records that have been imported into the system from OneSite. The TEMP prefix lets the 

system validate the resident record to ensure that it is eligible to be refunded. 

• 
Each resident to be refunded must be set up with a vendor record.  

Permissions 

Access can vary depending on your organization’s subscriptions and your permissions. If you do 

not see the option in the menu, then ask your System Administrator to check your permissions.

user’s permissions. 

Procedure 

To issue a virtual refund to a resident: 

1. 
Open the Accounts Payable menu. 

2. 
In the Daily Tasks section of the menu, select Pay AP Invoices. 

3. 
In the Payment method drop-down list, select RealPage Virtual Refunds. 

4. 
In the Bank drop-down list, select the bank from which to withdraw the payment. 

5. 
Set up any of the other filters to find the transaction that you want to refund. 

6. 
In the list of transactions, find the transaction that you want to refund, and click the check 

box in the Items selected column. 

7. 
Click the Pay Now button. The system refunds the amount to the resident’s debit card 

unless an approval process has been set up for refunds. 

If your system has set up an approval process for refunds, then you can monitor the 

transaction’s approval in the Approval workbench. After the refund is approved, the system 

refunds the amount to the resident’s debit card.

Adding an Approval Workflow for Virtual Refunds 

This procedure demonstrates how to create an approval workflow for RealPage virtual refunds. 

Prerequisites 

• 
Your company must have purchased the RealPage Virtual Refund feature. 

• 
Enable the RealPage Virtual Refund payment method (on page 722).  

• 
A/P Payment approvals must be enabled. 

Approval Configuration > A/P Payments > Enable Payment Approval 

Workflow 

• 
Create an approval policy for the virtual refund payment method. 

• 
Set up an approval workflow. 

• 
Use the Approval workbench to evaluate payments that use the RealPage Virtual Refunds 

payment method (on page 726). 

Creating an Approval Policy for Payment Method 

1. 
Open the Company menu. 

2. 
Select Approval Policy Manager. 

3. 
In the Policy type field, select Payment Method. 

4. 
In the Policy name field, type a name like “Virtual Refunds.” 

5. 
In the Approval routing and limits section, select the role or user to assign approvals of 

virtual refunds to. 

6. 
In the Payment method column, select RealPage Virtual Refunds for the payment method. 

7. 
Select the number of approvers that you want to require to approve virtual refunds. 

8. 
Click Save.

Click Save.

Importing Payment Data 

You can import A/P payments and manual payments.  

You can import only one bank account and payment type combination at a time. 

You can choose whether you want imported payments to go through the approval process in 

Approval configuration in the A/P payments section. The Enable A/P payment approval against 

each selected entry creation from CSV import option applies to A/P payments and not to 

manual payments. 

How to Get Here

additional options based on your permission settings.

#### Importing A/P Payments
*Source: `RP Accounting AP Daily Tasks User Guide.pdf`, Page 747*

Chapter 8: Paying A/P Invoices 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Daily Tasks User Guide 

Importing A/P Payments 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > All > Pay AP Invoices > Import`


See the How to Get Here (on page 728) topic for a list of ways to access this area. 

You can expedite your payment process by importing payment data. You can also import manual 

payments, payments that you made outside of the system. 

If an entity is marked Do not pay, then invoices for that entity cannot be processed by importing 
them. 

To import records of payments that need to be made: 

1. 
Open the Accounts payable menu. 

2. 
In the Daily tasks section, select the Pay A/P invoices option. 

3. 
Select the Import button. 

4. 
Click the Download template link. You can find the file in your browser’s default download 

location, typically your Downloads folder.  

5. 
Open the AP Payments.xls file in Excel and fill it with your data.  

You can import only one bank account and payment type at a time. 

6. 
Fill in the required columns: 

• 
VENDOR_ID: Type the unique identifier of the vendor to pay. 

• 
INVOICE_NO: Type the unique identifier of the invoice to pay. 

• 
PAYMENT_DATE: Type the date that you want to record as the date that the payment 

is made. 

• 
AMOUNT_TO_PAY: Type the amount that you want to pay towards the invoice. 

• 
PAYMENT_METHOD: Type one of the following: Printed Check, ACH or Electronic 

payment (if EFT or BACS), Cash, or Credit Card. 

• 
BANK_ACCT_ID: Type the bank account number to use for the payment. 

• 
INVOICE_CURR: Type the three-letter ISO-4127 currency code for the currency to use 

for the payment. The currency and its format must be defined in the system. Examples: 

USD (US dollars), BPS (UK), CAD (Canadian).

### Paying A/P Invoices
*Source: `RP Accounting AP Daily Tasks User Guide.pdf`, Page 750*

Paying A/P Invoices 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Daily Tasks User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Paying A/P Invoices 

The pay A/P invoices workflow often includes applying credits, such as advances or adjustments. 

After creation, payment requests can be processed, or approved and then paid, based on the 

chosen payment method, such as printed check, or generated electronic payment file. 

Alternatively, you can store payment requests in the Outbox and come back to pay them later. 

You can start the process of paying a specific A/P invoice from the actual A/P invoice page or 
from the A/P invoices list. 

Before You Begin 

A/P invoices must have records in the system. You can either import them or add them manually. 

Payment Workflow 

1. 
Find the A/P invoice you want to pay. The use of filters is optional. 

2. 
Select the A/P invoices to pay. 

3. 
Apply credits, advances, or adjustments (optional). 

4. 
If the payment approval feature is enabled, wait for approval of payment requests. 

5. 
Pay now, or store the A/P invoices in the outbox and pay them later. 

How the Outbox Fits into the Pay A/P Invoices Workflow 

When you pay A/P invoices from the Pay A/P invoices page, you create payment requests that 

can then be approved or processed for payment. The Pay A/P invoices page provides a couple of 

options for generating payment requests based on your needs: Pay now or pay A/P invoices 

using the outbox. If you want to use the outbox, you can select A/P invoices, or filter A/P invoices 

from the Pay A/P invoices list and add the resulting payment requests to your outbox as drafts. 

The outbox can hold multiple draft payment requests that differ from each other in their payment 

methods, currencies, and banks. 

Pay Now Workflow 

Use this workflow when you have an A/P invoice that you want to pay quickly. 

1. 
Go to the Pay A/P Invoices list. 

2. 
Select A/P Invoices that you want to pay. 

3. 
Click the Pay now button. 

---


<!-- Page 751 -->
Chapter 8: Paying A/P Invoices 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Daily Tasks User Guide 

Add to Outbox Workflow 

Use your outbox as kind of a holding area for work in progress. The outbox can hold multiple 

draft payment requests that differ from each other in their payment methods, currencies, and 

banks. 

1. 
Go to the Pay A/P Invoices list. 

2. 
Either select A/P Invoices directly, or filter A/P Invoices and then select the A/P Invoices that 

you want to pay. 

3. 
Click Add to outbox to add the selected payment requests to the outbox as drafts. 

4. 
When you are ready to pay the A/P invoices in the outbox, return to the Pay A/P Invoices 

list. 

5. 
Click the Outbox payments button. 

6. 
Select the A/P invoices that you want to pay. 

7. 
Click the Pay button. 

---
