Pay A/P Invoices Page 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > All > Daily Tasks > Pay A/P Invoices`


Use the Pay A/P invoices page to review the list of A/P invoices owed. The list is filtered to show 

only invoices from the last 180 days.  

From this page you can: 

• 
View an invoice’s details: Select a link in the A/P Invoice # column to view the invoice 

details. 

• 
Apply credits (on page 770) to A/P invoices. 

• 
Pay selected invoices (on page 758). 

• 
Generate a separate payment for each vendor. 

• 
Click the link in the Invoice # to view a specific invoice. 

• 
View the due date of an invoice. 

• 
View the amount of credit available for a specific invoice. 

• 
Specify an amount of credit to apply to an invoice. 

• 
Click the link in the Discounts column to view and change discount details (on page 768). 

• 
Click the Line details link to open the Invoice details page (on page 424) where you can 

view invoice details and change credits to apply and the amount to pay. 

• 
Store payments in the Outbox (on page 762). 

• 
Create a custom filter to load the A/P invoices (on page 738) that you want to pay. 

• 
Record a petty cash reimbursement (on page 783). 

If the page does not load all of your invoices, then go to the Setup tab, click the Configuration 

option, and then clear the Do not automatically load all records on Pay A/P invoices check box 

setting. When this option is selected, you must apply a filter before the system will load A/P 

invoices on this page. 

Invoices That Do Not Appear In This List 

• 
If an entity is marked Do not pay, then invoices for that entity do not appear in this list. 

• 
Declined invoices do not appear in this list. You can find declined invoices in the A/P 

Invoices list or in the Approval workbench. 

• 
Hidden invoices 

When your company subscribes to the RealPage Utility Management (UM) application, RealPage 

offers a feature that prevents customers from paying UM invoices, as the UM application makes 

the utility payments on customers’ behalf. These invoices are only hidden for customers for whom 

RUM makes payments. 

When the feature is enabled, the UM invoices do not appear on the Pay A/P invoices page, and 

the UM invoices do not have a Pay option when they appear in the A/P invoices list.

Loading A/P Invoices into the Pay A/P Invoices Page 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > Setup > Configuration > Do Not Automatically Load 
All Records On Pay A/P Invoices`


By default, the Pay AP Invoices page loads all A/P invoices automatically. If your company has 

large numbers of A/P invoices that take time to load, then you can disable the automatic loading 

on the Pay A/P invoices page. When disabled, the user must set up and apply a filter to cause the 

A/P invoices to load. 

You must have administrator permissions to change the setting. 

To disable the automatic loading of all A/P invoices: 

1. 
Open the Accounts Payable menu, and then click the Setup tab. 

2. 
Click the Configuration option. The Configure Accounts Payable page opens. 

3. 
In the Enable functionality section, select the Do not automatically load all records on Pay 

A/P invoices check box to disable automatic loading. Clear the check box to load all A/P 

invoices automatically when you open the Pay A/P invoices page. 

4. 
Click Save. 

When you disable automatic loading of invoices, the next time that users open the Pay A/P 

Invoices page, they must apply a filter to have the system load the A/P invoices, including a 

default filter.

Filtering on the Pay A/P Invoices Page 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > All > Daily Tasks > Pay A/P Invoices`


Setting filter options enables you to narrow the focus of the A/P invoices you want to pay. For 

instance, you might only want to pay A/P invoices that are due by Friday. You might need to pay 

an A/P invoice from a specific vendor. Used effectively, filters can display just the A/P invoices you 

want, so you can move them onto approval or payment in just a few clicks. 

The Pay A/P invoices page enables you to set filter options that speed up the process of selecting 

A/P invoices and generating payment requests in two ways. 

• 
On the fly: We floated up some common filtering fields that you can use to do some 

on-the-fly filtering, such as Vendor and Due date. 

• 
Advanced filters: You can create and apply a filter set at the most granular level. You can 

even save advanced filters for repeat filtering, and if there’s one you use the most 

consistently, you can make it your default filter so that each time you open Pay A/P invoices, 

your default filter is automatically applied, and you can get straight to work on the resulting 

filtered list. You can even share filters so that other users can benefit from applying them. 

If you have Select to Pay permissions, you automatically have Pay A/P invoices 
permissions. 

To filter A/P invoices for payment: 

1. 
Open the Accounts Payable menu. 

2. 
Select Pay A/P invoices. The Pay A/P invoices page opens. 

• 
Use Basic Filtering (on page 739) 

• 
Use Advanced Filtering (on page 742)

 >  Use this operator to specify an amount above a specific amount.

<  Use this operator to specify an amount below a specific amount. 

=  Use this operator to specify an exact amount.

Type the ending amount.

#### Filtering for Multi-entity Companies

Filtering for Multi-entity Companies 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > All > Daily Tasks > Pay A/P Invoices`


If your company has multiple entities, you can use the standard and advanced filtering options as 

well as a few options targeted for multi-entity A/P invoice processing. 

To limit the list of transactions to specific entities: 

1. 
In the Pay A/P invoices page, select a filter, and then click Edit filter. The Advanced filters 

page appears. 

2. 
Find Entities to pay, and then click the Select button. The multi-select box opens. Select 

entities that have a defined business relationship. 

3. 
Do one of the following: 

• 
Select Add all to include all entities in your filter, then click Done. 

• 
Click 
 Add next to each entity that you want to add to the filter, and then click 

Done. 

The entities that you selected appear in the Entities to pay list. Click the Edit link to edit this 

selection as needed.  

After you apply the filter, the resulting list includes only A/P invoices that are associated 

with the selected entities. 

To process A/P invoices only for entities that can pay the entire A/P invoice: 

You can hold off on paying A/P invoices for specific entities that don’t have the resources yet to 

pay in full. 

1. 
In the Pay A/P invoices page, click the Pay by entity button at the top of the page. 

2. 
Check the Select entities with ability to pay all A/P invoices in full check box. 

3. 
Click Apply filter. 

To include or exclude A/P invoices depending on whether they have multi-entity line 
items: 

1. 
In the Pay A/P invoices page, select a filter in the Filter by drop-down list and then click the 

Edit filter button. The Advanced filters page appears. 

2. 
Select one of the following: 

• 
Include: Include A/P invoices that have multi-entity line items so long as one line item 

meets the criteria. 

• 
Exclude: exclude A/P invoices that have multi-entity line items even though one or 

more line items meet the criteria. 

• 
Only: show only A/P invoices that have multi-entity line items; A/P invoices with 

multiple line items for the same entity are excluded.

This example shows invoices associated with financial entities that have the word “Bank” in the 

name. 

To filter for an A/P invoice detail, select A/P invoice item, and then set up the criterion: select an 

attribute, an operator, and a value.  

In this example, the filter will return only records that have a matching entry date.

Navigating with Filters 

The Advanced filtering page has two navigation options. A/P Workbench includes the ability to 

navigate and filter by any combination of vendor, A/P invoice, and A/P invoice item attributes. 

To add navigation attributes: 

1. 
Select one of the following objects: 

• 
Vendor 

• 
A/P invoice 

• 
A/P invoice item 

The Attribute drop-down populates with all attributes available for the selected object. 

2. 
Select the Attribute you want to filter by. For example, if you select Vendor, the Attribute 

drop-down contains vendor filtering criteria, such as vendor name, addresses, contacts, 

preferred payment method, and so much more. 

3. 
Select an Operator to act upon the attribute, such as equals, less than, not equal to, and 

more. 

4. 
Select a Value for the operator. 

5. 
Optional. Select the sorting criteria. 

Example of Navigation Filtering 

Example: Create a filter that displays all A/P invoices within the next month, for vendors whose 

names begin with the letters A - L, and sort the results in ascending order. 

1. 
Click the Due date range drop-down and select Next month. 

2. 
Under the Drill down filters section, select Vendor from the Object list. 

3. 
Select Vendor name as the Attribute. 

4. 
Select less than as the Operator. 

5. 
Select M as the Value. 

6. 
Under the Sort by section, select the following: 

• 
Attribute = Vendor name 

• 
Order = Ascending 

7. 
Save the filter. The Pay A/P invoices page appears. 

8. 
Click Apply filter to view the A/P invoices that meet the filter criteria.

Adding a Default Filter 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > All > Daily Tasks > Pay A/P Invoices`


While you are creating an A/P invoice filter, or after you’ve already created one, you can make it 

the default filter, which means that any time you open Pay A/P invoices, the default filter is 

automatically applied, and the filtered list is ready for selection and processing. For example, if 

you pay A/P invoices for vendors whose names begin with the letters A-L, you can create a filter 

to view just those vendor A/P invoices and make it your default filter. 

To make a new filter your default filter: 

1. 
In the Pay A/P invoices page, select Add a filter from the Filter by drop-down list. The 

Advanced Filters page appears. 

2. 
Add the new filter name, and then select the Default filter check box. 

3. 
Type or select the rest of the desired filtering criteria. 

4. 
After saving, click Apply filter to view the resulting filtered list. 

You can change the filtering criteria at will and then either use the new criteria once, or save 

the criteria as the default filter. 

To make an existing filter your default filter: 

1. 
In the Pay A/P invoices page, select the filter from the Filter by drop-down list. 

2. 
Click Edit filters. 

3. 
Select the Default filter check box and save the filter. 

You can change the filtering criteria at will and either use the new criteria one time, or save 

it to the default filter.

> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > All > Daily Tasks > Pay A/P Invoices`

Click the Clear filter button at the top of the Pay A/P invoices page.

### Paying A/P Invoices
*Source: `RP Accounting AP Daily Tasks User Guide.pdf`, Page 776*

Paying A/P Invoices 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Daily Tasks User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Paying A/P Invoices 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > All > Accounts Payable > Pay A/P Invoices > 
Payment Method`


The Pay A/P invoices page enables you to filter to select A/P invoices for payment, or to select 

A/P invoices directly from the list of all A/P invoices. 

You can personalize the number of A/P invoices you see on a page in your preferences. We 
recommend that you limit that number to 20-50 A/P invoices. Although you can actually view 
any number of A/P invoices per page, the system becomes incrementally slower the higher the 
number. 

In either case, the following fields enable you to tailor and target all of your payment requests: 

1. 
On the Pay A/P invoices page, select the Payment method. You can pay vendors by check, 

credit cards, record transfer, or cash. In most cases, you don’t actually make payments – you 

record them here. 

To set up a default payment method for paying A/P invoices, see Configuring Pay A/P 

Invoices Defaults. 

To pay using electronic payments (ACH, EFT, or BACS), see Paying a Vendor Using Electronic 

Payments (on page 902). 

2. 
If your company uses multiple currencies, select the appropriate currency options. 

• 
Select the A/P invoice Currency to use when paying the selected A/P invoice. If you 

choose your base currency here, the system selects the Use Base Currency Banks To 

Pay check box for you. If you select a foreign currency, the system clears this check 

box. 

To set up a default currency for paying A/P invoices, see Configuring Pay A/P Invoices 

Defaults. 

3. 
Select the Payment request method. 

• 
Use vendor preference (default): Based on the chosen method for the vendor, create 

one request per vendor or one per A/P invoice. 

• 
Merge requests into one per vendor: Create a separate request for each vendor—A/P 

invoices of the same payment date for a vendor are combined into one payment 

request. If selected, this method overrides any vendor preference. 

• 
Generate one request per A/P invoice: Create a separate payment request for each 

A/P invoice. If selected, this method overrides any vendor preference. 

• 
Merge request into one per vendor pay to contact: Create a separate payment 

request for each vendor pay to contact. This means that the pay to contact entered on 

---


<!-- Page 777 -->
Chapter 8: Paying A/P Invoices 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Daily Tasks User Guide 

the A/P invoice is what prints on the check and overrides the pay to contact entered 

on the vendor record.  

To print one check per vendor, be sure to choose Merge requests into one per vendor. To 
print one check per vendor pay to contact, choose Merge request into one per vendor Pay 

to contact. 

4. 
Depending on the payment method, select the Bank or Credit Card to be used. 

Bank: Select the bank account that you want to pay from. If your company has set up a 

default bank account, an account appears in this field automatically. You can change to a 

different account as needed. To set up a default bank account for paying A/P invoices, see 

Configuring Pay A/P Invoices Defaults. 

Set payment date to: Select the date the payment is to be made. 

Your system can be configured to require that the payment date is greater than the 
invoice’s date. Your system can also be configured to require that the payment date is 
greater than the G/L posting date. 

Send payment notifications from: Select the contact to be used for email notifications. You 

can have the system send payment notifications for a specific vendor by enabling the option 

in the vendor record. If you have configured a specific contact to be the default contact, you 

can override that contact here as needed. The system automatically includes the contact 

name and email address in the email body so that the vendor can communicate about any 

payment questions or issues. 

5. 
To select A/P invoices for processing, do one of the following: 

• 
Click the check box beside each A/P invoice that you want to add to a payment 

request. 

• 
Use the drop-down box above the A/P invoices list to select: 

• 
Only this page to automatically populate all check boxes for appropriate A/P 

invoices on the current page. 

You can clear all populated check boxes in a similar way using the same drop-down box. 

6. 
If you have vendor credits that you want to consume, you can apply credits in two ways: 

• 
You can click the link and then manually apply credits as required before creating a 

request. For example, you might want to apply it to a specific transaction rather than 

have the system auto-apply to the oldest transaction. 

• 
You can have the system automatically apply credits to all applicable selected A/P 

invoices. Click Apply credits above the A/P invoices list. 

In a multi-entity company, the system applies credit to the owning entity first. If you 
enable your company to limit credits to just the owning entity, then credits are applied to 

---



#### About Selecting A/P Invoices
*Source: `RP Accounting AP Daily Tasks User Guide.pdf`, Page 778*

Paying A/P Invoices 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Daily Tasks User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

the A/P invoices of the owning entity and no others; any remaining credit is reserved for 
more A/P invoices owned by that entity. 

7. 
Do one of the following: 

• 
Click Pay now to create a payment request. 

• 
Click Add to outbox to create one or more draft payment requests to be stored in the 

outbox until you’re ready to pay them. The Outbox page appears with a list of all draft 

payment requests. For more about the Outbox, see Paying Later: The A/P Invoices 

Outbox (on page 795). 

Outbox does not support Wells Fargo Payment Manager payments. To make Wells 
Fargo Payment Manager payments, select your payments and click Pay now. 

You can return to the Pay A/P invoices page and continue to define and add payments requests 

to the outbox as needed. 

About Selecting A/P Invoices 

When you select A/P invoices to pay, you can: 

• 
View and select A/P invoices for payment from your entire list of A/P invoices. This process 

works well if you don’t have a long list of A/P invoices. 

• 
Filter for a specific A/P invoice or set of A/P invoices. This process saves you time when you 

have many A/P invoices and only want to pay specific ones. 

• 
The Pay A/P invoices page is organized to make the standard, most-commonly used 

filtering fields available. For example, you can filter on the fly by due date or vendor. 

• 
Advanced filtering provides options for filtering in a way that makes sense for your 

unique business. You can create and save these unique filters and use them repeatedly 

to display a list of specific A/P invoices for payment. In addition, you can make a filter 

your default filter so that each time you open the Pay A/P invoices page, the system 

automatically applies the filter and displays the resulting set of A/P invoices. 

For multi-entity companies 
When viewing the Pay A/P invoices page from the entity level, the list only displays A/P invoices 
created at the entity level. To include A/P invoices created at the top level that are tagged to 
your entity, create a Filter set that includes the Show top level transactions option.

Partially Paying an A/P Invoice 

To partially pay an A/P invoice: 

1. 
Open the Accounts payable menu. 

2. 
Select Pay A/P invoices. 

Setting Filter Options 

1. 
Set the filter options in the Pay A/P invoices page to look for invoices based on certain 

criteria (such as date or vendor).  

2. 
Click Apply filter. 

Setting Payment Parameters 

1. 
Select a bank to use for processing the payment. 

2. 
Select the currency to use for the invoice. If your company is a multi-currency company, this 

field is required. 

3. 
Find the desired A/P invoice in the list and select the leftmost check box. 

4. 
In the Amount to pay column, enter the amount you want to pay. 

5. 
Select how you want to handle the payment request: 

• 
Click Pay now to create a payment request. 

• 
Click Add to outbox to save the payment requests for later processing.  

The partially paid invoice remains available for payment until the entire amount is paid. 

Processing Payments in the Outbox 

When you added payments to the outbox, the system created one or more draft payment 

requests and stored them in the outbox until you’re ready to pay them.  

To access the payment requests in the outbox: 

1. 
From the Pay A/P Invoices page, click the Outbox payments button. The system opens the 

Pay A/P Invoices Outbox list to show the draft payment requests.  

2. 
Select the check boxes in the leftmost column of the payments that you are ready to make. 

3. 
Select the Pay button.

Selected Status: Checks and ACH Electronic Payments 

The Selected status on an A/P invoice applies to both checks and ACH payments. You cannot 

unselect a check or ACH payment. The next steps that you can take depends on whether the 

selected item is a check or an ACH payment.  

Checks 

These options are available when you have a check in Selected status: 

• 
Confirm the check 

When you want to complete the payment process, you must confirm the check. 

• 
If the check has been printed, confirm the check. (on page 1037)  

• 
Cancel the payment (on page 498) 

You can cancel the payment only if the check has not been printed. 

• 
Open the View payment request list. 

• 
Cancel the payment. 

• 
Void the check 

You can void the check if the check has been printed but not yet confirmed. 

• 
Confirm the check (on page 1037). 

• 
Void the payment (on page 1008). 

ACH Electronic Payments 

These options are available when you have an ACH electronic payment in Selected status. 

• 
Confirm the Payment 

When an ACH electronic payment is in Selected status, the payment needs to be confirmed.  

To confirm an ACH electronic payment, see Confirming an Electronic Payment (on page 

916). 

• 
Delete the Payment 

If the ACH payment has not been confirmed, you can delete the payment.  

• 
Open the ACH payment file list. 

• 
Delete the file.  

• 
Cancel the Payment 

If the ACH payment has not yet been added to a payment file through ACH file generation: 

• 
Open the View payment request list. 

• 
Cancel the payment.

Issuing Virtual Refunds 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > All > Pay AP Invoices > RealPage Virtual Refunds`


You can issue refunds such as security deposits or overpayments directly through the system 

without relying on manual checks. Use the RealPage Virtual Refunds payment method to issue a 

refund. 

Prerequisites 

• 
Your company must have purchased the RealPage Virtual Refund feature.  

• 
The virtual refund payment method must be enabled in Cash Management (on page 722). 

• 
You can refund residents only when they have names that begin with TEMP. These denote 

records that have been imported into the system from OneSite. The TEMP prefix lets the 

system validate the resident record to ensure that it is eligible to be refunded. 

• 
Each resident to be refunded must be set up with a vendor record.  

Permissions 

Access can vary depending on your organization’s subscriptions and your permissions. If you do 

not see the option in the menu, then ask your System Administrator to check your permissions. 

This permission is required to issue refunds:

Administrator for assistance. If you have administrator privileges, you can assign permissions for a 

new feature to a user or to a role. See Roles and Permissions for a description of how to review a 

user’s permissions.

Procedure 

To issue a virtual refund to a resident: 

1. 
Open the Accounts Payable menu. 

2. 
In the Daily Tasks section of the menu, select Pay AP Invoices. 

3. 
In the Payment method drop-down list, select RealPage Virtual Refunds. 

4. 
In the Bank drop-down list, select the bank from which to withdraw the payment. 

5.

7.

unless an approval process has been set up for refunds. 

If your system has set up an approval process for refunds, then you can monitor the 

transaction’s approval in the Approval workbench. After the refund is approved, the system 

refunds the amount to the resident’s debit card.  

Applying a Discount to an A/P Invoice 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > All > Pay A/P Invoices`


Terms are added at the A/P invoice level. If a term applied to an A/P invoice includes a discount, 

the amount of the discount appears on the Pay A/P invoices page for that A/P invoice. You can 

click a discount amount to view or change the payment date of the A/P invoice and the date of 

the discount. 

Changing the dates can cause the system to include or exclude the discount as needed. For 

example, if you added a default term to a vendor record, that term automatically gets added to 

each new A/P invoice created for that vendor. It’s possible, you might have some A/P invoices for 

products that the default applies to and other A/P invoices for services that shouldn’t have the 

discount applied. In Pay A/P invoices, you can change the discount date to be out of the term 

range for the specific A/P invoice. If the date isn’t within the range of the term, for example within 

Net 30, or within the number of grace days, the discount won’t be applied.

 If you have Select to Pay permissions, you automatically have Pay A/P invoices permissions.

How RealPage Accounting Applies Credits 

RealPage Accounting uses the Waterfall method to automatically apply available vendor credit to 

one or more selected A/P invoices. 

The Waterfall method flows the available credit as follows: 

---

In a multi-entity company, the system applies credit to the owning entity first. If you enable your 
company to limit credits to just the owning entity, then credits are applied to the A/P invoices 
of the owning entity and no other; any remaining credit is reserved for other A/P invoices owned

Filtering A/P Invoices Before Applying Credit 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > All > Daily Tasks > Pay A/P Invoices > Vendor`


This procedure describes how to quickly filter for vendor A/P invoices for the purpose of applying 

credit before they are paid. 

1. 
Open the Accounts payable menu. 

2. 
In the Daily Tasks section, select Pay A/P invoices, and then find the A/P invoices that you 

want to credit and pay. 

3. 
Select the Vendor. 

Overview of Applying Credit to Invoices 

The Pay A/P invoices page enables you to easily apply one or more credits (advances or 

adjustments) to an A/P invoice as needed. 

You can apply credits in three ways: 

• 
Manually apply specific credit amounts to specific line items in an A/P invoice. Click the Line 

details link in the invoice’s row, and then change the amount in the Credits to apply field. 

Use this method when you want to apply a credit to a specific item in the invoice rather than 

have the system auto-apply the credit to the oldest charge.  

• 
Automatically apply credits to all selected A/P invoices using the Waterfall process (on page 

770), which consumes the credit from the oldest to the newest A/P invoices. To have the 

system automatically apply credits to all applicable selected A/P invoices, click the Apply 

credits button above the A/P invoices list. 

• 
From the Cash Management application, create charge payoffs with matching A/P invoices 

without applying credits so that you can apply credits from Accounts Payable.  

Credit Configuration 

The Enable Inline Credits To Be Automatically Applied To Invoices setting allows the system to 

apply an inline credit to an A/P invoice automatically. You can select this setting on the Configure 

Accounts Payable (on page 776) page. 

When your company uses this option, as you select invoices on the Pay A/P invoices page, you 

may see credits available in the form of adjustments or negative A/P invoices. You can also 

choose to apply these credits manually.  

When your company does not use this option, credits are still available as adjustments, negative 

A/P invoices, and negative line items. You can manually select the Apply Credits option to apply 

these credits. 

---


<!-- Page 791 -->
Chapter 8: Paying A/P Invoices 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Daily Tasks User Guide 

When to Apply Credits 

Be sure to apply credits before adding A/P invoices to the outbox. If you’ve already created draft 

payment requests and you need to apply credit to any of the A/P invoices in the request, remove 

the request from the outbox, apply the credits, and then add the A/P invoices back into the 

outbox. 

When to Apply Credits in Multi-Entity Companies 

In a multi-entity company, the system applies credit to the owning entity first, and then applies 

credit from the oldest to the newest A/P invoices. If you enable your company to limit credits to 

just the owning entity, then credits are applied to the A/P invoices of the owning entity and no 

other; any remaining credit is reserved for other A/P invoices owned by that entity. 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > All > Search & Find > A/P Invoices > Apply Credits`


To apply credit to A/P invoices: 

1. 
Find the A/P invoice to which you want to apply credit. 

2. 
In the Credit to apply column, type the amount of credit that you want to apply to the 

invoice. 

3. 
Click the check box in the first column (the Select column) to select the invoices to which 

you want to apply credit. 

4. 
Click the Apply credit button. The system applies credit against the selected invoice or 

invoices. 

5. 
Click Save.

#### Applying Credit Manually to One or More Lines in an A/P Invoice
*Source: `RP Accounting AP Daily Tasks User Guide.pdf`, Page 792*

Applying Credit Manually to One or More Lines in an A/P Invoice 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > All > Daily Tasks > Pay A/P Invoices > Credit Details`


If you have credits that can be applied, you can manually apply them to one or more lines in an 

A/P invoice rather than have the system do the work for you across a selection of A/P invoices. 

To manually apply credit to an A/P invoice: 

1. 
Open the Accounts payable menu. 

2. 
Select Pay A/P invoices. 

3. 
In Pay A/P invoices list, select the check box for the A/P invoice, and then click Line details. 

The A/P invoice details page opens. 

4. 
Click Credit details. The Apply credit page opens. 

Click the arrow at the top right of the dialog box to expand it. 

• 
The Amount column displays the credit amount. 

• 
The Credits available column displays how much of the credit amount is available to 

apply to the selected A/P invoice. 

5. 
Select one or more check boxes for credits that you want to apply. The system automatically 

zeros out the Credits available field and displays the specified credit amount in the Credits 

to apply field. You can change this amount to anything less than the total credit amount. 

6. 
Save the Apply credits page. The A/P invoice details page opens. Notice that the Credits to 

apply field on this page now displays the designated credit amount. 

7. 
Save the A/P invoice details page. The Pay A/P invoices page opens and displays the sum 

of the applied credits in the Credits to apply field of the A/P invoice. 

8. 
In the Pay A/P invoices page, click Add to outbox to create the payment request and move 

it into the outbox. 

9. 
Click Outbox payments to view the payment request list in the outbox. 

If you’re paying from the top level in your multi-entity company, and you’ve enabled the entity 
limiting restriction in the multi-entity console, you can only view and apply credits owned by a 
specific entity to that entity ’s A/P invoices.

#### Automatically Applying Credit Across All Selected A/P Invoices
*Source: `RP Accounting AP Daily Tasks User Guide.pdf`, Page 793*

Automatically Applying Credit Across All Selected A/P Invoices 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > All > Daily Tasks > Pay A/P Invoices > Apply Credits`


Having the system automatically apply credits for selected A/P invoices eliminates the need to 

manually apply credits. 

To use this feature, the Enable inline credits to be automatically applied to invoices option must 

be enabled. See Enabling Automatic Inline Credit (on page 776) in the RealPage Accounting 

online help system. You can also find this information in online help or by downloading the 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Setup User Guide. 

In a multi-entity company, the system applies credit to the owning entity first, and then applies 
credit from the oldest to the newest A/P invoices. If you enable your company to limit credits to 
just the owning entity, then credits are applied to the A/P invoices of the owning entity and no 
other; any remaining credit is reserved for other A/P invoices owned by that entity. 

To automatically apply credits to the line items of one or more A/P invoices: 

1. 
Open the Accounts payable menu. 

2. 
In the Daily Tasks section, select Pay A/P invoices. 

3. 
In Pay A/P invoices, select the appropriate A/P invoices. 

4. 
On the left side of the page above the A/P invoice list, click Apply credits. 

The system applies the available credit from the oldest to the newest A/P invoices in the 

payment request until the credit is consumed. 

If you’ve enabled entity override for one or more entities in Entities setup, and you’ve also 
enabled auto-application of credit, the system can ’t automatically apply credit at the top 
level to A/P invoices created at the top level. Auto-application of credit works only at the 
entity level for A/P invoices created at the entity level.

Recording Concessions 

A concession is a negative charge awarded to the customer as a short-term incentive. Examples of 

concessions include waived fees, reduced rent, nuisance discounts, and renovation credits. You 

can record a concession as either negative customer charges or credit memo adjustments. 

When recorded as a credit, the concession shows up as a credit in your financial records. 

Note that, if running reports such as the Trial Balance report on a CASH basis, concessions are 
not reflected until they are applied to charges. After a concession is applied to a charge as a 
zero-dollar receipt, the record of the concession appears in the general ledger as of the receipt 
date that it was applied. 

Changing the Amount Credited After Creating a Payment Request 

See How to Get Here (on page 778) for a list of ways to access this area. 

After you add a payment request, you can’t change the credited amount in the outbox. Instead, 

you must remove the payment request and create a new one. You can remove a payment request 

by going directly from the menu to the Payment requests page or by navigating from the Pay 

A/P invoices page to the outbox that contains the draft payment request. 

Step 1: Remove the Payment Request 

Follow the desired method to remove the payment request. 

To cancel a payment request: 

1. 
Open the Accounts payable menu. 

2. 
In the Daily Tasks section, select View payment requests.  

3. 
On the Payment Requests page, locate the payment request, and then click Cancel Request 

at the end of the line. 

To remove a payment request from the outbox: 

1. 
Open the Accounts payable menu. 

2. 
In the Daily Tasks section, select Pay A/P invoices.  

3. 
Click Outbox payments.  

4. 
In the Pay A/P invoices Outbox page, select the check box beside the payment request that 

you want to remove, and then click the Remove from Outbox button. 

Any A/P invoices in the request reappear in the Pay A/P invoices list. 

Step 2: Create the payment request again 

Select the appropriate invoice or invoices again, apply the correct credit, and click Add to outbox 

to add the draft request to the outbox.

#### Clearing a Credit Adjustment
*Source: `RP Accounting AP Daily Tasks User Guide.pdf`, Page 797*

Chapter 8: Paying A/P Invoices 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Daily Tasks User Guide 

Clearing a Credit Adjustment 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > All > Daily Tasks > Adjustments > Delete`


In the system, you create a debit memo to record a credit from a vendor, such as a credit for 

shipping costs, or a return of product. After you create a debit memo, if you need to clear it from 

the system, you can either reverse or delete it depending on where the adjustment stands in the 

workflow: 

• 
If you haven’t applied the adjustment to a vendor A/P invoice, you can delete the debit 

memo. 

• 
If you’ve applied the adjustment to a vendor A/P invoice, then you can reverse the debit 

memo. 

This topic describes how to clear a debit memo and answers questions about clearing debit 

memos when there are additional considerations, such as when a vendor pays a refund on a 

negative balance. 

Deleting a Debit Memo 

You can delete a debit memo if it has not yet been applied to an A/P invoice. 

To delete a debit memo: 

1. 
Open the Accounts payable menu. 

2. 
In the Daily Tasks section of the menu, select Adjustments. The A/P Adjustments page 

opens with a current list of debit memos. 

3. 
Select the check box on the right side of the appropriate debit memo, and click the Delete 

button. 

If you see a Reverse link instead of a check box, the debit memo has already been applied to 
one or more A/P invoices, and can only be reversed. 

4. 
Confirm that you want to delete the debit memo. 

The system clears the debit memo from the list and from the system. No record of it 

remains.

#### Reversing a Debit Memo
*Source: `RP Accounting AP Daily Tasks User Guide.pdf`, Page 803*

Chapter 8: Paying A/P Invoices 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Daily Tasks User Guide 

Reversing a Debit Memo 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > All > Daily Tasks > Adjustments > Reverse`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Cash Management > All > Reports > Check Registers > View > Void`


You can’t delete an adjustment if you’ve applied a portion, or all, of the available adjustment to 

one or more A/P invoices, but you can reverse it to clear the adjustment as follows: 

• 
If you’ve applied no payment on the adjustment from the vendor, such as a check or 

electronic payment, you can reverse the debit memo. 

• 
If you’ve applied a payment on the adjustment, such as a transfer of funds to your bank 

account, you have to void the entire applied payment, and then reverse the adjustment. 

After you reverse an adjustment, you can’t undo the reversal. However, you can create another 

adjustment to replace it. 

If you do not see a Reverse link, the debit memo hasn’t been applied to one or more A/P invoices. 

You can click the Delete link to delete it to clear the debit memo from the system. 

To reverse a debit memo that has no associated vendor payment: 

1. 
Open the Accounts payable menu. 

2. 
Select Adjustments. The A/P Adjustments page appears with a current list of debit memos. 

3. 
Click Reverse on the right side of the appropriate debit memo. 

The Transaction Reversal Date page appears. Select the date for reversing the transaction. 

This is usually the original transaction date or a later date. 

4. 
To reverse the adjustment, click Submit. 

The debit memo is cleared from the system. The A/P Adjustment list displays the reversal on 

two rows to show the balancing transactions for removing the debit memo from the system. 

5. 
Optional. If you want to reverse one or more A/P invoices associated with the adjustment, 

under Reverse, select the check box for each A/P invoice, and click Submit. 

Both the debit memo and the selected A/P invoices are cleared from the system. The A/P 

Adjustments list and the A/P invoices list display the reversal on two rows to show the balancing 

transactions for removing the debit memo and the unpaid A/P invoices from the system. 

To reverse a debit memo that has an associated vendor payment: 

If you’ve made a vendor payment associated with a debit memo, such as a transfer of funds to 

your bank account, you first void the payment in the bank or check register, then reverse the 

debit memo. 

---


<!-- Page 804 -->
Paying A/P Invoices 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Daily Tasks User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

To void the payment: 

1. 
Open the Cash Management menu. 

2. 
Select Reports and then select Check registers. 

3. 
Select the appropriate account. 

4. 
Click View to see the list of transactions. 

5. 
Click Void beside the payment associated with the vendor credit. The Void Payment Date 

page opens. 

6. 
Select the date for reversing the transaction. This is usually the original transaction date or a 

later date. 

7. 
To void the entry in the register, click Submit. 

The entry displays Void in the Cleared column of the register. 

8. 
Optional. If you want to reverse one or more A/P invoices associated with the adjustment, 

under Reverse, select the check box for each A/P invoice, and click Submit. 

9. 
Both the payment and the selected A/P invoices are cleared from the system. The payment 

is shown on the register as a Void and the A/P invoices list displays the reversal on two 

rows to show the balancing transactions for removing the debit memo and the A/P invoices 

from the system. 

Now you can reverse the adjustment.  

Reversing the Adjustment 

To reverse an adjustment: 

1. 
Open the Accounts payable menu. 

2. 
Select Adjustments. The A/P Adjustments page opens with a current list of debit memos. 

3. 
Click Reverse on the right side of the appropriate debit memo. The Transaction Reversal 

Date page opens. 

4. 
Select the date for reversing the transaction. This is usually the original transaction date or a 

later date. 

5. 
To reverse the adjustment, click Submit. 

6. 
The debit memo is cleared from the system. The A/P Adjustments list displays the reversal 

on two rows to show the balancing transactions for removing the debit memo from the 

system.

### Paying Later: Using the A/P Invoices Outbox
*Source: `RP Accounting AP Daily Tasks User Guide.pdf`, Page 813*

Chapter 8: Paying A/P Invoices 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Daily Tasks User Guide 

Paying Later: Using the A/P Invoices Outbox 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > All > Pay A/P Invoices > Outbox Payments`


The outbox is a holding area for draft payment requests that you’re not quite ready to process. 

For example, using the outbox can be highly efficient if you create multiple types of payment 

requests, such as requests that use different banks or currencies. If you have an aging report that 

you want to tie to, then adding requests to the outbox can make that task a no-brainer because 

you can view the total amount to be paid for all the requests. The outbox holds and stores 

requests until you are ready to move them on for payment. 

A company generally has one outbox per user who pays A/P invoices. Administrators can access 
all outboxes. 

This page lists the A/P invoices that you have previously selected for payment. These draft 

payment requests can have one or more associated A/P invoices with one or more credits that are 

applied or can be applied. 

Your outbox provides a summary of the number of A/P invoices and, of those A/P invoices the 

number that are currently selected for next-step processing based on the Outbox and Bank 

selection. 

From this page, you can: 

• 
Filter the list of payment requests based on the bank selected to process the payment 

• 
Process draft payment requests: select the invoices and click the Pay button. 

• 
Remove a payment request from the outbox 

• 
Return to the Pay A/P invoices page without further action 

• 
View a payment request’s details 

• 
When the Merge payment requests added to the outbox across all users check box is 

selected, the system detects when payment requests arrive in the outbox that share the 

same vendor, and allows you to bundle the payments into one request even when the 

payment requests are from different users.  

---

Group by Entity Page 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > All > Daily Tasks > Pay by Entity`


This menu option is available only at the top level. 

Use the Group by entity page to group all of one entity’s A/P invoices without having to use 

filters. Grouping invoices by entity makes it easier to review all invoices for one entity and allows 

you the flexibility to navigate into the A/P invoice activity for the entity. 

From this page, you can pay and apply credits to all of the A/P invoices at once for a selected 

entity—all without requiring the use of filters. 

Use this page to: 

• 
Find out how many invoices are owed by an entity, the amount owed by the entity, and view 

the funds available to the entity. 

• 
Review the list of A/P invoices of one entity. The Details link opens the Pay A/P invoices - 

[entity name] with a list of invoices for the selected entity. 

• 
Limit the list of entities that can pay all their A/P invoices in full. Select this option before 

trying to pay the full amount for any entities. 

• 
Pay the full amount due across all A/P invoices of an entity. 

• 
Optionally, use filters to limit the list by due date, vendor, and remove entities that cannot 

pay their invoices in full. 

• 
Specify a confirmation email address or string of addresses of over 7500 characters. 

• 
Apply a credit to an entity’s invoices. 

• 
Access the Bank account holdback page where you can review and adjust holdback 

amounts. Click the figure in the Holdbacks column to open the page.

#### Paying by Entity - A Comparison
*Source: `RP Accounting AP Daily Tasks User Guide.pdf`, Page 821*

Chapter 8: Paying A/P Invoices 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Daily Tasks User Guide 

Paying by Entity - A Comparison 

There are several ways to pay by entity. 

Paying at the Top Level 

You can pay at the top level by filtering on the entity. To use this method, you must have a bank 

account defined to use at the top level. For details on paying, see Paying A/P Invoices Basic Steps 

(on page 758). 

To pay at the top level: 

1. 
Open the Accounts payable menu. 

2. 
In the Daily Tasks section of the menu, select Pay A/P Invoices.  

3. 
Filter by entity. See Filtering on the Pay A/P Invoices Page (on page 738). 

Paying at the Top Level Using the Pay by Entity Feature 

You can use the Pay by entity option to group A/P invoices for payment. See Viewing and Paying 

A/P Invoices for Entities That Can Pay the Entire Invoice (on page 808). 

1. 
Open the Accounts payable menu. 

2. 
In the Daily Tasks section of the menu, select Pay by entity.  

3. 
In the Entities to pay section, click the Select button and choose the desired entity. 

4. 
Click Apply filter. The system displays the A/P invoices for the selected entity. 

5. 
Pay as usual.  

Paying at the Entity Level 

To pay at the entity level. 

1. 
Select the entity from the Top level menu. A tab with the selected entity becomes active.  

2. 
Open the Accounts Payable application. 

3. 
Select Pay A/P invoices. The system displays the A/P invoices for the selected entity. 

4. 
Pay as usual without the need to filter unrelated invoices

. 

Paying by Entity 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > All > Daily Tasks > Pay A/P Invoices > Pay by Entity`


You can hold off on paying bills for specific entities that don’t have the resources yet to pay in full. 

Use the Pay by entity option to view and pay A/P invoices for only those entities that can pay the 

entire bill. 

If an entity is marked Do not pay, then invoices for that entity do not appear in the Pay by Entity 
list. 

To use the pay by entity feature: 

1. 
Open the Accounts payable menu. 

2. 
In the Daily Tasks section of the menu, select Pay by entity. The Group by entity page 

opens. 

3. 
Select the Select entities with ability to pay all A/P invoices in full check box, and then click 

Apply filter. 

4. 
Apply other filters as needed. 

Selecting the Payment Method 

• 
Entity preference: Select this option to use the preferred payment method of the entity. 

When you select this option, the system displays all A/P invoices. 

• 
Printed check: Select this option to have the system print a check for the payment. When 

you select this option, the system displays all A/P invoices like the Entity Preference 

payment method. The payment made against selected A/P invoices overrides the existing 

payment preference (if any) with Printed Check. 

• 
Electronic payment: Select this option to use the defined automated payment service. 

• 
Record transfer: Select this option to send the payment by bank transfer. When you select 

this option, the payment made against selected A/P invoices overrides the existing payment 

preference (if any) with Record Transfer. 

• 
Cash: Select this option to record the payment method as cash. 

• 
Vendor preference: Select this option to use the preferred payment method of the vendor if 

it is electronic payment, printed check, or record transfer. The vendor record contains the 

vendor preferred payment method. 

• 
RealPage Payments: Select this option to record the payment method as the RealPage 

payment service. 

• 
Paymode-X: Select this option to record the payment method as the Paymode-X payment 

service. 

• 
Third party payment: Select this option to record the payment method as a third-party 

payment service.

RealPage Debit Card: Select this option to record the payment method as using the

sending them a check. 

• 
Petty cash reimbursement: Select this option to record the payment method as a petty cash 

reimbursement.

and Pay by entity in the Document Sequencing section of the Configure Accounts Payable page.

account. 

The alternate bank account is defined in the Accounts Payable configuration of each entity. 
This will populate the alternate bank account for each entity displayed on the Group by 

entity page.

Making the Payments

<!-- Page 835 -->
Chapter 8: Paying A/P Invoices 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Daily Tasks User Guide 

This page has five sections: 

a) This section lists the A/P invoices of the entity. 

b) This section contains the credits controls. Use these controls to clear credits, apply credits 

only to this page, or to apply credits to all invoices. 

c) This section contains payment details. 

d) The top section offers filters that you can use to limit the list of invoices for the entity. 

e) The third section appears at the far side of the payment details section, where you can find 

the bank balance, total selected invoices that you plan to pay, and the adjusted bank 

balance as it will be after you pay the selected invoices, and the number of invoices you 

have selected to pay. Even if the selected bank is a top-level bank account, the bank balance 

appears.

### A/P Adjustments Overview
*Source: `RP Accounting AP Daily Tasks User Guide.pdf`, Page 844*



#### Before You Begin
*Source: `RP Accounting AP Daily Tasks User Guide.pdf`, Page 844*

A/P Adjustments 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Daily Tasks User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

A/P Adjustments Overview 

Managing accounts payable adjustments includes adding, editing, exporting, and when necessary, 

deleting adjustments made to vendor accounts.  

Terminology 

Debit Memo (debit note): Decreases the overall amount you owe that vendor. For instance, If you 

receive a credit memo from a vendor enter it as a Debit Memo to reduce the amount you owe 

that vendor. 

Credit Memo (credit note): Increases the overall amount you owe that vendor. 

The most important adjustment information appears at the top of the page for quick and easy 

access. For example, in the edit and view pages, you can quickly scan adjustment date, adjustment 

total, amount paid, and amount due. 

If you received a cash or check refund from a vendor, learn how to process the refund (on page 

542). 

Before You Begin 

Access can vary depending on your organization’s subscriptions and your permissions. If you do 

not see the option in the menu, then ask your System Administrator to check your permissions. 

Permissions 

These permissions are required to view and manage A/P adjustments: 

Application 
Activities/Lists 
Permissions 

Accounts payable 
Adjustments 
List, View, Edit, Add, Delete, 

Reverse 

If your user account doesn’t have the permissions shown above, then ask your System 

Administrator for assistance. If you have administrator privileges, you can assign permissions for a 

new feature to a user or to a role. See Roles and Permissions for a description of how to review a 

user’s permissions.

#### Adding an A/P Credit or Debit Adjustment
*Source: `RP Accounting AP Daily Tasks User Guide.pdf`, Page 847*

Chapter 9: A/P Adjustments 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Daily Tasks User Guide 

Adding an A/P Credit or Debit Adjustment 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > All > 
 Adjustments`


To add an A/P adjustment: 

1. 
Open the Accounts payable menu. 

2. 
Select the 
 Add button next to the Adjustments option. The A/P Adjustment page 

opens. 

3. 
In the Date field, the date defaults to the current date. Enter a different date as needed. 

4. 
In the G/L posting date field, enter the date on which the transaction actually posts to the 

general ledger. Unless you change it, this date defaults to the transaction date. 

This field displays only if enabled on the Configure Accounts Payable page. 

5. 
In the Vendor drop-down list, select the vendor who is the source of the adjustment. You 

can either select a vendor from the list or type the name of the vendor for the adjustment. 

For vendors you use repeatedly, it’s best to enter them into the system. 

6. 
In the Pay to drop-down list, select the vendor contact to pay.  

The system automatically defaults this field from the Pay to contact field in the vendor 

record or, if none, from the vendor you selected in this page. You can override the default as 

required, for example, if the vendor has multiple offices and requests you to send the check 

to an office other than the one on record. 

7. 
In the Return to drop-down list, select the vendor contact for return of the purchase. The 

system automatically defaults the Return to contact from the purchasing transaction, which 

itself defaults from the vendor record. If neither exists, the system defaults this field to the 

vendor you selected in this page. Although in most cases, you won’t need to override the 

default, you can, for example, if you are returning a defective product and the vendor wants 

you to return it to a location other than the one on record. 

8. 
In the Type drop-down list, select whether the adjustment increases or decreases the overall 

amount owed to the vendor: 

• 
Select Credit Memo when the adjustment increases the amount owed. 

• 
Select Debit Memo when the adjustment decreases the amount owed. 

After you save this adjustment, the type cannot be changed directly. To change an 
adjustment from a Debit Memo to Credit Memo, or vice versa, delete or reverse the 
adjustment and create a new one. 

The system assigns an Adjustment number to this record. You can use this number to track 

this adjustment. 

---


<!-- Page 848 -->
A/P Adjustments 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Daily Tasks User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

9. 
In the Reference invoice number drop-down list, select or type a number such as a 

purchase order or account number that may be useful in searches or reports on the A/P 

invoice.  

This number shows on the G/L Details report, but does not print on the check or check 

remittance stub. 

10. 
In the Description field, type information that you want stored with this A/P invoice. This 

information prints on the Vendor Ledger report, but does not print on the check or 

remittance stub. 

11. 
In the Attachments drop-down list, select a document to associate with this adjustment.  

To reference an attached document, you must first load the scanned image, spreadsheet, 
or word-processor document. You can provide permanent, safe storage of attachments by 
uploading them to the system. You must have permissions for adding attachments . If you 
are using Firefox, Chrome, or Edge, you can drop your file on the Attachments box to attach 
the file to this record. See Attachments . 

Filling In the Currency Section 

If your company uses multi-currency transactions, select the currency for this adjustment. 

Filling In the Entries List 

1. 
Set up defaults as needed (on page 832).  

2. 
In the Location drop-down list, select the location to which to assign this payment. 

3. 
In the Account drop-down list, select the appropriate account to determine the account to 

which the system assigns the expense. If the account doesn’t exist, you can use the field 

level controls to add a new G/L account. To add a G/L account, you must be at the top level. 

You can use the field level controls Add, View, and Find.  

• 
Select Add to add a new G/L account.  

• 
To view an account, select a G/L account from the drop-down list, and then click the 

View option to open it.  

• 
Click Find to search for a G/L account’s record.  

4. 
Select the 1099 check box to add the line item amount to the vendor’s Form 1099. 

It is no longer necessary to create a negative A/P invoice. Flagging an item as 1099 in an 
adjustment allows you to pull the adjustment into the 1099 report. 

5. 
If you selected the 1099 check box, click the Show details tab, and then select the Form 

1099 Type and Form 1099 Box. 

6. 
In the Amount field, enter the actual amount of the transaction for this item in a 

single-currency company. 

---


<!-- Page 849 -->
Chapter 9: A/P Adjustments 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Daily Tasks User Guide 

If you’ve enabled multi-currency, the system displays Base Amount and Transaction 

Amount in place of Amount. 

Base Amount is the amount of the item in the base currency of your company. 

Transaction amount is the amount of the item in the currency you set for the A/P invoice. 

For example, if your base currency is USD and you create a 100 Euro A/P invoice, for the line 

item, you see the A/P invoice with 100 Euro as the Transaction Amount and 110 USD as the 

Base Amount (assuming a 1.1 exchange rate from Euro to USD). 

7. 
In the Department drop-down list, select the department to which to assign this payment. 

You can specify additional dimensions in the Details section.  

8. 
In the Unit drop-down list, select the unit to which to assign this payment. 

9. 
In the Segment type and Segment value fields, select the desired segment type and assign 

the segment value to identify this transaction.  

You can specify additional segment types and their values in the Details section. If the 

Segment type and Segment value fields do not appear, then your system may not have the 
segments feature enabled. 

10. 
In the Memo field, the memo stores information regarding this adjustment with the general 

ledger entry. 

Finishing the Adjustment 

When you finish entering the adjustment, save it as a draft or post it.  

Selecting Draft saves the adjustment as a draft without affecting the General Ledger or any 

subledger. With the ability to save A/P invoices, A/R invoices, and adjustments in draft state, you 

can save your progress so far. Later on, you or another user can come back and post the 

transaction. 

Selecting Post saves the adjustment and has the system validate the transaction when it is posted. 

For example, required departments or locations are not validated until posting. 

• 
Select Draft to save your progress on the transaction. The system saves the entry, but 

doesn’t post it. 

• 
Select Draft & new to save your progress on the transaction. The system saves the entry, but 

doesn’t post it, and opens a new adjustment.  

• 
Select Draft & Continue to save your progress on the transaction and continue working on 

it. 

• 
Select Post to save your transaction and post it to the General Ledger. 

• 
Select Post & new to post the transaction. The system validates the transaction and posts it 

to the General Ledger.

Setting Default Values 

In most Entries sections, you can add values directly to each line item, where needed, or click 

Show defaults to select default values to have the system automatically complete each line item. 

This article describes setting up default values. 

A default is information that the system automatically completes in a field or column. The default 

value can be some text, a number, or a selection from a drop-down list. The system gets this 

information from the Defaults section. After you fill in the default values, the system completes 

the fields or columns with the information that you set up. 

For example, say you have 14 units in a property that sustained damage due to a storm and the 

vendor repaired the same problem on 14 units on the property. You need to set up default values 

for the 14 line items that will require the same information.  

To set up default values: 

1. 
Click Show defaults to open the defaults area. The default area is displayed. The default 

area varies by transaction type: 

2. 
Fill in any of the default fields with the values that is likely to be the most frequently used 

value. 

You can always override any default value that the system completed with your default 
values. 

Looking at our example, we have six fields that we can set to default values: 

• 
Department 

• 
Location 

• 
Unit 

• 
Segment type 

• 
Segment value 

• 
Memo 

In this example, the segment type and segment values identify the areas of a large building.

Click the Apply defaults button. The system completes the related columns with your

4.

#### How the System Applies Credits
*Source: `RP Accounting AP Daily Tasks User Guide.pdf`, Page 852*

A/P Adjustments 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Daily Tasks User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

How the System Applies Credits 

On the Pay A/P Invoices page, click the Apply Credits button to have the system automatically 

apply a credit to one or more A/P Invoices. The system recognizes all items that have some credit 

amount and applies them in this order: 

1. 
Inline credits 

2. 
Advances 

3. 
Negative invoices 

4. 
Debit-memo adjustment 

If you define a sort order on the Pay A/P Invoices page and then click the Apply Credits button, 

then the system automatically applies the credits to the A/P invoices that meet your sort criteria. 

For example, if you specify a sort order of Payment Priority, Due Date, and Invoice Number, the 

system applies the credit in the following order as long as there is credit remaining. 

1. 
The system applies credit to A/P Invoices that have a specified payment priority starting 

from highest to lowest. 

2. 
If more than one A/P Invoice has the same priority, the system applies credit based on the 

due date, from oldest to most recent. 

3. 
If more than one A/P Invoice has the same priority and due date, the system applies credit 

based on the invoice number from lowest to highest. 

The sum that remains in the Amt To Pay field after all available credit is applied becomes the 

check amount.

Tracking Vendor Credits 

To track a vendor’s credits, use the adjustment number to find the invoice number or credit 

number. You can then use the invoice number or credit number to track a vendor’s credits. The 

adjustment number appears on: 

• 
Remittance emails: When a vendor has an email address defined for remittance 

correspondence, the system sends an email to the vendor with Credits Applied to Invoice 

information. 

• 
Check stubs: You must enable the Show recent credits applied to invoices on 

check/payment remittance option for the adjustment number to appear on check stubs. 

Editing an Adjustment 

For quick and easy editing, the most important elements of the adjustment appear at the top of 

the page, such as the adjustment date, adjustment total, amount paid, and amount still available 

to apply. You can even click the link to see details for partially- or fully paid adjustments. 

The type of adjustment can’t be edited. To change an adjustment from a Debit Memo to Credit 

Memo, or vice versa, delete or reverse the adjustment and create a new one. 

To edit an adjustment: 

1. 
Open the Accounts payable menu. 

2. 
Select Adjustments. The system displays a list of adjustments. 

3. 
On the list, find the adjustment you want, and click Edit. The system displays the A/P 

Adjustment page with information about the adjustment. 

4. 
Add, modify, or delete information as needed. 

If the adjustment has been partially or fully paid, to change the G/L account and other 

information, such as dimensions, click Reclassify. (You see this button only if Accounts 

Payable is configured to allow reclassification of adjustments, and you have permission to 

reclassify adjustments.)  

For more details, go to field-by-field descriptions (on page 852).

### Debit Memo Adjustments
*Source: `RP Accounting AP Daily Tasks User Guide.pdf`, Page 855*



#### Creating a Debit Memo Adjustment
*Source: `RP Accounting AP Daily Tasks User Guide.pdf`, Page 855*

Chapter 9: A/P Adjustments 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Daily Tasks User Guide 

Debit Memo Adjustments 

A debit memo adjustment decreases the overall amount that you owe a vendor. 

Creating a Debit Memo Adjustment 

Before you start creating a debit memo adjustment, have key information on hand: 

• 
Any supporting documents within or external to the system, such as an A/P invoice or actual 

credit memo from your vendor. If you haven’t already done so, scan any hard-copy 

supporting documents onto your local drive for easy upload to the system. 

• 
The amount of the decrease. 

• 
The general ledger accounts to be affected, such as shipping, expense, or inventory. 

To create a debit memo adjustment: 

Enter information that describes the debit memo. 

1. 
Open the Accounts payable menu. 

2. 
Select 
 next to the Adjustments option. The A/P Adjustment page opens. 

3. 
In the Date field, leave the current date or select a different date for the adjustment. Any 

date entered here is automatically populated to G/L posting date (and to Exchange rate 

date–if you’re a multi-currency company). You can change either date as needed, for 

example, if you want to create the adjustment today, but post it on a different date. 

4. 
In the Vendor drop-down list, select a vendor. You can also use the field level controls to 

Add a new vendor, select a vendor’s record, and then click View to open it, or select the 

Find option to search for a vendor’s record. To add vendors, you must be at the top level.  

The system completes the Pay to and Return to fields with information from the selected 

vendor record. 

5. 
Enter an Adjustment number, Reference A/P invoice number, or Description as needed. 

The A/P invoice number and reference number can be used to search, sort, and report on 

A/P invoices. 

If you’ve assigned document sequencing in Configure Accounts Payable, you can let the 
system assign an adjustment number; just leave the autofill text “—New—.” 

6. 
Select Debit Memo as the adjustment type. A debit memo decreases the overall amount 

that you owe the vendor. 

7. 
To store a digital version of a supporting document permanently and safely, in the 

drop-down next to the Attachments option, select an attachment. You can also click Add, 

and then upload your attachments. Learn more about who can add attachments in 

Permissions for attachments. 

---

Saving a Debit Memo Adjustment as a Draft 

If you’re not ready to post that A/P invoice, A/R invoice, or adjustment, you can save it as a draft 

without affecting the G/L or any subledger. With the ability to save A/P invoices, A/R invoices, and 

adjustments in draft state, you can save your progress so far. You or another user can come back 

later and post the transaction. 

The system validates transactions only when they are posted. For example, required 
departments or locations are not validated until posting. 

Prerequisites: Your ability to add a transaction in draft state or post a transaction depends on 

your permissions: 

• 
Add permission enables you to add, edit, delete, and save a transaction as a draft. 

• 
Add, Edit, and Post permissions enable you to add, edit, delete, and save a transaction as 

draft, and edit and post the transaction when you’re ready. 

To save a transaction in draft format: 

1. 
Add an A/P invoice, A/R invoice, or adjustment to your company. 

2. 
Save the transaction as a draft: 

• 
Draft & New: Select this option to have the system save the transaction but not post it, 

and then open a new blank transaction.  

• 
Draft: Select this option to have the system save the transaction but not post it, and 

close the page. 

• 
Draft & Continue: Select this option to save the transaction and continue working on 

it. 

Correcting a Debit Memo Adjustment 

If you entered the debit amount incorrectly, or if you misunderstood the amount the vendor was 

willing to reimburse you, you can edit the debit memo so long as you haven’t applied the 

decrease to any A/P invoices, and you haven’t closed the books. 

If you apply a debit memo, or close the books, and then discover an error, you can create a new 

debit or credit memo to adjust the decrease up or down, as required.

Deposit and Record a Refund from a Vendor 

Learn how to record a vendor refund for the following supported use cases. 

Scenario 1 

The vendor sent you a cash or check refund, and you need to record the amount. 

• 
You haven’t created an adjustment (credit memo) to account for the refund. You don’t need 

to balance anything on the Accounts Payable side. 

• 
You want to deposit the amount in your bank and are not planning on using the refund as a 

credit on a future A/P invoice. 

Do this: 

• 
Create an Other receipt to record the refund.  

Scenario 2 

The vendor sent you a credit to use on a future A/P invoice. 

Do this: 

1. 
Create an A/P adjustment (on page 837) (debit memo) to decrease the amount that you 

owe the vendor. 

2. 
Apply the adjustment (debit memo) to the next A/P invoice that you receive from the 

vendor on the Pay A/P invoices page. 

Debit memos decrease the overall amount that you owe a vendor. 

Scenario 3 

The vendor sent you a cash or check refund, and you need to record the amount. 

• 
You have created an adjustment to account for the refund. You need to balance on the 

Accounts Payable side. 

• 
You want to deposit the amount in your bank and are not planning on using the refund as a 

credit on a future A/P invoice. 

Do this: 

1. 
Create an AP Adjustment to clear the vendor balance. 

• 
Credit memo increases the overall amount that you owe a vendor. 

• 
Debit memo decreases the overall amount that you owe a vendor. 

2. 
Apply the adjustment to the vendor balance. 

3. 
Create an Other receipt to record the refund.

#### Entering a Credit that Requires a 1099 Adjustment

Entering a Credit that Requires a 1099 Adjustment 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > All > 
 AP Invoices`


When you need to record a credit from a vendor that involves 1099 status, such as for contracting 

services, creating a debit memo decreases the overall amount you owe that vendor, but it does 

not affect the 1099 status. To decrease the overall debt to this vendor and address the 1099 

status, create an A/P invoice with a negative number instead of a debit memo. 

To create an A/P invoice with a negative number: 

1. 
In the Summary section, fill in the Date, Vendor (Supplier), and Invoice number fields. 

2. 
In the Terms section, fill in the Due date field. 

3. 
If your system is a multi-currency system and the vendor must be paid in a different 

currency than the base currency, then fill in the Currency section. 

Filling In the Invoice Entries Section 

1. 
In the Account column (or Account label column if you enabled A/P account labels), select 

an account to categorize the expense. 

2. 
Clear the No Tax check box. 

3. 
Select the Location. The location determines the accounts that appear in the Accounts 

drop-down list. The chart type associated with the property determines the accounts in the 

list. For more information see Chart types in the RealPage Accounting online help or 

download the RealPage Accounting General Ledger Setup User Guide. For the A/P invoice to 

be posted, you must specify at least the account and an amount for each line item. 

4. 
In the Amount field, type the cost of the service as a negative number.  

5. 
For companies using multiple currencies, type the Transaction amount, which is the cost of 

the item expressed in the currency used in the transaction. The system calculates the Base 

amount in your company’s base currency using the exchange rate listed in the header. 

6. 
If you use departments and are assigning an expense to one, then select the appropriate 

department from the Department drop-down list. 

7. 
Type a Memo to indicate that this is a 1099 credit adjustment. 

You can include the memo on the check stub at printing time by selecting Check stub 

details on the Print checks page. 

8. 
If a specific unit is associated with the credit, then select the unit in the Unit drop-down list. 

9. 
Post the invoice.

Enter an Increase to the Amount Owed to a Vendor 

If you owe your vendor more than you initially thought, for example, you’ve incurred a late 

charge, then you can create a credit memo to record that increase. The process is similar to 

creating a debit memo. 

How to Handle Vendor Credit Received to Your Credit Card 

After you have paid the full amount of a vendor A/P invoice, you might receive a credit from the 

vendor as a refund on your credit card. In this case, instead of creating a debit memo in A/P 

adjustments, handle the refund by doing one of the following: 

• 
If you want to record the refund without affecting the subledger, add an adjusting journal 

entry for the credit. Debit the vendor’s account to reduce your liability, and then credit the 

expense account to decrease the expense.  

• 
Create a debit memo adjustment against the vendor. 

• 
Add a credit card transaction. 

Applying an A/P Adjustment as a Vendor Credit to an A/P Invoice 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > All A/P invoices > Pay A/P Invoices`


Say you create a credit or advance to decrease the amount of money you owe a vendor and 

you’re ready to process A/P invoices. 

You can apply the credit to one or more line items of the bills on the Pay A/P invoices page. You 

can also apply credits either manually or automatically and view credits applied to an A/P invoice 

from the Pay A/P invoices page. 

Apply credits before adding A/P invoices to the outbox. If you already created draft payment 
requests and need to apply credit to any of the A/P invoices in the request, remove the request, 
apply the credits, then add the A/P invoices back into the outbox. 

Option 1: Manually apply credits to bills and bill line items 

You can manually apply credits to one or more lines in an A/P invoice rather than have the system 

do the work for you across a selection of A/P invoices. 

If you need to, click the Clear credits button to clear the Credits to apply field. The Amount to 

pay field automatically updates to the correct amount. 

When you are paying from the top level 
If you enabled the restriction to limit credit to owning entities, you can view and apply credits 
only for an entity to A/P invoices created in that entity. 

1. 
Open the Accounts payable menu. 

2. 
Select the A/P invoices option. 

3. 
Select the Pay A/P invoices option. 

---


<!-- Page 861 -->
Chapter 9: A/P Adjustments 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Daily Tasks User Guide 

4. 
Apply a filter to load A/P invoices. 

5. 
Click Line details next to the appropriate A/P invoice. The A/P invoice details page opens. 

6. 
Click Credit details. The Apply credit page opens. The Amount column displays the credit 

amount. The Credits available column displays how much of the credit amount is available 

to apply to the selected A/P invoice. 

7. 
Select one or more check boxes next to the credits that you want to apply. The system 

automatically zeroes out the Credits available field and populates the credit amount in the 

Credits to apply field. You can manually change this amount to anything less than the total 

credit amount. 

8. 
Click Save and return to the A/P invoice details page. The designated credit amount 

appears in the Credits to apply field. 

9. 
Click Save and return to the Pay A/P invoice page. The sum of the applied credits appears 

in the Credits to apply field for that A/P invoice. 

10. 
Do one of the following: 

• 
Apply the credit to the A/P invoice (leaving a remaining balance to pay later, or if the 

credit completely pays off the A/P invoice). Click Pay now, or Add to outbox. 

• 
Enter the rest of the Amount to pay to pay off the A/P invoice. Click Pay now or Add 

to outbox. 

Option 2: Automatically apply credit across selected A/P invoices 

If your company is configured to apply credits automatically, you can do so for selected bills to 

eliminate the need to apply credits manually.  

If you need to, click the Clear credits button to clear the Credits to apply field. The Amount to 

pay field automatically updates to the correct amount.  


> **Navigation Path:** `1. 
Go to Accounts Payable > All > A/P invoices> Pay A/P invoices.`


2. 
Apply a filter to load A/P invoices.  

3. 
Select the appropriate A/P invoice.  

4. 
On the left side of the page above the bill table, click Apply credits.  

Credits are applied using the waterfall process. This is how it works: 
Available credit is applied from the oldest to newest A/P invoices in the payment request until 
the credit is consumed. The waterfall process flows the available credit as follows:  
1. Location 
2. Bill dates (oldest first) 
3. Payment priority (highest first) 
4. Recommended payment date (oldest first) 
5. Greatest amount due (greatest first)

Accounting applies credit to the owning entity first. If you configure your company to limit
