Unapplying a Vendor Credit (Debit Memo Adjustment) 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > Daily Tasks > Adjustments`


How you unapply (or remove) a vendor credit that was applied to an A/P invoice depends on: 

• 
Whether you applied the adjustment at the same time you made a payment against the A/P 

invoice, or if you performed these two actions separately. 

• 
Whether you printed and confirmed an associated payment (such as a check) against the 

A/P invoice. 

Vendor Credit 
A credit on a vendor account enables you to decrease the amount you owe to a vendor. 
Add a vendor credit by creating an A/P Adjustment and selecting Debit Memo as the Type. 
Creating a debit memo type adjustment signifies that you ’re debiting your Accounts Payable 
account, which reduces your liability to the vendor.  

Learn more about debit memo adjustments (on page 837). 

Scenario 1 

You completely paid off the A/P invoice with a vendor credit (debit memo adjustment) on the Pay 

A/P invoices page. 

The A/P invoice is marked as Paid. There’s no record of payment on the Posted Payments page or 

the Payment Request page because there are no outbound funds. 

Do this  

Reverse the adjustment on the A/P Adjustments page. 

Reversing the adjustment removes the associated vendor credit from the A/P invoice. The A/P 

invoice becomes available to select again for payment on the Pay A/P invoices page. 

After you reverse a transaction, you can ’t undo the reversal. However, you can create another 
transaction to replace the original. 

---

Scenario 2 

You applied the credit at the same time that you applied a cash or check payment to the A/P 

invoice. 

You haven’t yet printed and confirmed the associated check, and the A/P invoice and adjustment 

are in a Selected state. 

Do this  

• 
Cancel the payment request. 

The credit is removed from the A/P invoice, and both the credit and the A/P invoice return 

to a Posted state. You can then re-select the A/P invoice for payment on the Pay A/P 

invoices page and apply the credit how you like. 

Scenario 3 

Use this scenario when you need to edit the A/P invoice. 

You applied the credit at the same time that you applied a payment to the A/P invoice. You 

printed and confirmed the associated check, and the A/P invoice and the adjustment are both 

marked as Paid. 

Do this  

Void the posted payment that you made against the A/P invoice in the appropriate register. The 

A/P invoice and the adjustment go back into a Posted state, and you can select the A/P invoice 

for payment again on the Pay A/P invoices page. 

The adjustment remains in the system and can be applied as a vendor credit again. 

Scenario 4 

Use this scenario when you need to edit the adjustment. 

You applied the credit and payment separately (for example, you applied the credit to an A/P 

invoice, then came back later to pay the rest of the A/P invoice with a check). 

You haven’t yet printed or confirmed the check payment, and the A/P invoice is in a Partially paid 

state (the system has applied the credit as a payment). The adjustment is marked as Paid. 

Do this  

Reverse the adjustment on the A/P Adjustments list page. 

After you reverse a transaction, you can’t undo the reversal. However, you can create another 

transaction to replace the original. 

After you reverse the adjustment, the A/P invoice returns to a Selected state, and the 
adjustment is no longer available to apply to any other A/P invoice as a vendor credit.

Clearing a Credit Adjustment 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > All > Adjustments`


In RealPage Accounting, you create a debit memo to record a credit from a vendor, such as a 

credit for shipping costs, or a return of product. After you create a debit memo, if you need to 

clear it from the system, you can either reverse or delete it depending on where the adjustment 

stands in the workflow: 

• 
If you haven’t applied the adjustment to a vendor A/P invoice, you can delete the debit 

memo (on page 847). 

• 
If you’ve applied the adjustment to a vendor A/P invoice, then you can reverse the debit 

memo (on page 785). 

This topic describes how to clear a debit memo and answers questions about clearing debit 

memos when there are additional considerations, such as when a vendor pays a refund on a 

negative balance. 

Deleting a Debit Memo 

You can delete a debit memo if it has not yet been applied to an A/P invoice. 

To delete a debit memo: 

1. 
Open the Accounts payable menu. 

2. 
Select Adjustments. The A/P Adjustments page appears with a current list of debit memos. 

3. 
Select the check box on the right side of the appropriate debit memo, and click Delete. 

4. 
If you see a Reverse link instead of a check box, the debit memo has already been applied 

to one or more A/P invoices, and can only be reversed. 

5. 
Confirm that you want to delete the debit memo. 

The system clears the debit memo from the list and from the system. No record of it 

remains. 

---



#### Reversing a Debit Memo
*Source: `RP Accounting AP Daily Tasks User Guide.pdf`, Page 866*

A/P Adjustments 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Daily Tasks User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Reversing a Debit Memo 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > All > Daily Tasks > Adjustments > Reverse`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Cash Management > All > Reports > Check Registers > View > Void`


You can’t delete an adjustment if you’ve applied a portion, or all, of the available adjustment to 

one or more A/P invoices, but you can reverse it to clear the adjustment as follows: 

• 
If you’ve applied no payment on the adjustment from the vendor, such as a check or 

electronic payment, you can reverse the debit memo. 

• 
If you’ve applied a payment on the adjustment, such as a transfer of funds to your bank 

account, you have to void the entire applied payment, and then reverse the adjustment. 

After you reverse an adjustment, you can’t undo the reversal. However, you can create another 

adjustment to replace it. 

If you do not see a Reverse link, the debit memo hasn’t been applied to one or more A/P invoices. 

You can click the Delete link to delete it to clear the debit memo from the system. 

To reverse a debit memo that has no associated vendor payment: 

1. 
Open the Accounts payable menu. 

2. 
Select Adjustments. The A/P Adjustments page appears with a current list of debit memos. 

3. 
Click Reverse on the right side of the appropriate debit memo. 

The Transaction Reversal Date page appears. Select the date for reversing the transaction. 

This is usually the original transaction date or a later date. 

4. 
To reverse the adjustment, click Submit. 

The debit memo is cleared from the system. The A/P Adjustment list displays the reversal on 

two rows to show the balancing transactions for removing the debit memo from the system. 

5. 
Optional. If you want to reverse one or more A/P invoices associated with the adjustment, 

under Reverse, select the check box for each A/P invoice, and click Submit. 

Both the debit memo and the selected A/P invoices are cleared from the system. The A/P 

Adjustments list and the A/P invoices list display the reversal on two rows to show the balancing 

transactions for removing the debit memo and the unpaid A/P invoices from the system. 

To reverse a debit memo that has an associated vendor payment: 

If you’ve made a vendor payment associated with a debit memo, such as a transfer of funds to 

your bank account, you first void the payment in the bank or check register, then reverse the 

debit memo. 

---

A/P Adjustment Page 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > All > Daily Tasks > 
 Adjustments`


Use the A/P Adjustment page to enter credit or debit adjustments against vendors.  

For example, a vendor may credit you for a product return, for reparation on bad service, or for 

shipping fees in the case when shipping was offered for free and then charged against you. When 

you create an adjustment, you are unable to associate the adjustment to a specific A/P invoice 

from that vendor. However, during the invoice paying process, you can apply the adjustment to a 

specific A/P invoice. 

Duplicating an A/P Adjustment 

The Duplicate button lets you add similar transactions quickly. 

To duplicate an A/P adjustment: 

1. 
Open the Accounts payable menu. 

2. 
Select Adjustments. The Adjustments list opens. 

3. 
Click Edit next to the adjustment that you want to copy, and then click the Duplicate option. 

The system opens a new adjustment record with data copied from the source adjustment. 

4. 
Change the adjustment data as needed. 

5. 
Click Draft or Draft & new to save your progress on the transaction. The system saves the 

entry, but doesn’t post it. You can also Post or Post & new to post the transaction. The 

system validates the transaction and posts it to the General Ledger. 

Posting a Transaction 

After you create a transaction in Accounts Payable, Accounts Receivable, and the General Ledger, 

and click Post, if all requirements are met, the system records the transaction in the General 

Ledger. 

Printing a Transaction 

After creating a transaction, printing a copy of it is just a click away. You can print from the 

transaction page itself, such as from the A/P invoices or A/R invoices page, or from the 

transaction list page, whichever is more convenient. 

To print a transaction: 

• 
Transaction list page: Find the desired transaction and, at the end of the row, click Print. 

• 
Transaction page: Click Print at the top of the page. 

The system generates a PDF of the transaction, which you can view, print, or save to add as an 

email attachment as needed.

Vendor 
The vendor who is the source of the adjustment. You can either select a 

vendor from the drop-down list or type the name of the vendor for the 

adjustment. For vendors you use repeatedly, it’s best to enter them into 

the system. 

Pay to 
This field determines the vendor contact to be paid. The system 

automatically defaults this field from the Pay to contact field in the 

vendor record or, if none, from the vendor you selected in this page. You 

can override the default as required, for example, if the vendor has 

multiple offices and requests you to send the check to an office other 

than the one on record. 

Return to 
This field determines the vendor contact for return of the purchase. The 

system automatically defaults the Return to contact from the purchasing 

transaction, which itself defaults from the vendor record. If neither exists, 

the system defaults this field to the vendor you selected in this page. 

Although in most cases, you won’t need to override the default, you can, 

for example, if you are returning a defective product and the vendor 

wants you to return it to a location other than the one on record. 

Type 
Determines whether the adjustment increases or decreases the overall 

amount owed to the vendor. 

Credit Memo: Increases the amount owed 

Debit Memo: Decreases the amount owed 

The type of adjustment cannot be edited. To change an adjustment from 

a Debit Memo to Credit Memo, or vice versa, delete or reverse the 

adjustment and create a new one. 

Adjustment number 
The number the system uses to track the adjustment. 

Reference invoice 

number 

This is a number such as a purchase order or account number that may 

be useful in searches or reports on the A/P invoice. This number shows 

on the G/L Details report, but does not print on the check or check 

remittance stub.

### A/P Advances Overview
*Source: `RP Accounting AP Daily Tasks User Guide.pdf`, Page 876*

A/P Advances 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Daily Tasks User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

A/P Advances Overview 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > All > 
 Advances`


Use the Advance Payment feature when you need to pay a vendor prior to obtaining an A/P 

invoice. For example, create an advance when a vendor requires an up-front deposit on a fee.  

Most advances have only one line item. For example, an attorney might require an advance as a 

retainer, or a painting contractor might need an advance to buy the paint. However, the Create 

Advance Payment page enables you to create as many line items as needed. For example, say the 

painting contractor not only will buy the paint but will also hire some labor to clean up the 

building before painting it. You could have one line item for the paint and another for the labor. 

Moreover, multiple line items can have the same or different accounts. 

In addition, you can assign an account, department, and location to each line item. Assigning 

different accounts and departments can be useful in a multiple line-item situation. In our prior 

example, maybe you want to assign the cost of the paint to G&A, but the labor to Maintenance. 

What happens next depends on the payment method (for example check versus cash). In some 

cases (cash, for example), you don’t actually make a payment – you record the advance and when 

the A/P invoice is received and comes due, apply the credit to the A/P invoice amount. 

Advances cannot be saved as drafts. 

---



### A/P Advanced Payment Workflow
*Source: `RP Accounting AP Daily Tasks User Guide.pdf`, Page 877*

Chapter 10: A/P Advances 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Daily Tasks User Guide 

A/P Advanced Payment Workflow 

Assuming no approval process, the following example illustrates the simple flow and interaction 

between you and your company as you create and process an advance that has check as the 

payment method. 

If approval is enabled, then an approval cycle is included, which determines whether the advance 
payment request actually gets paid, modified, or declined. 

Paying an advance by other methods, such as credit card, cash, or transferring funds follows a 

similar flow: 

• 
Credit card: The system creates a matching credit-card transaction for the advance, and lists 

the payment in the Posted Payments page. After the A/P invoice is received, recorded, and 

comes due, you can select it and apply the advance as a credit to the total. 

• 
Record transfer and Cash payments: The system lists the advance payment in the Posted 

Payments page. After the A/P invoice is received, recorded, and comes due, you can select 

it, and apply the advance as a credit to the total. 

No matter what payment method you use, after the advance payment is posted, or printed and 

confirmed, you can view it in the Posted Advances page. You can view what transactions the 

advance was applied to and how much of the advance is still remaining. 

---

Advance Payment Workflow

3.

4.

5.

Adding Advance Payments

 Advances`


To create an advance payment to a vendor: 

1. 
Select 
 Add next to the Advances option. The Create advance payment page opens.  

2. 
In the Payment date field, click 
 Calendar to open a calendar to select a date. 

3. 
In the Vendor ID drop-down list, select a vendor. 

4. 
In the Payment Method drop-down list, select the method of payment. The payment 

method determines how the advance payment is processed in your company. 

When you select Credit Card, the system automatically creates a credit card transaction. 

When you select Record transfer, the Reference # field is displayed. Enter the unique 

identifier for the record transfer in this field. 

5. 
In the Bank drop-down list, select the bank from which to draw the funds for the advance 

payment. 

6. 
In the Description field, type any note you want to store with this record. 

Filling In the Line Items 

For each line in Items, set the following: 

1. 
Click the G/L Offset Account drop-down list, and then select an account to receive the 

expense. 

2. 
In the Amount column, type the amount of the expense. 

3. 
To add a note about this item, in the Memo column, type any information you want to store 

with this entry. 

4. 
In the Department drop-down list, click the drop-down arrow and select the department 

associated with this advance, as needed.  

5. 
In the Location drop-down list, click the drop-down arrow and select the location 

associated with this advance, as needed.  

6. 
In the Unit drop-down list, click the drop-down arrow and select the unit associated with 

this advance, as needed.  

7. 
In the Segment type 1 and Segment value 1 drop-down lists, select the desired segment 

type and its value to identify this transaction.  

8. 
In the Segment type 2 and Segment value 2 drop-down lists, select the desired segment 

type and its value to identify this transaction.

After you save the advance, the system automatically does the following based on the 

selected payment method: 

• 
Check: The system creates a payment request and adds the advance to the Print 

checks list in preparation for printing. After printing, the system adds the advance to 

the Posted payments list. 

• 
Credit card: The system creates a credit card transaction and adds the advance to the 

Posted payments list. 

• 
Record Transfer and Cash: The system adds the advance to the Posted Payments list.

#### Removing an Advance
*Source: `RP Accounting AP Daily Tasks User Guide.pdf`, Page 881*

Chapter 10: A/P Advances 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Daily Tasks User Guide 

Removing an Advance 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > All > Daily Tasks > Advances`


You can quickly cancel, void, or reverse an advance payment that hasn’t yet been applied to an 

A/P invoice. Which procedure you use depends on whether payment was made on the advance 

and the payment method. (For payment by check, the advance is paid after the check is printed 

and confirmed.) 

Payment method: Check - unpaid 

Procedure: Cancel the payment request (on page 498) 

System action: Removes the entry from the Payment requests page and the Print checks 

page. No record remains. 

Payment method: Check - paid 

Procedure: Void the check (on page 1007) in the check register 

System action: The Check Register and the Posted Advances pages display the original 

entry and the voided entry. The advance is no longer available for selection in the Pay A/P 

invoices page. 

Payment method: Credit Card 

Procedure: Reverse the payment in the credit card register 

System action: The Credit Card Register and the Posted Advances pages display the 

original entry and the voided entry. The advance is no longer available for selection in the 

Pay A/P invoices page. 

After you reverse the advance, you can’t undo the reversal. However, you can create 
another advance to replace it. 

Payment method: Record Transfer 

Procedure: Void the transfer in the bank register 

System action: The Bank register and the Posted advances pages display the original entry 

and the voided entry. The advance is no longer available for selection in the Pay A/P 

invoices page. 

---

### The Cash Payment Method
*Source: `RP Accounting AP Daily Tasks User Guide.pdf`, Page 900*

Payment Methods 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Daily Tasks User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

The Cash Payment Method 

After you pay an A/P invoice with cash, you record the payment. 

To create a record of a cash payment transaction, you need the following information: 

• 
Bank name 

• 
Bank G/L account 

• 
Payment date 

• 
Vendor name 

• 
Invoice 

The impact of recording a cash payment on accrual accounting is that it reduces the cash balance 

for the associated bank account and reduces the associated payable liability account. 

---



### Check Payment Methods
*Source: `RP Accounting AP Daily Tasks User Guide.pdf`, Page 901*

Chapter 11: Payment Methods 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Daily Tasks User Guide 

Check Payment Methods 

We offer different check payment methods. Choose which check payment to use based on what’s 

most important to you. 

• 
Cost: If you pay relatively few A/P invoices by check, printing checks yourself will usually 

cost less.  

• 
Currency: If all your checks are in US dollars, print checks in any way. If you need to print 

checks in Canadian currency you can print on standard pre-printed check stock or blank 

check stock. If you need to print checks in Mexican currency, print checks using blank check 

stock. 

• 
Maintenance: If you print on blank check stock, you need special ink (MICR), a printer that 

supports the ink, and confirmation from your bank that you’ve properly aligned your checks 

for printing. If you use pre-printed check stock, you need separate check stock for each 

checking account. 

---



### Record Transfer Payment Method
*Source: `RP Accounting AP Daily Tasks User Guide.pdf`, Page 902*

Payment Methods 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Daily Tasks User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Record Transfer Payment Method 

A record transfer is the back record of a funds transfer outside of the system. You won’t need to 

print a check, but you do need to record the transfer of funds from your bank account. 

Use a record transfer payment method when you’ve made payments outside of RealPage 

Accounting, for example, with a wire transfer or electronic funds transfer.  

How It Works 

Normally, you record all your A/P invoices in RealPage Accounting, but sometimes you pay them 

outside of the system such as when you use an electronic funds transfer (EFT). In these cases, use 

the Record Transfer payment method to mark the invoice as paid.  

Benefit 

Using this method reduces the vendor payables liability account without having to print a check. 

---



### Electronic Payment Method
*Source: `RP Accounting AP Daily Tasks User Guide.pdf`, Page 903*

Chapter 11: Payment Methods 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Daily Tasks User Guide 

Electronic Payment Method 

RealPage Accounting offers several electronic payment methods. By default, the ACH (Automated 

Clearing House) payment method is available, allowing you to pay an A/P invoice electronically. 

For multiple-currency companies, EFT and BACS are also available. 

Typically, property management companies use electronic payments to pay vendors and 

reimburse employees. This document focuses on paying vendors. 

Before you can use an electronic payment method, you must configure the system so that it can 

make the payments. See Electronic Payment Configuration Workflow. 

To pay a vendor using an electronic payment, follow these steps: 

1. 
Pay the vendor (on page 902). 

2. 
Generate a payment file (on page 906). 

3. 
Download the payment file. 

4. 
Send the file to your bank for processing. 

5. 
Confirm the payment.

### About Manual Payments
*Source: `RP Accounting AP Daily Tasks User Guide.pdf`, Page 910*

Payment Methods 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Daily Tasks User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

About Manual Payments 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > All > Daily Tasks > Banking > Manual Payment`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Cash Management > All > Periodic Tasks > Manual Payment`


Occasionally, you must deviate from the normal Accounts Payable workflow to pay A/P invoices. 

For example, if you had food delivered to the office and paid for it immediately or if you paid an 

unexpected COD for a delivered package. Previously, if you paid by check, you could quickly add 

an A/P invoice and record its payment at the same time. Manual payments allow you to easily 

record payments made by cash, credit card, or funds transfer. 

Manual Payments vs. Quick Checks 

Manual payments involve recording each payment, including handwritten checks, one at a time. If 

you have many handwritten checks to record, you can use quick check entry (on page 977) to 

enter the data for up to 100 handwritten checks on a single page. The difference between these 

two methods of recording is that manual payments provide more flexibility for reporting on 

various dimensions, while quick check entry offers support only for reporting on departments and 

locations.

This procedure describes how to make an electronic payment. In RealPage Accounting, you’ll see 

this referred to as ACH, EFT - Standard 005, and BACS in Payment method fields. If you work for 

a multi-currency company, see also Setting Up Vendors to Receive Foreign Electronic Payments 

(on page 109). 

Selecting the A/P Invoices to Pay with Electronic Payments 

To start the A/P invoice payment process: 

1. 
Open the Accounts payable menu. 

2. 
Select Pay A/P Invoices. 

3. 
On the Pay A/P invoices page, filter the A/P invoice payments as needed. 

If you’ve selected ACH or Electronic payment as the preferred payment method for 
selected vendors, you can use the Payment method drop-down menu to filter for only A/P 
invoices that should be paid by electronic payment. 

4. 
In Payment method, select ACH or Electronic payment. 

The list changes to show A/P invoices only from vendors for which you’ve enabled ACH or 

electronic payments.  

If you already filtered the list of A/P invoices so that it only shows electronic payments, 
this payment method will be completed for you. 

5. 
In the Bank drop-down list, select a bank that you have configured to accept your electronic 

payments.  

6. 
In the Set payment date to field, select or type the date the payment is to be made. 

7. 
Use the Send payment notifications from field to set the email address that the system 

sends notifications from. The system automatically includes a contact name and email 

address in the email body so that the recipient can communicate about any payment 

questions or issues. 

8. 
In the Payment description field, type the text that you want to associate with this payment. 

The information that you type appears in the Memo field on the View payment request 

page, in the Description field on the ACH payment field details page, in the description on 

the Bank reconciliation page, and in the Memo field on the Posted payment page.  

9. 
In the list of A/P invoices at the bottom of the page, select the A/P invoices you want to pay. 

---


<!-- Page 921 -->
Chapter 12: Banking 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Daily Tasks User Guide 

10. 
Type the amounts you want to pay in the Amount to pay column. 

By default, multiple A/P invoices from a single vendor will result in one payment.  

11. 
If you want to create separate payments for each A/P invoice, select the Separate vendor 

payment check box. 

12. 
Click the Pay Now button. The payments are saved as payment requests. 

If the payments don’t require approval first, the payments are also immediately available to 

be generated in a payment file. 

Payments aren’t posted until you generate the payment file and confirm that the 
payments were processed by your bank. 

What’s Next? 

• 
If payment approvals are enabled and you are an approver, select Approve payments and 

then approve the payments. If you are the only approver, you can generate the payment file. 

If you are not an approver or are not the only approver, select View payment requests and 

monitor the status. When the status changes to Approved, you can generate the payment 

file. 

• 
Generate the Payment File (on page 906).

been approved.

File Generation Workflow 

Use the Generate file list when it is time to make a vendor payment. 

1. 
Review the approved payment requests that have your preferred bank format selected as 

the payment method. 

2. 
Filter the list (on page 908) so that it contains only the payment requests that you want to 

add to the payment file. 

3. 
Generate the payment file (on page 906). 

After generating payment files, use the Payment File (on page 912) list to process the payment 

files. 

1. 
Download the payment file. 

2. 
Send the payment file to your bank for processing.

Use this page to filter your list of electronic payment requests. Filtering your list of electronic 

payments enables you to simplify your workflow processes. By setting specific filters, you can limit 

your list of payments to only those payment files that you want to generate right now. 

This page appears when you select the Customize list button from the Generate file list. 

The Generate file (filter page) contains three sections. Each section contains a group of controls 

that affects the payment files that ultimately get generated. 

• 
Payment range/sorting: This section contains controls that determine the number of 

payments displayed on a page, and allows you to select the fields by which to sort the 

electronic payments. 

• 
Filters: This section contains options by which you can restrict or filter the electronic 

payments. 

• 
Time period: This section allows you to constrain the electronic payments by a time period.

To customize the list of payments: 

1. 
From the Applications menu, select Accounts payable or Cash management, and then 

select the All tab. 

2. 
Select ACH file generation.  

3. 
Click the Customize list button. The system opens the Generate ACH File parameters page. 

Filling In the Payment Range/Sorting Section 

Define the sorting and number of records to display. By default, the system sorts electronic 

payments by date. 

1. 
In Sort by, click the Select link and select fields by which you want to sort by clicking 

Add next to the desired field. See Using the multi-select box for help. 

2. 
In Max rows, you can change the number of payments displayed on a page. Select 50, 100, 

or 200 rows. 

Assigning Filters in the Filters Section 

1. 
To filter the payments by the account they are drawn on, in the Checking account 

drop-down list, select the account. 

2. 
Specify whether you want to include only vendor payments, employee payments, or both by 

selecting the Select all vendors and Select all employees check boxes. 

3. 
In the From vendor/To vendor and From employee/To employee drop-down lists, select a 

beginning and ending range by ID number.  

4. 
In the Entity/Entity group drop-down list, select the entity or entity group by which you 

want to filter the payments. 

5. 
Select the Show entity level payments check box to include payment details for payments 

generated at the entity level. 

Set Date Filters in the Time Period Section 

1. 
To limit the listed payments by date, under Time period, you have two options: 

• 
Choose a time period by clicking Payment period and clicking a standard accounting 

period such as Current month, Prior quarter, and so on. Then enter an As of date 

from which the system calculates the corresponding time period. The As of date 

default is the current date. 

• 
Choose a date range by entering a start and end date in Start date and End date, 

respectively. 

2. 
When you have the filters set how you want them, click View. To return to the filters and 

format page, click the View button.

##### Confirming an Electronic Payment
*Source: `RP Accounting AP Daily Tasks User Guide.pdf`, Page 934*

Confirming an Electronic Payment 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > All > Daily Tasks > Banking > Electronic Payments > 
Payment File`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > All > Daily Tasks > Banking > ACH > ACH Payment 
File`


When the bank notifies you that the payment has been processed, you must confirm the payment 

file. One exception is when you upload a payment file to a bank’s SFTP site. If the upload is 

successful, then the system automatically confirms the payment on your behalf.  

You can disable the automatic confirmation of electronic payments using the Disable 

auto-confirmation of ACH files option in Cash Management configuration. This setting applies 
to ACH, EFT, and BACS electronic payments.  

To confirm a payment file: 

1. 
Open the Accounts Payable menu. 

2. 
In the Daily tasks section, in the Banking subsection, click Electronic payments (or ACH), 

and then select Payment file (or ACH payment file). The Payment file list opens. 

If your company is a single currency company, then the option under Banking is ACH, and the 
name of the payment file is ACH payment file. 
If your company is a multi-currency company, the option is Electronic payments, and the 
name of the payment file option is Payment file. 

3. 
Find the payment file that you want to confirm. 

4. 
Click the corresponding Confirm link. The status changes to Confirmed. 

The Confirm and Delete links are not available confirmed payments. 

5. 
Click the File description link of the confirmed payment to view the payment details.  

6. 
Click the Payment ID link. From this page, you can print the payment record or send a 

payment notice email to the vendor.

Use the Schedule (ACH) file generation list to automate ACH file generation so you don’t have to 

spend time selecting which payments to create a file for. From this list, you can: 

• 
Schedule a new ACH payment file. 

• 
View, edit, and delete scheduled files. 

• 
View the last execution date and next execution date. 

• 
View the result of the last execution. 

• 
Open a history log showing the results of all previous executions. 

• 
Turn a schedule off to stop generating the payment file. 

If the schedule runs successfully, the ACH file is created and added to the Payment file list (on 

page 912), where you can download the file or upload it directly to the bank via a secure FTP 

connection.  

If the schedule fails to run, you can click the Failure link in the Last result column to open the 

Execution log list and view the corresponding error log to help you troubleshoot your automated 

payment file (on page 925).

##### Scheduling an ACH Payment File
*Source: `RP Accounting AP Daily Tasks User Guide.pdf`, Page 941*

Chapter 12: Banking

Scheduling an ACH Payment File 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Cash Management > All > ACH / Electronic Payments > 
 Schedule 
(ACH) File Generation`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > All > Daily Tasks > Banking > ACH / Electronic 
Payments > 
 Schedule (ACH) File Generation`


To schedule an ACH payment file: 

1. 
Click the Add button in the upper-right corner of the Schedule ACH file generation list. 

The Schedule ACH file generation page opens. 

2. 
In the Schedule ID field, type a name for the schedule. This is a required field. 

3. 
In the Entity/entity group drop-down list, select the entity or entity group for which you are 

scheduling the payment file. If you want to schedule the payment file for all locations, leave 

the field blank. 

• 
Select the Include entity level check box if you want to include the entity or entity 

group name in the payment file. 

4. 
To include only payment requests from specific vendors in the payment file, select a range 

of vendor IDs from the Vendor from and Vendor to fields. 

5. 
To include only payment requests from a specific bank in the payment file, select a bank ID 

from the drop-down list. 

6. 
To include only payment requests of a specific vendor type in the payment file, select a 

vendor type from the Vendor type drop-down list. 

7. 
Leave the Status field as Active. 

8. 
In the Schedules section, set up a one-time or recurring schedule for generating the 

payment file: 

• 
Start date: Type or select the start date for the schedule. 

• 
Ending on: Select when the schedule should end. 

• 
Never: Continues running the schedule indefinitely. 

• 
Number of occurrences: Stops running the schedule after a specific number of 

occurrences. Define that number in the End after X occurrences field. 

• 
End date: Stops running the schedule on a specific date. Define that date in the 

End on field. 

• 
Repeat: Select the frequency of the schedule. This is how often a new payment file will 

be generated. 

• 
None: Runs once and does not repeat. 

• 
Days: Runs once every X number of days.

Viewing Execution Logs for a Scheduled ACH Payment File 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Cash Management > All > ACH / Electronic Payments > Schedule (ACH) 
File Generation > (Last Result)`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > All > Daily Tasks > Banking > ACH / Electronic 
Payments > Schedule (ACH) File Generation > (Last Result)`


Each time the schedule for an ACH payment file runs, the system creates a log file to record the 

result of the file generation attempt. These logs are added to an Execution log list specific to that 

schedule. You can open individual log files to view the status details and troubleshoot errors. 

To view execution logs for a scheduled ACH payment file, click the Success or Failure link in the 

Last result column. The Execution log list opens for that schedule.

If Successful 

If you clicked the Success link, the execution log opens to show the list of successful log entries 

for that payment file schedule. From this list, you can: 

• 
Click the View link to open the Scheduler log page containing the details of an individual 

log file. 

• 
Click the Delete link to delete an individual log file. 

• 
Click the Export button to export the list of successful log files. 

If Failed 

If you click the Failed link, the execution log opens to show the list of failure log entries for that 

schedule. From this list, you can:

##### Turning a Payment File Schedule On or Off
*Source: `RP Accounting AP Daily Tasks User Guide.pdf`, Page 945*



##### Deleting a Scheduled ACH Payment File
*Source: `RP Accounting AP Daily Tasks User Guide.pdf`, Page 945*

Chapter 12: Banking

RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Daily Tasks User Guide 

Turning a Payment File Schedule On or Off 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Cash Management > All > ACH / Electronic Payments > Schedule (ACH) 
File Generation > Turn Off/On`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > All > Daily Tasks > Banking > ACH / Electronic 
Payments > Schedule (ACH) File Generation > Turn Off/On`


You can turn off schedules for ACH payment files so they don’t continue running and generating 

payment files on a recurring basis. Schedules that are turned off are hidden from the Schedule 

ACH file generation list, but you can turn them back on at any time to resume the schedule. 

Turning a Payment File Schedule Off 

To turn a schedule off, click the Turn off link. The Status of the schedule is changed to Inactive, 

and it is hidden from the list. 

Turning a Payment File Schedule Back On 

To turn a schedule back on: 

1. 
Select the Include inactive check box at the top of the Schedule ACH file generation list. 

All inactive schedules are included in the list again. 

2. 
Find the schedule you want to make active again, and then click the Turn on link. 

The Status of the schedule is changed to Active, and it is unhidden from the list. 

Deleting a Scheduled ACH Payment File 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Cash Management > All > ACH / Electronic Payments > Schedule (ACH) 
File Generation > Delete`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > All > ACH / Electronic Payments > Schedule (ACH) 
File Generation > Delete`


Deleting a schedule is permanent and cannot be undone. If the schedule has already run on a 

previous date—or if you want to pause or disable the schedule temporarily—we recommend that 

you turn it off (on page 927) instead of deleting it so you don’t erase the log files from previous 

runs. 

To delete a scheduled ACH payment file: 

1. 
In the Schedule ACH file generation list, click the Delete link next to the payment file 

schedule. 

A confirmation message appears. 

2. 
Click OK to confirm.

#### ACH Frequently Asked Questions
*Source: `RP Accounting AP Daily Tasks User Guide.pdf`, Page 951*

Chapter 12: Banking 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Daily Tasks User Guide 

ACH Frequently Asked Questions 

Can I pay my independent contractors via ACH? 

Yes. If the vendor has a non-business bank account, be sure to choose PPD as the Standard entry 

class code for ACH payments in their vendor record. The PPD option formats the ACH payments 

correctly for a consumer account. 

What determines the payment date for posted payments? 

The estimated payment date that you enter on the Pay A/P invoices or Reimburse expenses page 

as the payment date. The actual payment date depends on when the bank receives and processes 

the payment. 

Can I void an ACH payment that I already sent to the bank? 

Yes, but you also need to contact your bank to cancel the payment. Voiding a payment in the 

system doesn’t affect the bank’s payment process. If you don’t contact your bank, it will proceed 

to issue the payment regardless of whether you void the payment here. 

Learn how to void a confirmed electronic payment (on page 936) and how to void a pending 

electronic payment (on page 934). 

Can I use ACH payments in a multi-currency, multi-entity environment? 

Any company can process electronic payments. However, you can issue these electronic payments 

only when transactions are in US dollars and are drawn on US banks.

Voiding Electronic Payments 

See How to Get Here (on page 919) for a list of ways to access this area. 

Voiding an electronic payment is similar to how you would void a check. The way you void a 

payment depends on whether or not it was confirmed. For pending electronic payments 

(payments you haven’t confirmed to the G/L), you can void a single payment or the entire 

payment file. 

 Voiding a payment in the system does not affect the bank’s payment process. If you’ve already 

sent the payment to the vendor or employee, you’ll need to contact your bank to alert them that 

you need to void the payment. 

Voiding Pending Payments 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Cash Management > All > Electronic Payments > Payment File > Void`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Cash Management > All > Electronic Payments > Payment File > Delete`


Void a Single Pending Payment within a Payment File 

If you’ve already sent the payment to the vendor, you’ll need to contact your bank to alert them 

to void the payment on their side. 

1. 
From the Applications menu, select Cash management and then select the All tab. 

2. 
In the Electronic payments section, select Payment file. 

3. 
When the Payment File list page displays, click the link for the payment file which contains 

the payment you want to void. 

The Payment File Details page appears with a list of payments that are either pending or 

confirmed. 

4. 
Click Void next to the individual payment you want to void. 

The voided payment then goes back to the View Payment Requests page where you can 

cancel the payment request. You can then reprocess the payment if necessary. 


> **Navigation Path:** `(Optional) To void the payment request, go to Accounts Payable > All > Payments > View`


payment requests.

##### Voiding a Confirmed Electronic Payment
*Source: `RP Accounting AP Daily Tasks User Guide.pdf`, Page 954*

Banking 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Daily Tasks User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Voiding a Confirmed Electronic Payment 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > All > Reports > A/P Invoices & Registers > Check 
Register > View > Void`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Cash Management > All > Reports > Registers > Check`


The way you void a confirmed electronic payment is similar to how you void a confirmed check. 

You can void confirmed electronic payments in the Check Register report. 

However, you’ll need to contact your bank and let them know you need to void the payment. 
Electronic payments aren ’t posted until the file is confirmed by the user. 

To void a confirmed electronic payment: 

1. 
Open the Cash management menu. 

2. 
In the Reports section, pause on Registers, and then select Check. 

3. 
On the Check Register page, you can filter to find the payment you want to void. You can 

also click View to view all payments. 

4. 
Locate the payment and click Void for the payment you want to void. 

The voided payment then goes back to the Pay A/P invoices page. You can then edit the 

payment and regenerate it in a new payment file. 

After the payment is voided, the associated A/P invoice appears again on the Pay A/P 

invoices page. There, you can regenerate or edit the A/P invoice and regenerate it as a new 

electronic payment. 

Electronic payments are posted after you confirm the payment. To avoid having to void a 
confirmed payment (for example, you find out it can’t be processed by your bank), send the 
file to your bank first and then confirm. This way, if your bank isn’t able to process one of 
your payments, you can void the payment individually before you confirm the file.

Setting Up Check Preferences 

The system can use a digital signature that you upload to the system on printed checks so that 

the digital signature appears on the printed checks. The system uses the signature of the person 

who selects the invoices to pay, and not the person who prints the checks. 

Create the desired digital signature as a GIF or JPG and then upload it to either the bank account 

record or to your user preferences. You can set up signatures in the system in two places:  

• 
On the bank account record. You can upload a signature associated with a checking 

account in the Cash Management application. 

• 
In your user preferences. The signature that you upload with the My preferences option is 

associated with your company user ID.  

When signatures are set up in both places, the system uses the signature that is set up in your 

user preferences, not the one set up in the bank account record. The user who selects invoices on 

the Pay A/P invoices page is the one whose signature goes on the check; it is not the user who 

prints the actual check. 

If you do not upload a signature file in your preferences, then the system uses the signatures 

associated with the checking account instead. 

If a digital signature is not set up in either location, then the check prints with a blank signature 

line. 

For information on creating a signature file, see Creating a Digital Check Signature.

Additional US banking requirements 

Some banks require the ON-US symbol to appear on the MICR line in front of the account

Foreign Check Formats 

If your company uses foreign transaction currencies, Canadian and Mexican check formats are 

available in addition to the standard US format. The system makes this choice based on the bank. 

If the bank is Mexican, so is the check format. The following illustration shows the Mexican format. 

Single Currency Companies 

Single-currency companies may also use Canadian and Mexican check formats. To do so, you 

define your company as Canadian or Mexican in Company Information, and the system displays 

Canadian and Mexican check-format choices on the Cash Management Preferences page.  

More specifically, you select Canadian or Mexican base currency in Company Info (Company > All 

> Configuration > Company) and click the Accounting tab on the Company information page 


> **Navigation Path:** `and then select the check format in Configure Cash Management (Company > Setup >`



> **Navigation Path:** `Subscriptions > Cash Management > Configure).`

Banking 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Daily Tasks User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Multiple Currency Companies 


> **Navigation Path:** `In Configure Cash Management (Company > Setup > Subscriptions > Cash Management >`


Configure), you have a choice between the currency of the bank account issuing the check or the 

location of the user. The default is to use the Bank account currency. 

However, say you have a company based in the US and the currency is USD. You also have an 

office in Canada. Users there want to print checks in Canadian format. In that case, select to use 

the Country currency. The system uses the user’s contact country code to determine the check 

format. You select the optional country code feature with the Use ISO Country List check box on 

the Company Information page (Company > All > Configuration > Company). You select the 

user’s contact country code by associating a contact with the user on the User Information page 


> **Navigation Path:** `(Company > Setup > Users). However, you specify the contact’s country with the Country Code`


drop-down list on the Mailing Info tab of the Contact Information page. 

If you have not enabled the country code feature, the system checks the user’s contact 

information to see if the manually entered country name is either Mexico or Canada to determine. 

If so, the system uses either the Mexican or Canadian check format. If not, the system uses the 

standard US version.

Check Stock 

There are two types of check stock: Blank and pre-printed. Both have advantages and limitations. 

Here’s what to consider as you choose for each of your checking accounts: 

Blank check stock: Requires MICR ink and an MICR ink printer. To address check alignment, you 

must work with your bank. Currency that you can use: USD, CAN, MEX 

Pre-print check stock: You can use any ink and any printer. To address check alignment, you can 

adjust it at your printer. Currency that you can use: USD and CAN. The check includes your bank 

account number, bank’s routing number, check number, and (optionally) your company’s name 

and logo.

High Security Check Stock 

High-security check stock reduces the risk of fraud related to: 

• 
Check washing (erasing details and re-writing the check) 

• 
Check forgery 

• 
Check copying 

High-security checks are currently only available for checks printed in USD. 

Ordering Check Stock 

To make sure your checks print correctly, order from our certified vendor. Click the link of the 

Specialty Checks and Forms website, shown below, to preview check styles.  

 http://www.specialtychecksandforms.com/ 

Multiple styles of checks are available for both blank and pre-printed checks, including standard 

checks, high-security checks, hologram checks, three checks per page, and checks positioned at 

the top, middle, and bottom. 

When ordering, get check stock that matches how you’ve set up to print from your checking 

account: pre-printed (High security or Standard) or blank. 

• 
Pre-printed check stock requires ordering check stock in advance, using separate check 

stock for each checking account, and printing from one checking account at a time. 

• 
Blank check stock requires MICR ink and a printer that supports the ink. You must also 

coordinate the alignment of check details with your bank. You can print checks in US, 

Canadian, or Mexican currency.

Select and manage the check stock for a bank account on the Bank account information page. 

You can choose different print settings and check stock for different checking accounts.

To set check stock settings:

In Cash management, select Bank Accounts.

Open the desired bank account by clicking its Edit link.

In the Bank Account Information record, click the Check Printing tab.

• 
Pre-printed check stock 

• 
Blank check stock (MICR printer ink required) 

• 
Disable check printing from this account 

5. 
Find the Print settings section. 

6. 
In Printing format: 

If you selected Blank check stock, choose one of these printing formats: 

• 
Standard: Prints the most quickly 

• 
Business: Prints amounts in a font that makes alterations difficult (for security) 

• 
Canadian: Available if you’re set up for foreign currency 

• 
Mexican: Available if you’re set up for foreign currency 

• 
Custom: You can select a custom check layout if you have created one and 

assigned it to the account. For details, see Custom check layouts (on page 965). 

If you selected Pre-printed check stock, choose one of the following:

#’s (USD and CAD) 

•

##### Setting Up MICR Information
*Source: `RP Accounting AP Daily Tasks User Guide.pdf`, Page 979*

Chapter 12: Banking 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Daily Tasks User Guide 

Setting Up MICR Information 

To set up MICR information: 

1. 
Open the Cash management menu. 

2. 
Select Bank accounts. 

3. 
Find the account with which you want to use pre-printed MICR checks, and then click Edit. 

4. 
Select the Check printing tab. 

Filling In the MICR (Magnetic Ink Character Recognition) Section 

Change the following settings if your bank requires a special alignment of the account number on 

your check. You do not need to change the default values unless your bank requests you do so. 

1. 
In Account number alignment, select the required alignment of the account number on 

your check.  

Normally, the account number is right aligned. 

2. 
Select the Left alignment button to align the account number to the left. 

3. 
In Account number positioning, enter the number of spaces required to position the 

account number on your check if you still need additional adjustment. You can enter up to a 

total of five spaces. 

4. 
In Check number length, enter the number of digits to use for your check numbers. For 

example, if your checks are currently 6 digits, and your current check number is 218 but you 

want the check number to be 7 digits, type “7” in this field. Your check number will be 

0000218 in the MICR. 

The minimum check number is 6. If your check number is 123456, and you type in a 
“5” in this field, the MICR still prints it as 123456.

##### MICR Template
*Source: `RP Accounting AP Daily Tasks User Guide.pdf`, Page 980*

Banking 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Daily Tasks User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

5. 
In Regional settings - United States, select the ON-US symbol check box if your bank 

requires the ON-US symbol to appear on the MICR line in front of the account number, and 

then select either Position 31 or Position 32 depending on your bank’s requirement.  

6. 
In Regional settings - Canada, select one of the following if your bank requires your check 

to confirm to the Canadian variation of the MICR format: 

• 
Code 45: Print the transaction code 45 on the MICR line. 

• 
US funds: Print “US Funds” under the check amount box for CPA member banks. 

MICR Template 

Amount: Position 1 to 12. This field starts and ends with the MICR Amount symbol, and is added 

later by the bank. 

ON-US: Position 13 to 32. This is a series of numbers that identifies an account number. 

Sometimes it may include the branch bank information. 

Transit: Position 33 to 43. This section contains a series of numbers that indicates the bank where 

the check is issued. This field is also known as the Routing number. The MICR Transit symbol is 

used to start and end the transit field. 

EPC: EPC occupies position 44 and is known as the External Processing Code. 

Auxiliary ON-US field: Position 45 to 58. The bank usually specifies what is included in this field. 

For example, the check serial number often goes here.  

Notes: 

• 
Make sure the MICR E138 characters are aligned against the right side of the boxes and 

positioned vertically. 

• 
You can use the CCodeMICR_X9.ttf (ConnectCodeMICR_X9.ttf) font available in the MICR 

E138 fonts package for compliance with this ANSI X9.100-160-1-2009/CPA006 standard. 

(http://www.barcoderesource.com/micrfont.shtml) 

• 
Canadian requirements: Positions 63, 64, and 65 are not used.

##### Canadian Payments Association Options
*Source: `RP Accounting AP Daily Tasks User Guide.pdf`, Page 981*

Chapter 12: Banking 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Daily Tasks User Guide 

Canadian Payments Association Options 

American and Canadian check formats differ slightly with regard to their use of the MICR format. 

Canada requires that all US dollar check payments conform to the Canadian variation of the MICR 

format. 

To print checks using the Canadian MICR format: 

1. 
Find the Regional settings - Canada section. 

2. 
Select Code 45 to print the transaction code 45 on the MICR line 

3. 
Select US Funds to print “US Funds” under the check amount box for CPA member banks 

Checking either check box prints the associated transaction codes on the checks. The 

default setting for both these check boxes is unchecked - that is, no conformation with the 

Canadian MICR check format. 

You can also apply this enhancement to any USD checking account, regardless of the 

entity’s base currency. 

Keep track of any MICR transaction codes you configure. If you select multiple transaction 
codes that conflict wi th each other (for example, both use MICR line item #14), both codes print 
in that space. You do not receive any warning about possible conflicts.

Reconciliation mode 
Select a default mode for reconciliation: 

• 
Manual: Enter miscellaneous charges from your bank statement 

yourself, and then check off the items that cleared the bank. 

• 
Automatch: Upload your bank statement, and then have the 

system match up cleared items based on criteria that you set, 

and check them off for you. 

• 
Automatch with review: Upload your bank statement, and then 

have the system match up cleared items based on criteria that 

you set, for you to examine and check off. 

You can change the default mode at the time of reconciliation.

##### Check Number FAQs
*Source: `RP Accounting AP Daily Tasks User Guide.pdf`, Page 986*

Banking 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Daily Tasks User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Check Number FAQs 

Your check number is determined in the Bank Account Information page. You can change this 

number in case of duplicate or incorrectly printed checks. 

Where can I set the next check number to use? 

You can set the next check number to use for your checking account on the Bank Account 

Information page. 

To set the next check number: 

1. 
Open the Cash Management menu. 

2. 
Select Bank Accounts, and then find the bank account for the check number to set up. 

3. 
Click Edit. 

4. 
In the Print settings section, you can set the Next check #. 

5. 
Click Save. 

For pre-printed check stock: On the Print Checks page, when you select Pre-printed checks for 

Check style and select your checking account, you can enter a Next check #. This is the number of 

the next check that’s set up to print. Entering a number in this field also updates the Next check # 

field in the Bank Account Information page for that checking account. 

Why aren’t the check numbers visible on the Print Checks page? 

The Check # column is blank until you print and confirm the check. Then, the check number will 

appear in this column. You can print a test check to see which check number is used. 

How do I change the check number on reprinted checks? 

How you change the check number and reprint a check depends on whether or not you have 

confirmed the check to the General Ledger. 

1. 
Void the check using one of the methods below: 

• 
Unconfirmed checks: If the check is unconfirmed, on the Print Checks page, select the 

Confirm/Void check box for the check you want to reprint with a new number, and 

click Void at the top of the page. 

• 
Confirmed checks: If you have confirmed the check, void it in the Check Register 

report. (on page 1008) This lets the system know the check number has already been 

used. 


> **Navigation Path:** `2. 
Set the next check number. Go to Cash Management > Setup > Accounts > Checking >`


Edit. In the Print settings section, you can set the Next check #. 

3. 
Reprint the check on the Print Checks page. Learn more about reprinting checks (on page 

1036) in a check run in Accounts Payable. 

---

Verifying and Correcting PDF Settings for Your Browser 

Chrome 

PDF reports and checks appear in a pop-up. Make sure you allow popups in your browser (the 

PDF appears in a pop-up). 

Depending on your version of Chrome, do one of the following to set Chrome to allow pop-ups: 

• 
Through Chrome v56: Go to Settings > Show advanced settings > Content settings > 

Pop-ups. 

• 
Chrome v57 and higher: Go to Settings > Show advanced settings > Content settings > 

Pop-ups and redirects. Change the setting from Blocked to Allowed. You can also click 

Allow to add specific sites such as RealPage.com. 

If you download a PDF but the files aren’t saved or you see the error “Failed - Forbidden,” disable 

the native Chrome PDF Viewer. 

Through Chrome v56: 

1. 
Open Google Chrome. 

2. 
In the address bar, enter chrome://plugins to see the list of plug-ins that are installed. 

3. 
Locate Chrome PDF viewer and put a check mark beside Disable. 

4. 
Return to RealPage Accounting and download the PDF file. 

Chrome v57 and later: 

1. 
Open Google Chrome. 

2. 
In the address bar, enter chrome://settings/content/pdfDocuments or go to Settings > 

Show advanced settings > Content settings > PDF documents. 

3. 
Enable Download PDF files instead of automatically opening them in Chrome.

##### Setting Up Preferences for Quick Check Entry
*Source: `RP Accounting AP Daily Tasks User Guide.pdf`, Page 996*

Banking 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Daily Tasks User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Setting Up Preferences for Quick Check Entry 

Before you start entering checks, you are prompted to set preferences for the summary. In most 

cases, preferences are already set to your work preferences, and you can click through to entering 

checks. However, you can adjust for each summary entered. 

To set preferences for recording multiple manually written checks: 

1. 
Open the Accounts payable menu. 

2. 
Pause on Checks, and then select Quick check entry. The preferences page opens. 

Filling In Your Preferences 

1. 
Each summary is assigned a single bank. To change the default bank, click Select Bank, then 

select the appropriate bank. 

2. 
If your checks are sequentially numbered, you can enter the starting check number and 

automatically increase the number of each new check by one. To allow this, select the 

Auto-increment check number check box. 

3. 
To automatically insert the decimal two digits from the right on amounts you type, select 

Auto insert decimal. 

4. 
To fill in values on each new check from the previous check in the group, select 

Auto-populate from last transaction. You can change the settings, but depending on your 

checks, this may save you data entry time. 

5. 
To add a document, such as a scan of the checks or a printed payment authorization, as a 

reference for the summary, in Attachments, click Add and add a PDF, MS Word, or Excel 

document. 

6. 
To view entered checks in a separate window rather than below the entry form, select Open 

list for fast entry pages in a separate window. 

If you do not post a summary before your session times out, your summary entries may be 
lost. 

7. 
Click Continue. The Quick check entry: manual page appears. 

What’s Next? 

Continue to Entering multiple checks (on page 979) 

---



##### Entering Multiple Checks (Quick Check Entry)
*Source: `RP Accounting AP Daily Tasks User Guide.pdf`, Page 997*

Chapter 12: Banking 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Daily Tasks User Guide 

Entering Multiple Checks (Quick Check Entry) 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > All > Checks > Quick Check Entry > Continue`



> **Navigation Path:** `To find this page, go to Applications > Accounts Payable > All > Checks > Quick Check Entry.`


The Quick Check Entry Preferences page appears. Click Continue. 

Be sure that the bank listed at the top matches the account your checks are drawn on. 

The bar across the top of the page displays values related to the summary to help you track 

whether your summary is complete. Start by entering a manually calculated total in My calculated 

total. The system fills in the other values as follows. 

Entering a Manually Written Check 

To enter a manually written check: 

1. 
In the Vendor Name drop-down list, select a vendor. 

2. 
If the check is dated other than today, in the Check Date field, type the correct date. 

3. 
In the Check Number field, type the number of the check. 

4. 
In the A/P invoice number field, type the invoice number. 

If your checks are sequential and you checked Auto Increment Check Number on the 
preferences page, you only need to type the first check number. 

Filling In the Line Entries for One Check 

1. 
If you are setting only one G/L Account for the entire check amount, you can type the 

amount in the Amount field to the right of the Invoice Number field to automatically add 

the amount to the first G/L Account line. Otherwise, type amounts in the Amount field next 

to the G/L Account that you are applying it to.

#### Printing Checks
*Source: `RP Accounting AP Daily Tasks User Guide.pdf`, Page 1002*



##### Printing Checks Workflow
*Source: `RP Accounting AP Daily Tasks User Guide.pdf`, Page 1002*

Banking 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Daily Tasks User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Printing Checks 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > All > Checks > Print Checks`


After configuring your system, setting up the bank account, and ordering check stock, see the 

Printing Checks Workflow (on page 984) to get started. 

Printing Checks Workflow 

Many users process and print checks throughout the day. The system defaults to settings you 

used for the last payment you processed. You can see all payments, including payments in other 

users’ queues. 

Check Printing Process 

1. 
Select: Select the A/P invoices that you want to pay. 

2. 
Wait for approval: If your checks require approval, you may need to wait for approvals 

before you can move to the next step. 

3. 
Preview: Before you print checks, the system shows a preview. The preview allows you to fix 

problems and avoid wasting ink and check stock.  

4. 
Print, save checks in a CSV file, or perform a check run 

5. 
Review: After you print checks, review them.  

6. 
Confirm: If the checks look OK, confirm them. This is important because the system doesn’t 

record A/P invoice payments in the General Ledger until you confirm that the checks printed 

correctly. 

The system will automatically confirm the checks while they are printing if you have enabled 
this setting on the Configure Cash Management page. 

---



##### Before You Begin
*Source: `RP Accounting AP Daily Tasks User Guide.pdf`, Page 1003*



##### When You Need to Create Check Runs
*Source: `RP Accounting AP Daily Tasks User Guide.pdf`, Page 1003*

Chapter 12: Banking 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Daily Tasks User Guide 

Before You Begin 

Access can vary depending on your organization’s subscriptions and your permissions. If you do 

not see the option in the menu, then ask your System Administrator to check your permissions. 

Permissions 

These permissions are required to print checks. 

Application 
Activities/Lists 
Permissions 

Accounts payable 
Print checks 
Run 

If your user account doesn’t have the permissions shown above, then ask your System 

Administrator for assistance. If you have administrator privileges, you can assign permissions for a 

new feature to a user or to a role. See Roles and Permissions for a description of how to review a 

user’s permissions. 

Prerequisites 

1. 
Before you can print checks, some configuration is required. See Configuring your system to 

use checks (on page 938). 

2. 
If this is the first time you’ve ever printed checks from the system, print a test check (on 

page 969). 

3. 
Create payment requests for the checks you want to print. 

4. 
If your company uses payment approvals, make sure that the payment requests for which 

you want to print checks have been approved. 

5. 
Confirm any checks that you have previously printed before printing more checks. See 

Confirm checks (on page 1037). 

6. 
If you want to use the current date as the check print date rather than the payment date, 

you can configure this on the Cash Management configuration page. Select the Use the 

current date as check print date check box. 

When You Need to Create Check Runs 

You don’t need to create a check run to print checks. However, if you have more than 100 checks 

to print, we recommend that you use check runs. When you create a check run, the PDF of checks 

is generated offline. Upon completion, you’ll be notified that the checks are ready to be printed.

#### Print Checks Page
*Source: `RP Accounting AP Daily Tasks User Guide.pdf`, Page 1004*

Banking 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Daily Tasks User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Print Checks Page 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > All > Banking > Checks > Print Checks`


Use the Print Checks page to: 

• 
Preview checks. 

• 
Save up to 1,000 checks in a CSV file. 

• 
Confirm checks: Confirm the checks that printed correctly. The system posts the payments 

to the General Ledger after the checks have been confirmed and the check number is linked 

to the payment request record. 

• 
Void unconfirmed checks. 

• 
View the payment request and the invoices included in it by clicking the Payment date link. 

• 
Print checks. 

You can only print checks for which you have approved payment requests. When approvals 
are enabled, only approved payment requests appear in the Print checks list.  

This page has three sections: 

• 
Filters: Use this section to limit the list of checks to the ones you want to work with. Be sure 

to click the More filters link to access all of the available filters. 

• 
Print options: Use this section to select how many checks to print per page, and to define 

the check style to use. 

• 
Checks to be printed/confirmed: Use this section to select the checks to print, confirm or 

void and to determine whether to include check stub details and vendor stub details. 

The Amount selected area shows the running total of selected checks. It appears at the top 

of the list of checks. 

The grand total of all checks appears at the bottom of the list on each page.  

---

RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Daily Tasks User Guide 

You can filter checks based on: 

• 
Checking account 

• 
Period and date 

• 
Vendor 

• 
Entity or entity group 

• 
Vendor type 

• 
Payment priority 

To print non-negotiable copies of checks that have already been printed and confirmed, see 
Printing payment copies. 

The Print Options section includes two fields: 

• 
Checks per page: Use one check per page to include printed stubs. Printing three checks 

per page omits the stub details. 

• 
Check Style: You can select pre-printed checks or use blank MICR checks. 

The Checks to be printed/confirmed section is where you select the checks that you want to Print, 

Confirm, or Void. 

You can also determine whether or not to include details:  

• 
Check stub details: Check stub details include account, department, and location. These 

details appear by your line items. You can also add the adjustment number to the check 

stub by enabling the Show recent credits applied to invoices on check/payment 

remittance (on page 782) option. 

• 
Vendor stub details: Vendor stub details include account, department, and location. These 

details appear by your line items. 

If these check boxes are unavailable, it may be because you have selected to print three 
checks to a page.
