##### Printing Checks from the Pay A/P Invoices Page
*Source: `RP Accounting AP Daily Tasks User Guide.pdf`, Page 1006*

Banking 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Daily Tasks User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Printing Checks from the Pay A/P Invoices Page 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > Checks > Print Checks`


Step 1: Select the A/P invoices to pay.  

When selecting the A/P invoices to pay by check, select these options: 

1. 
Open the Accounts payable menu. 

2. 
Select Pay A/P invoices. 

3. 
Select Check as the Payment method. 

4. 
If your company uses multiple currencies, in the Invoice currency drop-down list, select the 

currency, and then set the Exchange rate type. 

5. 
In the Payment request method drop-down list, select Merge requests into one per 

vendor if you want to create a single check per vendor. 

6. 
In the Bank drop-down list, select a checking account. 

7. 
Set the payment date. 

The check print date is the date that you selected the invoices for payment by default. 
Instead of using the payment date, you can use the current date for the check print date 
by selecting the Use the current date as check print date check box in the Cash 
Management Configuration page. 

8. 
Select the A/P invoices and enter the payment amounts. 

9. 
Click the Save button. 

If your checks require approval, you may need to wait for approvals before you can move to 
the next step. After approval, the Print checks page lists the A/P invoices that you 
selected to pay. 

Step 2: Preview and print the checks (Print Checks page) 

1. 
Open the Accounts payable menu. 

2. 
In the Banking section, click Checks, and then select Print checks.  

The Print checks page appears with the items you selected to pay (unless the payments 

require approval before being paid). 

3. 
Select the desired check view.  

The default check view is My checks. You’ll see only the checks you’ve selected to pay. To 

view another person’s checks, select their name from the Select check view drop-down list, 

or select All to view all checks available to print. 

4. 
Click the More filters link to expand the Filters section.  

---


<!-- Page 1007 -->
Chapter 12: Banking 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Daily Tasks User Guide 

Use the Filters section to simplify your check workflow. The Print Checks page automatically 

shows you only the checks for which you’ve created a payment request.  

5. 
Select a checking account if you want to print checks from one account. Leave it blank if you 

are printing from multiple accounts. 

Selecting Additional Filters (Optional) 

1. 
In the Time period section, you can specify either the check period or the start and end 

dates, but not both. Do only one of the following: 

• 
Select the Check period and specify an As of date. You can either type a date or click 

 Calendar and select the date from the calendar. 

• 
Set up a specific Start date and End date. You can either type the dates or click 

Calendar and then select the dates. 

2. 
Fill in the Check Range/Sorting section. 

To limit the checks to one vendor or a range of vendors: 

• 
Select the desired vendor in Vendor from. 

• 
If you want to print checks for just one vendor, leave Vendor to set to the same 

vendor that appears in Vendor from. 

• 
To print checks for a range of vendors, in Vendor to, select the vendor at the end of 

the range. 

3. 
To limit the checks to a specific vendor type, select the type from the Vendor type 

drop-down list. 

4. 
To limit the checks to a specific payment priority, select the desired priority from the 

Payment priority drop-down list. 

5. 
To sort the checks, click the link under Sort by and select the field or fields by which you 

want to sort. The system uses the order of the selected items for the sort order.  

6. 
Fill in the Entity/Entity Groups section. In the Entity drop-down list, you can filter by a single 

location or by a location group.  

You must have created a location group to use it for filtering. 

7. 
If you set specific filters that limit your list of checks to only the checks you want to print 

right now, you can then select all by clicking the top-most Print check box.  

8. 
When you have the filters set how you want them, click Apply filters.  

Filling In the Print Options Section 

1. 
In Checks per page, select One to print the check with a vendor stub and a check stub. 

Select Three to print three checks per page and exclude printed vendor and check stubs. 

2. 
Select the Check style: 

---


<!-- Page 1008 -->
Banking 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Daily Tasks User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

• 
Blank MICR checks: Lists checks from all checking accounts that you’ve set up for 

blank check stock. Select this option to print checks from one or more checking 

accounts. 

• 
Pre-printed checks: Lists all checking accounts that you’ve set up for pre-printed 

checks. Print checks from a single checking account to keep pre-printed check stock in 

order. The system lists all checking accounts that you’ve set up for pre-printed checks.  

• 
If you select Pre-printed checks, you must select a Checking account in the 

Filters section. This allows you to keep pre-printed check stock in sequential 

order.  

• 
If you select Pre-printed checks for Check style, the Next check number box 

appears. Type the Next check number from your pre-printed checks. 

Selecting the Checks to Print  

1. 
In the Checks to be printed/confirmed section, in the Print column, select the checks that you 

want to print. 

2. 
To print the details entered in the Pay To and Pay From fields on the check stub or vendor 

stub, select the check box for Check Stub Details or Vendor Stub Details, respectively. 

Although the Paid To and Paid For fields allow up to 1000 characters, the check stub 
detail area and the vendor stub detail area on printed checks allow only 55 characters 
total. To ensure that your complete text appears with the line item on printed checks, keep 
your notes brief. 

Unless you are printing three checks per page, check stubs are automatically included. There 

are two check stubs—one for your own records and one for vendors. Both check stubs list 

the A/P invoices paid with the check. 

The check boxes for Check Stub Details and Vendor Stub Details refer to additional coding 

details (account, department, and location) that can be included with line items on either 

check stub. 


> **Navigation Path:** `Since it ’s common to include details on the check stub that you retain for your records, you 
can set this up as a default on checking accounts. Go to Cash Management > Setup >`


Bank accounts and then edit the account. On the Check printing tab, under Print settings, 
select Print line-item detail on check stubs. 

Maximum number of check stub lines for pre-printed checks 
For pre-printed checks, check stubs include space for a maximum of 18 A/P invoices. To 
avoid overwriting the next pre-printed check, additional remittance lines can’t be included. 
If a particular check covers additional A/P invoices, you can print a payment copy for the 
check, which will include all remittance lines, and include the payment copy with the check.

---


<!-- Page 1009 -->
Chapter 12: Banking 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Daily Tasks User Guide 

3. 
To print additional details on a check, click in the Check Memo column, and then type the 

comment. 

4. 
Click Print. A window opens to show a PDF of your checks. 

If the PDF doesn’t appear, make sure you allow pop-ups in your browser. For more PDF 
troubleshooting, learn how to verify and correct the PDF settings (on page 1074 ) for your 
browser. 

5. 
Review the PDF. If you see any errors, such as incorrect dates or amounts, fix the checks and 

preview them again. 

Make sure your printer settings are set to print checks at their actual size (without 
scaling) and the orientation is set to portrait. 

6. 
When the PDF looks correct, print it. If you’re printing on: 

• 
Blank check stock: use a printer with MICR ink. 

• 
Preprinted check stock: load the printer, starting with the check that has the Next 

check number you entered in the Print options section. 

Confirming the Checks (Print Checks Page) 

To record the A/P invoices as paid, confirm that the checks printed correctly on the Print checks 

page. 

The system will automatically confirm the checks while they are printing if you have enabled this 
setting on the Configure Cash Management page. 

To confirm checks: 

1. 
Review the checks you printed. 

2. 
On the Print checks page, in the Confirm/Void column, the system selects all of the checks 

from the PDF you previewed, and then assigns a Check # for each payment to print. 

3. 
For each check: 

• 
If the check printed correctly, leave the Confirm check box selected. 

• 
If the check printed incorrectly, clear the check box. You can print these checks later. 

4. 
Click the Confirm button to record payments for the correct checks in the General Ledger.  

Your cash and your liabilities are reduced, and your vendor aging report no longer shows 

those A/P invoices.

page. 

The system will automatically confirm the checks while they are printing if you have enabled this 
setting on the Configure Cash Management page. 

To confirm checks: 

1. 
Review the checks you printed. 

2. 
On the Print checks page, in the Confirm/Void column, the system selects all of the checks 

from the PDF you previewed, and then assigns a Check # for each payment to print. 

3. 
For each check: 

• 
If the check printed correctly, leave the Confirm check box selected. 

• 
If the check printed incorrectly, clear the check box. You can print these checks later. 

4. 
Click the Confirm button to record payments for the correct checks in the General Ledger.  

Your cash and your liabilities are reduced, and your vendor aging report no longer shows 

those A/P invoices.

Voiding a Check 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > All > Check Register`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > All > Checks > Print Checks`


If you made a mistake when printing a check, or want to pay the A/P invoice at a later time, you 

can void the check. Voiding a check discards the check number and makes the A/P invoice 

available to be paid again. 

This topic describes how to void a check and provides a guide to common next steps, such as 

reprinting, changing the payment method, updating amounts, and more. 

Finding a Check to Be Voided 

The location of the check in the system depends on when you catch the mistake. 

If you already printed and confirmed the check, you’ll find the check by running a Check Register 

report.  

To run this report: 

1. 
Open the Accounts payable menu. 

2. 
Select Check register. 

If you printed the check, but didn’t confirm it, the check is still listed in the Print checks 
page. Go to Accounts payable > All > Checks > Print checks.

##### Void a Check That’s Already Been Confirmed
*Source: `RP Accounting AP Daily Tasks User Guide.pdf`, Page 1026*

Banking 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Daily Tasks User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Void a Check That’s Already Been Confirmed 

After a check has been confirmed, the transaction is complete, and the payment is recorded in the 

checking account. To void the check, you’ll run a Check register report, locate the check, and then 

void the payment. 

Step 1. Run a Check register report 

1. 
Open the Accounts payable menu. 

2. 
Select Check registers. 

3. 
(Optionally) Use the report filter options to narrow the report results based on the checking 

account, date range, or other options. 

4. 
Click View to display the report. 

Step 2. Void the check in the Check register report 

1. 
Locate the check in the Check Register report. 

2. 
Click the Void link next to the payment. 

Don’t see a Void link? The option to void a check in the Check Register report is available 
only when: 
- The check has been confirmed. 
- You have the appropriate permissions. To void A/P payments, you need permissions in 

Accounts Payable to void posted payments and (optionally) posted advances. 
- In a multi-entity environment, you are in the same entity that made the payment. For 
example, if you are displaying the Check Register report for the top -level entity and do not 
see a Void link, display the Check Register report for the entity from which the payment was 
made. 

3. 
Review the information in the Void Payment Date page. 

• 
By default, the void date is set to the current date, but you can change the date. 

• 
If you want to reverse the A/P invoice at the same time, click the Reverse check box. 

If you reverse the A/P invoice, it will not be available for you to repay it. 

4. 
Click Submit.

Step 3. Correct the Original Error 

After you have voided a check from the Check Register report, the A/P invoice is available to be 

paid again in the Select A/P invoices to pay page. 

Reprinting the Check with a New Number 

To reprint the check with a new number: 

1. 
Open the Accounts payable menu. 

2. 
Select Pay A/P invoices. 

3. 
Select a checking account as your payment method. 

4. 
Pay the A/P invoice again. 

Changing the Check 

To change the payment method, amount to pay, or date: 

1. 
Open the Accounts payable menu. 

2. 
Select Pay A/P invoices. 

3. 
Change the payment method, amount to pay, or other information. 

After you void the check, you can make some changes. However, the only way to change the 

amounts or line items on the A/P invoice is to reverse the A/P invoice. 

To edit the A/P invoice: 

1. 
Open the Accounts payable menu. 

2. 
Select A/P invoices. 

3. 
Find the A/P invoice to change and click the Edit link. 

Deleting the A/P Invoice Associated with a Check 

You can’t delete an A/P invoice after a payment has been entered, even if the payment was 

voided. 

If the invoice was entered directly in Accounts Payable, then you can reverse the invoice.  

If you use another application that can create A/P invoices, such as Spend management or Job 
cost, then you cannot reverse A/P invoices created through these other applications. Instead, 
remove the A/P liability by entering and applying a credit.

You may have an unused pre-printed check that was damaged (for example, it was torn or

Instead, change the Next check # on the Checking account information page to the number of

You can change the next check number to be printed in the Bank account information page.

On the Bank account information page, select the Check printing tab. 

5. 
In the Print settings section, find the Next check # field. 

6. 
Update the check number and click Save. 

Voiding a Quick Check 

Voiding a quick check follows the same process as when you void a confirmed check–by running 

the Check Register report. After you void a Quick Check, the associated A/P invoice is 

automatically reversed. 

Printing a Voided Check 

You can only void a check if it has been printed at least once.  

• 
After voiding the check, if you want to print it again, you must correct it. See Correcting an 

Error on a Voided Check (on page 1011). 

• 
After correcting the check, pay the A/P invoice again. See Paying A/P Invoices (on page 758). 

• 
After paying the A/P invoice, you can print the check. 

To print the corrected check: 

1. 
Open the Accounts payable menu. 

2. 
In the Banking section, click Checks, and then select Print checks.  

3. 
Find the desired check in the list, and select the Print check box. 

4. 
Click the Print button.

Setting a Check Void Date 

When you void a check, you can use the Void payment date page to choose the date on which 

the check should be voided. In addition, for checks used for A/P invoice payments, you have the 

option of reversing related A/P invoices at the same time that you void the check. 

Entering the Payment Void Date 

You can select the date for voiding the payment. This is usually the original payment date or a 

later date. 

You can void checks only within an open summary.  

To void a check that’s part of a closed summary: 

1. 
Open the summary. 

2. 
Void the check.  

3. 
Close the summary. 

If you try to void a printed check with a date that precedes the actual check date, you’ll receive 
an error. Either void the check on or after the date on the check. 

Reversing A/P Invoices Paid by This Check 

If the check was used to pay A/P invoices, this page also shows the A/P invoices that were solely 

paid by this check. If you want to reverse the A/P invoices in addition to voiding the check, select 

the appropriate check boxes. 

If you reverse an A/P invoice, a negative A/P invoice is created, thus ensuring a proper audit trail. 

In the A/P invoices list, the A/P invoice appears with the state “Reversed.” 

The transaction list does not appear if a credit has been used as part of the payment or an 
advance has been used as part of the payment. 

If you try to reverse a transaction with a date that precedes the actual transaction date, you
’ll 
receive an error. Either reverse the transaction on or after the original transaction date.

What Happens When the Check Is Voided? 

When you click the Submit button, you are returned to the page in which you clicked the Void 

link. There are now two line items for this transaction, and you can no longer click the link to void 

it again, even though it still displays the word, Void. 

In addition, the Document No. column displays the word, Voided. 

Both line items may not be visible. In a report, for example, you may have filtered or sorted on the 
date, and thereby excluded the second line item. 

Thus, the transaction is not zeroed out, and an audit trail is created. One line item is the original 

transaction. The other line added by the system is the reverse of that transaction, which produces 

a net effect of zero for that transaction. For example, say you have a check for $10. After voiding, 

you still have the original $10 check, but also a check for -$10, resulting in a net of zero. 

If you selected one or more A/P invoices, a negative A/P invoice is also created, resulting in a net 

of zero for those transactions as well.

##### Configuring Vendor Records for Joint Checks
*Source: `RP Accounting AP Daily Tasks User Guide.pdf`, Page 1038*

Banking 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Daily Tasks User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Joint Checks 

A joint check is a check made out to two parties. The recipients can cash the check only when it is 

signed by both parties.  

Property management companies may want to issue joint checks to ensure that subcontractors 

pay their vendors, which helps avoid lien and bond claims by the vendors. Vendors benefit from 

joint checks because they increase the chances that the vendors will be paid. 

How It Works 

When you create an invoice, the system uses the vendor’s Pay to contact as the default contact 

for vendor-related activities. The contact’s Print as field determines what appears in the Pay to 

the order of field on the check. 

Configuring Vendor Records for Joint Checks 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > All > Vendors > Edit > Primary Contact`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > All > Vendors > Edit > Contact List > Pay To 
Contact`


Before you can issue joint checks to two parties, update the vendor records of both signers.  

Updating Vendor Records Pay to Contact 

To update a vendor record so that the system issues joint checks:  

1. 
Create a new vendor record or open the vendor record of one of the vendors that you want 

to pay with a joint check.  

When creating checks, the system addresses the check to the same contact that appears on 

the invoice and uses the text in the Print as field of the contact record to fill in the Pay to 

the order of field on the check. The Pay to contact field often defaults to the vendor’s 

primary contact. When this is the case, you can change the Print as field of the primary 

contact on the vendor record. The primary contact’s information appears on the Vendor tab 

(the first page) of the vendor record. 

---


<!-- Page 1039 -->
Chapter 12: Banking 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Daily Tasks User Guide 

2. 
In the Primary contact section, type the names of both parties that must sign the joint check 

in the Print as field. 

3. 
Save the vendor record. 

Updating a Contact Record from the Vendor Record 

When the Pay to contact field does not default to the primary contact, you can change the 

contact record from the vendor record.  

1. 
In the vendor record, click the Contact List tab. 

2. 
In the Contact List section, find the contact that appears in the Pay to contact field, click the 

drop-down list, and then click the View link. 

The Contact information box opens for the contact. 

3. 
Click the Edit button. 

4. 
Change the Print as field in the contact record by typing the names of both parties that 

must sign the joint check. 

5. 
Save the vendor record.

#### Check Runs
*Source: `RP Accounting AP Daily Tasks User Guide.pdf`, Page 1042*

Banking 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Daily Tasks User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Check Runs 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > All > Checks > Check Run`


You don’t need to create a check run to print checks.  

When you have approved payment requests that are waiting to be paid by printed check, you can 

download up to 1,000 checks from the Print Checks list. Alternatively, you can use a check run to 

process up to 1,000 checks at a time offline.  

Upon completion, you’ll be notified that the checks are ready to be printed. 

Check Run Workflow 

1. 
Create a new check run which serves as a container for the checks you want to print all 

together.  

2. 
Add payments to the check run. 

The options you select for the check run determines how the checks for the payments in the 

run are processed. 

To prevent the possibility of generating duplicate check numbers, you can only process one check 
run at a time for a bank account. Start the next check run only after the current check run 
finishes.

Deleting a Check Run 

If a check run has not been run (the PDF file of the checks for the payments has not been 

created), you can delete the check run. 

To delete a check run: 

1. 
In the Check Run list, find the check run you want to remove and click Delete. The Delete 

link appears only if the status of the check run is Open. The system displays a delete 

confirmation page. 

2. 
Click OK.  

After the check run is deleted, the invoices that were in the check run remain available for 

payment by check. They appear on the Payments Request page with a status of Approved 

and can be added to another check run. If you don’t want to pay the invoice by check or 

you want to make other changes to the invoice, including deleting it, start by canceling the 

payment request. 

Adding Payment Requests to a Check Run from the Check Runs List 

The maximum number of checks that can be added to a check run is 1000. 

To add payment requests to a check run: 

1. 
Open the Accounts payable menu. 

2. 
Click Checks, and then select Check run. The list of check runs opens.  

3. 
Beside the appropriate check run, click the Add to check run link.  

The Add to Check Run page appears and displays a message indicating the number of 

checks that the system added to the check run.  

4. 
Click Back to return to the previous page. 

5. 
Click the Run link to initiate the check run. An offline process begins.  

6. 
Go to the Check run page to monitor its progress.

##### Voiding a Check in a Check Run
*Source: `RP Accounting AP Daily Tasks User Guide.pdf`, Page 1053*

Chapter 12: Banking 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Daily Tasks User Guide 

Voiding a Check in a Check Run 

Voiding an Unconfirmed Check 

Before the checks that were generated for a check run are confirmed, you void checks in the 

check run. In some cases, you might decide that you need to void all the checks and start over. 

To void a specific check: 

1. 
Open the Accounts payable menu. 

2. 
Pause on Checks, and then select Check run. The list of check runs opens. 

3. 
Beside the check run that contains the check you want to void, click Details. The system 

displays a list of checks in that check run. 

4. 
Beside the check you want to void, click Void. The system runs an offline process to confirm 

voiding the check. 

5. 
When you are through voiding one or more checks, you need to process the check run 

again to generate another PDF file of the checks in the run. 

To void all the checks: 

1. 
Open the Accounts payable menu. 

2. 
Pause on Checks, and then select Check run. The list of check runs opens. 

3. 
Beside the check run that you want to void all the checks, click Void All. The system runs an 

offline process to confirm voiding all the checks. Voiding all the checks essentially cancels 

the check run. 

4. 
After you’ve voided a check from a check run, the payment request for the A/P invoice 

remains listed on the Payment request page. You can choose to print the check for the A/P 

invoice again from the Print checks page or use a check run. 

If you voided the check because you found mistakes, you can correct an error on a voided check 

(on page 1011). 

Voiding a Confirmed Check 

After checks have been printed and confirmed, they appear in the Check Register report where 

you can void them. 

1. 
Open the Accounts payable menu. 

2. 
In the Reports column of the menu, select Check register. 

3. 
(Optional) Use the report filter options to narrow the report results based on the checking 

account, date range, or other options. 

4. 
Click View to display the report. 

5. 
Locate the check and click the Void link next to the payment.

6. 
Review the information in the Void Payment Date page. 

By default, the void date is set to the current date, but you can change the date. 

7. 
If you want to reverse the A/P invoice at the same time, click the Reverse check box. 

8. 
Click Submit. 

If you sent the check to your vendor, contact your bank to let them know you are voiding 

the check. 

After the check is voided, the payment request for the invoice no longer appears in the 

Payment request list. The invoice is available to be paid again in the Select A/P invoices to 

pay page unless you reversed the invoice when you voided the check. After you have an 

approved payment request for the invoice, you can choose to print the check for the invoice 

again from the Print Checks page or use a check run. 

If you voided the check because of mistakes, you can make corrections before reprinting the 

check for paying the invoice (on page 1011). 

Reprinting Checks in a Check Run 

How you reprint a check that was generated and printed from a check run depends mainly on 

whether the check has been confirmed, and whether you need to correct an error or just reprint 

an exact copy of the same check. 

Reprinting an unconfirmed check 

Reprinting unconfirmed checks depends on whether you are using pre-printed check stock or 

blank check stock and whether you need to reprint with corrections. 

To reprint a check on blank check stock without corrections: 

1. 
Open the Accounts payable menu. 

2. 
Pause on Checks, and then select Check run. The Check run list opens. 

3. 
Next to the check run with the check you want to reprint, click the Print link. 

Reprint any check in the PDF file as many times as you want. 

To reprint a check on pre-printed check stock or a check that needs correction: 

1. 
Void the check from the check run. You can void unconfirmed checks (on page 1010). 

2. 
If you need to, correct any errors (on page 1011).  

3. 
Print the check again. You can either print it from the Print checks page or add the payment 

request for the A/P invoice to a check run to print the check. 

Reprinting a Confirmed Check 

To reprint a confirmed check, you need to always void the check first regardless of the type of 

check stock (blank or pre-printed) and whether you need to reprint with corrections.

To reprint a confirmed check:

Void the check in the Check register report. See Voiding payments from a Check Register (on

After the check is voided, the payment request for the A/P invoice no longer appears in the 

Payment Request list. The A/P invoice is available to be paid again in the Select A/P

Confirming Printed Checks 

To record the A/P invoices as paid, confirm that the checks printed correctly on the Print Checks 

page. 

To confirm checks: 

1. 
Open the Accounts payable menu. 

2. 
In the banking section, click Checks, and then click Print Checks  

3. 
Review the checks you printed. 

4. 
In the Confirm/Void column, select all the checks from the PDF you previewed.  

5. 
Assign a Check # for each payment to be printed. 

6. 
For each check that: 

• 
Correctly printed, leave it selected. 

• 
Incorrectly printed, clear the check box. You can print these checks later.

General Ledger. Your cash and your liabilities are reduced, and your vendor aging no longer 

shows those A/P invoices.

Confirming a Check when the Accounting Period Is Closed 

If the checks were printed in a closed period, you must void the checks and re-issue them. See 

Re-issuing a Confirmed Check with the Same Check Number (on page 1038). 

Re-issuing a Confirmed Check with a New Check Number 

To re-issue a confirmed check with a new check number, you’ll need to: 

• 
Void the original check. 

• 
Recreate the payment. 

• 
Pay the A/P invoice again. 

This topic applies to both pre-printed check stock and blank check stock users. 

Re-issuing a Confirmed Check with a New Check Number 

To reprint a confirmed check: 

1. 
Void the check (on page 1008) in the Check register. 

• 
On the Check register page, locate the payment and click Void. 

• 
In the Void payment date page, select the date on which to void the payment. 

• 
(Optional) If you need to, reverse the A/P invoice (on page 341), select the Reverse 

check box and provide a reversal date. 

If you’ve already sent the payment to the customer, contact your bank to let them know 
you are voiding the check. 

2. 
Re-issue the payment on the Pay A/P invoices page. If you need to re-issue the A/P invoice 

as well (if you reversed the A/P invoice in the Check register page), go to the A/P invoices 

page (on page 365) to recreate it. 

3. 
Go to the Print checks page (on page 986) and select the check you want to reprint, and 

click Print. The system displays a preview of your check.  

4. 
Check that all the information is correct, and click 
 Printer. 

Make sure to enable pop ups in your browser (the PDF of your check appears in a pop
-up).

##### Reprinting a Confirmed Check with the Same Check Number
*Source: `RP Accounting AP Daily Tasks User Guide.pdf`, Page 1057*

Chapter 12: Banking 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Daily Tasks User Guide 

Reprinting a Confirmed Check with the Same Check Number 

You may have printed and confirmed a check that has incorrect information; for example, a 

transaction might have incorrect invoice dates. You want to correct the error and reprint the check 

using the same check number. In other cases, it may be better to re-issue a confirmed check with 

a new check number (on page 1038). 

As a best practice, we recommend that only one person print checks from the selected checking 
account at a time to avoid mistakenly issuing the same check number to a different transaction. 

To re-issue a confirmed check with the same number: 

1. 
Void the check (on page 1008) in the Check Register. 

• 
On the Check Register page, locate the payment and click Void. 

• 
On the Void Payment Date page, select the date on which to void the payment. 

• 
(Optional) If you need to, reverse the A/P Invoice by selecting the Reverse check box 

and providing a reversal date. 

2. 
Re-issue the payment on the Pay A/P invoices page. If you need to re-issue the A/P Invoice 

as well (you reversed the A/P Invoice in the Check Register page), go to the A/P Invoices 

page to recreate it. 

3. 
(Optional) Correct any errors. See Correcting Errors (on page 1081). 

4. 
Go to the Checking Account Information page to set the Next Check # to the number of 

the check you just voided. 

5. 
Before you change the check number, note which check number is actually next in line and 

listed. After you reissue your check, you’ll be coming back to this page to set the check 

number back to this number. 

6. 
Go to the Print Checks page and select the check you want to reprint, and the click Print. A 

pop-up preview of your check appears. Check that the information is correct, and click the 

 Print button. 

7. 
Make sure to enable pop-ups in your browser (the PDF of your check appears in a pop-up). 

8. 
Go back to the Checking Account Information page and set the Next Check # back to the 

correct number which you noted in step 4. 

---

Duplicating a Check Run 

To duplicate a check run: 

1. 
Open the Accounts payable menu. 

2. 
Select the Checks option, and then select Check run. A list of check runs opens. 

3. 
Find the check run that you want to copy, and then click the Edit link. 

4. 
Click the Duplicate button. The system makes an exact duplicate of the record. 

5. 
Change the information in the fields to create the new check run. Refer to Field-by-field 

descriptions as needed. 

6. 
Change the title to reflect the new check run. 

7. 
Make any additional changes to the record. 

8. 
Click the Save button. You can also click the Save and new button to save the record and 

create another new record. 

Printing or Exporting a Record’s Details 

Use the Print to button to view and download the information as a PDF file or as an XML file.  

1. 
Click the Print to button. The Print to box opens.  

2. 
Select a format by clicking either the PDF or XML icon. 

Printing a PDF 

Use the PDF format when you need to print a copy of the information. 

1. 
Click the PDF icon. After a moment, the record opens in an external application that 

supports the PDF format, such as Adobe Reader. 

2. 
Use the application’s commands to print the record. Typically, the command sequence is 

File > Print. 

3. 
If needed, use the application’s Save command to save the record as a PDF file.

#### Automated Check Runs
*Source: `RP Accounting AP Daily Tasks User Guide.pdf`, Page 1076*

Banking 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Daily Tasks User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Automated Check Runs 

RealPage Accounting offers automated check runs. 

The automated check run process runs after the system processes automated payments. 

Automated check runs are scheduled one hour after the automated payments process. If the 

payment process is still running, then the system delays the automated check runs until the 

payment process is finished. 

You configure an automated check run by setting up a filter to choose the checks you want to 

run, defining how you want the checks to print, and setting up the printing schedule. 

The system executes the check run and sends an email notification to the email addresses defined 

in the schedule. Afterwards, you can print and confirm the checks from the Check run list (on 

page 1027) or from the Schedule check run list (on page 1059).

##### Scheduling an Automatic Check Run
*Source: `RP Accounting AP Daily Tasks User Guide.pdf`, Page 1078*

Banking 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Daily Tasks User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Scheduling an Automatic Check Run 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > All > Daily Tasks > Banking > Checks > 
 Schedule 
Check Run`


You can create an automatic check run only at the top level. 

To create a check run and its schedule: 

1. 
Open the Accounts Payable menu. 

2. 
In the Banking section, pause on Checks, and then select 
 Add next to the Schedule 

check run option. The Schedule payments selection page opens. 

3. 
In the Check Run Schedule ID field, type a unique name for the check run schedule. 

4. 
In the Entity drop-down list, select the entity for which you want to execute a check run. 

Leave this field blank to select checks for all entities.  

5. 
Select the check box if you want to include entity-level checks in the check run. 

6. 
Use the From vendor and To vendor drop-down lists to select the beginning and ending 

vendor in a range to include a range of vendors in the check run. 

In From vendor, select the first vendor in a range of vendors to include. The system fills in 

the To vendor box with the same vendor, setting it up in case you want to filter by only one 

vendor. 

In To vendor, select the last vendor in a range of vendors. 

7. 
In Checking account, select the desired checking account that you’ve set up for pre-printed 

check stock. 

8. 
In Payment priority, if you want to filter by payment priority, select the priority of the 

payments for which you want to generate a check run.  

9. 
In the Sort by area, click the Select button and choose the item or items by which you want 

to sort the resulting checks. 

10. 
In the Vendor type drop-down list, if you want to create a check run for a specific vendor 

type, select the desired vendor type. 

11. 
The status is set to Active by default. To set the status to Inactive so that the check run 

schedule cannot be selected, select Inactive from the Status drop-down list. 

Setting Up Print Options 

1. 
Select how many checks to print per page.  

• 
One: Select this option to print your check with a vendor stub and a check stub. 

• 
Three: Select this option to use the entire paper space to print three checks per page 

and exclude printed vendor and check stubs. 

---


<!-- Page 1079 -->
Chapter 12: Banking 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Daily Tasks User Guide 

2. 
Select the check style: 

• 
Blank check stock (MICR): Select this option if you want to print checks from more 

than one checking account. 

• 
Pre-printed check stock: Select this option if you have pre-printed checks with a 

specific checking account.  

3. 
Select the Print detailed check stub check box to add transaction details to the check stub.  

4. 
Select the Print detailed vendor stub check box to add transaction details to the vendor 

stub.  

Setting Up the Schedule 

1. 
In the Start date field, type the date to begin the automatic check runs. The date must be 

today’s date or a future date. 

2. 
In the Ending on drop-down list, select an option: 

• 
End date: Select this option to stop running the check run schedule on a specific date, 

and then select the date to stop in the End on field. 

• 
Never: Select to run the check run without an end date. 

• 
Number of occurrences: Select to run the check run a set number of times, and then 

type the number of times in the End After box. 

3. 
In the Repeat drop-down list, select an option: 

• 
None: Select this option to never repeat this automatic check run. 

• 
Days: Select this option to repeat this automatic check run every certain number of 

days, and then type the number of days in the Every ___ Days field. 

• 
Weeks: Select this option to repeat this automatic check run every certain number of 

weeks, and then type the number of weeks in the Every ___ Weeks field. 

• 
Months: Select this option to repeat this automatic check run every certain number of 

months, and then type the number of months in the Every ___ Months field. 

4. 
In the Email results to field, type the email address of the person to notify about the results 

of the automatic check run. To have the system send the email to multiple addresses, use a 

semi-colon between email addresses. 

5. 
Click Save.

#### Resolving Common Check Problems
*Source: `RP Accounting AP Daily Tasks User Guide.pdf`, Page 1087*

Chapter 12: Banking 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Daily Tasks User Guide 

Resolving Common Check Problems 

Lost or Misplaced Check 

• 
The original check was lost in transit or by the recipient. Re-issue the confirmed check with 

the same check number (on page 1039) or Re-issue the confirmed check with a new check 

number (on page 1038). 

• 
The tenant or vendor never received it. Re-issue the confirmed check with the same check 

number (on page 1039). 

Damaged or Illegible Check 

• 
The check was printed incorrectly, smudged, or torn. Reprint the unconfirmed check (on 

page 999). 

• 
Bank scanners couldn’t read the MICR line. Re-issue the confirmed check with the same 

check number (on page 1039). 

Incorrect Information 

• 
Wrong payee name, amount, or date. Correct the record, and then reprint the unconfirmed 

check (on page 999). (If the check was confirmed, re-issue the confirmed check with the 

same check Number (on page 1039) or re-issue the confirmed check with a new check 

number (on page 1038).) 

• 
Address error on the check stub or envelope. Correct the vendor record, and then Reprint 

the Unconfirmed Check (on page 999). (If it was confirmed, re-issue the confirmed check 

with the same check number (on page 1039) or re-issue a confirmed check with a new check 

number (on page 1038).) 

If the vendor’s address is not correct, update the address on the vendor record (on page 
1083 ). This updates the Pay and Return to contact information of the vendor record. 
Correcting vendor contact information does not update existing posted or 
submitted/partially approved invoices, so you must edit the invoice(s) and update the Pay 

to and Return to contact on the existing invoices. The easiest way to do this is to remove 
the vendor name in those fields on the invoices, and then enter the vendor name again to 
have the system fill in the contact information with the updated address. 

Void and Replace 

• 
The original check was voided due to an error and needs to be reissued. Re-issue the 

confirmed check with the same check number (on page 1039) or re-issue a confirmed check 

with a new check number (on page 1038). 

• 
A stop payment was placed on the original check. Re-issue the confirmed check with the 

same check number (on page 1039) or re-issue the confirmed check with a new check 

number (on page 1038). 

---



##### My Bank Rejected My Checks
*Source: `RP Accounting AP Daily Tasks User Guide.pdf`, Page 1088*



##### Reprinting a Damaged or Illegible Check
*Source: `RP Accounting AP Daily Tasks User Guide.pdf`, Page 1088*

Banking 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Daily Tasks User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

System or Printer Error 

• 
The check didn’t print properly due to a technical glitch. Reprint the unconfirmed check (on 

page 999). 

• 
Paper jam or misalignment during printing. Reprint the unconfirmed check (on page 999). 

Duplicate for Documentation 

• 
A copy is needed for audit, recordkeeping, or reconciliation. Print a voided copy of the 

check (on page 1012). 

• 
A reprint is requested for internal files or external verification. Print a voided copy of the 

check (on page 1012). 

Tenant or Vendor Request 

• 
The recipient requests a reprint due to personal error or banking issues. If appropriate and if 

the check was confirmed, re-issue the confirmed check with the same check number (on 

page 1039) or re-issue the confirmed check with a new check number (on page 1038).) 

• 
You need a fresh copy for deposit or mobile banking. Print a voided copy of the check (on 

page 1012). 

My Bank Rejected My Checks 

Do you have the Magnetic Ink (MICR) Printing Specifications from your bank?  

They spell out exactly how your bank needs you to set up the line of MICR coding that appears at 

the bottom of your checks. Each bank has their own specification, and they sometimes refer to 

them as Check Printing Specifications or MICR Specifications. 

Do you have a MICR gauge?  

Slide your sample check beneath this transparent grid to verify that your MICR coding is properly 

aligned. If the alignment is off, make adjustments in the system. MICR gauges are available at 

most office supply stores and through our certified vendor. See Ordering check stock (on page 

958). 

Reprinting a Damaged or Illegible Check 

• 
If the damaged check was not confirmed, follow the directions in Reprinting an 

Unconfirmed Check (on page 999). 

• 
If the damaged check was confirmed, follow the directions in Re-issuing a Confirmed Check 

with the Same Check Number (on page 1039) 

---



##### Reprinting a Confirmed Check with the Same Check Number
*Source: `RP Accounting AP Daily Tasks User Guide.pdf`, Page 1089*

Chapter 12: Banking 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Daily Tasks User Guide 

Reprinting a Confirmed Check with the Same Check Number 

You may have printed and confirmed a check that has incorrect information; for example, a 

transaction might have incorrect invoice dates. You want to correct the error and reprint the check 

using the same check number. In other cases, it may be better to re-issue a confirmed check with 

a new check number (on page 1038). 

As a best practice, we recommend that only one person print checks from the selected checking 
account at a time to avoid mistakenly issuing the same check number to a different transaction. 

To re-issue a confirmed check with the same number: 

1. 
Void the check (on page 1008) in the Check Register. 

• 
On the Check Register page, locate the payment and click Void. 

• 
On the Void Payment Date page, select the date on which to void the payment. 

• 
(Optional) If you need to, reverse the A/P Invoice by selecting the Reverse check box 

and providing a reversal date. 

2. 
Re-issue the payment on the Pay A/P invoices page. If you need to re-issue the A/P Invoice 

as well (you reversed the A/P Invoice in the Check Register page), go to the A/P Invoices 

page to recreate it. 

3. 
(Optional) Correct any errors. See Correcting Errors (on page 1081). 

4. 
Go to the Checking Account Information page to set the Next Check # to the number of 

the check you just voided. 

5. 
Before you change the check number, note which check number is actually next in line and 

listed. After you reissue your check, you’ll be coming back to this page to set the check 

number back to this number. 

6. 
Go to the Print Checks page and select the check you want to reprint, and the click Print. A 

pop-up preview of your check appears. Check that the information is correct, and click the 

 Print button. 

7. 
Make sure to enable pop-ups in your browser (the PDF of your check appears in a pop-up). 

8. 
Go back to the Checking Account Information page and set the Next Check # back to the 

correct number which you noted in step 4. 

---



##### Reprinting an Unconfirmed Check

Reprinting an Unconfirmed Check 


> **Navigation Path:** `Accounts Payable > All > Banking > Checks > Print Checks`


Reprinting a check in property management accounting isn’t uncommon, and it’s usually done to 

correct, replace, or document a payment.  

If you’re printing on blank check stock and haven’t confirmed the check yet, you can reprint a 

check as many times as you’d like.  

Print the check again from the Print Checks page. The check will print with the same check 

number. Then, if you’re happy with the check, you can confirm it. 

If you have already confirmed the check, then you must instead re-issue the check (on page 

1039).  

Prerequisites 

• 
Preview the check and correct any errors before you print it. 

• 
The check must not have been confirmed. 

• 
Print on blank check stock.

•

• 
Administrator Role 

• 
Best Practice Accountant Role 

• 
Best Practice Accounts Payable Role  

• 
Best Practice CFO Role  

• 
Best Practice Controller Role  

• 
Cash Management - Full Role  

• 
ROLE FOR ONESITE USER Role

##### MICR Information on Checks
*Source: `RP Accounting AP Daily Tasks User Guide.pdf`, Page 1096*

Banking 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Daily Tasks User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

MICR Information on Checks 

Certain information is encoded in magnetic ink at the bottom of your check so that it can be read 

automatically. 

MICR code needs to be larger or in bold font 

• 
Make sure you’re using a MICR Toner Cartridge. You can’t use standard ink cartridges for 

checks. 

• 
Make sure you’re using a laser printer. You can’t use a dot matrix or inkjet printer for checks. 

Not sure if you have a laser printer? Go to the internet and enter your printer’s model 

number: the manufacturer’s website usually says whether you have a laser printer. 

• 
If the MICR font prints unevenly, or if numbers are oddly shaped, adjust the weight of the 

font. If characters look incomplete, use a bolder version of the font. If characters look 

smudged or blotchy, use a lighter version of the font. 

• 
If the MICR font is printing too dark/light or wide/narrow, you might need to do more than 

adjust the weight of the font: you might need to calibrate the MICR font to work with your 

printer. MICR font packages often come with a calibration tool to sync your fonts with your 

printer. 

• 
Use a Mac? Make sure you’ve set Adobe as your default PDF reader (not the Mac OS PDF 

reader). For fonts, make sure you’re using the MICR E13B font. If you don’t have it, free 

downloads are available. Search the internet for: micr font E13B download. 

• 
If printing on blank check stock becomes too much of a hassle, consider switching to 

pre-printed check stock.

Check Alignment 

Problem: The bank rejects your checks because the numbers at the bottom of the check are 

misaligned. 

Solution: The series of numbers at the bottom of the check, also known as MICR (“My-ker”), must 

be accurately aligned per the bank’s specifications. Two types of corrections are available: 

1. 
Adjusting the account number left to right relative to the routing number. 

2. 
Adjusting how the entire check image is printed on the sheet of check stock relative to the 

upper-left corner of the sheet. The following illustration shows the effects of both 

adjustments. 

a) 
Adjust the position of the entire check image relative to the sheet of check stock via 


> **Navigation Path:** `Company > Setup > My Preferences.`


b) 
Adjust the account number horizontally relative to the routing number via Cash 

Management > Lists and then select Checking Accounts > Check Printing 

Information tab.

You’re previewing a check before you confirm it, and you notice the check has the incorrect 

mailing address for your vendor. You can’t correct the address on the check you’re viewing. But 

you CAN void the check and create a new check. 

Step 1: Void the check you’re previewing. 


> **Navigation Path:** `1. 
Go to the Print Checks page (Accounts Payable > All > Daily Tasks > Banking > Check >`


Print checks). 

2. 
To the right of the check with the incorrect mailing address, select Confirm/Void. 

It’s probably still selected from when you previewed it. 

3. 
At the top of the page, click Void. 

Don’t print this same check again (it will have the old/incorrect mailing address). 

Step 2: Delete the payment request for the check 


> **Navigation Path:** `1. 
Go to Accounts Payable > All > Daily Tasks > View Payment Requests.`


2. 
On the Payment Requests page, to the right of the payment, click Delete. 

It’s probably at the top of the list. 

3. 
On the confirmation dialog, click OK. 

Step 3: Update the vendor’s mailing address 


> **Navigation Path:** `1. 
Go to Accounts Payable > All > Search & Find > Vendors.`


2. 
On the Vendors list, to the left of the vendor, click Edit. 

3. 
On the Vendor Information page, click the Contact List tab. 

4. 
Under Pay to/Return to, locate Pay to contact. 

Pay to contact shows the address to be printed on checks. 

5. 
Update the address to be printed on checks. 

6. 
If Pay to contact is Same as Vendor: 

• 
Click the Vendor tab. 

• 
Under Primary contact, update the mailing address. 

7. 
Click Save.

Workflow: Printing A/P Invoice Checks 

Printing and confirming A/P invoice payment checks is a multi-step process.  


> **Navigation Path:** `1. 
Print your checks. Accounts Payable > Banking > Checks > Print Checks`


2. 
Examine the checks to make sure that they are correct.  

3. 
Confirm the checks on the Print Checks page. Confirming a check records the A/P invoice as 

“Paid” in the General Ledger.  

After you confirm a check, you cannot reprint it without re-issuing it.  

Reprinting a Check on Pre-printed Check Stock 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > All > Daily Tasks > Banking > Checks > Print checks`


How you reprint your check depends on whether you have physically printed the check, or if you 

just selected to print but for some reason the check was not printed (the printer was not loaded, 

for example). 

If you’ve already printed on your check stock, and thus used a check number: 

1. 
On the Print Checks page, next to the payment, select the check box for Confirm/Void. 

2. 
Click Void at the top of the page. This voids the check number. 

3. 
You can either: 

• 
Print the check again using a new check number. Select the Print check box next to the 

payment and enter the Next check number field in the Print options section. This is the 

number of the next check in line to be printed. 

• 
Cancel the payment request by going to the Payment Request page (on page 672). Do 

this if you need to make a correction, for example, pay from a different bank account, 

or pay with another payment method. After you cancel the request, select the A/P 

invoice to pay again and print. The check will print using the Next check number 

entered in the Print options section. 

If the check and check number is still available to use: 

1. 
Select to Print the check again on the Print Checks page. 

2. 
When prompted, click OK to print the check again.

##### Fixing Check Runs
*Source: `RP Accounting AP Daily Tasks User Guide.pdf`, Page 1106*

Banking 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Daily Tasks User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Fixing Check Runs 

Check runs can fail for a number of reasons: 

• 
The routing number is missing on the bank account record. 

• 
The default bank G/L Account is missing on the bank account record. 

• 
The bank account’s Account ID is formatted incorrectly. 

To fix a check run: 

1. 
Open the Cash Management application, and then select Bank Accounts. 

2. 
Click Edit next to the bank account that you need to fix. 

3. 
Correct any of the three fields so that the contents are accurate. 

• 
Account ID cannot contain special characters other than a dash (-). A common 

character that causes check runs to fail is the percent (%) but any other special 

characters can cause a check run failure. 

• 
Routing number is the bank’s routing number. A routing number is a 9-digit number 

printed at the bottom of the check if you are printing on blank check stock. Otherwise, 

leave this field blank. 

• 
Default bank G/L account is the G/L account associated with the bank.

### Manual Payments
*Source: `RP Accounting AP Daily Tasks User Guide.pdf`, Page 1107*



#### Before You Begin

Chapter 12: Banking

Manual Payments 

This section describes how to record and manage manual payments. 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > All > Daily Tasks > Banking > Manual Payment`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Cash Management > All > Periodic Tasks > Manual Payment`


Occasionally, you must deviate from the normal Accounts Payable workflow to pay A/P invoices. 

For example, if you had food delivered to the office and paid for it immediately or if you paid an 

unexpected COD for a delivered package. Previously, if you paid by check, you could quickly add 

an A/P invoice and record its payment at the same time. Manual payments allow you to easily 

record payments made by cash, credit card, or funds transfer. 

Manual Payments vs. Quick Checks 

Manual payments involve recording each payment, including handwritten checks, one at a time. If 

you have many handwritten checks to record, you can use quick check entry (on page 977) to 

enter the data for up to 100 handwritten checks on a single page. The difference between these 

two methods of recording is that manual payments provide more flexibility for reporting on 

various dimensions, while quick check entry offers support only for reporting on departments and 

locations. 

Before You Begin 

Access can vary depending on your organization’s subscriptions and your permissions. If you do 

not see the option in the menu, then ask your System Administrator to check your permissions. 

Permissions 

These permissions are required to manage manual payments. 

Application 
Activities/Lists 
Permissions 

Accounts Payable 
Manual Payment 
List, View, Add, Print, Void 

If your user account doesn’t have the permissions shown above, then ask your System 

Administrator for assistance. If you have administrator privileges, you can assign permissions for a 

new feature to a user or to a role. See Roles and Permissions for a description of how to review a 

user’s permissions.

Use the Manual payments list to record one-off payments outside of the Accounts Payable 

workflow, such as: 

• 
Payments made with a hand-written check 

• 
Funds transfers from your bank to a utility company 

• 
Credit card payments made over the phone 

Adding a manual payment allows you to quickly add an A/P invoice and record the payment at 

the same time, bringing your General Ledger up to date. You can record payments made by 

check, cash, credit card, or funds transfer. 

If you have A/P invoices already entered into the system, you can use the record transfer feature 

to record any payment made outside of the system.

the payment, and a memo on a printed check.

In the A/P invoice number field, enter the number for the vendor A/P invoice. 

If you want to print the A/P invoice number on a check, type it in the Memo field. 

4. 
In the Attachments drop-down list, select an attachment. You can also click Add, and then 

upload your attachment if you want to store a digital version of a supporting document. 

Entering the Line Items 

For the payment to be posted, specify at least the account and an amount for each line item. 

Depending on your company, you may be required to enter other information, such as the 

department or location. Also, depending on how your company is set up, you can navigate to the 

detail level in line items to enter additional information. 

1. 
Set up default values (on page 369), if desired. You can override any default value on any 

line item as needed.  

2. 
Select the Account you want to post the expense to. 

You can use the field-level links to add a new G/L account, view a G/L account’s record, or 

find a G/L account’s record. To add or import G/L accounts, you must be at the top level. 

3. 
Select the 1099 check box to add the line item amount to the vendor’s Form 1099. If the 

vendor is not 1099-enabled, the 
 No symbol appears, indicating that you cannot select 

the 1099 check box. 

Duplicating a 1099 eligible manual payment creates a manual payment that is also 1099 
eligible. If you have configured Accounts Payable to enable form and box override, you can 
change the value in this check box. 

After you enter the account, the system automatically populates the Amount field. As you 

enter amounts, the Total row, or bottom of the Amount column, reflects the total amount 

of the payment. 

Negative line item amounts aren’t supported by manual payments. Instead, record your 
payment by creating an A/P invoice in Accounts Payable. Then pay it on the Pay A/P 

invoices page. 

4. 
If you use departments or locations and are assigning the transaction to them, click the 

Department or Location drop-down list, and then click the appropriate department or 

location, respectively.

Posting a Manual Payment 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > All > Daily Tasks > Banking > Manual Payment`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Cash Management > All > Periodic Tasks > Manual Payment`


How you post the payment to the General Ledger (G/L) depends on the payment method. 

Posting a Payment Made by Check 

To post a payment made by a handwritten check: 

• 
Click the Save & confirm button.  

The system posts the check to the G/L. In the Manual payments list, the State of the 

payment appears as Confirmed and the Payment method appears as Manual check. 

If you want to print the check before posting it, complete the following steps: 

1. 
Click the Save & print button. The details for the check reappear on the Manual payment 

page. 

2. 
Click the Print button. A PDF of the check appears in a new window. 

3. 
Send this PDF to the printer that has your check stock loaded and verify that the printed 

check is correct. 

In the Manual payments list, the State of the payment appears as Printed, and the Payment 

method appears as Manual check. 

4. 
Return to the Manual payment page for this payment, and then click the Confirm button. 

In the Manual payments list, the State of the payment changes to Confirmed. After you 

confirm the check, the system posts the check to the G/L. 

If you don’t confirm the check immediately, then you can continue adding other manual 
payments. However, you can’t add and print another check until you confirm this check. To 
return to the Manual payment page to confirm the check, click the View link next to the 
payment.

##### Voiding a Manual Payment
*Source: `RP Accounting AP Daily Tasks User Guide.pdf`, Page 1112*

Banking 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Daily Tasks User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Posting a Payment Made by Cash, Credit Card, or Record Transfer 

To post a payment made by cash, credit card, or record transfer: 

• 
Click the Save & confirm button.  

The system posts the check to the G/L. In the Manual payments list, the State of the 

payment appears as Confirmed. 

Voiding a Manual Payment 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > All > Daily Tasks > Banking > Manual Payment > 
Void`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Cash Management > All > Periodic Tasks > Manual Payment > Void`


You cannot edit or delete manual payments after they are saved and confirmed. However, you 

can void the payment, which automatically reverses the A/P invoice. Voiding a payment reverses 

its effect on the General Ledger (G/L) and leaves a record of both the original and voided 

payment. 

When you void a payment: 

• 
The system creates a new transaction that is the reverse of the transaction you are voiding. 

In other words, the transaction is not zeroed out, resulting in an audit trail. This produces a 

net effect of zero for that transaction. 

• 
The system treats the reversed entry as a new payment and places the reversed manual 

payment into its payment summary based on the auto-summary frequency. 

• 
Both transactions are labeled as Voided. However, there are now two: the original positive 

one and the new negative reversing one. The title of the summary contains wording similar 

to “Reversed Quick Payments.” 

• 
The system also reverses the A/P invoice that is associated with the voided payment in a 

similar manner, leaving two A/P invoices: the original positive one and a new negative 

reversing one. Both are labeled as Reversed. 

If a manual payment is in a summary, you must open the summary before you can void the 
payment. You cannot void a reconciled payment or a payment in a closed period. 

To void a manual payment: 

1. 
In the Manual payments list, locate the payment that you want to void, and then click the 

corresponding Void link. The Void payment date box opens. 

2. 
In the Void the payment on date field, type or select a date on or after the transaction date. 

3. 
In the Memo field, type an optional note to store with the G/L entry. 

4. 
Click the Submit button.

Editing or Deleting Manual Payments 

You cannot edit or delete manual payments after they are saved and confirmed. However, you 

can void a payment, which automatically reverses the A/P invoice.

Viewing a Manual Payment

View`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Cash Management > All > Periodic Tasks > Manual Payment > View`


You can view manual payment details on the Manual payment page. 

To view a manual payment record: 

• 
In the Manual payments list, locate the record that you want to view, and then click the 

corresponding View link. 

The Manual payment page opens. 

Reclassifying an A/P Invoice Paid by a Manual Payment 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > All > Search & Find > A/P Invoices > Edit > Reclassify`


When you add a manual payment, the system automatically creates an A/P invoice for the 

payment. While you can’t change the date, total amount, or vendor for the A/P invoice, you can 

change other information, especially if you want to change how the expenses were assigned. 

To reclassify an A/P invoice: 

1. 
Open the Accounts Payable menu. 

2. 
Select A/P Invoices. 

3. 
rom the A/P invoices list, find the A/P invoice associated with the manual payment. 

4. 
Click the Edit link. 

5. 
Click the Reclassify button. 

6. 
Edit the available fields according to your needs. 

Having trouble reclassifying? Check out some solutions (on page 418 ). 

If you can’t edit or reclassify the A/P invoice to your satisfaction: 

1. 
Void the manual payment (on page 533), which reverses the A/P invoice.  

2. 
Create a new manual payment (on page 1091).

### Record Transfers
*Source: `RP Accounting AP Daily Tasks User Guide.pdf`, Page 1122*



#### Recording a Payment with Record Transfer
*Source: `RP Accounting AP Daily Tasks User Guide.pdf`, Page 1122*

Banking 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Daily Tasks User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Record Transfers 

This section describes how to work with payments made using the bank record transfer payment 

method. 

Record Transfer is the payment method to select when you want to represent wire transfers or 

electronic funds transfer. You don’t need to print a check, but you do need to log the transfer of 

funds from your bank account to another account. 

Manual Payments 

When you use Manual Payments, the system creates a corresponding invoice. If you already have 

an A/P invoice which exists in the system and just need to record the payment, use the Record 

Transfer payment method when paying the A/P invoice. 

Recording a Payment with Record Transfer 

To record a payment using a bank transfer: 

1. 
Open the Accounts payable menu. 

2. 
Select Pay A/P Invoices. 

3. 
Filter for the invoice. 

4. 
From the Payment method drop-down, select Record transfer. 

5. 
If your system uses multiple currencies, select the Invoice currency. 

6. 
Select the Bank. 

7. 
Select the leftmost check box of the A/P invoice you want to pay. 

8. 
Click Pay now. The Add more details page opens. 

9. 
Add a memo as needed. 

10. 
Type a Document number. The Document number must be unique as it appears on the 

bank reconciliation to help identify the transaction. 

11. 
Click the Save button. 

• 
After you click Save, if you have enabled approvals for your company, the payment 

becomes a payment request. Click View Payment requests to view the payment 

awaiting approval. 

• 
If your company does not use the system’s approval process, the system pays the A/P 

invoice and posts it to the General Ledger. Go to Accounts payable’s All tab and select 

Payments to view posted payments. 

---



#### Voiding a Payment Made by Record Transfer
*Source: `RP Accounting AP Daily Tasks User Guide.pdf`, Page 1123*

Chapter 12: Banking 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Daily Tasks User Guide 

Voiding a Payment Made by Record Transfer 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Cash Management > Reports > Registers > Bank > View > Void`


You can void a payment made using the Record Transfer payment method in the Bank Register 

report. For multi-entity companies, void the payment at the top level if the payment was made at 

the top level (shared by all entities). If the payment was made at the entity level, switch to the 

entity in which the payment was made.  

To void a payment made by record transfer: 

1. 
In the Applications menu, select the Cash Management application, and then click the All 

tab. 

2. 
In the Reports section, hover over the Registers option, and then select Bank from the 

drop-down list. 

3. 
Configure the report filters so that the report includes the payment that you want to void. 

4. 
Click the View button. 

5. 
Find the payment that you want to void in the report. 

6. 
Click the Void link next to the payment.  

The Void payment date page opens. 

7. 
Review the information on the Void payment date page. By default, the void date is blank.  

8. 
Type or select the date that you want to void the payment. This is typically the transaction 

date or today’s date.  

If the payment is eligible for reversal, a Reverse check box appears in the lower portion of 
the page. To reverse the A/P invoice, select the Reverse check box. If you reverse the A/P 
invoice, then it will not be available for you to repay it. You will have to create a new A/P 
invoice. 

9. 
Click the Submit button.

## Periodic Tasks Overview
*Source: `RP Accounting AP Periodic Tasks User Guide.pdf`, Page 11*

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Periodic Tasks User Guide 

Periodic Tasks Overview 

These options appear in the Periodic Tasks section of the Accounts Payable menu: 

Site View: This option opens the Spend Management Site Experience on a new tab of your browser. Site 

Experience offers a scaled-down version of the RealPage Accounting system designed for non-administrators who 

need to approve and manage purchase orders and A/P invoices, run reports, and make online purchases for their 

properties.  

Approval Workbench Views (on page 14): Use this page to manage the views on the Approval Workbench page. 

Month End Section 

• 
Close Subledger (on page 37): Use this option to close a subledger. 

• 
Open Subledger: Use this option to open a subledger. 

• 
Subledger summaries (on page 29): Use this option to add and manage batch summaries of your 

transactions. 

Recurring A/P Invoices Section 

• 
Fees (on page 51): Use this option to calculate and post fees and view fee details. 

• 
Management fee workbench (on page 88): Use this option to calculate and post fees and view fee details in 

a workbench setting. 

• 
Recurring (on page 110): Use this option to work with recurring charges. 

Account Maintenance Section 

• 
Print payment copies: (on page 128) Use this option to print copies of payments made with checks. 

• 
Print FAS: (on page 152) Use this option to print final account statements. 

• 
Merge vendors: (on page 140) Use this option to merge vendor records to eliminate duplicate records. 

• 
Merge history: (on page 148) Use this option to review the list of merged vendor records. 

• 
Debt maintenance: (on page 159) Use this option to add and manage loan records.  

Expense Reports Section 

• 
My expenses (on page 194): Use this option to view a list of your expense reports. 

• 
Staff expenses (on page 216): Use this option to view a list of the expense reports of other employees. 

Assets (on page 249): Use this option to add and manage asset records. 

Contracts (on page 265): Use the Contracts option to view and manage contracts that have been executed with 

your vendors. The Contracts option is available only if it has been enabled for your company by RealPage Support.

## Reclassifying Invoices
*Source: `RP Accounting AP Periodic Tasks User Guide.pdf`, Page 16*

Periodic Tasks Overview 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Periodic Tasks User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Reclassifying Invoices 

Reclassification typically happens when an invoice was coded to a valid but incorrect G/L account 

— meaning the expense or revenue was recorded in the wrong category. The goal is to move it to 

the right account without changing the total amount or vendor record. 

Typical examples of reclassification include: 

• 
Reclassify a Utilities Expense to Repairs & Maintenance when the charge was for equipment 

servicing rather than usage. 

• 
Reclassify Rental income to Other income for non-rent charges such as late fees. 

• 
Reclassify Security Deposits Payable to Tenant Refunds Payable when the deposit was 

returned. 

What You Can Reclassify 

You can reclassify A/R and A/P invoices and adjustments. 

• 
Reclassifying an A/R invoice enables you to change how revenues are assigned for an 

invoice that was paid or partially paid.  

• 
Reclassifying an A/P invoice enables you to change how expenses are assigned for an A/P 

invoice that was paid or partially paid.  

For example, when you reclassify an A/P invoice, you could assign line items to different G/L 

accounts, or change the department, location, or other dimensions..  

When to Reclassify 

Consider reclassifying a transaction:  

• 
When the transaction is initially recorded in the wrong account. 

• 
When there’s a change in the accounting period. 

• 
When adjustments are needed to reflect the proper allocation of revenue or expenses. This 

ensures that financial statements accurately represent the company’s financial position and 

comply with accounting standards.  

Who Can Reclassify 

Only users who have special permission can reclassify invoices. They can edit accounting 

information on both partially and fully paid invoices. You can update almost anything on the A/P 

invoice except for the amount and the payment date. For example, if the A/P invoice was assigned 

to the wrong department, you can choose a different department from the drop-down menu. 

Accessing the Reclassify Function 

In the Financial Suite, you can reclassify a single invoice or adjustment, or you can reclassify 

several invoices or adjustments at the same time 

---


<!-- Page 17 -->
Chapter 1: Periodic Tasks Overview 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Periodic Tasks User Guide 

You can reclassify a single invoice or adjustment from the A/R Invoices or A/P invoices lists. Edit 

the invoice that you want to reclassify and click the Reclassify button. See Reclassifying an 

Invoice. 

You can reclassify multiple transactions at the same time using the Invoice Reclassification menu 

option. See Reclassifying Multiple Invoices (on page 19). 

Things to Keep in Mind When Reclassifying Transactions 

• 
Do not change the transaction total or vendor. 

• 
Always add a memo that explains why you reclassified the transaction. 

---



### Invoice Reclassification Page
*Source: `RP Accounting AP Periodic Tasks User Guide.pdf`, Page 18*



#### Before You Begin
*Source: `RP Accounting AP Periodic Tasks User Guide.pdf`, Page 18*

Periodic Tasks Overview 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Periodic Tasks User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Invoice Reclassification Page 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > All > Periodic Tasks > Month End > Invoice 
Reclassification`


Use this page to reclassify several invoices at the same time. 

This page has two sections: 

• 
Filters section: Use the upper section to find the invoices that you want to work on by 

applying filters. 

• 
Reclass operations section: Use the lower section to select the invoices that you want to 

reclassify and then either reclass the selected invoices or create reclass journal entries for 

them. 

The list of invoices is presented in a workbench. You can use the workbench controls to show and 

hide columns, sort the list based on the values in a column, and much more.  

Before You Begin 

Access can vary depending on your organization’s subscriptions and your permissions. If you do 

not see the option in the menu, then ask your System Administrator to check your permissions. 

Permissions 

These permissions are required to reclassify multiple transactions at the same time:  

Application 
Activities 
Permissions 

Accounts Payable 
Invoice reclassification 
Run 

If your user account doesn’t have the permissions shown above, then ask your System 

Administrator for assistance. If you have administrator privileges, you can assign permissions for a 

new feature to a user or to a role. See Roles and Permissions for a description of how to review a 

user’s permissions.
