#### Reclassifying Multiple Invoices
*Source: `RP Accounting AP Periodic Tasks User Guide.pdf`, Page 19*

Chapter 1: Periodic Tasks Overview 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Periodic Tasks User Guide 

Reclassifying Multiple Invoices 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > All > Periodic Tasks > Month End > Invoice 
Reclassification`


Things to Keep in Mind When Reclassifying Transactions 

• 
Do not change the transaction total or vendor. 

• 
Always add a memo that explains why you reclassified the transaction. 

Before You Begin 

• 
Make sure that the books for the affected periods are open. 

Opening the Page 

To reclassify multiple invoices at the same time: 

1. 
Open the Accounts Payable menu. 

2. 
In the Month End section of the Periodic Tasks section of the menu, select Invoice 

reclassification.  

Retrieving the Invoices 

1. 
Set up the filters that you need to retrieve the invoices to work on. You can set up as many 

filters as you need. You can filter by any of the following: 

• 
Start date/End date: Select the start and end date to retrieve invoices within  those 

dates 

• 
Property/Property group: Find invoices for a specific property or property group.  

• 
From account/To account: Find invoices that are assigned within an account range.  

• 
Account group: Find invoices with a specific account group 

• 
Vendor: Find invoices from a specific vendor. Vendors starting with TEMP or REIM are 

not eligible for reclassification. 

• 
Status: Find invoices with a specific status: Posted, Paid, or Partially paid. 

2. 
Click the Apply button to apply the filters and retrieve the invoices. 

Reclassifying the Invoices 

1. 
Select the check boxes of the invoices that you want to reclassify. 

---


<!-- Page 20 -->
Periodic Tasks Overview 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Periodic Tasks User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

2. 
Select the Reclass Invoice option to reclass the invoice only,  

or  

select the Create Reclass Journal Entry option and then specify the date in the Reclass date 

field to have the system generate one journal entry per invoice line. 

3. 
In the Set Reclass to G/L Account for all drop-down list, select the G/L account to reclassify 

the invoices. The system fills in the Reclass to GL Account column on each line in the list 

with the selected account. 

4. 
In the Memo/Reclass Description field, type a note about why you are reclassifying the 

selected invoices. 

5. 
Click the Update button. The system fills in the Reclass to G/L account and Memo columns 

in the list.  

6. 
Click the Reclass button to reclass the selected invoices. 

The system displays a confirmation message that the invoices are being processed offline.

### A/P Summaries Overview
*Source: `RP Accounting AP Periodic Tasks User Guide.pdf`, Page 26*

A/P Subledger 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Periodic Tasks User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

A/P Summaries Overview 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > All > Subledger > Subledger Summaries`


Summaries are collections of the same type of transactions, grouped together for processing. 

Until you or the system creates a new summary, no line items appear in the Summaries list. 

Summaries can be either opened or closed. When summaries are open in Accounts Payable, you 

can add and pay A/P invoices. In designing an accounts payable process, the system administrator 

can give access to the pages involved with managing A/P invoices, but not opening or closing 

summaries. You can reopen closed summaries as needed. 

Closing or opening a single summary doesn’t automatically close or open related summaries in 
the subledger period. To open or close related summaries, go to the Open or Close AP Subledger 
pages respectively. 

Summaries for A/P invoices are created in two ways: 

1. 
Automatically, by RealPage at intervals you select 

2. 
Manually, by specific summaries you create and name to handle special situations 

Automatically created summaries: The system can automatically create summaries so that a 

summary always exists for A/P invoices and other payments as they are entered throughout the 

day. Automatic summaries are created according to time intervals chosen by the administrator. 

Set the frequency of automatic summary creation in the Configure Accounts Payable page: 

1. 
Open the Company menu, and then select the Setup tab. 

2. 
Select Subscriptions. 

3. 
In the Subscriptions page, click Accounts Payable, then select Configure. The Configure 

Accounts Payable page appears. 

The system standardizes the date format for all automatically -created summaries on the 
internationally accepted format of YYYY -MM-DD24:MI:SS. Standardizing the date 
format in the summary title ensures transactions are always grouped or matched to the 
appropriate summary, and eliminates the risk of posting errors due to a date format 
mismatch. 

Manually created summaries: A manual summary is useful when you need a special summary for 

specific A/P invoices. You can use whatever date format your company prefers when you enter a 

summary manually. 

In Multi-Entity, Multi-Currency Companies 

If your company is a multi-entity, multi-currency company, the system recommends you set the 

system to automatically create summaries, so the system creates consistent summaries with the

Subledger Summaries 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > All > Subledger > Subledger Summaries`


Use the Summaries list to view a list of all manual and automatically created summaries in the 

Accounts Payable application, which includes summaries for A/P invoices, adjustments, and 

manual payments. You can sort and filter this list to see only the summaries you want. 

From this list, you can: 

• 
Add a new manual summary. 

• 
View a summary’s details. 

• 
Edit a summary’s details. 

• 
Delete a summary. 

• 
View the list of transactions in a summary. Click the link in the Summary name column to 

open the summary’s list of transactions. 

• 
Export the list of summaries. 

Use the list controls to create custom views and filter and sort the list. See Managing the List for 

details.

#### Adding an A/P Summary
*Source: `RP Accounting AP Periodic Tasks User Guide.pdf`, Page 30*

A/P Subledger 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Periodic Tasks User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Adding an A/P Summary 

This procedure refers to adding a summary, not adding items to the summary. 

To add an A/P summary: 

1. 
Open the Accounts payable menu. 

2. 
In the Periodic tasks/Month end section, select Subledger, and then select Subledger 

summaries. 

3. 
In the Summaries list, click Add. The system displays the Summary Information page. 

We recommend that you set up automatic summaries (daily or monthly) by going to 


> **Navigation Path:** `Company > Subscriptions, click Accounts payable, and then click Configure. The summary 
date is the date the General Ledger uses to post all transactions within that summary. 
Therefore, it is important that you do not combine transactions from different time 
periods within the same summary. Also, note that summaries are posted automatically to 
the G/L when transactions within those summaries are saved.`


4. 
In the Summary title field, type a name for the summary. The system uses this name to 

identify the summary throughout the Accounts payable application. 

5. 
In the G/L Posting date field, type the date or select the 
 Calendar button and click the 

date you want the items in this summary to post to the general ledger. The system 

completes the field with the current date, but you can change it. 

6. 
Leave the Status set to Active. 

7. 
Under Summary type, select the type of items you want this summary to contain: 

• 
A/P Invoice 

• 
Adjustment 

• 
Manual payment 

8. 
Click Save. The Summaries list opens. 

The summary you created is a manual summary even if the auto-summary feature is on. 

What’s Next? 

Click a summary name to add items to it for summary processing. For example, after adding a 

summary called Adjustment summary, click Adjustments summary to add adjustments.

Adding Items to a Summary 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > All > Subledger > Subledger Summaries`


To add an item to a summary: 

1. 
Open the Accounts payable menu. 

2. 
Pause on the Subledger option, and then select Subledger summaries. The Summaries list 

opens. 

3. 
Find the summary to which you want to add a transaction.  

Make sure that the transaction type of the summary matches the transaction type that 
you want to add. 

4. 
Click the summary name. The system opens the summary’s list of transactions.  

5.

Deleting a Summary 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > All > Subledger > Subledger Summaries`


Before you can delete a summary, make sure its status is open, and it does not contain any 

transactions. See Opening an AP summary (on page 41) and Viewing A/P summary content (on

1. 
Open the Accounts payable menu. 

2. 
Pause on the Subledger option, and then select Subledger summaries. The Summaries list 

opens. 

3. 
In the Summaries list, find the summary that you want to delete, and, at the end of the line, 

click Delete. The system displays a delete confirmation page. 

4. 
Click OK.

Click the Import button.

Closing the A/P Subledger 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > Subledger > Close Subledger`


From the Close AP Subledger page, you can close an open summary either by period or by 

summary name. Closed summaries can later be reopened. Summaries of manual payments are 

automatically closed. 

Closing a single summary doesn’t automatically close related summaries in the subledger period. 

To close related summaries, go to the Close A/P Subledger page. 

The system now alerts you about unconfirmed payments, A/P invoices on hold, and unconfirmed 
adjustments before you close the Accounts payable subledgers so that you can take necessary 
action on these items.

After you close a summary, you cannot post transactions to it until you reopen it. This 

prevents you from posting transactions to the wrong period. (The system uses the summary 

date as the posting date for almost all transactions.)

### Warning of Transactions Preventing the A/P Summary from Closing
*Source: `RP Accounting AP Periodic Tasks User Guide.pdf`, Page 39*

Chapter 2: A/P Subledger 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Periodic Tasks User Guide 

Warning of Transactions Preventing the A/P Summary from 
Closing 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > All > Periodic Tasks > Month End > Subledger > 
Close Subledger`


When you close an A/P subledger and the account has open items such as unconfirmed 

payments, A/P invoices on hold, and unconfirmed adjustments, the system displays a warning 

message. The warning message allows you to look at the outstanding A/P invoices and take 

appropriate action before closing the A/P subledger. This warning helps reduce the time spent in 

the closing process. 

Use the links in the warning message to access the A/P invoices that are presenting the 
problems. 

• 
Click the link to open the transaction or a list of transactions with issues that need to be 

resolved.  

• 
Open each transaction and resolve the issue: confirm or approve payments, confirm 

adjustments, resolve issues with A/P invoices that are on hold.

If you have a custom-named period, then you can use the first letter of your custom period 

to move to it.

### Fees Overview
*Source: `RP Accounting AP Periodic Tasks User Guide.pdf`, Page 46*

Fees 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Periodic Tasks User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Fees Overview 

You can charge a fee based on a percentage of the total cost, on the total number of units, or the 

number of occupied units. You can also invoice all tenants a flat fee. 

Use the Fees feature to set up management fees, calculate the fees, generate, and post A/P 

invoices. You can either calculate and invoice fees manually or schedule the fees to have the 

system generate A/P invoices automatically. You can also have the system create A/R invoices, if 

needed. Once the system has calculated a fee, you can recalculate the fee and create an A/P 

invoice for the adjustment (true-up). 

The parent property management company typically imposes a management fee on its locations 

for management services that might include advertising rental properties, compliance with laws, 

and property maintenance. 

Corporate offices may use this feature to invoice locations for management fees. Use this feature 

to: 

• 
Calculate management fees 

• 
Generate the A/P invoices for each location that a corporate office (or an external 

management company) manages 

• 
Have the system generate an A/R invoice (optional) 

• 
Delete or unpost a fee 

• 
Reverse an A/P invoice for a fee  

Fees can be unposted up until the fee is paid. 

In the image, notice that the parent entity has a vendor record associated with it. This is the 

mechanism by which the parent entity invoices its locations for the management fee. It acts as a 

vendor to its locations. The parent entity also has a customer record (not required by this feature) 

which is the mechanism through which the entity can pay for goods or services rendered by one 

of its locations. 

---


<!-- Page 47 -->
Chapter 3: Fees 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Periodic Tasks User Guide 

The fee record establishes a payment relationship between an entity and one or more locations. 

In the fee record, you define the vendor (the provider of the service, which is the parent entity) 

and which locations benefited from the management service. In this example, locations 1, 2, and 3 

are invoiced management fees.  

You can also choose to have the system generate an A/R invoice. If you choose to do this, the 

vendor and the A/R location must be the same entity. 

A fee definition primarily includes: 

• 
The vendor that provides the management service. (Select the vendor record associated 

with the corporate office.) 

• 
The location or location group* benefiting from the service. When a fee specifies a location 

group, the system calculates a fee for each location in the group. It also generates a 

separate A/P invoice and (if A/R is enabled) an A/R invoice for each location. 

• 
The type of fee which determines how the fee is calculated; set up a fee based on 

percentages, units (occupied units or total units) or a flat fee.  

The outcome of the fees feature can either be a journal entry for the fee, or an A/P invoice. 

Optionally, the system can generate an A/R invoice as well.  

Manual Versus Scheduled Fees 

You can manually generate A/P invoices for fees, or you can set up a billing schedule to have the 

RealPage Accounting system automatically generate A/P invoices. 

---



### Types of Fees
*Source: `RP Accounting AP Periodic Tasks User Guide.pdf`, Page 48*

Fees 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Periodic Tasks User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Types of Fees 

Property management companies charge fees for services that may include a setup fee, 

management fees, leasing fees, and maintenance fees. 

Setup fees are one-time fees that companies charge to set up a new account. Setup fees can 

include the cost of property handouts or inspection services that establish the condition of the 

property.  

Management fees are recurring fees that a customer pays each month. This fee covers the cost of 

managing rent payments and daily tasks associated with managing the property. Management 

fees are typically based on a percentage of the rent but can also be a flat fee. 

The system offers three types of fees: 

• 
Flat fees 

• 
Percentage fees (percentage of income and expense) 

• 
Unit-based fees 

Flat Fee 

The Flat fee allows you to charge a standard unchanging amount. For example, use the flat fee 

type when your company charges a flat management fee.  

Percentage Fees 

Use the Percentage fee type to charge a percentage of a total cost. For example, use the 

percentage fee type to charge a percentage-based management fee.  

When defining a percentage fee, you can also spread a cost across multiple accounts. When you 

set up a percentage fee, the system allows you to define a minimum and maximum amount to 

charge. 

Unit-based Fees 

Use Unit-based fees when you need to divide a flat fee evenly across a specific number of units. 

• 
Total units: Charge the same fee to all units. 

• 
Occupied units: Charge a fee calculated on the total number of units. For example, if the 

waste management vendor charges your property $1,000.00 for weekly pickup, you can 

spread the charge across multiple units using Occupied units. 

If Key Performance Indicators (KPI) are set up to retrieve occupied units ’ data from pulling 
Leasing & Rents, the system populates Occupied units in RealPage Accounting from the 
KPI data. 

Automatic entries may be generated as a general ledger journal entry or as an Accounts payable 

A/P invoice.

### Recalculating Fees
*Source: `RP Accounting AP Periodic Tasks User Guide.pdf`, Page 71*



#### When to Recalculate Fees
*Source: `RP Accounting AP Periodic Tasks User Guide.pdf`, Page 71*

Chapter 3: Fees 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Periodic Tasks User Guide 

Recalculating Fees 

This section describes how and when to recalculate fees. 

• 
When to Recalculate Fees (on page 71) 

• 
Recalculating Fees (on page 72) 

• 
Rerunning a Posted Fee (on page 73) 

• 
Viewing the Numbers that Support a Fee Calculation (on page 74) 

• 
Calculate Fees Box (on page 77) 

• 
Calculate Fees, Post Fee (on page 78) 

• 
Posting a Fee from the Calculate Fees Box (on page 79) 

• 
Unposting a Posted Fee (on page 79) 

• 
Calculate Fees, Calculation Report (on page 83) 

• 
Calculate Fees, True-Up (on page 85) 

When to Recalculate Fees 

When calculating a fee for the first time, the system displays the current activity and the charged 

amount. Each subsequent time the fees are calculated, the system overrides the previous 

calculation if it is not paid or posted. If you need to pay the fee in the same month that it was 

incurred, pay the first calculation. 

Occupied units cannot be recalculated in bulk. 

After the system calculates a fee, you can recalculate it at any time. For example, you may want to 

recalculate a fee to true-up the amount that was billed at the beginning of a month.  

Some companies recalculate continuously to pick up changes, Other companies recalculate on a 

quarterly or even on an annual basis to true-up the records. 

Companies recalculate fees in the same month to pick up variances from the time the fees were 

originally calculated. 

Some recalculate the prior month’s fees to pick up any adjustments from the prior period so that 

the system is up to date. This is called a true-up.

Exporting Lists 

You can export most lists to several available file formats and then import the data into an 

external application, such as Microsoft Word or Microsoft Excel. 

Although you can export up to 25,000 rows, if you want to save time and effort, we recommend 

that you filter your list to pinpoint only the information you need to export by creating a custom 

view. That way, when you export the list, you’ll have a spreadsheet tailored to the information you 

need. You can export any view of this list for use on your local computer. 

Use column filters, advanced filters, and views to filter the data. For instructions, refer to 

Managing Lists. 

If you have a sorted and filtered list that you use consistently, you can create and save it as a 

custom report for convenience. With a custom report, you need to set the filtering and 

parameters only once to enable you to generate the report as needed after that. 

1. 
Click the Export button. 

2. 
Select the format to which you want to export the list. 

• 
CSV: Select this format if you plan to move the data from one program to another. 

You can use files that you save in CSV format with any spreadsheet program. 

• 
Word: When you select this option, the system exports the list in Word format. If a list 

of conversion formats displays, select HTML document. 

• 
Excel: When you select this option, the system exports the list in XLS format. If you see 

an error message about file type and extension type incompatibility, you can disregard 

the message and select Yes. 

• 
PDF: Select this option if you plan to print or share the list. When you select this 

option, the system exports the list and tries to open the file in the browser. If 

prompted, select Yes to allow the PDF to open. 

• 
CSV for import: Select this option if you want to export data, change it, or add to it, 

and then import it into the system again. 

Some lists in RealPage Accounting do not have the CSV for import option.

Calculate Fees, True-Up 

Fees > Details List > Details 

In accounting, a true-up is the process of reconciling estimated or provisional financial figures 

with actual, final amounts. A true-up is an adjustment made to ensure that financial records 

accurately reflect reality. 

• 
True-ups correct discrepancies between what was projected and what actually occurred. 

• 
True-ups help meet accounting standards like GAAP by aligning records with the matching 

principle. 

• 
True-ups are often done at the end of a financial period when actual data becomes 

available.  

Use the Calculate Fees, True Up page to: 

• 
Recalculate the fee 

• 
Unpost the fee 

• 
Post the recalculation 

• 
View the General Ledger report for a G/L account or for the location

a) 
Click to open the General ledger report for the location.

Click to open the General ledger report for one of the fees.

### Types of Fees
*Source: `RP Accounting AP Periodic Tasks User Guide.pdf`, Page 91*

Chapter 3: Fees 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Periodic Tasks User Guide 

Types of Fees 

Property management companies charge fees for services that may include a setup fee, 

management fees, leasing fees, and maintenance fees. 

Setup fees are one-time fees that companies charge to set up a new account. Setup fees can 

include the cost of property handouts or inspection services that establish the condition of the 

property.  

Management fees are recurring fees that a customer pays each month. This fee covers the cost of 

managing rent payments and daily tasks associated with managing the property. Management 

fees are typically based on a percentage of the rent but can also be a flat fee. 

The system offers three types of fees: 

• 
Flat fees 

• 
Percentage fees (percentage of income and expense) 

• 
Unit-based fees 

Flat Fee 

The Flat fee allows you to charge a standard unchanging amount. For example, use the flat fee 

type when your company charges a flat management fee.  

Percentage Fees 

Use the Percentage fee type to charge a percentage of a total cost. For example, use the 

percentage fee type to charge a percentage-based management fee.  

When defining a percentage fee, you can also spread a cost across multiple accounts. When you 

set up a percentage fee, the system allows you to define a minimum and maximum amount to 

charge. 

Unit-based Fees 

Use Unit-based fees when you need to divide a flat fee evenly across a specific number of units. 

• 
Total units: Charge the same fee to all units. 

• 
Occupied units: Charge a fee calculated on the total number of units. For example, if the 

waste management vendor charges your property $1,000.00 for weekly pickup, you can 

spread the charge across multiple units using Occupied units. 

If Key Performance Indicators (KPI) are set up to retrieve occupied units ’ data from pulling 
Leasing & Rents, the system populates Occupied units in RealPage Accounting from the 
KPI data. 

Automatic entries may be generated as a general ledger journal entry or as an Accounts payable 

A/P invoice.

Calculating and Posting Flat Fees 

To calculate* and post a flat fee: 

1. 
Open the Accounts payable menu. 

2. 
Select the Management fee workbench option in the Periodic tasks section. 

3. 
In the Fee type drop-down list, select Flat. 

4. 
In the Calculated from and Calculated to drop-down lists, select the month/year 

combination to define the dates for which you are billing the fee. 

5. 
Click the Apply button. The list of flat fees active for that time appear in the list. 

6. 
Find the flat fees that you want to work with, and then select the check box in the leftmost 

column, selecting the rows in the list with a Calculated or blank Calculated status. 

7. 
Type or select the Posting date. The Posting date is required.  

The Invoice date is optional. 

8. 
Click the Calculate button. The status changes to Calculated. 

9. 
Check the Last posted month column. You should post the next available period. 

10. 
Select only the fees that have a Calculated status, and then click the Post button.  

After the system posts the fees, the list updates to show that fees have been posted. When 

fee posting fails, the system displays a View error link. Click the View error link to review the 

error details. 

* You might assume that flat fees do not need to be calculated because you bill them one month 
at a time. However, fees must have a Calculated status in order to be posted, so the calculation 
step is a necessary one. In addition, when the time frame spans multiple months, then the 
system does calculate flat fees.

#### Reverse Link Does Not Appear
*Source: `RP Accounting AP Periodic Tasks User Guide.pdf`, Page 100*

Fees 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Periodic Tasks User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Reverse Link Does Not Appear 

If you don’t see a reverse link for a transaction, it may be for reasons such as: 

• 
Your application doesn’t support reversals. 

• 
Your user permissions are not enabled for reversals. 

• 
You are trying to reverse a transaction that can’t be reversed.  

Check the following: 

• 
User permissions–Check to make sure that you have the proper user permissions. Check 

your user permissions to be sure that you are allowed to reverse this type of transaction. If 

you are still not sure, contact your administrator. 

• 
The transaction was already reversed–Check if the transaction has already been reversed. 

You can quickly check the state of the transaction by viewing it. 

• 
Transaction type–Check if you are trying to reverse a transaction type that cannot be 

reversed. The following are transactions that can be reversed. If you don’t see your 

transaction type in this list, it can’t be reversed. 

• 
Accounts Payable: A/P invoices, adjustments 

• 
Accounts Receivable: A/R invoices, adjustments, posted payments, advances 

• 
Cash Management: Charge card transactions (not related to A/P invoice payments), 

charge payoffs, fund transfers 

• 
General Ledger: Journal entries. 

Reversing a journal entry is a little different from reversing other kinds of 
transaction types. 

• 
Subledger period is closed–The period has to be open for the reversal transaction. If the 

period in which the transaction was created is closed, you can: 

• 
Open the closed period to reverse the transaction with the original date. 

• 
Reverse the transaction in the current open period. 

• 
Paid transaction–The transaction must be partially or fully paid, unless you specifically 

configured your application for reversal of unpaid transactions, such as invoices, expenses, 

or adjustments. 

• 
FYI: If the transaction state is: 

• 
Selected: Remove it from the selected state, and then reverse the transaction. 

• 
Partially paid or Paid, Reverse the payment first, and then reverse the transaction.

### About Recurring Transactions
*Source: `RP Accounting AP Periodic Tasks User Guide.pdf`, Page 108*



#### Before You Begin
*Source: `RP Accounting AP Periodic Tasks User Guide.pdf`, Page 108*

Recurring A/P Invoices 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Periodic Tasks User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

About Recurring Transactions 

If you pay the same A/P invoice on a regular basis—such as a monthly rent A/P invoice for 

$5000—you can save time by having the system automatically enter the A/P invoice for you. 

Recurring A/P invoices work best for situations such as rent, services, or subscriptions, where you 

pay the same amount to a vendor on a regular schedule. Use the Recurring A/P invoice page to 

automate the billing process. 

The system respects non-standard recurring transaction schedules and automatically enters and 

posts A/P invoices on the schedule you define. The transaction and G/L posting date for an 

automatically generated A/P invoice are the same, but you can change either. 

Management fees are also billed through recurring invoices. Learn about the Management Fees 

Workbench and Fees (on page 45). 

Before You Begin 

Access can vary depending on your organization’s subscriptions and your permissions. If you do 

not see the option in the menu, then ask your System Administrator to check your permissions. 

Permissions 

These permissions are required to work with recurring A/P invoices: 

Application 
Activities/Lists 
Permissions 

Accounts Payable 
Recurring A/P invoices 
List, View, Add, Delete 

If your user account doesn’t have the permissions shown above, then ask your System 

Administrator for assistance. If you have administrator privileges, you can assign permissions for a 

new feature to a user or to a role. See Roles and Permissions for a description of how to review a 

user’s permissions.

Use the Recurring A/P invoices list to view a list of all vendors for whom you have defined 

recurring A/P invoices. From this list, you can start the process of adding or editing the 

characteristics of the A/P invoices the system automatically enters for you on a recurring basis. In 

addition, you can turn off or delete a recurring A/P invoice so that no more A/P invoices are 

created. 

For multi-entity shared companies with multiple base currencies: You can create recurring A/P 
invoices only at the entity level. 

Use the Recurring A/P invoices list to: 

• 
Add a new recurring A/P invoice. 

• 
View a recurring A/P invoice’s details. 

• 
Edit a recurring A/P invoice’s details. 

• 
Turn off the schedule of a recurring A/P invoice. 

• 
View successful transactions created by a recurring A/P invoice. 

• 
View the error log of a failed recurring A/P invoice. 

• 
Import recurring A/P invoices. 

• 
Export the list of recurring A/P invoices. 

Use the list controls to create custom views and filter and sort the list. See Managing the List for 

details. 

The items you can see on this page vary slightly depending on whether your company is an 
enterprise, or a multi-entity shared company. If your company is a multi-entity shared company 
at the top level, you initially see only the items that were created at the top level. To see items 
created in the entities, select the Include private check box. Also, when you edit an item that was 
created in an entity, your changes apply to that entity. After you save your changes, you are 
returned to the top level.

1. 
Open the Accounts Payable menu.

Enter information that describes the recurring A/P invoice. 

1. 
Select the Vendor associated with this recurring invoice. You can also click the Add link in 

the drop-down list to create a new vendor.  

2. 
In the Pay to drop-down list, select the vendor’s contact to use for payments.  

3. 
In the Return to drop-down list, select the contact for return correspondence. 

4. 
In the A/P invoice sequence number field, select the numbering sequence to use for this 

series of invoices. You can also select the Add link in the drop-down list to create a new 

document sequence number. You can use the number to search, sort, and report on A/P 

invoices. 

If your A/P preferences require A/P invoice numbers, then you must fill in the 
A/P invoice 

sequence number. 

5. 
In the Reference number field, type the unique number associated with the invoice. For 

example, this can be a number that the vendor assigned to the invoice. You can use the 

reference number to search, sort, and report on A/P invoices. 

6. 
If this recurring A/P invoice is part of an ongoing contract, type a description of the contract 

in the Contract description field.  

7. 
Type the purpose of the recurring invoice in the Description field. 

8. 
If this recurring A/P invoice is part of an ongoing contract, type the contract ID in the 

Contract ID field.

Adding a Recurring A/P Invoice Based on an Existing Invoice 

To use an existing A/P invoice as the basis for a recurring A/P invoice: 

1. 
Open the Accounts payable menu. 

2. 
In the Search & Find section, select A/P invoices.  

3. 
Find the A/P invoice you want to use as the basis for a recurring A/P invoice, and then click 

Edit. 

4. 
Click the More Actions button, and then select Create recurring transaction. 

5. 
If the Leave site? message appears, click Leave. The Recurring invoice page opens. 

Filling In the A/P Invoice Details 

1. 
Enter details about the A/P invoice. Required fields include: 

• 
Vendor: Choose the vendor you’re paying. 

• 
A/P invoice sequence number: If your Accounts Payable preferences have been set up 

to require A/P invoice numbers, choose a numbering sequence that the system can 

use to automatically generate invoice numbers for recurring A/P invoices. 

• 
Term: Choose the A/P terms that the vendor extends to you. If you chose a default A/P 

term on the vendor’s record, this will be completed by the system. You can also add a 

new A/P term. 

• 
Line item details: For each line item on the A/P invoice, select the G/L account and 

enter the amount. You may also want to pick the department, location, and segment 

or specify other dimensional information. 

2. 
Add or edit any other information as needed, just as you would for a regular A/P invoice. 

Information such as the reference number, description, or contract ID can be used for 

searching and reporting on the A/P invoice later on. 

3. 
(Optional) If you need to specify different Ship To or Return To information for the vendor, 

you can do so on the Additional Information tab. 

4. 
The Vendor and Term on the Additional Information and Schedule tabs are for reference 

only. You can edit them only from the A/P invoice tab. 

5. 
On the Schedule tab, indicate when the first A/P invoice should be created, how often it 

should be repeated, and when it should expire. 

Start date: When the first A/P invoice should be created. 

Ending on: To keep the A/P invoice running perpetually, select “Never.” Otherwise, select a 

fixed number of A/P invoices to be created or a specific date when the recurring A/P invoice 

should expire.

Editing a Recurring A/P Invoice 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > All > Recurring > Edit`


You can edit a recurring A/P invoice any time until the last scheduled recurrence of the 

transaction. Your changes will apply only to future transactions, and will not affect 

previously-created A/P invoices. 

1. 
Open the Accounts payable menu. 

2. 
Select Recurring. 

3. 
Locate the desired A/P invoice, and click the Edit link. 

If you try to edit a recurring A/P invoice with locations to which your user account does not 
have access, an error message appears. 

4. 
Make your changes. 

5. 
On the Schedule tab, set the Next Execution Date to the date you want the system to 

create the next A/P invoice. 

Setting the Next Execution Date can prevent an inadvertent extra recurrence of the 

transaction. 

For example, if an A/P invoice is created on May 12 and on May 13 you change the 

recurring A/P invoice to run on the 16th of the month, you would set the next execution 

date to June 16 to avoid double payments in May. 

6. 
Click the Save button.

*Source: `RP Accounting AP Periodic Tasks User Guide.pdf`, Page 119*



#### Turning a Recurring Schedule On or Off
*Source: `RP Accounting AP Periodic Tasks User Guide.pdf`, Page 119*

Chapter 4: Recurring A/P Invoices 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Periodic Tasks User Guide 

Deleting a Recurring A/P Invoice 

If there is no chance that you’ll use a recurring A/P invoice any more, you can delete it instead of 

turning off the recurring schedule. For example, if a vendor contract has been permanently 

canceled, then you can delete the recurring A/P invoice that was set up for the vendor. The 

system removes the recurring A/P invoice from the Recurring A/P invoices list and creates no 

more A/P invoices. 

To delete a record: 

1. 
Open the Accounts payable menu. 

2. 
Select Recurring. The Recurring A/P invoices list opens. 

3. 
Find the record you want to remove. 

4. 
Select the check box at the end of the row, and click Delete. A delete confirmation page 

appears. 

Turning a Recurring Schedule On or Off 

You can activate or deactivate a recurring A/P invoice schedule as needed. For example, if a 

contract is put on hold, you can turn off a schedule to temporarily stop the system from 

automatically creating A/P invoices. When you are ready to restart the recurring schedule, you can 

turn the schedule back on. 

To activate or deactivate a schedule: 

1. 
Open the Accounts payable menu. 

2. 
Select Recurring. The Recurring A/P invoices list opens. 

3. 
Locate the row associated with the schedule, and click an option: 

• 
Turn on to activate the schedule. 

• 
Turn off to deactivate the schedule. 

When you turn off a schedule and then turn it on again at a later date, the system resumes the 
recurrence schedule from the turn-off point. If periods were closed in the meantime, the system 
generates an error message as it tries to create recurrences in each of those closed periods. As 
soon as it reaches an open period, the system generates those recurrences to the turn -on date. 
If you want to turn on the schedule and have the system generate recurrences from a later date, 
edit the Next execution date in the recurring schedule.

The frequency with which the A/P invoice recurs. You can select None,

be recurring, but you now only want it to run once. For instance, you 

may be trying out a new service on a 30-day trial. After the trial, you can 

change the schedule or delete the recurring A/P invoice. 

If you have set an A/P invoice to pay in months, you have the option of 

having the A/P invoice generate at End of the Month regardless of the 

start date. Otherwise, the A/P invoice will generate on the same day of 

the month as the start date.

Use the Print payment copies page to print copies of payments made with checks. You can print 

copies of payments that you issued out of Accounts Payable or Cash Management. For checks, 

the system prints non-negotiable copies of the original check.  

The Print payment copies page also lets you send payment notification emails. Learn more about 

notifying vendors that they’ve been paid. 

Workflow 

Printing checks is a multi-part process, much like running a report: 

1. 
Set up parameters so that the system retrieves the records you want to print. Specify the 

coverage period, set filters, select the check range, and how to sort, and select desired 

payment notifications. 

2. 
Click View to retrieve the records you want to print. 

3. 
Select the records for which you want to print checks, and then click Print/Email. 

Before You Begin

not see the option in the menu, then ask your System Administrator to check your permissions.

Printing Payment Copies 

Printing payment copies is a two-part process similar to running a report. Set up filters for the 

system to find the group of payments you want, and then select the items to print. 

Open the Print Payment Copies page from either Accounts Payable or Cash Management. 

To print payment copies: 

1. 
Open the Accounts payable menu. 

2. 
Select Print payment copies. 

To quickly see all payments sorted by check, in the Print payment copies page, click View. 
To refine the list of payment copies to print, click Customize to return to the Print 

Payment Copies filters page and follow the steps in Customizing and printing payment 

copies below. 
Copies of the check contain the same information as the original check. If any information 
changed since the check was paid originally (for example, if the contact name or address 
has changed), the copies will not reflect those changes.

Setting Print Filters 

Use the filters to focus the results of your print job. In effect, filters enable you to isolate and 

assemble just the data you want. You can set any combination of filters. 

To customize your results, change the filters as follows: 

1. 
To select the types of payments to include in your print job, click the Payment method 

drop-down list, and then click the payment type to include (check, credit card, record 

transfer, cash, or electronic payment). 

2. 
If you selected Check for your payment type, select how many Checks per page you want to 

print by clicking the drop-down list. To print one check per page and include a check and 

vendor stub, select One. To use the entire paper space to print three checks per page 

(without check or vendor stubs) select Three. 

3. 
To select a particular checking account, click the Checking account drop-down list, and then 

click the account you want to include. 


> **Navigation Path:** `Administrators can preset a default financial institution in Cash Management 
configuration (Cash Management > All > Setup > Configuration). For multi-entity shared 
companies, you can set a default bank account on an entity-by-entity basis.`


4. 
To show results for a specific vendor or range of vendors, use the Vendor from and Vendor 

to drop-down lists. 

5. 
To show results for a specific check or range of checks, use the From check and To check 

drop-down lists. 

6. 
To show voided checks, select the Include voided checks check box. 

7. 
To use the printed copies as remittance information for your vendors, then omit the 

watermark by clearing the Include File Copy Watermark check box. To use the printed 

copies as true internal file copies, then leave the check box selected. 

• 
This applies to any payment information that’s not part of a check stub. The stubs that 

accompany checks will always retain the File Copy watermark. 

The following filter options display only if you work in a multi-currency and multi-entity 

environment: 

• 
To filter the report by entity or entity group, select the entity or entity group from the 

Entity/Entity group drop-down list.  

You must select an entity if you want to run this report at the top level. The system 
uses the entity you specify to determine the appropriate currency. 

• 
Select the Show entity level checks check box to see the checks paid by the top-level 

company as well as the selected entity.

Sorting Payments 

Use the filters in the Check Range/Sorting section to control the sort order and the number of 

records to display per page. By default, the system sorts payments by date. You can sort by one or 

more of the items in the Sort By boxes. 

1. 
In the Check range/sorting section, in the Sort by, click the Select link to open the Selection 

box. See Using the Selection Box for instructions. 

• 
Click 
 Add to add an item to the Selected items list.  

• 
Remove an item by clicking the item in the box on the right, and then clicking the left 

arrow to move it back to the box on its left. 

• 
The system sorts the checks according to the order of the items in the Selected items 

column on the right. 

• 
To change the sort order of an item, select 
 Drag, and then drag the item to the 

desired sort order.  

2. 
To change the number of checks displayed on a page, in Max rows, select 50, 100, or 200. 

Sending Payment Notification Emails 

The system gives you the option to notify vendors and employees that they’ve been paid. Email 

notifications are available for vendor payments processed through Accounts Payable. 

For checks that you’ve already printed, you have the option to send payment notification emails 

from the Print payment copies page. 

You can also set up the system to automatically send payment notification emails whenever a 

payment is confirmed. If you set up automatic payment notifications, you don’t need to manually 

send notifications from the Print payment copies page unless you want to resend a notification. 

Learn more about Notify vendors that they’ve been paid. 

To send payment notification emails: 

1. 
Open the Accounts payable menu. 

2. 
Select Print payment copies. 

3. 
Use the filter options to narrow the list of payments. You can also click View to see all check 

payments. 

4. 
Select the Email option for any payments for which you want to send notification emails. 

5. 
For each payment, verify that there’s at least one email address listed in the Email address 

field. 

If the vendor or employee has an email address on record, it is completed for you.

Merging Vendors 

When you find duplicate vendor records in the system, you can merge them. 

This feature allows you to: 

• 
Compare two vendor records side-by-side, enabling you to confirm that they are duplicates. 

• 
Update the vendor records. 

• 
Update transactions that link to the vendors so that they all use the same record. 

As a result of the merge, only one vendor record will remain. The second vendor record becomes 

inactive. 

If you forget to include invoices linked to the vendor record that was inactivated, you must 
re-activate the inactive vendor record and repeat the merge of the two vendor records. 

Before You Begin 

Access can vary depending on your organization’s subscriptions and your permissions. If you do 

not see the option in the menu, then ask your System Administrator to check your permissions. 

Permissions 

These permissions are required to merge vendors. 

Application 
Activities/Lists 
Permissions 

Accounts payable 
Merge vendors 
Run, List 

If your user account doesn’t have the permissions shown above, then ask your System 

Administrator for assistance. If you have administrator privileges, you can assign permissions for a 

new feature to a user or to a role. See Roles and Permissions for a description of how to review a 

user’s permissions.

#### Merging Duplicate Vendors

Merging Duplicate Vendors 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > All > Periodic Tasks > Account Maintenance > 
Merge Vendors`


If either vendor has a parent-child relationship, you must break this relationship before you can 

merge the vendor records. 

To merge duplicate vendor records: 

1. 
Open the Accounts payable menu. 

2. 
In the Account Maintenance section, select Merge vendors. 

3. 
On the Merge vendor page, in the left column, in the Active vendor ID drop-down list, 

select the vendor you want to remain active. This is the vendor you want your A/P invoices 

to show. 

4. 
In the Record Update section, select the type of vendor merge that you want to perform: 

All: Select to merge all A/P invoices, for both historical and active vendors. 

Update historical A/P invoices only: Select this option to merge all historical payments. 

New vendor information appears in the system, but the checks have already been printed 

with the original vendor information. 

Update active A/P invoices only: This option updates open items with active vendor 

information only and the historical A/P invoices appear on the available, side but are not 

updated. 

Update A/P invoice range: If you have a specific A/P invoice range that you want to update, 

this option will pull over just that range. On the A/P invoice range, you are required to move 

the available A/P invoices to the selected column. 

Update date range: Select this option when you have a specific date range that you want to 

update. 

• 
In From date and To date, enter the starting date and ending date of the date 

range.  

• 
Click the Get AP invoices button. The system selects the available A/P invoices to 

the selected column. 

None: If you do not merge A/P invoices, but you want to merge a vendor, then select this 

option. 

5. 
Click the Select link and select or remove any invoices as needed. 

After the merge, the vendor on the right is merged. The system inactivates the original 

record. The original vendor record will no longer appear in your Vendor drop-down lists for 

selection. If there are open purchase orders, service contracts, or subcontracts, the system

### Printing Final Account Statements (FAS)
*Source: `RP Accounting AP Periodic Tasks User Guide.pdf`, Page 152*



#### Before You Begin
*Source: `RP Accounting AP Periodic Tasks User Guide.pdf`, Page 152*

Account Maintenance 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Periodic Tasks User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Printing Final Account Statements (FAS) 

A final account statement (FAS) document contains a recap of items and services billed and a 

confirmation of payments received. FAS documents reside in OneSite. RealPage Accounting can 

pull FAS documents from OneSite into the RealPage Accounting system so that you can print and 

email them.  

You can either print one FAS for an invoice, or you can print multiple FAS. 

• 
To retrieve one invoice, click the Print FAS button from an eligible A/P Invoice record. To be 

eligible for this feature, the invoice’s vendor name must begin with “TEMP.” 

• 
To retrieve multiple invoices’ FAS documents, select the Print FAS menu option in the 


> **Navigation Path:** `Periodic Tasks > Account Maintenance section of the Accounts Payable menu. You can`


retrieve one FAS document or multiple documents using the menu option. 

You must have the Print FAS permission to retrieve, print, and email FAS documents.  

Before You Begin 

Access can vary depending on your organization’s subscriptions and your permissions. If you do 

not see the option in the menu, then ask your System Administrator to check your permissions. 

Permissions 

These permissions are required to print final account statement (FAS) documents: 

Application 
Activities/Lists 
Permissions 

Accounts Payable 
Print FAS 
Run 

If your user account doesn’t have the permissions shown above, then ask your System 

Administrator for assistance. If you have administrator privileges, you can assign permissions for a 

new feature to a user or to a role. See Roles and Permissions for a description of how to review a 

user’s permissions. 

Transaction Eligibility 

For a transaction’s FAS document to be available to be retrieved by RealPage Accounting: 

• 
The transaction must have originated in OneSite.  

• 
The vendor name must start with “TEMP.” 

• 
The transaction must be in the “Paid” state. 

---

Debt Maintenance 

This section describes how to create loan records in the A/P application.  

Debt Maintenance List 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > All > Periodic Tasks > Account Maintenance > Debt 
Maintenance`


Use this list to create and manage loans. You can generate a loan or bond amortization schedule 

that matches the bank’s amortization schedule.  

In a loan record, you can attach supporting documentation and configure additional fees and 

escrows. This makes it possible to generate an A/P invoice, A/R invoice, or G/L entry every month 

for the correct principal and interest for that month plus any additional fees or escrows without 

having to change a recurring invoice or enter new invoices every month. 

From the list, you can: 

• 
Add a new loan 

• 
View and edit the details of a loan 

• 
Post loans to the General ledger manually 

• 
View the list of scheduled payments of a loan 

• 
Export a loan 

• 
Export the list of loans 

• 
Delete a loan

Before You Begin 

Access can vary depending on your organization’s subscriptions and your permissions. If you do 

not see the option in the menu, then ask your System Administrator to check your permissions. 

Permissions 

These permissions are required to add and manage loans. 

Application 
Activities/Lists 
Permissions 

Accounts payable 
Debt maintenance 
List, View, Add, Edit, Delete 

Accounts payable 
Loan types

If your user account doesn’t have the permissions shown above, then ask your System 

Administrator for assistance. If you have administrator privileges, you can assign permissions for a 

new feature to a user or to a role. See Roles and Permissions for a description of how to review a 

user’s permissions. 

Requirements 

Before you can post loans, be sure that your system has a Loan/Bond journal defined and linked 

on the Accounts Payable Configuration page.  

Adding a Loan 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > All > Periodic Tasks > Account Maintenance > 
Debt Maintenance`


To add a loan: 

1. 
Open the Accounts Payable menu 

2. 
Click the 
 Add button next to Debt maintenance to open a new loan record.  

Filling In the Loan Info Page 

1. 
In the Loan ID field, type a unique value to assign to the loan. The ID can be up to 20 

characters.  

2. 
In the Loan name field, type the text that you want to appear on the A/P invoice that the 

system creates. 

3. 
In the Description field, type a description of the loan. 

4. 
In the Loan number field, type the number assigned to the loan by the lender. 

5. 
In Payment frequency, select how often the borrower is required to make a loan payment. 

Options are Monthly, Quarterly, Annual, and Semi-Annually.  

6. 
In the Principal amount field, type the amount of the principal. 

---


<!-- Page 161 -->
Chapter 5: Account Maintenance 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Periodic Tasks User Guide 

7. 
In the First payment date field, type the date that the first payment is due. 

8. 
In the Rate type section, select Fixed or Variable (Manual Entry/Import).  

• 
Select Fixed if the interest rate is unchanging.  

• 
Select Variable (Manual Entry/Import) if the interest rate can vary.  

If you selected a Fixed Rate type, fill in the following fields: 

• 
In the Interest rate field, type the interest rate.  

• 
In the Posting option section, select Scheduled or Manual. 

• 
If you selected Scheduled, type the number of days prior to posting to schedule 

the payment in the Days Prior to post field. 

• 
In the Calculation option section, select Number of payments or Payment amount. 

• 
If you selected the Number of payments option, then type the number of 

payments that you want to make in the Number of payments field. 

• 
If you selected the Payment amount option, then type the amount of each 

payment in the Payment amount field. 

• 
In the Number of interest-only periods field, type the number of periods that will be 

paying off interest on the loan only. 

If you selected a Variable Rate type, fill in the following fields: 

• 
In the Interest rate field, type the interest rate.  

• 
In the Posting option section, select Scheduled or Manual. 

• 
If you selected Scheduled, type the number of days prior to posting to schedule 

the payment in the Days Prior to post field. 

• 
Optionally, type the amount of each payment in the Payment amount field. 

9. 
Select the Use 360 day year calculation check box to have the system calculate the interest 

rate by. 

10. 
Select the Calculate daily interest check box to have the system calculate the daily interest 

rate. 

11. 
Select the Has first month interest check box to have the system count the first month in 

calculating interest payments, and then type the number of days in the Number of days for 

the 1st month interest field. 

12. 
Select the Has balloon payment check box if the loan has balloon payments.  

• 
Type the number of payments in the Balloon payment number field. 

• 
If there is no interest on the balloon payment, select the Balloon payment has no 

interest check box. 

13. 
In the Reference number field, type a reference number as needed.

In the Term field, type the number of days after notification that the lender must be paid, 

expressed in days.

Adding Payments for Variable Interest Rates 

If you selected a variable interest rate type, an Add Payment for button appears in the Schedule 

section. The date reflects the payment frequency that you selected. Row 1 reflects the year for 

which you are adding payments. 

1. 
Click the Add Payments for (date) button to add a payment. The payment data appears on 

line 2. 

2. 
Fill in the principal and interest. 

3. 
Click the Add payment for button to add the next payment row. 

4. 
Continue adding payments in this way to fill out the schedule as needed. 

Importing a Payment Schedule 

To import a payment schedule: 

1. 
If you want to import a loan schedule, select the desired Import option: 

• 
Replace: Select this option to replace the loan schedule records in the system with 

imported ones. 

• 
Append: Select this option to add the imported loan schedule records to the existing 

records in the system. 

2. 
Download the template by clicking the Download Schedule template link.  

The Download Schedule template option appears only when: 

• 
The Rate Type is set to Variable (Manual Entry/Import)  

• 
The Rate Type is set to Fixed and the Generate option is set to Import. 

3. 
Fill the template with your external payment schedule data. 

4. 
Save the file in CSV format. 

5. 
Import the loan schedule data by clicking the Choose File button, and then selecting the 

CSV file.

Filling In the Payment Info Tab 

1. 
In the Processing Option drop-down list, select what you want the system to do:

• 
Direct to G/L: Select this option to generate a journal entry in the borrower’s books, 

and an A/R invoice for the selected customer in the lender’s books. 

• 
Internal (Borrower A/P invoice/Lender A/R Invoice): Select this option to generate an

borrower’s books.

journal entry in the borrower’s books and an A/R invoice for the selected customer in

#### Generating a Loan Schedule
*Source: `RP Accounting AP Periodic Tasks User Guide.pdf`, Page 168*

Account Maintenance 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Periodic Tasks User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Generating a Loan Schedule 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > All > Periodic Tasks > Debt Maintenance > Edit > 
Generate Schedule`


To generate a set of scheduled loan payments: 

1. 
Open the Accounts Payable menu.  

2. 
In the Periodic Tasks section, click Debt maintenance. 

3. 
In the Debt maintenance list, open the loan with the schedule that you want to import into. 

4. 
Click the Edit link of the loan that you want to schedule payments for. 

Setting Up the Calculation for the Scheduled Payments 

1. 
In Payment frequency, select how often the borrower is required to make a loan payment. 

Options are Monthly, Quarterly, Annual, and Semi-Annually.  

2. 
In the Principal amount field, type the amount of the principal. 

3. 
In the First payment date field, type the date that the first payment is due. 

4. 
In the Rate type section, select Fixed or Variable. Select Fixed if the interest rate is 

unchanging. Select Variable if the interest rate can vary.  

5. 
In the Interest rate field, type the current interest rate. 

6. 
In the Posting option section, select Scheduled. 

7. 
In the Days prior to post field, type the number of days before posting that you want to 

calculate the loan payment. 

8. 
In the Calculation option section, select an option: 

• 
Number of payments: Select this option if you want to calculate the payments based 

on a set number of payments. 

• 
Payment amount: Select this option if you want to calculate the payments based on a 

specific payment amount.  

9. 
If you selected Number of payments, then type the number of payments. If you selected 

Payment amount, then type the amount of the payment. 

10. 
In the Number of interest-only periods field, type the number of periods to dedicated to 

paying off interest on the loan only.  

11. 
Select the 360 day year calculation check box to have the system calculate the interest rate 

by taking the annual interest rate and dividing it by 360 to get the daily interest rate. This 

calculation assumes that there are 360 days a year and 30 days in each month.  

12. 
Select the Calculate daily interest check box to have the system calculate the daily interest 

rate. 

---

13. 
Select the Has first month interest check box to have the system count the first month in 

calculating interest payments.  

14. 
Select the Has balloon payment check box if the loan has balloon payments.  

• 
Type the number of balloon payments in the Balloon payment number field. 

• 
If there is no interest on the balloon payment, select the Balloon payment has no 

interest check box. 

Generating the Schedule 

1. 
In the Generate option section, select Generate. 

2. 
Fill in the Last historical date field to determine which schedule entries to mark as historical. 

The system marks all schedule entries “Historical” when they are less than or equal to the 

entered date. 

3. 
Click the Generate Schedule button. The system calculates the payments and then adds the 

information to the Schedule section. 

After generating the scheduled payments, you can edit the principal and interest figures of 
payments as needed. 

4. 
Click Save to save the schedule of payments. 

Importing Scheduled Payments into a Loan Record 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > All > Periodic Tasks > Debt Maintenance > Edit > 
Import`


To import a set of scheduled loans into a loan’s schedule: 

1. 
In the Debt maintenance list, open the loan with the schedule that you want to import into. 

2. 
Click the Edit link. 

3. 
Download the schedule template by clicking the Download schedule template link. The file 

downloads to the browser’s default download location.  

4. 
Open the CSV file and fill it with the data that you want to import.  

Required fields 

• 
LOAN_ID: Type the loan ID of the loan that you want to import into. The Loan ID must 

exist in the system prior to importing the data. 

• 
PAYMENT_NO: Type the payment number  

• 
INVOICE_NO: Type the invoice number. If you do not include a number in this column, 

the system will generate a number for the bill. The system generated bill number has 

the following format: <payment number - loan number>. 

• 
CREATED_DATE: Type the date that the payment was created. 

---


<!-- Page 170 -->
Account Maintenance 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Periodic Tasks User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

• 
GL_DATE: Type the date that the payment was posted to the General Ledger. 

• 
DUE_DATE: Type the date that the payment was due. 

• 
PRINCIPAL: Type line item #1 number on the bill. Type a non-zero value. Designate 

negatives with a leading dash. 

• 
STATUS: Type H for Historical, type P for Pending. If the status is set to Pending, the 

system creates an invoice for the payment. If the status is H, the system does not 

create an invoice. 

Optional fields 

• 
INTEREST: Type line item #2 on the bill.  

• 
ESCROW:  Type line item #3 on the bill.  

• 
OTHER_1: Type line item #4 on the bill. 

• 
OTHER_2: Type line item #5 on the bill. 

• 
OTHER_3: Type line item #6 on the bill. 

• 
OTHER_4: Type line item #7 on the bill. 

• 
OTHER_5: Type line item #8 on the bill. 

• 
OTHER_6: Type line item #9 on the bill. 

• 
OTHER_7: Type line item #10 on the bill. 

5. 
Save the file in CSV format.  

6. 
On the Loan info page, in the Generate option section, select the Import option. 

7. 
In the Import option section, select an option: 

• 
Replace: Select this option to replace all of the records in the scheduled loan 

payments with the records that you are about to import. 

• 
Append: Select this option to add the records that you are about to import to the 

existing list of scheduled loan payments. 

8. 
Click the Choose File button, and then double-click the CSV file that you added data to. The 

system imports the data based on your import option selection. 

9. 
Click Save.

Use this page to have the system generate a journal entry that transfers the principal part of the

• 
Select the Automatic principal reclass check box, and then select the source and 

destination accounts. 

Automatic Principal Reclass 

You can configure the system to generate a journal entry automatically that transfers the principal 

part of the payment from the specified long-term account to the short-term account each time a 

payment is made. 

1. 
Select the Automatic principal reclass check box to enable this feature. 

2. 
Select the account to transfer from in the Long term account (Credit) drop-down list. 

3. 
Select the account to transfer to in the Short term account (Debit) drop-down list. 

If a Building Account is defined, then the system creates an initial journal entry to credit the 

building account and debit the long-term account for the principal amount of the loan. 

4. 
To define a building account, select the building account in the Building Account 

drop-down list.

> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > All > Debt Maintenance > Edit > Details`

change. Make sure that the record that you select has Scheduled in the Posting option 

column. 

3. 
Click the Details link. The Loan Schedule list opens. 

4. 
Click the Edit link of the payment to change. The Loan Schedule Information page opens. 

5. 
Make the changes as needed. 

6. 
Click Save.

Maintenance > Details > View`

#### Posting Loan Invoices
*Source: `RP Accounting AP Periodic Tasks User Guide.pdf`, Page 178*

Account Maintenance 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Periodic Tasks User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Posting Loan Invoices 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > All > Periodic Tasks > Account Maintenance > Debt 
Maintenance > Post Loans`


You can post invoices for the loans that you created manually. 

Before any loan invoices can be posted, the system must have a Loan/Bond journal in the 
Accounts Payable configuration. See Defining the Loan Invoices Journal in the online help system 
or refer to the Accounts Payable Setup User Guide. 

To post loan invoices manually: 

1. 
Open the Accounts Payable menu. 

2. 
Select Debt Maintenance. The Debt maintenance list opens. 

3. 
Click the Post Loans button. 

4. 
Select the check boxes of the loans for which you want to post invoices.  

5. 
In the For the month field, type the date that you want to post for. By default, the system 

posts through the current month. 

6. 
In the Invoice/GL batch Date field, type the date for the batch.  

7. 
In the Send completion notification to field, type the email address where you want the 

system to send an email when the system completes posting the loans. 

8. 
Click the Post Selected Loans button. The system queues the posting and processes it 

offline. The system sends an email message when posting is complete.

#### Importing Loan Schedules
*Source: `RP Accounting AP Periodic Tasks User Guide.pdf`, Page 179*

Chapter 5: Account Maintenance 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Periodic Tasks User Guide 

Importing Loan Schedules 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > All > Periodic Tasks > Debt Maintenance`


To import loan records into the Debt Maintenance list: 

1. 
Open the Accounts Payable menu. 

2. 
Select Debt Maintenance. 

3. 
Download the template by clicking the Template button. 

4. 
Open the downloaded file in Excel.  

5. 
Fill the template with the loan data that you want to import. 

• 
Loan_ID: This field must contain a unique loan identifier. 

• 
PAYMENT_NO: Type the unique number associated with the payment, up to 4 

characters. 

• 
CREATED_DATE: Type the date that the loan payment was made. 

• 
GL_DATE: Type the date that the payment was posted to the general ledger. 

• 
DUE_DATE: Type the date that the payment was due.  

• 
Line item #1 on the bill: Type a non-zero number. Type the number with a leading 

dash to a designate negative number. 

• 
Status: Type H for Historical or P for Pending. 

6. 
Optionally, fill in any of the non-required columns of the template.  

7. 
Save the file in CSV format (on page 357). 

8. 
Import the file. 

9. 
Click the Import button. The Loan Schedule box opens. 

10. 
Click the Choose File button, find the CSV file with the data that you want to import, and 

double-click it. 

11. 
If the data in the CSV file includes dates that are not in MM/DD/YYYY format, select the date 

format used in the data that you are importing. 

12. 
Leave the File Encoding option set to Auto detect unless you’re unable to import your file. 

Depending on your operating system, you may need to select a different type of file 

encoding. 

13. 
If your import box has a Process offline check box, you can select it to process the import 

offline. Select this option for large files. 

14. 
In the Email results to this address field, type the email address where you want the system 

to send import results and error data. 

---

Expense Reports

Introduction to Expense Reports 

Use the expense reports feature to track and record business-related spending to ensure accurate 

reimbursement and financial transparency.  

An expense report is a record of business-related costs such as travel, meals, or office supplies. 

Employees typically submit expense reports to request reimbursement for out-of-pocket 

expenses. 

Expense reports are important because they ensure accurate reimbursement of employee 

expenses, provide transparency and accountability in company spending, support budget 

management and financial planning, and maintain compliance with tax and audit requirements. 

Getting Started with Expense Reports 

Before you can start using the expense report feature, you must set up your preferences including 

the notifications that you wish to receive. 

• 
Set Up Preferences for Expense Reporting (on page 192) 

• 
Configuring Expense Report Notifications (on page 193) 

After you have configured your preferences and notifications, you can begin adding expense 

reports. You can add your own expense reports. If you have permissions (on page 216), you can 

also add expense reports on behalf of someone else. 

• 
Adding an Expense Report (on page 195) 

• 
Creating an Expense Report for Someone Else (on page 217) 

Set Up Preferences for Expense Reporting 

If you plan to create and submit expense reports for reimbursement, change your preferences to 

allow for expense report notifications. Set up expense report notification preferences in the 

Unified Platform. See Configuring expense report notifications (on page 193).

Filling In the Expenses Section Manually 

1. 
In the Date column, type or select the date that you incurred the expense. This field is 

required. 

2. 
In the Location column, select the location associated with the expense. This field is 

required. 

3. 
In the Department column, select the department to associate with the expense. This field is 

required. 

4. 
In the Expense category column, select the appropriate category for the expense. Examples 

of employee expenses include Airfare, Hotel, Meals, and Gasoline. Examples of property 

expenses include Office supplies and Employee recognition. This field is required. 

5. 
In the Amount column, type the amount of the expense. This field is required. 

If you selected IRS mileage in the Expense category field, and then click the Amount field, a 

box opens to collect mileage-related information: 

• 
In Miles, type the number of miles driven. 

• 
In Rate, type the amount per mile that the company reimburses. The default rate is .67. 

If the Rate field is not available, it means that your system is configured to use the IRS rate. 

The system will calculate the mileage based on the configured rate. 

If your system renamed the IRS Mileage field to anything else, such as Mileage or Gas, this 

feature will not open the box, and you must enter the rate manually. 

If you select Hotel in the Expense category field, and then click the Amount field, a box 

opens to collect additional data: 

• 
In the Nightly rate field, type the rate for one night’s stay at the hotel. 

• 
In the Nightly taxes field, type the amount on the bill for taxes.  

• 
In the Nights field, type the number of nights spent at the hotel. 

6. 
In the Reimbursement type column, select the appropriate reimbursement type to assign it 

to the expense. Your company determines the available reimbursement types.  

• 
Select Employee when an employee needs to be reimbursed. 

• 
Select Property when a property needs to be reimbursed. 

• 
Select P-Card vendor when a P-card vendor needs to be reimbursed. 

7. 
In the Memo column, type a brief description of the expense. 

If the expense was gasoline or hotel, the system completes the Memo field. 

8. 
In the Unit column, select the unit associated with the expense. 

9. 
In the Attachment section:

The Status column shows where the expense report is in the approval process.  

• 
Draft: The expense report has been created but has not been submitted to the 

approval process. 

• 
Submitted: The expense report has been submitted but has not yet been approved. 

• 
Approved: The expense report has been approved. 

The Payment Status column shows the status of invoices created from the expense report.  

• 
Pending: The system has created invoices from the report, and they are waiting to be 

paid. 

• 
Partially paid: The system has created invoices for some of the expenses on the report. 

• 
Paid: The system has created all invoices from the expense report.

Exporting Lists 

You can export most lists to several available file formats and then import the data into an 

external application, such as Microsoft Word or Microsoft Excel. 

Although you can export up to 25,000 rows, if you want to save time and effort, we recommend 

that you filter your list to pinpoint only the information you need to export by creating a custom 

view. That way, when you export the list, you’ll have a spreadsheet tailored to the information you 

need. You can export any view of this list for use on your local computer. 

Use column filters, advanced filters, and views to filter the data. For instructions, refer to 

Managing Lists. 

If you have a sorted and filtered list that you use consistently, you can create and save it as a 

custom report for convenience. With a custom report, you need to set the filtering and 

parameters only once to enable you to generate the report as needed after that. 

1. 
Click the Export button. 

2. 
Select the format to which you want to export the list. 

• 
CSV: Select this format if you plan to move the data from one program to another. 

You can use files that you save in CSV format with any spreadsheet program. 

• 
Word: When you select this option, the system exports the list in Word format. If a list 

of conversion formats displays, select HTML document. 

• 
Excel: When you select this option, the system exports the list in XLS format. If you see 

an error message about file type and extension type incompatibility, you can disregard 

the message and select Yes. 

• 
PDF: Select this option if you plan to print or share the list. When you select this 

option, the system exports the list and tries to open the file in the browser. If 

prompted, select Yes to allow the PDF to open. 

• 
CSV for import: Select this option if you want to export data, change it, or add to it, 

and then import it into the system again. 

Some lists in RealPage Accounting do not have the CSV for import option.

#### Creating Invoices from an Approved Expense Report
*Source: `RP Accounting AP Periodic Tasks User Guide.pdf`, Page 205*

Chapter 6: Expense Reports 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Periodic Tasks User Guide 

Creating Invoices from an Approved Expense Report 

Your system administrator can configure the system to create reimbursement invoices 

automatically after an expense report is approved. If the system is not configured this way, then 

you must create the A/P invoices for each approved expense report manually. 

After it’s configured, users only need to pay the A/P invoices to reimburse the employee, 

property, or P-Card vendor. 

To configure the system to create reimbursement invoices automatically, see Configuring expense 

reports in the online help or in the Accounts Payable Setup User Guide. 

How the Create Reimbursement Invoice Feature Works 

When an expense report is approved, the system automatically creates an invoice or invoices 

based on the information in the expense report. The reimbursement type determines how many 

invoices that the system creates.  

• 
If the expense report contains several items, but only one reimbursement type, then the 

system creates only one invoice for all expenses.  

• 
If the expense report contains expenses of all three reimbursement types, then the system 

creates one invoice for each reimbursement type (Employee, Property, and P-card vendor). 

---

Staff Expenses List

Expenses`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Time & Resources > All > Periodic Tasks > Staff Expenses`


This list displays all expense reports created by anyone in the company.  

Use this list to add, view, edit, and delete expense reports. You can also import expenses from a 

CSV file and export the list of expense reports. 

If your user account is only permitted to view and access specific entities, then the list includes 

expense reports only for the entities that you are permitted to view.  

Use the list controls to create custom views and filter and sort the list. See Managing the List for 

details. 

Before You Begin 

Access can vary depending on your organization’s subscriptions and your permissions. If you do 

not see the option in the menu, then ask your System Administrator to check your permissions. 

Permissions 

These permissions are required to work with staff expense reports. Staff expenses permissions 

allow you to access expense reports created by your employees, or on behalf of your employees.

Accounts Payable 
Staff Expenses

If your user account doesn’t have the permissions shown above, then ask your System 

Administrator for assistance. If you have administrator privileges, you can assign permissions for a 

new feature to a user or to a role. See Roles and Permissions for a description of how to review a 

user’s permissions.
