#### Creating an Expense Report for Someone Else
*Source: `RP Accounting AP Periodic Tasks User Guide.pdf`, Page 217*

Chapter 6: Expense Reports 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Periodic Tasks User Guide 

Creating an Expense Report for Someone Else 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > All > Periodic Tasks > Expense Reports > 
 Staff 
Expenses`


The process of creating an expense report for someone else is the same as creating your personal 

expense report except that you specify the name of the user for whom you are creating it. You 

can create an expense report for anyone. 

To create an expense report on behalf of another user: 

1. 
Open the Accounts Payable menu. 

2. 
Click 
 Staff expenses. The Staff expense report page opens. 

3. 
In the User drop-down list, select the user for whom you are creating an expense report. 

4. 
The system completes the Date filed field with today’s date. This is the date that the 

expense report is to be filed. You can change the date by typing or selecting a different 

date. 

The system assigns a unique identifier to the expense report after you submit it. It appears 

in the Expense report number field the next time that you open the expense report. 

5. 
In the Expense report name field, type a name for the report. 

6. 
Select the Corporate expense report check box if you do not want the corporate expense 

report to appear in Site View.  

7. 
In the Description field, type more details about the expense report, such as the reason or 

purpose of the expenses. 

Setting Default Values 

Selecting default values is one method of speeding up data entry. Use this section to choose the 

values that you want the system to complete for you in the Entries list. (optional)  

After choosing the values and applying them, the system completes the fields in the Entries list 

with the values that you selected. After the system completes the fields, you can change any of 

the values, such as when one row requires a different value than the others. 

To set up default values: 

1. 
Click the Show defaults link to expand the area. 

You can specify a default value for one field, or for as many fields as are offered in the 
Defaults section.  

2. 
For each field that you want to prefill, choose the value that you enter most frequently or 

choose a value that is a standard value for the list of line items in this invoice. 

---


<!-- Page 218 -->
Expense Reports 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Periodic Tasks User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

3. 
Click the Apply defaults button. The system completes the column or columns with your 

default values. Learn more about Setting default line items. 

Next, you can either enter expenses manually, or use a template to speed up the expense entry 

process. 

Using an Allocation Template to Fill In the Expense Entries List 

You can create allocation templates on the Accounts Payable Setup tab using the Templates 

option. 

1. 
Click the Apply Template button. 

2. 
Select the desired template to use for expenses. 

3. 
Type the amount of the expense. 

4. 
Select the expense category. 

5. 
Select the reimbursement type. 

6. 
Click the Apply button. 

To use this template again later, click the Save Template button and then save these 
values as a template. 

Saving the Template 

You can fill in the desired values and then save them as a template without leaving the page. 

1. 
Click the Save Template button. 

2. 
Type a name for the template. 

3. 
Type a description such as the purpose of the template. 

4. 
Select the template type. 

5. 
Type a memo that will help you remember why you created this template. 

6. 
Click Save. You can access and edit templates saved this way on the Accounts Payable 

Setup tab by selecting the Templates option. 

Filling In the Expenses Section Manually 

1. 
In the Date column, type or select the date that the expense was incurred. This field is 

required. 

2. 
In the Location column, select the location associated with the expense. This field is 

required. 

3. 
In the Expense category column, select the appropriate category for the expense. Examples 

of employee expenses include Airfare, Hotel, Meals, and Gasoline. Examples of property 

expenses include Office supplies and Employee recognition. This field is required. 

---


<!-- Page 219 -->
Chapter 6: Expense Reports 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Periodic Tasks User Guide 

4. 
In the Amount column, type the amount of the expense. This field is required. 

• 
When you click the Amount field after selecting the IRS Mileage expense category, a 

box opens where you can enter the miles driven.  

• 
When the Rate field is available, type the rate at which your company reimburses for 

mileage. If the Rate field is not available, it is configured to use the IRS rate.  

• 
Click Save. The system inserts the calculated amount in the Amount field, and inserts a 

note about the miles and rate in the Memo field. 

5. 
In the Reimbursement type column, select the appropriate reimbursement type to assign it 

to the expense. Your company determines the available reimbursement types.  

• 
Select Employee when an employee needs to be reimbursed. 

• 
Select Property when a property needs to be reimbursed. 

• 
Select P-Card vendor when a P-card vendor needs to be reimbursed. 

6. 
In the Memo column, type a brief description of the expense. 

7. 
In the Unit column, select the unit associated with the expense. 

8. 
In the Attachment section: 

To add an attachment to the expense record: 

• 
Click the 
 Add button. The Upload Attachment box opens.  

• 
Click the Choose Files button and locate the invoice, scanned receipt, or other 

documentation that supports your expense.  

• 
Click Upload. The filename appears in the Attachment column. 

To remove an attachment: 

• 
Click the 
 Remove Attachment button to remove the current attachment. 

9. 
If your company uses dimensions and segments in expense reports, the Segment Type 1 

column appears. If it does not, then return to step one of this section to add another 

expense, or continue to the Saving the expense report section. 

• 
Select a segment in the Segment Type 1 column, and then select the value for the 

segment in the Segment Value 1 column.  

• 
Click the Show details tab. The Details section opens. 

• 
Select any dimension values that you need to associate with the expense. 

• 
Select additional segment types and values as needed. 

• 
Close the Details section by clicking the Hide details tab. 

If the Segment type and Segment value fields do not appear, then your system does not 
have the segments feature enabled.

Saving the Expense Report 

If you are not finished entering your expenses, save the expense report as a draft. You can come

Importing Staff Expenses 

• 
Importing Draft Staff Expenses (on page 220) 

• 
Importing Approved Staff Expenses (on page 223) 

Importing Draft Expenses 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > All > Periodic Tasks > Expense Reports > Staff 
Expenses > Import`


You can import expenses from the Staff expenses page or from the Import data page. This 

procedure describes importing from the Import data page.  

When you add expense data to the import file, add the User ID of the user who incurred the 

expense and the amount. You can also specify the expense report name to associate an expense 

with a specific expense report.  

After importing the CSV file, these expenses appear in users’ My expenses lists. The system sends 

an email message to each user who had expenses in the imported file. The user must add 

additional information, attach any required receipts and invoices, and then submit the expenses 

for approval. 

To import expenses: 

1. 
Open the Company menu. 

2. 
Select Import data. 

3. 
In the Set Up Master List, Open Invoices and Adjustments section, find the Expense Reports - 

Draft row, and then select Template. The template (on page 388) for draft expenses 

downloads to your browser’s default download location.  

Preparing the Data for Importing 

1. 
Export the unapproved, draft expenses data from your other system. 

2. 
Open the downloaded template (on page 353) in Microsoft Excel or your favorite 

spreadsheet application. 

3. 
Fill in the template with the unapproved expense data that you want to import. Take care to 

exactly match the template’s data structure as you do this.  

---


<!-- Page 221 -->
Chapter 6: Expense Reports 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Periodic Tasks User Guide 

Do not use leading zeros in ID fields. If you MUST use leading zeros in IDs, convert the 
column of ID numbers to text format in Excel before importing the file content. Excel does 
not remove the leading zeros when you save the file. Remember to do this every time you 
use a template to import information that requires IDs. 

4. 
Fill in the required columns: 

• 
USER_ID: Type the ID of the user who the expense is being submitted for. 

• 
AMOUNT: Type the amount of the draft expense. 

5. 
Optionally, fill in the remaining columns. Many of the valid values differ by company 

because your company configures expenses in your system depending on your business 

needs. See Configuring Expense Reports. 

• 
EXP_REPORT_NAME: Type the expense report name. 

• 
DATE_FILED: Type the date that the expenses were filed. The default value is today’s 

date. 

• 
DESCRIPTION: Type a description of the expense. 

• 
DATE: Type the date. The default value is today’s date. 

• 
EXPENSE_CATEGORY: Type the category of the expense.  

• 
REIMBURSEMENT_TYPE: Type who or what will be reimbursed: Employees, Property, 

or P-card vendor. 

• 
LOCATION_ID: Type the unique identifier of the location associated with the expense.  

• 
MEMO: Type a note about the expense.  

• 
UNIT: Type the unit number associated with this expense.  

• 
CORPORATE_EXP_REPORT: Type “true” if this is a corporate expense report or type 

“false” if not. Corporate expense reports do not appear in Site View. 

• 
DEPARTMENTID: Type the unique identifier of the department that is associated with 

the expense. 

• 
SEGMENTTYPE_1: Type the segment type associated with the expense. 

• 
SEGMENTVALUE_1: Type the segment value of segment 1 that is associated with the 

expense. 

• 
SEGMENTTYPE_2: Type a second segment type to associate with the expense. 

• 
SEGMENTVALUE_2: Type the segment value of segment 2 that is associated with the 

expense. 

• 
SEGMENTTYPE_3: Type the third segment type to associate with the expense. 

• 
SEGMENTVALUE_3: Type the segment value of segment 3 associated with the 

expense. 

• 
SEGMENTTYPE_4: Type the fourth segment type to associate with the expense.

•

STAFFEXPNSRPTITEM_CUSTOMERID: Type the unique identifier of the customer that

In the Email results to this address field, type your email address to have the system notify 

you when the import is complete. If the import generates errors, the error report is sent to 

this email address. 

7. 
Click the Import button. The system groups all imported expense reports by User ID. 

The system sends an email to the users who have had expenses imported on their behalf. 

The user must review and update the expense report and then submit it for approval.

not remove the leading zeros when you save the file. Remember to do this every time you

standard import function with one difference. When you import expenses, you must specify 

whether the expenses are draft or approved.

Download the desired staff expenses template. 

• 
If you want to import staff expenses before they have been approved, then click the 

Staff Expenses - Draft template link. 

• 
If you want to import staff expenses that have been approved, select the Staff 

Expenses - Approved template link. 

2. 
Prepare your data for importing. 

3. 
Import the expense data.  

For details, refer to Importing staff expenses (on page 220).

#### Editing an Approved Expense Report (Reopen)
*Source: `RP Accounting AP Periodic Tasks User Guide.pdf`, Page 231*

Chapter 6: Expense Reports 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Periodic Tasks User Guide 

To put an expense report invoice on hold: 

1. 
Open the Accounts payable menu. 

2. 
In the Expense Reports section, click My Expenses or Staff Expenses, whichever type of 

expense report is associated with the A/P invoice that you want to put on hold. 

3. 
Open the desired expense report. 

4. 
Click the A/P Invoice Info tab. 

5. 
Click the link in the Invoice number column to open the invoice.

Editing an Approved Expense Report (Reopen) 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > All > Staff Expenses > View > Reopen`


After an expense report is approved, the expense report and the invoice(s) tied to it cannot be 

edited. If you need to make a change to either the expense report or the invoice, then you can 

reopen the expense report. 

When you reopen an expense report, the system deletes the A/P invoices that are associated with 

it and changes its status to Draft. After it’s reopened, you can change all fields in the expense 

report. Edit the expense report to correct the errors, and then resubmit it. 

After invoices are paid, you cannot change any fields in the expense report that are tied to 

invoices.  

Reopening an expense report requires the Reopen permission. You can only reopen an expense 

report from the Staff Expenses list. 

Reopening a report cannot be undone. 

To reopen an expense report: 

1. 
Open the Accounts Payable menu. 

2. 
In the Expense reports section of the menu, select Staff Expenses. The Staff Expenses list 

opens. 

3. 
Click the View link of the expense report that you want to reopen. 

4. 
Click the Reopen button. The expense report opens to allow you to make changes.  

5. 
Edit the expense report to correct the errors. 

6. 
Click the Draft button to save it without submitting it, or click the Submit button to 

resubmit the changed expense report for approval with its changes.

applications. Choose the appropriate application for the type of approval workflow that you need.

Spend Management: Subscribe to the Spend Management application to use the approval

•

process with job cost change orders.

### Troubleshooting Expense Reports
*Source: `RP Accounting AP Periodic Tasks User Guide.pdf`, Page 245*

Troubleshooting Expense Reports 

Error: Unable to submit the expense report because the user’s manager is not defined in the 

Reports To field.  

• 
Solution: Please contact your system administrator and ask them either to update the 

expense report configuration with the name of the person to whom the employee reports 

or to update the User’s record with the manager in the Reports To drop-down list. 

Error: Unable to submit the expense report because you do not have a Vendor ID defined in the 

expense configuration. Please contact your system administrator and ask them to create a vendor 

record for you and configure your preferred payment method. Then have the system 

administrator select your vendor ID in the expense report configuration’s User management 

section. 

• 
Solution: When you create an expense report for an employee, the employee must have a 

vendor record associated with their user record.  

Error: Unable to save the expense report configuration because you enabled the Accounting 

reviewer feature but did not assign anyone to the Expense report accounting reviewer role. 

• 
Solution: Assign someone to the Expense report accounting reviewer role. See Assigning 

the reviewer role to users.

### Assets Overview
*Source: `RP Accounting AP Periodic Tasks User Guide.pdf`, Page 248*

Assets 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Periodic Tasks User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Assets Overview 

Tracking your company’s assets is the first and most important step in generating accurate 

financial reports. Assets are your company’s biggest investments that include property, 

equipment, investments, patents, and trademarks.  

Use RealPage Accounting to track any kind of asset. You can track assets by entering the 

information directly with the Assets option in the Accounts Payable menu, or you can enter asset 

information as you enter A/P invoices into the system. 

Before you can enter asset information as you enter A/P invoices, the system administrator must 

enable the feature.  

RealPage Accounting can share asset data with other RealPage products, including Fixed Assets, 

Facilities, and OPS Technology products, if your company subscribes to any of these products. 

Integrating Assets Between RealPage Accounting and Facilities 

You can integrate Accounting with Facilities so that asset records are shared between the two 

applications. When integration is enabled, regardless of where and how you add an asset in 

RealPage Accounting, when you add an asset record, a coordinating record is also added to the 

Facilities application. All updates to asset records are shared between Facilities and RealPage 

Accounting. Asset disposal is also shared between the two applications.  

To integrate assets with Facilities, see Configuring Asset Integration with Facilities. 

You can create assets from both the Fixed Assets and Accounts Payable applications. When you 

create an asset record, the system automatically creates a matching record for the asset in 

Facilities. If you update an asset in RealPage Accounting, the information is also updated in 

Facilities. If you update an asset in Facilities, the information is also updated in RealPage 

Accounting. 

---

*Source: `RP Accounting AP Periodic Tasks User Guide.pdf`, Page 249*

*Source: `RP Accounting AP Periodic Tasks User Guide.pdf`, Page 249*

> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > All > Periodic Tasks > Assets > Assets`


Use the assets list to add and manage asset records.  

Assets are associated with a specific location and entity. You can limit users’ access to one entity 

or a subset of entities in the system. When a user account is limited to specific entities, the user 

can see only assets that are associated with the entities that they are restricted to. 

Use the list controls to create custom views and filter and sort the list. See Managing the List for 

details. 

Before You Begin 

The system needs asset categories and asset types defined before users can add assets to the 

system. If you are a system administrator, you can add asset categories and types. See Adding an 

asset category and Adding an asset type in online help or download (on page 337) the RealPage 

Accounting Accounts Payable Setup User Guide. 

Permissions 

Access can vary depending on your organization’s subscriptions and your permissions. If you do 

not see the option in the menu, then ask your System Administrator to check your permissions. 

These permissions are required to add and manage asset records.

records are also shared between Facilities and RealPage Accounting. 

Adding an Asset Manually (Accounts Payable) 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > All > Assets > 
 Assets`


You can create assets from both the Fixed Assets and Accounts Payable applications. When you 

create an asset record, the system automatically creates a matching record for the asset in 

Facilities. If you update an asset in RealPage Accounting, the information is also updated in 

Facilities. If you update an asset in Facilities, the information is also updated in RealPage 

Accounting. 

To add a new asset manually: 

1. 
Open the Accounts Payable menu. 

2. 
In the Assets section, select the 
 Add button next to the Assets option. 

3. 
In the Asset name field, type a name for the asset. 

4. 
Categorize the asset by selecting a category from the Category drop-down list. 

5. 
Assign a type to the asset by selecting it from the Type drop-down list. 

6. 
In the Serial number field, type the serial number of the asset. If a red asterisk appears by 

the field name, then the serial number is required. 

7. 
In the Model number field, type the model number of the asset. If a red asterisk appears by 

the field name, then the model number is required. 

8. 
Enter the warranty number. 

9. 
Select the property where the asset is located from the Location drop-down list. 

10. 
 In the In service date field, type or select the date that the asset began to be used. 

11. 
 In the Warranty end date field, type or select the date that the warranty expires. 

12. 
 In the Out of service date field, type or select the date when the asset is due to be retired.

Importing Assets 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > Import Data > Set Up AP Master List, Open Invoices 
and Adjustments > Assets > Import`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > All > Assets > Assets > Import`

The Financial Suite provides import templates for many types of records so you can quickly add 

and update data throughout the system. We recommend that you download a new template 

whenever you use the import feature to ensure that your template is always up to date.  

If you are setting up your company for the first time, it’s best to import data in the order listed on 

the Import data page. Templates on the Import data page are automatically customized based 

on your company’s configuration, including any dimensions or custom fields that you’ve created. 

Importing asset information into RealPage Accounting adds a new asset record to RealPage 

Accounting’s Accounts Payable and Fixed Assets, and to the Facilities application. 

Importing Historical Assets Information From Facilities into RealPage Accounting 

For every asset record that you want to import into Accounting, fill in the FACILITIES_ASSET_ID 

column with the asset ID from the Facilities application. This tells the system that the asset already 

exists in Facilities, and that it is creating historical asset information. The system will not create a 

new asset record in Facilities. Without the FACILITIES_ASSET_ID column filled in, the system will 

create duplicate records in Facilities.

Downloading the Import Template 

To download the import template for assets: 

1. 
Open the Company menu, and then click the Import data menu option. The Import data 

page opens. 

2. 
In the Set up A/P master list, open invoices, and adjustments section, click the Template link 

next to Assets. 

The system either downloads the Assets.xls file or prompts you to open or save the file, 

depending on your browser’s settings. 

3. 
Open the Assets.xls file and fill in the required asset information: 

• 
ASSET_NAME: Type a descriptive name to identify the asset. 

• 
CATEGORY: Type the name of the asset class or asset category to associate with the 

asset. 

• 
TYPE: Type what kind of asset the asset is; for example, “Air conditioner,” “Ceiling fan,” 

“Clothes washer,” etc. 

See the Asset types list in Accounts Payable to add and manage asset types. 

• 
LOCATION_ID: Type the ID of the property where the asset is located. 

• 
ASSET_COST: Type the original cost of the asset. 

• 
ACCT_NO: Type the G/L account number associated with the invoice. 

• 
FACILITIES_ASSET_ID: If the asset information that you are importing is from the 

Facilities application, type the asset ID from the Facilities application in this field. When 

there is an ID in this field, this tells the system that you are importing historical asset 

information into Accounting.  

4. 
Optionally, fill in additional information and invoice details associated with each asset: 

• 
SERIAL_NUMBER: Type the asset’s serial number. 

• 
MODEL_NUMBER: Type the asset’s model number. 

• 
WARRANTY_NUMBER: Type the asset’s warranty number. 

• 
IN_SERVICE_DATE: Type the date that the asset was placed in service. Typically, this is 

the date the asset began being used; it does not have to be the same as the purchase 

date. 

• 
WARRANTY_START_DATE: Type the date the asset’s warranty coverage begins. 

• 
WARRANTY_END_DATE: Type the date the asset’s warranty coverage expires. 

• 
OUT_OF_SERVICE_DATE: Type the date that the asset was disposed or taken out of 

service. 

• 
INVOICE_NO: Type the invoice number associated with the asset, if any. 

---


<!-- Page 253 -->
Chapter 7: Assets 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Periodic Tasks User Guide 

• 
INVOICE_DATE: Type the invoice date. 

• 
VENDOR_ID: Type the ID of the vendor from which the asset was purchased. 

• 
UNIT: Type the unit number where the asset is located. 

• 
DEPARTMENT_ID: Type the ID of the department associated with the asset.  

• 
SALVAGE_VALUE: Type the amount that the asset is estimated to be worth at the end 

of its useful life, when all depreciation is expensed. 

• 
DEPRECIATION_CONVENTION: Type when to start the asset’s depreciation schedule. 

Valid values include: 

• 
P: Start depreciating the asset the month that the asset is placed in service. If you 

leave this field blank, the schedule defaults to this option. 

• 
N: If the asset was placed in service between the 1st and the 15th of the month, 

then start depreciating the asset on the first day of that month. If the asset was 

placed in service between the 15th and the 31st of the month, then start 

depreciating the asset on the first day of the next month. 

• 
M: Always treat the asset as if it started in the middle of the quarter (the quarter 

is determined by the date it was placed in service). Mid-quarter depreciation 

prevents the asset from exceeding its maximum depreciation for the year. This 

option is applicable only to assets whose asset book is set to depreciate assets on 

a Quarterly basis. Asset books are defined in the asset class. 

• 
QUANTITY: Type the quantity of assets on the invoice. 

• 
CONDITION: Type the condition of the asset. Valid values include: 

• 
N: New 

• 
UG: Used/Good 

• 
UF: Used/Fair 

• 
UP: Used/Poor 

• 
DEPARTMENT: Type the name of the department associated with the asset. 

5. 
Optionally, fill in the opening balances for the financial and tax books associated with the 

asset: 

You can import only the books that match the asset class. If you enter a date and amount 
for the Tax book but the asset class does not support the Tax book, then it will be ignored. 
Likewise, if you do not enter both the opening balance and the thru date, it will be ignored.  

• 
GENERAL_OPENING_BALANCE: Type the opening balance for the “General” asset 

book. 

• 
GENERAL_THRU_DATE: Type the date through which to set the opening balance for 

the “General” asset book. 

• 
TAX_OPENING BALANCE: Type the opening balance for the “Tax” asset book.

Filling In the Asset Information 

To enter asset information: 

1. 
In the Invoice entry section, select the asset’s category from the Category drop-down list. 

2. 
Select the asset’s type from the Type drop-down list. 

3. 
Click the Asset button. The Asset entry box opens. 

4. 
The system completes the number in the Asset cost field with the number that you typed in 

the line item. If there are multiple assets, then you can separate the costs onto the different 

rows in the Asset entry box. 

5. 
In the Model number field, type the asset’s model number. 

6. 
In the Serial number field, type the serial number on the asset. 

7. 
In the In service date field, type or select the date that the asset was put into use. 

8. 
In the Warranty end date field, type or select the date that the asset’s warranty expires. 

9. 
If there are multiple asset purchases, continue entering asset information in the next row.  

10. 
When you have finished entering asset information, click Save. 

Saving the A/P Invoice 

When entering the transaction information, save it as a draft or post it. The system validates 

transactions only when they are posted. For example, required departments or locations are not 

validated until posting. 

• 
Click Draft or Draft & new to save your progress on the transaction without affecting the 

subledger or G/L. Later, you or another user can review and post it. 

• 
Click Post or Post & new to post the transaction. 

After you save an A/P invoice that has an asset, the system creates an Asset record. You can 

access the asset’s record from the Periodic tasks section of the Accounts Payable menu. 

If an edit needs to be made on an asset and the asset was created on invoice entry, the asset 

must be edited from the asset record. You cannot make edits from the invoice. See Viewing and 

editing assets (on page 257).

### About Contracts
*Source: `RP Accounting AP Periodic Tasks User Guide.pdf`, Page 264*

Bids and Contracts 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Periodic Tasks User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

About Contracts 

A contract is an agreement between a vendor and your company. You can use contract records in 

RealPage Financial Suite as a repository for information about a job.  

In the Contracts list, you can find two kinds of contracts, offline and online. 

• 
An offline contract is one that is created in RealPage Financial Suite.  

• 
An online contract is one that is created in Vendor Marketplace’s Bids & Contracts. 

In addition to these two kinds of contracts, the Contracts list contains transactions associated 

with a contract, including subcontracts, purchase orders, and service contracts. 

• 
Service contracts are for recurring or scheduled services. 

• 
Purchase orders are for products or services that do not have a set monthly amount. 

• 
Subcontracts are for specific jobs that are defined in the Job Cost application. 

A contract record can be associated with only one of these transactions. 

If your company does not subscribe to the Spend Management application, then the Contracts list 

is for reference purposes only. You can create contract records, and you can view both online and 

offline contracts, but you will not be able to associate purchase orders, subcontracts, or service 

contracts with your contracts. 

Contract Setup 

• 
Before you begin creating contracts, create the various contract types that your company 

needs in the Contract Types list. 

• 
If you want the system to review contract documents and pull out key clause information for 

display, then set up the clauses and keywords to look for on the AI Configuration page. See 

Company > AI Configuration > AI Contract Screening. The purpose of this feature is to 

have the system read the text of a contract and extract the desired clauses from it, making 

the clause information more visible to users.  

Contract Usage Workflow 

• 
Create a service contract, subcontract, or purchase order. 

• 
When the vendor or contracted party sends an invoice to your company, create the invoice 

• 
Match the invoice with the service contract, subcontract, or purchase order. 

• 
When the contract is completed, pay the vendor. When this is a contract for a recurring 

service, create a recurring invoice (on page 112).  

---



### Contracts List
*Source: `RP Accounting AP Periodic Tasks User Guide.pdf`, Page 265*

Chapter 8: Bids and Contracts

Contracts List

> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > Contracts`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Spend Management > All > Periodic Tasks > Contracts`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Finance Agent > All > Contracts`


Use the Contracts list to view and manage contracts and their associated records.  

The Contracts list can include both of the following record types of contracts: 

• 
Online contracts: When the contract was created in the Bids and Contracts application, then 

the contract is an online contract. These types of records have a check mark in the Online 

column. 

• 
Offline contracts: When you create a contract in the RealPage Financial Suite (using either 

Spend Management or Accounts Payable), then the contract is an offline contract. 

From this list, you can: 

• 
Create a new contract.  

• 
Create a service contract from a contract. After creating a service contract from a contract, 

the Contracts list shows the transaction number and links it to the transaction.  

• 
Create a subcontract from a contract. After creating a subcontract from a contract, the 

Contracts list shows the transaction number and links it to the transaction.  

• 
Create a purchase order from a contract. After creating a purchase order from a contract, 

the Contracts list shows the transaction number and links it to the transaction.  

After creating one of these transactions, if you have the approval workflow turned on, the 
system submits the record for approval. 

• 
View a contract, subcontract, or purchase order from a contract that is associated with it. 

• 
Delete a contract. To delete a transaction that is associated with a contract, go to the Spend 

Management application.  

• 
Export the list of contracts.

AI Contract Screening 

If you want to use AI to scan an attached contract document for contract clauses, the clauses and 

their keywords must be set up in AI Configuration. You can set up clauses and their keywords in 

the AI Contract Screening section of the AI Configuration Powered by Lumina page. Go to 

Company > AI Configuration > AI Contract Screening. 

Adding Contracts 

There are two ways to add contracts to the system. You can: 

• 
Add a contract manually (on page 267) 

• 
Add a contract by importing 

Adding a Contract Manually 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > All > Bids & Contracts > 
 Contracts`


To add a contract record: 

1. 
Type a unique identifier for the contract in the Contract ID field. 

2. 
In the Vendor field, select the vendor to associate with the contract.  

3. 
In the Total Amount field, type the amount associated with the contract. This is a required 

field. 

4. 
In the Location field, select the location associated with the contract. The Location is a 

required field. 

5. 
In the Contracted party field, type the name of the individual, group or organization that is 

participating in the contract.  

6. 
In the Tax field, type the amount of tax on the contract. 

7. 
In the Contract type drop-down list, select the type of contract that you are creating. 

Contract types are customizable.  

8. 
In the Description field, type a description of the contract and its purpose. 

9. 
In the Shipping field, type the amount associated with shipping. 

10. 
In the Contract text field, type or paste the text of the contract. 

Filling In the Title Section 

1. 
In the Title field, type the title of the contract. This is a required field. 

2. 
In the Start date field, type the date that work starts against the contract. 

3. 
In the End date field, type the date that work associated with the contract ends. 

4. 
In the Awarded Bid ID field, type the unique identifier that is associated with the bid. 

5. 
In the Effective date field, type the date that the contract takes effect. 

---


<!-- Page 268 -->
Bids and Contracts 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Periodic Tasks User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

6. 
In the Approved date field, type the date that the contract is approved. 

7. 
In the Approved by field, type the name of the person who approved the contract. 

8. 
In the Executed by vendor on field, type the date that the vendor signed the contract.  

9. 
In the Contract reference number field, type the reference number from an external source 

associated with the contract. 

10. 
In the Executed on field, type the date that the contract was signed. 

11. 
In the Executed by date field, type the name of the person who executed the contract. 

12. 
In the Notes field, type any comments as needed. 

Attaching a Contract Document to the Record 

Use the Documents section to attach a file to the Contract record. For example, if you have the 

contract in a document file format, you can upload the file to attach it to the contract record. If 

you have a scanner attached to your system, you can use the device to scan in the pages so that 

the contract document is attached to the contract record. 

To upload a document from your computer: 

1. 
Click the Choose File button, and then click the file that you want to attach.  

2. 
Click the Attach button. 

If your company has configured the system to use AI contract screening, when you attach 
a file to a contract record, the system reads the contract and identifies key clauses, and 
then displays the key pieces of information so that users do not have to search for the 
information in the attachment. 

To use your scanner device to attach a contract: 

1. 
Type a name for the document that you plan to scan in.  

2. 
Click the Scan button. 

When you attach a document, whether uploaded or scanned in, the document shows in the 

Attachment list.  

Saving the Contract 

• 
Click the Draft button to save the contract and keep working on it. 

• 
Click the Save button to save your changes and close the page.

When you create a purchase order from a contract, the system completes some of the fields using 

information from the contract, such as Item Description, SKU, Qty, and Price. If taxes and 

shipping are defined in the contract, then they appear as separate line items in the Entries list. 

To create a purchase order associated with a contract: 

1. 
Select the Contracts option. 

2. 
Select the check box of the contract on which to base a new purchase order. 

3. 
Click the Create button, and then select Purchase order. 

4. 
In the Create type section, select the Purchase order option. 

5. 
Click the 
 Calendar button in the Date field, and then select the date of the purchase 

order. 

6. 
Click the 
 Calendar button in the Encumbrance date field, and then select the date of the 

encumbrance. 

7. 
Select a vendor from the Vendor drop-down list. 

If the vendor that you need is not available in the drop-down list, click the Add link and then 
add a new vendor record. 

8. 
Select the Use Company address for bill to check box if you want to use the vendor’s 

company address to send bills to. When you select this option, the Bill to field is not 

available. 

9. 
If you want to select a specific contact to send bills to, select the contact in the Bill to 

drop-down list. If the Bill to list is not available, then clear the Use Company address for bill 

to check box. 

10. 
In the Ship to drop-down list, select the contact record with the address where you want to 

ship goods or deliver services. 

11. 
Click the Saved items link if you want to view an offline shopping list of frequently used 

items for the vendor you entered on the purchase order. Select and apply items from this 

list to quickly populate them as line entries in the purchase order.  

---

RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Periodic Tasks User Guide 

When you access the Saved items list from the Purchase order information page, only the 
items that are saved for the vendor that you entered on the purchase order appear in the 
list. If you do not see the item(s) that you are looking for, you can add them to the list for 
the future.  

12. 
If this is a blanket purchase order, select the Blanket check box, and then select the 

appropriate option: 

• 
Blanket PO validated on item quantities 

• 
Blanket PO validated on dollar value only 

13. 
Click the Calendar button in the Expiry date field to select the date that the blanket 

purchase order expires. This option appears only when the Blanket option is selected. 

14. 
Select the Line entry type. If you implement the Job Cost application and this purchase 

order should be entered as a job cost, select the Job Cost option. Otherwise, select 

Standard. The system adjusts the entries list based on your selection. 

15. 
Type a description of the purchase in the Description field. 

16. 
Click the Spend control button to view the monthly and year-to-date available budget for 

the vendor and property on the purchase order. 

Using an Allocation Template 

1. 
Click the Apply template button if you want to apply an allocation template when adding a 

purchase order. The Apply template box opens. 

2. 
Select the allocation template to use from the Template drop-down list. This causes all 

line-item entries to inherit the defined allocation. 

If an allocation template is not listed, click Find to search for the template and apply it. 

3. 
Type an amount in the Amount field. 

4. 
Select the G/L account to use from the G/L account drop-down list. 

5. 
Click the Apply button. 

---


<!-- Page 272 -->
Bids and Contracts 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Periodic Tasks User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

6. 
Click the Save template button to add a new allocation template when adding a purchase 

order. The Save template box opens. 

7. 
Type a name for the new allocation template in the Name field. 

8. 
Optionally, type a description of the allocation template in the Description (optional) field. 

9. 
Select the type of allocation template to use from the Template Type drop-down list. 

10. 
Optionally, type any additional information you want to include in the Memo (optional) 

field. 

11. 
Click the Save button to save the new template. 

Finishing the Purchase Order 

1. 
Use the Attachments drop-down list to add an attachment. 

If you are using Firefox, Chrome, or Edge, then you can drag your files from the file explorer 

into the Attachments box. The file can either be on your computer or you can attach a file 

that has already been added to the system. 

Select an attachment from the drop-down list or click the Add link to upload a file from 

your computer. 

• 
Show all/Show unattached: This link changes the contents of the drop-down list 

between showing all files to showing unattached files. Unattached files are files that 

are not yet attached to any other record in the system. 

• 
Add: Click this link to open the Select attachments box where you can click the 

Choose files button to upload a file from your computer to the system. 

• 
View: You can view a document before attaching it. Click the document that you want 

to review, and then click the View link. 

• 
Find: Click this link to search the files that are stored in the system. 

2. 
Click the Show all columns link to ensure that all of the columns are displayed while you fill 

in the line entries list. 

3. 
To complete the line entry list: 

• 
For standard line entries, refer to Standard Line Entry list in Fields. 

• 
For job cost line entries, refer to Job Cost Line Entry list in Fields. 

4. 
In the SKU column, verify the information. 

---

RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Periodic Tasks User Guide 

• 
The default entry is SKU1 for the first line, SKU2 for the second line, and so on. You can 

replace this entry with a valid SKU to help auto-match invoices to purchase orders 

when processing invoices, but you cannot leave it blank. 

5. 
If this is a standard line entry type list, click the first field in the list to get the Show details 

tab to appear. 

6. 
Click the Show details tab to open the Details section where you can see the Dimensions 

and Segments fields for the line item. For more information, see the Fields (on page 297) 

topic for purchase orders. 

7.

entry row opens with the Dimensions and Segments fields open. Enter all information. 

• 
If there are no more line-item entries, the <<Previous row button is activated. Click 

this button to return to the previous line-item. 

• 
If there are more line-item entries, the Next row >> button is activated. Click this 

button to move to the next line-item. 

8. 
After entering the information, click the Hide details tab to close the Details section. 

9. 
Complete the Tax amount, Shipping amount, and Discount amount fields below the 

entries list if applicable, and then click the Distribute button. This distributes the amounts 

across each line item in the table. 

10.

Setting Up the Contract Expiration Alert 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > Ledger Sentry`


To set up the contract expiration notification: 

1. 
In the Company application, select the Ledger sentry option. 

2. 
In the Ledger sentry page, find the Alerts and notifications section. 

Click the 
 Add button to add a row for the new alert if needed. 

3. 
In the Rule item column, select If contracts are expiring in the next XX days. 

4. 
In the Criteria column, type the number of days before contract expiration to have the 

system notify the users. The contract expiration is based on the End date that you defined in 

the contract record.  

5. 
In the Notify column, select the contract expiration role that you set up. 

6. 
Click Save. 

Contract Information Page 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > All > Periodic Tasks > Bids and Contracts > 
Contracts > Add/Edit/View`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > Contracts > Add/Edit/View`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Spend Management > All > Periodic Tasks > Contracts > Add/Edit/View`


The content of the Contract information page varies depending on whether the record is a 

service contract, a subcontract, or a purchase order, and whether the contract is online (created in 

Bids and Contracts) or offline (created in RealPage Financial Suite). 

• 
The top section of a record contains information about the contract. 

• 
The Bids and contract attachments section lists the files attached to the contract record 

when the contract is an online contract. 

• 
The Create type section is where you select the type of record that you want to create and 

associate with the open record: a purchase order, service contract, or subcontract. 

• 
The (Date) section reflects the type of record that you chose in the Create type section, a 

service contract, subcontract, or purchase order. 

• 
The Documents or Attachment sections allow you to attach a file to the record. The 

Attachments section and drop-down list appears when you do not have scanning enabled. 

The Documents section appears when scanning is enabled. The scanner setting is available 

in My Preferences (on page 328).

If the AI contract screening feature is configured, whenever you attach a document to a 

contract record, the system reviews the document for clauses and keywords in the 

document, and then displays the clause information prominently in the contract record. 

• 
When you create a transaction, you can add items in a purchase order, or the job tasks in a 

service contract or subcontract. After you save the transaction, the list does not appear 

when viewing the contract. You must open the transaction to view the list of items. 

After you save the record, additional links appear on the record. The links vary depending on the 

record type and whether your system uses the approval workflow for service contracts, purchase 

orders, and subcontracts: 

• 
Subcontracts have a link to the parent contract in the Date section of the record. The 

Contract ID number is a link to the parent contract. 

• 
Records that traveled through the approval workflow have an Approval history link. Clicking 

the link opens the Approval history box so that you can review the record’s progress 

through the approval workflow. 

• 
Records that have been matched with A/P invoices have a Matched invoices link. Clicking 

the link opens the Matched invoices box where you can access the A/P invoice that is 

matched to the purchase order. 

When AI Contract Screening is enabled in your system, the Contract record has a Clauses 

tab where the system has extracted your clauses and keywords of interest.

• 
Click each field that has text to expand it so that you can read the text in its entirety.  

• 
You can also change the clause text on the Contract Information page as needed. 

Deleting a clause in the contract deletes all information in a contract that is tied to that 
clause.

Available Budget Page 

See How to Get Here (on page 303) for a list of ways to access this page. 

This page opens when you click the Spend control button on an A/P invoice, purchase order, or 

subcontract. 

The tabs on the Available budget page change depending on the Line entry type that you 

selected in the transaction:  

• 
Standard 

• 
Job Cost 

• 
Both 

Standard Line Items 

If you selected Standard as the Line entry type of an A/P invoice or purchase order, then the 

Available budget page includes three tabs, (Month, Year to date, and Current Year), that show 

the monthly, year-to-date, and current-year spending for a property and account. 

Use the Current year tab to view the full-year budget and current activity and compare it to the 

planned activity for the remainder of the year.

Job Cost Line Items 

If you selected Include Job cost as the Line entry type on an A/P invoice or purchase order—or if 

the transaction is a subcontract—then the Available budget page shows only job cost budget 

amounts. You can view the amount budgeted, the actual amount spent, and the budget 

remaining for the job cost code. 

Standard and Job Cost Line Items

view the available budget.

Adding a Contract Type 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > Setup > More > Contract Type`


To add a contract type: 

1. 
Open the Accounts Payable menu. 

2. 
Click the Setup tab of the menu. 

3. 
In the More section, click the 
 Add button next to Contract type. The Contract Type 

Information page opens. 

4. 
In the Contract type field, type the text that you want to appear in drop-down lists of 

contract types. 

5. 
In the Description field, type a description of the purpose or usage of the contract type. 

6. 
In the Status drop-down list, select Inactive to prevent the option from appearing in the 

Contract type drop-down list. Active is the default value. 

7. 
Click Save. 

Editing and Viewing a Contract Type 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > Setup > More > Contract Type`


To view the details of a contract type: 

1. 
Open the Accounts Payable menu, and then click the Setup tab of the menu. 

2. 
Click the Contract type option. The Contract Types list opens. 

3. 
Find the contract type that you want to view, and then click the View option. The Contract 

type Information page opens and shows the details. 

To edit the details of a contract type: 

1. 
Open the Accounts Payable menu, and then click the Setup tab of the menu. 

2. 
Click the Contract type option. The Contract Types list opens. 

3. 
Find the contract type that you want to change, and then click the Edit link. 

4. 
Make the desired changes and then click the Save button.

### Notifications for Expiring Contracts
*Source: `RP Accounting AP Periodic Tasks User Guide.pdf`, Page 313*



#### Before You Begin

RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Periodic Tasks User Guide 

Notifications for Expiring Contracts 

You can use the Ledger Sentry to have the system send emails to users when a contract is about 

to expire. 

To set up the alert, you need to: 

• 
Add a contract expiration role (on page 313) for the users who are to receive the contract 

expiration alerts. 

• 
Assign the role to the users you want to notify (on page 314). 

• 
Set up the alert (on page 282). 

Before You Begin 

Before you can have the system notify multiple people when a contract is about to expire, you 

must add a role and assign the new role to the people who you want to notify.  

• 
Adding a New Role (on page 313) 

• 
Assigning the Role (on page 314)  

Adding a Contract Expiration Notification Role 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > Setup > 
 Roles`


To add a role for the purpose of notifying users of an expiring contract: 

1. 
In the Name field, type a name that describes the purpose of this role. For example, you can 

call it “Contract Notification.” 

2. 
Click Save. 

3. 
Select the check box next to Accounts Payable. 

4. 
Click the Permissions link. 

5. 
Select all permissions that the users need to take action on an expiring contract, such as: 

• 
Contract permissions (on page 266): These permissions let you view and manage 

contract records. 

• 
Contract type permissions (on page 308): These permissions let you add and change 

contract types. 

• 
Contract Activity Report permissions: This permission lets you run the Contract Activity 

report. 

6. 
Save the permissions. 

7. 
Save the role. 

What’s Next? 

• 
Assigning the Contract Expiration Notification Role to Users (on page 314) 

---

Assigning the Contract Expiration Notification Role to Users

To assign the contract notification role to people who need to be aware of expiring contracts: 

To determine who gets notified:  

1. 
Open the Company menu, and then click the Setup tab. 

2. 
Click the Users option. The Users list opens. 

3. 
Click the Edit link of a user who needs to be notified when a contract is expiring.

*Source: `RP Accounting AP Periodic Tasks User Guide.pdf`, Page 315*

Setting Up the Contract Expiration Alert 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > Ledger Sentry`


To set up the contract expiration notification: 

1. 
In the Company application, select the Ledger sentry option. 

2. 
In the Ledger sentry page, find the Alerts and notifications section. 

Click the 
 Add button to add a row for the new alert if needed. 

3. 
In the Rule item column, select If contracts are expiring in the next XX days. 

4. 
In the Criteria column, type the number of days before contract expiration to have the

Click Save.

Payable and Spend Management.

### Invoice Processing Upload
*Source: `RP Accounting AP Periodic Tasks User Guide.pdf`, Page 318*



#### Uploading Invoice Processing Invoices
*Source: `RP Accounting AP Periodic Tasks User Guide.pdf`, Page 318*

Full Service 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Periodic Tasks User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Invoice Processing Upload 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable/Spend Management > All > Invoice Processing Upload`


Use the Invoice Processing Upload page to send invoices into RealPage Invoice Processing from 

your properties. After invoices are uploaded, the system processes them and adds them to your 

workbench. If there are any questions during processing, exceptions appear on the Invoice 

exception queue (on page 322) page. 

Uploading Invoice Processing Invoices 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable/Spend Management > All > Invoice Processing Upload`


For more information about importing a current or historical invoice, see Importing an A/P 

Invoice. 

To upload invoices: 

1. 
On the Invoice Processing Upload page, click the Upload link for the property from which 

you want to upload invoices. The OpsInvoice Image Inbox page opens. 

2. 
Click the New button. The Add Image File page opens. 

3. 
Click the Upload link next to the Image field, and then select the file you want to upload. 

Files must be in PDF format for the system to accept them. You can upload only one file, 
but it can contain multiple invoices. 

4. 
Type the number of invoices included in the file in the Invoice Count field. 

5. 
Type notes related to the invoices for processing in the Notes field. 

6. 
Click the Save button. The system uploads the file and adds it to the Invoice Processing 

Upload page with a status of Pending. 

---

#### Resolving an Exception Invoice
*Source: `RP Accounting AP Periodic Tasks User Guide.pdf`, Page 322*

Full Service 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Periodic Tasks User Guide

Invoice Exception Queue 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable/Spend Management > All > Invoice Exception Queue`


Use the Invoice Exception Queue page to resolve invoice processing issues submitted from the 

RealPage Invoice Processing team. Occasionally, the team requires clarifications on an invoice to 

process it accurately. When this occurs, the team notes the invoice as an exception and sends it to 

the Invoice Exception Queue with a Pending Review status. The 
 Invoice exception button near 

the top of the page appears with a number when there are invoices in the exception queue. 

See Resolving an Exception Invoice (on page 322) for more information on how to comment on 

the exception and send the invoice back to the team. 

Resolving an Exception Invoice 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable/Spend Management > All > Invoice Exception Queue`


When the RealPage Invoice Processing team sends an invoice to the Invoice Exception Queue, the 

 Invoice exception button near the top of the page appears with a number. 

To resolve an exception invoice: 

1. 
Click the 
 Invoice exception button. The Invoice exception queue page opens. 

2. 
Click the link in the Invoice OID field to open the invoice. 

3. 
Update the list of invoice comments and exceptions, and then send the invoice back to the 

team for final processing: 

• 
When you click the comment box, a list of the exception messages appears. You can 

enter part of the exception message to narrow the list, and then make a selection. 

• 
You can also type free-form text as an exception message. 

4. 
After you enter all exception messages that apply, click the Add Comment button. The 

messages are added to the area below the list of invoice exception messages. You see the 

date the message was added, the user ID of the person who added the message, the 

comment for the action, and the description of the message that was selected. 

5. 
Choose an action: 

• 
To save updates and return to the list of invoices, click the Save button. 

• 
If the invoice should be voided, click the Void button, and then click Void again to 

proceed with voiding the invoice. 

• 
If the invoice is ready to go to the team, click the Route to Pending QC button. The 

invoice no longer appears on the Invoice Exception Queue page.

How to Read Paths 

If you have ever been puzzled over a path in the documentation, this topic describes what it all 

means. 

Application Menus and Tabs 

Most paths begin with the Applications menu. This menu is located in the upper-left corner next 

to the Home button. When you select an application, the name of the Applications menu 

changes to the application that you selected. 

Menus have two tabs, All and Setup. The All tab is available to all users, but the Setup tab is 

restricted to users with full or limited administrator privileges. 

The Company application has two tabs, All and Setup. The All tab contains setup options for 
global features and is available to all users with the appropriate permissions. The Setup tab is 
restricted to administrators only. 

---


<!-- Page 339 -->
Chapter 11: Help and Support 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Periodic Tasks User Guide 

Simple Paths 

This is an example of a simple path: 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > General Ledger > All > Search & Find > Journal Entry`


The first three parts in a path are standard; they translate to “Click the Applications menu (a), 

select the name of the application (b), and then select the menu tab (c).” 

The next steps in the path—the menu section (d) and the menu option (e)—direct you to a 

specific list or page in the application. 

a) Click the Applications menu.  

b) Select the application. 

c) Select the menu tab. 

d) Find the menu section or subsection, if any. 

e) Click the menu option.  

If you see the 
 icon in a path, then you can click the  icon in front of the menu option to add 
a new blank record.

Paths with Multiple Options 

Some paths offer multiple choices. The choices are separated with a “/” symbol.  


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Receivable/Accounts Payable > Setup > Taxes > Authorities > 
View/Edit`


In this example, Accounts Receivable/Accounts Payable means that the same option is available 

in two applications’ menus, Accounts Payable and Accounts Receivable. Likewise, View/Edit 

means that you can select either the View or the Edit link to get to the page that you need.

Audit Trails 

Each action you take can impact your financial statements, so both internal and external 

stakeholders need to know how things have changed and who made those changes. The system 

audit trail keeps track of the changes so that you know who made changes to a particular record 

and when they made the changes. The View audit trail command is available on most records. 

Viewing Audit Trails 

You can access the audit trail of a record. The method of accessing the audit trail varies based on 

the record type. 

Accessing the Audit Trail  

1. 
Open the record that you want to examine. 

2. 
Click the More actions button, and then select the View audit trail option.  

Instead of the More Actions button, some records have a View Audit Trail button. 

The Audit trail list opens with a list of changes that users have made.  

Exporting a Record’s Audit Trail 

You can export data from the audit trail to a file in one of three formats, Microsoft Excel, CSV, or 

PDF. 

1. 
Open the audit trail. 

2. 
Click the audit trail’s More actions button, and then select the format to which you want to 

export: 

• 
Export to CSV 

• 
Export to Excel 

• 
Export to PDF 

If the audit trail table is lengthy, you can change the size of the list. From the More actions 
drop-down list, select Table size, and then select the number of rows that you want to be 
able to view. 

---

Importing Appendix 

In many places in the system, you can choose to import information instead of entering or editing 

each record manually. The following section shows how the import process works, what you need 

for importing information, and the best practices for importing successfully. 

A P P E N D I X A 

---



#### Importing Workflow
*Source: `RP Accounting AP Periodic Tasks User Guide.pdf`, Page 346*

Appendices 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Periodic Tasks User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Importing Workflow 

In many places in the system, you can choose to import information instead of entering or editing 

each record manually. 

To import information in Accounting systems: 

1. 
Download a template (on page 352). 

2. 
Enter your data (on page 353), and then save the file as a comma delimited (.csv) file (on 

page 357). 

3. 
Import the file into the system.  

4. 
As needed, resolve errors in the .csv file and re-import. 

As a best practice, before you import any objects, export the object list. This provides a “before” 
record in case you need to make post-import comparisons. 

Downloading Templates 

Most imports start with getting a template from the page that stores the objects you are 

importing. Typically, these are list pages. When you download these templates, they are tailored 

to your company, including specific dimensions and custom fields.  

As a best practice, always download a new template before entering your data, even if you have 
downloaded the template in the past. This ensures you are using the most current version of the 
template. 

To download an import template: 

1. 
Go to the page that lists the objects you are importing.  

2. 
Click the Template button in the upper-right corner of the page. 

• 
The system either downloads the file or prompts you to open or save the file, 

depending on your browser’s settings. 

• 
By default, this file uses the .xls file type. 

3. 
Open the file. 

Entering Data and Saving the File 

To enter your data: 

1. 
Open the template you downloaded from the object’s list page. 

2. 
Enter your information.  

While entering information, keep in mind to: 

• 
Use header descriptions in the template as a guide for entering information correctly. 

---


<!-- Page 347 -->
Appendix A: Appendices 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Periodic Tasks User Guide 

• 
Leave the template headers as they are. Any header changes will cause an import 

error. 

• 
Complete every required field. Any missing required information will cause an import 

error. 

• 
Avoid using leading zeros in ID fields where possible. If you must use leading zeros in 

IDs, convert the column of ID numbers to text format in Excel before importing the file 

content. You must do this every time you import information that requires IDs. 

3. 
When your changes are complete, use the Save as option to save the file as a comma 

delimited (.csv) file. 

Importing your Data 

1. 
On the page that stores the objects you are importing, click Import. The system opens the 

Import (object type) information box. 

2. 
Click Choose file, select the file you saved, and then click Open. 

3. 
By default, the Date format drop-down list value is “MM/DD/YYYY.” Use this drop-down list 

to select the date format used in the import file. 

This list is available for only some imports. 

4. 
By default, the File encoding drop-down list is set to “auto detect.”  

This setting should accommodate most imports, but you can change this as needed. 

5. 
If you are uploading a large file, select the Process offline check box. This allows the system 

to process the import file while you continue to work in the system. 

If you do not select this check box, you must wait until the upload process is complete. 

6. 
By default, the Email results to this address field is pre-filled to the email address of the 

person currently signed on.  

You can change this as needed. To enter multiple email addresses, enter each email address 

separated by a semicolon (;) or comma (,). 

---


<!-- Page 348 -->
Appendices 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Periodic Tasks User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

When the system completes the process, it sends a success or error email message to the 

entered Email results to this address email address(es). If the import had any errors, those 

errors are listed in this email message. 

7. 
Depending on the data you are importing, the Import (object type) information box might 

include additional fields, such as Date format or Post to. For more information about these 

additional fields, refer to the documentation for that specific import process. 

8. 
Click Import. 

The system processes the import and shows a success or error message, depending on the 

import results. 

9. 
Click Done. 

Resolving Errors 

There are a number of reasons imported records fail, such as duplicate entries or invalid field 

content. RealPage provides information about the failed records in an attempt to help you fix the 

import error. 

When an import fails: 

• 
The confirmation page shows how many records failed and provides a link to download a 

.csv file that contains only the failed records.  

If you close this box without downloading this file, you cannot re-access this file. 

• 
The system sends an email message to the email address provided on the Import 

information box. This email includes a list of the error(s) that occurred in the failed import, 

the error code, and each unique instance of the error. 

The error message email lists error messages in sections, with the sections listed in the order the 

records erred in the file. However, the error at the bottom of each section is the first error that 

was encountered for that record during import. 

As a best practice when reading the error message email, start at the top of the email, scroll to 

the first error message section, and then read the error message section from the bottom up. 

Repeat this process for each error section. 

---


<!-- Page 349 -->
Appendix A: Appendices 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Periodic Tasks User Guide 

The example below shows a sample error message.  

================================================== 

Error BL01001973  

================================================== 

BL01001973-1 Description: Duplicate account number. The account number 
‘4150’ already exists. 

BL01001973-1 Correction: Enter unique account number.  

BL01001973-2 Description: Unable to create record. Could not create GL 
Account record!  

================================================== 

• 
In this example, start at error “BL01001973-2 Description: Unable to create record. Could not 

create G/L Account record!”  

• 
As this error does not identify the root issue, look to the next error “BL01001973-1 

Correction: Enter unique account number.” This identifies why the G/L account wasn’t 

created, but hasn’t identified how to correct the issue.  

• 
The final error message, “BL01001973-1 Description: Duplicate account number. The 

account number ‘4150’ already exists” describes the issue in more detail and suggests a 

correction – find and replace the duplicate account number. 

Error codes, such as BL01001973 above, are internal codes. These internal codes might help 

RealPage locate the source of a systemic issue if one is identified.

not see the option in the menu, then ask your System Administrator to check your permissions. 

Permissions

Application

You must also have specific permissions for the type of object that you are importing. For 

example, if you are importing customer data, then you must have permissions to list, view, add, 

and edit customer data. For more information about the specific permissions that you need to 

complete an import, refer to the documentation for that specific object type. 

If your user account doesn’t have the permissions shown above, then ask your System

Downloading Import Templates 

Each object has a unique template that you must use for importing data. There are three ways 

you can find a template for your object type: 

• 
Download the template directly from a list. 

• 
Use the Download template link in the Import box. 

• 
Download the template from the Import data page. 

Downloading directly from a list 

• 
In some lists, such as the Working budgets list, the list has a Template button that you can 

click to download the template that you need. 

Downloading from an Import box 

• 
In other lists that have an Import button, click the Import button to open the Import box, 

where a Download template link appears next to the Choose File button. 

Downloading from the Import Data Page 

If you don’t find a download button in the list or a link in the Import box, then you can download 

the template file from the Import data page. See Download a Template from the Import Data 

Page (on page 352). 

---



#### Downloading a Template from the Import Data Page
*Source: `RP Accounting AP Periodic Tasks User Guide.pdf`, Page 352*

Appendices 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Periodic Tasks User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Downloading a Template from the Import Data Page 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > Import Data`


We recommend downloading a new blank template from the Import data page whenever you 

import information into the system. This is important because:  

• 
Templates are automatically customized based on your company configuration, including 

dimensions and custom fields you created.  

• 
Templates can be updated at any time, especially when a new version of RealPage 

Accounting is released. This means that an older template might not work.  

To download a template:  

1. 
Open the Company menu. 

2. 
Select Import data. The Import data page lists the information that you can import.  

3. 
Find the type of data that you want to import.  

4. 
Click the Template link to download the template. You can find the file in your browser’s 

default download location.  

A prompt opens at the bottom of the web page, asking if you want to Open, Save, or 

Cancel. 

• 
Open: Opens the file in Excel. 

• 
Save: Saves the file to your browser’s default download folder. 

• 
Save as: Saves the file under a new name and in a different location. 

• 
Save and Open: Saves the file to your local computer, and then opens the file in Excel. 

5. 
Click Save. 

Save the template to your computer, and then continue downloading templates as needed until 

you have downloaded all of the templates for data that you want to import. 

If you have a database administrator (DBA) of your other system, give the downloaded templates 

to your DBA. Ask the DBA to: 

• 
Export the data from your other system, as specified in the import template spreadsheets. 

• 
Put the applicable data into each spreadsheet. 

• 
Save the spreadsheet as a comma-delimited file (CSV). 

If you do not have a DBA, or if your DBA does not have time to complete the whole task, you can 

complete the tasks. Refer to the following topics for guidance on creating importable data.
