Filling In an Import Template with Data 

Perform the following steps for each item that you want to import: 

1. 
Open the template in Excel and review the data structure. The information in the template 

file can help you formulate extraction queries. 

2. 
Export the data from your other source. 

3. 
Copy the exported data into the template file for the same kind of object. Take care to 

exactly match the template’s data structure as you do this. 

Avoid using leading zeros in ID fields. If you must use leading zeros in IDs, convert the 
column of ID numbers to text format in Excel before importing the file content. Excel does 
not remove the leading zeros when you save the file. Remember to do this every time you 
use a template to import information that requires IDs. 

4. 
Fill in the required columns. 

5. 
Save the file in CSV format (on page 357). 

Now that you’ve entered your data and looked through it for any of the common issues imports 

can have, you are ready to import your file to your system.  

About CSV Templates 

There are some things you should know about the CSV templates and how they behave before 

adding your data. 

Removing All Commas from Your CSV File 

RealPage recommends removing all commas from your CSV file. 

A CSV file is a Comma Separated Values file (also sometimes known as a comma delimited file). If 

there are commas in the data of your file (for example, if your numbers are formatted like 10,000 

or if you use commas between words in a field), your data will be shifted one column over 

because that is how the file is intended to work. This will either cause errors in the information or 

cause the whole import to fail. 

RealPage recommends you do not keep your actual data in a CSV file. Instead, use an Excel 
workbook to take advantage of the formatting options of Excel. When you’re ready, export your 
data as a CSV file for import into RealPage Accounting. In this way, your data is formatted 
correctly for import, but you also have Excel functionality in your workbook. 

Column Order 

You can change the order of the columns as you see fit, as long as the information in the header 

cell doesn’t change. 

---


<!-- Page 354 -->
Appendices 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Periodic Tasks User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Do not rename or otherwise change the headers in your templates. If you change the headers, 
your import will fail. 

However, some templates require information to be imported in a specific order. For example, 

transaction data should not be imported before information about the transactions has been 

imported. Header columns containing information about the entire import need to stay to the left 

of detail columns (columns that contain the details of an account, transaction, vendor, etc.). 

RealPage recommends reviewing the column order of the original template before moving 

columns around. 

Adding Additional Columns 

If you need to keep other related information in your template document, you can add your own 

columns for this information. If you add your own columns, use a # (hashtag) symbol before the 

name of any column you add. Examples: 

#BudgetNotes 

#ClientInfo 

If by chance you use a name already in use by the system, the # (hashtag) will make sure that the 

information in your columns is not imported by accident. 

You can also use the # (hashtag) to write notes to yourself in your template. If you place the # 

(hashtag) at the start of a row, the whole row of information is ignored during import. 

You can create rows of notes by starting the row with # in the first column. 

Hiding Columns for Easy Data Entry 

When editing your file in Excel, you can hide columns you won’t be using for data entry. 

Be sure to enter required information in your file. Hiding required columns and not entering 
required information will cause your import to fail. 

Data Must Conform to the Business Logic of RealPage 

For example, the Budget ID field on the Budget Information page allows a 20-character ID to be 

entered. It follows then that the Budget import template would have the same limitation: if you 

try to import a Budget ID with more than 20 characters in your CSV file, your import fails. 

How data should be formatted is found in the header description row, under the header row. 

You can also see a field-by-field description for your specific template in this help. 

Go to Importing Data, find the template you want to know more about, and click the 

corresponding link. 

---


<!-- Page 355 -->
Appendix A: Appendices 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Periodic Tasks User Guide 

Blank Fields Overwrite Existing Data 

A blank value in a cell is considered to be the desired value (a blank) for the field referenced by 

the column heading for the record being imported. 

In almost all cases, a blank field will overwrite existing data in RealPage to also be blank. 

Say you had the existing value 111 Elm St. as the address for a customer and you import a blank 

for this field. If you go to the normal user interface and examine the contents of that field, you will 

see that the original value 111 Elm St. is replaced by nothing, and the field is blank. 

This is not true, however, for these templates: 

• 
Update Vendor 1099 Transactions 

• 
Update Vendor 1099 Opening Balances 

If the value is blank in certain fields, the import does not overwrite the existing value. To remove 

the existing value in these few cases, enter the value NULL. These cases are clearly identified in 

their header descriptions. 

Budgets are an exception. Budgets can be appended with new dates, with new lines not 
previously budgeted, or they can be overwritten if same date/account combinations are used. 

Calculated Field Values 

If you used a formula to come to a value in a field, you can leave the result in place as long as you 

match the RealPage field value for decimals. 

Accounting Application Page Help 

In most cases, there is an exact match between the application pages (and the business logic with 

which they behave) and the data that you import. This includes the constraints on that data and 

any dependencies that may exist between the data in the import file and other data in the system, 

or other data that you also import. 

After you have added all of your data, you save the Excel spreadsheet as a CSV file. 

Debits and Credits Must Balance 

When importing a file that includes debits and credits, your debits and credits must balance. 

RealPage adheres to accepted accounting rules, which require debits and credits to balance. 

Likewise, if you require accounts to balance by location, then when you import location balances 

using a CSV template, the location debits and credits must also balance. 

Duplicating Records 

If an identical record already exists in the system, the import for that record typically fails because 

RealPage detects that the record exists and does not allow duplicates. 

---


<!-- Page 356 -->
Appendices 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Periodic Tasks User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Duplicates are not allowed in account numbers, departments, locations, employees, customers, 

and vendors. Although you can have duplicate transactions, the transaction summary name must 

be unique per application. 

Journal entries are an exception. The system does not check for duplicate journal entries, so 
when importing journal entries, be sure to check that they have a unique ID or name.

Line Numbers 

See the Line number examples (on page 357) page for more information on how to use lines 

numbers in your CSV imports. 

Special Characters 

UTF-8 is supported in imported files, so character accents and other special characters are 

imported correctly. 

RealPage recommends that you remove commas from all numbers and do not use commas in any 

text fields. 

CSV Data Exported from Non-Excel Software 

When exporting data from other applications, the other software might use a non-standard 

approach to quoting, which could cause problems when importing into the system. 

As noted above, RealPage recommends removing all commas from text fields in a CSV file. 

However, there could be times in which removing the commas is not the ideal solution. In this 

case, CSV files do allow quotes around a value that contains a comma, and the system accepts 

this in an import. For example: 

1,2,3, “All, with exceptions” 

There may also be instances when you need to include a quote mark inside a statement with a 

comma. In this case, you would use a second set of quote marks, as follows: 

1,2,3, “All, with “inventory” exceptions”

Saving the Template as a CSV File 

In Excel: 

1. 
Click File, and then select Save As. 

2. 
Click Browse and select where you want to save the file. 

3. 
In File name, type a name that represents the data that the template contains. 

4. 
In Save as type, select CSV (Comma delimited) (*.csv). 

5. 
Click the Save button. 

Some transactions have Import buttons on their lists so that you can import the transactions 
without having to leave the list. You can use this method whenever you have already downloaded 
the template that you need, filled it with the appropriate data, and saved the file in CSV format. 

Line Number Examples 

When you import information into RealPage Accounting that uses line numbers, such as journal 

entries, invoices, or adjustments, use the following tips to ensure that your line numbers import 

correctly. 

Journal Entry Line Numbers 

When importing general ledger journal entries (including statistical journal entries), the number of 

the line item in the CSV file defines the order in which those lines are imported. There are a few 

things you can do when entering journal entry information into the CSV file that will make 

reconciliation of the journal entries easier after import: 

• 
Group debits and corresponding credits together 

• 
Enter information in the CSV template as if you were entering it in a regular journal (group 

information in a reasonable manner) 

In the G/L journal entry example below, LINE_NO 1 and 2 are entries for legal and professional 

fees and are accounted for in the DEBIT column. The corresponding CREDIT for Accounts Payable 

in line 3 equals the fees; debits match the credits. 

---


<!-- Page 358 -->
Appendices 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Periodic Tasks User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

In line 4, a DEBIT is entered for another legal fee, with the corresponding CREDIT in line 5. Again, 

debits match the credits. 

In this example, line items in the LINE_NO start at 1 and proceed sequentially. This example also 

groups related debits and credits together, so that reconciliation is easier. The LINE_NO column 

determines the order in which the line items are imported into the system and how they will 

appear in your journal entry. RealPage recommends entering information in the CSV file as if you 

are entering it in a real journal entry. This way, when you revisit the journal entry after import, 

your entries make sense. 

Exchange Rates in Journal Entries 

When uploading G/L journal entries, the exchange rate is not required. However, if you want to 

use your own exchange rate, you must add the exchange rate to the journal entry line. The journal 

entry line number is referenced by the system. Enter journal entry line numbers as described in 

Journal entry line numbers. Line numbers are important to ensure proper line-header consistency. 

If you don’t enter a line number, or enter line numbers out of sequence, the import will fail. 

If you want to use the exchange rate provided by RealPage, leave the exchange rate column blank 

in the CSV file.

Multiple Journal Entry, Invoice, or Adjustment Line Numbers 

When you enter multiple journal entries, invoices, or adjustments, you must start the line number 

count over at 1. 

When you enter a single journal entry, invoice, or adjustment into a CSV file, you start the 

LINE_NO column at one for the line entries and continue sequentially. Below is an example of a 

single invoice entered in a CSV file. 

Figure 1: An example of an invoice, with sequential line numbers. 

a) Total Due column 

b) The AMOUNT column adds up to the TOTAL_DUE. 

c) The line numbers start at 1 and continue in sequential order. 

When you enter multiple journal entries, invoices, or adjustments into a CSV file, there are several 

things you can do to ensure your information imports correctly into the system: 

• 
Group information in a reasonable manner. 

• 
When importing invoices, make sure that the AMOUNT column and the TOTAL_DUE column 

have the same amount for each entry. 

• 
LINE_NO refers to the line item number, so when entering formation into the CSV file, start 

the LINE_NO at 1, and then list each following line item in sequential order. 

In the example below, you can see the first line item entry of a customer invoice has been marked 

as line 1 in the LINE_NO column. This invoice has line items entered in sequential order, and the 

AMOUNT column for the first invoice (in orange) and the TOTAL_DUE column equal the same 

amount. 

The second invoice (in pink) has line items that also start at 1 and continue in sequential order. 

This invoice also has the TOTAL_DUE and the AMOUNT columns equaling the same amount. 

These concepts apply to journal entries and adjustments as well: when more than one journal, 

invoice, or adjustment is added to a CSV file, you must restart the line number (LINE_NO) count at 

1 for the line items to be imported correctly. 

---

When adding data for multiple line numbers in the same template file, be sure to start the line 
numbers over at one, as shown in the following image.

If your journals, invoices, or adjustments have line items and you do not enter a line number in the 
LINE_NO column, or enter line numbers out of sequence, the import will fail.

Use Row Numbers to Find Errors 

When importing A/P invoices or A/R invoices using a CSV file, if errors are found during upload, 

the entire CSV file is rejected. You can find the errors in the file if you use row numbers in the Do 

Not Import column. If your CSV file is rejected because errors are found, the error file contains the 

original row number, allowing you to quickly pinpoint where to make changes. 

a) Number the rows in the “Do not import” column. 

b) Error file contains original row numbers.

*Source: `RP Accounting AP Periodic Tasks User Guide.pdf`, Page 363*

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Periodic Tasks User Guide 

Best Practices for Preparing Data for Import 

Follow these best practices to prepare your data. 

• 
Download a template from the Import data page. 

Always use the latest template, especially following a product release. 

Use the correct template for the data object that you want to import. 

• 
Use the column descriptions as a guide to enter information. 

Do not change the titles in the header row. 

The header titles correlate to fields in the system. Incorrect header titles may cause an 

upload error. When you download a template from the Import data page, the correct 

headers are in the template. 

Read the header descriptions in the template. 

The header description is the cell under the header row that explains the type of 

information to include in each column. If you enter information in the wrong format, or with 

an incorrect accepted value, it may cause an error in your import. 

Enter required information. 

Read the description field to determine which information is required. If you do not enter 

the required information, your import may fail. 

• 
Save the data as a comma-separated value, or CSV, file. When saving from Excel, choose the 

comma delimited file (.csv) type. 

The file has the file extension .csv after you save it. 

• 
Leave the file open until your import is successful. Excel can sometimes reformat the file if 

you close it before the import is successful.

#### Loan Schedule Data
*Source: `RP Accounting AP Periodic Tasks User Guide.pdf`, Page 384*

Appendices 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Periodic Tasks User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Loan Schedule Data 

Below are the columns in the Loan schedule template: 

• 
LOAN_ID 

• 
PAYMENT_NO 

• 
INVOICE_NO 

• 
CREATED_DATE 

• 
GL_DATE 

• 
DUE_DATE 

• 
PRINCIPAL 

• 
INTEREST 

• 
ESCROW 

• 
OTHER_1 

• 
OTHER_2 

• 
OTHER_3 

• 
OTHER_4 

• 
OTHER_5 

• 
OTHER_6 

• 
OTHER_7 

• 
STATUS 

To understand the import process, it’s important to understand the columns in the loan schedule 

template. Below is an explanation of available columns and the impact they have in the automatic 

A/P invoice creation process. 

LOAN_ID: 
This is the unique identifier of the loan. The system uses the ID to link 

the payment to the loan. 

Required: Yes 

PAYMENT_NO 
The value must be unique for each loan payment. 

Four characters maximum 

Required: Yes 

---


<!-- Page 385 -->
Appendix B: A/P Data Structures Appendix 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Periodic Tasks User Guide 

BILL_NO 
The system uses this value to populate the Invoice number field on 

the system-created A/P invoice. If the BILL_NO is blank, the system 

automatically creates an invoice number upon creating the 

system-created A/P invoice. The system-generated invoice number is 

created in the following format: <Payment number - Loan number>. 

Optional.  

30 characters maximum. 

CREATED_DATE 
The scheduler uses this value to determine if the system should create 

an A/P invoice or not. The scheduler creates A/P invoices for payments 

containing a CREATED_DATE less than or equal to the current date. It 

also uses this value to populate the Date field on the A/P invoice. 

Required: Yes 

GL_DATE 
The system uses this value to populate the G/L posting date field on 

the system created A/P invoice.  

If your system does not have the G/L posting date field enabled, the 
GL_DATE in the loan schedule template should equal the 
CREATED_DATE. 

Required: Yes 

DUE_DATE 
The system uses this value to populate the Due date field on the 

system-created A/P invoice. 

Required: Yes 

PRINCIPAL 
The system uses this value to populate the principal line item on the 

system-created A/P invoice. 

Required: Yes 

INTEREST 

ESCROW 

OTHER 1-7 

The system uses these values to populate the Amount fields on the 

line items for the system-created A/P invoice.  

You must, at a minimum, have a G/L account for the desired line items 
if you are importing amounts for their corresponding columns. 

Required: No 

---



#### Bank Reconciliation Data
*Source: `RP Accounting AP Periodic Tasks User Guide.pdf`, Page 386*

Appendices 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Periodic Tasks User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

STATUS 
The scheduler uses this value to determine if the system should create 

an A/P invoice or not. Applicable statuses include: 

• 
Historical: The system does not create A/P invoices for 

payments with a Historical status. These payments appear on 

the Loan schedule list only. 

• 
Pending: The system creates A/P invoices for payments with a 

Pending status on the CREATED_DATE specified for the 

payment. 

Required: Yes

### Accounts Payable Setup Workflow
*Source: `RP Accounting AP Setup User Guide.pdf`, Page 14*

General Configuration 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Setup User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Accounts Payable Setup Workflow 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > Setup > Configuration`


To configure Accounts Payable, follow these general steps: 

1. 
Select the Configuration option and enable the desired functions. 

2. 
Restart the RealPage Accounting system to allow it to reset with the functionality you 

selected. 

3. 
Configure the rest of Accounts payable: 

From the Configure Accounts Payable page: 

• 
Accounting settings in A/P 

• 
Thresholds in A/P 

• 
Enable functionality in A/P 

• 
Document dashboard queues 

• 
Screen settings in A/P 

• 
1099’s 

• 
Set up dimensions in A/P 

• 
Set up document sequencing for A/P 

• 
Set defaults for the payment method and bank account 

• 
Enable the system to use inline credits and apply them to A/P invoices. 

• 
Enable A/P payment approvals 

• 
Enable vendor approvals 

• 
Set payment priorities 

• 
A/P aging 

• 
Tax and shipping 

Refer to other sections to configure specific features such as fees, terms, loan types, A/P account 

labels, and A/P allocations. 

A/P allocations and approval policies are set up at the top level.

### Configure Accounts Payable Page
*Source: `RP Accounting AP Setup User Guide.pdf`, Page 15*

Chapter 1: General Configuration 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Setup User Guide 

Configure Accounts Payable Page 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > Setup > Configuration`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > Setup > Subscriptions > Applications > Configure (Accounts 
Payable)`


Use the Configure accounts payable page to configure Accounts Payable functions. This page is 

composed of around 13 sections, depending on the features that your company has chosen to 

enable. 

• 
Accounting settings: Use this section to select journals, G/L accounts, and summary 

frequencies to use with Accounts payable. Refer to Configuring A/P accounting settings (on 

page 7). 

• 
Thresholds: Use this section to select desired system responses to events. Refer to 

Configuring A/P thresholds (on page 10).  

• 
Enable functionality: Use this section to select optional functionality. Refer to Enabling A/P 

functionality (on page 12). 

• 
Document dashboard queues: Use this section to set up document queues that appear on 

dashboards. Refer to Configuring document dashboard queues (on page 20). 

• 
Screen settings: Use this section to set up G/L posting date preferences. Refer to 

Configuring A/P screen settings (on page 19). 

• 
1099s: Use this section to determine how the system handles 1099-related transactions. See 

Configuring 1099 A/P settings (on page 21). 

• 
Dimensions setup: Use this section to select the dimensions you want to use in the system. 

Refer to Configuring A/P dimensions (on page 22). 

• 
Document sequencing: Use this section to allow the system to number selected 

transactions automatically and to select the numbering sequence for each transaction type. 

Refer to Configuring A/P document sequencing (on page 23). 

• 
Pay A/P invoices defaults: Use this section to configure the default payment method, 

default bank account, and default currency. Refer to Configuring Pay A/P invoices defaults 

(on page 25). 

• 
Credits: Use this section to allow the system to apply an inline credit in an A/P invoice to an 

A/P invoice automatically. Refer to Enabling automatic inline credit application (on page 27). 

You can send payments through an approval process before being issued. Payment 
approvals are located in the Approval workbench in the Company application. For 
information on configuring A/P payment approvals, see the Filling In the A/P Payments 
section in Configuring Transaction Approvals. 

• 
Vendor approval settings: Use this section to configure the vendor approval workflow. 

Refer to Configuring vendor approval settings (on page 27).

#### Configuring A/P Accounting Settings
*Source: `RP Accounting AP Setup User Guide.pdf`, Page 17*

Chapter 1: General Configuration 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Setup User Guide 

Configuring A/P Accounting Settings 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > Setup > Configuration > Accounting Settings`


In the Accounting settings section, you can set up default journals, G/L liability accounts, and 

summary frequencies. 

• 
Journals: Records A/P invoice, adjustment, and payment transactions  

• 
G/L accounts: Posts transactions, such as accounts payable, penalties, and more 

• 
Summary frequencies: Determines how often the system posts A/P invoices, adjustments, 

manual payments, and payment summaries to the G/L 

If you enabled multi-book accounting, you can select the default journals to be used for accrual 
books and cash books. 

To configure A/P accounting settings: 

1. 
Open the Accounts payable menu, and then select the Setup tab. 

2. 
Select Configuration. 

3. 
Locate the Accounting settings section. 

Filling In the Journals Section 

In the Journals subsection, select the default journals. The system uses these journals for 

automatically recording the following transactions: 

1. 
In the Payments drop-down list, select the journal to use for payment transactions. 

2. 
In the Loan invoices and journals drop-down list, select the journal to use for loan invoices.  

Filling In the Accrual Basis Reporting Subsection 

This section appears only when your system uses the accrual method of accounting. 

1. 
In the A/P invoices drop-down list, select the journal to use for A/P invoices.  

2. 
In the Adjustments drop-down list, select the journal to use for accrual A/P adjustments. 

Filling In the Cash Basis Reporting Subsection 

This section appears only when your system uses the cash method of accounting. 

1. 
In the A/P invoices drop-down list, select the journal to use for A/P invoices. 

2. 
In the Adjustments drop-down list, select the journal to use for cash adjustments. 

---


<!-- Page 18 -->
General Configuration 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Setup User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Filling In the G/L Accounts Section 

In the G/L Accounts subsection, select the General Ledger accounts that you want the system to 

use for posting the following Accounts Payable transactions: 

1. 
In the Accounts payable drop-down list, select the standard account to use for offsetting 

transactions. 

In general, you configure G/L accounts at the top level. One exception is that you can 
specify different default A/P accounts for each entity at the entity level. For more 
information, see Specifying Different Default Accounts By Property . 

2. 
In the Discounts drop-down list, select the account to use based on payment terms. 

3. 
In the Penalties drop-down list, select the account to use based on payment terms. 

4. 
In the Vendor advances drop-down list, select the account to use for vendor advances. This 

can be changed on a transaction basis. 

5. 
In the Multi-currency gain and loss drop-down list, select the account for currency 

conversion. This option appears only when your company uses multiple currencies. 

Filling In the Summary Frequency Section 

In the Summary frequency subsection, select how often the system creates and processes A/P 

transactions: 

1. 
In the A/P invoices and in the Adjustments drop-down lists, select the desired summary 

frequency: 

• 
Daily: The system creates a daily summary and posts it to the G/L for each transaction 

day. Daily is recommended because it gives you the most granular reporting. 

• 
Monthly: The system creates a single summary at the end of each month and no 

matter what the transaction date is within that period, it will always be posted as of the 

last day of that month. This frequency doesn’t provide the daily granular level of 

reporting. 

• 
One per A/P invoice, One per A/P invoice adjustment: The system creates and posts a 

summary for each A/P invoice or adjustment. Per-transaction summaries can increase 

system performance, particularly if your transactions result in a large number of 

journal entries with unique G/L account and dimension combinations.  

• 
User Specified. The system only uses manually created summaries. It continues to use 

the manual summary until you select or create another. 

2. 
In the Manual payments drop-down list, select the desired summary frequency for creating 

and processing manual payments: 

---


<!-- Page 19 -->

RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Setup User Guide 

• 
Daily: The system creates a daily summary and posts it to the G/L for each transaction

In the Payments drop-down list, select the desired summary frequency for creating and

payment method.

Configuring A/P Thresholds 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > Setup > Configuration > Thresholds`


Use the Thresholds section to configure how the system responds when these events occur:  

• 
When posting in the future 

• 
When a credit limit is exceeded 

• 
When the vendor is on hold 

You can also set up system alerts and controls for additional actions in the system. For more 

information, refer to Ledger Sentry in online help or download (on page 360) the RealPage 

To set up A/P thresholds: 

1. 
Open the Accounts payable menu, and then click the Setup tab. 

2. 
Select the Configuration option. 

3. 
Locate the Thresholds section. 

You can set thresholds for events so that if an event occurs, the system responds as desired.

4. 
In the If posting in future period section, select the system response if a user attempts to set 

a future period date as the General Ledger posting date. 

• 
Warn: Displays a warning message, but allows the user to proceed. 

• 
Don’t allow transactions to be created: Displays a message requesting the user to 

select a date within the current period. 

• 
Do nothing: The user can proceed with the transaction without any alert or action on 

the part of the system. 

Do nothing is the default. 

The subledgers share the same posting periods as the general ledger. 

5. 
In the If credit limit is exceeded section, select the desired system response to an attempt to 

enter an invoice that exceeds the credit limit with a vendor. 

• 
Warn: Displays a warning message, but allows the user to proceed. 

• 
Don’t allow transactions to be created: Displays a message showing the total due for 

the vendor and your set credit limit. The transaction can’t be created as entered. 

• 
Do nothing: The user can proceed with the transaction without any alert or action on 

the part of the system. 

Do nothing is the default. 

6. 
In the If vendor is on hold section, select the desired system response to an attempt to enter 

an A/P invoice from a vendor with an On Hold status: 

• 
Warn: Displays a warning message, but allows the user to proceed. 

• 
Don’t allow transactions to be created: Displays a message that the vendor is 

currently on hold. The transaction can’t be created. 

• 
Do nothing: The user can proceed with the transaction without any alert or action on 

the part of the system.

Don’t allow transactions to be created is the default.

Click the Save button or continue to Enabling A/P Functionality (on page 12).

#### Enabling A/P Functionality
*Source: `RP Accounting AP Setup User Guide.pdf`, Page 22*

General Configuration 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Setup User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Enabling A/P Functionality 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > Setup > Configuration > Enable Functionality`


Use the Enable Functionality section to enable or disable Accounts Payable features. 

This topic describes how to customize the way your company uses Accounts Payable features.  

To customize Accounts Payable functionality: 

1. 
Open the Accounts payable menu. 

2. 
Click the Setup tab of the menu. 

3. 
Select the Configuration option. 

4. 
Find the Enable functionality section. 

5. 
Selecting the Enable accounts payable G/L account override in invoice and adjustment 

entry option enables you to override the default G/L account as you create a transaction. 

You can override: 

• 
An entire A/P invoice or adjustment 

• 
One or more specific line-items in an A/P invoice or adjustment 

• 
All transactions involving a specific vendor 

To use this feature, you must also flag the override accounts and grant permissions. See 

Flagging an account as an override account (on page 17). 

6. 
Select the Enable account labels check box if you want to require the use of account labels. 

Account labels provide restricted access to G/L accounts, and a means of textually naming 

them. Using account labels, you can: 

• 
Associate an account number with an intuitive name that is easy to recognize and 

select from a drop-down list. 

• 
Categorize different products, expenses, and services. 

• 
Restrict access to only G/L accounts that have labels. 

See Adding A/P account labels (on page 81). 

7. 
Select the Enable allocation in invoice entry check box to enable transaction allocations. 

When enabled, the Allocation field appears in the Invoice entries section during invoice 

creation, allowing users to select an allocation template that defines how the system is to 

distribute amounts automatically. See A/P allocations (on page 90). 

8. 
Select the Enable assets in invoice entry check box to allow users to add information about 

assets when entering an invoice. Clear the check box to prevent users from entering asset 

information in invoices.  

---


<!-- Page 23 -->
Chapter 1: General Configuration 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Setup User Guide 

9. 
Select the Enable asset integration with Facilities check box to integrate asset records with 

Facilities. Additional options appear. 

• 
In the Default Asset G/L Account drop-down list, select the G/L account to associate 

with asset transactions that are created in the Facilities application. 

• 
In the Default Dispose Gain/Loss Account drop-down list, select the account to use 

for recording asset disposals.  

• 
In the Error failure results to field, type the email address where you want the system 

to send notifications of asset integration failures.  

10. 
Select the Enable invoice entry control validation check box to have the system notify you 

when the total of the line items does not equal the total of the overall A/P invoice. The 

system message helpfully displays the amount left to distribute.  

11. 
To allow the company to consolidate payment requests from multiple users in order to 

create one check to a vendor, select the Enable merge payments added to the outbox 

across all users check box. 

12. 
To allow users to select a specific bank account from which to draw funds to pay the invoice, 

select the Enable bank account selection in A/P invoice check box.  

After enabling the bank account selection function, it cannot be disabled. The option still 
appears on the page, but it cannot be changed.  

13. 
Select the Do not allow duplicate vendor tax ID check box to have the system check to 

ensure that a vendor record that you are adding does not already exist. If you enter a 

duplicate ID, the system allows you to perform a search to find the vendor record with the 

tax ID you are entering. 

Filling In the Enable Independent Release and Processing of Payments for Line Items in 
the Same A/P Invoice Section 

1. 
In the Release to pay section, select the desired option to enable independent release and 

processing of payment for line items in the same A/P invoice: 

• 
Select Don’t enable to show all line items. 

• 
Select Enable and show all, including items yet to be released for payment. 

• 
Select Enable and show only items released for payment. 

The ability to release only specific line items of an A/P invoice for payment gives you tighter 

control over your cash outflows. Pay only certain line items of an invoice, and pay others as 

you want. The invoice remains partially paid in the system until every line item has been 

paid. This is especially helpful for companies that have multiple entities – for example, if one 

entity has funds available to make a payment but another entity does not. For example, if 

you enter a multi-line invoice that has some items due immediately and others due in 30 

days, use this feature to release for payment only those items that are due immediately. 

Then return to this invoice in a month and release for payment the line items that were due 

---


<!-- Page 24 -->
General Configuration 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Setup User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

in 30 days. This gives you greater control over your cash outflows and ensures that only 

those items you are ready to pay are selected for payment. 

2. 
Select the Enable reclassification for invoices and adjustments check box to enable users 

to edit accounting information on both partially and fully paid A/P invoices and 

adjustments. The users must also have the Reclassify permission for A/P invoices and 

adjustments, depending on the type of transaction that you want to be able to reclassify. 

See Before you begin. 

3. 
Select the Enable reversal of unpaid invoices check box as needed.  

A/P invoices can be reversed, but after being enabled for reversal, they can’t be deleted. 
Selecting Enable reversal of unpaid A/P invoices changes the following pages:  
- Accounts Payable: A/P invoices replaces Delete with Reverse. 
- Permissions: A/P invoices makes Delete a read-only selection. 

4. 
Select the Enable creating, editing, and deleting foreign currency invoices check box to 

allow the system to handle foreign currencies in your A/P invoice entry process. 

Even after you enable multi-currency transactions on the Configure general ledger page, 
you must enable multi-currency in the applicable individual applications. This gives you the 
option to configure your company so that users can make multi-currency transactions in 
Accounts Payable but not Accounts Receivable, and so forth. 

5. 
Select the Payment dates must be greater than their invoices dates check box to enforce a 

rule that the payment date must be on or after the A/P invoice date. 

6. 
Select the Payment dates must be greater than their G/L posting dates check box to 

enforce a rule that the payment date must be on or after the G/L posting date. 

7. 
Select the Post charges to Leasing & Rents when Utility reimbursement payments are 

made check box to have the system post a charge to OneSite Leasing & Rents when you 

make a utility reimbursement payment. The system will create a UTILCKGVN charge within 

Leasing & Rents. 

8. 
Select the Do not automatically load all records on Pay A/P Invoices check box to prevent 

the Pay A/P invoices page from loading all A/P invoices. When selected, users must apply a 

filter to load A/P invoices. Clear the check box to have the Pay A/P Invoices page load all 

A/P invoices. 

9. 
Select the Show holdbacks in Pay A/P invoices check box when you want to include 

holdbacks in the list of A/P invoices to be paid on the Pay A/P invoices page. Clear the 

check box to prevent holdbacks from appearing. Holdbacks represent funds that are held 

back so that the company has the funds to pay its expenses. Holdbacks are used to calculate 

a location’s available cash.

10. 
Select the Bypass vendor site restrictions on external invoices check box to exempt 

external invoices from vendor restrictions. External invoices include eInvoices which come 

from OpsTechnology/Storefront and oInvoices come from Invoice Processing. Invoices that 

you manually import are not considered external invoices. 

11. 
Select the Advance posting date when subledger is closed check box to allow users to 

make end-of-month payments even if the Accounts Payable subledger is closed. The system 

automatically advances any A/P transactions (invoices, payments, advances, or adjustments) 

to the first of the next month if the books are already closed for the period you’re posting 

them to. 

This setting applies to A/P invoices from expense reports, management fees, intercompany 
bills, or petty cash cards. 

12. 
Select the Enable export of AP Invoices check box to allow the transfer of A/P invoices to 

an external accounting system. 

13. 
Select the Enable merging of payment requests check box to have the system merge 

payment requests when making payments to the same vendor. 

Filling In the Management Fees Section 

1. 
Select the Enable Fees check box to use the system’s fee management feature. Additional 

configuration is required. For configuration information, see Management fees (Legacy). For 

feature usage information, see Management fees workbench. 

2. 
Select the Auto receive A/R invoice (of default company) on A/P invoice payment check 

box, as needed. When fees are paid, the system automatically creates a matching A/R 

invoice. 

3. 
In the Undeposited funds account drop-down list, select the account to which the system 

should add the funds from collected management fees.  

The system only applies funds to this account when the A/P invoices are fully paid. 

4. 
Select the Bank check box to enable the system to deposit the management fees directly 

into the default bank account of the entity instead of into the Undeposited Funds account. If 

an entity does not have a default bank account defined, then the system deposits the 

management fees into the Undeposited Funds account. 

5. 
Click the Save button to save your changes.

#### Flagging an Account as an Override Account
*Source: `RP Accounting AP Setup User Guide.pdf`, Page 27*

Chapter 1: General Configuration 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Setup User Guide 

Flagging an Account as an Override Account 

Flagging an override account is a two-step process. 

1. 
Flag the account as a Payables or Receivables account. 

2. 
Grant permissions. 

Flagging the Account as Payables or Receivables 

1. 
Open the General Ledger menu. 

2. 
Find the desired account and click the Edit link. 

3. 
In the G/L Account alternative drop-down list, select Payables account or Receivables 

account as appropriate. 

The system adds the account to the filtered list of override accounts that you can select 

from in specific pages, such as transaction pages, and vendor and customer pages. 

Payables account: The system adds the account to the filtered list of A/P G/L accounts 

available as override accounts in A/P invoice, adjustment, and vendor pages. 

Receivables account: The system adds the account to the filtered list of A/R G/L accounts 

available as override accounts in A/R invoice, adjustment, and customer pages. 

Granting Permissions 

Grant permissions to selected users to override the default G/L account in A/P invoice and 

adjustment transactions, and for A/P invoice or adjustment transactions involving specific 

vendors.

Bypassing Vendor Restrictions for External Invoices 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > Setup > Configuration > Enable Functionality > 
Bypass Vendor Site Restrictions On External Invoices`


You can have the system bypass vendor restrictions on external invoices, eInvoices, and oInvoices. 

1. 
Open the Accounts Payable menu, and then select the Setup tab of the menu. 

2. 
Click Configuration. 

3. 
On the Configure Accounts Payable page, find the Enable functionality section.

Configuring A/P Document Sequencing 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > Setup > Configuration > Document Sequencing`


In the RealPage Financial Suite, document sequences refer to the system’s automatic numbering 

feature used to assign unique identifiers to new records. This helps ensure consistency and avoids 

duplication. 

Automatic numbering, also known as document sequencing, is available only in select features in 

RealPage Accounting. These features use pre-defined numbering plans to assign sequential 

identifiers—typically when creating new records or transactions. 

If you prefer to number a transaction type manually, do not assign a document sequence for the 

transaction type. 

Before You Begin 

You must create a new document numbering scheme before you see it as an option in this 

section. 

• 
Configure a document sequence for the desired record type in Company > All > Settings > 

Document Numbering. 

Assigning Document Sequences 

In Accounts payable, you select the configured document sequence that you want to use for each 

eligible transaction type: 

• 
A/P credit adjustments 

• 
A/P debit adjustments 

• 
Vendor records 

• 
Transfer payments 

After a document sequence is configured and assigned, the system automatically assigns a 

sequential ID to each new transaction or record, ensuring a smooth and consistent flow of unique 

identifiers.

Open the Accounts payable menu, and then click the Setup tab. 

2. 
Select Configuration. The Configure accounts payable page opens.

### Configuring AI Invoice Approvals
*Source: `RP Accounting AP Setup User Guide.pdf`, Page 45*

Chapter 1: General Configuration 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Setup User Guide 

Configuring AI Invoice Approvals 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > Setup > Configuration > AI Invoice Approvals`


Use the AI invoice approval feature to let the system automatically review and approve A/P 

invoices. When you submit a new invoice, the system calculates a confidence percentage for the 

invoice. For an A/P invoice to be approved, it must pass the confidence percentage (AI match) 

that is above a specific threshold and must fall below a specified dollar amount. 

To set up AI Invoice approvals feature for use, you configure the match threshold and the dollar 

amount.  

To configure AI approvals for A/P invoices: 

1. 
Open the Accounts Payable menu. 

2. 
Select the Setup tab of the menu. 

3. 
Select the Configuration menu option.  

4. 
Find the AI invoice approvals section. 

5. 
Set the criteria for the system to use to calculate the confidence percentage for an invoice. 

• 
For XX number of days, type the number of days to use in the calculation. 

• 
For Count of invoices posted within XX days, type the number of invoices that the 

vendor needs to have submitted within the time period. 

• 
For Total invoice amount variance percent, type the variance percentage that the new 

invoice must fall within when compared to the average of previous invoices. 

6. 
Select the Calculate check box to have the system calculate the AI Match confidence level 

for new invoices.  

Any invoices submitted before this option is enabled will not have an AI match percentage. 

When you submit a new invoice, the system calculates a confidence percentage for the 

invoice. Each time the invoice is approved in the approval workflow, it recalculates the 

confidence level as a percentage. The calculation works as follows: 

---


<!-- Page 46 -->
General Configuration 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Setup User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

• 
If the number of invoices within the last XX days equals or exceeds the number 

defined, then the system assigns 50% to the match level. If the number of invoices 

within the last XX days is less than the number defined, then the system assigns 25% 

to the match level. 

• 
If the invoice is within the invoice variance amount, then the system assigns 25% to 

the match level. 

• 
If a purchase order (PO) is matched to the invoice, then the system assigns 25% to the 

match level. 

The default criteria for AI invoice approvals is 90 days, three invoices, and 10% variance. 

7. 
Optionally, select the Auto approve check box to enable automatic approvals based on 

specific thresholds: 

• 
In the first field, type the percent threshold required to auto-approve invoices. For 

example, 90 means the invoice must have at least a 90% AI match percentage. 

• 
In the second field, type the amount threshold required to auto-approve invoices. For 

example, 350 means the invoice amount must be equal to or below $350.00. 

The Auto approve check box appears only if your company subscribes to the Finance Agent. 

You can set up alerts and notifications based on thresholds to notify a group of people in 

your organization when invoices are submitted that cross that threshold. The system 

provides several predefined roles and criteria by default. You can add or edit rules as 

needed to adjust them. 

8. 
Click Save. 

---

Document Sequencing Section 

You can enter IDs for certain transaction and record types manually as you create them, or you 

can have the system add the IDs for you based on a preset plan. 

With a preset ID plan, your company automatically generates new IDs or numbers for the related 

transactions and records. For example, you can create a document sequence plan for vendors that 

automatically creates a new vendor ID, such as “VEND-0100” and increments the number each 

time a new vendor is created. 

This Document sequencing section enables you to do the following: 

• 
Select a preset ID plan on specific transactions and records. 

• 
Set a warning on duplicate IDs if manual entry is used. 

• 
Require IDs on certain types of transactions and documents (A/P and A/R only). 

If you don’t select a document numbering sequence for a particular type of transaction or record, 

users will be required to enter an ID or number at the time that they create the new transaction or 

record. 

In addition to saving users time, auto numbering ensures that users cannot use an ID twice or 
skip a number altogether.

Calculate 
Select this check box to have the system calculate the AI Match 

confidence level for new invoices.  

Any invoices submitted before this option is enabled will not have an AI 

match percentage. 

When you submit a new invoice, the system calculates a confidence 

percentage for the invoice. Each time the invoice is approved in the 

approval workflow, it recalculates the confidence level as a percentage. 

The calculation works as follows: 

• 
If the number of invoices within the last XX days equals or 

exceeds the number defined, then the system assigns 50% to 

the match level. If the number of invoices within the last XX days 

is less than the number defined, then the system assigns 25% to 

the match level. 

• 
If the invoice is within the invoice variance amount, then the 

system assigns 25% to the match level. 

• 
If a purchase order (PO) is matched to the invoice, then the 

system assigns 25% to the match level.

### Configuring AI Invoice Approvals
*Source: `RP Accounting AP Setup User Guide.pdf`, Page 64*

Configuring the AI Features in Accounts Payable 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Setup User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Configuring AI Invoice Approvals 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > Setup > Configuration > AI Invoice Approvals`


Use the AI invoice approval feature to let the system automatically review and approve A/P 

invoices. When you submit a new invoice, the system calculates a confidence percentage for the 

invoice. For an A/P invoice to be approved, it must pass the confidence percentage (AI match) 

that is above a specific threshold and must fall below a specified dollar amount. 

To set up AI Invoice approvals feature for use, you configure the match threshold and the dollar 

amount.  

To configure AI approvals for A/P invoices: 

1. 
Open the Accounts Payable menu. 

2. 
Select the Setup tab of the menu. 

3. 
Select the Configuration menu option.  

4. 
Find the AI invoice approvals section. 

5. 
Set the criteria for the system to use to calculate the confidence percentage for an invoice. 

• 
For XX number of days, type the number of days to use in the calculation. 

• 
For Count of invoices posted within XX days, type the number of invoices that the 

vendor needs to have submitted within the time period. 

• 
For Total invoice amount variance percent, type the variance percentage that the new 

invoice must fall within when compared to the average of previous invoices. 

6. 
Select the Calculate check box to have the system calculate the AI Match confidence level 

for new invoices.  

Any invoices submitted before this option is enabled will not have an AI match percentage. 

When you submit a new invoice, the system calculates a confidence percentage for the 

invoice. Each time the invoice is approved in the approval workflow, it recalculates the 

confidence level as a percentage. The calculation works as follows: 

---


<!-- Page 65 -->
Chapter 2: Configuring the AI Features in Accounts Payable 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Setup User Guide 

• 
If the number of invoices within the last XX days equals or exceeds the number 

defined, then the system assigns 50% to the match level. If the number of invoices 

within the last XX days is less than the number defined, then the system assigns 25% 

to the match level. 

• 
If the invoice is within the invoice variance amount, then the system assigns 25% to 

the match level. 

• 
If a purchase order (PO) is matched to the invoice, then the system assigns 25% to the 

match level. 

The default criteria for AI invoice approvals are 90 days, three invoices, and 10% variance. 

7. 
Optionally, select the Auto approve check box to enable automatic approvals based on 

specific thresholds: 

• 
In the first field, type the percent threshold required to auto-approve invoices. For 

example, 90 means the invoice must have at least a 90% AI match percentage. 

• 
In the second field, type the amount threshold required to auto-approve invoices. For 

example, 350 means the invoice amount must be equal to or below $350.00. 

The Auto approve check box appears only if your company subscribes to the Finance Agent. 

You can set up alerts and notifications based on thresholds to notify a group of people in 

your organization when invoices are submitted that cross that threshold. The system 

provides several predefined roles and criteria by default. You can add or edit rules as 

needed to adjust them. 

8. 
Click Save.

### AI Invoice Scanning
*Source: `RP Accounting AP Setup User Guide.pdf`, Page 66*



#### Configuring AI-Invoice Scanning
*Source: `RP Accounting AP Setup User Guide.pdf`, Page 66*

Configuring the AI Features in Accounts Payable 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Setup User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

AI Invoice Scanning 

You can enable the AI Invoice Scanning feature which allows the system to read in an A/P invoice 

and create a new A/P invoice record from it. 

Configuring AI-Invoice Scanning 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > AI Configuration > AI-Invoice Scanning`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Finance Agent > Setup > AI Configuration > AI-Invoice Scanning`


Your company must either subscribe to the Finance Agent application, or you can contact 

RealPage to have the AI-Invoice scanning feature enabled. After enabling the feature, you can 

configure the scanning feature. 

To configure AI-Invoice scanning: 

1. 
Open the Company menu, and then click the AI Configuration option.

The expense report approval process uses the approval infrastructure of RealPage Accounting. 

Clients are not required to create approval policies and approval workflows because the expense 

reports feature comes with an approval policy and workflow.  

Some additional configuration is required. Follow these steps to set up the system to use the 

expense report approval process: 

1. 
Edit the User record of each user who will be reviewing expense reports as accounting 

reviewers, and assign them the role of Expense Report Accounting Reviewer (on page 62).  

2. 
For users who will be submitting expense reports: 

•

vendor record for an employee (on page 63).

fields. 

3. 
Fill in the expense reports configuration page. See Configuring expense reports (on page

### Understanding the Expense Reports Approval Process
*Source: `RP Accounting AP Setup User Guide.pdf`, Page 71*

Chapter 3: Expense Report Configuration 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Setup User Guide 

Understanding the Expense Reports Approval Process 

The expense report approval process uses the approval infrastructure of RealPage Accounting, 

but the expense report feature includes a built-in approval policy and workflow for its approvals. 

Creating an approval policy or workflow for expense reports is not necessary. 

Two Levels of Approvals 

There two levels of approvals.  

1. 
Review and approval by the user’s manager. 

2. 
Review and approval by people assigned to the Expense report accounting reviewer role.  

The use of the Expense report accounting reviewer is optional. Your company may choose 
not to enable the Accounting reviewer role for expense reports. 

The Expense Report Reimbursement Process 

1. 
When someone submits an expense report, the system uses the built-in Reports To 

approval policy. The policy routes the expense report to the user’s manager for approval.  

2. 
When the manager approves an expense report, the system routes it to an Expense report 

accounting reviewer. 

When an expense report passes all approvals, the system creates A/P invoices. It creates one 

invoice for each reimbursement type (employee, property, or P-Card vendor) in the expense 

report. 

3. 
Your team pays the A/P invoices that reimburse the employee, property, or P-Card vendor.

### Configuring Full Service Syncing and Invoice Defaults
*Source: `RP Accounting AP Setup User Guide.pdf`, Page 84*

Full Service Configuration 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Setup User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Configuring Full Service Syncing and Invoice Defaults 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > Setup > Full Service`


You can configure how to synchronize objects between the RealPage Financial Suite and 

OpsInvoice Processing. If you want to synchronize the systems quickly, you can choose to sync 

only properties or only vendors to save time.  

Changing Sync Defaults  

You can make changes that affect synced invoices as you sync the two systems. 

1. 
Open the Accounts Payable menu. 

2. 
Click the Setup tab of the menu. 

3. 
Click Full Service. 

4. 
In the Invoices section, in the Default G/L account drop-down list, select the G/L account to 

associate with invoices when the invoice does not have an assigned G/L account. 

5. 
In the Default Approver if no workflow is assigned for oInvoice drop-down list, select the 

user or role who you want to evaluate oInvoices when the system does not have an 

approval workflow configured to handle oInvoices. 

To synchronize: 

1. 
To synchronize properties between systems, click the Sync Properties button. The system 

initiates the sync process. 

2. 
To synchronize vendors between systems, click the Sync vendors button. The system 

initiates the sync process. 

3. 
To upload the property-vendor relationships to OpsInvoice Processing, click the Upload 

Relations to OPs button. 

4. 
To synchronize everything and save your changes, click the Sync button.  

---



### Configure Full Service For Spend Management Page
*Source: `RP Accounting AP Setup User Guide.pdf`, Page 85*

Chapter 4: Full Service Configuration 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Setup User Guide 

Configure Full Service For Spend Management Page 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > Setup > Full Service`


Use this page to synchronize properties and vendors with OpsInvoice Processing so that RealPage 

Accounting can exchange oInvoices. 

This page is composed of two sections: 

• 
Sync: Use this section to determine when the systems were last synced, and use the buttons 

to initiate a partial sync of properties, vendors, or relationships between vendors and 

properties. 

• 
Invoices: Use this section to determine how the system handles oInvoices that come from 

OpsInvoice Processing. 

How It Works 

While RealPage Accounting runs daily jobs to sync the two systems, on occasion, users may need 

to sync the vendor, the property, or the property-vendor relationships if you edit the vendor or 

property record or if you select the buttons to sync each option. 

The system runs a sync every three hours to import new oInvoices. 

This page offers three buttons that allow you to sync partial information. Click a button to sync 

properties, vendors, or the property-vendor relationships. 

• 
Sync properties 

• 
Sync vendors 

• 
Upload relations to OPs 

The three sync buttons allow you to sync what you need, when you need it. For example, if you 

just added a new vendor to a property, you need to sync the vendors, and then sync the 

property-vendor relationships. 

When you perform a partial sync, the system syncs the selected information (properties, vendors, 

or the property-vendor relationships). If there have been no changes since the last sync, the 

system does nothing. 

When you click the Sync button, the system saves any changes and syncs everything. 

---

A/P Account Labels Overview 

Account labels provide more precise, common-language naming of accounts for end users. An 

example of an account label might be “Benefits - Health.” Accounts payable account labels are 

available if you have account labels enabled in Accounts Payable.  

RealPage Accounting offers account labels for both Accounts Receivable and Accounts Payable. 

A/P Account Labels can be linked to 1099 forms and categories. After creating and saving an A/P 

account label, when you open the account label for editing, a link to Form 1099 appears. 

In Multi-entity companies: 
Accounts payable account labels are a master object. Master objects can either be accessible 
to all entities, or exclusive to a specific entity. 

Before You Begin

not see the option in the menu, then ask your System Administrator to check your permissions.

### Allocation Templates Overview
*Source: `RP Accounting AP Setup User Guide.pdf`, Page 100*



#### Before You Begin
*Source: `RP Accounting AP Setup User Guide.pdf`, Page 100*

A/P Allocation Templates 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Setup User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Allocation Templates Overview 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > Setup > Templates`


Allocations are either dynamic allocations or transaction-based dimensions. An allocation splits a 

cost across multiple properties. The template stores the allocation rules: the list of properties that 

are splitting the allocation and how much each property is to pay. 

When you create an A/P invoice or journal entry and apply an allocation to it, the system 

automatically divides the amount based on the way you defined it in the allocation template. 

For example, if a company distributes rental revenues across five sales offices, the allocation 

assigns a value of 20% each to sales office. When you choose this allocation in a transaction, for 

example, an invoice, 20% of that invoice is automatically owed to each sales office. 

Before You Begin 

Access can vary depending on your organization’s subscriptions and your permissions. If you do 

not see the option in the menu, then ask your System Administrator to check your permissions. 

The user must have Administrator privileges to add and edit A/P allocations. 

Permissions 

These permissions are required to add new A/P allocations. 

Application 
Activity 
Permissions 

Company 
Transaction allocations 
List, View, Add, Edit, Delete 

If your user account doesn’t have the permissions shown above, then ask your System 

Administrator for assistance. If you have administrator privileges, you can assign permissions for a 

new feature (on page 290) to a user or to a role. See Roles and Permissions (on page 290) for a 

description of how to review a user’s permissions. 

Dependencies 

• 
You must be at the top level to create A/P allocation templates. 

Recommendations 

You can create effective A/P allocation templates using location groups. Start by creating the 

location group (on page 91), and then set up the A/P allocation template. 

---



#### Adding a Location Group
*Source: `RP Accounting AP Setup User Guide.pdf`, Page 101*

Adding a Location Group 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Reports > Dimension Groups > 
 Location`


To add a location group: 

1. 
Open the Reports menu. 

2. 
In the Dimension groups section, click the 
 Add button next to Location.  

The Location group information page opens. 

3. 
In the Location group ID field, type a unique identifier for the group. 

When displayed elsewhere in the system, the location group will be listed with the ID and 
name together (ID--Name), as in NAOPS--North America Operations. IDs can’t be changed 
after you’ve saved the group, but you can edit the name at a later time. 

4. 
In the Name field, type a descriptive name for the group that other users will understand. 

This is the text that appears in Location, Property, and Entity/Entity group drop-down lists 

throughout the system. 

5. 
In the Description field, type a brief description of what this group includes or how it’s used. 

6. 
In the Location group contact drop-down list, select the user who is responsible for this 

location group. This information is only for your benefit; the system does not use this 

information anywhere else. 

7. 
In the Group type drop-down list, select the type of group you want to create: 

• 
All members: Select this option if you want to filter which locations are included in the 

group based on the criteria of your choice. For example, you might define a “US 

Locations” group which includes all members but then filters the results to only 

locations in the United States. 

• 
Specific members: Select this option if you want to choose specific locations to 

include in the group. 

Tip: To include all active members of a group (such as all customers), select All 

members as the group type. Then, in the Filters section, set the Field to “Status, ” 
the Operator to “equals,” and the Value to “Active.” See Determining What’s in the 
Dimension Group for more information. 

8. 
If you set the Group type to “All members,” then three additional fields appear: 

• 
In the Sort order drop-down list, select whether you want to sort the members of the 

location group in ascending or descending order. 

• 
In the Sort field drop-down list, select the field by which you want to sort the 

members of the location group. 

---


<!-- Page 102 -->
A/P Allocation Templates 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Setup User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

• 
In the Max matches field, type the maximum number of locations to include in the 

group. Leave this field blank to include all matching members. 

9. 
Select the Dimension structure check box to create a dimension structure from the location 

group. 

Creating a dimension structure from a group enables you to add the group to the rows or 
columns of a financial report. If you don’t select this check box, then the group can be used 
only for filtering reports. 

In a multi-entity environment, how do I select entity-specific members? 

If you’re creating a dimension group at the top level, then you can’t include members that 
belong to an entity. Try creating the dimension group from the entity itself. 

10. 
If you are a user with administrative privileges and you are creating a location group, then 

you have the option to make the location group public or private. If you are not an 

administrative user, then any location group that you create will automatically be private. 

See Making a Location Group Public or Private for more information. 

Fill In the Members Section 

This section appears only if you selected “Specific members” from the Group type drop-down list. 

1. 
Click the first blank row of the Members list and select the first location to add to the group. 

2. 
Continue adding locations to the group by selecting the next blank row. 

To add more rows to the list, click 
 Add. 
To delete extraneous rows, click 
 Delete. 

Set Up Filter Conditions 

Use this section to set up filters for the location group. With filters, you can: 

• 
Create field/value tests that will determine which locations are included in the group. 

• 
Create an expression with conditions that determine members of the group. 

To set up filters: 

1. 
In the Field drop-down list, select the field that you want to use for a condition’s test. 

2. 
In the Operator drop-down list, select the comparison operator. 

3. 
In the Value drop-down list, type the value to compare. 

---


<!-- Page 103 -->
Chapter 6: A/P Allocation Templates 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Setup User Guide 

4. 
Continue adding rows to the list as needed, especially if you are building conditions for an 

expression: 

• 
Click 
 Add to add another row.  

• 
Click 
 Delete to delete a row. 

Because an expression uses the row numbers in the Filters list, you must write the 
expression last. 

5. 
In the Filter conditions field, select the logic that the system should use when filtering 

locations: 

• 
All (AND): All tests must result in a True state to include a member in the group. 

• 
Any (OR): At least one test must result in a True state to include a member in the 

group. 

• 
Expression: Select to type a Boolean expression in the Condition box below it. 

For example, say you’ve defined three field/value tests in the Filters list: 

• 
Country is the US 

• 
Base currency is USD. 

• 
Location Contact Name starts with “Ed.” 

In this case, you can set filter conditions as follows: 

• 
Select All (AND) to include a location only when all of these tests are true. 

• 
Select OR to include any location in which at least one of these tests is true. 

• 
Select Expression if you want to set up a more complex combination. When you select 

Expression, type the condition logic in the Condition field that appears below. Use the 

row numbers of the Filters list in the expression.

Example of a Condition 

You want the system to find properties with an amount between $150 and $999. 

Each row is a condition. 

Row 1: 

Field = Status 

Operator = equals 

Value = Active 

Row 2:  

Field = First tax month 

Operator = equals 

Value = January 

Expression Examples 

(1 AND 2) OR (2 AND 3) 

If the first two expressions both evaluate to true OR if the second and third expressions both 

evaluate to true, then the location is included in the group.  

(1 AND 3) OR 2 

If the first and third conditions both evaluate to true or the second condition evaluates to true, 

then the location is included in the group.

#### Adding A/P Allocation Templates
*Source: `RP Accounting AP Setup User Guide.pdf`, Page 106*

A/P Allocation Templates 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Setup User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Adding A/P Allocation Templates 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > Setup > 
 Templates`


A/P allocation templates allow you to tell the system how to distribute costs amongst properties 

when applied to an A/P Invoice entry. A/P allocation template provides the ability to enter line 

items on A/P invoices faster using preset lists of properties (property groups). 

To add an A/P allocation template: 

1. 
Open the Accounts payable menu, and then select the Setup tab. 

2. 
Select the 
 Add next to Templates. The Templates page opens. 

3. 
In Name, type a name for the allocation template. 

Suppose you have four offices, and you divide rental income proportionately to square 
footage, but you divide interest income equally. You create an allocation for each set of 
allocation types. Your IDs might be RENT and INTEREST along with corresponding 
descriptions. 

4. 
In the Description field, type a description for the allocation to help users identify which 

allocation to use. 

5. 
In the Template type drop-down list, select Percent or Amount. 

Percent: Select this type to allocate a percentage of the A/P invoice to multiple properties. 

Amount: Select this type to allocate a specific amount to multiple properties. 

6. 
In the Memo field, type a memo that describes this allocation.  

7. 
In the Status drop-down list, select Active to allow users to select this allocation template. 

Select Inactive to prevent users from being able to select this allocation template. It will not 

appear in selection lists. 

Select Inactive to hide unused items. When set to Inactive, the system retains the data 
but hides the inactive item on lists, drop-down lists, and so on. If you want to permanently 
remove an allocation template, you must delete it. 

If you selected Percent, the Template list contains these columns: Property, Account, 

Department, and Percent. 

If you selected Amount, the list contains these columns: Property, Account, Department, 

and Amount. 

---


<!-- Page 107 -->
Chapter 6: A/P Allocation Templates 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Setup User Guide 

Filling In the Template List 

You can specify an individual property or select a group of properties.  

To specify an individual property: 

1. 
Select a property from the drop-down list. 

2. 
Specify the account. 

3. 
Select a Department. 

4. 
Type the percentage or amount for each property.  

5. 
Continue selecting individual properties as needed, and then click the Save button. 

Specifying a Group of Properties 

Use the Create from Property Group drop-down list to fill the list with properties from an existing 

Property group.  

To specify a group of properties: 

1. 
Select a property group from the Create from property group drop-down list. 

2. 
Click the Apply button. 

When you select a property group that has a Percent template type, the system evenly 

distributes 100 percent of the costs to the properties in the list. 

When you select Amount, you must manually type the amount to charge each property. 

The user can override the percentage or amount in the A/P invoice.

Copy the data from the current record to a new record of the same type. 

This button appears when editing an existing template record. 

Print to 
Generate a PDF file of the terms so that you can print it or download the 

terms information in XML format. 

This button appears when editing an existing template record. 

Cancel 
Close the record without saving the changes. 

More actions > View 

audit trail 

Review the log of changes to the record, which includes who made each 

change and when the change was made. 

More actions > Save 

and New 

Save this record and create another one. 

This button appears when creating a new template record.

### Management Fee Configuration Process

#### Before You Begin
*Source: `RP Accounting AP Setup User Guide.pdf`, Page 114*

Management Fees Configuration 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Setup User Guide

Management Fee Configuration Process 

Follow these steps to configure the management fees feature: 

1. 
Enable fees 


> **Navigation Path:** `Accounts Payable > Setup > Configuration > Enable Functionality > Enable Fees`


See Enabling the Fees Feature (on page 106). 

2. 
Add permissions for fees 


> **Navigation Path:** `Company > Users > Subscriptions > Accounts Payable > Fees`


See Enabling Permissions for the Fees Feature (on page 107). 

3. 
Add a fee (on page 108)  


> **Navigation Path:** `Accounts Payable > Setup > Fee Template`


See Adding a Fee Template (on page 108). 

4. 
Associate your entity with a customer record and a vendor record.  

Company > All > Entities > Edit > Additional Information.  

Ensure that your entities are associated with a customer record and vendor record. Without 

these associations, your fee will fail when generated.  

See Associating a Vendor and Customer With an Entity (on page 107). 

Before You Begin 

Access can vary depending on your organization’s subscriptions and your permissions. If you do 

not see the option in the menu, then ask your System Administrator to check your permissions. 

The user must have limited or full Administrator privileges to create fee templates. 

Permissions 

These permissions are required to create fee templates: 

Application 
Activity 
Permissions 

Accounts payable 
Fees 
List, View, Add, Edit, Delete 

If your user account doesn’t have the permissions shown above, then ask your System 

Administrator for assistance. If you have administrator privileges, you can assign permissions for a 

new feature (on page 290) to a user or to a role. See Roles and Permissions (on page 290) for a 

description of how to review a user’s permissions. 

Dependencies 

• 
You must have created a vendor record for the entity that you are using. This allows the 

system to generate an A/P invoice for the fee.

Company > All > Entities > Edit > Additional Information tab > Vendor 

• 
If you want to calculate fees only for occupied units, your company must be using KPIs. See 

Adding a KPI Setup in the online help or download the Company User Guide 

• 
Create a customer record and associate it with the entity. Go to Company > All > Entities > 

Additional Information Tab > Customer 

If you have not created a customer record for the entity you are using, the system cannot 
generate an A/R invoice. 

Complete these tasks before using the fees feature: 

• 
Enable the fee feature. See Enabling the Fees Feature. (on page 106) 

• 
Enable permissions for the management fees feature. See Enabling Permissions for the Fees 

Feature. (on page 107)  

• 
Add a fee template. See Adding a Fee Template. (on page 108)

JOURNAL ENTRY 

When you select Journal entry, these fields appear: 

1. 
In the Journal drop-down list, select the journal where you want to create the journal entry. 

2. 
In the Expense account drop-down list, select the debit account to use for journal entries. 

3. 
In the Credit account drop-down list, select the credit account to use for journal entries. 

If the Location differs, then this alternative location only creates one journal entry (JE). 

4. 
In the Credit location drop-down list, select the corporate entity or entity that represents 

your management company. This is the location to use for the credit side/location of the 

journal entry.  

The debit side of the journal entry will be the entity that the fee is being calculated for. 

Filling In the Fee Type Section 

Select the appropriate Fee type: 

• 
Percentage: Select this option to charge a percentage of the total as the fee that the system 

will apply for the G/L accounts chosen. 

• 
Flat fee: Select this option to charge a flat fee. 

• 
Total units: Select this option to charge the same fee to all units. Use this option when you 

have fees based on the units being managed.  

• 
Occupied units: Select this option to charge a fee calculated based on the total number of 

units. Use this option when the fees are based on the units for which you are receiving rent.

If KPIs are enabled, the system completes the Occupied units field.
