Percentage 

If you selected Percentage, the percentage list opens. 

1. 
Click the first row in the Percentage column and type the percentage to charge. For 

example, for 3.5%, enter 3.5 in Percentage column. 

2. 
In the Account from drop-down list, select the starting account in the account range to use 

it as the basis of calculation. You may enter multiple percentages and G/L account ranges as 

needed. 

3. 
In the Account to drop-down list, select the ending account in the account range to use it 

as the basis of calculation. You may enter multiple percentages and G/L account ranges as 

needed. 

If you have additional fees to charge, continue adding percentages of fees. If you need to 

add a row to the table, click 
 Add at the end of the row. 

4. 
In the Min field, type a minimum amount to charge per month. When the calculated fees do 

not reach this amount, the system adjusts the A/P invoice to the number you enter here. 

5. 
In the Max field, type a maximum amount to charge per month. When the calculated fees 

exceed this amount, the system lowers the fee to the amount on the A/P invoice. 

6. 
Select the Fee on debit transactions check box when you want the fee to display in G/L 

account activity as a positive number (debits minus credits). Clear the check box to have the 

G/L account activity display as a negative number (credits minus debits). 

7. 
To calculate the management fees by journal, select the journal or journals in the Journals 

drop-down list. If you don’t select any journals, the system calculates the management fees 

on all journals. 

Flat Fee 

If you selected Flat fee, type the amount to charge in the Flat fee amount field. 

Total Units 

If you selected Total units, the following fields are displayed: 

• 
Unit amount: Type the amount you want to charge. 

• 
Unit count: Type the number of units that will be charged.

system.

Filling In the Schedule Fees Tab  

To create a fee schedule, click the Schedule fees tab.  

1. 
In the Action drop-down list, select how you want the system to generate the A/P invoice:  

• 
Auto Calculate: The system calculates charges without automatically posting, allowing 

you to review the charges prior to posting. 

• 
Auto Calculate and Post: The system calculates and posts charges automatically. 

• 
Manual: The system does not automatically calculate charges. You must handle this 

process with the Periodic tasks > Fees option. 

2. 
In the Start Date field, fill in the date to start running the fee billing process.  

In the Ending On field, select when you want the system to stop running the fee charging 

process: 

Never: The system charges fees indefinitely unless someone changes this fee template. 

Number of Occurrences: The system runs the fee charges as many times as you indicate 

here. If you select Number of occurrences, type the number of occurrences in the End after 

box. 

End Date: Select to have the system generate fee charges until it reaches a specific date. In 

the End on box, select or type the lease’s end date, the date to stop billing the fee. 

3. 
In the Repeat drop-down list, select None, Months, or Years.  

If you selected Months or Years, type the number next to the Every field. 

4. 
In the Auto Calculate drop-down list, select Current Month or Prior Month, depending on 

when you are scheduling your fees.

Hiding the Vendor’s Tax ID 

Use this feature to obscure vendors’ tax IDs from users and grant the ability to see the tax IDs to 

other users.  

Before You Begin 

There are two requirements for enabling this feature: 

• 
RealPage customer support must install the Tax ID custom package. After installing the 

package, the Vendor activity has a new permission, View tax ID. 

• 
The View Tax ID permission controls whether users can see a vendor’s tax ID in clear text or 

not. Enable or disable the permission to the users or roles as needed. 

Checking the Tax ID Package 

The Hide Tax ID package must be installed in your environment.  

To check whether you have this package installed: 

1. 
Open the Company menu, and then select the Setup tab.  

2. 
Select the Subscriptions option. 

3. 
Click the Custom packages tab. 

4. 
Look for Hide tax ID. 

After confirming that the package is installed on your system, grant the View tax ID 

permission. 

Permissions 

Access can vary depending on your organization’s subscriptions and your permissions. If you do 

not see the option in the menu, then ask your System Administrator to check your permissions. 

This permission is required to be able to see a vendor’s tax ID in clear text.

Administrator for assistance. If you have administrator privileges, you can assign permissions for a 

new feature (on page 290) to a user or to a role. See Roles and Permissions (on page 290) for a 

description of how to review a user’s permissions.

Before you can issue joint checks to two parties, update the vendor records of both signers.  

Updating Vendor Records Pay to Contact 

To update a vendor record so that the system issues joint checks:  

1. 
Create a new vendor record or open the vendor record of one of the vendors that you want 

to pay with a joint check.  

When creating checks, the system addresses the check to the same contact that appears on 

the invoice and uses the text in the Print as field of the contact record to fill in the Pay to 

the order of field on the check. The Pay to contact field often defaults to the vendor’s 

primary contact. When this is the case, you can change the Print as field of the primary 

contact on the vendor record. The primary contact’s information appears on the Vendor tab 

(the first page) of the vendor record. 

2. 
In the Primary contact section, type the names of both parties that must sign the joint check 

in the Print as field. 

3. 
Save the vendor record.

*Source: `RP Accounting AP Setup User Guide.pdf`, Page 141*

Vendor (Supplier) Types 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > Setup > Types`


Use vendor types to organize your vendors into categories, and then use those categories for 

filtering lists and reporting. 

For example, you might have multiple vendors for office supplies. You can create a vendor type 

called Office Supplies and tag all the office-supply vendors with that type, then create a report 

that aggregates the total amount spent on office supplies for the year. Or if you’re a single 

company (no entities), you might want to create a hierarchy of vendors based on regions of the 

country so that you can report on total costs and costs per region.  

By setting up meaningful vendor types, you can more quickly manage and report vendor 

information. By setting up vendor types with parent types, you create a hierarchy that shows how 

your vendors are organized. The Standard Industrial Classification code is an example of an 

official standard for classifying suppliers; however, you can create a hierarchy that reflects the 

unique characteristics of your business. For example, many companies use vendor types to 

differentiate between suppliers and contractors.  

Before You Begin 

Access can vary depending on your organization’s subscriptions and your permissions. If you do 

not see the option in the menu, then ask your System Administrator to check your permissions. 

Permissions 

These permissions are required to work with vendor types.

Administrator for assistance. If you have administrator privileges, you can assign permissions for a 

new feature (on page 290) to a user or to a role. See Roles and Permissions (on page 290) for a 

description of how to review a user’s permissions.

To view the vendor type list:

#### Using Vendor Types in Multi-entity, Multi-currency Companies
*Source: `RP Accounting AP Setup User Guide.pdf`, Page 144*



#### Adding a Vendor Type
*Source: `RP Accounting AP Setup User Guide.pdf`, Page 144*

Vendor (Supplier) Configuration 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Setup User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Using Vendor Types in Multi-entity, Multi-currency Companies 

Vendor types can be common (that is, accessible) to all entities, or exclusive (private) to a specific 

entity. Creating vendor types in an entity restricts them to that entity. If you do create a vendor 

type in a specific entity, use a naming convention to differentiate it at the top level. 

Best practice: Create vendor types at the top level to be shared across all the entities. 

Adding a Vendor Type 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > Setup > 
 Types`


Best practice: Create vendor types at the top level so that they can be shared across all the 
entities.  

1. 
Open the Accounts payable menu, and then select the Setup tab. 

2. 
Select the 
 Add next to Types. The Vendor type Information page opens. 

3. 
In Name, type the text that you want to appear in the Vendor types drop-down list when a 

user creates a new vendor. 

4. 
In Parent type, select a vendor type that you want to use to categorize the vendor type. 

Categorize records according to type for filtering, sorting, and grouping opportunities. 

These types can take advantage of an additional layer of grouping by assigning a Parent 

type. If you assign a Parent type within your types, you can also get a native roll-up of any 

types assigned the parent type during reporting. 

For example, if you set up the vendor types Contractor and Subcontractor and then you 

make Contractor the parent type of Subcontractor, you can filter financial reports using the 

Contractor vendor type, all vendors assigned to both the vendors Contractor and 

Subcontractor are included in the report.  

5. 
Click the Save button.  

What’s Next? 

Assigning a Form 1099 form to a vendor type (on page 138) 

---

#### Using a Vendor Type for 1099 Contractors
*Source: `RP Accounting AP Setup User Guide.pdf`, Page 146*

Vendor (Supplier) Configuration 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Setup User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Using a Vendor Type for 1099 Contractors 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > Setup > 
 Types`


If you are setting up multiple contractors who receive Form 1099, you can save time by creating a 

vendor type, such as Contractors assigning the vendor type a 1099 form and box, and then 

flagging the appropriate vendor contractors with the vendor type. Any vendor flagged with that 

vendor type automatically becomes associated with the vendor type 1099 form and box. 

Alternatively, as you add vendors to your company, you can flag them as 1099 and associate them 

individually with a 1099 form and box. 

To create a vendor type and assign it a default Form 1099: 

1. 
Create and save a new vendor type (on page 134). 

2. 
Click Edit beside the vendor type you just created. The Vendor Type Information page 

appears. 

3. 
Click the Form 1099 link. The Form 1099 Information page appears. 

4. 
Select the appropriate 1099 form and box. 

5. 
Click Save to save the form and box selection, and then click Save again on the Vendor type 

information page. 

The next time you open the Vendor type information page, you see the selected 1099 form 

name. 

To flag a vendor as a vendor type: 

1. 
Open the Accounts payable menu. 

2. 
Select Vendors. The Vendors list opens. 

3. 
Click Edit next to the desired vendor. 

4. 
On the Vendor Information page, select the Additional Information tab. 

5. 
In the Type ID field, select the vendor type from the drop-down menu. 

The next time you open the Vendor information page and view the Additional information 

tab, you should see the specific 1099 Form assigned from the vendor type. If you see a 

different form, it may be because you’ve already assigned a 1099 form at the vendor level, 

and that form overrides the form assigned from the vendor type. To resolve the issue, edit 

the vendor record to remove the overriding form. 

After a vendor is associated with the vendor type 1099 form, if you want to change the 
form, you can either remove the vendor type from the vendor record, or edit the vendor 
type to change the 1099 form for all associated vendors. 

---

### Vendor Visibility
*Source: `RP Accounting AP Setup User Guide.pdf`, Page 152*



#### Before You Begin
*Source: `RP Accounting AP Setup User Guide.pdf`, Page 152*

Vendor (Supplier) Configuration 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Setup User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Vendor Visibility 


> **Navigation Path:** `Company > Setup > Subscriptions > Multi Entity Console > Configure > Entity 
Restrictions > Vendors`


When your company has multiple entities, you can use the vendor visibility feature to prevent 

entities from inadvertently using the wrong vendors.  

This feature allows you to restrict the use of a vendor to selected entities and locations. You can 

add or remove restrictions at will. The Vendor visibility page enables you to view, edit, group 

update, and manage multi-entity restrictions for vendors. Use the multi-entity console to enable 

vendor restrictions. 

In addition to updating vendor restrictions individually, you can use the import and export 

features on the Vendor visibility page to: 

• 
Export your vendor restrictions list so that you can print or use the information in another 

application. The export is available in one of several standard formats (CSV, Excel, Word, 

PDF). 

• 
Update your vendor restrictions list by exporting selected data, making changes, and then 

importing your changes. 

Before You Begin 

Access can vary depending on your organization’s subscriptions and your permissions. If you do 

not see the option in the menu, then ask your System Administrator to check your permissions. 

To use the vendor visibility feature, your company must have multiple entities. 

Permissions 

These permissions are required to import vendors, view vendor visibility, and import vendor 

restriction data. 

Application

Vendor Groups 

Use vendor groups to categorize vendors in order to post transactions to specific G/L accounts 

based on these categories. 

If you want to categorize vendors for reporting, see Vendor Types (on page 131). 

You can view, add, deactivate, or delete vendor groups from the Accounts Payable application. 

There is only one set of vendor groups in the system. Regardless of where you access the vendor 

groups, you will be working with the same set of data. 

About Vendor Groups 

You can create vendor groups that are specific to your business. Then you assign a vendor group 

to each vendor record. Finally, you can map the vendor group to G/L accounts on transaction 

definitions. 

For example, say you have different vendors who supply hardware. You could have one vendor 

group called Hardware. If you wanted to track data in more detail, you could create more vendor 

groups, such as Mainframe, Minicomputer, and so on.  

In this example, if you buy a part from a Mainframe vendor, the purchase transaction could post 

to a different G/L account than the one for a Minicomputer vendor from whom you purchased 

the same part. You could also filter list views by vendor G/L groups. 

Before You Begin 

Access can vary depending on your organization’s subscriptions and your permissions. If you do 

not see the option in the menu, then ask your System Administrator to check your permissions. 

Permissions 

These permissions are required to work with vendor groups.

description of how to review a user’s permissions.

#### Adding a Vendor Group
*Source: `RP Accounting AP Setup User Guide.pdf`, Page 161*

Chapter 8: Vendor (Supplier) Configuration 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Setup User Guide 

Adding a Vendor Group 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > Setup > 
 Groups`


1. 
Open the Accounts payable menu, and then select the Setup tab. 

2. 
In the Vendors section, select 
 Add next to Groups. The Vendor group information (on 

page 157) page opens. 

3. 
In the Vendor group ID field, type a unique identifier for the vendor group. 

4. 
In the Name field, enter a descriptive name for the vendor dimension group. 

When displayed elsewhere in the system, the dimension group is listed with the ID and 
name together (ID--Name), as in NAOPS--North America Operations. IDs can’t be changed 
once you’ve saved the group, but you can edit the name at a later time. 

5. 
(Optional) In the Description field, enter any description that will remind you of what this 

group includes or how it’s used. 

6. 
From the Group type drop-down menu, select the type of group you want to create and 

then define the group. 

• 
Select Specific members if you want to hand pick the locations, departments, 

customers, vendors, employees, items, projects, or classes to include in the group. 

• 
Select All members if you want to filter based on criteria of your choice. For example, 

you might define a “Direct Customers” group which includes all members but then 

filters the results to only customers where the Customer Type field is equal to “Direct.” 

7. 
In the Sort order drop-down list, select the sort order of the vendors in the group: 

Ascending or Descending. It sorts in order by the field that you select in the next option, 

Sort field. 

8. 
In the Sort field, select the field that you want the system to use for the sort order. 

9. 
In the Max matches field, type the number of desired matches. You can also leave it blank 

to include all members of the group. 

Use Max matches when you want to select only the top or bottom matches based on the 
value of a field.  
To set it up: 
Select All members as the group type.  
Select Sort order and then select the field to use.  
Select the number of matches in the Max matches field. 
Non-numeric fields are matched alphabetically. 

---


<!-- Page 162 -->
Vendor (Supplier) Configuration 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Setup User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

If you are planning to show top or bottom matches in a financial report, such as showing the 
top customers by revenue, don’t use the Max matches option for the group. 

10. 
Select the Dimension structure check box to create a dimension structure based on the 

vendor group. 

By creating a dimension structure, you can add the group to the rows or columns of a 

financial report. If you don’t select the Dimension structure check box, you can only use the 

vendor group for filtering reports. 

11. 
In the Filters section, set up filters if you want the system to define the members of the 

group through a filter. Each row of the Filters list represents one test or filter. A filter is 

composed of three parts: 

• 
Field: The field to use as the test or comparison. 

• 
Operator: The comparison operator. Valid values include equals, not equal to, greater 

than, less than, is one of, is not one of, is empty, is not empty, and contains. 

• 
Value: The value to look for in the field.  

Example 

Suppose you want to create a group of vendors in Dallas.  

Rather than manually searching for vendors in Dallas, you can set up a filter to have the 

system automatically include every vendor record by setting up a filter on the City field that 

contains the value “Dallas.” 

Filter: City equals Dallas 

The field is City, the operator is equals, and the value is Dallas. 

12. 
Use Condition type when you have defined multiple filters: 

• 
Select All (AND) to require that a vendor match all of the filters you set up. 

• 
Select Any (OR) to require that a vendor record match at least one of the filters. 

13. 
Select Expression if you want to enter an expression for the system to user for the filter. 

14. 
Click the Save button.

Exporting Lists 

You can export most lists to several available file formats and then import the data into an 

external application, such as Microsoft Word or Microsoft Excel. 

Although you can export up to 25,000 rows, if you want to save time and effort, we recommend 

that you filter your list to pinpoint only the information you need to export by creating a custom 

view. That way, when you export the list, you’ll have a spreadsheet tailored to the information you 

need. You can export any view of this list for use on your local computer. 

Use column filters, advanced filters, and views to filter the data. For instructions, refer to 

Managing Lists. 

If you have a sorted and filtered list that you use consistently, you can create and save it as a 

custom report for convenience. With a custom report, you need to set the filtering and 

parameters only once to enable you to generate the report as needed after that. 

1. 
Click the Export button. 

2. 
Select the format to which you want to export the list. 

• 
CSV: Select this format if you plan to move the data from one program to another. 

You can use files that you save in CSV format with any spreadsheet program. 

• 
Word: When you select this option, the system exports the list in Word format. If a list 

of conversion formats displays, select HTML document. 

• 
Excel: When you select this option, the system exports the list in XLS format. If you see 

an error message about file type and extension type incompatibility, you can disregard 

the message and select Yes. 

• 
PDF: Select this option if you plan to print or share the list. When you select this 

option, the system exports the list and tries to open the file in the browser. If 

prompted, select Yes to allow the PDF to open. 

• 
CSV for import: Select this option if you want to export data, change it, or add to it, 

and then import it into the system again. 

Some lists in RealPage Accounting do not have the CSV for import option. 

---

> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > Setup > Tax > Authorities`


Tax authorities are agencies (for example, cities, states, provinces, federal, or HMRC, for example) 

for whom you are collecting sales and other taxes. If your organization uses VAT, the Tax 

authorities list shows all of the tax authorities in your system.  

You can create tax authorities, including hierarchies of tax authorities with parent-child 

relationships, and modify existing ones. Tax authorities are shared between Accounts Receivable 

and Accounts Payable and thus appear on the Setup menu of both applications.  

You use tax authorities by assigning a line item in a transaction to a tax authority when the item is 

taxable.

will pay the taxes that you collect from this authority. 

You can create a hierarchy of tax authorities. 

•

If the tax authority you are creating is a child of another tax authority, then select its 

parent from the Parent authority drop-down list.

If your organization is using VAT taxes (UK only), the Tax details list shows all the tax details you 

have created to which items can be assigned.  

Use the Tax detail list to view the details of a specific type of tax to be applied to a line item. 

When the system calculates the taxes, the tax schedule map applies the chosen tax details to any 

taxable line items in invoices.  

You assign the tax detail in the tax schedule using the Tax schedules detail tab. 

Before You Begin

not see the option in the menu, then ask your System Administrator to check your permissions.

#### Adding Tax Details
*Source: `RP Accounting AP Setup User Guide.pdf`, Page 182*

Tax Configuration 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Setup User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Adding Tax Details 

These are the most direct options for adding tax details. You may have additional options based 

on your permission settings.  


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Receivable > Setup > Tax > 
 Details`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > Setup > Tax > 
 Details`


Not only can you specify the tax rate, but you can also specify a taxable range such that items 

with costs below a minimum are not taxed, and the tax stops when the cost of the item goes 

above the maximum.  

You can also specify an absolute minimum and/or maximum taxable amount. A minimum is that 

which must be paid when the calculated tax on an item is too low; the maximum tax overrides the 

calculated tax if that tax goes above the maximum taxable amount. In addition, you can also 

choose a tax authority (City of San Jose, for example) for whom you are collecting the taxes.  

To add tax details: 

1. 
Open the Accounts Receivable or Accounts Payable menu. 

2. 
Click the Setup tab of the menu.  

3. 
In the Tax section, click 
 Add next to Details. The Tax details information page opens. 

4. 
In the Detail ID field, type a name for the tax detail. After you save this name, it can’t be 

changed.  

5. 
In the Description field, type a description of the tax, such as Excise tax for Equipment. 

6. 
In the Minimum taxable amount field, If the item is not taxed until its cost passes a specific 

threshold, type that amount in the Minimum taxable amount box. 

7. 
In the Maximum taxable amount field, if the tax tops out at another limit, type that amount 

in the Maximum taxable amount box. For example, say items under $200 are not taxable. 

You enter $200 as the minimum. Taxes will not be added in any document using this tax 

detail for items under $200. However, for items over $200, the tax in the Percent field is 

added.  

8. 
In the Include in taxable amount drop-down list, click one of the following:  

• 
Full amount - include the cost from zero up to the maximum taxable amount.  

• 
Amount within range - include the amount between the minimum and maximum 

taxable amount.  

To save the record and open a new record page, click Save & new.  

9. 
In the Percent field, type the tax rate. For example, type 6 to apply a tax of 6%. 

---


<!-- Page 183 -->
Chapter 9: Tax Configuration 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Setup User Guide 

10. 
In Minimum tax and Maximum tax fields, if an item has a fixed minimum or maximum tax 

regardless of amount, then enter those amounts.  

The Accounts Receivable application always uses account labels for tax computations. 

11. 
In the G/L Account drop-down list, select the general ledger account to which this tax is to 

be assigned. You can use the field-level links to add a new G/L account, view a G/L account’s 

record, or find a G/L account’s record. To add or import G/L accounts, you must be at the 

top level. 

The Account label field displays only if tax schedules are enabled in the Accounts 
Receivable application. Both the Account label field and the G/L account field must 
reference the same general ledger account number. In other words, if you selected an 
account label already, choose the G/L account that is used by this account label. If you 
select the G/L account first, then select an account label that references that G/L 
account.  

12. 
In the Account label drop-down list, select the account label for the general ledger account 

you selected in the G/L account drop-down list. 

13. 
In the Tax authority drop-down list, select the tax authority to which this tax belongs.  

14. 
In the Status drop-down list, select Active to add the new item to the Tax details 

drop-down list. Or select Inactive to prevent the new item from appearing in the list. To see 

the inactive tax details later, select the Show inactive check box in the list page.  

15. 
Click the Save button. You can also click the More actions button, and then select Save & 

new. The system saves the record and opens a new blank record. 

---

> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > Setup > Tax > Schedules`


A tax schedule record identifies the tax details that are applied when the schedule is referenced. 

For example, you could create a schedule named “Dallas - State & Local” where two tax details 

(“Dallas Local” and “Texas State”) are assigned. When the system references this schedule, it 

applies both taxes. 

Create and use tax schedules to help you determine which tax schedule to apply to each line item. 

Tax schedules are applicable only if you’re using VAT taxes (UK only). 

To find your tax schedules, go to the Accounts Receivable menu, and then click the Setup tab.  

• 
To edit or view your tax schedules, click Schedules.  

• 
To add a new tax schedule, click 
 Add.  

About Tax Schedules 

A tax schedule is where one or more tax details are assigned. For example, you could create a 

schedule named Los Gatos - State & Local where two tax details (Los Gatos Local and California 

State) are assigned. When this schedule is referenced, both taxes are applied.

options based on your permission settings.

In the Tax section, select Schedules. The Tax schedules list opens.

> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Receivable > Setup > Tax > Schedule Maps`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > Setup > Tax > Schedule Maps`


A tax schedule map associates tax schedules with account labels (via account label tax groups) 

and customers (via contact tax groups). The tax schedule contains the tax detail records, which 

define the amount of tax to apply.  

When a user enters an invoice for a customer in a contact tax group and the user enters a line for 

an account label in an account label tax group, the tax schedule map tells the system which tax 

schedules to use for the subtotal tax account label. 

The Memo field displays the names of the tax detail records associated with the tax schedules 

assigned to the tax subtotal based on the tax schedule map.

#### Tax Schedule Map Overview
*Source: `RP Accounting AP Setup User Guide.pdf`, Page 195*



##### Before You Begin
*Source: `RP Accounting AP Setup User Guide.pdf`, Page 195*

Chapter 9: Tax Configuration 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Setup User Guide 

Tax Schedule Map Overview 

A tax schedule map shows you which tax schedules apply to which account labels and contact tax 

groups associated with those labels. In other words, if the item is taxable and the contact is in a 

certain city, the system applies a particular tax schedule. 

Example 

When computer hardware is purchased (account label tax group) by a person in London (contact 

tax group), add both a sales tax and value-added tax (tax schedule with tax two details). 

When you create an invoice, the system evaluates all tax schedule maps against the line items in 

the invoice along with to whom the invoice is issued, and then knows which tax schedules to 

apply to each line item. 

The tax schedule map includes the account label tax group, contact tax group, and tax schedule. 

Before You Begin 

Access can vary depending on your organization’s subscriptions and your permissions. If you do 

not see the option in the menu, then ask your System Administrator to check your permissions. 

Permissions 

These permissions are required to work with tax schedules and tax schedule maps.

#### Exporting Lists
*Source: `RP Accounting AP Setup User Guide.pdf`, Page 206*

Loan Types 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Setup User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Exporting Lists 

You can export most lists to several available file formats and then import the data into an 

external application, such as Microsoft Word or Microsoft Excel. 

Although you can export up to 25,000 rows, if you want to save time and effort, we recommend 

that you filter your list to pinpoint only the information you need to export by creating a custom 

view. That way, when you export the list, you’ll have a spreadsheet tailored to the information you 

need. You can export any view of this list for use on your local computer. 

Use column filters, advanced filters, and views to filter the data. For instructions, refer to 

Managing Lists. 

If you have a sorted and filtered list that you use consistently, you can create and save it as a 

custom report for convenience. With a custom report, you need to set the filtering and 

parameters only once to enable you to generate the report as needed after that. 

1. 
Click the Export button. 

2. 
Select the format to which you want to export the list. 

• 
CSV: Select this format if you plan to move the data from one program to another. 

You can use files that you save in CSV format with any spreadsheet program. 

• 
Word: When you select this option, the system exports the list in Word format. If a list 

of conversion formats displays, select HTML document. 

• 
Excel: When you select this option, the system exports the list in XLS format. If you see 

an error message about file type and extension type incompatibility, you can disregard 

the message and select Yes. 

• 
PDF: Select this option if you plan to print or share the list. When you select this 

option, the system exports the list and tries to open the file in the browser. If 

prompted, select Yes to allow the PDF to open. 

• 
CSV for import: Select this option if you want to export data, change it, or add to it, 

and then import it into the system again. 

Some lists in RealPage Accounting do not have the CSV for import option.

#### Duplicating Records
*Source: `RP Accounting AP Setup User Guide.pdf`, Page 210*

Loan Types 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Setup User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Duplicating Records 

If your goal is to create one record and reuse it as the starting point for additional records, use 

the Duplicate function. Most types of records can be duplicated—including A/P invoices, A/R 

invoices, recurring invoices, adjustments, entities, vendors, contacts, journals, G/L accounts, 

user-defined books, document numbering sequences, contracts, service tickets, email templates, 

and reporting account sets. When you open a record and it includes a Duplicate button, you can 

use it as a template to quickly create a new record.  

For invoices, you can also create a future draft of an invoice as you add it, and set the date to 

create the future draft. See Adding an A/P Invoice Manually and look for the section called 

“Creating a Future Draft Invoice.” 

To duplicate recurring invoices, look for the Duplicate option that is located in the More actions 
button menu. 

To duplicate a record: 

1. 
Open the record that you want to duplicate by clicking View or Edit.  

2. 
Click the Duplicate button. The system creates a new record that is identical to the original. 

After you duplicate a record, the copy of the record stays open so that you can change its 

details.  

3. 
Fill in the fields.  

4. 
The system sets the status to Active. You can leave the status set to Active or select Inactive 

to prevent the item from appearing in lists. 

5. 
Click the Save button. You can also click the More actions button, and then select Save & 

New. The system saves the record and then opens a new blank record.

A/P Terms Configuration 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Setup User Guide

A/P Terms Overview 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > Setup > Terms`


Terms are a list of rules for doing business with your vendors. 

You can add any rules that a vendor establishes for extending credit to you in the A/P Terms 

Information page. When you add a term for a specific vendor and select it from the vendor 

Information page, that term becomes the default whenever you perform transactions involving 

that vendor, such as entering A/P invoices. 

For multi-entity shared companies 

A/P Terms is a master object. Master objects can either be common (that is, accessible) to all 

entities or exclusive (“private”) to a specific entity. RealPage recommends that you create vendor 

terms at the top level to be shared across all the entities. However, you can create vendor terms in 

an entity, so they are restricted to that entity. If you do create them in the entities, use a naming 

convention that differentiates them at the top level. 

Before You Begin 

Access can vary depending on your organization’s subscriptions and your permissions. If you do 

not see the option in the menu, then ask your System Administrator to check your permissions.

RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Setup User Guide

A/P Terms List 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > Setup > Terms`


Use the A/P Terms list to view the list of rules that a vendor establishes for extending credit to 

your company. 

From this list, you can: 

• 
Add a new term 

• 
Edit terms 

• 
View the terms details 

• 
Delete an A/P term 

• 
Export the list of A/P terms 

Adding Terms 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > Setup > 
 Terms`


To add A/P terms: 

1. 
Open the Accounts Payable menu, then select the Setup tab. 

2. 
Select the 
 Add next to Terms. The A/P Terms information page opens. 

3. 
In the Name field, type the name of this term. The system displays the name on A/P invoice 

and vendor entry pages. 

4. 
In Description, type a note about the purpose and use of this term. 

5. 
In the Status drop-down list, select Active if you want this item to appear in drop-down 

lists. Select Inactive to prevent the item from appearing in drop-down lists. 

Filling In the Due Section 

The due date is a combination of the day(s) and what the day(s) references: 

• 
To set terms that reference the number of days from the A/P invoice date, such as Net 30, 

type the number of days in Day, and select of the month from AP/AR invoice date from the 

adjacent list. 

---


<!-- Page 217 -->
Chapter 11: A/P Terms Configuration 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Setup User Guide 

• 
To set a day on a month referenced from the A/P invoice date, type the day of the month in 

Day, and select a month setting from the adjacent list. For instance, to set terms for the 15th 

of the month after the A/P invoice date, type 15 in Day, and select of the month from 

AP/AR invoice date in the adjacent list. 

Filling In the Discount Section 

The discount is a combination of the day(s), what the day(s) references, the dollar or percent 

discount, and the number of grace days. When you pay the A/P invoice in full, the system 

automatically calculates the discount based on the terms that you set here. 

To set a discount that references the number of days from the A/P invoice date, such as 2%-10: 

1. 
Type the number of days in Day. 

2. 
Select from invoice A/P invoice date from the adjacent drop-down list. 

3. 
In the Amount field, type the discount amount. 

4. 
Select $ or % from the adjacent drop-down list. 

5. 
In the Grace days field, type the number of days before the vendor withdraws the discount. 

To set a discount based on a day on a month referenced from the A/P invoice date: 

1. 
In the Day field, type the day of the month. 

2. 
Select a month setting from the adjacent drop-down list. 

3. 
Type the discount amount in Amount. 

4. 
Select $ or % from the adjacent list. 

5. 
Type the number of days before the vendor withdraws the discount in Grace days.

Selecting the Calculation Method 

You can set how the system calculates discounts in transactions that use this term. You can 

calculate the discount: 

• 
Based solely on the line-items total, excluding added charges (such as taxes and shipping). 

• 
Based on the invoice total, including all charges. 

Filling In the Penalty Section 

To set a penalty for paying after the due date, in the Penalty section set the following: 

1. 
In the Cycle drop-down list, set cycle to the time span in which the penalty accrues, such as 

Weekly, Biweekly, Monthly, and so on. 

2. 
In the Amount field, type the penalty amount. 

3. 
Select $ or % from the drop-down list. 

4. 
In the Grace days field, type the number of days after the due date that the vendor applies. 

5. 
Click the Save button. You can also click the More actions button, and then select Save & 

new. The system saves the record and opens a new blank record.

### Asset Configuration Workflow

Asset Configuration 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Setup User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Asset Configuration Workflow 

Follow these steps to configure your system to use assets. 

1. 
Grant asset permissions to users (on page 214). 

2. 
Add asset categories (on page 217). 

3. 
Add asset types (on page 222). 

4. 
Enable the capture of asset data during invoice entry (optional) (on page 215). 

5. 
Requiring asset category and type by G/L account (optional) (on page 216). 

Before You Begin 

Grant the following permissions to users who need to enter asset information into the system. If 

you plan to enable the asset capture during invoice entry, then grant these permissions to users 

who enter invoices. 

Permissions 

These permissions are required to enter asset information, manage the information, and run the 

Asset report. 

Application 
Activities 
Permissions 

Accounts Payable 
Assets 
List, View, Add, Edit, Delete 

If your user account doesn’t have the permissions shown above, then ask your System 

Administrator for assistance. If you have administrator privileges, you can assign permissions for a 

new feature (on page 290) to a user or to a role. See Roles and Permissions (on page 290) for a 

description of how to review a user’s permissions. 

---



#### Enabling Asset Capture on Invoice Entry
*Source: `RP Accounting AP Setup User Guide.pdf`, Page 225*

Chapter 12: Asset Configuration 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Setup User Guide 

Enabling Asset Capture on Invoice Entry 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > Setup > Configuration > Enable Assets In Invoice 
Entry`


You must be at the top level to enable and disable this setting. You can enable and disable the 

setting from Central configuration or from Accounts Payable configuration. 

To enable asset capture during invoice entry: 

1. 
Open the Accounts payable menu, and then select the Setup tab. 

2. 
Select the Configuration option. 

3. 
In the Enable functionality section, select the Enable assets in invoice entry check box. 

4. 
Click Save. When enabled, the system adds asset-related fields at the end of the Invoice 

entries section. 

---



#### Requiring Asset Category and Type by G/L Account
*Source: `RP Accounting AP Setup User Guide.pdf`, Page 226*

Asset Configuration 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Setup User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Requiring Asset Category and Type by G/L Account 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > General Ledger > All > Accounts > Edit > Require Asset Category/Type 
During Invoice Entry`


To require asset information for a specific G/L account during invoice entry: 

1. 
Open the General Ledger menu, and then select Accounts. 

2. 
Find the desired G/L account, and then click the Edit link. 

3. 
Select the Require asset category/type during invoice entry check box. 

4. 
Click Save. When users select this G/L account during invoice entry, the system requires that 

users select an asset category and type before they can save the invoice.

Asset Categories List 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > Setup > More > Asset Categories`


Use the Asset categories list to add and manage asset categories that appear in the Asset 

category drop-down list when adding an Asset record to the system. The list uses categories that 

are also used with the Facilities application. You can add custom categories to the list using the 

 Add Asset Category option on the Accounts Payable menu’s Setup tab. 

Before You Begin

not see the option in the menu, then ask your System Administrator to check your permissions.

Application 
Activities 
Permissions 

Accounts Payable 
Asset Categories 
List, View, Add, Edit, Delete

Administrator for assistance. If you have administrator privileges, you can assign permissions for a 

new feature (on page 290) to a user or to a role. See Roles and Permissions (on page 290) for a 

description of how to review a user’s permissions. 

Adding an Asset Category 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > Setup > More > 
 Asset Categories`


You can add a category to the Asset categories drop-down list. Add categories before you add 

asset types. 

To add an asset category: 

1. 
Open the Accounts Payable menu, click the Setup tab. 

2. 
Click the 
 Add button next to the Asset categories option. 

3. 
In the Category field, type the text that you want to appear in the Asset category 

drop-down list. 

4. 
In the Description field, type the text that you want to appear in the Asset categories list.  

5. 
Click Save.

*Source: `RP Accounting AP Setup User Guide.pdf`, Page 228*

*Source: `RP Accounting AP Setup User Guide.pdf`, Page 228*

Asset Configuration 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Setup User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Viewing and Editing Asset Categories 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > Setup > More > Asset Categories > Edit/View`


You can view the details of an asset category or use the Edit mode to change an asset category’s 

description. 

How to Get Here 

1. 
Open the Accounts Payable menu, and then click the Setup tab. 

2. 
Select the Asset categories option. 

To view an asset category: 

• 
Find the asset category record that you want to open and click the View option. 

When viewing an asset category, you can: 

• 
Click the Print to button to print the record or download the record as XML code. 

• 
Click the Edit button to change the asset category record. 

• 
Click the Duplicate button to create a copy of the asset category record. 

• 
Click the More actions button and then select View audit trail to view a log of 

changes to the record. 

To edit an asset category: 

1. 
Find the asset category that you want to change. 

2. 
Click the Edit link. 

When editing an asset category record, you can do all of the things that you can do in View 

mode, plus you can add or change the description of the asset category. 

3. 
Click Save to save your changes. 

Deleting an Asset Category 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > Setup > More > Asset Categories > Delete`


Deleting an asset category removes it from Asset category drop-down lists.  

You can only delete an asset category that you added. 

To delete an asset category: 

1. 
Open the Accounts Payable menu, and then click the Setup tab. 

2. 
Click the Asset categories option. 

3. 
Find the asset category that you want to delete, and then click the Delete link. 

4. 
Click OK to confirm the deletion. 

---

be able to save a new asset record of this type.

be able to save a new asset record of this type.

Click Save to save your changes.

### About Automated Payments
*Source: `RP Accounting AP Setup User Guide.pdf`, Page 244*

Automatic Payment Configuration 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Setup User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

About Automated Payments 

Use this feature to have the system automatically pay your bills. To configure the automatic 

payment, you set up a filter that determines which invoices to pay, and then define the schedule 

on which to pay them.  

To configure a scheduled payment, you set up the filters to retrieve the invoices that you want the 

system to pay, which bank account that you want to use to pay with, and the method that you 

want to use to pay. You can pay by entity by paying at the entity level.  

All of the invoices in a payment schedule share the same payment schedule. You can create 

multiple payment schedules.  

After you configure a payment schedule’s filter and schedule, the system automatically runs 

scheduled payments. As part of the payment task, the system: 

• 
Sets the payments’ date to the date that the scheduler runs on. 

• 
Sends the payment requests through the approval queue if approvals are enabled. 

• 
Runs the scheduled payments before running the scheduled check runs. 

• 
Skips the failed invoice and continues processing the rest of the invoices when a payment 

fails. You can find failed payments in the Pay A/P invoices list.  

• 
Sends emails to notify the designated users about the payments.  

If the payment schedule uses the Add to outbox option, then you can open the Pay A/P Invoices 

Outbox to review the payments before paying the invoices. 

After the system pays the invoices, you can review and print the checks. See Viewing details of a 

payment request in a check run.

•

see turned off schedules when the Include inactive check box is selected. 

• 
Click the Last result column to sort by the last result. Click again to reverse the sort order. 

This sort helps you find the “Failed” schedules so that you can rerun them. 

• 
Click the number in the Execution count column to open the Payment requests list.

new feature (on page 290) to a user or to a role. See Roles and Permissions (on page 290) for a 

description of how to review a user’s permissions. 

Scheduling an Automatic Payment 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > Setup > More > 
 Schedule Payments Selection`


To add a new payment schedule: 

1. 
Open the Accounts Payable menu, and then click the Setup tab of the menu. 

2. 
In the More section, click the Schedule payments selection option. 

3. 
Click the Add button. The Schedule payments selection page opens. 

4. 
In the Payments Schedule ID field, type a unique name for the payment schedule. 

5. 
In the Filter drop-down list, select the desired filter to apply to the list. The filters in this list 

come from the Pay A/P Invoices page. The entity that you select in the filters is used for the 

Pay by entity option if you choose it. 

6. 
In the Bank section, select an option: 

• 
Select bank: When you created the payment schedule at the top level, selecting this 

option gives you access to bank accounts that are available to all entities (bank 

accounts that were not created at the entity level). If you created the payment 

schedule at an entity’s level, then selecting this option gives you access to both the 

top level bank accounts and the entity’s bank accounts. Select the bank in the Bank 

drop-down list, and then select the Bank G/L account. 

• 
Pay by entity: Select this option to use the entity’s default bank or its alternate bank 

account. Select Default or Alternate in the Bank drop-down list. 

---


<!-- Page 247 -->
Chapter 14: Automatic Payment Configuration 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Setup User Guide 

7. 
In the Payment method drop-down list, select the payment method that you want the 

system to use for the automatic payment. In addition to the standard payment methods, 

you can select the entity’s preference or the vendor’s preference. 

8. 
In the Payment request method drop-down list, select the desired payment request 

method.  

• 
Use vendor preference: Select this option to use the method that the vendor prefers. 

This option is specified in the vendor’s record on the Payment information tab. 

• 
Generate one request per A/P invoice: Select this option to generate a payment 

request for each A/P invoice. 

• 
Merge requests into one per vendor: Select this option to merge the payment 

requests into one request for each vendor. 

• 
Merge request into one per vendor pay to contact: Select this option to merge the 

payment requests into one request for each vendor pay to contact. 

The default method is Use vendor preference.  

9. 
Select the Only pay when funds are available check box to prevent the system from 

sending automatic payments when the bank account does not have enough funds to cover 

the payment. The system checks the bank balance and runs the schedule if the total amount 

of the invoices that you select for payment is less than the bank balance. If the amount is 

more, then the scheduled payment fails. Clear the check box to make the payment without 

checking the bank balance. 

10. 
Select the Automatically apply credits check box to have the system apply any credits for 

the vendor to the payment before using funds in the bank account. This setting is 

independent of the Enable inline credits to be automatically applied to invoice option on 

the Accounts Payable Configuration page.  

11. 
Select the Add to outbox check box when you want the system to process the payment, but 

you want to be able to review them before they are sent. Payments are merged per vendor. 

You can access the processed payment information from the Outbox on the Pay A/P 

invoices page. After you review the payments, you must click the Pay Now button to release 

the payments. 

12. 
In the Send payment notifications from drop-down list, select the contact that you want 

the system to use as the email address from which it sends notification emails. 

13. 
In the Status drop-down list, select Inactive to stop the system from processing automatic 

payments. The default is Active. 

---


<!-- Page 248 -->
Automatic Payment Configuration 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Setup User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Setting Up the Schedule 

1. 
In the Start date field, type the date to begin automatic payment processing. The date must 

be today’s date or a future date. 

2. 
In the Ending on drop-down list, select an option: 

• 
End date: Select this option to stop automatic payments on a specific date, and then 

select the date to stop in the End on field. 

• 
Never: Select to process the payments without end. 

• 
Number of occurrences: Select to process automatic payments a set number of times, 

and then type the number of times in the End After box. 

3. 
In the Repeat drop-down list, select an option: 

• 
None: Select this option to never repeat this automatic payment. 

• 
Days: Select this option to repeat this automatic payment every certain number of 

days, and then type the number of days in the Every ___ Days field. 

• 
Weeks: Select this option to repeat this automatic payment every certain number of 

weeks, and then type the number of weeks in the Every ___ Weeks field. 

• 
Months: Select this option to repeat this automatic payment every certain number of 

months, and then type the number of months in the Every ___ Months field. 

• 
End of Month: Select this option to repeat this automatic payment at the end of every 

month. Type the number of months in the blank for the Every ___ End of Month field, 

and then select the End of Month check box. For example, to repeat the payment 

every other month, type a “2.” 

4. 
In the Email results to field, type the email address of the person to notify about the 

payment schedule results. To have the system send the email to multiple addresses, type a 

semicolon between email addresses. 

5. 
Click Save.

### Check Preferences

#### Uploading Your Signature
*Source: `RP Accounting AP Setup User Guide.pdf`, Page 260*

Check Configuration 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Setup User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Check Preferences 

The system can use a digital signature that you upload to the system on printed checks so that 

the digital signature appears on the printed checks. The system uses the signature of the person 

who selects the invoices to pay, and not the person who prints the checks. 

Create the desired digital signature as a GIF or JPG and then upload it to either the bank account 

record or to your user preferences. You can set up signatures in the system in two places:  

• 
On the bank account record. You can upload a signature associated with a checking 

account in the Cash Management application. 

• 
In your user preferences. The signature that you upload with the My preferences option is 

associated with your company user ID.  

When signatures are set up in both places, the system uses the signature that is set up in your 

user preferences, not the one set up in the bank account record. The user who selects invoices on 

the Pay A/P invoices page is the one whose signature goes on the check; it is not the user who 

prints the actual check. 

If you do not upload a signature file in your preferences, then the system uses the signatures 

associated with the checking account instead. 

If a digital signature is not set up in either location, then the check prints with a blank signature 

line. 

For information on creating a signature file, see Creating a Digital Check Signature (on page 315). 

Uploading Your Signature 

(User Name) > My Preferences  


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > Configuration > My Preferences`


To upload a signature: 

1. 
On the Preferences page, find the Check preferences section. 

2. 
Click the Upload signature button.  

The Upload signature image box opens. 

3. 
Click the Choose files button and select the file with your signature image. After a moment, 

a preview of your signature appears. 

If you don’t like it, or if you are replacing an existing signature, click the Remove signature 

button and choose another signature image. 

4. 
Click the Save button. 

To adjust printer offsets, see Aligning Your Printer to Print Checks (on page 318).

*Source: `RP Accounting AP Setup User Guide.pdf`, Page 261*

Uploading Signatures for Users Other Than Yourself 

You can upload signatures for any user who is authorized by your company to sign checks. This is 

done by the user by clicking their sign-in name at the top of any page and then clicking My 

preferences. See Setting up check preferences for details. 

If you are an administrator and want to upload several signatures for users, you can do this 

(one-by-one) from the Company application. 

To upload signatures for users other than yourself: 

1. 
Open the Company menu, and then select the Setup tab. 

2. 
Select Users. 

3. 
Find a user that you have a signature file for and click the Preferences link. 

4. 
Find the Check signatures section and click the Upload signature button. The Upload 

Signature Image box appears.  

5. 
Click the Browse button and select the file with the signature image. After a moment, a 

preview of the signature appears.  

If you don’t like it, or if you are replacing an existing signature, click the Remove signature 

button and choose another signature image. 

6. 
Click the Save button. 

Repeat steps 3 -5 for additional users. 

Displaying Recent Credits on Checks 

You can show recent credits applied to invoices on the check or payment remittance. The credits 

that display are recent credits applied to invoices in the last 30 days by the vendor. 

The checks printed for vendors display recent credits applied to invoices in the last 30 days at the 

end of the check, grouped by vendor. The check includes the following information: 

• 
Invoice date: This is the date on the invoice. 

• 
Invoice number: This is the unique number assigned to the invoice. 

• 
Invoice Amount: This is the total invoice amount. 

• 
Credits Applied: This is the total credits applied towards an invoice. 

The system includes the information in the Print payment copies and Remittance email sent after 

successful payments using check and electronic payment methods. The system also includes 

invoices paid at the entity level using credits. 

When printing multiple checks for multiple vendors, the system includes recent credits only once 

per vendor.

Where to Get Electronic Payment Information for Your Bank 

When you decide to issue standard electronic payments, you must first inform your bank. The 

bank will in turn send you details about how it wants to format your electronic payments. This 

information is often in a document called a specification sheet. When you receive this information 

from your bank, you then enter that information on the Electronic Payment Bank Configurations 

page. 

The field names used on the Electronic Payment Bank Configuration page reflect the 

terminology of the payment service, making it easy to map the information on your bank’s 

specification sheet to the bank configuration record. 

If you select ACH, then ACH terminology is used.  

If you select EFT - Standard 005, then EFT related terminology is used.  

If you select BACS, then the terminology is related to BACS.

Adding an ACH Bank Configuration 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Cash Management > Setup > More > 
 ACH Bank Configurations`


Adding an ACH bank allows you to issue standard ACH payments from any checking account 

linked to this bank. 

Before performing any of the following procedures, contact your bank and get their ACH payment 
specifications. 

Filling in the File Header Information Section 

To add file header information for an ACH bank configuration: 

1. 
In the Bank ID field, type a unique ID for your bank. This ID can be any name that helps you 

identify the bank. Enter up to 20 characters. 

2. 
In the Immediate destination name field, type the name of your bank, as specified by the 

bank. Enter up to 23 characters. 

3. 
In the Immediate destination ID field, type the bank’s routing number. Enter up to 9 

characters. 

4. 
In the Immediate origin name field, type the name of the origin bank. Enter up to 23 

characters. 

5. 
In the Immediate origin ID field, type the origin bank’s routing number. Enter up to 10 

characters. 

6. 
In the Reference code field, check with your bank whether this should be filled in or left 

blank. Enter up to 8 characters. 

7. 
In the Status drop-down list, select whether this account is active or inactive. 

8. 
Select the Include EOF marker check box if your bank expects a carriage return at the end 

of the ACH payment file. 

Filling in the Bank SFTP Details Section 

1. 
In the Send to drop-down list, select the SFTP storage site for the bank. 

To configure SFTP details, open the Company application, and then select the menu’s 

Setup tab. In the Storage section, click the Cloud Storage option. See Adding a cloud 
storage target . 

2. 
In the Path field, enter the SFTP path where you want to upload the payment file. If you 

leave this field blank, the system uploads the file to the root folder in the selected SFTP site. 

3. 
Click the Save button. 

After generating the payment file, the system displays a check box next to the file in the 

Payment file list, which you can use to upload the file to the bank’s SFTP site.

#### Changing the Numbering Sequences for Payments
*Source: `RP Accounting AP Setup User Guide.pdf`, Page 278*

Electronic Payment Method Configuration 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Setup User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

The recommended setup generates the most common type of ACH payment file (service 

class code 220) and automatically sets up numbering sequences for standard ACH 

payments. 

If your bank uses service class code 200 for ACH payments 
Most banks expect to receive files that use service class code 220, which is a type of ACH 
payment file that contains only payments (credits). If your bank requires service class 
code 200, a format that allows both credits and debits: 
Clear the Use the recommended setup check box. 
In the Service class code drop-down menu, select 200 (credits only). Service class 200 will 
be used for compatibility with your bank, but the payment file will continue to contain only 
credits. 

2. 
Click the Save button. 

Changing the Numbering Sequences for Payments 

To make setup easier, we automatically create the numbering sequences required for ACH 

payments. This includes the batch and trace numbers that banks require for payment files and the 

payment numbers used when posting payments to Accounts Payable.  

If you want to override the default numbering sequences, you can do so in the Payment 

numbering setup section. 

Using Batch Numbers (Required) 

This is a unique numbering sequence used to automatically number payment batches. 

• 
Numbers must be 7 digits. with no prefixes or suffixes. 

• 
For the Sequence ID, it’s recommended that you incorporate the bank name (such as 

“MyBank_ACH_Batch”) to distinguish this batch from other batches. 

Using Trace Number Sequence (Required) 

This number is created by concatenating the bank’s routing number with a unique numbering 

sequence. 

• 
Numbers must be 7 digits, with no prefixes or suffixes. 

• 
You can use the same pattern as for summary numbers, but be sure to create a unique 

sequence with a different Sequence ID, such as “MyBank_ACH_Payment.” 

Using Payment Number Sequence 

This is required, but you can re-use a trace number. 

You can create a unique payment number sequence to post confirmed payments to A/P. You can 

also choose to use the same number sequence that you selected for the trace number.

#### Restricting a Bank Account to One or More Entities/Locations
*Source: `RP Accounting AP Setup User Guide.pdf`, Page 279*

Chapter 17: Electronic Payment Method Configuration

RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Setup User Guide 

Restricting a Bank Account to One or More Entities/Locations 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Cash Management > All > Search & Find > Bank Accounts > Edit > 
Restrictions`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Cash Management > Setup > Accounts > Bank Accounts > Edit > 
Restrictions`


In a shared multi-entity company, you can restrict an account to specific entities or locations to 

prevent entities from paying bills out of the wrong bank account. The ability to restrict bank 

accounts by entity is a configuration option that your system administrator can turn on in a 

multi-entity shared environment. See Entity Restrictions for more information. 

If you create a bank account at the entity level, then it is already restricted to that entity, and 
the Restrictions tab does not appear. Similarly, if you create a bank account at the entity level of 
a parent entity, it is not accessible to the parent entity ’s child entities/locations. If you want to 
apply location restrictions and allow child locations to access a bank account, you must create 
the bank account at the top level. 

Applying Entity Restrictions to a Bank Account 

To restrict a bank account: 

1. 
In the Bank accounts list, click the Edit link next to the account name.  

The Bank account information page opens. 

2. 
Click the Restrictions tab. 

3. 
Select a restriction option: 

• 
Unrestricted: This option makes the account available to the top-level company and 

all entity-level locations. This is the default. 

• 
Restricted to top-level only: This option makes the account inaccessible to entity-level 

locations. 

• 
Restricted: This option makes the account accessible to locations or location groups 

that you specify. 

4. 
If you select the Restricted option, click the Select button, and then use the multi-select box 

to choose one or more locations or location groups that can access the bank account. For 

instructions using the selection box, see Using the multi-select box (on page 329). 

You can’t remove a location restriction if the location is set as the owner location for the 
account, or if this bank account is configured as the default bank account.

#### Enabling Vendors to Receive ACH or Foreign Electronic Payments
*Source: `RP Accounting AP Setup User Guide.pdf`, Page 280*

Electronic Payment Method Configuration 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Setup User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

How Restricting by a Location Affects Inter-Entity Transactions 

When you restrict a bank account to a location or location group, only that location or group has 

access to that account. If another location is paying the A/P invoices for the first location, the 

location can’t use the account to pay A/P invoices, because it doesn’t own that account. If the 

locations are in different entities, the system can create an IET due-to/due-from transaction. 

For example, suppose a location for Texas receives an A/P invoice but a Corporate location pays it 

from an account owned by Corporate. In this case, an inter-entity transaction (due-to/due-from) 

will be created between the two locations or entities. You can see the IET in the following General 

Ledger report. 

In a case where a bank account is restricted by location and another location within the same 

entity pays the A/P invoice, no IET is generated because both locations are children of the entity. 

Enabling Vendors to Receive ACH or Foreign Electronic Payments 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > All > Vendors > Edit > Payment Information > 
Enable ACH/Enable Electronic Payments`


Before you can start using standard electronic payments (ACH, EFT, or BACS), you must select the 

vendors that can be paid via electronic payment and provide their bank account details. 

If you already have electronic payment information for vendors, you can import the information 

instead. See Importing Vendor Electronic Payment Information (on page 271). 

The following example shows how to enable ACH payments. If your company is a multi-currency 

company, additional electronic payment services (EFT or BACS) are available.  

To enable a vendor to receive ACH payments: 

1. 
Open the Accounts payable menu. 

2. 
Select Vendors. 

3. 
Find the vendor to change, and then click the Edit link. 

4. 
On the vendor record, select the Payment Information tab. 

5. 
In the Payment services section, click Enable ACH or Enable Electronic payments. 

6. 
Select ACH in the Bank format drop-down list. The Electronic payment bank details section 

opens. 

If your vendor needs to receive payments in EFT or BACS format, select the desired format 
in the Bank format drop-down list. 

7. 
Enter the routing number, account number, and account type.

Importing Vendor Electronic Payment Information (ACH, EFT, BACS) 

If you want to pay vendors electronically, you can save time by importing electronic payment 

information for your vendors. In the import file, you can enable electronic payment as a payment 

method for selected vendors and specify the routing number and other information required for 

depositing the payment in the vendor’s account.

Fill in the required fields.

VENDOR_ID: Type the unique vendor ID.

ELECTRONIC_PAYMENT_ENABLE: Type “True” or “T” to enable electronic payments.

• 
ACH_ACCOUNT_TYPE: Type “Checking Account” or “Savings Account.” This field is 

required when BANKFORMAT is set to “ACH.” 

• 
ACH_SEC_CODE: Type “CCD,” “CTX,” or “PPD.” This field is required when 

BANKFORMAT is set to “ACH.” The default value is “CCD.” 

• 
EFTBRANCHID: Type the financial institution’s branch ID. This field is required when 

BANKFORMAT is set to “EFT.” 

• 
EFTACCOUNTNUMBER: Type the account number. This field is required when 

BANKFORMAT is set to “EFT.” 

• 
BACSACCOUNTNAME: Type the name of the account. This field is required when 

BANKFORMAT is set to “BACS.”

### Roles and Permissions
*Source: `RP Accounting AP Setup User Guide.pdf`, Page 300*



#### Assigning Permissions for a New Feature
*Source: `RP Accounting AP Setup User Guide.pdf`, Page 300*

Common Tasks 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Setup User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Roles and Permissions 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > Setup > Users/Roles`


Permissions determine the specific features and activities that a user can access and the reports 

that the user can run. 

User-Based Permissions 

If you have not enabled roles in your company, then your company employs user-based 

permissions. With this permissions model, each user or user group has its own set of permissions. 

When you assign permissions to a particular user, your selections expand or limit what that user 

can see and do. 

Role-Based Permissions 

If your company enabled roles, then you use role-based permissions in your system. Using this 

permissions model, you can define a set of roles, and then assign the roles to users or user 

groups. For example, you can define an A/P Clerk role that includes permissions to enter and pay 

A/P invoices. 

Reviewing a User’s Permissions 

To review a user’s actual permissions: 

1. 
Open the Company menu, and then click the Setup tab. 

2. 
Select Users. 

3. 
Find the user, and then click the View permissions & roles link. The system opens the 

Permissions & roles report page. 

4. 
Review the user’s permissions. Optionally, click Print, and then use your printer’s dialog box 

to print the report. 

5. 
When you are finished viewing the user’s permissions report, click the Close button. 

Assigning Permissions for a New Feature 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > Setup > Users > Subscriptions > Permissions`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > Setup > Roles > Subscriptions > Permissions`


When RealPage adds a new feature, it often comes with new permissions that you must enable 

before users can use the new feature. 

To add permissions for a new feature: 

• 
Open the Company menu, and then select the Setup tab of the menu.

Click the Subscriptions link.  

4. 
Find the application that offers the new feature, and then select the Permissions link. The 

application’s permissions window opens. 

5. 
Find the new feature’s permission, and then enable the desired permissions. 

Be sure to check the Reports section at the bottom of the permissions page for any new 
reports that have been added to support the new feature. 

6.

7. 
Click the Save button on the Roles subscriptions page.

Configuring Permissions for Vendor Approvers 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > Setup > Roles > Subscriptions`


As a best practice, create a new role for each level of vendor approver and then assign the role to 

the appropriate users. 

Make sure each role is assigned to more than one user. Approvers cannot approve their own 
vendor requests, so if an approver adds or edits a vendor and they are the only person with 
permission to approve that vendor, the vendor request will get stuck in the approval queue. 

Creating Vendor Approver Roles 

To create a vendor approver role: 

1. 
Open the Company menu, and then select the Setup tab. 

2. 
Click Roles and then click the Add button. 

3. 
In Name, type an appropriate name to reflect the purpose of the role, such as Vendor 

approvers 1. 

If you name all vendor approver roles consistently, it will pay off when you assign the roles 
later. 

4. 
In the Description, describe the purpose of level one approvers: First level approves all 

vendors and then click the Save button.  

The Vendor approvers 1 - Roles subscriptions page is displayed.  

5. 
Select Accounts payable, and then click the Permissions link. 

6. 
Click 
 Expand to expand the permissions box. 

7. 
Find Approve vendors, and then select the List check box and the Level1 check box. 

8. 
Click the Save button. 

9. 
Repeat the process by creating new roles for Level2 and Level3 vendor approvals. 

We recommend setting up approval levels separately because the system sends one email 
for each level of approval. If you assign multiple levels to a single user or role, the approver 
will receive multiple emails for each vendor record in the approval workflow.

### Managing Lists
*Source: `RP Accounting AP Setup User Guide.pdf`, Page 305*

Chapter 19: Common Tasks 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Setup User Guide 

Managing Lists 

Lists provide access to like records. After you create a record, you can access it from its list. Most 

lists allow you to add, edit, view, and delete the records in it. You can also export the list to an 

XML file or a PDF file. After exporting a list, you can import the list into an external application like 

Excel, and then print the list from that application. 

Some lists allow you to access related information. For example, from the customers list, you can 

also access the customers A/R ledger and view a breakdown of the total amount that the 

customer owes. 

Since the list page is where you perform most of your work, the system provides several features 

to let you filter and sort lists and create and manage custom views of your data. 

• 
Sorting (on page 296): Sort the list alphabetically by the data in the desired column. 

• 
Filtering (on page 297): Filter lists so that you see only the data that you need. 

• 
Views (on page 304): Create a custom view to determine which columns appear in your lists, 

and apply a filter so that the list appears just the way you want it. 

Lists and Links 

Each list is unique and can offer links to let you navigate into an associated record to see more 

detailed data. For example, some invoice lists have a Preview link that, when clicked, opens the 

invoice in PDF format in a browser window. Another type of list may have a link to the customer 

record or the vendor record. 

Many reports present figures as links that, when clicked, open the associated record. This example 

shows links in the Debit and Credit columns of a journal entry. When you click a link, the system 

navigates to more information, allowing you to delve into the details.
