#### Filtering Lists
*Source: `RP Accounting AP Setup User Guide.pdf`, Page 307*

Chapter 19: Common Tasks 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Setup User Guide 

Filtering Lists 

Using Column Filters 

Column filters are text boxes that appear at the top of each column. Filters let you find items in a 

list that match the text that you enter. 

To apply a column filter: 

• 
Type the text that you want to find in the column filter, and then press ENTER. 

The system searches for matches, and then displays the matches in the list. 

If a text box does not appear at the top of a column, the column is not searchable. 

---


<!-- Page 308 -->
Common Tasks 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Setup User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Using the Wild Card Character 

• 
Use the % symbol as a wild card or placeholder. For example, typing “san%” in the City 

column’s filter would find both San Francisco and Santa Diego. 

• 
Placing the % in front of text tells the system to find these letters in the middle of text in a 

field. 

• 
Placing % at the end of a word tells the system to find the word and any letters that follow 

the word. 

• 
Use % to filter text columns only. The % symbol does not work on non-text columns such as 

date columns or amount columns. 

• 
For best success, anticipate differences and adapt your filter to account for them. 

To find records that contain a specific value: 

• 
Type the first part of the value. 

If you are looking for a contact in a city that starts with “San,” then you can filter the Contact 

list by typing “san” in the City filter field, then and pressing ENTER. The system searches for 

contacts with a city that begins with San, such as San Jose, San Francisco, and Santa Fe. 

• 
If you know only part of the text that you want to find, type “%” and then type the text that 

you have. 

For example, if you are looking for a contact with the letters “Will” in the name, but you do 

not have the full, correct name of the business, type “%will%” in the Contact name filter of 

the Contacts list, and then press ENTER. The system searches for matches, retrieving all 

contacts that contain the letters “will” in the Contact name field. 

Example 

Your company uses this standard format for naming invoice summaries: Invoices: Month Year. 

When you want to find all June summaries, type “%June” in the filter above the Summary column, 

and then press ENTER to apply the filter. Placing the % in front of June tells the system that the 

word “June” appears in the middle of the text string. Placing % at the end of the word “June” tells 

the system to find the word June and any word with letters that follow the word “June,” such as 

“Juneteenth.” 

---


<!-- Page 309 -->
Chapter 19: Common Tasks 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Setup User Guide 

Searches for Units 

You can search for a unit by entering any part of the unit ID. The system will find matches for any 

part of the unit ID string. For example, if the units in your property are configured with an 

alphanumeric pattern such as A-10, A-11, A12, B-20, B-21, B-22, then you can enter any part of 

the string, such as “22,” and the system will find B-22.  

The string does not have to start with the entered value to match. Typing “A” finds a list of units 

on the A floor as in our example or all units that have “A” in the unit ID. 

Displaying One-Time Items 

Some quick-entry records are set for one-time use. For example, you may have a seasonal 

customer, such as a Halloween supply store, or customers who pay only once and are not likely to 

purchase again. 

Create the customer record so that you can record the cash receipt, but because you don’t need 

to see that customer in your customer list regularly, flag the customer as Exclude from the 

company contact list. One-time customers aren’t included in the list unless you specify them to be 

included. 

To include one-time items in the list, select the Include One-Time check box. The system displays 

the one-time items along with regular items and adds a One-Time column to show which items 

are one-time records. 

Example 

You may have a customer who purchases from you only once a year, and you do not want to see 

the customer’s name in the list all the time. You still need to create a Customer record so that you 

can record the cash receipt, but since you do not need to see the customer in your Customers list 

regularly, edit the Customer record, and select the One-Time Use check box.

Including Inactive Records in Search Results 

Almost every kind of record in the system has a Status field with choices of Active and Inactive.

the inactive records in search results. 

•

search. The system refreshes the list and adds a Status column to indicate which items are 

active and which are inactive. 

• 
Clear the Include Inactive check box to prevent inactive items from appearing in the list. 

A list can contain items that are inactive but still present because they link to transaction data. For 

example, you may have a vendor who no longer carries items you need to purchase. In the vendor 

record, you flag the vendor as Inactive. Inactive vendors aren’t included in the list unless you 

select Include Inactive. 

One-time use customers do not appear in the Company application’s Contacts list unless you 
select the Include one-time check box.

Exporting Lists 

You can export most lists to several available file formats and then import the data into an 

external application, such as Microsoft Word or Microsoft Excel. 

Although you can export up to 25,000 rows, if you want to save time and effort, we recommend 

that you filter your list to pinpoint only the information you need to export by creating a custom 

view. That way, when you export the list, you’ll have a spreadsheet tailored to the information you 

need. You can export any view of this list for use on your local computer. 

Use column filters, advanced filters, and views to filter the data. For instructions, refer to 

Managing Lists. 

If you have a sorted and filtered list that you use consistently, you can create and save it as a 

custom report for convenience. With a custom report, you need to set the filtering and 

parameters only once to enable you to generate the report as needed after that. 

1. 
Click the Export button. 

2. 
Select the format to which you want to export the list. 

• 
CSV: Select this format if you plan to move the data from one program to another.

• 
Word: When you select this option, the system exports the list in Word format. If a list 

of conversion formats displays, select HTML document. 

• 
Excel: When you select this option, the system exports the list in XLS format. If you see 

an error message about file type and extension type incompatibility, you can disregard 

the message and select Yes. 

• 
PDF: Select this option if you plan to print or share the list. When you select this 

option, the system exports the list and tries to open the file in the browser. If 

prompted, select Yes to allow the PDF to open. 

•

and then import it into the system again.

Displaying a Hierarchical View 

Some lists, such as the Locations list, can display a hierarchical structure of parent-child 

relationships using icons and indentations. 

Use the Display Hierarchy check box to view the list to help you identify locations that are 

subsidiaries of parent records. 

Parent records can have up to five levels of child records, allowing you to view and act on the 

records as needed. You can still sort and search for records as you would in any view. 

If the parent record is not visible because of permission restrictions, or if you filtered the list in a 

way that the parent is not visible, the system still shows the child as indented and colored to 

indicate that it is a child in a relationship. 

To toggle between flat view and hierarchical view of a list: 

• 
To switch to a flat view, clear the Display hierarchy check box on the white bar above the 

list. Clearing the check box causes all items to be displayed by their unique ID, whether they 

have relationships to other items. 

• 
To return to the hierarchical view, select the Display hierarchy check box. 

The default for a list that has hierarchical items is to display the hierarchical view. 
Hierarchical items include Locations, departments, vendors, and customers.

General Ledger Accounts

> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > General Ledger > All >

To add a G/L account: 

1. 
From the top level, open the General Ledger menu. 

2. 
In the Search & Find section, click the 
 Add button next to the Accounts menu option. 

The General Ledger accounts page opens. 

3. 
Enter the account number. After you save the account record, the account number cannot 

be edited. 

We recommend using dimensions instead of sub-accounts. This simplifies reporting when 
rolling up for reports.  

4. 
In the Title field, type a name for the account as you want it to appear as the heading on 

reports, for example, Assets.  

After you save the account record, you have the option to create additional titles for the

from custom titles, such as account titles in other languages or a variation of an account 
title that an entity ’s users are more familiar with. 

5. 
In the Category drop-down list, select the category of account that you are creating. 

Categories are permanently pre-assigned to account groups, which are used in financial 

reports and graphs that are supplied with the system. 

For example, you would assign the Petty Cash account to the category Cash and Cash 

Equivalents, which is assigned to the Cash and Cash Equivalents account group and appears 

on financial reports and graphs that contain this account group. If you do not want this 

account to be in your financials, then delete the text in this field so it is blank. 

The Category field is displayed only for companies that were created with a setup template 

or chose one later. If you need to assign categories to many accounts, the easiest way is to 

export your chart of accounts, make the changes in the file, and then upload the file. 

When Your System Was Set Up With the Services Template 
By default, the categories Manpower and Direct materials are assigned to account groups

that are only used in the reports Project Profitability and Project Estimation Versus Actual. 
These two categories do not appear in balance sheet reports or income statements. If you 
assign an account to either of these two categories, and you want it to show up in your 
balance sheet, income statement, or other reports, you must manually assign these 
categories to the appropriate account groups. 

6. 
In the Account type drop-down list, select either Balance sheet account or Income 

statement account. 

• 
Balance sheet accounts are snapshots of the current state of a company’s assets, 

liabilities, and equity at a specific time. 

• 
Income statement accounts (sometimes called profit and loss statements) are 

cumulative for the selected period. 

7. 
For Normal balance, select either Debit or Credit. 

When you create an account, you specify whether the normal balance, from an accounting 

standpoint, is a debit or credit. For example, expense accounts are normally debit accounts. 

Sales accounts are normally a credit. If you were to run a Trial Balance report, the normal 

balance of the accounts is what determines whether the account is a credit or debit. 

8. 
For the Period end closing type, select whether the account is a closing or non-closing 

account. For closing accounts, select an account in the Close into account drop-down list. 

• 
Instead of manually closing accounts at year-end, you can set them to be closing 

accounts and then specify the account in which to close that period. 

• 
Income statement accounts should be closing accounts; balance sheet accounts 

should be non-closing accounts. 

• 
For all income statement accounts, the close-into account will typically be Retained 

Earnings. The system then zeros closing-type accounts into retained earnings at 

year-end. 

9. 
In the G/L account alternative drop-down list, select a G/L account for the system to use as 

an alternative payables account. The account override must be enabled for this field to 

appear. 

10. 
The default status is Active. If you want to prevent this G/L account from appearing in lists, 

select Inactive in the Status drop-down list. (You can still list inactive accounts by clicking 

the Include inactive check box in lists.) 

You cannot make a G/L account inactive when the account is selected on the configuration 
page of an application or if the account is being used in a budget. 

11. 
Select the Disallow Direct Posting check box to prevent direct entry of journal entries to the 

subledger control account (for example, Accounts Payable, Accounts Receivable, etc.).

*Source: `RP Accounting AP Setup User Guide.pdf`, Page 325*

Banking and Checks 

These are tasks related to banking and checks. 

Creating a Digital Check Signature 

The signature file must be 3.0” wide x 0.36” high, 150 dpi, and saved as a GIF or JPG file no larger 

than 10K. If you have a scanner and a little experience in computer graphics, you can create the 

signature yourself. If not, ask a local desktop-publishing service to scan your signature and resize 

it for you. 

1. 
Sign your name in a 3.0” wide by 0.36” high frame. 

2. 
Scan the signature. Use 150 dpi resolution. 

3. 
Save the file as a 16-bit color GIF or JPG file. The file size can’t exceed 10K. 

4. 
Open the file in a graphics program and verify that it appears correctly. 

5. 
Click the Save button. 

Don’t be concerned if your graphics program tells you that the size of the image is greater than 

3.0” wide by 0.36” high. However, be sure to maintain the correct aspect ratio of 3.0” wide by 

0.36” high. Otherwise, the system enlarges or reduces the image to fit the bounding box, so the 

image appears distorted both on your printed checks and through the check delivery service. 

---


<!-- Page 326 -->
Common Tasks 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Setup User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Good Digital Signatures 

The most effective signature fills the box, leaving little white space. 

If your signature does not fill the box, it appears distorted on your printed checks or through the 

RealPage Check Delivery service. 

Good: The signature fills the box. 

Too small: The signature leaves too much white space. 

Unclear: The signature is too small and too far to the left.

Aligning Your Printer to Print Checks 

(User Name) > My Preferences 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > Configuration > My Preferences`


This topic assists you in adjusting printer offsets to align your check PDFs with your printer. The 

adjustments are applied to any printer on which you print a PDF check image. The adjustment 

process does not affect the printing of non-RealPage PDFs or RealPage PDFs other than checks. 

The adjustments you make are unique to you as a user. Other users may have different PDF 

offsets. Thus, if you must have two sets of adjustment parameters for two printers, you need to 

have two users with different adjustment parameters. 

Measure the distance of the crosshairs from the top and left edges of the sheet of paper. Use a 

ruler that has a decimal scale. If the measurements are not exactly 1”, then click the adjustment 

controls on your Preferences page until the relative position of the printed image is exactly 1” 

from the top and left edges of the sheet of paper. 

The illustration below shows the controls. Click the horizontal arrows to move the image left or 

right; click the vertical ones to move the image up or down. 

Each click moves the image by 0.05.” Thus, if your image is offset to the right by 0.10,” click the 

horizontal offset left arrow 
 two times. If the image is offset downward by 0.15,” click the up 

arrow 
 three times.

Actions on Records 

These are tasks that you can perform on Accounts Payable records. 

Editing the line-item display 

If you are an administrator, RealPage Accounting enables you to customize field placement on the 

line-item table by promoting and demoting fields between the line item and its detail area. For 

example, if your company uses some dimensions more frequently, you can display the frequently 

used dimensions, including user-defined dimensions, at the line level, and move the 

less-frequently used dimensions to the line-item detail. 

Any change made to the display of line items in a transaction-entry screen affects all users of that 

screen. 

To edit the display of line items: 

1. 
On the appropriate transaction page, click More Actions, and then click Edit Entries layout. 

2. 
Click the line item of interest. The Show Details tab appears. 

3. 
Click Show Details. The line-item details appear in a drop-down. 

4. 
Drag a field to promote or demote it to or from the line-item level. 

Using Field-Level Controls in Drop-Down Lists 

The system offers two kinds of drop-down lists – those with field-level controls at the top and 

those without. This example shows the field-level controls. 

---


<!-- Page 333 -->
Chapter 19: Common Tasks

RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Setup User Guide 

Field Level Options 

The most common field level options are Add, View, and Find. 

• 
Add: If you cannot find the record that you need, you can add a new record right from 

where you need it. Clicking Add opens a new blank record for the same type of object. For 

example, if you are selecting G/L accounts, then clicking Add opens a new blank record so 

that you can create a new account. 

• 
View: Use the View command when you want to verify that you are selecting the correct 

record. Select the item that you want to view, and then click the View command to open the 

record. 

• 
Find: Use this option when you have looked through the drop-down list and don’t find the 

record that you need, but you believe that it exists. Click the Find option. The system opens 

a box in which you can type the text to search for the desired record. If you don’t find it, you 

can click Cancel and then click the Add option to add a new record. 

You must be at the top level to create new customer, vendor, and G/L account records.

Filtering without Field-level Controls 

This drop-down list does not have field-level controls at the top. In these lists, type the first letter 

of your selection to scroll to the first item in the list. 

In this example, we are searching for straight-line rent. 

Type “S” and the system places the focus at the top of the Ss in the list, just one item away from

Keep typing and the system will find your selection and insert it into the field for you. 

If you still don’t find what you need, click the Find link. 

In the example below, we are searching for the “Late” account label:

Type “L” to list only items that start with “L.” 

• 
Type “La” and the system inserts the value into your field, because it is the only item that 

starts with La. 

• 
In a more complicated situation, type Find. The system opens a selection box where you 

can filter the list so that you can choose the desired record.

attachment to a record (on page 344).

#### Duplicating Records
*Source: `RP Accounting AP Setup User Guide.pdf`, Page 340*

Common Tasks 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Setup User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Duplicating Records 

If your goal is to create one record and reuse it as the starting point for additional records, use 

the Duplicate function. Most types of records can be duplicated—including A/P invoices, A/R 

invoices, recurring invoices, adjustments, entities, vendors, contacts, journals, G/L accounts, 

user-defined books, document numbering sequences, contracts, service tickets, email templates, 

and reporting account sets. When you open a record and it includes a Duplicate button, you can 

use it as a template to quickly create a new record.  

For invoices, you can also create a future draft of an invoice as you add it, and set the date to 

create the future draft. See Adding an A/P Invoice Manually and look for the section called 

“Creating a Future Draft Invoice.” 

To duplicate recurring invoices, look for the Duplicate option that is located in the More actions 
button menu. 

To duplicate a record: 

1. 
Open the record that you want to duplicate by clicking View or Edit.  

2. 
Click the Duplicate button. The system creates a new record that is identical to the original. 

After you duplicate a record, the copy of the record stays open so that you can change its 

details.  

3. 
Fill in the fields.  

4. 
The system sets the status to Active. You can leave the status set to Active or select Inactive 

to prevent the item from appearing in lists. 

5. 
Click the Save button. You can also click the More actions button, and then select Save & 

New. The system saves the record and then opens a new blank record. 

---

Printing or Exporting a Record’s Details 

Use the Print to button to view and download the information as a PDF file or as an XML file.  

1. 
Click the Print to button. The Print to box opens.  

2. 
Select a format by clicking either the PDF or XML icon. 

Printing a PDF 

Use the PDF format when you need to print a copy of the information. 

1. 
Click the PDF icon. After a moment, the record opens in an external application that 

supports the PDF format, such as Adobe Reader. 

2. 
Use the application’s commands to print the record. Typically, the command sequence is 

File > Print. 

3. 
If needed, use the application’s Save command to save the record as a PDF file. 

Exporting as XML 

Use the XML format when you need to export the record and import it into an external 

application. 

1. 
Click the XML icon.  

The XML appears in the RealPage Accounting system window. 

2. 
Put your cursor in the window where the XML is displayed. 

3. 
Press CTRL + A to select all text. 

4. 
Press CTRL + C to copy the text. 

5. 
Open a new file in a text editor like Notepad. 

6. 
Press CTRL + V to paste the XML text into the new file. 

7. 
Save the file named with an XML extension. Example: Test.XML

Adding a Transaction Currency 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > Multi-currency > Transaction Currencies > Add`


To add a currency: 

1. 
In the Applications menu, select the Company application, and then click the All tab. 

2. 
In the Multi-currency section, select the Transaction currencies menu option. The

Filling In the Format Section 

1. 
In the Currency format drop-down list, select the nationality of the currency.

In the Currency subunit drop-down list, select the sub-unit of currency, such as cents, 

pence, or centavos. 

4. 
In the Currency symbol drop-down list, select the standard currency symbol. 

5. 
In the Thousand separator drop-down list, select the symbol that separates numbers into 

thousands—usually a comma. 

6. 
In the Decimal separator drop-down list, select the symbol that separates decimals— 

usually a period. 

7. 
In the Alignment drop-down list, select “Left” or “Right” to align the monetary units. This 

controls whether the currency symbol displays to the left or to the right of the number. 

Under Currency sample, the system displays a preview of how the currency will appear with the 
current settings.

### Attachments Overview
*Source: `RP Accounting AP Setup User Guide.pdf`, Page 350*



#### Before You Begin
*Source: `RP Accounting AP Setup User Guide.pdf`, Page 350*

Attachments 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Setup User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Attachments Overview 

Attachments are bundles of one or more files that you associate with a transaction or record, such 

as a letter of credit, an invoice, or a photo. For example, if you have a contract signed by a 

customer, you can attach the contract to the customer record. You can attach as many files or 

combinations of file types as you need and bundle them into a single attachment record. 

To attach a document, you first need to create an electronic version of it. If it is a paper copy, scan 

the document, and then save it as one of the supported file types:  

• 
Word 

• 
PDF 

• 
Excel 

• 
Text 

• 
JPG 

• 
PNG 

Attaching Files to Transaction Records 

The Enable single scan upload setting in your user preferences changes the way that the system 

treats attachments. These differences are described below: 

When scanning is disabled: 

• 
You can select one attachment record to associate with a transaction, but the attachment 

record can contain multiple files as needed. 

• 
You can create folders for storing attachments from the transaction record. 

• 
You can access the attachment folders from the transaction record. 

When scanning is enabled: 

• 
You can add multiple attachments to a transaction record. 

• 
You can scan a document to attach it directly to the transaction record. 

• 
You cannot create or access attachment folders. 

For instructions on enabling the Enable single scan upload option, see Enabling the Scanning 

Feature. 

Before You Begin 

Access can vary depending on your organization’s subscriptions and your permissions. If you do 

not see the option in the menu, then ask your System Administrator to check your permissions. 

• 
Decide if you need to add an attachment that is already stored in the system or if you need 

to upload a new document into the system. Existing attachments are files that someone has 

already added to the system. 

---

To work with attachments, you must have List and View permissions in the Company application 

for both Attachments and Attachment Folders. You cannot restrict access to attachment folders

Adding a New Attachment to a Record 

This topic describes how to attach a file to a record when the file is not yet stored in the system. 

To attach a file to a record when the file is already in the system, see Adding an Existing 

Attachment to a Record (on page 344). 

The steps for attaching documents to transactions and records are different depending on 

whether the Enable single scan upload option is enabled or disabled in your user preferences. 

Adding a New Attachment to a Record When Scanning is Disabled  

To add a new attachment to a record when scanning is disabled: 

1. 
Add a new record or edit an existing record to open the information page. 

2. 
Click the Attachments drop-down list, and then click the Add link. 

The Select attachments page opens. 

3. 
Type a unique ID for the attachment record. If your company is configured to auto-number, 

then the system automatically displays an ID for the attachment. 

4. 
Type a Name that identifies your attachment. If you leave this field blank, the system 

automatically adds a Name for the attachment based on the first file that you upload. You 

can change this name as needed. 

---


<!-- Page 353 -->
Chapter 21: Attachments 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Setup User Guide 

Since an attachment record may contain more than one file, choose a name that describes 

all of the files in your attachment. For example, if you attached 20 scanned invoices to 

support 20 invoices, then you could name the attachment “Invoice Scans - 20 Files.” 

5. 
Select the Folder where you want to store your attachment in the system. If you have the 

appropriate Attachment permissions, you can create a folder:  

• 
Click the down arrow beside the Folder field, and then click Add. 

• 
Type a Name for the folder. 

6. 
Optionally, type a Description of the attachment. 

7. 
In the Attach files section: 

• 
Click the Choose files button, select the file(s) you want to attach, and then click the 

Open button. Alternatively, you can drag and drop files directly from your file explorer 

into the browser window. 

• 
If you have Commercial Property Management or Condo and Co-Op, and you 

purchased the portal add-on, then the Display on portal check box also appears. 

Select the check box for any attachment that you want the tenant or owner to be able 

to access on their portal. 

8. 
Attach additional files as needed. 

9. 
Click the Save button. 

Adding a New Attachment to a Record When Scanning is Enabled 

To add a new attachment to a record when scanning is enabled: 

1. 
Add a new record or edit an existing record to open the information page. 

2. 
Find the Documents section. 

3.

button to upload it to the record. The file appears in the list of attachments.

Record for more information. 

4. 
Continue attaching files as needed. 

5. 
Save the record. 

When you save the record, the system stores the attached files in a new attachment record 

in the Attachments list.

### Importing Workflow
*Source: `RP Accounting AP Setup User Guide.pdf`, Page 356*

Importing 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Setup User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Importing Workflow 

In many places in the system, you can choose to import information instead of entering or editing 

each record manually. 

To import information in Accounting systems: 

1. 
Download a template. 

2. 
Enter your data (on page 349), and then save the file as a comma delimited (.csv) file (on 

page 354). 

3. 
Import the file into the system.  

4. 
As needed, resolve errors in the .csv file and re-import. 

As a best practice, before you import any objects, export the object list. This provides a “before” 
record in case you need to make post-import comparisons. 

Downloading Templates 

Most imports start with getting a template from the page that stores the objects you are 

importing. Typically, these are list pages. When you download these templates, they are tailored 

to your company, including specific dimensions and custom fields.  

As a best practice, always download a new template before entering your data, even if you have 
downloaded the template in the past. This ensures you are using the most current version of the 
template. 

To download an import template: 

1. 
Go to the page that lists the objects you are importing.  

2. 
Click the Template button in the upper-right corner of the page. 

• 
The system either downloads the file or prompts you to open or save the file, 

depending on your browser’s settings. 

• 
By default, this file uses the .xls file type. 

3. 
Open the file. 

---


<!-- Page 357 -->
Chapter 22: Importing 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Setup User Guide 

Entering Data and Saving the File 

To enter your data: 

1. 
Open the template you downloaded from the object’s list page. 

2. 
Enter your information.  

While entering information, keep in mind to: 

• 
Use header descriptions in the template as a guide for entering information correctly. 

• 
Leave the template headers as they are. Any header changes will cause an import 

error. 

• 
Complete every required field. Any missing required information will cause an import 

error. 

• 
Avoid using leading zeros in ID fields where possible. If you must use leading zeros in 

IDs, convert the column of ID numbers to text format in Excel before importing the file 

content. You must do this every time you import information that requires IDs. 

3. 
When your changes are complete, use the Save as option to save the file as a comma 

delimited (.csv) file. 

Importing your Data 

1. 
On the page that stores the objects you are importing, click Import. The system opens the 

Import (object type) information box. 

2. 
Click Choose file, select the file you saved, and then click Open. 

3. 
By default, the Date format drop-down list value is “MM/DD/YYYY.” Use this drop-down list 

to select the date format used in the import file. 

This list is available for only some imports. 

4. 
By default, the File encoding drop-down list is set to “auto detect.”  

This setting should accommodate most imports, but you can change this as needed. 

---


<!-- Page 358 -->
Importing 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Setup User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

5. 
If you are uploading a large file, select the Process offline check box. This allows the system 

to process the import file while you continue to work in the system. 

If you do not select this check box, you must wait until the upload process is complete. 

6. 
By default, the Email results to this address field is pre-filled to the email address of the 

person currently signed on.  

You can change this as needed. To enter multiple email addresses, enter each email address 

separated by a semicolon (;) or comma (,). 

When the system completes the process, it sends a success or error email message to the 

entered Email results to this address email address(es). If the import had any errors, those 

errors are listed in this email message. 

7. 
Depending on the data you are importing, the Import (object type) information box might 

include additional fields, such as Date format or Post to. For more information about these 

additional fields, refer to the documentation for that specific import process. 

8. 
Click Import. 

The system processes the import and shows a success or error message, depending on the 

import results. 

9. 
Click Done. 

Resolving Errors 

There are a number of reasons imported records fail, such as duplicate entries or invalid field 

content. RealPage provides information about the failed records in an attempt to help you fix the 

import error. 

When an import fails: 

• 
The confirmation page shows how many records failed and provides a link to download a 

.csv file that contains only the failed records.  

If you close this box without downloading this file, you cannot re-access this file. 

• 
The system sends an email message to the email address provided on the Import 

information box. This email includes a list of the error(s) that occurred in the failed import, 

the error code, and each unique instance of the error. 

The error message email lists error messages in sections, with the sections listed in the order the 

records erred in the file. However, the error at the bottom of each section is the first error that 

was encountered for that record during import. 

As a best practice when reading the error message email, start at the top of the email, scroll to 

the first error message section, and then read the error message section from the bottom up. 

Repeat this process for each error section. 

---



#### Filling In an Import Template with Data
*Source: `RP Accounting AP Setup User Guide.pdf`, Page 359*

Chapter 22: Importing 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Setup User Guide 

The example below shows a sample error message.  

================================================== 

Error BL01001973  

================================================== 

BL01001973-1 Description: Duplicate account number. The account number 
‘4150’ already exists. 

BL01001973-1 Correction: Enter unique account number.  

BL01001973-2 Description: Unable to create record. Could not create GL 
Account record!  

================================================== 

• 
In this example, start at error “BL01001973-2 Description: Unable to create record. Could not 

create G/L Account record!”  

• 
As this error does not identify the root issue, look to the next error “BL01001973-1 

Correction: Enter unique account number.” This identifies why the G/L account wasn’t 

created, but hasn’t identified how to correct the issue.  

• 
The final error message, “BL01001973-1 Description: Duplicate account number. The 

account number ‘4150’ already exists” describes the issue in more detail and suggests a 

correction – find and replace the duplicate account number. 

Error codes, such as BL01001973 above, are internal codes. These internal codes might help 

RealPage locate the source of a systemic issue if one is identified.  

Filling In an Import Template with Data 

Perform the following steps for each item that you want to import: 

1. 
Open the template in Excel and review the data structure. The information in the template 

file can help you formulate extraction queries. 

2. 
Export the data from your other source. 

3. 
Copy the exported data into the template file for the same kind of object. Take care to 

exactly match the template’s data structure as you do this. 

Avoid using leading zeros in ID fields. If you must use leading zeros in IDs, convert the 
column of ID numbers to text format in Excel before importing the file content. Excel does 
not remove the leading zeros when you save the file. Remember to do this every time you 
use a template to import information that requires IDs. 

4. 
Fill in the required columns. 

5. 
Save the file in CSV format (on page 354). 

Now that you’ve entered your data and looked through it for any of the common issues imports 

can have, you are ready to import your file to your system.

#### Preparing Your CSV File for Import
*Source: `RP Accounting AP Setup User Guide.pdf`, Page 360*

Importing 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Setup User Guide

Preparing Your CSV File for Import 

The Import data page is a quick way to import your information into the system. However, the 

way you prepare your CSV files directly affects the success or failure of importing your data. Learn 

the CSV import process to streamline the import process. 

This topic provides general information about preparing CSV files for import. Links to information 
about specific templates can be found in the Import data into the system, which lists all import 
topics. 

Workflow 

The following illustration shows the steps to download, prepare, and import a CSV file. 

Most imports start with getting the most recent template from the Import data page. When you 

get your templates from this list, you get templates that have been tailored to your specific 

company, including specific dimensions. 

Next you add your data, using the correct formatting as explained in the template. After you’ve 

added your data, you should then review the data with our best practices in mind. This helps 

eliminate anything that might make your import fail. 

After preparing your data, you are ready to import. 

Downloading a Template 

We recommend downloading a new blank template from the Import data page whenever you 

import information into the system. This is important because: 

• 
Templates in the Import data page are automatically customized based on your company 

configuration, including dimensions and custom fields you created. 

• 
Templates can be updated by RealPage at any time, especially when a new version of 

RealPage Accounting is released. This means that an older template might not work. 

To download an import template: 

1. 
Open the Company menu. 

2. 
Click Import data. The Import data page opens with a list of information that you can 

import into the system. 

3. 
Decide on the type of information to upload, and then click the Template link associated 

with that information. 

---

RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Setup User Guide 

Other Templates 

RealPage may have additional CSV import templates that are not found on the Import data page. 

Contact your RealPage Support Representative for any templates that have been customized for 

your company. 

Adding Your Data 

After you download the appropriate template, add your data. 

The following example shows a portion of a standard CSV file for importing accounts receivable 

invoices after it has been opened in Excel, but before data has been added. The top row is the 

header row, (the data labels for all of your data), and the second row contains descriptions of the 

kinds of data to enter in the column. 

a) Some fields are not required. 

b) Some fields are required. 

c) Header row 

d) Header description row 

Each template contains a set of pre-defined headers, such as BUDGET_ID, ACCT_NO, and soon. 

You enter your data into the blank cells below the header and header description rows without 

changing the headers. 

It is important to read the description for each of the column headers. Some columns are 
required and if left blank will cause your import to fail. 

---

RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Setup User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

The following illustration shows a portion of the template after the data has been added. The 

description row has been hidden for this example. 

To add your data: 

1. 
Open the template that you downloaded from the Import data page. 

2. 
Enter your information. Use the header descriptions as a guide for how to enter information 

correctly. 

• 
Do not change the headers. 

The header titles in the header row correlate to fields in UI. Incorrect header titles will 

cause an import error. When you download a template, the correct headers are in the 

template. 

• 
Read the header descriptions. 

The header description is the cell under the header row that explains what type of 

information is accepted for each column. If you enter information in the wrong format, 

or with a value not accepted by the column, it will cause an error in your import. 

• 
Enter required information. 

Some data is required, while others are not. Read the description field to determine 

which information is required. If you do not enter the required information, your 

import will fail. 

3. 
After entering your data, save the file as a comma-separated value (CSV) file. When saving 

from Excel, select the comma delimited file type. The file will have the file extension .csv 

after you save it.

Order of CSV Imports 

In some cases, CSV imports must be performed in a specific order because of dependencies 

within the data. For example, if you have transactions that require locations, but you have not 

entered or imported the locations, the transaction import fails. 

It is always best to follow the order of the steps as they are presented in the Import data page 

when performing any type of import. Not all the steps are required. For example, you may not use 

territories anywhere in your accounting data, therefore creating them is optional. 

In a few cases there are circular references. For example, an employee record can reference a 

department and vice versa. Problems that would otherwise result from such circular references 

have been eliminated for the purposes of importing by removing certain items. If you absolutely 

must have this data, you need to enter it manually. 

Formatting Dates 

When uploading your CSV file, you can select a format for the dates in your file. 

The RealPage Financial Suite supports 24 date formats: 

DD MM YY 
MM DD YY 
YY MM DD 

DD.MM.YY 
MM.DD.YY 
YY.MM.DD 

DD/MM/YY 
MM/DD/YY 
YY/MM/DD 

DD-MM-YY 
MM-DD-YY 
YY-MM-DD 

DD MM YYYY 
MM DD YYYY 
YYYY MM DD 

DD.MM.YYYY 
MM.DD.YYYY 
YYYY.MM.DD 

DD/MM/YYYY MM/DD/YYYY 
YYYY/MM/DD 

DD-MM-YYYY MM-DD-YYYY 
YYYY-MM-DD 

When you select a date format here, the system attempts to import your file using the selected 

date format. If the system can’t import your file with the selected date format, it attempts to 

discover the date format used in your file and import the data using that date format.

#### Importing the CSV File
*Source: `RP Accounting AP Setup User Guide.pdf`, Page 365*

Chapter 22: Importing 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Setup User Guide 

Importing the CSV File 

Now that you’ve entered your data and looked through it for any of the common issues imports 

can have, you are ready to import your file into the system. 

To import your CSV file: 

1. 
Open the Company menu. 

2. 
Select Import data. 

3. 
Find the information type you want to import, and then click the corresponding Import link. 

4. 
Click the Choose file button, and then select the CSV file that you want to import. 

5. 
If the CSV file includes dates that are not in mm/dd/yyyy format, select the date format that 

the data uses in the Date format field. 

The system attempts to import your file using the selected date format. If the system can’t 

import your file with the selected date format, it attempts to discover the date format used 

in your file and import the data using that date format. 

6. 
Leave the File encoding option set to Auto detect unless you’re unable to import your file. 

Depending on your operating system, you may need to select a different type of file 

encoding. 

7. 
If your import box includes a Post to section, select one of the following: 

• 
Select Historical if your data is not active. 

• 
Select General Ledger to post imported invoices to the G/L. 

8. 
If the file that you’re importing is large, consider selecting the Process offline option to 

process the import offline. This will cause the import to run at a later time, when the system 

is less busy. If you prefer to import the data immediately and wait for the results, do not 

select the Process offline check box. 

9. 
Type the email address to which import results and errors should be sent in the Email 

results to this address field. You can enter multiple email addresses, separated by a 

semicolon (;) or comma (,). 

RealPage highly recommends entering an email address. 

10. 
Click the Import button. After an import, the system informs you if the import was 

successful and how many records were imported. 

In a completely successful import, the confirmation page lets you verify that all of the 

records in your original file were successfully imported without having to manually verify 

them.

#### How to Read Paths
*Source: `RP Accounting AP Setup User Guide.pdf`, Page 371*

Chapter 23: Help and Support 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Setup User Guide 

How to Read Paths 

If you have ever been puzzled over a path in the documentation, this topic describes what it all 

means. 

Application Menus and Tabs 

Most paths begin with the Applications menu. This menu is located in the upper-left corner next 

to the Home button. When you select an application, the name of the Applications menu 

changes to the application that you selected. 

Menus have two tabs, All and Setup. The All tab is available to all users, but the Setup tab is 

restricted to users with full or limited administrator privileges. 

The Company application has two tabs, All and Setup. The All tab contains setup options for 
global features and is available to all users with the appropriate permissions. The Setup tab is 
restricted to administrators only. 

Simple Paths 

This is an example of a simple path: 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > General Ledger > All > Search & Find > Journal Entry`


The first three parts in a path are standard; they translate to “Click the Applications menu (a), 

select the name of the application (b), and then select the menu tab (c).” 

---


<!-- Page 372 -->
Help and Support 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Setup User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

The next steps in the path—the menu section (d) and the menu option (e)—direct you to a 

specific list or page in the application. 

a) Click the Applications menu.  

b) Select the application. 

c) Select the menu tab. 

d) Find the menu section or subsection, if any. 

e) Click the menu option.  

If you see the 
 icon in a path, then you can click the  icon in front of the menu option to add 
a new blank record. 

Paths with Multiple Options 

Some paths offer multiple choices. The choices are separated with a “/” symbol.  


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Receivable/Accounts Payable > Setup > Taxes > Authorities > 
View/Edit`


In this example, Accounts Receivable/Accounts Payable means that the same option is available 

in two applications’ menus, Accounts Payable and Accounts Receivable. Likewise, View/Edit 

means that you can select either the View or the Edit link to get to the page that you need.

Audit Trails 

Each action you take can impact your financial statements, so both internal and external 

stakeholders need to know how things have changed and who made those changes. The system 

audit trail keeps track of the changes so that you know who made changes to a particular record 

and when they made the changes. The View audit trail command is available on most records. 

Viewing Audit Trails 

You can access the audit trail of a record. The method of accessing the audit trail varies based on 

the record type. 

Accessing the Audit Trail  

1. 
Open the record that you want to examine. 

2. 
Click the More actions button, and then select the View audit trail option.  

Instead of the More Actions button, some records have a View Audit Trail button. 

The Audit trail list opens with a list of changes that users have made.  

Exporting a Record’s Audit Trail 

You can export data from the audit trail to a file in one of three formats, Microsoft Excel, CSV, or 

PDF. 

1. 
Open the audit trail. 

2. 
Click the audit trail’s More actions button, and then select the format to which you want to 

export: 

• 
Export to CSV 

• 
Export to Excel 

• 
Export to PDF 

If the audit trail table is lengthy, you can change the size of the list. From the More actions 
drop-down list, select Table size, and then select the number of rows that you want to be 
able to view. 

---

*Source: `RP Accounting AP Setup User Guide.pdf`, Page 374*

Help and Support 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Setup User Guide

Fields 

Audit Trail Columns 

Date 
This is the date and time of the change to the record, presented in the time zone 

defined in your preferences. 

Action 
This column indicates the type of update made to the record (whether it was 

created, modified, or deleted). It also indicates whether the system performed the 

action as part of a workflow, or if a user performed the action. 

Completed by This is the ID of the user who made the change. 

If the transaction is an eInvoice or oInvoice, the audit trail displays 

realpageaccounting as the user who submitted the transaction. This is because 
eInvoices and oInvoices are created electronically, either by the vendor through 
Storefront or through Invoice Processing. 

The system previously designated CPAUser as the user who submitted 
electronic invoices. 

Source 
This is the source from which the record was accessed or changed. 

Field 
This is the name of the field that was changed. 

Before 
This is the data that appeared in the field before the user saved the change. 

After 
This is the changed data that appears in the field after the user saved the change. 

Buttons 

Audit Trail Box/Audit Trail Page 

Done 
Saves any changes and opens the previous page 

Help 
Opens the Online Help page 

More actions 
Opens a drop-down list with the following options: 

• 
Export to CSV: Downloads the report as a CSV file 

• 
Export to Excel: Downloads the report as an XLS file 

• 
Export to PDF: Downloads the report as a PDF file 

• 
Table size: Allows you to select the number of rows you want to 

display per application page

A/P Reports 

This chapter describes each report in detail. The reports are presented in the same order as they appear on the 

Accounts Payable menu. A/P reports are grouped into two sections:  

• 
Vendors reports  

• 
A/P invoices and registers 

Standard A/P reports are reports that are typical to any Accounts Payable application and have already been 

created for you. You can either run them as they are or make slight modifications to them, such as setting filters to 

specify which items to include and from what time period or selecting from formatting options. 

You create standard reports by configuring the filters available in the report settings page. Depending on the 

report, the report settings page presents 10-30 filter options such as accounting period, custom date ranges, 

detail level, summary views, sorting, grouping, and dimensional analysis.

## List of A/P Reports
*Source: `RP Accounting AP Reports User Guide.pdf`, Page 10*

A/P Reports 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Reports User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

List of A/P Reports 

A/P Ledger report (on page 120) 

This report shows a list of vendors to whom you owe or owed money and either how many days it 

took you to pay them or how many days past due your payment is. Use this report to determine 

how well you are paying your accounts payable. 

A/P Recurring report (on page 128) 

This report shows a list of recurring A/P invoices from your vendors, along with details about the 

recurring payments, such as the frequency with which the A/P invoice is paid, how many times the 

recurring bill has been paid, the term, amount and so on. 

A/P Invoice Analysis report (on page 142) 

This report helps you analyze your purchases by showing you the expense line items in A/P 

invoices. For example, this report can show you how much of a certain type of stationery you 

ordered over a specific period of time and from which vendors. Use this report to review your A/P 

invoices. 

A/P Invoice Register report (on page 135) 

This report provides you with the list of A/P invoices you received from the specified vendors in 

the specified time period. Each line of the report contains information about the A/P invoice, 

including its date, the vendor ID and name, the A/P invoice number, the description (if any) you 

have entered, the due date, and the amount of the A/P invoices. 

Asset Report (on page 198) 

Use this report to keep track of the assets that you have on hand. The report shows the assets’ 

categories and types, their location, identifying numbers, and dates. 

Check Register report (on page 214) 

This report allows you to view and output check register entries. You can also create a package of 

documents and store the package in the reporting portal. 

Contract Activity Report (on page 203) 

This report allows you to view the list of contracts across the company, for one property or all 

properties, and for one contract or all contracts. 

Document Dashboard report (on page 176) 

This report shows the number of document images queued for action.

Expense Report Ledger (on page 193) 

The summary version of this report shows the list of expense reports, their status, and totals. The 

detail version of this report shows the list of expenses and the status of invoices. 

Management Fee report (on page 181) 

This report lists accounts and the fee amounts charged. 

RealPage Payments report (on page 186) 

This report lists payments made to RealPage Payments, the third-party payment service. 

Reclassification report (on page 208) 

This report displays a list of documents with data that was reclassified from one account to 

another in the past month and the names of those who reclassified them. Use this report to 

reclassify expenses from one account to another and 1099 categories. 

Recurring A/P Invoice Status report (on page 170) 

This report shows the list of recurring invoices from your vendors, along with details about the 

recurring payments. 

Selected A/P Invoices report (on page 165) 

This report shows invoices selected for payment that have not yet been confirmed. 

Top Expense report (on page 152) 

This report shows the top 20 or top 50 expenses that are posted, paid, and selected for payment 

for the time period. 

Unit Cost report (on page 159) 

This report shows unit costs. Use this report to review your highest expenses. 

Vendor Aging report (on page 9) (Supplier Aging report) 

This report shows a list of vendors (suppliers) to whom you owe or owed money and either how 

many days it took you to pay them or how many days past due your payment is. Use this report 

to determine how well you are paying your accounts payable. 

Vendor Insurance report (on page 48) (Supplier Insurance report) 

This report shows a list of vendors (suppliers) and their insurance coverage information. You can 

filter the report to see just vendors who have required insurance, and by insurance expiration 

date.

Reports Workflow 

This workflow represents creating a simple report. 

1. 
Select the desired report. 

2. 
Set up the report’s parameters: 

• 
Time period 

• 
Filters 

• 
Format 

• 
Titles 

3. 
Run the report. 

• 
If you don’t get the results that you expected, then click the Customize button, change 

the parameters, and then run it again. 

• 
If you are satisfied with the results, then process and store the report. 

• 
If you want to run it again some other time, then you can memorize the report’s 

settings.  

You can also: 

• 
Email the report. 

• 
Print the report. 

• 
Export the report into another file format. 

• 
Add the report to a dashboard.

### Vendor (Supplier) Aging Report
*Source: `RP Accounting AP Reports User Guide.pdf`, Page 15*

Chapter 1: A/P Reports 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Reports User Guide 

Vendor (Supplier) Aging Report 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > All > Reports > Vendors Reports > Vendor Aging`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Spend Management > All > Reports > Vendor Reports > Vendor Aging`


The Vendor aging report shows how long invoices from vendors have been outstanding. The 

report lists vendors with outstanding invoices and shows either how many days it took you to pay 

them or how many days past due your payment is. The report shows: 

• 
Vendors and suppliers you owe money to 

• 
How much you owe 

• 
How long those amounts have been due  

This report also can be generated as a chart. See Vendor Aging chart (on page 272). 

Report Usage 

Use this report to determine how well you are paying your accounts payable. 

• 
Spot and correct problems in the management of payables early enough to protect your 

trade credit with the vendor. 

• 
Avoid late fees. 

• 
Manage and improve cash flow. The report gives you a good indication of the amount of 

cash needed to cover your expenses. Compare what your expenses were during the same 

period last year. 

The report provides a clear snapshot of liabilities.  

Some A/P invoices do not appear in the report: 

• 
Escheated invoices 

• 
Aged payables appear in the Vendor Aging report only if you select the Include aged 

payable invoices check box. 

The Vendor Aging report is a standard report. If you are looking for information on financial 
reports, see Creating a Financial Report.

•

•

Summary Report 

Each row represents a vendor. The columns show how long their invoices have been unpaid. 

“0-30” represents zero days to 30 days, “31-60” represents 31 days to 60 days, and so on.

Customizing and Running the Vendor Aging Report 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > All > Reports > Vendors Reports > Vendor Aging`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Spend Management > All > Reports > Vendor Reports > Vendor Aging`


The Vendor Aging report is a standard report. If you are looking for information on financial 
reports, see Creating a Financial Report. 

To customize and run the Vendor aging report: 

• 
From the Vendor Aging Report page, fill in the Reporting Currency section. This section 

appears only when you are working in a multi-currency system. 

• 
In the Reporting currency drop-down list, select the currency to use for the report. 

• 
In the Convert currency from section, select whether to convert the currency using the 

entity’s Base currency or the currency that was used in the transaction, Transaction 

currency. 

Filling In the Time Period Section 

Define the time period for the report. 

1. 
From the Aging periods drop-down list, select the aging period to include in the report. 

Aging periods are user-defined. For information, see Configuring A/P aging periods. 

2. 
In the Report as of section, select Today to report vendor aging as of today. Select Selected 

date and then type a date or click 
 Calendar and select a date. 

Type “p” in a date field to automatically insert the last day of the prior month. See 
Specifying Dates in Getting Started for a full list of shortcut keys related to entering 
dates.  

---


<!-- Page 19 -->
Chapter 1: A/P Reports 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Reports User Guide 

3. 
In the Date to use section, select the date type for which you want to see invoices. 

• 
A/P Invoice date: Show invoices that have the specified A/P invoice date. 

• 
Due date: Show invoices that have the specified due date. 

• 
G/L posting date: Show invoices that posted to the general ledger on the specified 

date. 

4. 
In the Based on section, select the date type to determine how the report is aged. 

• 
A/P invoice date: Base the aging on the date of the vendor invoice. 

• 
Due date: Base the aging on the invoice’s due date. 

• 
G/L posting date: Base the aging on the date the invoice posted to the general ledger. 

Filling In the Filters Section 

Set up a filter as needed. Using filters is optional. 

1. 
To filter the report by A/P accounts, click the Select button to open the multi-select box, 

and then select the desired A/P accounts. 

If you have already selected items, in place of the Select button, a box appears that shows a 

list of the selected items.  

2. 
Use the From vendor and To vendor drop-down lists to select the beginning and ending 

vendor in a range to include a range of vendors (suppliers) in the report. 

• 
From the From vendor drop-down list, select the first vendor in a range of vendors to 

include in the report. The system fills in the To vendor box with the same vendor, 

setting it up in case you want to include only one vendor in the report. 

• 
From the To vendor drop-down list, select the last vendor in a range of vendors. 

3. 
From the Vendor type drop-down list, if you want to limit the report to a certain vendor 

type, select the type here. 

The next two drop-down lists appear only if your company is multi-currency enabled. 

4. 
From the Transaction currency drop-down list, if you want to filter for a specific transaction 

currency, select the currency to filter for. 

5. 
From the Exchange rate types drop-down list, select the desired exchange rate type to filter 

for. 

---

6. 
From the Location drop-down list, to limit the report to a specific location, select the 

location. 

• 
Select the Individual report check box to create a separate report for each selected 

location. 

• 
Select the Prompt on run check box to have the system prompt you for a location 

when it is about to run the report. 

7. 
From the Department drop-down list, to limit the report to a specific department, select the 

department here. 

• 
Select the Individual report check box to create a separate report for each selected 

department. 

• 
Select the Prompt on run check box to have the system prompt you for a department 

when it is about to run the report. 

8. 
From the Show for drop-down list, select one of the following options: 

• 
All locations: Include vendor aging data for all locations. 

• 
This location: Include vendor aging data for the selected location only. 

• 
Child locations: Include vendor aging data for the additional locations (buildings) on a 

property. 

9. 
From the Job drop-down list, select the job to filter by. 

If you want to filter by job and the Job drop-down list does not appear below the Show for 
(locations) section, go to the Format section of the page, and select the Include G/L detail 
check box, and then return to the Filters section. 

Filling In the Format Section 

Use this section to specify the type of report you want to create. 

1. 
From the Sort by drop-down list, select how you want to sort the report. You can sort by 

Vendor ID, Vendor name, Amount, Amount (descending order), G/L posting date, or G/L 

posting date (descending order). 

The abbreviation “desc” after an option means “Descending order”—in this case, reverse 
alphabetical or reverse numerical order. The default sort order and number of options 
changes depending on whether you want a summary report or a detail report. Vendor ID is 
the default sort order.

2. 
Use the Group by drop-down list to arrange related data together by group according to

drop-down box and click on these options: 

• 
None

•

•

3. 
In the Report type section, select Summary or Detail. 

• 
The Summary report type condenses all account details to a single line. 

• 
The Detail report type displays one line per customer per account. It also includes 

additional columns of information. 

4. 
Select the Include G/L detail check box to include invoice details in the report. The 

additional details include G/L account, location, memo, department, job, and unit for each 

line item. This option is available only when you select the Detail report type. 

5. 
Select the Include aged payable invoices check box to include aged payable invoices in the

6. 
Select the Include job check box to include invoices associated with job records. This option 

is selectable only when the Include G/L detail check box is selected. 

This option is available only when your company subscribes to the Job Cost application. 

7.

This option cannot be combined with an A/P account filter. If you filter for an A/P account,

pending approval in the Vendor Aging report.

10.

You can use up to 80 characters, including spaces, in each title, subtitle, and footer.

You can type over any default name that appeared automatically. 

2.

The subtitle displays in smaller type, directly beneath the main title. 

3.

Footer text displays at the bottom center of the report.

#### Running the Vendor Aging Report to Reconcile to the General Ledger
*Source: `RP Accounting AP Reports User Guide.pdf`, Page 23*



##### Vendor (Supplier) Aging Report Columns
*Source: `RP Accounting AP Reports User Guide.pdf`, Page 23*

Chapter 1: A/P Reports 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Reports User Guide 

Running the Vendor Aging Report to Reconcile to the General Ledger 

To use the Vendor Aging report to reconcile Accounts Payable to the General Ledger: 

1. 
Run the Vendor Aging report (on page 12). 

2. 
Identify any discrepancies by reviewing the Vendor Aging report and balances for Accounts 

Payable in the General Ledger. 

3. 
Ensure that the total amounts on the Vendor Aging report match the corresponding totals in 

the General Ledger. 

4. 
Investigate and resolve any variances or discrepancies between the two.  

If you have discrepancies, check the following: 

1. 
Open the Accounts Payable menu, click the Setup tab, and then select the Configuration 

option. Ensure that Display reversals as historical transactions is selected. 

2. 
Check to make sure that there are no invoices on the Vendor Aging report with a payment 

date that is earlier than the invoice date.

Vendor Aging Report Troubleshooting

##### Why Doesn’t the Vendor Aging Report Match my A/P Balance?
*Source: `RP Accounting AP Reports User Guide.pdf`, Page 28*

A/P Reports 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Reports User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Why Doesn’t the Vendor Aging Report Match my A/P Balance? 

If the Vendor Aging report does not match the A/P balance, the difference is usually caused by 

timing, filters, aging settings, or transactions such as credits, voids, and adjustments. In most 

cases, the report and the ledger are not being compared on the same basis. 

Common Causes 

1. 
Different as-of dates 

If the Vendor Aging report is run for one date and the A/P balance is reviewed for another, 

the totals may not match. 

2. 
Filter differences 

The report may be limited by: 

• 
Property 

• 
Entity 

• 
Vendor 

• 
Status 

• 
Account selection 

If the A/P balance includes a broader or different set of records, the totals will differ. 

3. 
Invoice date vs. due date aging 

Some users expect aging buckets to be based on one date type while the report is using 

another. This can make balances appear in unexpected buckets and affect reconciliation. 

4. 
Unapplied credits or partial payments 

Credits, adjustments, and partial payments may still affect open balances even if the user 

expects the item to be fully resolved. 

5. 
Voids, reversals, or adjustments 

Voided checks, reversed transactions, or manual adjustments can create differences 

between the aging report and the A/P balance if they were posted in a different period or 

not reviewed together. 

6. 
Period timing differences 

An invoice or payment may be entered in one accounting period but reflected differently 

depending on the report date or posting status. 

7. 
Data entry issues 

Incorrect invoice amounts, duplicate entries, wrong vendors, or posting errors can all cause 

the Vendor Aging report to differ from the A/P balance.  

8. 
Manual entries 

---


<!-- Page 29 -->
Chapter 1: A/P Reports 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Reports User Guide 

When you book a manual entry against the A/P account, the entry shows on the General 

Ledger report but not on the Vendor Aging report. 

How to Troubleshoot 

Confirm the as-of date used for both the Vendor Aging report and the A/P balance. 

1. 
Review all filters and selections on the report. 

2. 
Verify whether aging is based on invoice date or due date. 

3. 
Check for open credits, partial payments, voids, reversals, and adjustments. 

4. 
Reconcile report totals to supporting A/P transaction detail. 

5. 
Review recent entries for posting or data entry errors. 

Best Practice 

When comparing the Vendor Aging report to the A/P balance, make sure both are reviewed using 

the same: 

• 
Date 

• 
Scope 

• 
Accounting period 

• 
Transaction set 

When to Escalate 

If the totals still do not match after reviewing dates, filters, and transaction activity, gather: 

• 
Report parameters 

• 
Example vendors or invoices 

• 
Amount of the variance 

• 
Relevant accounting period 

Then route the issue for deeper accounting or product support review. 

---



##### How Are Aging Buckets Calculated in the Vendor Aging Report?
*Source: `RP Accounting AP Reports User Guide.pdf`, Page 30*

A/P Reports 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Reports User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

How Are Aging Buckets Calculated in the Vendor Aging 
Report? 

This topic explains how aging buckets are calculated in the Vendor Aging report and how invoice 

timing affects whether balances appear as current, 30, 60, 90, or older. 

Symptoms 

• 
Users do not understand why invoices appear in a certain aging bucket. 

• 
Invoice balances seem to be aged incorrectly. 

• 
Similar invoices appear in different aging periods. 

• 
Users are unsure whether aging is based on invoice date or due date. 

• 
The report totals appear correct, but bucket placement is confusing. 

Possible Causes 

• 
Aging is based on a specific date field selected by the report logic. 

• 
The report is being reviewed using the wrong as-of date. 

• 
Due dates, invoice dates, or posting dates differ from user expectations. 

• 
Credits or adjustments affect how balances appear by bucket. 

• 
Users are interpreting aging logic differently than the system applies it. 

Resolutions 

1. 
Confirm the report as-of date 

Verify the date used to age all invoice balances on the report. 

2. 
Review the date basis for aging 

Determine whether the report ages transactions by invoice date, due date, or another date 

field. 

3. 
Compare invoice dates and due dates 

Check whether the invoice timing supports the bucket shown. 

4. 
Review bucket ranges 

Confirm how current, 30, 60, 90, and older periods are defined in the report. Ensure that 

there are no overlapping periods. When periods overlap, an aging invoice can potentially 

appear in two buckets. 

5. 
Check balances with adjustments or credits 

Determine whether partial payments, credits, or adjustments affect the aged balance. 

6. 
Compare summary buckets to detail 

Drill into individual invoice records to verify the aging classification. 

---


<!-- Page 31 -->
Chapter 1: A/P Reports 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Reports User Guide 

7. 
Review report settings and filters 

Confirm that no settings are changing the expected aging behavior. 

8. 
Escalate if bucket calculations appear incorrect 

If invoice timing and report setup do not explain the result, contact your administrator or 

support team. 

Additional Information 

• 
Aging buckets group balances based on how old the open amount is relative to the report 

date. 

• 
Confusion often comes from not knowing which transaction date controls the aging result. 

• 
Credits and adjustments can make aging appear inconsistent when reviewed only at 

summary level. 

• 
Reviewing invoice-level detail can help explain bucket placement.

##### Why Does the As-of Date Change the Vendor Aging Report Totals?
*Source: `RP Accounting AP Reports User Guide.pdf`, Page 32*

A/P Reports 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Reports User Guide

Why Does the As-of Date Change the Vendor Aging Report 
Totals? 

This topic explains why changing the as-of date can affect Vendor Aging report totals and how 

transaction timing influences aged balances. 

Symptoms 

• 
The same report shows different totals on different dates. 

• 
Vendor balances change when only the as-of date is updated. 

• 
Users expect stable totals but see changes across reporting periods. 

• 
Report comparisons become difficult because totals do not remain consistent. 

Possible Causes 

• 
The report includes only transactions open as of the selected date. 

• 
Payments, adjustments, or credits changed balances after the earlier date. 

• 
Transactions were posted between report periods. 

• 
Different aging buckets apply based on the selected date. 

• 
Users are comparing reports run for different reporting cutoffs. 

Resolutions 

1. 
Review the selected as-of date 

Confirm the exact date used when running the report. 

2. 
Compare transaction activity between dates 

Check for payments, postings, adjustments, or credits entered between the report periods. 

3. 
Review open balances as of each date 

Confirm whether invoices were still open on one date but not another. 

4. 
Check aging bucket movement 

Determine whether invoices shifted into older buckets as time passed. 

5. 
Compare detail for both report runs 

Review invoice-level records to see which transactions changed between dates. 

6. 
Confirm reporting period expectations 

Make sure all users are comparing reports for the same cutoff date. 

7. 
Review posting timing 

Verify whether transactions were entered earlier but posted later. 

8. 
Escalate if date-based changes appear incorrect

If totals change without any visible transaction reason, contact your administrator or 

support team.

Vendor Aging reports are date-sensitive and reflect open balances as of a specific point in 

time. 

• 
Even small date changes can affect balances, aging buckets, and included transactions. 

• 
Comparing reports without matching as-of dates often leads to confusion. If the Date to 

use and Based on dates are not both G/L posting dates, then the aging does not tie to the 

General Ledger report. 

• 
Reviewing transaction detail is the best way to explain date-related differences.

##### Why Don’t Paid Invoices Appear on the Vendor Aging Report?
*Source: `RP Accounting AP Reports User Guide.pdf`, Page 34*

A/P Reports 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Reports User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Why Don’t Paid Invoices Appear on the Vendor Aging Report? 

This topic explains why paid invoices may not appear on the Vendor Aging report and how 

open-item reporting affects which transactions are included. 

Symptoms 

• 
Paid invoices are missing from the report. 

• 
A vendor balance seems incomplete because prior invoices are not listed. 

• 
Users cannot find invoices that were recently paid. 

• 
The report shows fewer invoices than expected. 

Possible Causes 

• 
The Vendor Aging report includes only open transactions. 

• 
Paid or fully applied invoices are excluded by design. 

• 
Voided or settled items do not meet the report criteria. 

• 
The report date is after the invoice was cleared. 

• 
Filters or settings exclude certain transaction types. 

Resolutions 

1. 
Check the invoice status 

Confirm whether the missing invoice is paid, voided, or otherwise resolved. 

2. 
Review the as-of date 

Determine whether the invoice was still open on the selected reporting date. 

3. 
Review payment and application activity 

Confirm whether the invoice balance was fully offset by payment, credit, or adjustment. 

4. 
Compare to invoice history or transaction detail 

Use detailed records to confirm the invoice lifecycle and current status. 

5. 
Confirm user expectations 

Make sure the report being used matches the need for open balances versus historical 

transaction review. 

6. 
Escalate if open invoices are missing 

If an invoice is still open but does not appear, contact your administrator or support team. 

Additional Information 

• 
Vendor Aging reports typically focus on unpaid or open balances rather than full invoice 

history. 

• 
Paid invoices may need to be reviewed in a different inquiry or transaction report. 

• 
The as-of date determines whether an invoice was open at the time of reporting.

• 
Vendor balances appear duplicated. 

• 
The same invoice seems to appear more than once. 

• 
Totals look too high compared to expectations. 

• 
Aging detail appears to overstate what is owed. 

• 
Users cannot explain why balances exceed vendor statements or A/P review totals. 

Possible Causes 

• 
Multiple invoice lines or related transactions are shown separately. 

• 
Credit memos or adjustments are not being interpreted correctly. 

• 
Unapplied payments remain open alongside invoices. 

• 
Summary and detail views are being compared incorrectly. 

• 
The report includes multiple open transactions that appear related.

Review invoice-level detail

the report is showing separate related transactions. 

2. 
Compare summary and detail views 

Confirm whether the report is grouping or separating balances in different ways. 

3. 
Check for credits and adjustments 

Review whether credit memos, debit adjustments, or corrections affect the total shown. 

4. 
Review unapplied payments 

Determine whether payments remain open and appear separately from invoices. 

5. 
Confirm invoice numbers and references 

Verify whether similar invoice numbers represent the same item or different entries. 

6. 
Check balance calculations 

Confirm that line items, remaining balances, and offsets are being interpreted correctly. 

7. 
Compare to vendor inquiry or transaction history 

Use supporting detail to explain each open amount shown.

Check whether the credit is applied 

Confirm whether the negative amount has already been matched against an invoice. 

4. 
Review aging bucket placement 

Determine where the credit appears and how it affects the vendor total. 

5. 
Compare summary totals to detail 

Verify how the report reflects credits at both levels.

Check for unapplied transactions 

Confirm whether credits or payments remain open independently.
