How Do I Reconcile Vendor Aging Report Summary Totals to 
Invoice Detail? 

This topic explains how to reconcile Vendor Aging report summary totals to invoice-level detail 

and identify where differences begin. 

Symptoms 

• 
Summary totals are clear, but supporting invoice detail is not. 

• 
Users cannot trace a vendor total back to individual invoices. 

• 
Detail balances do not seem to add up to the summary. 

• 
Reconciliation is difficult during month-end or statement review. 

• 
Users are unsure which transactions make up a vendor’s aged balance. 

Possible Causes 

• 
Credits, adjustments, or unapplied payments affect summary totals. 

• 
Filters differ between summary and detail views. 

• 
Users are comparing different dates or report scopes. 

• 
Some transactions are grouped or displayed differently at summary level. 

• 
Open balance detail is being interpreted incorrectly. 

Resolutions 

1. 
Confirm the report date and scope 

Make sure summary and detail are being compared using the same as-of date and filters. 

2. 
Review vendor-level summary totals 

Identify the vendor total that needs to be reconciled. 

3. 
Drill into invoice-level detail 

Review all open transactions contributing to that vendor balance. 

4. 
Check for credits and adjustments 

Include negative balances, unapplied payments, and correcting entries in the review. 

5. 
Add detail balances carefully 

Confirm that all invoice and credit amounts net to the summary total. 

6. 
Review excluded or zero-balance items 

Determine whether some transactions exist in history but do not contribute to aging. 

7. 
Compare transaction references 

Match invoice numbers, dates, and remaining balances between views.

##### What Date Is Used to Age Invoices on the Vendor Aging Report?
*Source: `RP Accounting AP Reports User Guide.pdf`, Page 44*

A/P Reports 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Reports User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

What Date Is Used to Age Invoices on the Vendor Aging 
Report? 

This topic explains which date is used to age invoices on the Vendor Aging report and why 

understanding the aging date basis is important when reviewing balances. 

Symptoms 

• 
Users are unsure why invoices appear in a certain aging bucket. 

• 
Similar invoices age differently than expected. 

• 
Aging totals appear correct, but the date logic is unclear. 

• 
Users do not know whether aging uses invoice date, due date, or posting date. 

• 
Report interpretation varies between users. 

Possible Causes 

• 
The report uses a date basis different from the user’s expectation. 

• 
Users assume aging is based on due date when another date is used. 

• 
The as-of date changes how invoice timing is interpreted. 

• 
Posting timing and invoice timing differ. 

• 
Documentation or report labeling does not clearly explain the aging basis. 

Resolutions 

1. 
Review the report definition 

Determine which transaction date the Vendor Aging report uses for aging. 

2. 
Confirm the as-of date 

Verify the reporting cutoff date applied to all aging calculations. 

3. 
Compare invoice date, due date, and posting date 

Review the invoice record to see which date best explains the aging result. 

4. 
Check aging bucket placement 

Confirm whether the invoice’s assigned bucket aligns with the report date basis. 

5. 
Compare similar invoices 

Review invoices with similar timing to determine whether aging is behaving consistently. 

6. 
Review report documentation or setup 

Confirm whether the date basis is fixed or influenced by report options. 

7. 
Validate with invoice-level detail 

Use transaction detail to test how the report ages specific invoices.

• 
Aging reports depend on both the selected report date and the transaction date basis used 

by the report.

Misunderstanding the date basis is a common reason users question bucket placement. 

•

• 
Reviewing detail helps confirm how aging is being applied.

Vendor ID, Vendor Name, Vendor Type, Term, Tax ID, Credit Limit, Credit Limit Desc, 

Balance, Balance Desc, Status, or On Hold. 

The abbreviation “desc” after an option means “descending order”—in this case, reverse 
alphabetical or reverse numerical order. By default, the system sorts this report by 

Vendor ID. However, you may want to examine those vendors with whom you have high 
balances. In that case, choose Balance Desc so that the vendors with high balances are 
listed first. You may want to examine the list to check for low credit limits, in which case 
you would choose Credit Limit. 

4. 
In the Line format drop-down list, set the report to display the filtered information in a 

single line format or a multi-line format. 

• 
The single line format displays all of your filtered information on a single line. This 

produces a much wider report that may extend past a single page, even in landscape 

mode. This format is useful for exporting vendor data to a CSV file. 

• 
The multi-line format displays each category of your filtered information on its own 

line. This may result in a much longer report, but when you print the report, it will fit 

within the width of a page. Multi-line produces a vertical report with the vendor 

information organized below each vendor name.

1099/1096 Report 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > All > Reports > Vendors Reports > 1099/1096`


Accounts Payable 1099/1096 reports and forms include: 

• 
1099 Report (on page 97): Displays a list of payments classified as 1099 income paid to 

vendors. 

• 
Create 1099 File (on page 92): Creates a data file that you can send to a third-party service 

that specializes in printing and mailing 1099 forms. 

• 
Form 1096 (on page 59): This is the cover sheet for all 1099 forms submitted by your 

company. Use one 1096 for all 1099s you submit that are of a specific type. 

• 
Form 1099 (on page 65): Prints the proper 1099 form for each individual, business, or 

organization that receives a payment. 

• 
DE 542 Form (on page 116): Prints the form required for California’s independent 

contractors. 

You can run the 1099 report, print 1099 forms, and generate 1099 e-files for the current year and 

previous year. You can either print your 1099 forms or export your 1099 data to a file to send to a 

printing service.  

Use Form 1096 to create a cover sheet for your 1099 reports.

#### Preparing for Accurate 1099 Reports
*Source: `RP Accounting AP Reports User Guide.pdf`, Page 62*

Preparing for Accurate 1099 Reports 

To prepare for accurate 1099 report generation, we recommend that you create a custom 1099 

vendor list to be sure you haven’t left an eligible vendor out or maybe tagged one as eligible who 

shouldn’t be. 

You can also use the report in Accounts Payable called the 1099 Vendor report that includes 
this information. 

1. 
On your vendor list control bar, click Manage views > Create new view. 

2. 
Select the column Form 1099 Type check box. 

3. 
Open the Step drop-down list, and then select Save advanced options. 

4. 
Give the view a name in the Name field, such as “View Includes 1099 Type.” 

5. 
Click Save. 

---


<!-- Page 63 -->
Chapter 1: A/P Reports 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Reports User Guide 

6. 
Apply the view by clicking All on the list control bar, and then select the view that you just 

created. 

Learn more about creating custom list views. 

Income from non-employment needs to be reported on a Form 1099. 

• 
The system has a dedicated contact solely for printing Form 1099. You can stop editing the 

vendor contact to print out the forms, and then edit it once again to put the information 

back to the original contact. 

• 
There’s no need to turn on account labels or import to update transaction 1099 information. 

The system has a 1099 option and form override at the line level of a transaction. 

• 
You can exclude credit card payments from the 1099 total. 

• 
Removing a Vendor’s 1099 Status 

There’s no need to export all affected transactions, then import them again with the 

changed status. After you change a vendor status, we’ll ask you if you want to change all of 

the associated transactions. You can also continue to use the previous method as needed. 

For example, you can continue to use the previous method if you have multiple vendors 

with transactions that require a status change.

business, or organization that receives payments from your company. 

Form 1096 is the cover sheet for the 1099 forms submitted by your company. Use one 1096 for all 

1099s you submit that are of a specific type. For example, if you file ten 1099-MISC forms for 

Miscellaneous Information, you fill out just one 1096 form as the cover sheet for those ten forms. 

If you submit a group of 1099-DIV forms, you would print another 1096 to submit with those 

forms. 

The system prints your company information on Form 1096, and also prints: 

• 
The 1099 form type required 

• 
The number of forms of that type that are included 

• 
The total amount being reported for the included forms 

Preparing to Print 1096 Forms 

Printing out your 1096 is the culmination of a year of system-accumulated 1099 information. 

Before you print the 1096, it’s a good idea to generate a report of the 1099s in your system by 

form type to verify that the results are as expected. 

To generate a 1096 report: 

1. 
Open the Accounts payable menu. 

2. 
In the Reports column, click 1096/1099, and then select 1096 forms. The Form 1096 page 

opens. 

3. 
Print out the 1096 report by the appropriate form type (for example 1099-MISC, 

Miscellaneous Information). 

4. 
From the report, total up the amounts by form type. 

5. 
Open the Accounts payable menu. 

6. 
In the Reports column, click 1096/1099 and then select 1096 form to test print one 1096 

form on blank paper.  

7. 
Be sure to select the form type and option for printing the total number and total amount 

of submitted forms. 

8. 
Check the printout as follows: 

• 
Is the 1099 type selected? 

• 
Do the number of forms (displayed in Box 3) match the report? 

• 
Does the total amount (displayed in Box 5) match your calculated total?

Buttons 

Customize 
Opens the report’s customization page to change filters and time periods 

and to exclude specific types of data. 

The Customize button appears only after viewing a report or ledger. 

View 
Opens the report in your browser. 

Print 
Displays the report in printable PDF format so you can print it or save it on 

your computer. 

Process & store 
Generates the report and stores it for later access. 

Available formats include HTML, printable (PDF), Excel, CSV 

(comma-separated value), and Text. You can store reports (on page 236) in 

the system, and then access them with the My stored reports option in 

the menu.  

Email 
Sends the report as an email message. Click to open the Email report box, 

and then fill in the To field with the recipient’s email address. 

This button is not available for all reports. 

Add to dashboard 
Adds the report to a dashboard. 

Select the dashboard that you want to add it to, type a name for the 

report, and then type a description of the report.  

Select the Public check box to make the report available on a dashboard. 

This option is not available for all reports.  

Memorize 
Memorizes (that is, saves) the report in the system so you can refer to it 

later or modify and re-run it. 

Reports that you memorize can be scheduled to run on a recurring basis 
and can be automatically emailed. 

Export 
Exports the report to a separate file that you can then distribute or save on 

your computer. 

The file formats for exporting report data vary by report. 

Select 
Opens the multi-select box, where you can select items to filter by. 

In the multi-select box, select the items that you want to include in the 

report.  

The option to multi-select items is not available for all reports.

Printing 1099 Forms on Blank Paper 


> **Navigation Path:** `Accounts Payable > Reports > 1096/1099 > 1099 Form`


To print 1099 forms on blank paper: 

1. 
Open the Accounts Payable menu. 

2. 
In the Reports column, click 1099/1096, and then select 1099 Form. 

3. 
In the Format section, select the desired form in the Form to print drop-down list. 

4. 
Select the Print on blank paper (Copy B) check box. 

5.

6.

Copy C is not valid with 1099 -NEC forms. 

7. 
Click the Print button. 

Distributing Form 1099 Copies 

Form 1099 copies should be distributed in the following manner: 

• 
Copy 1 is sent by the payer to the state tax department. 

• 
Copy 2 is sent to the recipient for their state income tax return. It provides the same income 

information as Copy B (used for federal filing), but is specifically intended to be attached to 

the recipient’s state tax return if their state requires it. 

• 
Copy A is sent by the payer to the IRS. Copy A appears in red, similar to the official IRS form. 

Copy A cannot be printed from the RealPage Financial Suite on blank stock / plain paper. 

This copy must be printed on a pre-printed form due to the red ink and to meet IRS filing 

requirements. 

• 
Copy B and other copies of this form are printed with black ink. Copy B is for the recipient. 

Copy 2 is used for filing with the recipient’s state income tax return, when required. 

• 
Copy C of a 1099 form is kept by the payer for their own records to document what was 

reported to the IRS and the recipient.

tribal government, or their political subdivisions, or qualified volunteer fire departments. A

authorities, community redevelopment agencies, and similar governmental entities that

catch or the FMV of a distribution in kind to each crew member of fishing boats with 

normally fewer than 10 crew members. A fishing boat has normally fewer than 10 crew 

members if the average size of the operating crew was fewer than 10 on trips during the 

preceding 4 calendar quarters. 

In addition, report cash payments of up to $100 per trip that are contingent on a minimum 

catch and are paid solely for additional duties (such as mate, engineer, or cook) for which 

additional cash payments are traditional in the industry. However, do not report on Form 

1099-MISC, Miscellaneous Information, any wages reportable on Form W-2. 

10.

or health care services. Include payments made by medical and health care insurers under 

health, accident, and sickness insurance programs. If payment is made to a corporation, list 

the corporation as the recipient rather than the individual providing the services. Payments 

to persons providing health care services often include charges for injections, drugs, 

dentures, and similar items. In these cases, the entire payment is subject to information 

reporting. You are not required to report payments to pharmacies for prescription drugs. 

The exemption from issuing Form 1099-MISC, Miscellaneous Information, to a corporation 

does not apply to payments for medical or health care services provided by corporations, 

including professional corporations. However, you are not required to report payments 

made to a tax-exempt hospital or extended care facility or to a hospital or extended care

The entry in box 5 may include any of the following: (a) designated Roth contributions or

were required to be included in the income of the employee when contributed (after-tax 

contributions), (b) contributions made by the employer but considered to have been 

contributed by the employee under section 72(f), (c) the accumulated cost of premiums paid 

for life insurance protection taxable to the employee in previous years and in the current 

year under Regulations section 1.72-16 (cost of current life insurance protection) (only if the 

life insurance contract itself is distributed), and (d) premiums paid on commercial annuities. 

Do not include any DVECs, elective deferrals, or any contribution to a retirement plan that 

was not an after-tax contribution. 

Generally, for qualified plans, section 403(b) plans, and non-qualified commercial annuities, 

enter in box 5 the employee contributions or insurance premiums recovered tax free during 

the year based on the method you used to determine the taxable amount to be entered in 

box 2a. On a separate Form 1099-R, include the portion of the employee’s basis that has 

been distributed from a designated Roth account.

In 6- Net unrealized appreciation in employer’s securities, use this box if a distribution 

from a qualified plan (except a qualified distribution from a designated Roth account) 

includes securities of the employer corporation (or a subsidiary or parent corporation) and 

you can compute the NUA in the employer’s securities. Enter all the NUA in employer 

securities if this is a lump-sum distribution. If this is not a lump-sum distribution, enter only 

the NUA in employer securities attributable to employee contributions.

the employee’s contributions over the cash and other property (not including the annuity

along with the current actuarial value, the percentage of the total annuity contract each 

Form 1099-R represents.

cooperative under section 199A(g) and passed through to the patron. This amount must 

have been designated in a written notice sent to the patron from the cooperative within the

qualified items of income, gain, deduction, or loss from qualified trades or businesses that 

are not a specified service trade or business (SSTB) for purposes of section 199A. Examples 

of income that are not qualified items include tax-exempt income, capital gains, and income 

that isn’t effectively connected with the conduct of a trade or business within the United 

States.

Certain Government Payments (Form 1099-G) 

1. 
Select the Certain Government Payments (Form 1099-G) form. 

When you choose Certain Government Payments from the Form name box, the Default 

1099 box drop-down list includes these options: 

• 
1 - Unemployment compensation 

• 
2 - State or local income tax refunds, credits, or offsets 

• 
4 - Federal income tax withheld 

• 
5 - RTAA payments 

• 
6 - Taxable grants 

• 
7 - Agriculture payments  

• 
9 - Market Gain 

2. 
Select the desired Default 1099 box. 

3. 
In the Entity drop-down list, select the entity that is to generate the 1099 form. 

4. 
In the Initial values for year drop-down list, select a year to associate the values with a tax 

year.  

5. 
In 1 - Unemployment compensation, enter to report payments of $10 or more in 

unemployment compensation, including Railroad Retirement Board payments for 

unemployment. 

If you make payments from a contributory program that has been deemed to be in the 

nature of unemployment compensation, such as California’s Family Temporary Disability 

Insurance payments or governmental paid family leave program payments, file a separate 

Form 1099-G for payments from each contributory program. Enter the total amount before 

any income tax was withheld. If you withhold federal income tax at the request of the 

recipient, enter it in box 4. 

6. 
In 2 - State or local income tax refunds, credits or offsets, enter select to report refunds, 

credits, or offsets of state or local income tax of $10 or more you made to recipients. These 

include refunds or carry-forward credits of overpayments of tax due to refundable state tax 

credits and incentive payments that are paid under an existing state tax law and 

administered by the state taxing agency. Filmmaker incentive credits, home improvement 

credits paid in low-income areas, and solar panel installation credits are some types of state 

programs which are generally reportable in box 2, to the extent a refund is paid by the state 

taxing agency or amount allowed as carry-forward credit to the next taxable year. 

7. 
In 4 - Federal income tax withheld, enter backup withholding on payments required to be 

reported in box 6 or 7. You must backup withhold on such payments at a rate of 24% if a 

recipient does not furnish its TIN to you or if you are notified by the IRS that the TIN is 

incorrect.

8. 
In 5 - RTAA payments, enter the Reemployment Trade Adjustment Assistance (RTAA)

9. 
In 6 - Taxable grants, enter any amount of a taxable grant administered by a federal, state, 

or local program to provide subsidized energy financing or grants for projects designed to 

conserve or produce energy, but only with respect to energy property or a dwelling unit 

located in the United States. Also, enter any amount of a taxable grant administered by an 

Indian tribal government. Report amounts of other taxable grants of $600 or more. State

10.

11. 
In 9 - Market Gain, enter market gain associated with the repayment of a CCC loan whether

12.

13. 
Select the 2nd TIN Not. check box if you were notified by the IRS twice within three 

calendar years that the taxpayer provided an incorrect TIN. If you select this check box, the 

IRS will not send you any further notices about this account. 

However, if you received both IRS notices in the same year, or if you received them in 

different years but they both related to information returns filed for the same year, do not 

check the box at this time. For purposes of the two-notices-in-three-years rule, you are 

considered to have received one notice and you are not required to send a second “B” 

notice to the taxpayer on receipt of the second notice.

*Source: `RP Accounting AP Reports User Guide.pdf`, Page 99*

RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Reports User Guide 


> **Navigation Path:** `Go to Accounts Payable > My Stored Reports to view the results. Depending on the format you`


select, the results appear as a CSV file or an Excel file. This is a partial example of the results 

stored in Excel format: 

Customizing the 1099 File 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > All > 1099/1096 > 1099, Create File`


To customize the 1099 file: 

1. 
Open the Accounts payable menu.  

2. 
In the Reports section, click 1099/1096, and then select 1099, create file. 

3. 
Click the Year ending drop-down box, and then select the year for which you want data. 

Typically, you print 1099 and 1096 forms after the end of the year. 

Filling In the Filters Section 

Use the filters to focus the results of your report. In effect, filters enable you to isolate and 

assemble just the data you want. You can set any combination of filters. 

To customize your report results, change the filters as follows: 

1. 
To show results for all vendors, check the Select all vendors check box. 

2. 
To show results for a specific vendor or a group of vendors, use the From vendor and To 

vendor drop-down boxes. 

3. 
To show results for all employees, check the Select all employees check box. 

4. 
To show results for a specific employee or a group of employees, use the From employee 

and To employee drop-down boxes. 

How to use the From/To fields: 

All From/To field pairs work the same way. Use them to get search results in as broad or as 

fine a range as you need—from everything in the system down to a single specific object. 

To run this report for a single object: 

• 
Click the down arrow next to the From box, and from the menu that appears, click the 

object you want. 

• 
Click the down arrow next to the To box, and from the menu that appears, click the 

same object. 

---


<!-- Page 100 -->
A/P Reports 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Reports User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

To run this report for a specific range of objects: 

• 
Click the down arrow next to the From box, and from the menu that appears, click the 

object you want at the beginning of the range. 

• 
Click the down arrow next to the To box, and from the menu that appears, click the 

object you want at the end of the range. 

To run this report for all objects: 

Leave both boxes blank. 

If you have a large number of objects, or if this report takes too long to process, use the 

From and To boxes to run a series of smaller reports. For example, you can run five reports, 

one each for objects whose names begin with A–E, then F-J, K-O, P-T, and U–Z. 

An object is a catch -all term that refers to any specific data item in the system. 
Customers, vendors, items, and accounts are all examples of objects. 

5. 
In the Entity/Entity group drop-down list, select the subordinate entity for which to create a 

1099 file. Entity Group is the same as Location Group. 

The system displays the Entity/Entity Group drop-down list only if your company is at the 

top level of a multi-entity shared structure of multiple companies.  

Select the Individual report check box to have the system generate one report per location. 

If you select the Individual Report option, you must click the Process & Store button when 
you have finished customizing the report. 

Select the Individual reports in a single file option to generate individual reports for each 

property and then combine them in one file.  

Select the Prompt on run check box to have the system ask the user to select a location 

before it will run the report.  

6. 
Select the Exclude credit card payments check box to exclude those payments from the 

1099 total. 

Filling In the Format Section 

Use this section to specify the form to use when printing and to determine the sort order. 

To format this report: 

1. 
Select the form to use for printing. The options include:  

• 
Dividend Income (Form 1099-DIV) (on page 69) 

• 
Interest Income (Form 1099-INT) (on page 72) 

• 
Miscellaneous Information (Form 1099-MISC) (on page 75)

• 
Distributions From Pensions, Annuities, Retirement or Profit-Sharing Plans, IRAs, 

Insurance Contracts, etc. (Form 1099-R) (on page 78) 

• 
Proceeds From Real Estate Transactions (Form 1099-S) (on page 84) 

• 
Taxable Distributions Received (Form 1099- PATR) (on page 85)

2. 
To sort the 1099 file results, click the Sort By drop-down list, and then click the category to 

sort by. The options include Vendor ID/Employee ID, or Vendor name/Employee name. 

Processing the 1099 Report 

You can generate reports on-demand and store them for later access. You use the Storage 

Options box to choose the report date, format, and where to store the report after it is processed. 

Once processed, you can access them through the My Stored Reports option on the Accounts 

Payable menu. 

If you want to process and store the same report on a recurring basis, consider scheduling it. 

1. 
Click the Process & Store button. The Storage options box is displayed. 

2. 
In the Run report on field, type the date you want the report to cover. 

3. 
In the Delivery options section of the Storage Options page, type a Report name. 

4. 
From the Report type drop-down list, select the format in which you want the system to 

save the report.  

5. 
Click OK. 

Retrieving the Report 

You can retrieve your report from the Accounts Payable application’s menu or the Reports 

application. 


> **Navigation Path:** `Reports > All > Reports > My Stored Reports`



> **Navigation Path:** `Accounts Payable > All > Reports > My Stored Reports`


Once you’ve stored a report, you can easily change the report format by going to My Stored 

Reports, and then clicking Process & Store again.  

Reports in the My Stored Reports list can only be accessed by you.

#### 1099 Reports

Chapter 1: A/P Reports

RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Reports User Guide 

1099 Reports 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > All > 1099/1096 > 1099 Reports`


The 1099 Report displays a list of payments classified as 1099 income paid to vendors. 

The 1099 report is a standard report. If you are looking for information on financial reports, see 
Creating a Financial Report.  

Generate the 1099 report to: 

• 
Verify that you set up your vendors with the correct 1099 form. 

• 
Review the amounts paid to 1099 vendors for a specific year. 

The 1099 report includes only payments classified as 1099 income paid to vendors. You can 

create the report to include either all 1099 categories or a specific 1099 category. You can sort the 

results by vendor name or by 1099 category. 

When you have imported initial balances and have not paid an invoice in RealPage Accounting, 

the initial balance displays on the 1099 report. 

When an invoice was paid with multiple payments, the system displays the invoice amount on the 

report once to determine an accurate total invoice amount of all invoices. 

Filters 

You can filter the report by: 

• 
Vendor 

• 
Entity 

• 
1099 form type 

• 
Minimum eligible amounts or all amounts 

• 
Transaction information (1099 only or non-1099) 

• 
Include or exclude credit card payments 

This report is available in two versions: summary and detail. 

Grouping the Report 

You can group the report for entities that share federal IDs and legal contact information. When 

vendors share the same tax ID, then the report combines the data for these vendors under one 

vendor. Set the Validate and Issue 1099 by Tax ID and Legal Contact Information (on page 102) 

setting to use this grouping.  

---


<!-- Page 104 -->
A/P Reports 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Reports User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Interpreting 1099 Report Conditions 

• 
When you run the 1099 report at the top level for a single entity, the property’s name 

appears on the printed report rather than the company’s name. 

• 
When an invoice is paid with multiple payments, the report shows the invoice only once. 

• 
When an invoice number appears twice under a vendor, then the invoice amount appears 

only on the first occurrence of the invoice number. 

• 
When there is an opening balance, the opening balance appears on the report even if no 

invoices have been paid to the vendor during the year.

##### Customizing and Running the 1099 Report
*Source: `RP Accounting AP Reports User Guide.pdf`, Page 105*

Chapter 1: A/P Reports 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Reports User Guide 

Customizing and Running the 1099 Report 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > All > Reports > 1099/1096 > 1099 Reports`


To customize and run the 1099 Report: 

1. 
Open the Accounts payable menu. 

2. 
In the Reports section, click 1099/1096, and then select 1099 reports. 

Filling In the Time Period Section 

You can use one of the pre-defined reporting periods available from the Reporting Period and As 

of Date boxes, or create your own reporting period using the Start Date and End Date boxes. 

In the Time Period section, do one of the following: 

• 
Use the Reporting Period drop-down list to select the desired reporting period and either 

type a date in the As of Date field or use the calendar tool to select a date. 

• 
Type a specific Start date and/or a specific End date or use the calendar tool to select the 

desired date(s). 

If you complete all of the time period fields (that is, if you fill in the Reporting Period and As of 

Date fields in addition to the Start Date and End Date fields), then the system bases your report 
only on the specified start and end dates. It ignores the As of Date specified. 

Filling In the Filters Section 

1. 
Select the Select all vendors check box to run 1099 reports for all vendors. 

2. 
Use the From vendor and To vendor drop-down lists to select the beginning and ending 

vendor in a range to include a range of vendors in the report. 

In the From vendor drop-down list, select the first vendor in a range of vendors to include 

in the report. The system fills in the To vendor drop-down list with the same vendor, setting 

it up in case you want to include just one vendor in the report. 

In the To vendor drop-down list, select the last vendor in a range of vendors.  

Alternatively, leave the value in both fields set to the same vendor if you want to report on 

just one vendor. 

If your system has the employee dimension enabled, then you can filter the 1099 report by 
employees. 

3. 
Select the Select all employee check box to run 1099 reports for all employees. 

---


<!-- Page 106 -->
A/P Reports 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Reports User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

4. 
Use the From employee and To employee drop-down lists to select the beginning and 

ending employee in a range to include a range of employees in the report. 

In the From employee drop-down list, select the first employee in a range of employees to 

include in the report. The system fills in the To employee drop-down list with the same 

employee, setting it up in case you want to include just one employee in the report. 

In the To employee drop-down list, select the last employee in a range of employees. 

Alternatively, leave the value in both fields set to the same employee if you want to report 

on just one employee. 

5. 
In the Group by drop-down list, select the desired option:  

• 
Vendor tax ID: Select this option to group the report by vendor tax ID.  

The option to group by vendor tax ID appears only when the Validate and issue 1099 

by Tax ID and Legal Contact information (on page 102) option is enabled for 1099s. 
When enabled, the system creates a single 1099 record for all vendor records that 
share the same tax ID. The report also groups data for entities when they share the 
same federal ID and legal contact information.  

• 
Vendor/Employee: Select this option to group the report by vendor. 

• 
1099 category: Select this option to group the report by 1099 category. 

• 
None: Select this option if you do not want to group the data in the report. 

6. 
In the Entity/Entity group drop-down list, select an entity or entity group to filter the report 

so that it includes only vendors and/or employees associated with the selected entity or 

entity group. 

7. 
Select the Individual report check box if you want the system to generate only one report 

per entity or entity group. If you select this option, then you must click the Process & store 

button at the end. 

8. 
Select the Prompt on run check box if you want the system to prompt the user to select an 

entity or entity group before running the report. 

9. 
In the 1099 form type section, choose the 1099 form types to include.  

• 
Click the Select button to make initial selections.  

• 
Click the Add/Edit link to add or change selections. 

• 
To include all 1099 form types, don’t select anything. 

10.

Buttons 

Customize 
Opens the report’s customization page to change filters and time periods

View 
Opens the report in your browser. 

Print 
Displays the report in printable PDF format so you can print it or save it on

Process & store

Memorize 
Memorizes (that is, saves) the report in the system so you can refer to it 

later or modify and re-run it. 

Reports that you memorize can be scheduled to run on a recurring basis 
and can be automatically emailed. 

Export 
Exports the report to a separate file that you can then distribute or save on 

your computer.

*Source: `RP Accounting AP Reports User Guide.pdf`, Page 111*

Chapter 1: A/P Reports

RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Reports User Guide 

1099 Electronic Filing 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > All > Reports > Vendor Reports > 1099/1096 > 
1099 Electronic Filing`


Use the 1099 Electronic Filing menu option to generate 1099 electronic files and submit filings in 

a single place. After generating your files, upload your tax files to the IRS. 

• 
If you generated a text file, go to https://fire.irs.gov to upload the file. 

• 
If you generated a CSV file, go to https://www.id.me/ to upload the file. 

1099 updates align with changes the IRS made for the 2024 tax year. Additional updates to the 

existing 1099 report and file generation are needed to allow clients the ability to run 1099’s across 

their whole portfolio. 

This feature is available at the top level only. 

Before You Begin 

Access can vary depending on your organization’s subscriptions and your permissions. If you do 

not see the option in the menu, then ask your System Administrator to check your permissions. 

Permissions 

These permissions are required to work with 1099 electronic filing. 

Application 
Activities/Lists 
Permissions 

Accounts Payable 
1099 Electronic Filing 
Run

Administrator for assistance. If you have administrator privileges, you can assign permissions for a 

new feature to a user or to a role. See Roles and Permissions for a description of how to review a 

user’s permissions. 

Prerequisites 

You must enter the Transmitter Control Code (on page 106) for your business into the Accounting 

system.

##### Adding Your Transmitter Control Code to the System
*Source: `RP Accounting AP Reports User Guide.pdf`, Page 112*

A/P Reports 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Reports User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Adding Your Transmitter Control Code to the System 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > Configuration > Company > General Information > 
Company Information > Transmitter Control Code`


Before you can file electronically, your company must obtain an IRS Transmitter Control Code 

(TCC) from the Internal Revenue Service. The TCC is a five-digit code that identifies the business 

that is transmitting electronic returns.  

To obtain a TCC code, complete a request for a TCC code through the IRS application on the 

IRS.gov website. It can take up to 45 days to obtain a TCC code, so be sure to plan in advance. 

To add your transmitter control code: 

1. 
Open the Company menu.  

2. 
In the Configuration section, click the Company option. The Company information page 

opens to the General Information tab. 

3. 
Click the Edit button. 

4. 
In the Company information section, find the Transmitter control code field, and then type 

your five-digit code. 

5. 
Click Save. 

---

*Source: `RP Accounting AP Reports User Guide.pdf`, Page 113*

Chapter 1: A/P Reports

1099 Electronic Filing Page 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > All > Reports > Vendor Reports > 1099/1096 > 
1099 Electronic Filing`


Use this page to set up options to run the 1099 report for vendors, employees, or both. You can 

run the 1099 report, print 1099 forms, and generate 1099 e-files for the previous year (2024) or 

two years prior (2023). After generating the report, you can file it with the IRS. 

• 
If you generated a text file, go to https://fire.irs.gov to upload the file.  

• 
If you generated a CSV file, go to https://www.id.me/ to upload the file. 

This page has three sections: 

• 
Time period: Use this section to set the year of the 1099 report. 

• 
Filters: Use this section to limit the 1099s. You can filter by vendor or range of vendors, 

employee or range of employees, entity or entity group. You can also choose to exclude 

credit card payments, and vendor payments made with a virtual card. You can also choose 

to generate a 1099 report that combines state and federal reports into one. The Combined 

Federal/State filing check box may be selected only if IRS approval has already been 

received, or a test file is being generated for the purpose of receiving IRS approval. You can 

also select the option to generate a test file. 

• 
Format: Use this section to choose the 1099 form type to generate. You can also set the sort 

order to sort by name or ID. 

Filing the 1099 Form Electronically 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > All > Reports > Vendor Reports > 1099/1096 > 
1099 Electronic Filing`


You can only use this feature at the top level. 

Workflow: 

1. 
Fill in the 1099 Electronic Filing page. 

2. 
Click Generate. 

3. 
Review your forms and make any adjustments as needed. 

4. 
Go to the irs.gov website and run the IR application.  

Filling In the 1099 Electronic Filing Page 

1. 
In the Time period section, select the tax year that you are filing in the Year ending 

drop-down list. 

Filling In the Filters Section 

1. 
In the Generate section, select the desired option to use for submitting the 1099 file: 

---


<!-- Page 114 -->

• 
Text file submitted through FIRE: Select this option to have the system generate a 

text file that you can submit to https://fire.irs.gov. 

• 
CSV file submitted through IRIS: Select this option to have the system generate a CSV 

file that you can submit to https://www.id.me. 

2. 
Select the Select all vendors check box if you are filing a 1099 for all of your vendors at one 

time. 

Otherwise, select the vendor or range of vendors that this 1099 form covers in the From 

vendor drop-down list. 

If you want the 1099 form to cover a range of vendors, select the vendor at the end of the 

list in the To vendor drop-down list.  

A vendor must meet the minimum to report on. The system totals the vendor amounts for 
both parent and child vendors to arrive at the vendor total. When the report or form 
generates, it includes the total of both parent and child vendor. 

3. 
Select the Select all employees check box if you are filing a 1099 for all of your employees 

at one time. 

Otherwise, select the employee or the starting employee in a range of employees that this 

1099 form covers in the From employee drop-down list. 

4. 
If you want the 1099 form to cover a range of employees, then select the employee at the 

end of the list in the To employee drop-down list.  

5. 
Use the Entity/Entity group drop-down list to select an entity or entity group to limit the 

1099 forms to the employees or vendors of the selected entities. 

• 
Select the Individual report check box if you selected an entity group (location group). 

This option creates a separate report for each entity. The order of the entities in a 

group determines the order in which the system creates the reports. 

You must select an entity group (location group) if you select the Individual report 

option. Also, you must select Process & Store when you select the Individual report 

option. 

• 
Select the Prompt on run check box if you want to be able to choose the entity or 

entity group when you run the report. 

6. 
Select the Exclude credit card payments check box if you want to prevent tax payment 

using credit cards. 

7. 
Select the Exclude vendor payments virtual card check box if you want to prevent tax 

payment using virtual card payments. 

8. 
Select the Test file check box when you are not submitting real tax files but are generating a 

test file to get approval for submitting combined federal and state taxes.

Generating and Storing the 1099 E-Files 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > All > Reports > Vendor Reports > 1099/1096 > 
1099 Electronic Filing`


When you generate a 1099 e-file, the system checks if you have multiple entities and if you have 

enabled the Issue Separate setting.  

When selected, the system generates the 1099 e-file in text format and stores it in My Stored 

Reports where you can view it at will. You can also download the file so that you can submit it to 

the IRS.  

To generate a 1099 e-file: 

1. 
Select the tax year that you want to file from the Year ending drop-down list. 

2. 
In the Filters section, in the Generate section, select one of the options: 

• 
Text file submitted through FIRE: Select this option if you want to generate and 

submit a text file to the IRS. 

• 
CSV file submitted through IRIS: Select this option if you want to generate and submit 

a CSV file through the Information Returns Intake System (IRIS). 

3. 
Set up the filters to have the system generate the e-file for the desired vendors.  

• 
Select the Select all vendors check box to generate forms for all vendors. 

• 
To generate a file for a single vendor, select the vendor in the From Vendor 

drop-down list. Use this option if you want to generate a correction file for a specific 

vendor, too. 

• 
To include a range of vendors, in the From Vendor drop-down list, select the vendor 

at the beginning of the vendor list, and then in the To Vendor drop-down list, select 

the vendor at the end of the range. All vendors in between the two vendors will be 

included.  

4. 
Set up the filters to have the system generate the e-file for the desired employees. 

• 
Select the Select all employees check box to generate forms for all employees. 

---


<!-- Page 118 -->

• 
To generate a file for a single vendor, select the vendor in the From Vendor 

drop-down list. 

• 
To include a range of employee, in the From employee drop-down list, select the 

employee at the beginning of the employee list, and then in the To employee 

drop-down list, select the employee at the end of the range. All employees in between 

the two employees will be included.  

5. 
Select the entity or entity group for which you are generating the 1099 e-file.  

6. 
In the Format section, in the 1099 form type section, click the Select button, select the 

desired forms to include in the file, and then click the Done button.  

7. 
Click the Process & Store button. This generates the form for all entities at the same time 

and stores it in a single file.  

8. 
If your system is enabled for multiple TCC codes, then the Transmitter Control Code box 

opens. Type the transmitter control code for the company that you want to generate forms 

for, and then click Process & Store. 

9. 
Fill in the Storage Options (on page 238) box.  

 The system generates the 1099 form based on your 1099 settings in the Multi Entity 

console. 

• 
Issue a separate 1099 per entity: Creates a separate 1099 form for each entity. 

•

• 
Run property groups that do not have the same Tax ID: Creates the 1099 forms for 

location groups even if the locations do not share the same tax ID. 

• 
Validate and issue 1099 by Tax ID and Legal Contact information: Creates the 1099 

file only when the locations share both the same tax ID and legal contact information. 

This option also groups vendors with the same tax ID.

DE 542 Form 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > All > 1099/1096 > DE542 Form`


Employers in California are required to register their businesses with the California Employment 

Development Department (EDD). The EDD issues an eight-digit employer payroll tax account 

number, also known as a state ID number, state employer Identification Number, or SEIN. 

Employers who pay more that $600 to an independent contractor or agrees to pay a contractor 

more than $600 must file a Form DE 542 with the EDD.  

Any business or government entity that is required to file a Federal Form 1099-MISC, 

Miscellaneous Information for service performed by an independent contractor must report using 

this form. 

You must report to the Employment Development Department within twenty (20) days of either 

making payments of $600 or more OR entering into a contract for $600 or more with an 

independent contractor in any calendar year, whichever is earlier. State and county agencies use 

the information on this form to assist in locating parents who are delinquent in their child support 

obligations. 

Customizing and Running the DE 542 Form 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > All > Reports > 1096/1099 > DE 542 Form`

1. 
Open the Accounts payable menu. 

2. 
In the Reports section, click 1096/1099, and then select DE 542 form.

• 
Type the starting and ending dates to identify the form’s period of coverage. 

Filling In the Filters Section 

1. 
If you want to filter by a vendor, a range of vendors, or all vendors use the From vendor and 

To vendor fields. 

How to use the From/To fields: 

All From/To field pairs work the same way. Use them to get search results in as broad or as 

fine a range as you need—from everything in the system down to a single specific object. 

To run this report for a single object: 

• 
Click the down arrow next to the From box, and from the menu that appears, click the 

object you want.

object you want at the beginning of the range.

### A/P Ledger Report
*Source: `RP Accounting AP Reports User Guide.pdf`, Page 126*

A/P Reports 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Reports User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

A/P Ledger Report 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > All > Reports > Vendors Reports > A/P Ledger`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Spend Management > All > Reports > Vendor Reports > A/P Ledger`


The A/P Ledger report provides a detailed list of vendor accounts, including what’s owed to each 

vendor. This report shows the beginning balance for the period you have selected as well as each 

transaction for each vendor. Use this report to see if the balance in the A/P ledger agrees with 

that in the general ledger and to see which vendors have balances greater than zero. 

The A/P Ledger report is a standard report. If you are looking for information on financial reports, 
see Creating a Financial Report.  

You can adjust the time period, vendor, vendor type, and payment summary to meet your 

reporting needs. Normally, this report shows only vendors with balances greater than zero. 

However, you can choose to include zero-balance vendors as well. In the report, you can click the 

vendor name link to open the Vendor Information page. 

This report includes only posted invoices. Invoices must be approved before they are posted, and 

only posted invoices appear in this report.  

Aged payables and escheated invoices do not appear in the A/P Ledger report.  

Intended Users of This Report 

• 
Accountants, controllers, anyone who needs to see who owes money to whom. 

• 
Accountants and controllers who need to balance the A/P ledger and the control account. 

• 
Accountants and controllers who need to make sure the beginning A/P ledger balance plus 

the net accounts payable activity for the current day equals the ending A/P ledger balance 

for the day.

To customize and run the A/P Ledger report: 

1. 
On the A/P Ledger page, use the Time Period section to define the time period you want

•

or click 
 Calendar, and then select the date from the calendar. Select the Prompt

to ask for the reporting period.

specific Start date and End date. You can either type the dates or click 
 Calendar 

and select the date from the calendar. Select the Prompt on run check box to have the 

system prompt you when you run the report to ask for the date range.

Specifying Dates in Getting Started for a full list of shortcut keys related to entering 
dates.

desired summary.

system fills in the To vendor box with the same vendor, setting it up in case you want to 

include just one vendor in the report.

Buttons 

Customize 
Opens the report’s customization page to change filters and time periods 

and to exclude specific types of data. 

The Customize button appears only after viewing a report or ledger. 

View 
Opens the report in your browser. 

Print 
Displays the report in printable PDF format so you can print it or save it on 

your computer. 

Process & store 
Generates the report and stores it for later access. 

Available formats include HTML, printable (PDF), Excel, CSV 

(comma-separated value), and Text. You can store reports (on page 236) in 

the system, and then access them with the My stored reports option in 

the menu.  

Email 
Sends the report as an email message. Click to open the Email report box, 

and then fill in the To field with the recipient’s email address. 

This button is not available for all reports. 

Add to dashboard 
Adds the report to a dashboard. 

Select the dashboard that you want to add it to, type a name for the 

report, and then type a description of the report.  

Select the Public check box to make the report available on a dashboard. 

This option is not available for all reports.  

Memorize 
Memorizes (that is, saves) the report in the system so you can refer to it 

later or modify and re-run it. 

Reports that you memorize can be scheduled to run on a recurring basis 
and can be automatically emailed. 

Export 
Exports the report to a separate file that you can then distribute or save on 

your computer. 

The file formats for exporting report data vary by report. 

Select 
Opens the multi-select box, where you can select items to filter by. 

In the multi-select box, select the items that you want to include in the 

report.  

The option to multi-select items is not available for all reports.

## A/P Invoice Register
*Source: `RP Accounting AP Reports User Guide.pdf`, Page 141*



### Before You Begin
*Source: `RP Accounting AP Reports User Guide.pdf`, Page 141*

Chapter 1: A/P Reports 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Reports User Guide 

A/P Invoice Register 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > All > Reports > AP Invoices & Registers > A/P 
Invoice Register`


The A/P Invoice Register report displays the invoices you received from vendors in the specified 

time period, as well as any account adjustments that were entered. Each invoice that is listed 

shows the date, vendor ID and name, invoice number, description (if any), due date, and amount. 

The A/P Invoice Register report is a standard report. If you are looking for information on financial 
reports, see Creating a Financial Report.  

Using the report, you can: 

• 
View A/P invoices and adjustments. 

• 
See the payment details for invoices, including the payment method and date. 

• 
See credit details, including which invoices a particular adjustment was applied to. 

• 
See subtotals of billing amounts by vendor or location. 

This report does not have a specific permission assigned to it, which means that anyone can run 
the report. 

Before You Begin 

This report does not have a specific permission assigned to it which means that anyone can run 

the report.

### Customizing and Running the A/P Invoice Register Report
*Source: `RP Accounting AP Reports User Guide.pdf`, Page 142*

A/P Reports 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Reports User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Customizing and Running the A/P Invoice Register Report 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > All > Reports > A/P Invoices & Registers > A/P 
Invoice Register`


The A/P Invoice Register report displays the invoices you received from vendors in the specified 

time period, as well as any account adjustments that were entered. Each A/P invoice that is listed 

shows the date, vendor ID, and name, A/P invoice number, description (if any), due date, and 

amount. 

Before running the report, you can select the time period and types of items to include as well as 

specify how you want the report to appear. 

To customize and run the A/P Invoice Register report: 

1. 
Open the Accounts Payable menu. 

2. 
In the A/P Invoices and Registers section, select the A/P invoice Register option. 

Filling In the Reporting Account Labels Section 

1. 
Select the Substitute with reporting accounts labels check box to use reporting accounts 

labels instead of the G/L account (or account labels, if enabled). 

2. 
In the Reporting account set drop-down list, select the set of reporting account labels you 

want to use in the report. 

If you select a reporting account set of labels, you must also select the Display transaction 

details check box in the Filters section. 

3. 
Select the Prompt on run check box if you want the system to prompt you for this decision 

at run time. 

Filling In the Time Period Section 

You can use one of the predefined reporting periods available from the Reporting period and As 

of date fields, or create your own reporting period using the Start date and End date fields. You 

can specify either the reporting period or the start and end dates, but not both.  

In the Time period section, do one of the following: 

• 
Use the Reporting period drop-down list to select the desired reporting period, and then 

type a date in the As of date field or click the 
 Calendar button and select a date. These 

periods are relative to the As of date. All periods begin on the first day of the period—that 

is, the first day of the month/quarter/year you select. For example, select Prior month as the 

reporting period, and then select a vendor to limit the report to a list of invoices from that 

vendor. 

• 
Type a specific Start date and/or a specific End date or click the 
 Calendar button in 

each field and select the desired date(s). 

---


<!-- Page 143 -->
Chapter 1: A/P Reports 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Reports User Guide 

Type “p” in a date field to automatically insert the last day of the prior month. See 
Specifying Dates in Getting Started for a full list of shortcut keys related to entering 
dates.  

• 
Select Prompt on run to have the system prompt you for this information at runtime. 

If you don’t specify a reporting period and you don’t select Prompt on run, then the generated 
report uses the current month to date. 

Filling In the Filters Section 

1. 
To limit the report to one vendor, select the vendor from the Vendor drop-down list. 

2. 
To limit the report to one vendor type, select the vendor type from the Vendor type 

drop-down list. 

3. 
Select the Transaction currency to assign the base currency the report should use. This 

option appears only for companies that have multiple entities and that use multiple 

currencies. 

4. 
In the Location drop-down list, select a location to limit the scope of the A/P Invoice 

Register report to one location or location group. This option appears only for companies 

that have multiple entities and that use multiple currencies. 

• 
Select the Individual report check box to have the system generate one report per 

location. 

You must click the Process & Store button at the end if you select the Individual 

Report option. 

• 
Select the Prompt on run check box to have the system ask the user to select a 

location before it will run the report.  

5. 
In the Unit drop-down list, select a unit to limit the scope of the report to just one unit. 

6. 
In the Department drop-down list, select a department or department group to limit the 

scope of the A/P Invoice Register report to one department or department group. This 

option appears only for companies that have multiple entities and that use multiple 

currencies. 

• 
Select the Individual report check box to have the system generate one report per 

department. 

You must click the Process & Store button at the end if you select the Individual 

Report option. 

• 
Select the Prompt on run check box to have the system ask the user to select a 

department before it will run the report. 

---


<!-- Page 144 -->
A/P Reports 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Reports User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

7. 
In the Show for drop-down list, select the desired locations to include. This selection applies 

regardless of the location selected in the Location drop-down list.  

• 
All Locations: Display the data of the location/entity you selected and its children. 

• 
This Location: Only display the data of the location/entity you selected and not of its 

children. 

• 
Child Locations: Only display the data of the children of the location/entity you 

selected. 

8. 
Select the Display transaction details check box to add columns of detail for each 

transaction in the report. This includes Account Label (or G/L Account), Department, 

Location, Allocation and Memo. By default, this check box is not selected, which means the 

report will not include any details. 

9. 
Select the Display payment details check box to show how the A/P invoice was paid. 

This option operates at the document level. This option is particularly useful when you pay 

an invoice with more than one check. Four new columns appear in the report for this data: 

Paid By, Method, Pay Date, and Bank Account. The Paid By column shows the document 

number that paid the A/P invoice. Typically, this is your check number. In this case, the 

Method column displays Printed Check, but it could also contain other methods such as 

Online or Discount. In addition, the Amount Paid column is expanded to show the amounts 

paid by each document. 

By default, this check box is not selected, which means the report will not include payment 

details. 

10. 
Select the Show credit details check box to show how adjustments were applied to A/P 

invoices. Selecting this option changes the Paid by column to a Paid by/Paid to column and 

adds information about the A/P invoices to which the adjustment was applied. 

11. 
Select the Hide paid documents check box if you are interested in viewing only those A/P 

invoices that have not yet been fully paid. This removes the paid A/P invoices from the 

report to make it simpler to sort through.  

By default, this check box is not selected, which means the report will include paid A/P 

invoices as well as unpaid ones. 

12. 
Select the Display owner information only check box to display all A/P invoice line items 

that have been released for payment. 

This option is unavailable if you did not also select the Display Transaction Details check 

box. This option appears only if you have enabled the Release to Pay feature. 

Filling in the Format Section 

1. 
In the Sort by drop-down list, select the field by which to sort the report: Date, Date Desc 

(descending), Vendor ID, Vendor Name, Vendor ID/Invoice Number, Invoice Number, Due 

---


<!-- Page 145 -->
Chapter 1: A/P Reports 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Reports User Guide 

Date, Due Date (descending), Amount, Amount desc (descending), Amount Paid, or Amount 

Paid desc (descending). Vendor is the default sort order. 

2. 
In the Page orientation area, to set the page layout of the report, select either Portrait or 

Landscape. 

3. 
You can group the report data by vendor or location. Select the desired grouping in the 

Group by drop-down list. 

Filling In the Titles Section and Running the Report 

Use this section to add a title, subtitle, and footer to your report. Titles, subtitles, and footers 

apply only to the PDF version of the report (click Print to get the PDF version). 

1. 
By default, the system completes the Report title 1 field with the system-assigned report 

name. This title displays in large type at the top of the page directly under your company 

name. You can leave the title as the default, or change it by typing over the default name in 

Report title 1.  

2. 
In Report title 2, type the text that you want to appear under the title of the report. This 

subtitle displays in smaller type, directly beneath the main title. 

3. 
In Footer text, type the text that you want to appear in the footer of the report. Footer text 

displays at the bottom center of the report. 

You can use up to 80 characters, including spaces, in each title, subtitle, and footer. 

4. 
Click the View button to run the report.  

View, process, memorize, export, or customize the report or add it to the dashboard by 
clicking one of the buttons at the top of the page. You can use trial and error to get the 
precise results you want. Fill in the desired fields, and click View to see the report. To 
refine the report further, click Customize to return to the report setup page. Repeat this 
process until you’re satisfied. Also, for complex financial reports you plan to run regularly, 
save the report when you are done setting it up. The next time you are ready to run the 
report, change only the As of date before running the report.

A/P Invoice Analysis Report

Use this report to help you analyze your purchases. The report shows the expense line items in

ordered over a specific period of time and from which vendors. 

The A/P Invoice Analysis report is a standard report. If you are looking for information on financial 
reports, see Creating a Financial Report. 

You can filter this report by: 

• 
Vendor 

• 
Vendor type 

• 
Account 

• 
Property 

• 
Unit 

• 
Department  

When you include asset category and type in the detailed report, it shows invoiced amounts 

associated with different categories. This report is helpful to accountants and controllers who 

want to see how the money is being spent by the asset. 

This report also can be generated as a chart. See A/P Invoice Analysis chart (on page 266).

> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > All > Reports > A/P Invoices & Registers > Report`


To customize and run the A/P Invoice analysis report: 

1. 
Open the Accounts payable menu. 

2.

invoice analysis, and then select Report. The A/P Invoices analysis report page opens,

Filling In the Time Period Section 

You can specify either the reporting period or the start and end dates, but not both.  

To select a reporting period for the report: 

1. 
In the Reporting period drop-down list, select a reporting period for the report. If you do 

not specify a reporting period, the system generates a report for the current month to date. 

2. 
Select or enter the As of date of the reporting period. 

Select the Prompt on run check box if you want the system to prompt you for this choice 

when you run the report. 

To select a start and end date: 

1. 
In the Start date field, select the start date of the time period for the report. 

2. 
In the End date field, select or enter the end date of the time period for the report. 

Type “p” in a date field to automatically insert the last day of the prior month. See 
Specifying Dates in Getting Started for a full list of shortcut keys related to entering 
dates.  

Select the Prompt on run check box if you want the system to prompt you for this choice 

when you run the report. 

If you complete all of the time period fields (that is, if you fill in the Reporting period and As 

of date fields in addition to the Start date and End date fields), the system bases your 
report only on the specified start and end dates. It ignores the As of date specified. 

Filling In the Filters Section 

Set up filters to narrow your results. Using filters is optional. 

1. 
To show results for a specific vendor or range of vendors, select one or more vendors in the 

From vendor and To vendor fields. In UK versions, these fields are called From Supplier and 

To Supplier.) 

• 
To run the report for a single vendor, select the vendor in the From vendor (supplier) 

drop-down list. The system completes the To vendor field with the same vendor.  

• 
To run the report for all vendors, leave the fields blank. 

• 
To run the report for a range of vendors, select the first vendor in the list. In To 

vendor, select the ending vendor in the range. 

How to use the From/To fields: 

All From/To field pairs work the same way. Use them to get search results in as broad or as 

fine a range as you need—from everything in the system down to a single specific object.

An object is a catch -all term that refers to any specific data item in the system. 
Customers, vendors, items, and accounts are all examples of objects. 

2. 
To show results for one type of vendor (supplier), in Vendor (supplier) type, select the 

vendor (supplier) type you want the report to include. 

3. 
To show results for a specific account or range of accounts, use the From account and To 

account drop-down lists.

report to transactions that took place in a specific currency.

• 
Select the Prompt on run check box if you want the system to prompt you for this

•

Filling In the Titles Section and Run the Report 

Use this section to add a title, subtitle, and footer to your report. Titles, subtitles, and footers 

apply only to the PDF version of this report. (Click Print to get the PDF version). 

The system completes the Report Title 1 field with the system-assigned report name. This title 

displays in large type at the top of the page directly under your company name. 

1. 
In Report Title 1, you can leave the title as the default, or change it by typing over the 

default name.  

2. 
In Report title 2, enter the text that you want to appear under the title of the report. This 

subtitle displays in smaller type, directly beneath the main title. 

3. 
In Footer text, type the text that you want to appear in the footer of the report. Footer text 

displays at the bottom center of the report. 

You can use up to 80 characters, including spaces, in each title, subtitle, and footer. 

Running the Report 

When you have finished configuring the report, click one of the following buttons: 

• 
View: Runs and displays the report directly in your browser.  

• 
Print: Exports the report to a printable PDF file. 

• 
Process & store: Allows you to process and store the report in the My stored reports list. 

• 
Add to dashboard: Adds the report to one of your custom dashboards. 

• 
Memorize: Memorizes the report and stores it in the Memorized reports list. 

• 
Export: Exports the report to a Word, CSV, Excel, or Text file. 

What’s Next?  

After you run the report, you can email the report to others. Use trial and error to get the precise 

results you want by filling in the desired fields and then clicking View to run the report. If you 

want to refine the report further, click Customize to return to the report setup page. Repeat this 

process as needed.

A/P Invoice Analysis Report Columns

Summary Report Columns 

G/L Account

Amount/ 

Txn Amount

The Detailed A/P Invoice Analysis report contains the following columns: 

Detailed Report Columns 

Account 
This is the account number of the checking account. 

Date 
This is the date on which the A/P invoices were received by you from the 

vendor. 

G/L posting date 
This is the date that the A/P invoices post. 

Vendor (Supplier) 
This is the ID associated with your vendor followed by vendor’s name. 

Invoice # 
This is the vendor’s billing account number with your company. 

Description 
This is the type of items charged to you (for example, legal consulting, 

monthly bill, or telecommunications costs). 

Department 
This is the number and name of the department to which the A/P 

invoice is charged. 

Location (Location 

area) 

This is the physical location associated with the invoice. 

Memo 
This column contains the memo text of the line item. 

Unit

Use the Titles section to add a title, subtitle, and footer to your PDF report. Titles, subtitles, and

Customizing and Running the Unit Cost Report 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > All > Reports > A/P Invoices & Registers > Unit Cost`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Spend Management > All > Reports > Vendor Reports > Unit Cost`


The Unit Cost report is a standard report. If you are looking for information on financial reports, 
see Creating a Financial Report. 

To customize and run the Unit Cost report: 

1. 
Open the Accounts Payable menu. 

2. 
In the A/P Invoices and Registers section, select Unit Cost. 

Filling In the Time Period Section 

You can use one of the predefined reporting periods available from the Reporting Period and As 

of Date fields or create your own reporting period using the Start Date and End Date boxes. You 

can specify either the reporting period or the start and end dates, but not both. 

Type “p” in a date field to automatically insert the last day of the prior month. See Specifying 
Dates in Getting Started for a full list of shortcut keys related to entering dates. 

In the Time Period section, do one of the following: 

• 
Use the Reporting period drop-down list to select the desired reporting period and then 

either type a date in the As of Date field or use the calendar to select a date. These periods 

are relative to the As of Date. All periods begin on the first day of the period—that is, the 

first day of the month/quarter/year you select. For example, select Prior month as the 

---


<!-- Page 167 -->
Chapter 1: A/P Reports 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Reports User Guide 

reporting period, and then select a vendor to limit the report to a list of payments to that 

vendor. 

• 
Type a specific Start date and/or a specific End date or use the calendar in each field to 

select the desired date(s). 

Type “p” in a date field to automatically insert the last day of the prior month. See 
Specifying Dates in Getting Started for a full list of shortcut keys related to entering 
dates.  

• 
Select Prompt on run to have the system prompt you for this information at run time. 

If you don’t specify a reporting period and you don’t select Prompt on run, the generated 
report uses the current month to date. 

Filling In the Filters Section 

Set the Filters to get the specific data you want. You can include specific types of data, such as 

specific vendors, accounts, location, and unit. 

To get fewer and more precise results in your report, set more filters. 

1. 
Use the From Vendor and To Vendor fields to choose one vendor, a range of vendors, or all 

vendors. Leave the fields blank to include all vendors in the report. 

2. 
Use the Account from and Account to fields to choose one account or a range of accounts. 

Leave the fields blank to include all accounts in the report. 

3. 
In the Account group drop-down list, choose an account group to filter the report by. 

4. 
In the Location drop-down list, select a location to limit the scope of the Unit Cost report to 

one location or location group. 

Select the Individual report check box to have the system generate one report per location. 

You must click the Process & Store button at the end if you select the Individual Report 
option. 

Select the Prompt on run check box to have the system ask the user to select a location 

before it will run the report. 

5. 
In the Unit drop-down list, select a unit to limit the scope of the report to the unit cost for 

one unit. 

Filling In the Format Section 

• 
In the Report type drop-down list, choose the format the report, Summary or Detail. 

Filling In the Titles Section and Run the Report 

Use this section to add a title, subtitle, and footer to your report. Titles, subtitles, and footers 

apply only to the PDF version of this report. (Click Print to get the PDF version).

Customizing and Running the A/P Selected Invoices Report 

To customize and run the A/P Selected Invoices report: 

1. 
Open the Accounts payable menu. 

2. 
In the A/P Invoices & Registers section, select Selected A/P invoices. The Selected Invoices 

report parameters page opens. 

Filling In the Filters Section 

This report does not have a date filter so that it includes all unconfirmed payments. 

1. 
To show results for one type of vendor, in Vendor type, select the vendor type you want the 

report to include. 

2. 
To show results for a specific vendor or range of vendors, select one or more vendors in the 

From vendor and To vendor fields. 

• 
To run the report for a single vendor, select the vendor in the From vendor 

drop-down list. The system completes the To vendor field with the same vendor.  

• 
To run the report for all vendors, leave the fields blank. 

• 
To run the report for a range of vendors, select the first vendor in the list. In To 

vendor, select the ending vendor in the range. 

How to use the From/To fields: 

All From/To field pairs work the same way. Use them to get search results in as broad or as 

fine a range as you need—from everything in the system down to a single specific object. 

To run this report for a single object: 

• 
Click the down arrow next to the From box, and from the menu that appears, click the 

object you want. 

• 
Click the down arrow next to the To box, and from the menu that appears, click the 

same object. 

To run this report for a specific range of objects: 

• 
Click the down arrow next to the From box, and from the menu that appears, click the 

object you want at the beginning of the range. 

• 
Click the down arrow next to the To box, and from the menu that appears, click the 

object you want at the end of the range.

precise results you want. Fill in the desired fields, and click View to see the report. To 
refine the report further, click Customize to return to the report setup page. Repeat this 
process until you’re satisfied. Also, for complex financial reports you plan to run regularly, 
save the report when you are done setting it up. The next time you are ready to run the 
report, change only the As of date before running the report.

applied

### Recurring A/P Invoice Status Report
*Source: `RP Accounting AP Reports User Guide.pdf`, Page 176*

A/P Reports 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Reports User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Recurring A/P Invoice Status Report 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > All > Reports > AP Invoices & Registers > Recurring 
A/P Invoice Status`


The Recurring A/P Invoice Status report shows a list of recurring invoices from your vendors, along 

with details about the recurring payments, such as the frequency with which the invoice is paid, 

how many times the recurring invoice has been paid, the term, amount, and so on. Within the 

report, you may navigate into vendor information or the recurring invoice itself. 

The Recurring A/P Invoice Status report is a standard report. If you are looking for information on 
financial reports, see Creating a Financial Report. 

You can adjust the time period, vendor, vendor type, and payment summary to meet your 

reporting needs. Normally, this report shows only vendors with balances greater than zero. 

However, you can choose to include zero-balance vendors as well. In the report, you can click the 

recurring invoice number to review the recurring invoice, as needed. 

You can filter this report by: 

• 
Transaction type (A/P invoices, Vendor bill, Purchase order, and PO receiver) 

• 
Transaction currency 

• 
Vendor or range of vendors 

• 
Location 

• 
Department 

• 
All transactions or failed transactions only 

• 
Include all headers

Before You Begin
