user’s permissions. 

Customizing and Running the Recurring A/P Invoice Status Report 

To customize and run the Recurring A/P Invoice Status report: 

1. 
Click the Applications menu, select Accounts payable, and then select the All tab. 

2. 
Under A/P Invoices & Registers, select Recurring A/P invoice status report. The Recurring 

A/P invoice status report parameters page is displayed. 

Before running the report, you can select the time period and types of items to include and 

specify how you want the report to appear. 

Filling In the Time Period Section 

You can specify either the reporting period or a date range, but not both.  

To select a reporting period for the report: 

1. 
In the Reporting period drop-down list, select a reporting period for the report. If you do 

not specify a reporting period, the system generates a report for the current month to date. 

2. 
Select or enter the As of date of the reporting period. 

Select the Prompt on run check box if you want the system to prompt you for this choice 

when you run the report. 

To define a date range: 

1. 
In the Start date field, type the starting date of a date range or select the 
 Calendar 

button and then select the start date of date range that you want the report to cover. 

2. 
In the End date field, type the end date of the date range for the report. 

---


<!-- Page 178 -->
A/P Reports 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Reports User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Type “p” in a date field to automatically insert the last day of the prior month. See 
Specifying Dates in Getting Started for a full list of shortcut keys related to entering 
dates.  

3. 
Select the Prompt on run check box if you want the system to prompt you for this choice 

when you run the report. 

If you complete all of the time period fields (that is, if you fill in the Reporting period and As 

of date fields in addition to the Start date and End date fields), the system bases your 
report only on the specified start and end dates. It ignores the As of date specified. 

Filling In the Filters Section 

1. 
In the Transaction type drop-down list, select a transaction type to filter the report so that it 

only includes transactions of the selected type. 

2. 
In the Transaction currency drop-down list, filter the report so that it only includes 

transactions in the selected currency. 

3. 
Use the From vendor and To vendor drop-down lists to select the beginning and ending 

vendor in a range to include a range of vendors in the report. 

In From vendor, select the first vendor in a range of vendors to include in the report. The 

system fills in the To vendor box with the same vendor, setting it up in case you want to 

include just one vendor in the report. 

In To vendor, select the last vendor in a range of vendors.  

Alternatively, leave the value in both fields set to the same vendor if you want to report on 

one vendor. 

4. 
In the Location drop-down list, select a location to include only transactions of the selected 

location. 

5. 
In the Department drop-down list, select a department to include only transactions of the 

selected department. 

6. 
Select the Show only failed check box to limit the report to only including failed recurring 

transactions. 

7. 
Click the Show all headers check box to show the transaction header fields in the report. 

Filling In the Titles Section 

Use this section to add a title, subtitle, and footer to your report. Titles, subtitles, and footers 

apply only to the .pdf version of this report. (Click Print to get the PDF version). 

---

Customizing and Running the Management Fee Report 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > All > A/P Invoices & Registers > Management Fee 
Report`


To customize and run the Management Fee report: 

1. 
Open the Accounts payable menu. 

2. 
In the A/P Invoices & Registers, select Management fee report. The parameters page opens. 

Filling In the Time Period Section 

To define the report’s time period, select the As of date: 

• 
In the As of date field, select or type the starting date of the report’s coverage. 

Type “p” in a date field to automatically insert the last day of the prior month. See 
Specifying Dates in Getting Started for a full list of shortcut keys related to entering 
dates.  

Filling In the Filters Section 

Set up report filters to narrow your results. Using filters is optional. 

1. 
To limit the report to one property, in the Property drop-down list, select a property. 

2. 
To limit the report to one management reporting code, select the code type from the 

Management Reporting Codes drop-down list. 

3. 
If you selected an MRC, then select the specific code in the Code drop-down list. 

4. 
To filter by fee type, click the Fee type drop-down list, and then select the desired type 

(Percentage, Flat, Total Units, or Occupied Units). 

5. 
Under Show transaction information: 

• 
Select Summary for a compact report. 

• 
Select Details for a full report. 

6. 
Select the Include calculated check box to include calculation status in the detailed version 

of the report. The State column shows either Posted, Calculated, or Recalculated. 

7. 
Select the Include activity check box to include the monthly activity in the report. 

8. 
Click the View button to run the report.

Management Fee Report Columns 

The default Management Fee report contains the following columns: 

Summary Report Columns 

Property 
This column contains the name of the property that has been charged 

fees. 

Fee type 
This column lists the fee type: Flat fee, Percentage, Total units, and 

Occupied units. 

Activity Month/Year 
This column shows the fee activity for the month and year.  

The activity columns appear only when the Include activity check box is 

selected. 

Month/Year 
This column indicates the amount in fees charged for the selected 

coverage period. 

Total 
This column shows the total amount of fees for the time period and 

each property. The Total row at the bottom shows the total amount for 

all properties. 

The detailed version of the report adds these columns: 

Detailed Report Columns 

Fee ID 
This column contains the unique identifier of the fee. 

Fee 
This column indicates whether the fee is a percentage or a fixed amount. 

G/L range 
This column contains the G/L range associated with the fee. 

State 
This column contains the status of the calculation:  

• 
Calculated: The fee is calculated but not posted. 

• 
Posted: The fee has been calculated and posted. 

• 
Recalculated: The fee has been recalculated.

Filling In the Time Period Section 

You can use one of the predefined reporting periods available from the Reporting period and As 

of date fields, or create your own reporting period using the Start date and End date boxes. You 

can specify either the reporting period or the start and end dates, but not both.  

In the Time period section, do one of the following: 

• 
Use the Reporting period drop-down list to select the desired reporting period and then 

either type a date in the As of date field or use the calendar to select a date. These periods 

are relative to the As of date. All periods begin on the first day of the period—that is, the 

first day of the month/quarter/year you select. For example, select Prior month as the 

reporting period, and then select a vendor to limit the report to a list of payments to that 

vendor. 

• 
Type a specific Start date and/or a specific End date or use the calendar in each field to 

select the desired date(s). 

Type “p” in a date field to automatically insert the last day of the prior month. See 
Specifying Dates in Getting Started for a full list of shortcut keys related to entering 
dates.  

Filling In the Filters Section 

Set the Filters to get the specific data you want. You can include or exclude payment details. 

To get fewer and more precise results in your report, set more filters. 

1. 
To show results for a specific vendor or range of vendors, select one or more vendors in the 

From vendor and To vendor fields. 

• 
To run the report for a single vendor, select the vendor in the From vendor 

drop-down list. The system completes the To vendor field with the same vendor.  

• 
To run the report for all vendors, leave the fields blank. 

• 
To run the report for a range of vendors, select the first vendor in the list. In the To 

vendor drop-down list, select the ending vendor in the range.

How to use the From/To fields: 

All From/To field pairs work the same way. Use them to get search results in as broad or as 

fine a range as you need—from everything in the system down to a single specific object. 

To run this report for a single object: 

• 
Click the down arrow next to the From box, and from the menu that appears, click the 

object you want. 

• 
Click the down arrow next to the To box, and from the menu that appears, click the 

same object. 

To run this report for a specific range of objects: 

• 
Click the down arrow next to the From box, and from the menu that appears, click the 

object you want at the beginning of the range. 

• 
Click the down arrow next to the To box, and from the menu that appears, click the 

object you want at the end of the range. 

To run this report for all objects: 

Leave both boxes blank. 

If you have a large number of objects, or if this report takes too long to process, use the 

From and To boxes to run a series of smaller reports. For example, you can run five reports, 

one each for objects whose names begin with A–E, then F-J, K-O, P-T, and U–Z. 

An object is a catch -all term that refers to any specific data item in the system. 
Customers, vendors, items, and accounts are all examples of objects. 

2. 
To filter the report so that it includes only RealPage Payments from one location, select the 

location from the Location drop-down list. 

3. 
Select the Show payment details check box to include payment details in the report. For the 

additional details that are included, see RealPage payments report columns (on page 191). 

Filling In the Format Section 

Select how you want to sort the report. 

• 
Click the Sort by drop-down box, and then select the item by which to sort the report. You 

can sort by date, third-party payment number, vendor name, vendor ID, or amount.

RealPage Payments Report Columns 

The standard RealPage Payments report contains the following columns: 

Standard Report Columns 

As of date 
This date appears at the top of the report to indicate the report’s period 

of coverage. 

Vendor 
This is the vendor to whom payments were made during the selected 

time period. 

Third Party Payment 

No 

This is the unique identifier of the third-party payment. 

Amount 
This is the amount on the payment request sent to the third-party 

service. 

Paid amount 
This is the amount that the third-party payment service paid the vendor. 

This column appears further to the right in the report when you have 
selected to include payment details. 

Location 
This is the location associated with the vendor invoice. This column 

contains “MULTIPLE” when the vendor is being paid on behalf of 

multiple locations. 

Third Party Status 
This is the status of the payment at the third-party payment processor. 

Third Party Date 
This is the date that the third-party processor changed the status noted 

in the Third-party status column. 

Total (vendor) 
This is the total payments made to the vendor. 

When you select the Show payment details check box, the report includes these additional 

columns and rows: 

Detailed Report Columns 

Payment method 
This is the payment method used to pay the vendor. “AvidPay check” 

appears when the RealPage Payments third-party payment service has 

been used. 

Status date 
This is the date that RealPage Payments paid the vendor. 

Check/Payment 

number 

This is the unique identifier of the check or payment that RealPage 

Payments made to the vendor. 

Total (property) 
This is the total paid by the property.

The A/P Reclassification report displays a list of documents with data that was reclassified from 

one account to another and the names of those who reclassified them. This report is useful for 

accountants and controllers, and those who are responsible for managing the company’s 

financials. You can use this report as an audit trail. 

The A/P Reclassification report is a standard report. If you are looking for information on financial 
reports, see Creating a Financial Report. 

The Accounts Receivable application also offers a Reclassification Report for A/R transactions.

not see the option in the menu, then ask your System Administrator to check your permissions.

Customizing and Running the A/P Reclassification Report 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > All > Reports > A/P Invoices & Registers > 
Reclassification`


To customize and run the reclassification report: 

1. 
Open the Accounts payable menu. 

2. 
In the A/P Invoices & Registers, select Reclassification. The A/P Reclassification report 

parameters page opens. 

Filling In the Time Period Section 

You can specify either a reporting period or a date range, but not both.  

To run a report for a reporting period: 

1. 
In the Reporting period drop-down list, select a reporting period for the report. If you do 

not specify a reporting period, the system generates a report for the current month to date. 

2. 
In the As of date field, select or type the starting date of the reporting period. 

Type “p” in a date field to automatically insert the last day of the prior month. See 
Specifying Dates in Getting Started for a full list of shortcut keys related to entering 
dates.  

Select the Prompt on run check box if you want the system to prompt you for this choice 

before the report runs. 

To run a report on a date range: 

1. 
In the Start date field, type the start date of the date range for the report or click 

Calendar and select the date. 

2. 
In the End date field, select or type the end date of the date range for the report or click 

Calendar and select the date. 

Select the Prompt on run check box if you want the system to prompt for this choice before 

the report runs. 

If you complete all of the time period fields (that is, if you fill in the Reporting period and As 

of date fields in addition to the Start date and End date fields), the system bases your 
report only on the specified start and end dates. It ignores the As of date specified. 

---


<!-- Page 216 -->
A/P Reports 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Reports User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Filling In the Filters Section 

Set up report filters to narrow your results. Using filters is optional. 

1. 
Select either document number or vendor type. 

• 
To show a specific document number, in Document number, select the document 

number from the drop-down list or click the Find link to search for it. 

• 
To show results for one type of vendor, in Vendor type, select the vendor type you 

want the report to cover. 

2. 
To show results for a specific vendor or range of vendors, select one or more vendors in the 

From vendor and To vendor fields. 

• 
To run the report for a single vendor, select the vendor in the From vendor 

drop-down list. The system completes the To vendor field with the same vendor.  

• 
To run the report for all vendors, leave the fields blank. 

• 
To run the report for a range of vendors, select the first vendor in the list. In To 

vendor, select the ending vendor in the range. 

How to use the From/To fields: 

All From/To field pairs work the same way. Use them to get search results in as broad or as 

fine a range as you need—from everything in the system down to a single specific object. 

To run this report for a single object: 

• 
Click the down arrow next to the From box, and from the menu that appears, click the 

object you want. 

• 
Click the down arrow next to the To box, and from the menu that appears, click the 

same object. 

To run this report for a specific range of objects: 

• 
Click the down arrow next to the From box, and from the menu that appears, click the 

object you want at the beginning of the range. 

• 
Click the down arrow next to the To box, and from the menu that appears, click the 

object you want at the end of the range.

To run this report for all objects: 

Leave both boxes blank. 

If you have a large number of objects, or if this report takes too long to process, use the 

From and To boxes to run a series of smaller reports. For example, you can run five reports, 

one each for objects whose names begin with A–E, then F-J, K-O, P-T, and U–Z. 

An object is a catch -all term that refers to any specific data item in the system. 
Customers, vendors, items, and accounts are all examples of objects. 

3. 
Select a user from the User ID drop-down list to limit the report to transactions that the 

user has reclassified.  

4. 
Under Include, select the transactions to include: 

• 
All: Select to include A/P invoices, adjustments, and purchases transactions.  

• 
A/P invoices only: Include only A/P invoices that were reclassified. 

• 
Adjustments only: Include only adjustments that were reclassified. 

• 
Purchases only: Include only purchase transactions that were reclassified. 

Filling In the Format Section 

Use this section to specify the sort order and to change the page layout of the report. 

To format this report: 

1. 
To sort the report results, click the Sort by drop-down list, and then click the category to 

sort by: 

Vendor ID: Sort numerically by the unique identifier of vendors. This is the default selection. 

Vendor name: Sort alphabetically by vendor name. 

Document date: Sort chronologically by the date of the documents. 

Document number: Sort numerically by document number.  

Reclassification date: Sort chronologically by the date that items were reclassified. 

2. 
To change the page layout, click the Page orientation drop-down list, and then select either 

Portrait or Landscape. Portrait is the default layout.

### Check Register Report
*Source: `RP Accounting AP Reports User Guide.pdf`, Page 220*

A/P Reports 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Reports User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Check Register Report 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > All > Reports > A/P Invoices & Registers > Check 
Register`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Cash Management > All > Reports > Registers > Check`


Use the Check Register report to view and output check register entries. This report provides a list 

of payments made through a specified bank (or multiple banks). You can view a list of payments 

made by check or view a list of all payments and their corresponding payment method (for 

example, by check, EFT, cash, or transfer of funds). 

The Check Register report is a standard report. If you are looking for information on financial 
reports, see Creating a Financial Report.  

Reconciliation Status 

By default, the report displays the reconciliation status of each payment entry, such as In Transit 

or Cleared. You can disable this option as needed when you customize and run the report. 

Voiding Checks 

You can void checks from Check Register report or filter the report to show only voided checks. 

The Void option appears only when the following conditions are true: 

• 
The check has been confirmed. 

• 
You have the appropriate permissions. To void A/P payments, you need permissions in 

Accounts Payable to void posted payments and (optionally) posted advances. 

• 
If you are in a multi-entity environment, you are in the same entity that made the payment. 

For example, if you are displaying the Check Register report for the top-level entity and do 

not see the Void link, try opening the report for the entity from which the payment was 

made. 

---

You do not have the Void permission for Posted payments.

system. You must contact Avid to begin the void process. 

• 
The payment was made at the top level, but you are viewing the report at the entity level. 

• 
The payment was made at the entity level, but you are viewing the report at the top level.

The transaction is not eligible to be voided because it has already been voided.

Customizing and Running the Check Register Report 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > All > Reports > A/P Invoices & Registers > Check

The Check Register report includes payment information so that you can know whether you paid 

an A/P invoice by ACH, cash, check, or transfer. This report offers both Summary and Detail 

versions.  

You can access the Check Register report from the Cash management application as well, but the

##### Check Register Report Columns
*Source: `RP Accounting AP Reports User Guide.pdf`, Page 226*

A/P Reports 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Reports User Guide

Check Register Report Columns 

Depending on your configuration, the Check Register report contains the following columns. 

Some columns are labeled differently depending on whether you’re running the report from the 

Accounts Payable application or the Cash Management application. 

Columns 

Bank 
This is the account ID and bank name associated with the checking 

account. 

Date 
This is the date on which the check was written. When you pay A/P 

invoices, the register displays the date you set in the Set payment date 

to field. 

When the check date and payment date are different, both dates appear 

in the column. The dates are formatted as [Payment Date]-Check Date 

[Check Date]. For example, if the check was dated 8/14/2025 but the 

payment date was set to 8/15/2025, then the Date column would 

display: 

08/15/2015-Check Date (08/14/2025) 

The transaction date is often different than the original check date for 

voided payments. 

The Date column does not display two dates when the Sort by field is 
set to Date on the report configuration page.

Setting Up Standard Report Parameters 

The first step in creating a report or chart is to define the coverage of the report. Each report has 

a different set of parameters, although most reports have these parameter types: 

• 
Period: This section lets you choose a reporting period or define a date or a date range for 

which you want data.  

• 
Filters: This section lets you define the data to include in the report. 

• 
Format: This section allows you to define how to sort and group the data. Some reports 

allow you to set the report’s page orientation. 

• 
Titles: This section allows you to define the text that appears at the top and bottom of the 

report pages. 

Refer to each report for specific instructions on configuring a report’s parameters. 

What’s Next? 

• 
Running a Report (on page 230) 

Running a Report 

After setting up a standard report’s parameters (time period, filters, format, and titles), click the 

View button to run the report.  

Examine the results. If you don’t like the results, then click the Customize button to return to the 

report’s setup page and make desired changes. 

If you do like the results, there are several things that you can do next. 

• 
To save the report’s results, click the Process & Store button to save the results.  

• 
To save the report’s settings so that you can use them again, memorize the report.

Memorizing Standard Reports and Charts 

Use the Memorize button to save a report or chart so that you can refer to it later or modify and 

re-run it. 

To memorize a report or chart: 

1. 
Click the Memorize button. The Memorize Report Parameters box opens. 

2. 
In the Name field, type a name that will make sense to others if you plan to make the report 

or chart available to others. 

3. 
Select the Public check box to make the report or chart available to others in their 

Memorized reports list. Clear the check box to make the report or chart available only to 

yourself. 

4. 
Click the Save button. 

Scheduling a Memorized Report or Chart 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Reports > All > Reports Center > Memorized > More Actions > Edit 
Schedule`


See the How to Get Here topic for a list of ways to access memorized reports. 

Use the Schedule memorized report page to schedule a memorized report or chart to run 

automatically and routinely. 

Accessing the Schedule Memorized Report Page  

You can schedule a report or chart from either the Reports application or the application where it 

was originally memorized. 

To schedule a report from the Reports application: 

1. 
Open the Reports menu, and then click the Reports center option. The Reports center page 

opens.  

2. 
Select the Memorized tab. 

3. 
In the (View) drop-down list, select the application associated with the report, or select All 

applications. 

4. 
Find the report or chart you want to schedule, and then click More actions. 

5. 
Select the Edit schedule option. The Schedule memorized report page opens. 

---


<!-- Page 238 -->
Working with Reports 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Reports User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

To schedule a report from another application: 

1. 
In the Applications menu, select the application where the memorized report is located, and 

then select the All tab. 

2. 
In the Reports section, click the Memorized reports option. 

3. 
Find the report or chart you want to schedule, and then click the Schedule link. The 

Schedule memorized report page opens. 

Filtering the Report 

1. 
In the Department/group and Location/group drop-down lists, select a specific department 

or location (or group of departments or locations) by which to filter the report. If you leave 

the filters blank, then the report will run for all departments and locations. 

2. 
If you are scheduling a financial report and the report is set to prompt for G/L account 

groups, then the G/L account group selection box appears. Select one or more G/L account 

groups to filter the report by. 

3. 
In the As of date field, type or select the date from which the scheduled report should 

display data. Leave this field blank to use the current date. If you enter an As of date, that 

date will always be used regardless of when the schedule is run. 

Type “p” in a date field to automatically insert the last day of the prior month. See 

Specifying Dates in Getting Started for a full list of shortcut keys related to entering dates. If 

you enabled reporting account labels in the General Ledger, then you have the option to 

substitute the account labels in the report with the reporting account set’s labels: 

• 
To enable reporting account labels, select the Substitute with reporting accounts 

labels check box. The Reporting account set drop-down list appears. 

• 
In the Reporting account set drop-down list, select the reporting account set whose 

labels you want to use. 

Scheduling the Report 

1. 
In the Start date field, type or select the date on which to start running the report.  

Typically, the Start date is a date in the future. If you select a date in the past, then the 
report executes immediately after you save it. The Start date also determines the date 
that the system schedules the report to run in future occurrences; for example, if you are 
scheduling the report to run weekly and the Start date is on a Monday, then the system will 
run the report every Monday. 

Type “p” in a date field to automatically insert the last day of the prior month. See 

Specifying Dates in Getting Started for a full list of shortcut keys related to entering dates.  

2. 
In the Ending on field, select when to stop running the report:  

---


<!-- Page 239 -->
Chapter 2: Working with Reports 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Reports User Guide 

• 
Never: Run the report indefinitely. 

• 
Number of occurrences: Stop running the report after a specific number of 

occurrences.  

• 
In the End after field, type the number of occurrences after which to stop running 

the report; for example, type “5” to stop after five occurrences. 

• 
End date: Stop running the report on a specific date.  

• 
In the End on field, type or select the date on which to stop running the report. 

3. 
In the Recurrence drop-down list, select an option: 

• 
None: Run the report once on the scheduled date. 

• 
Days: Run the report once every X days. 

• 
Weeks: Run the report once every X weeks. 

• 
Months: Run the report once every X months.  

• 
Select the End of month check box to disregard the start date and run the report 

on the last day of the month. 

• 
Years: Run the report once a year. 

4. 
If you selected Days, Weeks, Months, or Years, type the number of times to run the report 

in the Every field.  

5. 
In the Email results to field, type the email address where you want the system to send the 

report results. 

• 
Click Save. 

Storing and Delivering the Report 

1. 
Select one or more delivery options for the report: 

• 
Email: Sends the report in an email. 

• 
Store report: Stores the report in the My stored reports list. 

• 
Store in cloud: Stores the report in a cloud-storage target. 

• 
Store in Reporting Portal: Stores the report in the selected owner portal(s). 

2. 
Fill in the fields corresponding with each section. 

---


<!-- Page 240 -->

© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Email 

1. 
In the To field, type the email address to which you want to send the report. 

2. 
Select the CC me check box if you want the system to send a copy of the email message to 

your inbox. 

3. 
In the Subject field, type the subject of the email message. 

4. 
In the Report type drop-down list, select a report format: 

•

• 
CSV: Sends the report in a comma-separated values (CSV) file.

5.

includes the report.

appears in the My stored reports list in the Title column. 

2. 
In the Report type drop-down list, select a report format: 

• 
HTML: Saves the report as an HTML file. 

• 
Printable: Saves the report as a printable PDF file. 

• 
CSV: Saves the report in a comma-separated values (CSV) file. 

• 
Excel: Saves the report in an Excel file. 

• 
Text: Saves the report in a text file.

Store in Cloud 

1. 
In the Send to drop-down list, select a cloud-storage target where you want to deliver the

that others have defined and marked as public. If you’re an administrator, you can see all

2.

• 
HTML: Saves the report as an HTML file.

Printable: Saves the report as a printable PDF file. 

• 
CSV: Saves the report in a comma-separated values (CSV) file. 

• 
Excel: Saves the report in an Excel file. 

• 
Text: Saves the report in a simple text file. 

Store in Reporting Portal 

1. 
In the Report name field, type the name of the report as you want it to appear in the owner 

portal(s). 

2. 
In the Report type drop-down list, select a report format: 

• 
HTML: Saves the report as an HTML file. 

• 
Printable: Saves the report as a printable PDF file. 

• 
CSV: Saves the report in a comma-separated values (CSV) file. 

• 
Excel: Saves the report in an Excel file. 

3. 
In the Publish to field, select the folder to which you want to upload the report. 

The system creates default folders based on the reporting periods set up in General 
Ledger; however, you can create custom folders to upload documents to on the 

Configuration page for the Reporting Portal application. 

4. 
Select the Owner(s) for which you are uploading the report. 

Saving the Report Schedule 

When you have finished configuring the report schedule and delivery options, click Save to 

schedule the memorized report.

Storing Reports 

You can generate reports on demand and store them in My stored reports for later access. Use 

the Storage options page to choose the report format and where to store the report after it is 

processed. 

If you plan to process and store the same report on a recurring basis, consider scheduling it. 

Generating and Storing a Report 

To generate and store a report: 

1. 
Locate your report type and select the option to process or run it. 


> **Navigation Path:** `• 
Financial report: In the Financial reports list (General Ledger > All > Financial`


Reporting, then click Financial reports), locate the report, and then click the Process & 

store link. 


> **Navigation Path:** `• 
Report groups: In the Report groups list (Reports > More > Reports Groups), locate`


the report group, and then click the Run link. 

• 
Other reports: Start by displaying the report. For example, you might display a 


> **Navigation Path:** `Customer Aging report by going to Accounts Receivable > All > Reports > Customer`


Aging Report. Select report options as needed and then click the Process & store 

button. 

2. 
On the Storage options page, select the date to run the report on, where the report should 

be stored, the report name, and the format of the report. 

If you’re running a report group, you can run the report for multiple locations or entities at 

once. To ensure that the reports are collated by entity (so that each entity’s reports appear 

together), select the Grouped by Location/Entity check box. 

3. 
Follow the instructions below for selecting the report format and storage location. 

Storing in Stored Reports 

• 
Reports are stored in My Stored Reports, which you can access from any application menu. 

For example, to access a stored Accounts Receivable report, go to Accounts Receivable > 


> **Navigation Path:** `All > My Stored Reports.`


• 
Reports in the My stored reports list can only be accessed by you. 

---

RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Reports User Guide 

To store a report: 

1. 
In the Delivery options section of the Storage options page, select a storage location option: 

• 
Store Report 

• 
Store in Cloud 

Cloud storage must be set up and enabled with permissions to use the cloud storage 
feature. See the Cloud Storage section in the Company User Guide for more 
information. 

2. 
Enter the Report name. 

3. 
From the Report type drop-down list, select the format in which the report should be saved. 

Learn more about the choices for report format (on page 237). 

4. 
Click OK. 


> **Navigation Path:** `5. 
When you are ready to retrieve your report, go to the Reports > More > My Stored`


Reports.

Storing a Report in a Cloud-Storage Target 

You can deliver a report to a secure, cloud-based location such as Dropbox, Box, Google Drive, or

To do this, you need to set up cloud-storage targets in RealPage Accounting. The targets that you 

define will be available as storage options for reports.

Adding a Report to a Dashboard from a Report 

You can add reports only to dashboards that you created, so before you can add a report to a 

dashboard, you must create a custom dashboard. 

To add a report to a dashboard: 

1. 
Run the report that you want to add to your dashboard. 

2. 
From the report’s results page, click the Add to dashboard button. This adds the report as a 

component on your dashboard. 

3. 
In the Add to dashboard field, type the dashboard’s name. 

4. 
In the Description field, type a description of the report.  

5. 
Select the Public check box if you want other system users to be able to see the dashboard 

and this report. Clear the Public check box if you do not want others to be able to view this 

report on the dashboard.  

6. 
Click OK. The system stores the report in the Memorized reports list. 

Exporting Standard and Custom Reports 

After running a report, you can export the information for use in other applications. 

To export a standard report: 

1. 
From the Applications menu, select your application, and then select the All tab. 

2. 
In the Reports section, select the standard report that you want to export. 

3. 
Configure the report settings.  

4. 
Click the Export button and select the format in which you want to export the report. 

To export a custom report from the Reports application: 

1. 
Click the Applications menu, select Reports, and then select Reports center. 

2. 
Find the report that you want to export. 

3. 
Click the Export button, and then select the desired format in which you want the system to 

export the report: 

• 
Word creates a document in Microsoft Word format. Click the Download the file link 

to open the file in Word so that you can name and save the file. 

• 
Excel formatted reports are saved to your browser’s download location. 

• 
CSV (comma-separated values) files are saved to your browser’s default download 

location. 

• 
Text formatted reports open in a new tab. Select the desired text, copy it, and paste it 

into a text file.

### Custom Reports
*Source: `RP Accounting AP Reports User Guide.pdf`, Page 255*

Chapter 2: Working with Reports 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Reports User Guide 

Custom Reports 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Platform Services/Customization Services > All > Custom Reports`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Reports > All > Operational Reports > Custom Reports`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Reporting Portal > All > Reports > Custom Reports`


In addition to standard and financial reports, you can build custom reports. Create custom reports 

to get insight and answers from the unique information stored in your system. Financial reports 

are based on account groupings such as assets and liabilities, while custom reports and 

dimension structures are based on records and fields either grouped together or separately. 

For example, you can create a custom report that displays vendor contact information. You can 

control which vendors you want to display, such as active vendors in certain regions, and select 

the details to include about the vendors. You can then sort and display the results to highlight 

what is most important to you. 

With a custom report, you can: 

• 
Report on fields from almost any record or transaction in the system, and any related data. 

• 
Customize the report for your needs. 

• 
Run the reports, export them in another format, or add them to dashboards. 

Before you can export a report or add it to a group, you need to memorize the report.  

Creating Custom Reports 

Custom reports are created with the custom report wizard, which walks you through the steps to 

create a report. Only users who have permission to Customization Services can add and edit 

reports by going to the Custom Reports list on the Customization services menu. 

You can run the custom report from the Reports application. 

Adding a Custom Report to an Application’s Menu 

If you use a custom report on a regular basis, you can add the custom report to an application’s 

menu. For example, a report with payables-related data can be added to the Accounts Payable 

menu. After adding a custom report to the A/P menu, you can run the custom report by clicking 

the Custom Reports menu option, which displays a list of all of the custom reports that you have 

added to the Accounts Payable menu. 

The Custom Reports option displays on menus only after you (or someone else) has added at 

least one custom report to the application’s menu. The Custom Reports option does not appear 

on a menu if no one has added any custom reports to the application’s menu. 

---



#### Using the Custom Report Wizard to Create Positive Pay Reports
*Source: `RP Accounting AP Reports User Guide.pdf`, Page 256*

Working with Reports 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Reports User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Using the Custom Report Wizard to Create Positive Pay Reports 

Using the custom report wizard, you can create a report that you send to the bank for processing 

positive pay.  

Positive pay is a fraud prevention system in which you send the bank a list of checks processed by 

your company’s Accounts Payable department for a specific time frame. The bank then honors 

only the checks that appear on the list. Your report might differ slightly based on the bank’s 

requirements for the positive pay file. This example takes you step-by-step through a common 

method of creating this report. 

---



### Positive Pay Report
*Source: `RP Accounting AP Reports User Guide.pdf`, Page 257*



#### Before You Begin
*Source: `RP Accounting AP Reports User Guide.pdf`, Page 257*

Chapter 2: Working with Reports 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Reports User Guide 

Positive Pay Report 

Create positive pay reports when your company uses a positive pay system with the bank. This 

report is sent on a schedule based on when you process your checks in Accounts Payable. 

The report creates a flat list to send to the bank that includes all checks written for the time 

period, the amount, and the payee. It can contain more, but this is the minimum. The bank then 

compares the checks presented with the list and accepts only those that appear there. 

This report is created using the custom report wizard. You’ll notice that voided checks are 

included in the report. These can be removed, but are often left in the report so the bank knows 

that these check numbers aren’t valid. 

Before You Begin 

To build custom reports, you must be subscribed to Customization Services. If you do not yet 

subscribe to Customization Services, contact your RealPage representative for subscription 

information. 

Access can vary depending on your organization’s subscriptions and your permissions. If you do 

not see the option in the menu, then ask your System Administrator to check your permissions. 

The user must have Administrator privileges to create the Positive Pay report. 

Permissions 

These permissions are required to create the Positive Pay report. 

Application 
Reports 
Permissions 

Platform services or 

Customization services 

Custom reports 
List, View, Add, Edit, Delete 

If your user account doesn’t have the permissions shown above, then ask your System 

Administrator for assistance. If you have administrator privileges, you can assign permissions for a 

new feature to a user or to a role. See Roles and Permissions for a description of how to review a 

user’s permissions.

### Viewing a Monthly Chart
*Source: `RP Accounting AP Reports User Guide.pdf`, Page 271*

Chapter 3: Accounts Payable Charts 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Viewing a Monthly Chart 

When the chart’s customization page loads, click the View button. The chart displays, showing all 

results for the month to date. 

To refine the report, click the Customize button to return the customization page and follow the 

steps for customizing the chart. 

Reports have two kinds of settings, persisting and non-persisting. 

Persisting settings retain any changes you make from session to session. When you return to this 

page to run this report again, each setting displays exactly as you set it before. For example, if you 

type “My Latest Report” into the Report title 1 field, the next time you run this report, the Report 

title 1 box displays My latest report. 

Persisting settings include: 

• 
Settings in the Format section 

• 
Settings in the Titles section 

• 
Check boxes in the Filters section 

Non-persisting settings do not retain your changes. Instead, every time you return to this page to 

run this report or chart, the settings are set to the system defaults. If you changed these settings 

the last time you ran this report, you will have to change them again. 

Non-persisting settings include: 

• 
Settings in the Time Period section 

• 
Drop-down lists in the Filters section 

Not all reports include all of the above sections.

Before You Begin

user’s permissions. 

Customizing and Running the A/P Invoice Analysis Chart 

To customize and create the A/P Invoice analysis chart: 

1. 
Open the Accounts payable menu. 

2. 
In the A/P Invoices & Registers section, select A/P invoice analysis, and then select 

Graph. The Invoices analysis chart parameters page opens. 

If you want to see every result for a particular category, do not make selections from any 
of the data entry boxes. You can run this report or chart without entering any search 
information. If you do that, however, it may take a long time to run and may return too 
many results to be useful. One exception is that multi-entity, multi-currency companies 
must select a location before running a report or chart. 

Filling In the Time Period Section 

You can specify either the reporting period or the start and end dates, but not both.  

To select a reporting period for the chart: 

1. 
In the Reporting period drop-down list, select a reporting period for the chart. 

If you do not specify a reporting period, the system generates a chart for the current month 

to date. 

2. 
Select or enter the As of date of the reporting period. 

Type “p” in a date field to automatically insert the last day of the prior month. See 
Specifying Dates in Getting Started for a full list of shortcut keys related to entering 
dates.  

---


<!-- Page 274 -->
Accounts Payable Charts 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Reports User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

3. 
Select the Prompt on run check box if you want the system to prompt you for this choice 

when you run the chart. 

To select a start and end date: 

1. 
In the Start date field, select the start date of the time period for the chart. 

2. 
In the End date field, select or enter the end date of the time period for the chart. 

3. 
Select the Prompt on run check box if you want the system to prompt you for this choice 

when you run the chart. 

If you complete all of the time period fields (that is, if you fill in the Reporting period and As 

of date fields in addition to the Start date and End date fields), the system bases your 
chart only on the specified start and end dates. It ignores the As of date specified. 

Filling In the Filters Section 

Set up filters to narrow your results. Using filters is optional. 

1. 
To show results for a specific vendor or range of vendors, select one or more vendors in the 

From vendor and To vendor fields. 

• 
To run the graph for a single vendor, select the vendor in the From vendor drop-down 

list. The system completes the To vendor field with the same vendor.  

• 
To run the graph for all vendors, leave the fields blank. 

• 
To run the graph for a range of vendors, select the first vendor in the list. In To vendor, 

select the ending vendor in the range. 

How to use the From/To fields: 

All From/To field pairs work the same way. Use them to get search results in as broad or as 

fine a range as you need—from everything in the system down to a single specific object. 

To run this report for a single object: 

• 
Click the down arrow next to the From box, and from the menu that appears, click the 

object you want. 

• 
Click the down arrow next to the To box, and from the menu that appears, click the 

same object. 

To run this report for a specific range of objects: 

• 
Click the down arrow next to the From box, and from the menu that appears, click the 

object you want at the beginning of the range. 

• 
Click the down arrow next to the To box, and from the menu that appears, click the 

object you want at the end of the range. 

---


<!-- Page 275 -->
Chapter 3: Accounts Payable Charts 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Reports User Guide 

To run this report for all objects: 

Leave both boxes blank. 

If you have a large number of objects, or if this report takes too long to process, use the 

From and To boxes to run a series of smaller reports. For example, you can run five reports, 

one each for objects whose names begin with A–E, then F-J, K-O, P-T, and U–Z. 

An object is a catch -all term that refers to any specific data item in the system. 
Customers, vendors, items, and accounts are all examples of objects. 

2. 
To show results for one type of vendor, in Vendor type, select the vendor type you want the 

chart to cover. 

3. 
To show results for a specific account or range of accounts, use the From account and To 

account drop-down lists. 

4. 
To filter by location, in the Location drop-down list, select the location that you want to 

include in the chart.

## Vendor Aging Chart
*Source: `RP Accounting AP Reports User Guide.pdf`, Page 278*

Accounts Payable Charts 

RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Reports User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Vendor Aging Chart 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > All > Reports > Vendors Reports > Vendor Aging >`


 Graph 

The Vendor Aging chart illustrates how many days vendor invoices have aged before they were 

paid. Use any of several types of charts (for example bar, line, pie, and so on) to visually track how 

often vendors were paid by time period, account, vendor, and more. Use this chart when you want 

to see a visual representation of the Vendor Aging report. 

The Vendor Aging chart is a standard chart. If you are looking for information on financial graphs, 
see Creating a Financial Graph. 

You can display the chart as of the default of today, or another date you enter, and can base the 

chart on the invoice date, due date, or G/L posting date. You can filter the list by a single vendor 

or all vendors. You can chart aging period totals or vendor totals, or you can chart vendor totals 

by your top vendors.

Storing Standard Reports and Charts 

You can process any report or chart on demand and have the system store it. The Process & store 

option is particularly useful when running large reports. It is also useful to maintain reporting 

history for a specific point in time. 

After setting up a report or chart, you have these options: 

• 
To run the report or chart and view it, click the View button. 

• 
To run the report or chart and store it, click the Process & store button. 

You can process and store the report or chart either before or after viewing it. 

Emailing Standard Reports and Charts 

The Email option is available after running the report. 

To email a report or a chart: 

1. 
Click the Email button. The Email report box opens. 

2. 
In the To field, type the email address of the person to whom you want to send the report. 

To enter multiple addresses, separate each address with a comma (,) or semi-colon (;). 

3. 
Click the CC me check box if you want the system to send an email to your Inbox. 

4. 
In the Subject field, type the text that you want to appear in the subject line of the email 

message. 

5. 
In the Message field, type a message to the recipient. The system completes the signature 

line and fills the From field with your email address. 

6. 
Click OK. 

Adding a Memorized Standard Chart to a Dashboard 

Before You Begin 

Before you can add a chart to the dashboard, create a custom dashboard. For more information, 

see Adding a dashboard. 

To add a chart to a dashboard: 

1. 
Create the chart that you want to add. 

2. 
From the created chart’s page, click the Add to dashboard button.  

3. 
In the Add to dashboard parameters box, select the dashboard to which you want to add 

the chart. 

4. 
In the Description field, type a description of the chart.  

---

Scheduling a Memorized Report or Chart 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Reports > All > Reports Center > Memorized > More Actions > Edit 
Schedule`


See the How to Get Here topic for a list of ways to access memorized reports. 

Use the Schedule memorized report page to schedule a memorized report or chart to run 

automatically and routinely. 

Accessing the Schedule Memorized Report Page  

You can schedule a report or chart from either the Reports application or the application where it 

was originally memorized. 

To schedule a report from the Reports application: 

1. 
Open the Reports menu, and then click the Reports center option. The Reports center page 

opens.  

2. 
Select the Memorized tab. 

3. 
In the (View) drop-down list, select the application associated with the report, or select All 

applications. 

4. 
Find the report or chart you want to schedule, and then click More actions. 

5. 
Select the Edit schedule option. The Schedule memorized report page opens. 

To schedule a report from another application: 

1. 
In the Applications menu, select the application where the memorized report is located, and 

then select the All tab. 

2. 
In the Reports section, click the Memorized reports option. 

---


<!-- Page 288 -->

RealPage Accounting Accounts Payable Reports User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

3. 
Find the report or chart you want to schedule, and then click the Schedule link. The 

Schedule memorized report page opens. 

Filtering the Report 

1. 
In the Department/group and Location/group drop-down lists, select a specific department 

or location (or group of departments or locations) by which to filter the report. If you leave 

the filters blank, then the report will run for all departments and locations. 

2. 
If you are scheduling a financial report and the report is set to prompt for G/L account 

groups, then the G/L account group selection box appears. Select one or more G/L account 

groups to filter the report by. 

3. 
In the As of date field, type or select the date from which the scheduled report should 

display data. Leave this field blank to use the current date. If you enter an As of date, that 

date will always be used regardless of when the schedule is run. 

Type “p” in a date field to automatically insert the last day of the prior month. See 

Specifying Dates in Getting Started for a full list of shortcut keys related to entering dates. If 

you enabled reporting account labels in the General Ledger, then you have the option to 

substitute the account labels in the report with the reporting account set’s labels: 

• 
To enable reporting account labels, select the Substitute with reporting accounts 

labels check box. The Reporting account set drop-down list appears. 

• 
In the Reporting account set drop-down list, select the reporting account set whose 

labels you want to use. 

Scheduling the Report 

1. 
In the Start date field, type or select the date on which to start running the report.  

Typically, the Start date is a date in the future. If you select a date in the past, then the 
report executes immediately after you save it. The Start date also determines the date 
that the system schedules the report to run in future occurrences; for example, if you are 
scheduling the report to run weekly and the Start date is on a Monday, then the system will 
run the report every Monday. 

Type “p” in a date field to automatically insert the last day of the prior month. See 

Specifying Dates in Getting Started for a full list of shortcut keys related to entering dates.  

2. 
In the Ending on field, select when to stop running the report:  

• 
Never: Run the report indefinitely. 

• 
Number of occurrences: Stop running the report after a specific number of 

occurrences.  

• 
In the End after field, type the number of occurrences after which to stop running 

the report; for example, type “5” to stop after five occurrences. 

• 
End date: Stop running the report on a specific date.  

---

In the End on field, type or select the date on which to stop running the report.

Days: Run the report once every X days.

About the Accounts Payable Application

Use Accounts Payable to create, manage, and merge vendor
records; create, post, and pay A/P invoices, advances, and
adjustments; approve payments, and reconcile checking
accounts.
Use the Company application to subscribe to the Accounts
Payable application.
Configure Accounts Payable and its features with the Setup
tab's Configuration command.

Add a Vendor

1. In Accounts Payable, select 
 next to Vendors.
2. Type the vendor information in each tab below:

▪
Vendor
▪
Additional Information
▪
Contact List
▪
Payment Information
▪
Restrictions
▪
Insurance/License

3. Select 1099 eligible on the Additional information tab as
needed.
4. Click Save.

Edit a Vendor

1. In Accounts Payable, select Vendors.
2. Find the vendor to change and click Edit.
3. Edit the vendor information.
4. Click Save.

Add an A/P Invoice

Add an A/P invoice to the system for payment to a vendor.

1. In Accounts Payable, select Create an A/P invoice.
2. Fill in the top section.
3. Fill in the details in the Invoice Entries section.
4. Click Post or Submit.

Edit an A/P Invoice

Make a correction to an A/P Invoice.

1. In Accounts Payable, select A/P invoices.
2. Find the A/P Invoice to change.
3. Click Edit.
4. Make the necessary changes to the A/P Invoice.
5. Click Save.

A/P invoices transferred from OneSite Leasing & Rents can only be
edited at the Top level.

Delete an A/P Invoice

Delete an A/P invoice from the system.

1. In Accounts Payable, select A/P invoices.
2. Locate the A/P Invoice that you want to delete.
3. Click the Delete link. If you only see Reverse it means that the
Enable reversal of unpaid A/P Invoices check box is selected.
The A/P Invoice must be reversed instead. To disable this
option, go to Accounts Payable's Setup tab and select
Configure. Find the Enable reversal of unpaid A/P Invoices
check box and clear it.

A/P Invoices transferred from OneSite Leasing & Rents can only be
deleted at the Top Level.

Reclassify an A/P Invoice

Change the G/L code of an A/P invoice that is not in a closed
period. Reclassify it instead of deleting and re-entering an A/P
invoice.

1. In Accounts Payable, select A/P invoices.
2. Find the A/P invoice to reclassify.
3. Click Edit.
4. Click the Reclassify button.
5. Make the necessary changes to the G/L coding.
6. Click Save.

Add an Adjustment Credit/Debit Memo

Account adjustment debit memo decreases the balance due. A
credit memo increases the A/P Invoice amount.

1. Open the Accounts Payable menu, and then select
Adjustments.
2. Fill in the credit/debit memo information.
3. Click Save.

Pay A/P Invoices

Select posted A/P Invoices for payment.

1. In Accounts Payable, select Pay A/P Invoices.
2. Create or choose a saved filter.
3. Click Apply Filter.
4. Select Payment method.
5. Select Invoice currency.
6. Select Payment request method.
7. Select Bank.
8. Select the invoices to pay.
9. Click Apply credits if there are open credits for any vendor to
be paid.
10. Click Add to Outbox to put the invoices in payment draft mode,
or click Pay Now to pay vendors.

Click Pay by Entity to use the Entity payment view.

Select A/P Invoices to Pay

Select posted A/P Invoices for payment.

1. In Accounts Payable, select Pay A/P invoices.
2. Set up filters that will retrieve the A/P invoices that you want to
pay.
3. Click Apply filter.
4. Select the Payment method, Invoice currency, and the Bank
where your payment account resides.
5. Select an A/P Invoice to pay.
6. In the Amount to pay column, type the amount that you want to
pay.
7. Click Apply credits if there are open credits for any vendor to
be paid.
8. Click Pay now to pay the selected A/P Invoices.
9. Repeat steps 2 through 8 as needed.

To leave the page, select another option from the menu.

Adding a Manual Payment

Use the manual payment option to quickly add a bill and record
the payment at the same time.

1. In Accounts payable, select Manual payment.
2. Select the Payment method.
3. Fill in the Date section.
4. Fill in the Pay to section.
5. Enter the line items.
6. Post the payment.

Remove an A/P Invoice from the Payment Request

To remove full payment request:

1. In Accounts Payable, select View payment request.
2. Find the A/P Invoice that needs to be removed.
3. Click the Cancel Request link

To remove one line item from payment request:

1. In Accounts Payable, select View payment request.
2. Select Edit next to the payment request to edit.
3. Clear the check box of the line item to remove.
4. Click Save.

Quick Check Entry

Add a recording of a check written outside of the system.

1. In Accounts Payable, on the All tab, roll over Checks and then
select Quick check entry.
2. Select the Bank account that the check was written from.
3. Click Continue.
4. Enter the A/P Invoice information.
5. Click Enter.
6. Click Post.

Download a CSV Check File

Download a CSV file of selected checks. The most common
use of CSV check files is when check printing is performed
offsite.

1. In Accounts Payable, on the All tab, roll over Checks and then
select Print Checks.
2. Select Confirm/Void check boxes for checks that need to be
voided, if any.
3. Click the Void button as needed.
4. Select the Print column check boxes of the checks to cut.
5. Select the type of detail desired on the check stubs.
6. Click CSV – Check Level and select the layout.
7. Download the CSV file.
8. Select the Confirm check box for checks that need to be
confirmed.
9. Click Confirm to remove downloaded checks from the list.

Print Checks

Print selected invoices for check printing.

1. In Accounts Payable,pause on Checks, and then select Print
Checks.
2. To void checks, select the Confirm/Void check box, and then
click the Void button.
3. To select the checks to cut, select the check boxes in the Print
column.
4. Select the Check stub details check boxes as needed.
5. Select the Vendor stub details check box as needed.
6. Click Print.
7. Print the PDF file to a printer with MICR toner.
8. Select the Confirm check box for checks that need to be
confirmed.
9. Click Confirm to remove printed checks from the list.

Void a Check

Void a check that was paid in error or when the vendor never
received payment and needs to be reissued a new check.

1. In Accounts Payable, select Check register in the Reports
column of the menu.
2. Select a location, bank, .
3. Click View.
4. Find the check to be voided on the check register.
5. Click Void.
6. Type a void date.
7. Type a note in the Memo field.
8. Click Submit.

To reverse an A/P Invoice, go to Accounts Payable and select A/P
Invoices. Find the A/P invoice and then click Reverse.

Generating a Payment File

Generate the ACH or electronic payment file that contains the
payments you want to make.

1. In Accounts Payable or Cash Management, click the All tab.
2. In the ACH or Electronic payments section, select ACH file
generation or File generation.
3. Select the payment requests you want to send to the bank for
processing.
4. Click Generate file to generate a payment file for the selected
payments (one file per bank).
5. Send each payment file to its corresponding bank in their
preferred format.
6. After the bank receives the file and sends it to the vendor, click
Confirm.

Open/Close the A/P Period

Open the subledger to allow users to book additional
transactions in the reporting period. Close the subledger so that
no one can book additional Accounts Payable transactions.

1. In Accounts Payable, on the All tab, roll over Subledger and
then select Open subledger/Close subledger.
2. Select Entity/Entity group.
3. Select the period to open/close.
4. Click Open/Close.

A/P Single Scan

Scan attachments into A/P Invoices.


> **Navigation Path:** `1. Connect a scanner to your computer.
2. Navigate to Your Name > My preferences.
3. In the Personalize interactive behavior section, select the
Enable single scan upload check box.
4. Click Save.
5. In Accounts Payable, on the All tab, select Create an A/P
invoice.
6. Install the software to connect the scanner to our application.
The Scan button is now available.`


Approve A/P Invoices

1. Open the Accounts Payable menu.
2. Click Approval Workbench.
3. Select A/P Invoice.
4. Find the invoice that you want to review.
5. Click View and review the invoice.
6. Click Approve.

## Introduction to RealPage Spend Management
*Source: `RP Financial Suite Spend Management User Guide.pdf`, Page 13*

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage® Financial Suite Spend Management User Guide 

Introduction to RealPage Spend Management 

RealPage Spend Management is a web-based purchasing system that enables the delivery of enterprise spending 

visibility to ensure compliance and control. Spend Management provides a way for companies to set a budget and 

control spending automatically. Use Spend Management to analyze the impact of sourcing strategies on key 

categories, assess business savings, and review compliance with preferred suppliers and contracts. These activities 

can provide ongoing control of spending for improved profitability. 

Spend Management lets you manage purchase orders, service orders, accounts payable (A/P) invoices, approvals, 

vendors, and contracts. You can complete such tasks as: 

• 
Establishing policies for spending 

• 
Setting up service contracts and subcontracts 

• 
Entering purchase orders 

• 
Creating change orders 

• 
Managing purchase orders against budgets or spending limits 

• 
Creating A/P invoices that match with purchase orders 

The Spend Management Workbench (on page 166) provides a central location for you to complete these regular 

tasks. 

Spend Management is the purchasing and budget control component of the RealPage Accounting System for the 
property. Spend Management is fully integrated with RealPage Accounting.

### Spend Management Workflow
*Source: `RP Financial Suite Spend Management User Guide.pdf`, Page 18*

Spend Management Configuration 

RealPage® Financial Suite Spend Management User Guide

Spend Management Workflow 

Use Spend Management to organize all procured goods, services, and large contracted jobs – and 

their associated invoices – in one space. 

The following image depicts the flow for each type of order into A/P invoices. 

• 
Purchased goods: Add a purchase order for purchased goods. Optionally, log goods 

received. Create an A/P invoice that matches the purchase order. 

• 
Service contract: Add a service contract for procured services, and then generate a service 

order for each date of service. Create an A/P invoice for each service order. 

• 
Contracted job: If you use the Job Cost application, add a subcontract for each contracted 

job. Create an A/P invoice that matches the subcontract. 

Use the Spend Management Workbench (on page 166) to manage the flow of transactions.

### Preparing for Spend Management Configuration
*Source: `RP Financial Suite Spend Management User Guide.pdf`, Page 23*

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage® Financial Suite Spend Management User Guide 

Preparing for Spend Management Configuration 

Before you configure Spend Management, you must set up budgets and spend policies for use with the 

application. If you plan to implement Full Service Spend Management, see Full Service Spend Management (on 

page 150) for more information. 

1. 
Create a budget that includes the dimensions you want to validate: 

• 
Ensure that you use Accrual or Accrual and Cash books. 

• 
Configure and enable the dimensions you want to validate for purchasing, accounts payable, and the 

general ledger (G/L). 

• 
Optionally, create a threshold budget for use with Spend Management only. This sort of budget might 

represent 90% (or some other percentage) of your total, actual budget, and Spend Management sends 

warnings when you reach this threshold. Creating a threshold budget prepares you for any 

adjustments you may have to make to your actual budget. 

2. 
For multi-entity companies, consider which entities you want to include in Spend Management validation 

and which entities you want to exclude. 

3. 
Choose the reporting periods to use for the budget duration on the Approval Configuration (on page 44) 

page. See Configuring Transaction Approvals (on page 45) for more information. 

4. 
If applicable, set up your committed expenses for use with Spend Management. 

5. 
If you want to validate purchasing transactions with Spend Management: 

• 
Create and verify the purchase documents and accounts that Spend Management uses. 

• 
If applicable, consider how your item G/L groups map to your G/L accounts for items that use 

non-posting transaction definitions. 

6. 
Set up the Spend Policy Manager (on page 81). 

When you finish setting up the budget and spend policies to use with the application, you will next adjust your 

individual user preferences for a better work environment. Go to the My Preferences page for more information. 

After you finish preparing for Spend Management configuration, go to the Configure Spend Management (on 

page 12) page. 

C H A P T E R 2

#### Configure Spend Management Page
*Source: `RP Financial Suite Spend Management User Guide.pdf`, Page 24*



##### Before You Begin
*Source: `RP Financial Suite Spend Management User Guide.pdf`, Page 24*

Preparing for Spend Management Configuration 

RealPage® Financial Suite Spend Management User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Configure Spend Management Page 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Spend Management > Setup > Configuration`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > Setup > Subscriptions > Applications > Configure (Spend 
Management)`


Use the Configure Spend Management page to configure and define the settings for the Spend 

Management application. This page contains the following sections: 

• 
Thresholds: Use this section to enable tolerance rules for A/P invoices. Tolerance rules allow 

for A/P invoices that do not match the budgeted amount to be approved if they do not 

exceed a certain amount. 

• 
Enable functionality: Use this section to enable the logging of the receipt of goods to a 

journal, allow change orders to be performed, require attachments from site users, or enable 

the Storefront feature. 

• 
Journals: If you enable the receipt of goods functionality, use this section to set up journals 

for logging the receipt of goods. This section only appears if the Enable receipt of goods 

check box is selected. 

• 
G/L accounts: If you implement Job Cost, use this section to choose the account for 

retainage on contracts. 

• 
Document sequencing: Use this section to set up prefixes for document numbers for 

orders, service contracts, and subcontracts. Using prefixes for different documents allows for 

easier identification of the document type. For example, you can set up service contracts 

with a prefix of “SC-” so that you can easily identify a document numbered “SC-3001” as a 

service contract. 

Before You Begin 

The RealPage Accounting Spend Management subscription must be enabled for you to access 

Spend Management. 

Access can vary depending on your organization’s subscriptions and your permissions. If you do 

not see the option in the menu, then ask your System Administrator to check your permissions. 

Permissions 

The user must have full or limited Administrator privileges to configure Spend Management. 

If your user account doesn’t have the permissions shown above, then ask your System 

Administrator for assistance. If you have administrator privileges, you can assign permissions for a 

new feature to a user or to a role. See Roles and Permissions (on page 604) for a description of 

how to review a user’s permissions.

##### Configuring Spend Management
*Source: `RP Financial Suite Spend Management User Guide.pdf`, Page 25*

Chapter 2: Preparing for Spend Management Configuration 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage® Financial Suite Spend Management User Guide 

Configuring Spend Management 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Spend Management > Setup > Configuration`


To configure the Spend Management application, complete the following sections on the 

Configure Spend Management page. 

Thresholds 

To allow a variance between the amount of an invoice and a purchase order: 

1. 
Select the Enable tolerance rules check box. Additional options for setting a range for the 

variance appear. 

• 
Select the Allow a range for order to Accounts Payable invoice variance check box. 

This lets you set a variance range above or below the budgeted purchase order (PO) 

amount for the accounts payable (A/P) invoice to pass through the system without 

being flagged for approval. 

2. 
Choose whether to set the threshold at a certain Percentage or a fixed dollar Amount, and 

then type the data in the numeric field. 

3. 
To skip any invoice approval requirements if the purchase order amount is within tolerance, 

select the Bypass invoice approval if within PO/SO tolerance check box. Additional 

approval requirement settings appear: 

• 
Select the If outside of PO/SO tolerance do not allow match option to restrict a 

purchase order or service contract outside of tolerance from matching to the order. 

• 
Select the If outside of PO/SO tolerance allow match and send for approvals option 

to allow a purchase order or service contract outside of tolerance to be submitted and 

processed via the approval workflow. 

---


<!-- Page 26 -->
Preparing for Spend Management Configuration 

RealPage® Financial Suite Spend Management User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

The following example shows a Thresholds section with options enabled. 

In this example, if the budgeted purchase order amount is for $300.00 and the A/P invoice is for 

$325.00, the system flags the invoice for approval since it is over budget by more than 1.25%. 

However, if the purchase order from which the invoice was generated is within tolerance, the 

invoice will not require approval since the option to bypass approval is selected. 

Enable Functionality 

Select any (or none) of the following options: 

• 
Enable receipt of goods: This option opens the Journals section for logging the receipt of 

goods. 

• 
Do not create receipt of goods journal entries: This option allows you to not create 

journal entries when goods are received if the amount recorded is not needed. 

• 
Allow change orders: This option allows for POs to be updated using change orders. 

• 
Attachment required to submit from site user: This option enables the system to require 

attachments from Spend Management Site Experience users. 

• 
Enable editing an invoice to a matched order: This option enables the system to edit an 

invoice to a matched order. 

• 
Disable auto close for subcontracts: This option allows you to close subcontracts in Site 

Experience manually, thereby bypassing the automatic close function. 

• 
After enabling and matching all invoices to the subcontract, the status of the 

subcontract shows as Full Invoice Match. 

• 
The option to manually close the subcontract when needed appears on the 

Subcontract list page and the Spend Management Workbench page. 

---


<!-- Page 27 -->

RealPage® Financial Suite Spend Management User Guide 

• 
Enable subledger A/P close for Site Experience: This option allows you to define specific 

dates for the Site View subledger to close each month of the year. 

You can set up close calendars for each year (on page 22) to apply at the top-entity level. If 
you have entities with different close dates, then you can override the subledger close 
dates at the entity level (on page 23) from the Entity information page. 

• 
After enabling the subledger, the Define subledger site close here option appears. 

Click Here to open the Subledger AP close for Site View box. See Subledger A/P 

Close for Site View List (on page 22) for more information. 

• 
Click the Apply Subledger Close to core Accounting check box if you want the close 

date to be applied to the RealPage Accounting subledger account. 

• 
Enable consolidated service contracts: This option enables the consolidation of service 

contracts. 

After this feature is enabled in Spend Management > Configuration, it cannot be disabled. 

• 
Enable online shopping: This option enables the Storefront feature. If you enable this 

feature, you must also complete the following configuration settings: 

• 
For each property that will shop online, generate an account number with the vendor. 

See Requesting a Vendor Account for a Property for Online Shopping for more 

information. 

• 
Set up catalog mapping. See Catalog Mapping (on page 27) for more information. 

• 
Select the General Ledger (G/L) account to associate with online orders from the 

Default G/L account drop-down list. This account acts as the default account for 

product categories that are not mapped. 

• 
Select the Do not allow to post to Default GL check box to prevent eInvoice 

transactions posting to the default general ledger account. The system displays an 

error message upon saving, submitting, approving, or posting a previously booked 

eInvoice to the default G/L. If this happens, a different expense account must be 

entered. 

• 
Select the Disable Auto Matching check box to enhance control over invoice 

processing by disabling automatic matching of purchase orders to eInvoices. With this 

feature turned off, users manually match purchase order to invoices after the item has 

been received to ensure greater accuracy and accountability by aligning invoice 

approval with confirmed receipt of goods. 

• 
Select a default approver to assign to online orders from the Default approver if no 

workflow is assigned for eInvoice drop-down list. 

• 
G/L accounts for Site Experience: This option determines which General Ledger accounts 

are seen and reported on with the Site Experience.

• 
Automatically set Require PO on new vendors: Select this check box to enable the Require 

PO - Spend functionality to automatically check for new vendors added in RealPage 

Accounting and Vendor Credentialing to ensure that all vendor invoices adhere to standard 

business processes. 

You can make changes to the General Ledger account group that determines which 
accounts are seen and reported on by clicking the Click here link. 

• 
Set no tax on PO line items: Select this check box to enable the No Tax field automatically

Journals

G/L Accounts

Document Sequencing 

To set up special numbering or prefixes for orders, service contracts, or subcontracts: 

• 
To select a prefix for order numbers, select a sequencing type from the Prefix to be used for

• 
To select a prefix for service contract numbers, select a sequencing type from the Prefix to

• 
To select a prefix for subcontract numbers, select a sequencing type from the Prefix to be

Document sequencing is fully customizable. You can add and modify document sequence 

options. See Document Sequence Information (on page 33) for more information about adding 

and modifying document sequence options. 

Enable Functionality for Custom PO 

To set up functionality for custom purchase orders: 

1. 
Select the Enable Custom PO check box to add custom text and workflow history to a 

printed or emailed purchase order. 

2. 
In the Additional verbiage field, enter text specifying any terms you want to include, 

policies on how to pay your vendors, or requirements for insurance. 

3. 
Select the Include Workflow History check box to include the approval workflow history to 

show who approved it, at what time, and for which workflow it applies. 

Saving the Spend Management Configuration 

After you finish choosing your configuration options for Spend Management, click the Save 

button. The system saves your configurations and opens the Spend management home page.

first—day of the month or days before the end of the month—is 

when Site View closes. 

• 
During this closed period, if a Site View user enters an invoice, a 

warning message appears reminding the user that Site View is 

closed for said time and the transaction will post in the next 

period.
