Catalog Mapping 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Spend Management > Setup > Configuration > Enable Functionality > 
Catalog Mapping`


Use the Catalog Mapping feature to map categories of goods to specific general ledger (G/L) 

accounts. 

Although you must designate a default G/L account in the Default G/L account field as part of the 

configuration for online shopping, you can map different types of purchases for tracking in 

specific accounts. For example, you can map appliance purchases to a G/L account for appliance 

purchases and map office supplies to a G/L account for office supplies purchases. 

SKUs (stock keeping units) for RealPage invoices are now listed in the Catalog Mapping feature 
below RealPage One. If you receive RealPage invoices electronically as eInvoices, you can now 
assign the G/L accounts to the category. Those G/L accounts then appear on invoices for that 
category automatically. 

Additionally, you can map subcategories to different G/L accounts from those of the parent 

categories, as shown in the example below. 

---



##### Mapping G/L Accounts to Categories
*Source: `RP Financial Suite Spend Management User Guide.pdf`, Page 40*



##### Mapping a G/L Account to a Category
*Source: `RP Financial Suite Spend Management User Guide.pdf`, Page 40*

Preparing for Spend Management Configuration 

RealPage® Financial Suite Spend Management User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

In this example, the Appliances parent category is mapped to the 6516.01--Appliances G/L 

account for appliances, and the Electrical parent category is mapped to the 6515.04--Electrical & 

Lighting G/L account for electrical and lighting. However, some subcategories to each of these 

parent categories are mapped to other accounts. For instance, since the Door Bells category is 

mapped to the 6516.07--Doors & Windows G/L account, purchases in the Door Bells category will 

be logged to the 6516.07--Doors & Windows account instead of the 6515.04--Electrical & Lighting 

account. 

Mapping G/L Accounts to Categories 

There are two methods for mapping G/L accounts to categories: 

• 
Map the accounts and categories manually. See Mapping a G/L account to a category (on 

page 28) for more information. 

• 
Import a mapping file. See Importing a catalog mapping file (on page 30) for more 

information.  

Mapping and Chart Types 

You can assign multiple G/L accounts to one category or the same G/L account to multiple 

categories. The extent to which you can assign multiple G/L accounts to a category depends on 

whether you have chart types enabled. 

When the chart types feature is not enabled, you can: 

• 
Map one G/L account to multiple parent categories. For example, account 

5600--Maintenance Supplies can be mapped to Appliances, Electrical, and HVAC. However, 

the account cannot be mapped to a parent category, such as HVAC, and a subcategory, 

such as Heaters. 

When the chart types feature is enabled, you can: 

• 
Map multiple G/L accounts to one category if the G/L accounts are in different charts of 

accounts or chart types. 

• 
Filter the list of accounts by choosing a chart type at the top of the list. 

• 
Map one G/L account to multiple parent categories. For example, you can map account 

5600--Maintenance Supplies to Appliances, Electrical, and HVAC. However, you cannot map 

the account to a parent category, such as HVAC, and a subcategory, such as Heaters. 

Mapping a G/L Account to a Category 

To map a General Ledger (G/L) account to a category: 

1. 
Open the Spend Management menu. 

2. 
Click the Setup tab, and then click Configuration. 

---

3. 
From the Configure spend management page, click the Catalog mapping link in the Enable 

functionality section. The Catalog Mapping box opens. 

4. 
Find the G/L account and category you want to map. 

Use the Chart of accounts and Category mapping fields to search for the G/L account and 

category: 

• 
To find a G/L account, type part of the account name in the Chart of accounts field, 

and then select the account from the list. 

• 
To find a category, type part of the category name in the Category mapping field, and 

then select the category from the list. 

5. 
Drag the G/L account to the category. The G/L account appears at the bottom of the 

category. 

In the following example, a G/L account for appliances covers the overall Appliances 

category and a different G/L account for appliance parts covers the Replacement Parts 

subcategory.

Document Sequence Information 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Spend Management > Setup > Configuration > Document Sequencing`


Use the Document Sequence Information box to set up prefixes for document numbers for 

orders, service contracts, and subcontracts. Using prefixes for different documents allows for 

easier identification of the document type. For example, you can set up service contracts with a 

prefix of “SC-” so that you can easily identify a document numbered “SC-3001” as a service 

contract. 

Viewing Document Sequence Information 

You can view the document sequence information for any of the document sequences in the 

Document sequencing section on the Configure Spend Management (on page 12) page. 

To view the document sequence information for a particular document sequence: 

1. 
Select the document sequence from the drop-down list. This puts the document sequence 

in focus. 

2. 
Click the drop-down list again, and then click the View link. The Document Sequence 

Information box for that document sequence opens. 

Adding a New Document Sequence 

You can add a new document sequence to use for identifying purchase orders, service contracts, 

and subcontracts in the Document sequencing section of the Configure Spend Management 

page. 

To add a new document sequence for a particular document sequence, click the drop-down list, 

and then click the Add link. The Document Sequence Information box opens, and this box 

features two tabs: Basic settings and Advanced settings. 

Basic Settings 

The fields under this tab are required. 

1. 
Type a unique identifier for the document sequence in the Sequence ID field. This name 

appears in the drop-down lists in the Document sequencing section of the Configure Spend 

Management (on page 12) page. 

2. 
Type the name of the document sequence in the Print title field. This is the title that prints 

on the document. 

3. 
Type the first number of this document sequence in the Starting number field. 

4. 
Type the next number in the document sequence in the Next number field. 

5. 
Select Active from the Status drop-down list. 

---



##### Editing a Document Sequence
*Source: `RP Financial Suite Spend Management User Guide.pdf`, Page 46*

Preparing for Spend Management Configuration 

RealPage® Financial Suite Spend Management User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Advanced Settings 

The fields under this tab are not required, but the options here let you differentiate your 

document sequences with prefixes and suffixes. 

1. 
Type a number (1-16) in the Fixed number length field to limit the number of characters in 

the document sequence number. The formatted number appears with left-padded zeros. 

For example, if you type a 4 in this field and the document is number 111, the system 

displays the number as 0111. 

2. 
Type a prefix in the Fixed prefix field if you want to add a fixed prefix to identify the 

document type. 

For example, if you want all of your purchase orders to begin with PO, type PO in this field. 

3. 
Type a character or space in the Prefix separator field if you want to separate the prefix 

from the rest of the number. 

For example, if you want your documents to begin with PO-, type the hyphen (-) in this field 

and PO in the Fixed prefix field. 

4. 
Type a character or space in the Suffix separator field if you want to separate the suffix from 

the rest of the number. 

For example, if you want your documents to end with -S, type the hyphen (-) in this field and 

S in the Fixed suffix field. 

5. 
Type a suffix in Fixed suffix field if you want to add a fixed suffix to identify the document 

type. 

For example, if you want all of your subcontracts to end with S, type S in this field. 

6. 
Type the last number of the document sequence in the Ending number field if you want the 

document sequence to end with a particular number. 

Reviewing the Document Sequence 

As you complete each field, the Sample number field updates with an example of the formatted 

document sequence number. 

Saving the Document Sequence 

When you are satisfied with the format of the new document sequence information, click the Save 

button. The box closes and the new document sequence appears in the drop-down lists in the 

Document sequencing section of the Configure spend management page. 

Editing a Document Sequence 

To edit a document sequence: 

1. 
Select the document sequence from the drop-down list. This puts the document sequence 

in focus.

sequences unless you delete it from the Document numbering page in the Company 
application.

type a 4 in this field and the document is number 111, the system displays 
the number as 0111. 

Fixed prefix 
Type a prefix in this field if you want to add a fixed prefix to identify the 
document type. For example, if you want all of your purchase orders to 
begin with PO, type PO in this field. 

Prefix separator 
Type a character or space in this field if you want to separate the prefix from 
the rest of the number. For example, if you want your documents to begin 
with PO-, type the hyphen (-) in this field and PO in the Fixed prefix field. 

Suffix separator 
Type a character or space in this field if you want to separate the suffix from 

the rest of the number. For example, if you want your documents to end 

with -S, type the hyphen (-) in this field and S in the Fixed suffix field. 

Fixed suffix 
Type a suffix in this field if you want to add a fixed suffix to identify the 

document type. For example, if you want all of your subcontracts to end with 

S, type S in this field. 

Ending number 
Type the last number of the document sequence in this field if you want the 

document sequence to end with a particular number. 

Sample number 
This is an example of the formatted document sequence number.

Expense Allocations (Templates) 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Spend Management > Setup > Expense Allocations`


A/P allocation templates let you tell the system how to distribute costs among properties when 

applied to an A/P Invoice entry. Use these templates to add line items on A/P invoices faster with 

preset lists of properties (property groups). Use the Templates page to add, edit, view, and delete 

A/P allocation templates. You can also export the list of templates. 

• 
Click Add to add a new template. 

• 
Click View to review the details of a template. 

• 
Click Edit to change a template. 

• 
Click Delete to delete a template. 

• 
Click Export to export the list of templates. 

Use the standard list management tools to sort and filter the list, and to create custom views of 

the list.

Name 
This column contains the name of the allocation.

Template type

Amount.

Viewing a Template 

To view an allocation template: 

1. 
From the Templates page, click the View link next to the allocation template you want to 

view. The Template page loads. 

2. 
After you finish viewing the template, click the Done button. The Templates page loads. 

Printing a Template 

To print an allocation template: 

1. 
From the Templates page, click the View link next to the allocation template you want to 

print. The Template page loads. 

2. 
Click the Print to button, and then select an option. The system displays the allocation 

template in the browser for printing. 

3. 
Print the template from the browser. 

4. 
After you finish printing the template, click the back button in your browser to get back to 

the Template page. 

5. 
Click the Done button. The Templates page loads. 

Adding a Template 

A/P allocation templates let you tell the system how to distribute costs among properties when 

applied to an A/P Invoice entry. Use these templates to add line items on A/P invoices faster with 

preset lists of properties (property groups). 

To add a new allocation template: 

1. 
From the Templates page, click the Add button. The Template page loads. 

2. 
Type a name for the allocation template in the Name field. 

3. 
Type a description of the allocation template in the Description field. 

4. 
Select a template type from the Template drop-down list: 

• 
Percent: This template type lets you allocate a percentage of the A/P invoice to 

multiple properties. 

• 
Amount: This template type lets you allocate a specific amount to multiple properties. 

5. 
Type a memo for the allocation template in the Memo field.

Deactivating a Template 

Set allocation templates as inactive to hide unused items. The system retains the data but hides 

the inactive item on lists and drop-down lists. To permanently remove an allocation template, 

delete it. 

Inactive allocation templates are not selectable, and they do not appear on the Templates page 

unless the Include Inactive check box is selected. 

To deactivate an allocation template: 

1. 
From the Templates page, click the Edit link next to the allocation template you want to 

deactivate. The Template page loads. 

2. 
Select Inactive from the Status drop-down list. 

3. 
Click the Save button. The Templates page loads. 

Activating a Template 

To activate an allocation template: 

1. 
From the Templates page, select the Include Inactive check box to view the template in the 

list. 

2. 
Click the Edit link next to the allocation template you want to activate. The Template page 

loads. 

3. 
Select Active from the Status drop-down list. 

4. 
Click the Save button. The Templates page loads. 

Exporting the Templates List 

To export the list of A/P allocation templates: 

1. 
From the Templates page, click the Export button. 

2. 
Select the format in which to export the list: CSV, Excel, Word, or PDF. Your browser 

downloads the file. 

If the PDF opens in your browser window, click the Download button, or press CTRL + S to 
save the file.

Approval Configuration Page 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > Approvals > Approval Configuration`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Spend Management > Setup > Approvals > Approval Configuration`


Use the Approval configuration page to configure transaction approval workflow settings for 

journal entries, A/P invoices, purchase orders, service contracts, subcontracts, job cost 

transactions and change orders, and A/P payments. 

This page is divided into the following sections based on the type of transaction: 

• 
Journal entry approvals: This section contains settings for the journal entry approval 

workflow. 

• 
A/P invoice approvals: This section allows you to configure the approval process for A/P 

invoices. 

• 
Purchase orders: This section contains settings for the purchase order approval workflow. 

• 
Service contract: This section contains settings for service contract approvals and 

notifications. 

• 
Subcontract: This section contains settings for subcontract approvals and notifications. 

• 
Job cost: This section contains settings for the job cost transaction approval workflow and 

job cost change order approval workflow. 

• 
Budget check: This section allows you to choose the kind of budget check to use with the 

Spend Management application. 

• 
A/P payments: This section contains settings for A/P payment approvals and notifications. 

Before You Begin 

Access can vary depending on your organization’s subscriptions and your permissions. If you do 

not see the option in the menu, then ask your System Administrator to check your permissions. 

Permissions 

These permissions are required to manage approval configuration.

##### Configuring Transaction Approvals
*Source: `RP Financial Suite Spend Management User Guide.pdf`, Page 57*

Chapter 2: Preparing for Spend Management Configuration 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage® Financial Suite Spend Management User Guide 

Configuring Transaction Approvals 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > Approvals > Approval Configuration`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Spend Management > Setup > Approvals > Approval Configuration`


To configure transaction approvals, fill in the section corresponding with the transaction type. 

Filling In the Journal Entry Approvals Section 

1. 
Select the Enable journal entry approval check box to enable the approval workflow for 

journal entries. Clear the check box to disable journal entry approvals. 

2. 
Select the Ability to delete declined approvals check box if you want the system to delete 

declined transactions. This option is useful when your normal system configuration prohibits 

deleting transactions and you want to override the configuration to allow for deleting 

declined transactions. Clear the check box to retain declined journal entries. 

3. 
Select the Allow deletion of approved journal entries check box to enable deletion of 

journal entries after approval. 

4. 
Select the Email notifications check box to have the system notify approvers when a new 

journal entry requires their attention. Clear the check box to prevent the system from 

sending emails when journal entries are waiting for approval. 

5. 
Select the Advance G/L posting dates when period is closed check box if you want the 

system to automatically change the posting date to the next open date if an entry was 

submitted for approval in a period that is already closed. 

6. 
Select the Allow workflow assignment at journal entry check box to enable workflow type 

and workflow selection when creating a journal entry. 

7. 
In the Unrestricted section, click the Select button, and then choose one or more users to be 

the Unrestricted user. The users you choose can see all journal entries queued for approval. 

Unrestricted users can also act on the transactions even if the approvals are not assigned to 

them. For instructions on using the selection box, see Using the Multi-Select Box. 

8. 
In the Enable journal entry approval against each selected invoice creation type section: 

• 
Select the From CSV import check box to have the system evaluate journal entries that 

were imported from CSV files for approval. Clear the check box to allow imported 

journal entries to post without going through the approval process. 

• 
Select the From recurring journal entry check box to have the system evaluate journal 

entries that are created by recurring transactions for approval. Clear the check box to 

allow recurring journal entries to post without going through the approval process. 

9. 
Select a default approver from the Approver assigned if a user is inactive or a user is not 

present in a role drop-down list. The default approver receives transactions for approval if 

---


<!-- Page 58 -->
Preparing for Spend Management Configuration 

RealPage® Financial Suite Spend Management User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

there is an inactive user in the role or if there is no user in the role. For more information, 

see Defining a default approver (on page 52). 

Filling In the A/P Invoice Approvals Section 

Fill in this section to have the system send A/P invoices through the approval process. Otherwise, 

skip to the Purchase Orders section. 

1. 
Select the Enable A/P invoice approval check box to enable the approval workflow for A/P 

invoices. Clear the check box to disable A/P invoice approvals. 

2. 
Select the Ability to delete declined approvals check box if you want the system to delete 

declined transactions. This option is useful when your normal system configuration prohibits 

deleting transactions and you want to override the configuration to allow for deleting 

declined transactions. Clear the check box to retain declined A/P invoices. 

3. 
Select the Email notifications check box to have the system notify approvers when a new 

A/P invoice requires their attention. Clear the check box to prevent the system from sending 

emails when A/P invoices are waiting for their approval. 

4. 
Select the Advance G/L posting dates when period is closed check box if you want the 

system to automatically change the posting date to the next open date if an invoice was 

submitted for approval on a period that is already closed. 

5. 
Select the Allow workflow assignment at A/P entry check box to enable workflow type and 

workflow selection when creating an A/P invoice. 

6. 
Select the Enable preventing or warning a user when adding an A/P invoice that exceeds 

the budget check box if you want to prevent or warn a user from adding an A/P invoice that 

exceeds the available budget. In the Prevent or warn field, select the desired setting: 

• 
Prevent: Select this option to restrict the user from creating an A/P invoice that 

exceeds the budget. 

• 
Warn: Select this option to display a warning message when the user creates an A/P 

invoice that exceeds the budget. The user can choose to proceed anyway. 

This setting also applies to Spend Management Site Experience. 

You can assign permissions to specific users to allow them to bypass these restrictions (on 
page 54). When a user has these permissions, they can enter an A/P invoice without 
restriction. 

7. 
Select the Advance to next approver after XX days if the approver has not approved it 

check box if you want to keep the workflow moving when an approver is not available to 

review invoices. Type the number of days to wait before advancing the invoice to the next 

approver. Otherwise, clear the check box if you want all approvers to have a chance to 

review every invoice. 

---


<!-- Page 59 -->
Chapter 2: Preparing for Spend Management Configuration 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage® Financial Suite Spend Management User Guide 

8. 
Select the Always require approval for eInvoices and oInvoices check box to require 

approval for all eInvoices and oInvoices.  

Clear this option to send invoices through the approval only when: 

• 
There is no approval workflow set up for the location. 

• 
The invoice is coded to a default G/L account. 

• 
If you want an edited invoice to go through the default approval workflow only when a 

user is not present or is inactive in the role of the workflow.  

This setting applies to both eInvoices and oInvoices if your company receives both. If you 
receive only one invoice type, it applies only to that invoice type. 

9. 
Select the Advance to next approver after XX days if the approver has not approved it 

check box if you want to skip approvers who do not approve the A/P invoice within a 

specific number of days. For example, type 3 to skip the approver after three days. This 

prevents transactions from getting held up in the approval workflow.  

The system will never skip the final approver to ensure that a user has reviewed the 
invoice before being posted. 

10. 
Under the Unrestricted label, click the Select link and then choose one or more users to be 

the Unrestricted user. The users you choose can see all A/P invoices queued for approval. 

Unrestricted users can also act on the transactions even if the approvals are not assigned to 

them.  

If users have already been selected, click the Add/edit link to add or remove users. For 

instructions on using the selection box, see Using the multi-select box. 

11. 
Under the Enable A/P invoice approval against each selected invoice creation type label: 

• 
Select the From CSV import check box to have the system evaluate A/P invoices that 

were imported from CSV files for approval. Clear the Enable preventing or warning a 

user when adding an A/P invoice that exceeds the budget check box to allow 

imported A/P invoices to post without going through the approval process. 

• 
Select the From recurring invoice check box to have the system evaluate A/P invoices 

that are created by recurring invoices for approval. Clear the check box to allow 

recurring invoices to post without going through the approval process. 

• 
Select the From bill back template check box to have the system evaluate A/P invoices 

that are created by the bill back process for approval. Clear the check box to allow bill 

backs to post without going through the approval process. 

12. 
Select the Disable auto approve check box to prevent the system from automatically 

approving A/P invoices.

Defining a Default Approver 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > Approvals > Approval Configuration`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Spend Management > Setup > Approvals > Approval Configuration`


You can define a default approver for any transaction type (journal entries, A/P invoices, purchase 

orders, service contracts, subcontracts, job cost change orders, and A/P payments) if you enable 

approvals for that transaction type on the Approval configuration page. A default approver is a 

user that the system automatically assigns to review and approve a transaction when it detects a 

“gap” in the approval configuration. What constitutes a gap differs depending on the transaction 

type: 

• 
If the transaction is a journal entry, A/P invoice, purchase order, service contract, 

subcontract, or job cost change order, the default approver is automatically assigned if the 

user role that was set up as the approver is not assigned to any users, if there is an inactive 

user in the role, or if no one with that role has access to the transaction’s entity. 

• 
If the transaction is an A/P payment, the default approver is automatically assigned if a 

location is not assigned to a workflow for the payment method(s) selected from the 

Payment method drop-down list. 

How It Works 

The process for default approvers works as follows: 

1. 
A new transaction is submitted for approval. 

2. 
The system checks if there is a gap at any point in the workflow. 

3. 
If a gap is detected, a warning message appears at the top of the page to alert the person 

submitting the transaction. Warning messages appear in both RealPage Financial Suite and 

Spend Management Site Experience. 

---


<!-- Page 65 -->

4. 
The system notifies the default approver and routes the transaction to them for approval. If 

you are an admin user, a record of this action appears on the Approval history page.

Bypassing the Prevent or Warn When Exceeding a Budget Setting 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > Setup > Roles > Subscriptions > (Company) > Permissions`


If you have configured approvals so that the system will Prevent or Warn users from entering an 

A/P invoice or purchase order that exceeds the budget, you can bypass this setting at the user 

level through their user permissions. When a user has these permissions, they can enter an invoice 

or purchase order without restriction. 

The Enable preventing or warning... setting is located on the Approval configuration page in 
both the A/P invoice approvals and Purchase order approvals sections. See Configuring 
Transaction Approvals (on page 45) for more information. 

Assigning Bypass Permissions 

Assign one or more bypass permissions to a user or a role. With these permissions, the user can 

create the selected transaction type without restriction. 

These permissions are required to bypass the Prevent or Warn setting:

Disabling Auto-Approvals for Transactions 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > Approvals > Approval Configuration`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Spend Management > Setup > Approvals > Approval Configuration`


You can disable auto-approvals for A/P invoices, purchase orders, service contracts, and A/P 

payments. Auto-approving can occur when: 

---


<!-- Page 67 -->
Chapter 2: Preparing for Spend Management Configuration 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage® Financial Suite Spend Management User Guide 

• 
A user enters the transaction and is assigned to the first level of approval for that 

transaction. 

• 
A role requires more than one Required approver. 

• 
A transaction requires approval from multiple approval policies, and some of the same roles 

are defined for these policies. When a user who is assigned a specific role approves the 

transaction for that role, the system auto-approves transactions for that role in other 

policies and does not require a second approval from that role. 

To prevent the system from automatically approving transactions in any of the above scenarios, 

select the Disable auto approve check box for that transaction type on the Approval 

configuration page. When auto-approve is disabled, the system will require approval at each step 

in the approval workflow (on page 85). 

If an approval workflow applies to more than one of these transaction types, but you’ve disabled 
auto-approve for only one of the transaction types, then the system will auto-approve for one 
but not the other. 

Disabling Auto-Approvals  

To disable auto-approvals for A/P invoices, purchase orders, or service contracts: 

1. 
On the Approval configuration page, find the section that corresponds with the transaction 

type: 

• 
A/P invoice approvals 

• 
Purchase orders 

• 
Service contract  

2. 
Select the Disable auto approve check box. 

3. 
Click Save.

with that role to approve an invoice before it can move to the next level.  

Someone enters an A/P invoice that triggers the approval workflow. The following users have the 

Property Manager role and receive a notification that an invoice is pending approval:

Charlie

Automatically Advancing A/P Invoices and Purchase Orders to the Next Approver After 
XX Days 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > Approvals > Approval Configuration`


You can configure approvals so that A/P invoices and purchase orders automatically advance to 

the next approver if they are not approved within a set number of days. This prevents transactions 

from getting held up in the approval workflow. The system will continue skipping approvers until 

the invoice or purchase order reaches the final approver. The last person will not be skipped to 

ensure that at least one person reviews the transaction before it gets posted. 

To enable this feature: 

1. 
In the Applications menu, select the Company application, and then click the All tab. 

2. 
In the Approvals section, select the Approval configuration menu option. 

The Approval configuration page opens. 

3. 
In the A/P invoice approvals and/or Purchase orders section, select the Advance to next 

approver after XX days if the approver has not approved it check box. 

4. 
Type the number of days that the system should wait before advancing the invoice or 

purchase order to the next approver. For example, if you set the threshold to 4 days, then 

the invoice or purchase order will move to the next approver if it is not approved within four 

days. 

5. 
Click the Save button at the top of the page.

Approval Policy Manager List 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > Approvals > Approval Policy Manager`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Spend Management > Setup > Approvals > Approval Policy Manager`


The Approval policy manager list is a central location where you can manage your system’s 

approval policies. When new transactions are entered, the system compares them against the 

policies to determine the approval’s route. If the details of the transaction (amount, vendor, G/L 

account, etc.) match a policy, then the system assigns the approver(s) set in that policy. You can 

apply approval policies to journal entries, A/P invoices, purchase orders, service contracts, 

subcontracts, job cost change orders, A/P payments, and purchase order change orders.  

Use this list to view and manage the existing approval policies. From this list, you can: 

• 
Add new approval policies. 

• 
Edit existing approval policy details. 

• 
View existing approval policy details. 

• 
Export the list of approval policies. 

• 
Use the list controls to sort, search, and create custom views of the list. 

When you enable approvals for a transaction type, RealPage Accounting auto-generates a 
default policy and a default workflow for routing transactions of this type to the user (or role) 
you have set as the default approver. Default policies and workflows are visible only to admin 
users. The system uses these default policies and workflows only under certain conditions; see 
Defining a default approver (on page 52) for more information. 

Before You Begin 

Access can vary depending on your organization’s subscriptions and your permissions. If you do 

not see the option in the menu, then ask your System Administrator to check your permissions.

how to review a user’s permissions.

Adding Approval Policies

 Approval Policy Manager`

To add an approval policy: 

1. 
In the Policy type drop-down list, select the approval policy type. The available types 

include: 

User: Use this policy type to send all transactions to a specific user or role. You can combine 

this policy with one or more other policies that are based on other criteria in the approval 

workflow. 

Amount: Use this policy type to have the system check for transactions that are based on 

the amount of the transaction or change order. The system sends transactions of the 

amount you enter (or higher) to the selected approvers. Amount policies recognize the 

approver level of the person submitting the transaction or entering the change order; the 

system auto-approves (on page 76) transactions up to the submitter’s level in the approval 

hierarchy. 

Tiered amount: Use this policy type to have the system check for transactions that are 

based on the amount of the transaction or change order. Each approver has a limit to the 

amount he or she can approve. When a transaction or change order comes in that is over an 

approver’s limit, each approver must approve it to move the transaction to the next level. 

Tiered amount policies recognize the approver level of the person submitting the 

transaction or entering the change order; the system auto-approves (on page 76) 

transactions up to the submitter’s level in the approval hierarchy. 

Vendor: Use this policy type to have the system check for transactions that include a specific 

vendor. The system sends all transactions for the selected vendor to the designated 

approver or approvers. 

Vendor type: Use this policy type to have the system check for transactions that include a 

specific vendor type. The system sends all transactions for the selected vendor type to the 

designated approver or approvers. 

G/L account: Use this policy type to have the system check for transactions associated with 

a specific G/L account, such as Travel and Entertainment. The system sends all transactions 

tagged with a G/L account or G/L account range to the selected approver or approvers. 

Job: Use this policy type to have the system check for transactions associated with a specific 

job. 

Job type: Use this policy type to have the system check for transactions associated with a 

specific job type.

Accounting reviewer: Use this policy type to collect all A/P invoices and put them in an A/P 

invoice approval queue. The invoices must be approved before they can be posted. After 

creating this policy type, apply the policy to a workflow, and then assign the workflow to the

Journal type: Use this policy type to collect all journal entries for a journal, and then put

Payment method: Use this policy type to have the system check for A/P payments made

associated with a specific bank account. The system sends all transactions for the selected

Auto-Approving Transaction Amounts Through the Submitter Level 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > Approvals > Approval Policy Manager`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Spend Management > Setup > Approvals > Approval Policy Manager`


If an approval policy is based on the amount of a transaction (the policy type is set to Amount or 

Tiered amount), then RealPage Financial Suite will automatically approve transactions up to the 

submitter’s level of approval. This means that if the user who submitted the transaction is higher 

in the approval hierarchy, the system auto-approves the lower levels. For example, a CFO who 

enters a transaction in a multi-level approval workflow does not need approval from approvers at 

lower levels, such as a Property Manager or Regional Manager. 

---


<!-- Page 89 -->
Chapter 2: Preparing for Spend Management Configuration 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage® Financial Suite Spend Management User Guide 

Example 1: Amount Policy 

XYZ Company has set up an Amount policy to require approval for transactions over $500.00. The 
policy designates four (4) levels of approval—Property Manager, Regional Manager, Asset 
Manager, and CFO—for four (4) different amount ranges. The image below illustrates this policy. 

A user with the Regional Manager role is entering a new A/P invoice. The system can 
auto-approve invoices up to the Regional Manager’s amount range. For example: 

• 
If the Regional Manager enters an invoice for $600.00, then the system auto-approves the 
invoice instead of routing it to the Property Manager because the Regional Manager is 
higher in the approval hierarchy than the Property Manager. 

• 
If the Regional Manager enters an invoice for $2,000.00, then the system auto-approves the 
invoice instead of routing it to the Regional Manager role because the Regional Manager is 
the one who submitted the transaction. 

• 
If the Regional Manager enters an invoice for $3,000.00, then the Asset Manager must 
approve the invoice because the amount is above the Regional Manager’s approval limit. 

Example 2: Tiered Amount Policy 

In an alternate scenario, XYZ Company has set up a Tiered amount policy to require approval for 

transactions over $500.00. The policy designates four (4) levels of approval—Property Manager, 

Regional Manager, Asset Manager, and CFO—for four (4) different amount ranges. Unlike the 

Amount policy, the Tiered amount policy does not route transactions directly to the approver 

assigned to the amount range. Instead, the transaction must be approved in tiers, starting from 

the lowest level and progressing to the highest level required for the transaction amount. 

---

A user with the Regional Manager role is entering a new A/P invoice. The system can 

auto-approve invoices up to the Regional Manager’s amount range. For example: 

• 
If the Regional Manager enters an invoice for $600.00, then the system auto-approves the 

invoice for the Property Manager tier because the Regional Manager is higher in the 

approval hierarchy than the Property Manager. 

• 
If the Regional Manager enters an invoice for $2,000.00, then the system auto-approves the 

invoice for both the Property Manager and Regional Manager tiers. 

• 
If the Regional Manager enters an invoice for $3,000.00, then the system auto-approves the 

invoice for the Property Manager and Regional Manager tiers; however, the Asset Manager 

must still approve the invoice.

> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > Approvals > Spend Policy Manager`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Spend Management > Setup > Approvals > Spend Policy Manager`


The Spend policy manager page lets you set up and tie rules for spending to budgets in the 

general ledger (G/L). You can reference spend policies while viewing, editing, or reviewing 

transactions. 

Adding a New Spend Policy 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > 
 Spend Policy Manager`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Spend Management > Setup > 
 Spend Policy Manager`


Review existing spend policies before adding a new one. 

To add a new spend policy, set a policy name, and then set up the approval routing and limits. 

You can specify multiple roles and users for approvals for various amounts or percentages that a 

transaction is over budget. 

For example, you can assign a first-tier approval to a role and a second-tier approval to a user at a 

higher authority level, as shown in the example below. 

To add a new spend policy: 

1. 
Type the name of the new policy in the Policy name field. 

2. 
Select Active from the Status drop-down list. 

3. 
In the Role/user column, select the role or user that you want to approve transactions that 

exceed the over percentage or amount. 

4. 
In the G/L account from column, select the G/L account that is to flag transactions for 

approval. 

For example, choose “6700.016--Miscellaneous” as the G/L account to ensure that anything 

tagged as Miscellaneous goes through an approval process.

5. 
Set the percentage or amount over budget where you want to require approval as follows: 

You are not required to enter both an Over Percentage and Over Amount for a line item 
approval. However, you can enter both, if applicable. 

• 
To require approval for a transaction that is over budget by a certain percentage, type 

that percentage in the Over percentage field. 

• 
To require approval for a transaction that is over budget by a certain amount, type 

that amount in the Over amount field. 

• 
To require approval for a transaction that is over budget by a certain percentage or a 

certain amount, type the percentage in the Over percentage field and the amount in 

the Over amount field. 

6. 
In the Require approvers column, select the highest level of approval required for 

transactions, up to four. 

If you select a specific user in the Role/user column, the Require approvers column 
defaults to 1. If you select a role in the Role/user column, you can select up to 4 in the 

Require approvers column. 

7. 
When you are satisfied with the spend policy, click the Save button.

You cannot edit the Policy name field, but you can edit the other fields.

Duplicating a Spend Policy 

Duplicating a spend policy lets you create a new spend policy based on an existing one. 

To duplicate a spend policy:

On the Spend policy manager page, click the Duplicate button.

Approval Workflow List 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > Approvals > Approval Workflow`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Spend Management > Setup > Approvals > Approval Workflow`


Use the Approval workflow list to create approval workflows. An approval workflow associates 

approval policies with properties. 

From this list, you can: 

• 
Add an approval workflow. 

• 
Edit an approval workflow’s details. 

• 
View an approval workflow’s details. 

• 
Delete an approval workflow. 

• 
Export the list of approval workflows. 

• 
Change the view between the workflow list and the property workflow list. 

When you enable approvals for a transaction type, RealPage Accounting auto-generates a 
default policy and a default workflow for routing transactions of this type to the user (or role) 
you have set as the default approver. Default policies and workflows are visible only to admin 
users. The system uses these default policies and workflows only under certain conditions; see 
Defining a default approver (on page 52) for more information. 

Default View 

The default view shows a list of all approval workflows created for your company.

1. 
In the Name field, type a name that describes the purpose of the workflow; for example, 

“Job Approvals”. Workflow names cannot exceed 60 characters and cannot include any 

special characters except en dashes (–) or underscores (_). 

2. 
In the Transaction section, select the check box for each type of transaction this workflow is 

going to contain. Only the transactions for which approvals are enabled appear in this list.  

• 
Account payable invoice (AP) 

• 
Purchase order (PO) 

• 
Job cost transaction (JCT) 

• 
Job cost change order (JC) 

• 
Service contract (SC) 

• 
Subcontract (SUB) 

• 
eInvoice (EI) / oInvoice (OI) 

• 
Journal entry (JE) 

• 
Corporate invoice (CI) 

• 
Payment (PYMT) 

• 
Purchase order change order (POCO) 

The following workflow types apply to A/P invoices: 

• 
Distribution (D): This option appears only if the Investor Tracking application is 

enabled and A/P invoice approvals are enabled. If selected, then invoices created from 

a distribution will go through the approval workflow before being posted. 

• 
Petty cash reimbursement (PCR): This option appears only if Debit cards for petty 

cash is enabled and A/P invoice approvals are enabled. If selected, then invoices 

created from a card transaction will go through the approval workflow before being 

posted. 

You can apply a workflow to multiple types of transactions or create a separate workflow if 
you want to apply different policies to different types. However, you cannot combine the 

Journal entry, Payment, or Purchase order change order selections with other transaction 
types. 

Selecting the Policies 

1. 
In the Policy name column, select the first policy to add to the workflow. The system 

completes the policy type column. Click the link to view the policy’s details. 

2. 
Click the Override check box if you want the policy to be an override. 

When selected, this policy is the only policy that is followed when the criterion is met. All 

other policies are discarded, and the policy will be the only approval required by the 

selected properties.

The system applies the approval policies in the order they appear in the workflow’s

Selecting the Properties 

Click the Select button and choose the properties that you want to use this approval workflow. 

For help, see Using the Multi-Select Box. 

If workflows are not assigned to a property, they are visible for all properties. The workflows 
that are not assigned to a property are available for selection if you choose to assign a workflow 
while entering a transaction. 

Defining Conditions 

You can set up conditions to determine whether transactions require approval. The system applies 

the workflow policies to a new transaction only when the conditions are met. 

This section is optional. 

1. 
Select the Enable conditions check box to enable conditions for the approval workflow. 

A blank list appears for you to choose the criteria that you want to apply to the workflow. 

2. 
Select the Filter condition: 

• 
All (AND): Select to run the approval workflow when all conditions are met. 

• 
Any (OR): Select to run the approval workflow when any condition is met. 

• 
Expression: Select when you want to write an expression, a combination of AND and 

OR logic that determines whether or not to run the approval workflow. 

3. 
In the Policy type column, select a policy type that you want to use for a condition’s test. 

The following policy types are available to use in a workflow condition: 

• 
G/L account 

• 
G/L account group 

• 
Vendor 

• 
Vendor type 

• 
Amount 

• 
Job 

• 
Job type 

• 
Journal type 

• 
Department 

When Payment is the selected transaction, then the policy type drop-down list also 

includes: 

• 
Payment method

• 
Bank account 

The following options are not approval policy types but can be used when defining 

conditions for approval workflows:  

• 
Submitter 

• 
Submitter role 

Submitter conditions set criteria for approval workflows based on the user (or user role) who 

submitted the transaction. For more information, see Submitter Conditions in Approval 

Workflows (on page 95). 

4. 
In the Operator column, select the logical expression that you want to use to evaluate the 

condition: 

• 
Equal to (IN): The condition is true when the policy type is equal to (or in the range of) 

the From and To criteria. 

• 
Not equal to (NOT IN): The condition is true when the policy type is not equal to (or 

not in the range of) the From and To criteria. 

• 
Within: The condition is true when the G/L account defined in the policy is in the 

selected account group in the From drop-down list. This operator is available only with 

the G/L account group policy type. 

5. 
In the From and To columns, select the criterion or range of criteria. 

Example of a Condition 

If the amount is between $150 and $999, then the condition is true. 

6. 
Continue adding new conditions to the list as needed, especially if you are building 

conditions for an expression.

You can set up conditions to determine whether or not transactions require approval. When a

does it apply the workflow policies to the transaction. If the conditions are not met, then the 

system does not apply the workflow policies to the transaction.

Select the Enable conditions check box to enable conditions for the approval workflow.

2. 
Select the Filter condition: 

• 
All (AND): Select to run the approval workflow when all conditions are met. 

• 
Any (OR): Select to run the approval workflow when any condition is met. 

• 
Expression: Select when you want to write an expression, a combination of AND and 

OR logic that determines whether or not to run the approval workflow. 

3. 
In the Policy type column, select a policy type that you want to use for a condition’s test. 

The following policy types are available to use in a workflow condition: 

• 
G/L account 

• 
G/L account group 

• 
Vendor 

• 
Vendor type

Amount 

• 
Job 

• 
Job type 

• 
Journal type 

• 
Department

includes: 

• 
Payment method 

• 
Bank account

conditions for approval workflows:  

• 
Submitter

Submitter Conditions in Approval Workflows 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > Approvals > 
 Approval Workflow`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Spend Management > Setup > Approvals > 
 Approval Workflow`


You can set up submitter conditions for approval workflows based on the user (or user role) who 

submitted the transaction. These conditions can be used to: 

• 
Apply the workflow only when a specific user or user role—such as a President or 

CFO—enters a transaction.  

• 
Apply the workflow to every user except a specific user or group of users. 

---


<!-- Page 108 -->
Preparing for Spend Management Configuration 

RealPage® Financial Suite Spend Management User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

To define submitter conditions, set the Policy type of the condition (on page 93) to “Submitter” 
or “Submitter role”. 

Example 1 

The approval workflow should apply only when Kim Johnson enters a transaction. 

Set up the condition as follows: 

• 
Policy type: Submitter 

• 
Operator: Equal to (IN) 

• 
From: Kim Johnson 

• 
To: Kim Johnson 

If you are specifying a single user, make sure to set the From and To fields to the same user. 

Example 2 

The approval workflow should apply only when Kim Johnson or Alex Garcia enters a transaction. 

Set up the condition as follows: 

Row 1 

• 
Policy type: Submitter 

• 
Operator: Equal to (IN) 

• 
From: Kim Johnson 

• 
To: Kim Johnson 

Row 2 

• 
Policy type: Submitter 

• 
Operator: Equal to (IN) 

• 
From: Alex Garcia 

---

*Source: `RP Financial Suite Spend Management User Guide.pdf`, Page 109*

Chapter 2: Preparing for Spend Management Configuration 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage® Financial Suite Spend Management User Guide 

• 
To: Alex Garcia 

If you are specifying multiple users or roles, make sure to set the Filter condition to “Any (OR)”. 
This tells the system that the condition is met if Kim Johnson or Alex Garcia enter a transaction. 

Example 3 

The approval workflow should apply to every user who enters a transaction except the CFO. 

Set up the condition as follows: 

• 
Policy type: Submitter Role 

• 
Operator: Not equal to (NOT IN) 

• 
From: CFO

Properties Section 

Property

When you submit a new transaction, the selected properties are the first 

criteria that the system uses to look up workflow rules. If the system 

finds a workflow, then the transaction is compared to the policies (and, if 

enabled, conditions) to determine which approvers to assign to the 

transaction. 

Conditions Section 

Enable conditions 
Select to use conditions in this approval workflow. 

Filter conditions 
Select the desired operator the system is to use when evaluating the 

conditions: 

• 
All (AND): The workflow applies when all conditions in this 

section are met. 

• 
Any (OR): The workflow applies when any condition in this 

section is met. 

• 
Expression: The workflow applies when conditions are met 

according to the written expression. An expression is a 

combination of AND and OR logic used to string multiple 

conditions together. Because an expression uses the row 

numbers from the conditions list, you write the expression after 

you define your conditions. 

(Expression field) 
This field appears only when you select Expression in the Filter 

conditions drop-down list. Type a written expression using a 

combination of AND and OR logic between condition row numbers. 

Expression Examples: 

(1 AND 2) OR (2 AND 3) 

If the first and second conditions both evaluate to true OR if the second 

and third conditions both evaluate to true, then the approval workflow 

runs. 

(1 AND 3) OR 2 

If the first and third conditions both evaluate to true OR the second 

condition evaluates to true, then the approval workflow runs. 

Policy type

conditions (on page 95) based on the specific user or user role who

Approval Workbench 

See the How to Get Here (on page 104) topic for a list of ways to access this area. 

Use the Approval workbench page to view the transactions waiting for approval. This page has 

two sections: 

• 
A filters section to control which transactions appear in the workbench. 

• 
A transactions list to approve, close, decline, view, or edit pending transactions. You can also 

add another approver or export the transaction to Excel. 

You can switch between two workbench views using the following buttons: 

• 
My approvals: Displays the transactions assigned to you for approval. 

AI Approvals in RealPage Accounting streamlines the A/P invoice approval process using AI

Before You Begin 

Access can vary depending on your organization’s subscriptions and your permissions. If you do 

not see the option in the menu, then ask your System Administrator to check your permissions. 

Subscriptions 

Your company must subscribe to the Company application and at least one of the following 

applications. Choose the appropriate application for the type of approval workflow that you need. 

• 
Accounts Payable: Subscribe to the Accounts Payable application to use the approval 

process with A/P invoices, A/P payments, and expense reports. Approvals of new and 

changed vendors also requires you to subscribe to the Accounts Payable application. 

• 
Spend Management: Subscribe to the Spend Management application to use the approval 

process with purchase orders, service contracts, and subcontracts. 

• 
General Ledger: Subscribe to the General Ledger application to use the approval process 

with journal entries. 

• 
Job Cost & Reserves: Subscribe to the Job Cost & Reserves application to use the approval 

process with job cost change orders.

Approving and Declining Transactions 

See the How to Get Here (on page 104) topic for a list of ways to access the Approval workbench.  

This page has two views, View All and My Approvals. You must be in the Approval Workbench - 

My Approvals view to approve and decline transactions. If you are on the Approvals Workbench 

- View All view, click the My Approvals button to change to the My Approvals view.  

From the My Approvals view, you can approve or decline transactions individually or in bulk. If 

you are reviewing A/P invoices, then you can use the Review and approve button to quickly 

approve or decline invoices back-to-back (on page 112). 

When you approve a transaction, the system looks up the next approver. If the next approver 
previously approved the transaction, then the system sets the status of the transaction to 
Approved. 

Approving One Transaction 

To approve one transaction: 

1. 
Click the Approve link. 

The Approve [transaction type] box opens. 

2. 
Optionally, in the Comments box, type a comment. 

3. 
Click the Approve button.

Reviewing and Approving A/P Invoices 

See the How to Get Here (on page 104) topic for a list of ways to access this area. 

When the Approval workbench is filtered by A/P invoices, an additional button appears in the 

upper-right corner labeled Review & approve. This button allows you to quickly open and review 

invoices in the order they appear in the approval queue.  

To review and approve A/P invoices: 

1. 
From the Applications menu, select Company, and then select the All tab. 

2. 
Select Approval workbench. 

3. 
Select the A/P invoice option. Set any other filters as needed. 

4. 
Click the Apply button. The system filters the list so that it shows only A/P invoices. 

5. 
Click the Review & approve button. The A/P invoice page opens. If the A/P invoice has an 

attachment and you have enabled the image viewer, the attachment displays in a separate 

window. If not, the invoice image will show on the same page as the invoice. 

If the Review & approve button does not appear, there are no A/P invoices in queue to 
approve. 

6. 
Review the A/P invoice. You can also edit the invoice at the same time. 

7. 
Click one of the buttons: 

• 
Approve & next: Approve the current A/P invoice, and then have the system display 

the next A/P invoice to evaluate. If you made any changes to the invoice, your changes 

are saved and the invoice is routed to the next person for approval. 

• 
Approve & next > Next: Skip the current A/P invoice and display the next A/P invoice 

in your queue. Any changes you made to the invoice will not be saved.

When an eInvoice is created in Accounting, goes through approvals, and then gets posted, 
RealPage Accounting sends an update to OpsMerchant to change the partner status from 

Pending to Approved. This ensures that the vendor is aware of the current status of the 
invoice. We also send updates to OpsMerchant when the eInvoice is paid or voided, along 
with the payment details.

Sending a Transaction Back to the Previous Approver 

See the How to Get Here (on page 104) topic for a list of ways to access the Approval workbench. 

Some transactions require approvals from multiple levels. If a transaction pending your approval 

was approved by someone else, you can send the transaction back to that approver instead of 

declining the transaction outright. 

To send a transaction back to the previous approver: 

1. 
On the Approval workbench - My approvals page, click the Send back link in the Send 

back column next to the transaction. 

The Send back box opens. 

2. 
Type your reason for sending back the transaction in the Comments field. 

3. 
Click the Send back button. 

The system loads the Approval workbench - My approvals page, and the transaction no 

longer appears in your queue. 

Sending Back Multiple Transactions 

To send back multiple transactions to the previous approver: 

1. 
From the Approval workbench - My approvals page, select the check box next to each 

transaction that you want to send back to the previous approver. 

2. 
Click the Send back link in the Send back column next to any of the transactions that you 

selected. 

The Send back box opens. 

3. 
Type your reason for sending back the transaction in the Comments field. 

4. 
Select the additional approver from the Additional approver drop-down list. 

5. 
Click the Send back button. 

The system loads the Approval workbench - My approvals page, and the transactions no 

longer appear in your queue.

Job cost

subcontracts, and journal entries. 

Include declined 
Select this check box to include declined transactions in the list so you 

can edit and resubmit them. 

By default, declined transactions are not included in the workbench. If 
you want to include them by default, then create a custom workbench 
view (on page 113) with the Include declined option selected and save 
it as the Default view. 

The presence and order of the remaining filters and columns depend on which transaction type 

you select. Use the workbench column controls (on page 155) to further filter the list. Filter 

selections will carry over even if you switch to a different transaction type in the workbench.

AI match 
This is a system-calculated percentage based on the number of invoices 

received for a vendor within a specific period. Based on the AI match 

level, you can enable the system to automatically approve those invoices 

if it is over a specified confidence percentage and below a specified 

dollar amount. See AI Invoice Approvals for more information.

Actions 
Click the action link you want to complete for the transaction: 

• 
Edit: Edit the purchase order. 

• 
View: View the purchase order details. 

• 
Approve: Approve the purchase order and enter optional 

comments for the approval. 

• 
Decline: Decline the purchase order and specify the reason you 

are declining it. 

• 
Dispute: Dispute the purchase order and specify the reason you 

are disputing it. 

• 
Close: Confirm that the purchase order is closed and change the 

status of the purchase order to Closed. 

• 
Delete: Delete the purchase order. Purchase orders can be 

deleted only if you have if the Delete permission for purchase 

orders and if the purchase has not been matched to any 

invoices.  

If you have the Delete permission, then both the Close and 

Delete options appear next to declined purchase orders. If you 
do not have the Delete permission, then only the Close option 
appears.

Preparing for Spend Management Configuration 

RealPage® Financial Suite Spend Management User Guide

Approval History List 

See the How to Get Here (on page 137) topic for a list of ways to access this area. 

Use this page to review a transaction’s approval history. This page displays when you click a status 

in the Approval workbench. 

When you enable approvals for a transaction type, RealPage Financial Suite auto-generates a 
default policy and a default workflow for routing transactions of this type to the user (or role) 
you have set as the default approver (on page 52). Default policies and workflows are visible 
only to admin users, including any events or actions logged in the approval history. 

Columns 

• 
Policy type: This column shows the policy type that the system used to approve the item. 

• 
Policy name: This column shows the policy name that the system used to approve the item. 

Click the link to view policy details. 

• 
Workflow name: This column shows the name of the workflow that the system used in the 

transaction. Click the link to view workflow details. 

• 
Approver role/user: This column contains a link to information about the person who 

decided on the approval. Click to view the role assignment details. You can find out who is 

assigned to a particular role with this link. 

• 
Approved/Declined by: This column contains the user name of the person who made the 

approval decisions. 

• 
Event date: This column contains the date that the transaction last underwent an approval 

event. (It was submitted for approval or partially approved.) 

• 
Comments: This column contains the comments the approver made along with his decision. 

• 
State: This column contains the status of the approval. 

• 
Action type: This column contains the approval status of the transaction. 

• 
Action comments: This column contains the comments associated with the action in the 

state. 

• 
Submitted by: This column contains the name of the user who submitted the transaction. 

“Console member” appears when the user accesses RealPage Financial Suite through the 
console rather than by logging in directly.

Viewing a Monthly Report 

To run a report using default settings: 

1. 
When the report settings screen appears, click the View button.  

The system opens a report showing all results for the default reporting period. 

2. 
To refine the report, click the Customize button to return to the main report screen, and 

then follow the steps in customizing and running this report. 

Customizing and Running the Report 

To see every result for a particular category, do not make selections from any of the data entry 
boxes. You can run this report without entering any search information. However, the report 
may take a long time to run and may return too many results to be useful.  

Before running the report, you can select the types of items to include and specify how you want 

the report to appear. 

To customize and run the report: 

1. 
In the Time period section, create your own reporting period. 

• 
Select Today if you want to generate the report for the current date. 

• 
Select Selected date if you want to generate the report for a different date, and then 

select your preferred date. 

2. 
In the Filters section, include or exclude specific types of objects in the report. As a general 

rule, set more filters to get fewer and more precise results. 

• 
In the Transaction type drop-down list, select to return results only for a specific 

transaction type. 

• 
In the From vendor and To vendor drop-down lists, select a range of vendors for 

which you want to return results. 

• 
In the Location drop-down list, select to return results only for a specific location. 

• 
Select the Individual report check box to generate an individual report for each 

location. 

• 
Select the Prompt on run check box to require a location before running the report. 

• 
In the Show for drop-down list, select whether you want to display results for all 

locations, parent locations, or child locations.

Approval History Audit Report 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > Approvals > Approval History Audit Report`


Use the Approval History Audit report to review your company’s transaction approval history, 

audit your approval workflows and policies, and verify whether approvals are in compliance with 

those policies. You can filter the report by single or multiple transaction types, including A/P 

invoices, purchase orders, service contracts, subcontracts, payments, and expense reports. You 

can also filter by specific transaction numbers, statuses, vendors, or locations. 

Before You Begin 

Access can vary depending on your organization’s subscriptions and your permissions. If you do 

not see the option in the menu, then ask your System Administrator to check your permissions. 

Permissions 

These permissions are required to run the Approval History Audit report. 

Application 
Activities/Lists 
Permissions 

Company 
Approval History Audit Report Run 

If your user account doesn’t have the permissions shown above, then ask your System 

Administrator for assistance. If you have administrator privileges, you can assign permissions for a 

new feature to a user or to a role. See Roles and Permissions (on page 604) for a description of 

how to review a user’s permissions. 

Customizing and Running the Approval History Audit Report 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > Approvals > Approval History Audit Report`


To customize and run the Approval History Audit report: 

1. 
Open the Company menu. 

---


<!-- Page 158 -->
Preparing for Spend Management Configuration 

RealPage® Financial Suite Spend Management User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

2. 
In the Approvals section, select the Approval history audit report option. 

The report configuration page opens. 

Defining the Report Period 

In the Time period section, define the time period for the report. You can either select the 

Reporting period and As of date or select a date range to identify the report’s coverage period 

but not both. 

Type “p” in a date field to automatically insert the last day of the prior month. See Specifying 

Dates in Getting Started for a full list of shortcut keys related to entering dates.  

To run a report for a reporting period: 

1. 
In the Reporting period drop-down list, select the reporting period. 

2. 
In the As of date field, select the date to begin the report coverage.  

3. 
Select the Prompt on run check box if you want to be able to choose the reporting period 

and As of date when you run the report. 

To run a report for a date range: 

Specify the starting and ending dates to identify the report’s period of coverage. 

Filtering the Report 

Optionally, in the Filters section, select any filters you want to apply to the report: 

• 
Transaction type: Select one or more transaction types. 

• 
Transaction number: Type one or more transaction numbers. To filter by specific transaction 

numbers, the Transaction type filter must be set to a single transaction type. If you are 

entering multiple transaction numbers, insert a comma between each number (for example, 

INV-0003, INV-0023). 

• 
From vendor/To vendor: Select a range of vendor IDs. 

• 
Vendor type: Select a vendor type. 

• 
Location: Select a location or location group. 

• 
Select the Individual report check box if you want to generate one report per location. 

If you select this option, then you must click the Process & store button at the end. 

• 
Select the Prompt on run check box to prompt users to select a location before 

running the report. 

• 
Status: Select one or more transaction approval statuses. 

Labeling the Report 

In the Titles section, define the report title, subtitle, and footer text:

1.

2.

Titles, subtitles, and footers apply only to the PDF version of the report (click Print to get the 
PDF version). You can use up to 80 characters, including spaces, in each field. 

Running the Report 

When you have finished configuring the report, click one of the following buttons: 

• 
View: Runs and displays the report directly in your browser.

Memorize: Memorizes the report and stores it in the Memorized reports list. 

• 
Export: Exports the report to a Word, CSV, Excel, or Text file. 

What’s Next?

results you want by filling in the desired fields and then clicking View to run the report. If you 

want to refine the report further, click Customize to return to the report setup page. Repeat this 

process as needed.

Full Service Spend Management 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > Setup > Subscriptions > Full Service Spend Management`


Full Service Spend Management integrates RealPage Invoice Processing with RealPage 

Accounting, allowing you to create new invoices in Accounts Payable and Spend Management 

from scanned invoices without inputting the invoices manually. 

To use Full Service Spend Management, you must subscribe to the service. Contact your RealPage 

representative for more information. After enabling and configuring this service, Full Service 

options appear in both Accounts Payable and Spend Management.

*Source: `RP Financial Suite Spend Management User Guide.pdf`, Page 165*

RealPage® Financial Suite Spend Management User Guide 

Workbenches 

The Workbench feature puts all of your spend activities into one location. Spend Management features two 

workbenches: the Spend management workbench and the Approval workbench. 

• 
Spend management workbench (on page 166): This workbench allows you to search for, view, and act on 

transactions, including A/P invoices, purchase orders, service contracts, and subcontracts. 

• 
Approval workbench (on page 101): This workbench allows you to view and approve (or decline) 

transactions awaiting approval.

#### Workbench Features
*Source: `RP Financial Suite Spend Management User Guide.pdf`, Page 166*

Workbenches 

RealPage® Financial Suite Spend Management User Guide

Workbench Features 

The workbench is a central location where you can monitor and manage transactions. The 

workbench offers controls that allow you to: 

• 
View all columns available in Accounting 

• 
Use SmartGrid technology to: 

• 
Rearrange the columns 

• 
Customize and save which columns you see by default 

• 
Group and ungroup transactions based on different fields, like vendor or property 

• 
Apply operators to columns 

• 
Multi-select different filters for the following: 

• 
Property 

• 
Transaction type 

• 
Status 

• 
Submitted by 

• 
Next approver 

• 
Units 

• 
Save filter settings as a view and then reapply the view any time that you return to the 

workbench 

• 
Retain filters when switching between transaction types to alleviate selecting and applying 

the same filters again on both Approval and Spend Management Workbenches 

• 
Select the option to include future orders 

• 
Export the data in the workbench to an Excel file

All workbench columns have a menu with additional options. Roll over the column header to

 Options icon. If you do not see the menu, expand the width of the column (by 

dragging the column edge on the header bar) and try again. 

Using Column Options 

Click the Options 
 icon to open the column menu. The default tab allows you to: 

• 
Pin column: Affix the column to the left or right side of the list. Select No pin to return the 

column to its sort order. 

• 
Autosize this column/Autosize all columns: Have the system resize the column or all 

columns based on the columns’ contents. 

• 
Group or Ungroup: Group the list by the selected column or (if grouped) ungroup the list 

by the selected column. Only some columns can be grouped. 

• 
Reset columns: Reset the columns to their default settings.

Min: Finds the smallest number in the column.

Managing Workbench Views 

Workbench views let you save filtered views of the current workbench page for each access each 
time you load the workbench. The Apply view drop-down list features the available views on the 
workbench page. 

To apply a view to a page, select a view from the Apply view drop-down list, as shown below. 

To add a new view or update a current view, see Adding or updating a workbench view (on page 
162). 

Adding or Updating a View 

To add or update a view: 

• 
To add a new view, click Save view as. 

• 
To update the current view, click Update view. 

The Save View As box shown below opens. 

a) View name: Type the name of the new view in this field. 

b) Default view: Select this check box if you want to make this view the default view when you 

load the page. 

c) Make public: Select this check box if you want to allow other users to use this view. 

d) Save: Click this button when you are ready to save the view.

Spend Management Views

Use the Spend management views page to review a list of all custom views created in Spend 

Management, including views created for the Spend management workbench, Approval 

workbench, and Spend inquiry pages. You can also use this page to delete views that you 

created. 

Removing a Custom View 

To remove a custom view from Spend Management: 

1. 
From the Spend management views page, click the Delete link next to the custom view you 

want to delete. A prompt appears at the top of the page. 

You can only remove a view that you created. 

2. 
Click the OK button. The system removes the custom view.

Export 
Exports the list to a CSV, Excel, Word, or PDF file. 

Exporting from a Workbench 

To export from a workbench: 

1. 
Right-click any data in the workbench to display the export controls menu. 

2. 
Click the Export button, and then select the file format that you want the system to use to 

export the data. 

• 
CSV Export: This format makes it easy to move the data from one program to another. 

You can use files that you save in the CSV format with any spreadsheet program. After 

selecting this option, the system exports the list as a CSV file. 

• 
Excel Export (.xlsx): After selecting this option, the system exports the list in Excel’s 

native format. 

• 
Excel Export (.xml): After selecting this option, the system exports the list in XML 

format. 

The location of the exported file depends on your browser’s default download 
functionality. 

All three of these export formats export the entire list, including these links: 

• 
Actions: Exports the HTML code for editing, viewing, approving, and declining the 

transaction. 

• 
Add approver: Click to add another approver for the transaction. 

• 
Send back: Send the transaction back to the requester. 

• 
Status: Click to view the transaction’s approval history.

Spend Management Workbench 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Spend Management > All > Workbench`


The Spend management workbench page allows you to search for, view, delete, and act on 

transactions, including A/P invoices, purchase orders, service contracts, and subcontracts. 

As shown in the example below, the Spend management workbench page allows you to manage 

your orders and invoices from a single page. You can set up views of transaction lists for easier 

future reference. 

a) Apply view: Select a quick view from the drop-down list. 

b) Transaction type: Select a transaction type. 

c) Apply filters: Choose from a variety of filter criteria, and then click the Apply button to 

apply filters to the transactions list. 

d) Transactions list: This table provides a list of the resulting transactions from the filter criteria 

chosen above. 

The Transaction type column in the Transactions list displays the transaction type selected 
in the Transaction type field filter. If there is no specific transaction type selected, this 
column will display all transaction types. 

e) Save view as: This button allows you to save the current list view for future reference. 

f) 
Package invoices: This button allows you to select the invoices to include in the package. 

---
