g) Add: This button allows you to add new transactions. 

h) Done: This button takes you back to the Spend management home page. 

i) 
Export to Excel: This button allows you to export the information in the transaction list to an 

Excel spreadsheet. 

A/P Invoice View 

The A/P Invoice view includes details such as the actions that can be taken on an invoice, 

transaction details, invoice number, status, vendor and property name, total amount, submission 

details, next approver, description, and the matched order, if applicable. If needed, you can click 

the Status link to view more information about the approval history of the A/P invoice. 

The links and buttons in the A/P Invoice view let you access the following tasks: 

• 
Add A/P invoices 

• 
View A/P invoices 

• 
Edit A/P invoices 

• 
Delete A/P invoices 

Purchase Order View 

The Purchase Order view includes details such as the actions that can be taken on a purchase 

order, transaction details, order number, status, storefront status, vendor and property name, 

associated amounts, submission details, next approver, and description. You can close purchase 

orders directly from this view. If needed, you can click the Status link to view more information 

about the approval history of the purchase order. 

The links and buttons in the Purchase Order view let you access the following tasks: 

• 
Add purchase orders 

• 
View purchase orders 

• 
Edit purchase orders 

• 
Delete purchase orders 

• 
Create change orders 

• 
Receive goods 

• 
Create invoices for purchase orders 

Service Contract View 

The Service Contract view includes details such as the actions that can be taken on a service 

contract, transaction details, the contract/order number, date details, status, vendor and property 

name, associated amounts, submission details, next approver, and description. 

The links and buttons in the contract view let you access the following tasks: 

• 
If you filter for the Service contract transaction type:

Spend Management Home Page > Workbench

Finding a Transaction 

To find a transaction, apply filters to the workbench, and then review the filtered list: 

1. 
Select one of these options: 

• 
A/P Invoice: This option filters results for A/P invoices. 

• 
Purchase Order: This option filters results for purchase orders. 

• 
Service Contract: This option filters results for service contracts. 

• 
Subcontract: This option filters results for subcontracts. 

• 
Job Cost Change Order: This option filters results for job cost change orders. 

2. 
Select any of the criteria in the top section of the workbench to filter for the transactions 

you want to find. See Filters in Fields (on page 182) for more information.

Available Budget Page 

See How to Get Here (on page 172) for a list of ways to access this page. 

This page opens when you click the Spend control button on an A/P invoice, purchase order, or 

subcontract. 

The tabs on the Available budget page change depending on the Line entry type that you 

selected in the transaction:  

• 
Standard 

• 
Job Cost 

• 
Both 

Standard Line Items 

If you selected Standard as the Line entry type of an A/P invoice or purchase order, then the 

Available budget page includes three tabs, (Month, Year to date, and Current Year), that show 

the monthly, year-to-date, and current-year spending for a property and account. 

Use the Current year tab to view the full-year budget and current activity and compare it to the 

planned activity for the remainder of the year.

Job Cost Line Items 

If you selected Include Job cost as the Line entry type on an A/P invoice or purchase order—or if 

the transaction is a subcontract—then the Available budget page shows only job cost budget 

amounts. You can view the amount budgeted, the actual amount spent, and the budget 

remaining for the job cost code. 

Standard and Job Cost Line Items 

If you selected Both as the Line entry type for an A/P invoice, then the Available budget page 

includes an additional tab labeled Job cost. The tab shows the amount budgeted, the actual 

amount spent, and the budget remaining for the job cost code.

Viewing the Available Budget While Creating a Purchase Order 

See the How to Get Here (on page 172) topic for a list of ways to access this area. 

To check the available budget as you create a purchase order, click the Spend control button on 

the Purchase order information page. The Available budget page opens based on the Line entry 

type you selected in the purchase order: 

• 
If you selected Standard line items for the purchase order, then the page displays the 

monthly and year-to-date budget and spending amounts on the Month and Year to date 

tabs, respectively. 

• 
If you selected Job cost line items for the purchase order, then the page displays the job 

cost budget and spending amounts. 

If the project is over budget, then the number in the Remaining column is red and appears in 
parentheses. 

Fields 

The Available budget page is accessible from purchase orders, A/P invoices, and subcontracts. 

The fields that appear in the list vary depending on the type of transaction that the Available 

budget page is opened from, and the Line entry type associated with the transaction.

invoice.

Transaction Status Definitions 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Spend Management > All > Workbench`


The Spend management workbench page allows you to search for, view, delete, and act on 

transactions, including A/P invoices, purchase orders, service contracts, and subcontracts. 

Each transaction has its own set of status and definitions. 

A/P Invoices Statuses 

The following is a list of statuses for A/P Invoices. 

• 
Aged Payable: This invoice has been created, but is unpaid and has passed the due date. 

• 
Declined: The invoice was declined and closed. 

• 
Draft: The invoice has been created, but has not yet been submitted or posted. 

• 
Escheated: The invoice is transferred to the state. 

• 
Paid: The invoice has been fully paid. 

• 
Partially Approved: The invoice has been approved by at least one reviewer, but has not 

completed journeying through the approval queue. Click the link to review the invoice’s 

approval history. 

• 
Partially Paid: The invoice has been partially paid. 

• 
Posted: The invoice has been posted to the general ledger. 

• 
Reversal: The invoice is created when you reverse a transaction, which causes the balance to 

zero out. 

• 
Reversed: The invoice was reversed by a second transaction, which essentially zeroed out 

the balance in the G/L. Your company retains a record of the reversed invoice and the 

reversal transaction for audit trail purposes. 

• 
Selected: The invoice has been selected for payment, but has not yet been submitted. 

---


<!-- Page 190 -->
Workbenches 

RealPage® Financial Suite Spend Management User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

• 
Submitted: The invoice has been created and submitted for approval. Click the link to 

review the invoice’s approval history. 

Purchase Orders Statuses 

The following is a list of statuses for Purchase Orders. 

• 
Approved: The purchase order is approved. 

• 
Canceled: The purchase order is canceled. 

• 
Closed: The purchase order was closed and marked as complete. 

• 
Declined: The purchase order was declined and closed. 

• 
Draft: The purchase order has been created, but has not yet been submitted or posted. 

• 
Partial Invoice Match: The purchase order matched a partial invoice. 

• 
Partially Approved: The purchase order has been approved by at least one reviewer, but has 

not completed journeying through the approval queue. Click the link to review the purchase 

order’s approval history. 

• 
Partially Received: The purchase order has been partially received. 

• 
Received: The purchase order has been selected for payment, but has not yet been 

submitted. 

• 
Submitted: The purchase order has been created and submitted for approval. Click the link 

to review the purchase order’s approval history. 

Service Contracts Statuses 

The following is a list of statuses for Service Contracts. 

• 
Approved: The service contract is approved. 

• 
Canceled: The service contract is canceled. 

• 
Closed: The service contract was closed and marked as complete. 

• 
Declined: The service contract was declined and closed. 

• 
Partially Approved: The service contract has been approved by at least one reviewer, but 

has not completed journeying through the approval queue. Click the link to review the 

service contract’s approval history. 

• 
Submitted: The service contract has been created and submitted for approval. Click the link 

to review the service contract’s approval history. 

Subcontracts Statuses 

The following is a list of statuses for Subcontracts. 

• 
Approved: The subcontract is approved. 

• 
Canceled: The subcontract is canceled. 

• 
Closed: The subcontract was closed and marked as complete. 

• 
Declined: The subcontract was declined and closed.

*Source: `RP Financial Suite Spend Management User Guide.pdf`, Page 193*

Chapter 3: Workbenches

RealPage® Financial Suite Spend Management User Guide 

1. 
From the Spend management workbench page, find the purchase order for which you want 

to log receipt of goods, and then click the Receive link next to the transaction. The Receipt 

of goods page loads for the purchase order. 

2. 
For each line item received, click in the Qty rec’d field, and type the number of items 

received. 

3. 
Click Save. The Spend management workbench page loads with the purchase order 

displayed as follows: 

• 
If all goods on the purchase order are received, the purchase order appears with a 

Received status, and the Create invoice option is available. Also, the Received amount 

reflects the Total amount of the purchase order and the Open amount is 0.00. 

• 
If only some of the goods on the purchase order are received, the purchase order 

appears with a Partially Received status, and the Create invoice option is available. 

Also, the Received amount reflects the total amount of received goods, and the Open 

amount reflects the Total amount of the purchase order minus the Received amount. 

After you log received goods for a purchase order, you can create an A/P invoice. To create an 

invoice for the received goods, see Creating an A/P Invoice for a Transaction (on page 181). 

Creating an A/P Invoice for a Transaction 

To create an A/P invoice for a transaction: 

1. 
From the Spend management workbench page, click the Create invoice link next to the 

transaction for which you want to create an invoice. The A/P invoice page opens with 

information from the matched order included. 

The Create Invoice link in the Actions column is specific to the Purchase Order and 

Subcontract transactions. See Workbench List Fields (on page 182) for more information 
about the different actions you can take for each type of transaction. 

2. 
Complete the required fields for the A/P invoice, including the Date, Total invoice amount, 

Invoice number, and Due date. See A/P invoice Fields (on page 278) for more information. 

3. 
Click the 
 drop-down list next to the Submit & new button, and then select Submit. The 

system creates the A/P invoice and loads the Spend management workbench page. 

Paying an A/P Invoice for a Transaction (Workbench) 

To pay an A/P invoice for a transaction: 

1. 
From the Spend management workbench page, click the View link next to the A/P invoice 

you want to pay. The A/P invoices page loads. 

The Pay button is available only if the status of the A/P Invoice is Posted or Partially Paid. 

2. 
See Paying an A/P Invoice (on page 254) for more information.

Approval Workbench - View All 

Before You Begin 

Access can vary depending on your organization’s subscriptions and your permissions. If you do 

not see the option in the menu, then ask your System Administrator to check your permissions. 

Subscriptions 

Your company must subscribe to the Company application and at least one of the following 

applications. Choose the appropriate application for the type of approval workflow that you need. 

• 
Accounts Payable: Subscribe to the Accounts Payable application to use the approval 

process with A/P invoices, A/P payments, and expense reports. Approvals of new and 

changed vendors also requires you to subscribe to the Accounts Payable application. 

• 
Spend Management: Subscribe to the Spend Management application to use the approval 

process with purchase orders, service contracts, and subcontracts. 

• 
General Ledger: Subscribe to the General Ledger application to use the approval process 

with journal entries. 

• 
Job Cost & Reserves: Subscribe to the Job Cost & Reserves application to use the approval 

process with job cost change orders.

Filtering Transactions in the Approval Workbench 

See the How to Get Here topic (on page 104) for a list of ways to access the Approval workbench. 

The filter options on the Approval workbench page change depending on the transaction type 

you select. 

To filter the approval queue: 

1. 
Select the transaction type: 

• 
A/P invoice 

• 
Purchase order 

• 
Service contract 

• 
Subcontract 

• 
Job cost change order 

• 
Journal entry 

• 
A/P payment 

• 
Expense report 

2. 
Select additional filter criteria as needed. See the section below that corresponds with your 

transaction type for a list of available filter options. 

3. 
If you want to hide declined transactions from the list so you can edit and resubmit them, 

select the Included declined check box.  

By default, declined transactions are not included in the workbench. If you want to include 
them by default, then create a custom workbench view (on page 113) with the Include 

declined option selected and save it as the Default view. 

4. 
Click the Apply button. 

The approval queue refreshes with a list of transactions that meet the selected criteria. 

The system retains your filter selections even if you switch to a different transaction type 
in the workbench. To clear and reset filters, click the Clear button.

Approving and Declining Transactions 

See the How to Get Here (on page 104) topic for a list of ways to access the Approval workbench.  

This page has two views, View All and My Approvals. You must be in the Approval Workbench - 

My Approvals view to approve and decline transactions. If you are on the Approvals Workbench 

- View All view, click the My Approvals button to change to the My Approvals view.  

From the My Approvals view, you can approve or decline transactions individually or in bulk. If 

you are reviewing A/P invoices, then you can use the Review and approve button to quickly 

approve or decline invoices back-to-back (on page 112). 

When you approve a transaction, the system looks up the next approver. If the next approver 
previously approved the transaction, then the system sets the status of the transaction to 
Approved.

The Approve [transaction type] box opens.

3. 
Click the Approve button.

Reviewing and Approving A/P Invoices 

See the How to Get Here (on page 104) topic for a list of ways to access this area. 

When the Approval workbench is filtered by A/P invoices, an additional button appears in the 

upper-right corner labeled Review & approve. This button allows you to quickly open and review 

invoices in the order they appear in the approval queue.  

To review and approve A/P invoices: 

1. 
From the Applications menu, select Company, and then select the All tab. 

2. 
Select Approval workbench. 

3. 
Select the A/P invoice option. Set any other filters as needed. 

4. 
Click the Apply button. The system filters the list so that it shows only A/P invoices. 

5. 
Click the Review & approve button. The A/P invoice page opens. If the A/P invoice has an 

attachment and you have enabled the image viewer, the attachment displays in a separate 

window. If not, the invoice image will show on the same page as the invoice. 

If the Review & approve button does not appear, there are no A/P invoices in queue to 
approve. 

6. 
Review the A/P invoice. You can also edit the invoice at the same time. 

7. 
Click one of the buttons: 

• 
Approve & next: Approve the current A/P invoice, and then have the system display 

the next A/P invoice to evaluate. If you made any changes to the invoice, your changes 

are saved and the invoice is routed to the next person for approval. 

• 
Approve & next > Next: Skip the current A/P invoice and display the next A/P invoice 

in your queue. Any changes you made to the invoice will not be saved.

When an eInvoice is created in Accounting, goes through approvals, and then gets posted, 
RealPage Accounting sends an update to OpsMerchant to change the partner status from 

Pending to Approved. This ensures that the vendor is aware of the current status of the 
invoice. We also send updates to OpsMerchant when the eInvoice is paid or voided, along 
with the payment details. 

Exporting Transactions to Excel 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > Approvals > Approval Workbench`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Spend Management > All > Workbench`


You can export transaction data from the Approval workbench or Spend management 

workbench to an Excel file. The data included in the file depends on the columns that you have 

enabled in the workbench. 

To export data using the Export to Excel button: 

1. 
Click the Export to Excel button in the upper-right corner of the approval queue. 

The Excel file downloads with any column data configured in the workbench. 

2. 
In the Save as box, name the Excel file, and determine a file location for the exported file. 

3. 
Click Save.

#### Approval History List
*Source: `RP Financial Suite Spend Management User Guide.pdf`, Page 233*

Chapter 3: Workbenches 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage® Financial Suite Spend Management User Guide 

Approval History List 

See the How to Get Here (on page 137) topic for a list of ways to access this area. 

Use this page to review a transaction’s approval history. This page displays when you click a status 

in the Approval workbench. 

When you enable approvals for a transaction type, RealPage Financial Suite auto-generates a 
default policy and a default workflow for routing transactions of this type to the user (or role) 
you have set as the default approver (on page 52). Default policies and workflows are visible 
only to admin users, including any events or actions logged in the approval history. 

Columns 

• 
Policy type: This column shows the policy type that the system used to approve the item. 

• 
Policy name: This column shows the policy name that the system used to approve the item. 

Click the link to view policy details. 

• 
Workflow name: This column shows the name of the workflow that the system used in the 

transaction. Click the link to view workflow details. 

• 
Approver role/user: This column contains a link to information about the person who 

decided on the approval. Click to view the role assignment details. You can find out who is 

assigned to a particular role with this link. 

• 
Approved/Declined by: This column contains the user name of the person who made the 

approval decisions. 

• 
Event date: This column contains the date that the transaction last underwent an approval 

event. (It was submitted for approval or partially approved.) 

• 
Comments: This column contains the comments the approver made along with his decision. 

• 
State: This column contains the status of the approval. 

• 
Action type: This column contains the approval status of the transaction. 

• 
Action comments: This column contains the comments associated with the action in the 

state. 

• 
Submitted by: This column contains the name of the user who submitted the transaction. 

“Console member” appears when the user accesses RealPage Financial Suite through the 
console rather than by logging in directly.

##### Viewing Approval Policy Details from Approval History

How to Get Here 

These are the most direct options for accessing the Approval history list. You may have additional 

options to access the workbench, depending on your permissions. 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > Approval Workbench > (Status)`


1. 
In the Applications menu, select the Company application, and then click the All tab. 

2. 
In the Approvals section, select the Approval workbench option. 

3. 
In the approval queue, find the desired transaction, and then click the link in the Status 

column. 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > All > Approval Workbench > (Status)`


1. 
In the Applications menu, select Accounts Payable, and then click the All tab. 

2. 
Select the Approval workbench option. 

3. 
In the approval queue, find the desired transaction, and then click the link in the Status 

column. 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Spend Management > All > Approval Workbench > (Status)`


1. 
In the Applications menu, select Spend Management, and then click the All tab. 

2. 
Select the Approval workbench option. 

3. 
In the approval queue, find the desired transaction, and then click the link in the Status 

column. 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Spend Management > Setup > Approvals > Approval Workbench > 
(Status)`


1. 
In the Applications menu, select Spend Management, and then click the Setup tab. 

2. 
In the Approvals section, select the Approval workbench option. 

3. 
In the approval queue, find the desired transaction, and then click the link in the Status 

column.

You can view the details of an approval policy that was used to decide on a transaction.

Apply filters (on page 105) to the workbench so that the desired transaction appears in the 

list.

Performance Dashboard Features 

The performance dashboard is a central location that allows you to: 

• 
View your spending by each category per quarter. 

• 
View your spending as a percentage based on the number of each type of invoice per 

quarter. 

• 
View the number of invoices and orders that are open more than 30 days per quarter. 

• 
View the average time for a transaction to be approved from the date it was submitted. 

• 
View the number of purchase orders that are compliant and non-compliant per quarter. 

• 
View the number of manual invoices for online vendors and offline orders for catalog 

vendors per quarter. 

• 
View the vendor metrics, the number of each type of vendor, per market channel. 

Viewing the Performance Dashboard 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Spend Management > Performance Dashboard`


The Performance dashboard page allows you to view multiple performance metrics in one 

location.

<!-- Page 241 -->
Chapter 4: Performance Dashboards

a) Spend by category: Displays all categories for catalog vendors and the amount spent on 

that category each quarter. 

b) Spend % by invoice type: Displays the number of each type of invoices each quarter as a 

percentage. 

c) Aging items: Displays invoices and purchase orders that are open for more than 30 days per 

quarter. 

d) Workflow cycle time: Displays the average time it takes a transaction to be approved from 

the date it is submitted. 

e) Purchase order compliance: Displays compliant and non-compliant purchase orders. 

Compliant indicates that the purchase order created date is before the invoice created 
date. 

f) 
Spend compliance: Displays the number of manual invoices for online vendors or the 

number of offline orders for catalog vendors. 

g) Vendor metrics: Displays the number of each type of vendor, total number of vendors, and 

marketing channels.

A/P Invoice Overview 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > All > A/P Invoices`


Managing A/P invoices includes adding, editing, and deleting A/P invoices received from vendors. 

The most important information appears at the top of the A/P invoice page for quick and easy 

access. For example, you can quickly scan to find the A/P invoice date, A/P invoice total, amount 

paid, and amount due. These fields change depending on the status of your A/P invoice. For 

example, if your payment is overdue then the banner includes the Overdue field that shows 

number of days that it is overdue in red text. 

You can pay an A/P invoice directly from the page when you are editing or viewing a posted A/P 

invoice. When the A/P invoice is partially or fully paid, you can click the link to view payment 

details. 

You can use the Ledger Sentry to set up a past due threshold. When an A/P invoice reaches the 

threshold, the system can send the user an email. Set up the threshold in the Ledger Sentry 

(Company > Ledger Sentry). 

Not ready to post or pay an A/P invoice? You can save it in draft format and post or pay it later.

Select the Show future draft invoices check box to filter the list so that future draft 
invoices are included in the list.  

Customizing the List 

You can add more columns to the list, like Payment method and Payment number, by creating a 

custom view. Use the list controls to create custom views and filter and sort the list. See 

Managing the List (on page 611) for details. 

Additional Options 

Some additional options are available in this list that may or may not appear in the example. 

• 
After selecting the invoice or invoices to include in a package, click one of the following 

buttons: Generate Package or Show Only Selected Invoices. The Generate Package button 

will generate an invoice package containing the invoices that are selected from the A/P 

Invoices list. The Show Only Selected Invoices button lists only the A/P invoices that are 

selected. Click the Cancel Package button to clear all selections. 

• 
Transaction types: Invoices that appear in this list can come from RealPage Accounting or 

from other sources. When invoices are generated in other parts of the system, they are 

called eInvoices (on page 708), or oInvoices (on page 712). eInvoices come from Storefront, 

and oInvoices come from Full Service. When Full Service’s Invoice Processing process 

creates an A/P invoice record, the process inserts the account number in the oInvoice’s 

Reference number field. 

Management Fees 

Management fees are billed with recurring invoices. To create a fee, create a recurring A/P invoice 

and then create an A/R invoice to bill the site back for the fee. Fees work differently than 

intercompany billing. For fees, the A/R liability isn’t relieved. Instead, the A/R invoice stays open 

until you apply a payment against the fee’s invoice.  

Utility Invoices 

When your company subscribes to the RealPage Utility Management (UM) application, RealPage 

offers a feature that prevents customers from paying UM invoices, as the UM application makes

the utility payments on customers’ behalf. These invoices are only hidden for customers for whom 

RUM makes payments. 

When the feature is enabled, the UM invoices do not appear on the Pay A/P invoices page, and 

the UM invoices do not have a Pay option when they appear in the A/P invoices list.  

Contact RealPage Support to enable this feature. 

Distributions 

Investor distributions appear in the A/P invoices list with a Transaction Type of “Distribution.” 

Invoices List in a Multi-entity Company 

In multi-entity companies, transaction lists at the entity level include transactions created at the 

top level that have been tagged to your entity. However, if no transactions have been posted in 

the last six months that fit the criteria, then entity-level transaction lists only include entity-level 

transactions. 

If you want to see older transactions created at the top level for your entity, then select the 

Include top level transactions check box at the top of your list. 

For Multi-entity Shared Companies with Multiple Base Currencies 

For invoices at the top level, you must select the base currency and transaction currency, and the 

location, so the system can determine the appropriate currency. For invoices at the entity level, 

you need to select only the transaction currency.

Importing an A/P Invoice 

You can import CSV files of invoices into Spend Management. For more information, see 

Importing Data into RealPage Accounting. 

To import historical invoices, make sure to select the Historical option in step 5. 

To import an A/P invoice: 

1. 
On the A/P invoices list page, click Import. The Import box opens. 

2. 
Click the Choose file button, and then select a CSV file of the invoice to import. 

3. 
Select a date format from the Date format drop-down list. 

4. 
Select a file encoding option from the File encoding drop-down list. 

5. 
Choose whether to post the invoice to the General Ledger or create a Historical import. 

• 
If you select Historical as the import mode, you can select the Process Offline check 

box. This is useful when your import file is large. 

Historical imports do not post to the General Ledger. 

6. 
Type your email address in the Email results to this address field. 

7. 
Click the Import button. The system imports the file. 

Deleting an A/P Invoice 

Only users with Delete permissions may delete an A/P invoice. The option to delete A/P invoices 

(including drafts) is unavailable if your Accounts Payable application is configured to allow the 

reversal of unpaid invoices. 

To delete an A/P invoice: 

1. 
Select the Delete check box next to the invoice you want to delete. 

2. 
Click the Delete button. 

3. 
Click the OK button. The system deletes the invoice.

#### Packaging Invoices
*Source: `RP Financial Suite Spend Management User Guide.pdf`, Page 269*

Chapter 5: A/P Invoices 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage® Financial Suite Spend Management User Guide 

Packaging Invoices 

This section describes how to create a package of invoices. You can create a package of A/P or 

A/R invoices. 

Use this feature when you need to provide a set of invoices to another party. Many customers use 

this feature to create a package of invoices for stakeholders. Customers who do not own the Job 

Cost and Reserves application can use the packaging feature to collect a set of invoices for the 

draw request document bundle, which they then submit to the lender as a request to release 

funds. 

When you generate the package, you can specify the components that you want to include in the 

package: 

• 
Cover page: Include a cover page and either use the system default cover page or import a 

custom cover page. 

• 
Summary: This is a list of the invoices in the package. 

• 
Attachments: Include the attachments of the invoices in the package. 

• 
Printed invoice: For A/R invoice packages, you can include the A/R invoices in printable 

format. 

• 
Printed AP invoice: For A/P invoice packages, you can include the A/P invoices in printable 

format. 

• 
Payment information: For A/P invoice packages, you can include additional payment 

information. 

• 
Proof of payment: For A/P invoice packages, you can include the proof of payment 

information when it is available. 

• 
Include separator pages: You can choose to include or exclude pages between the invoices. 

The separator page contains this text “The following invoices are included in this package:” 

and it lists the invoices in the package with these details: vendor name, invoice number, 

invoice date, amount of the payment, payment method, payment number, and the number 

of documents associated with the invoice.  

Packaging the invoices does not change the status of the invoices or their presence in the 
invoices list. 

If you are packaging A/P invoices, you have the choice of saving the package of invoices in a ZIP 

file or a printable PDF file.  

A/R invoice packages are saved as PDF files and open in Adobe Acrobat after the system creates 

the package.  

Regardless of file format, the system saves the package in your browser’s default download 

location.

Moving In and Out of Packaging Invoices Mode 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > All > A/P Invoices > Package Invoices`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Receivable > All > A/R Invoices > Package Invoices`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Spend Management > All > Workbench > A/P Invoices > Package 
Invoices`


When you click the Package Invoices button, you enter into Packaging mode. If you choose 

another option from the menu and then return to invoices, the system displays the Package 

Invoices list, not the Invoices list. In other words, the invoices list will still be in Packaging mode. 

To return to the invoices list from the Package Invoices list, you can either generate the package 

or cancel the package. 

• 
When you generate a package, the system builds the package and saves it where your 

browser saves downloaded files, and then returns to the Invoices list. 

• 
You can cancel the current package, which leaves Packaging mode and returns to the 

invoice. 

Creating A/P Invoice Packages 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > All > A/P Invoices > Package Invoices`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Spend Management > All > Workbench > A/P Invoices > Package 
Invoices`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > All > Invoice Research > (search) > Package Invoices`


Use the Package invoices button when you want to bundle a set of invoices. You can package 

invoices from the A/P invoices list or from the Spend Management workbench. 

To create an invoice package: 

1. 
Click the Package invoices button. The page name changes to reflect that it has entered 

packaging mode. 

2. 
Filter the list so that the invoices that you want to package are displayed in the list. 

For example, you can use the A/P invoice list’s filters (on page 613) to help you find the 

invoices to include in the package. Each box above the column is a filter. Enter the text that 

you want to find in a column to find matching A/P invoices. You can also apply a custom 

view that you previously saved to get a list of A/P invoices that you want to package.  

Likewise, on the workbench, you can use the workbench controls to filter the list of invoices. 

For example, the column control lets you filter the data in the column. Click the Clear button 

to reset filters, including the column filters. 

3. 
Select the invoices to include in the package. 

---


<!-- Page 271 -->
Chapter 5: A/P Invoices 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage® Financial Suite Spend Management User Guide 

After you select at least one invoice, check boxes appear to the left of the Edit links in the 

list, and three buttons appear: 

• 
Show Only Selected Invoices 

• 
Generate Package 

• 
Cancel Package 

While in packaging mode, you can also create new A/P invoices. If your company uses the 
approval workflow, then the system sends the new A/P invoice through the approval 
process before you can include it in the package. You must also go through the process of 
posting and paying the invoice before it can be included in an A/P invoice package. 

Showing Only Selected Invoices 

• 
Click the Show Only Selected Invoices button to remove unselected A/P invoices from the 

list so that you see only the invoices that will be included in the package. This action cannot 

be undone. If you accidentally exclude an A/P invoice, you must cancel the package and 

start over. 

Generating the Package 

1. 
Click the Generate Package button to open the Generate Invoice Package box. 

2. 
In the Package Option drop-down list, select the type of package that you want to create, 

Document (PDF) or Compressed (Zip). 

3. 
Finalize the package by selecting what to include in the package in addition to the invoices. 

You can choose to include: 

• 
Cover page: Select this check box, and then click the Browse button to find and select 

the cover page that you want to use. 

• 
Summary: Select this check box to include a summarized list of invoices in the 

package. 

• 
Attachments: Select this check box to include any attachments that the invoice records 

might have in the package. 

• 
Printed A/P invoice: Select this check box to include a printable version of the invoice. 

• 
Payment information: Select this check box to include additional payment information 

in the package. 

• 
Proof of payment: Select this check box to include proofs of payment when they are 

available. 

• 
Include separator pages: Select this check box if you want the system to include a 

separator page between each invoice. The separator page contains this text “The 

document(s) that follow are for:” and then lists the details about the invoice that 

follows, including Vendor ID, Vendor Name, Invoice Number, Invoice Date, and Invoice 

Amount.

Downloading the A/P Invoice Template 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > Import data`


Templates are used for importing data into the system. Each type of data has a unique template 

designed for that data object. When your system was set up, RealPage worked with your 

company to design each template so that the import of data includes all of the fields that your 

company wants uploaded when importing. 

The purpose of downloading a template is so that you can fill the template with the data that you 

want to import into the system. For example, if you want to import A/P invoice data, then you 

download the A/P invoice template, fill it with data, and them import the A/P invoice template. 

If your goal is to create one invoice and reuse it as the starting point for additional invoices, use 
the Duplicate function instead of a template. 

To find and download the template for A/P invoice data: 

1. 
Open the Company menu. 

2. 
Click Import data. 

3. 
Find the Set Up AP Master List, Open Invoices and Adjustments section. 

4. 
Find the Accounts Payable Invoices row, and then select the Template link. A prompt opens 

at the bottom of the browser page asking if you want to Open, Save, or Cancel.

Filling In the Template 

To fill in the A/P invoice template: 

1. 
Open the template in Excel and review the data structure. This information can help you 

formulate extraction queries from your data source. 

2. 
Export the data from your other system.

template’s data structure exactly as you do this. 

Avoid using leading zeros in ID fields. If you must use leading zeros in IDs, convert the 
column of ID numbers to text format in Excel before importing the file content. Excel does 
not remove the leading zeros when you save the file. Remember to do this every time you 
use a template to import information that requires IDs.

Click the Save button.

When you have trouble opening a PDF file, try the following: 

•

Using the Match Order Page 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > All > A/P Invoices > Edit > Match Order`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Spend Management > All > Workbench > A/P Invoices > Match Order`


The Match order page lists all of the open transaction orders for the selected vendor and 

property. Use the Match order page to select transaction line items to match to the A/P invoice. 

The Match order page has four sections: 

a) (Transaction): This field lists the type of transactions that are open for the invoice’s vendor. 

b) Invoice details: This section contains the transaction line item to match. 

c) Order: This section contains a list of transactions associated with this vendor and property. 

When populated, a View details link is activated. Click this link to see a list of its line items. 

---


<!-- Page 286 -->
A/P Invoices 

RealPage® Financial Suite Spend Management User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

d) Transaction details: This section contains a list of line items of the selected transaction. Click 

the Order# link to view and review the order. Select the check box of the line items in the 

transaction to have the system match them to the items in the invoice, and then click Apply. 

To match an invoice when adding a transaction: 

1. 
From the transaction page, click the Match order button when it is activated. The Match 

order page opens. 

By default, the system shows the next service order in the current month. Any service 
orders not matched from the previous month display as well. Match the A/P invoices with 
purchase orders created by Spend Management before saving and posting them. When 
you match line items, the G/L account on the purchase order overrides the invoice’s G/L 
account. This is true for all three types of invoices: A/P Invoices, oInvoices, and eInvoices. 

2. 
From the drop-down list at the top of the Match order page, select the type of transaction 

that you want to match, purchase orders, service contracts, or subcontracts. 

3. 
Select one or more transaction line items in the order to match them to the invoice. View 

the details of the transaction and select the line item(s) in the corresponding transaction 

section. 

• 
You can also select the top check box in the Select column to select all transactions. 

• 
If the item is a purchase order, the order number and the SKU number appear in the 

invoice’s line item. 

• 
If the item is a subcontract or service order, the item number and item description 

appear in the invoice’s line item. 

Multiple transaction line items can be added to an order and vice versa to improve 
matching functionality. Two frequent scenarios are an invoice with one line item that can 
be matched to multiple lines of a purchase or service orders and an invoice with multiple 
line items that can be matched to a single line of a purchase or service order. The selected 
quantity on both the invoice and the order should match. 

4. 
Select the Include future service orders check box to view or match to a service order from 

a future month. 

---

To match a partial quantity of a transaction: 

If the Receipt of Goods function is not enabled in Spend Management, then when an invoice 

contains and matches a partial quantity, the transaction partially matches the quantity and 

remains open to match the remaining quantity. This changes the transaction’s status to Partial 

Invoice Match. Then if an online invoice is created for only the amount received, the automatic 

matching function will take into consideration that the quantity of the invoice matches the 

quantity of the transaction.

##### Editing an A/P Invoice
*Source: `RP Financial Suite Spend Management User Guide.pdf`, Page 297*

Chapter 5: A/P Invoices 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage® Financial Suite Spend Management User Guide 

Apply Template 

Apply 
Applies the allocation template to the A/P invoice 

Save Template 

Save 
Saves the allocation template from the invoice for future use 

Editing an A/P Invoice 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Spend Management > All > Workbench > A/P Invoice > Edit`


To edit an A/P invoice: 

1. 
From either the Spend management workbench page or the A/P invoices list page, click 

the Edit link next to the A/P invoice you want to edit. The A/P invoice page opens. 

2. 
From the Top section of the A/P Invoice page, make changes in the fields as needed. See 

Fields (on page 278) for more information. 

3. 
Click the Match Order button to match any orders to the A/P invoice. The Match Order box 

opens. See Using the Match Order Box (on page 273) for more information. 

When editing an A/P invoice, a list of orders in the Match Order box shows only the orders 
for the location defined in the invoice. Therefore, it is no longer necessary to select the 
invoice line items individually. When you edit an A/P invoice and match it to an order, the 
line item amount of the A/P invoice must equal the line item amount of the order. When 
tolerance rules are enabled in Spend Management configuration and you edit an A/P 
invoice, the system compares the total original A/P invoice amount to the total of items 
matched to determine if it is within the range. Additionally, if the Receipt of Goods 
function is enabled, when you edit an A/P invoice, the system allows you to update the 

QTY field in the Match Order box when matching the invoice to the purchase order. 

4. 
In the Term section of the A/P Invoice page, make changes in the fields as needed. See 

Fields (on page 278) for more information. 

---


<!-- Page 298 -->
A/P Invoices 

RealPage® Financial Suite Spend Management User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

5. 
Click the Spend control button to view the monthly and year-to-date available budget for 

the vendor and property on the A/P invoice. See Available Budget box (on page 171) for 

more information. 

• 
In the Term section of the A/P Invoice page, if the Line entry type field shows Job 

Cost or Both, the Available Budget box will include the Job Cost tab, which displays 

the budget for the cost codes defined. See Available Budget box (on page 171) for 

more information. 

6. 
Click the Apply template button to apply an allocation when editing an A/P invoice. The 

Apply Template box is displayed. 

This causes all line item entries to inherit the defined allocation. 

• 
Select the allocation template to use from the Template drop-down list. 

If an allocation template is not listed, click Find to search for the template and apply 
it. 

• 
Type an amount in the Amount field. 

• 
Select the G/L account to use from the G/L account drop-down list. 

• 
Click the Apply button. 

7. 
Click the Save template button to add a new allocation template when editing an A/P 

invoice. The Save Template box is displayed. 

• 
Type a name for the new allocation template in the Name field. 

• 
Optionally, enter a description of the allocation template in the Description (optional) 

field. 

• 
Select the type of allocation template to use from the TemplateType drop-down list. 

• 
Optionally, type any additional information you want to include in the Memo 

(optional) field. 

---


<!-- Page 299 -->
Chapter 5: A/P Invoices 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage® Financial Suite Spend Management User Guide 

• 
Click the Save button. 

8. 
Click the Asset button on each line item entry as needed to open the Asset Entry box. 

Complete the asset information. 

• 
Click Save to submit any changes made and return to the previous page. 

• 
Click Close to close the Asset Entry box without saving any changes and return to the 

previous page. 

9. 
Complete the Tax amount, Shipping amount, and Discount amount fields, if applicable, 

and then click the Distribute button. This applies the amounts in these fields to each line 

item in the table. 

10. 
Type in any notes about the invoice in the Notes field. 

11. 
Click the Post button. The system saves changes and posts the A/P invoice. 

• 
Alternatively, click the Duplicate button to save changes and open a new duplicate 

invoice. 

• 
Click the Print button to print the invoice. 

• 
Click the Cancel button to cancel the changes and return to the AP Invoice page.

##### Sending a Message Regarding an A/P Invoice
*Source: `RP Financial Suite Spend Management User Guide.pdf`, Page 300*

A/P Invoices 

RealPage® Financial Suite Spend Management User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Sending a Message Regarding an A/P Invoice 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > All > A/P Invoices > Edit > Messaging`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > All > Invoice Research > (search) > Edit > Messaging`


You can send a message about an A/P invoice to other system users, to external users, and to 

vendors. To send the message to the vendor, the vendor’s email address must be defined in the 

Vendor record. 

To send an email message regarding an A/P invoice: 

1. 
Open the Accounts Payable menu. 

2. 
Select either A/P Invoices or Invoice Research. 

3. 
Click the Edit link next to the A/P invoice you want to discuss. The A/P invoice information 

page opens. 

4. 
Click the Messaging tab. 

5. 
Choose who will receive the message: 

• 
To send the message to someone who has an account in the system, click the To 

drop-down list, and then select the desired user.  

If the vendor record does not have an email address defined, then the system does 
not send the email. You can either edit the vendor record, add an email address to it, 
and then try again, or type the vendor’s email address in the External user email 
field. 

• 
To send the message to someone who does not have an account in the system, type 

the person’s email address in the External user email field.  

• 
To send emails to multiple addresses, type the addresses in the External user email 

field and separate email addresses with a comma. Do not add spaces between email 

addresses. 

6. 
Type the message in the Message text field. 

7. 
Add attachments: 

• 
To add the invoice as an attachment, select the Include Invoice as Attachment check 

box. 

• 
To add an attachment other than the invoice, select the attachment from the 

Attachments drop-down list. 

8. 
Click the Send button. The system sends the message and records it in the Chat history 

table. 

---

3.

• 
If all goods on the purchase order have been received, the purchase order appears

amount reflects the Total amount of the purchase order and the Open amount is 

0.00. 

• 
If only some of the goods on the purchase order have been received, the purchase 

order appears with a Partially Received status, and the Create invoice option is 

available. Also, the Received amount reflects the total amount of received goods, and 

the Open amount reflects the Total amount of the purchase order minus the 

Received amount. 

After a purchase order has been partially or fully received, you cannot delete it, even if the 
purchase order has not been matched to any invoices yet. 

After you log received goods for a purchase order, you can create an A/P invoice. To create an 

invoice for the received goods, see Creating an Invoice from a Purchase Order (on page 303).

Packaging Purchase Orders 

This section describes how to create a package of purchase orders. 

Use this feature when you need to provide a set of purchase orders to another party. Many 

customers use this feature to create a package of purchase orders for stakeholders. Customers 

who do not own the Job Cost and Reserves application can use the packaging feature to collect a 

set of purchase orders for the draw request document bundle, which they then submit to the 

lender as a request to release funds. 

When you generate the package, you can specify the components that you want to include in the 

package: 

• 
Cover page: Include a cover page and either use the system default cover page or import a 

custom cover page. 

• 
Summary: This is a list of the purchase orders in the package. 

• 
Include AP attachments: Include the attachments of the purchase orders in the package. 

• 
Include PO attachments: Include the attachments of the purchase orders in the package. 

• 
Include alternative bids: For purchase order packages, you can include alternative bids 

information. 

• 
Proof of payment (if available): For purchase order packages, you can include the proof of 

payment information when it is available. 

• 
Approval workflow: For purchase order packages, you can include the approval workflow. 

Packaging the purchase orders does not change the status of the purchase orders or their 
presence in the purchase orders list. 

Generating the package results in a PDF file with the information that you selected. The system 

saves the package in PDF format in your browser’s default download location. 

Creating Purchase Orders Packages 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > All > A/P Invoices > Package Invoices`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Spend Management > All > Workbench > Package Invoices`


Use the Package purchase orders button when you want to bundle a set of purchase orders. You 

can package purchase orders from the Purchase Orders list page or from the Spend 

Management workbench. 

To create a purchase order package: 

1. 
Click the Package purchase orders button. The page name changes to reflect that it has 

entered packaging mode. 

2. 
Filter the list so that the purchase orders that you want to package are displayed in the list. 

---


<!-- Page 320 -->
Purchase Orders 

RealPage® Financial Suite Spend Management User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

3. 
Select the purchase orders to include in the package. 

After you select at least one purchase order, the following three buttons appear: 

• 
Show Only Selected Purchase Orders 

• 
Generate Package 

• 
Cancel Package 

While in packaging mode, you can also create new purchase orders. If your company uses 
the approval workflow, then the system sends the new purchase order through the 
approval process before you can include in the package. You must also go through the 
process of posting and paying the invoice before it can be included in a Purchase Order 
package. 

Showing Only Selected Purchase Orders 

• 
Click the Show Only Selected Purchase Orders button to remove unselected purchase 

orders from the list so that you see only the purchase orders that will be included in the 

package. This action cannot be undone. If you accidentally exclude a purchase order, you 

must cancel the package and start over. 

Generating the Package 

• 
Opens the Generate Purchase Orders Package box where you finalize the package by 

selecting what to include in the package in addition to the purchase orders. You can choose 

to include a cover page, summary, attachments, alternative bids, approval workflow, and 

proofs of payment. After selecting the desired options, click the Build package button to 

create the package. 

Canceling the Package 

• 
Click the Cancel package button to discard the package and return to the Purchase Orders 

list page or Spend Management workbench. 

---

message appears.

Adding a New Purchase Order 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Spend Management > All > Workbench > Purchase Order > Add`


Use the Purchase order information page to add a new purchase order. To create a new purchase 

order, complete the following required fields. See Fields (on page 322) for more information 

about the additional fields on this page. 

1. 
Click the 
 Calendar button in the Date field, and then select the date of the purchase 

order. 

2. 
Click the 
 Calendar button in the Encumbrance date field, and then select the date of 

the encumbrance. 

3. 
Select a vendor from the Vendor drop-down list.  

If the vendor is not available in the drop-down list, see Adding a New Vendor (on page 659). 

4. 
Optionally, after you select the vendor, click the Saved items link to view an offline 

shopping list of frequently used items saved for that vendor. See Applying a Saved Item to a 

Purchase Order (on page 322) for more information. 

5. 
If you want to bill to the company address, select the Use company address for bill to 

check box. Otherwise, select the property that is being billed for the purchase from the Bill 

to drop-down list. 

If the purchase order is for a property that is not in the Bill to list, click the Add link at the 

top of the list, and then complete the Contact Information (on page 679) box. 

The Bill to drop-down list is not selectable if you are billing to the company. However, you 
can opt to bill to the company and ship to a property.

Applying a Saved Item to a Purchase Order 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Spend Management > All > Search & Find > 
 Purchase Order > Saved 
Items`


When you create a new purchase order, you can select a vendor for the purchase order and then 

open a list of saved items for that vendor. If any items have been stored for that vendor, then you 

can quickly select them from the list and populate them as line entries in the purchase order.  

To select and apply one or more saved items and then apply them to a purchase order: 

1. 
On the Purchase order information page, click the Saved items link under the Vendor 

drop-down list. 

The Saved items box opens with a list of frequently used items saved for that vendor. 

You must select a vendor for the purchase order before you can access the Saved items 
list. 

2. 
In the Saved items table list, select the Select check box next to the desired item(s), and 

then click the Apply button. 

If you do not see the item that you are looking for in the list, you can add a new saved item 
for that vendor. See Adding a Saved Item (on page 460) for instructions. 

The Saved items box closes and the selected items populate as line entries in the purchase 

order.

##### Editing a Purchase Order
*Source: `RP Financial Suite Spend Management User Guide.pdf`, Page 342*

Purchase Orders 

RealPage® Financial Suite Spend Management User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Editing a Purchase Order 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Spend Management > All > Workbench > Purchase Order > Edit`


You can edit only purchase orders that have a status of Draft, Submitted, Partially Approved, or 

Declined. To update a purchase order that has already been approved, see Adding a Change 

Order for a Purchase Order (on page 302). 

To edit a purchase order: 

1. 
From either the Spend management workbench page or the Purchase orders page, click 

the Edit link next to the purchase order you want to edit. The Purchase order information 

page opens. 

To create an exact duplicate instead of editing the current purchase order, click the 

Duplicate button. 

2. 
If you choose to send a manually entered purchase order directly to an online vendor, select 

the Send purchase order to vendor check box. 

3. 
In the Documents section, click one of the following options: 

• 
Click the Choose file button to open a box, locate a file, and then click Open to add it 

to the purchase order. Click the Attach button to upload it to the purchase order. 

• 
Type a name for the attachment in the File name field, and then click Scan to upload it 

to the purchase order. 

4. 
In the eSign Documents section, view the information of any documents listed. 

5. 
Click the Spend control button to view the monthly and year-to-date available budget for 

the vendor and property on the purchase order. 

6. 
Click the Apply template button to apply an allocation when editing a purchase order. The

Duplicating a Purchase Order 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Spend Management > All > Workbench > Purchase Order > View`


To create a new purchase order based on an existing purchase order: 

1. 
From the Purchase orders page, click the View link next to the purchase order you want to 

duplicate. The Purchase order information page loads for that purchase order. 

2. 
Click the Duplicate button. The Purchase order information page loads with editable fields 

for the new purchase order. 

You can also duplicate a purchase order from the edit page. See Editing a Purchase Order 
(on page 330) for more information. 

3. 
Complete the fields provided. See Fields (on page 322) for more information. 

4. 
After you complete all of the sections, either click the Draft button to save the purchase 

order as a draft or click the Submit button to submit the purchase order for processing. The 

Purchase orders page loads. 

Printing a Purchase Order 

To print a purchase order: 

1. 
From the Purchase order information page, click the Print/email button. The Print/email 

purchase order box opens. 

2. 
Select the Print option. 

3. 
Click the Proceed button. The system opens a PDF file of the purchase order for printing.

Service Contracts and Service Orders 

This chapter features guidance for working with service contracts and associated service orders in Spend 

Management. 

The Service Contracts feature lets you access and manage service contracts and associated service orders. It 

includes several pages that let you: 

• 
View a list of all service contracts 

• 
View detailed information and service orders for specific service contracts 

• 
Add new service contracts and associated service orders 

• 
Edit existing service contracts 

• 
Duplicate service contracts 

• 
Cancel service contracts 

• 
Cancel service orders 

• 
Close service contracts

Service Contracts 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Spend Management > All > Search & Find > Service Contract`


The Service contracts page provides a list of service contracts along with available actions. 

Viewing a Service Contract 

To view a service contract: 

1. 
From the Service Contracts page, find the service contract you want to view. 

2. 
Click the View link next to the service contract. The Service Contract Information (on page 

351) page opens. 

Closing a Service Contract 

To close a service contract: 

• 
From the Service Contracts page, click the Close link next to the service contract you want 

to close. The system closes the service contract and closes all open service orders associated 

with the service contract. 

Any service orders that are matched to an invoice  remain matched to the invoice. 

Canceling a Service Contract 

To cancel a service contract: 

• 
From the Service Contracts page, click the Cancel link next to the service contract you want 

to cancel. The system cancels the service contract and cancels any open service orders for 

which invoices have not been created. 

Viewing a Service Order 

To view a service order: 

1. 
From the Service Contracts page, find the service contract related to the service order you 

want to view. 

2. 
Click the View link next to the service contract. The Service Contract Information page 

opens. 

---

3. 
Click the Detail link next to the related service. The Service Order Details (on page 374) box 

opens. 

4. 
To close the box, click the X button. 

Creating an Invoice for a Service Order 

To create an invoice for a service order: 

1. 
From the Service Contracts page, find the service contract related to the service order you 

want to view. 

2. 
Click the View link next to the service contract. The Service Contract Information page 

opens. 

3. 
Click the Edit button. The Service Contract Information page reloads with editable fields. 

4. 
Click the Detail link next to the related service. The Service Order Details (on page 374) box 

opens. 

5. 
Select the check box next to the service order for which you want to create an invoice. You 

can select multiple orders. 

6. 
Click the Create invoice button. The A/P Invoice page opens with information from the 

service order included. 

7. 
Complete the required fields for the A/P invoice, including the Date field, Total invoice 

amount field, and Due date field. See A/P invoice Fields (on page 278) for more 

information. 

8. 
Click the 
 drop-down list next to the Submit & new button, and then select Submit. The 

system creates the A/P invoice, and the Service Contracts page loads. 

Canceling a Service Order 

You can cancel individual service orders without canceling whole service contracts. For example, a 

landscaping contract is set up for weekly property maintenance and the landscaper skips a week. 

In this example, you would cancel the service order that was generated for that week instead of 

creating an invoice for it. 

To cancel a service order: 

1. 
From the Service Contracts page, find the service contract related to the service order you 

want to view. 

2. 
Click the View link next to the service contract. The Service Contract Information page 

opens. 

3. 
Click the Detail link next to the related service. The Service Order Details (on page 374) box 

opens.

Service Contract Information 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Spend Management > All > Workbench > Service Contract`


Use the Service contract information page to add, edit, and duplicate service contracts. Also use 

this page to access service orders. 

On service contracts with a status of Approved, you can close or cancel service contracts in bulk 

by selecting the check box at the beginning of each row. 

1. 
Select the check box for each service contract to close or cancel. The Close/Cancel button 

appears. 

2. 
When all service contracts are selected, click the Close/Cancel button. A confirmation 

message appears. 

3. 
Click the OK button to confirm the action. 

How to Get Here 

These are the most direct options for accessing the Service Contract Information page. You may 

have additional options based on your permission settings.

Adding a New Service Contract 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Spend Management > All > Workbench > Service Contract > Add`


Use the Service contract information page to add a new service contract.  

To create a new service contract: 

Complete the following required fields (on page 361). 

1. 
Click the 
 Calendar button in the Start date field, and then select the start date of the 

service contract. 

2. 
Click the 
 Calendar button in the End date field, and then select the end date of the 

service contract. 

Type “p” in a date field to automatically insert the last day of the prior month. See 
Specifying Dates in Getting Started for a full list of shortcut keys related to entering dates.  

3. 
Use the Vendor drop-down list to select a vendor. If the vendor is not available in the 

drop-down list, see Adding a New Vendor (on page 659). 

4. 
If you want to send the bill to the company address, select the Use Company Address for 

Bill To check box. 

Otherwise, in the Bill to drop-down list, select the contact who you want to send the bill to. 

If the billing contact is not in the list, you can add a contract record by clicking the Add link 

at the top of the list, and then complete the Contact Information (on page 679) box. 

5. 
Type the total amount of the service contract in the Contract amount field. 

6. 
Type a description of the contracted service in the Description field. 

Working with Attachments 

If your Spend Management configuration requires you to add an attachment, attach a document 

to the service contract using one of the following methods. The method that you use depends on 

whether you have scanning enabled in your preferences. 

Method 1: When you have scanning disabled in your preferences, use the Attachments field to 

add documents to a record. 

When the Attachments field appears, you can attach a file to the record. You can attach a file that 

has already been added to the system or you can upload a file from your computer. You can also 

---


<!-- Page 365 -->
Chapter 7: Service Contracts and Service Orders 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage® Financial Suite Spend Management User Guide 

drag your files from the file explorer into the Attachments box if you are using Firefox, Chrome, 

or Edge web browsers. 

• 
To select a file that is already stored in the system, select the document that you want to 

attach from the Attachments drop-down list. 

• 
To upload a document from your computer, click the Add link in the Attachments 

drop-down list, and then click the Choose Files button. 

• 
Click the Show All/Show unattached link to change the contents of the drop-down list 

between showing all files to showing unattached files. Unattached files are files that are not 

yet attached to any other record in the system. 

• 
To view a document before attaching it, click the document that you want to review, and 

then click the View link. 

• 
To find a document in the system, click the Find link. 

• 
If you are using Firefox, Chrome, or Edge, you can drop your file on the Attachments box to 

attach the file to this record.  

If you have enabled the single scan feature in your preferences, then the Attachments field does 
not appear. Instead, the record has a Documents section where you can attach files. Follow 
method 2 instead. 

Method 2: If you have scanning enabled in your preferences, then you use the Documents section 

to add documents to a record. The Documents section appears in place of the Attachments field 

when you have enabled the single scan feature (on page 641) in your Preferences settings. 

Use the Documents section to store a digital version of a supporting document in this record. You 

can either upload a document from your computer or scan a document if you have a scanner 

attached to your computer. Learn about who can add attachments in Permissions for 

attachments. Learn more about scanning documents (on page 641). 

To upload a document: 

1. 
Click the Choose file button. 

2. 
Locate the document that you want to associate with this record. 

3. 
Select the document and click the Open button. 

4. 
Click the Attach button. 

To scan a document: 

1. 
In the File name field, type a name for the document that you are about to scan.  

2. 
Click the Scan button. 

3. 
In the Select Source box, select the scanner that is attached to your computer. 

4. 
Click the Select button.

Generating Orders and Invoices for Regular Service Contracts 

1.

 Remove button.

On a regular service contract order, each service order is a portion of the total 
amount of the service contract. For example, Fee 1 was entered as $250 with a 
frequency of every 2 weeks. During the time period of the service contract, May 01 –

calculated at one-third of the amount of the service contract, or $83.33.

Service Order Information 

Use the Service Order Information page to view, duplicate, print, and email service orders. 

How to Get Here 

This is the most direct option for accessing the Service Order Information page. You may have 

additional options based on your permission settings. 

Spend Management > Workbench > Service Contract > Transaction Type – Service 
Order > View 

1. 
From the Spend management application, choose Workbench. The Spend management 

workbench page appears. 

2. 
Select Service contract from the transaction options. 

3. 
Select Service order from the Transaction type drop-down list. 

4. 
Select additional filtering criteria if needed, and then click Apply. The service orders load. 

5. 
Click the View link next to the service order you want to view. The Service Order 

Information page for that service order loads. 

Printing a Service Order 

To print a service order: 

1. 
From the Service Order Information page, click Print/Email. The Print/Email Service 

Contract box opens. 

2. 
Select the Print option. 

3. 
Click the Proceed button. The system opens a PDF file of the service order for printing. 

4. 
Print the service order, and then close the PDF file.

by the contract. The Service Contract Frequency box allows you to set the frequency of service 

order line items in service contracts and generate service orders.

Information) > Edit > Frequency`

3.

Service Contract Frequency box opens. 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Spend Management > Spend Management Workbench > View (Service 
Contract Information) > Edit > Frequency`

Contract Information page.

Adding a Change Order for a Subcontract 

To add a change order for a subcontract: 

1. 
From the Subcontracts page, find the subcontract you want to change, and then click the 

Change Order link in the Actions column next to the transaction. The Change subcontract 

page loads. 

2. 
To add a line entry to the table, click the CO link for the item you want to adjust. A new line 

opens with a version number added. 

3. 
Type the ADJUSTMENT to the cost in the Schedule value field. 

In the example below, the change order is to remove $10,000.00 to change the total cost to 

$590,000.00. 

4. 
Optionally, type a brief note regarding the purpose of the change order in the Memo field 

for future reference. 

5. 
Click the Save button. The Subcontracts page loads with the updated purchase order. 

Creating an A/P Invoice for a Subcontract 

To create an invoice from a subcontract: 

1. 
From the Subcontracts page, find the subcontract for which you want to create an invoice, 

and then click the Create invoice link in the Actions column next to the transaction. The A/P 

invoice page loads. 

2. 
Complete the required fields for the A/P invoice, including the Date field, Total invoice 

amount field, and Due date field. See A/P invoice Fields (on page 278) for more 

information. 

3. 
Click the 
 drop-down list next to the Submit & new button, and then select Submit. The 

system creates the A/P invoice, and the Subcontracts page loads.

Packaging Subcontracts 

This section describes how to create a package of subcontracts. 

Use this feature when you need to provide a set of subcontracts to another party. Many 

customers use this feature to create a package of subcontracts for stakeholders. Customers who 

do not own the Job Cost and Reserves application can use the packaging feature to collect a set 

of subcontracts for the draw request document bundle, which they then submit to the lender as a 

request to release funds. 

When you generate the package, you can specify the components that you want to include in the 

package: 

• 
Cover page: Include a cover page and either use the system default cover page or import a 

custom cover page. 

• 
Summary: This is a list of the subcontracts in the package. 

• 
Include AP attachments: Include the attachments of the subcontracts in the package. 

• 
Include PO attachments: Include the attachments of the subcontracts in the package. 

• 
Proof of payment (if available): For subcontracts, you can include the proof of payment 

information when it is available. 

• 
Approval workflow: For subcontracts, you can include the approval workflow. 

Packaging the subcontracts does not change the status of the subcontracts or their presence in 
the subcontracts list. 

Generating the package results in a PDF file with the information that you selected. The system 

saves the package in PDF format in your browser’s default download location. 

Creating Subcontracts Packages 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > All > Subcontracts > Package Subcontracts`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Spend Management > All > Subcontracts > Package Subcontracts`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Spend Management > All > > Workbench > Subcontracts > Package 
Subcontracts`


Use the Package subcontracts button when you want to bundle a set of subcontracts. You can 

package subcontracts from the Subcontracts list page or the Spend management workbench. 

To create a subcontract package: 

1. 
Click the Package subcontracts button. The page name changes to reflect that it has 

entered packaging mode. 

2. 
Filter the list so that the subcontracts that you want to package are displayed in the list. 

---


<!-- Page 394 -->
Subcontracts 

RealPage® Financial Suite Spend Management User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

3. 
Select the subcontracts to include in the package. 

After you select at least one subcontract, the following three buttons appear: 

• 
Show Only Selected Subcontracts 

• 
Generate Package 

• 
Cancel Package 

Showing Only Selected Subcontracts 

• 
Click the Show Only Selected Subcontracts button to remove unselected subcontracts from 

the list so that you see only the subcontracts that will be included in the package. This 

action cannot be undone. If you accidentally exclude a subcontract, you must cancel the 

package and start over. 

Generating the Package 

• 
Opens the Generate Subcontracts Package box where you finalize the package by selecting 

what to include in the package in addition to the subcontracts. You can choose to include a 

cover page, summary, attachments, approval workflow, and proofs of payment. After 

selecting the desired options, click the Build package button to create the package. 

Canceling the Package 

• 
Click the Cancel package button to discard the package and return to the Subcontracts list 

page or the Spend management workbench. 

---

Adding a New Subcontract 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Spend management > All > Workbench > Subcontract > Add`


Use the Subcontract information page to add a new subcontract. 

You must set up a job in the Job Cost application before you can set up a subcontract for the job. 

To create a new subcontract, complete the following required fields. See Fields (on page 391) for 

more information about the additional fields on this page. 

1. 
Click the 
 Calendar button in the Date field, and then select the start date of the 

subcontract. 

2. 
Click the 
 Calendar button in the Expiration date field, and then select the end date of 

the subcontract. 

Type “p” in a date field to automatically insert the last day of the prior month. See 
Specifying Dates in Getting Started for a full list of shortcut keys related to entering dates.  

3. 
Use the Contractor drop-down list to select a contractor. 

If the contractor is not available in the drop-down list, see Adding a New Contractor (on 

page 659). 

4. 
If you want to bill to the company address, select the Use company address for bill to 

check box. Otherwise, select the property that is being billed for the purchase from the Bill 

to drop-down list. 

If the purchase order is for a property that is not in the list, click the Add link at the top of 

the list and complete the Contact Information (on page 679) box. 

5. 
Type a description of the contracted service in the Description field. 

6. 
If your Spend Management configuration requires you to add an attachment, use the 

Attachments drop-down list to add an attachment (on page 631).  

7. 
Complete the line entry table. See Line Entry Table in Fields (on page 391) for more 

information. 

8. 
Optionally, preview the approval workflow.

9. 
Click the Submit button. The system submits the subcontract for processing.

Storefront 

RealPage® Financial Suite Spend Management User Guide

Storefront Home Page 

Use the Storefront home page to begin shopping. You can perform a quick search for an item, 

select a vendor catalog, shop by category, or submit a quick order. 

a) Shop by: Choose an option for shopping: 

• 
Vendor catalogs: Shop from specific vendor catalogs. 

• 
Browse categories: Shop from a general list of categories such as Electrical or 

Plumbing. 

• 
Category index: Shop from an alphabetical list of categories such as Tools - 

Screwdrivers or Tools - Wrenches. 

• 
Shopping lists: Shop from a previously saved list. 

• 
Frequent purchases: Shop from a list of frequently purchased items. 

• 
Quick order: Shop using a quick order form. Use this feature if you already know the 

SKUs and quantities of the products you want to order. 

b) Quick search: Type an item, category, or SKU in the field, and then click the Shop button. 

This option appears with each of the shopping options. 

c) Vendor catalogs: This is the tab that loads initially. To shop from a specific vendor’s catalog, 

select a vendor catalog to shop by, and then click the Shop Selected button. To shop all 

vendor catalogs, click the Shop All Catalogs link. 

Before You Begin 

Access can vary depending on your organization’s subscriptions and your permissions. If you do 

not see the option in the menu, then ask your System Administrator to check your permissions.
