The online shopping feature must be enabled in your Site Experience configuration to access 

Storefront. 

See Configuring Spend Management in the Spend Management Configuration Guide for more 

information. 

If your user account doesn’t have the permissions shown above, then ask your System 

Administrator for assistance. If you have administrator privileges, you can assign permissions for a 

new feature to a user or to a role. See Roles and Permissions (on page 604) for a description of 

how to review a user’s permissions. 

How to Get Here 

These are the most direct options for accessing the Storefront page. You may have additional 

options based on your permission settings. 

 Shopping Cart 

• 
From any page, click the 
 Shopping cart button in the top bar. The Storefront page 

opens. 

Spend Management Workbench > 
 Storefront 

• 
From the Spend Management Workbench page, select the 
 Storefront button. 

When you first open the Storefront, you must select a property. See Accessing the Catalog for a 

Property (on page 401) for more information. 

Accessing the Catalog for a Property 

To shop for a property, you must access its catalog. 

When you first access the Storefront feature, the Please select a property to shop for box 

appears. 

To access the catalog for a property: 

1. 
Select the property from the drop-down list in the Please select a property to shop for box. 

2. 
Click the Shop catalogs button. The Storefront page loads with available vendor catalogs 

for the property. 

You can shop in only one property catalog at a time. This means that after you start an order from 

a catalog, you must complete it before accessing another property catalog. At that time, return to 

the Spend Management Workbench page, select the 
 Storefront button, and then repeat the 

steps to access the catalog for a property.

Vendor Catalogs 

 Storefront > Vendor Catalogs 

Use the Vendor Catalogs link to shop from specific vendor catalogs. Choose from 

RealPage-hosted catalog vendors and punchout catalog vendors (if available). 

a) Show Selected Only: Activate this switch to show only the vendors you selected. Deactivate 

this switch to view all available vendors. 

b) Vendor Button: Click on a vendor button to select the vendor. 

c) Shop Selected: Click this button to shop from the vendors you selected. 

Selecting a Vendor Catalog 

 Storefront > Vendor Catalogs > RealPage Hosted Catalogs/Punchout Catalogs 

To select a vendor catalog: 

1. 
From the Vendor Catalogs tab, select a vendor catalog tile from either the RealPage Hosted 

Catalogs or the Punchout Catalogs section. 

Online vendor catalogs are hosted by RealPage. Punchout vendor catalogs are hosted by 
the vendor. Both types of catalogs appear in the web application; you will not need to 
navigate to a different site. 

2. 
Click the (Vendor Catalog) button to select the vendor catalog you want to view. 

3. 
Click the Shop Selected button to open the selected catalog. 

• 
For RealPage hosted vendors, the Storefront catalog (on page 416) page loads with 

products from the selected vendor catalog(s). 

• 
For Punchout vendors, the Punchout Vendor Catalog (on page 403) page opens 

requesting a delivery ZIP code be entered to start the process.

#### Storefront Catalog
*Source: `RP Financial Suite Spend Management User Guide.pdf`, Page 428*

Storefront 

RealPage® Financial Suite Spend Management User Guide

Storefront Catalog 

The Storefront Catalog page allows you to search for specific products in your vendor’s catalog. 

a) Selection criteria: This provides selection criteria for narrowing the product list. Use any or 

all of the selection criteria on the left side of the page to narrow the product list and locate 

the products you want to order: 

• 
Your selection: Search for products using a keyword: 

• 
To search for a product, type a keyword in the Enter Keyword to Search field, 

and then click the Go button. 

• 
To refine your search, click the Refine Search link, type the keyword in the second 

search box, and then click the Go button. 

• 
Category: Narrow the search by product category by clicking the product categories 

you want to search. 

• 
Supplier: Narrow the search by supplier by clicking the supplier you want to use. 

The date shown next to each supplier is when the supplier’s catalog was last 
updated. 

• 
Price: Narrow the search by price range by clicking a price range. 

• 
Brand: Narrow the search by product name brand by clicking a brand name. 

b) Products found: This shows the number of product search results found. 

c) Sort By: This lets you sort products by product name, brand, supplier, or price. 

d) Page: This lets you view more search results if available. 

---



##### Finding a Product in the Catalog
*Source: `RP Financial Suite Spend Management User Guide.pdf`, Page 429*

Chapter 9: Storefront 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage® Financial Suite Spend Management User Guide 

e) View: This lets you choose a product list view: 

• 
 List view: This format has a single product listed on a row, and each row includes 

the product name, brand name, product description, supplier name, last refresh date, 

SKU, and price per unit. If available, there is also a picture of the product. 

• 
 Grid view: This format has three products listed on each row. This view shows the 

same information as the List view except for the product description. 

f) 
Product list: This is the list of product search results based upon the selection criteria. 

Finding a Product in the Catalog 

To find a product in the catalog: 

1. 
Use any or all of the selection criteria on the left side of the page to narrow the product list 

and locate the products you want to order: 

• 
Your selection: To search for products using a keyword, type the word in the Enter 

Keyword to Search field, and then click the Go button. 

• 
Category: To narrow the search by product category, click the product category you 

want to view. 

• 
Supplier: To narrow the search by supplier, click the supplier you want to use. 

The date shown next to each supplier is when the supplier’s catalog was last 
updated. 

• 
Price: To narrow the search by price range, click a price range. 

• 
Brand: To narrow the search by product brand, click a brand name. 

The Products found list updates as you narrow your search criteria. 

2. 
To refine your product search, use the Refine Search feature under Your selection. 

• 
Click the Refine search link. 

• 
Type a word or number in the Refine Search field, and then click the Go button. 

For example, if you want to filter a list of doorknobs for only satin nickel colored doorknobs, 

type “satin nickel” in the Refine Search field, and then click the Go button. The Products 

Found list updates with only satin nickel doorknobs. 

3. 
Optionally, select a Sort By option to sort products by product name, brand, supplier, or 

price. 

4. 
Optionally, choose a View for the product list. 

• 
 List view: This format has a single product listed on a row, and each row includes 

the product name, brand name, product description, supplier name, last refresh date, 

SKU, and price per unit. If available, there is also a picture of the product.

#### Product Configurator
*Source: `RP Financial Suite Spend Management User Guide.pdf`, Page 432*

Storefront 

RealPage® Financial Suite Spend Management User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Product Configurator 

Storefront Catalog > Add to Cart 

The Product Configurator page appears when a purchase requires additional information for an 

order, such as a specific unit, choice of related products, or installation schedule. For example, 

carpets, vinyl, and tile with installation require a unit number, related goods and services, and 

installation dates on the order. If the Product Configurator page appears, you must complete the 

page before adding the product to the shopping cart. 

Product Configurator Example 

In this example, the Product Configurator page must be completed to add a carpet purchase to 

the shopping cart. 

The image shown above is an example of a Product Configurator page for a carpet product. The 
information requested on the page may differ depending on your product selection. 

Completing the Product Configurator Page 

To complete the Product Configurator page: 

1. 
Begin typing the unit number in the Unit Number field, and then select the unit number 

from the drop-down list. 

The system updates the Unit Size (sqft) field and the fields for carpet, tile, vinyl, or paint size 

with the square footage of the unit. These fields cannot be edited. 

In this example, the system updates the Carpet Size (sqft) field. 

---



##### Fields
*Source: `RP Financial Suite Spend Management User Guide.pdf`, Page 433*

Chapter 9: Storefront 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage® Financial Suite Spend Management User Guide 

2. 
Complete the remaining fields, which depend on the selected product. 

In this example, you would complete these steps: 

• 
Update the quantity in the Qty field. 

• 
Select the options for carpet padding and labor from the Product Name drop-down 

list in each row. 

• 
Select whether floor prep is needed from the Floor Prep option: Yes or No. 

• 
Select whether there are steps in the unit from the Steps option: Yes or No. 

• 
If this is a partial carpet installation, select the Partial Installation check box, and then 

type the room names that require carpeting in the If Partial List Rooms field. 

• 
Select dates from the 1st/2nd/3rd Choice calendars and select a time frame from the 

drop-down lists. Only the 1st Choice is required. 

Suppliers also have the option of supplying the available installation dates. 
Therefore, when you click the calendar, the only dates shown are those that the 
supplier has available for installation. 

3. 
Click the Add to Cart button. The system adds the item to your shopping cart. 

4. 
When you finish adding products to the shopping cart, click the 
 Shopping Cart button 

to review your order and check out. See Using the Shopping Cart Pane to Review Your 

Order (on page 425) for more information.

#### Order Page
*Source: `RP Financial Suite Spend Management User Guide.pdf`, Page 447*



##### Completing an Order
*Source: `RP Financial Suite Spend Management User Guide.pdf`, Page 447*

Chapter 9: Storefront 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage® Financial Suite Spend Management User Guide 

Order Page 

 Storefront > 
 Shopping Cart > Proceed to Checkout 

Use the Order page in Storefront to complete the purchase. 

When the status of a General Ledger account is changed to Inactive, the system validates that 
the G/L account is not associated with an open online purchase order or eInvoice. If the G/L 
account is associated with an open online purchase order or eInvoice, the status cannot be 
changed to Inactive. This ensures that all orders and electronic invoices are routed successfully 
through RealPage Accounting. 

These sections guide you through the purchase process: 

• 
Edit your order: This section allows you to update product quantities, split purchase orders, 

add promotion codes, check the available budget, and select whether to use a standard 

purchase order or a job cost order. 

• 
Review your order: This section lets you review and confirm the order after the system has 

confirmed pricing and availability. 

• 
Order confirmation: This section provides the order confirmation. 

When an eInvoice is created in Accounting, goes through the approval process, and is posted, the 

RealPage Accounting system sends an update to OpsMerchant to change the partner status to 

Approved. This ensures that the vendor is aware of the current status of the invoice. 

Updates are also sent to OpsMerchant when the eInvoice is paid or voided, along with the 

payment details. 

Completing an Order 

To complete an order: 

1. 
From the Shopping cart pane or page, click the Checkout button. The Ready to Checkout? 

box opens. 

2. 
Click the Checkout button. The Order page loads with the Edit your order tab activated. 

---


<!-- Page 448 -->
Storefront 

RealPage® Financial Suite Spend Management User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

3. 
To display the line item columns, select the following options: 

• 
Select the Show Image check box to have an image of the line item product appear at 

the beginning of the row. 

• 
Select the Show Segments check box to display the Segment Type 1 – 4 and Segment 

Value 1 – 4 fields in the line item row. 

• 
Select the Show Dimensions check box to display the Vendor, Class, Customer, 

Project, and Employee fields in the line item row. 

The Show Segments and Show Dimensions check boxes are not available for the Job 

Cost order type. 

4. 
For the Order Type, select either Standard or Job Cost. 

5. 
Click the Show defaults link to expand the following additional fields: 

• 
Property - this field is pre-populated with the property code 

• 
Customer 

• 
Vendor 

• 
Project 

• 
Class 

• 
Unit 

• 
Segment Type 1 - 4 

• 
GL Code 

• 
Segment Value 1 - 4 

6. 
Click the Apply defaults button to use the defined defaults on a purchase order to reduce 

the amount of time spent keying in large orders. 

• 
Click the Hide defaults link to close these additional fields. 

7. 
Make any changes needed on this tab, and then click the Review Your Order button. 

• 
To update the quantity for a product, type the new quantity in the Qty field. 

• 
To update the general ledger (G/L) code for a product, begin typing the account 

number or description in the G/L Code field, and then select the G/L account from the 

drop-down list. 

• 
To update the unit associated with a product, begin typing the unit number in the Unit 

field, and then select the unit from the drop-down list. 

• 
To enter a short note for a product, begin typing in the Memo field. 

• 
To update the shipping cost for a product, type the shipping cost in the Shipping field. 

The Shipping amount for an online order is applied to the purchase order created by 
the online order in Storefront. 

---


<!-- Page 449 -->
Chapter 9: Storefront 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage® Financial Suite Spend Management User Guide 

8. 
Review the order and make any necessary changes. 

• 
To add a description to the order, type in the Description field. 

9. 
To split the purchase order between properties, click the Split link and then complete the 

Split PO box. See Splitting a Purchase Order (on page 438) for more information. 

10. 
If you have a promotion code for the vendor: 

• 
Click the Add promotion code button. The Enter supplier promotion code box opens. 

• 
Type the promotion code in the field. 

• 
Click the Apply button to confirm the code and close the box. 

11. 
To check your available budget: 

• 
Click the Spend Control button. The Available Budget box opens. 

• 
Click the Month tab to verify your monthly budget per property. 

• 
Click the Year To Date tab to verify your year-to-date budget per property. 

• 
Click the Done button to return to the Order page. 

12. 
Click the Review Your Order button. The system confirms pricing and availability with the 

vendor, and then the Order page refreshes with the Review your order page. 

The system updates item quantities and pricing depending upon availability and pricing 
from the vendor, and these updates appear on the Review your order page. For example, 
if you request 15 items of a product and only 10 items are available from the vendor, the 

Review your order page lists a quantity of 10 instead of 15. 

13. 
Review your order to verify expected item quantities and pricing: 

---



##### Splitting a Purchase Order
*Source: `RP Financial Suite Spend Management User Guide.pdf`, Page 450*

Storefront 

RealPage® Financial Suite Spend Management User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

• 
If you are ready to submit your order, click the Submit Your Order button. The Order 

page refreshes with the Order Confirmation page. 

• 
If you need to edit the order, click the Edit button to return to the Edit your order 

page. 

The system records one order per vendor, so you may see multiple orders listed, as 
indicated by the Total Number of Orders field. Additionally, the RealPage Accounting 
system sends an update to OpsMerchant to change the partner status to Approved when 
an eInvoice is created in Accounting, goes through the approval process, and is posted. 
This ensures that the vendor is aware of the current status of the invoice. Updates are also 
sent to OpsMerchant when the eInvoice is paid or voided, along with the payment details. 

14. 
Review your order by clicking the link in the Order Number field. The Purchase Order 

Information page opens. 

15. 
Click the Continue Shopping button to return to the Storefront page. 

Splitting a Purchase Order 

During the checkout process, you can make purchases for multiple properties at the same time by 

splitting the purchase order for a line item. This option simplifies your purchase process by not 

requiring you to repeat the full checkout process multiple times, and this may let you take 

advantage of deals on large-quantity purchases. 

To split a purchase order: 

1. 
From the Edit your order section of the Order page, click the Split link next to the line item 

with products you want to distribute across multiple properties. The Split PO box opens 

with the quantity and property from the original line item. 

2. 
Type the number of items to send to the property in line 1. 

3. 
For each property you want to add: 

• 
In the line item table, click the 
 Add button. 

• 
Select the property from the Property drop-down list. 

• 
Type the number of items to send to that property in the Qty field. 

4. 
Click the Calculate button. The total number of items in the Qty column must equal the 

original line item quantity. Otherwise, a message appears at the top of the page. 

5. 
Click the Save button to close the box. The system updates the order with the split order. 

---

receive goods; and create change orders. However, you cannot use this page to add new

Spend Inquiry 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Spend Management > All > Periodic Tasks > Spend Inquiry`


The Spend inquiry page lets you create custom inquiries into company and property expenditures 

by reporting period. Use the Spend inquiry page to perform spend inquiries on A/P invoices, 

purchase orders, service contracts, and subcontract transactions. 

As shown below, this page has a layout similar to the Spend Management Workbench (on page 

166), but the focus is on viewing spending by reporting period. For example, you may want to 

compare spending for certain equipment or services among properties over the past year or 

quarter. 

Additionally, you can export inquiries to Excel for review and reporting purposes. 

Before You Begin 

The RealPage Accounting Spend Management subscription must be activated to access Spend 

Management. 

Access can vary depending on your organization’s subscriptions and your permissions. If you do 

not see the option in the menu, then ask your System Administrator to check your permissions. 

Permissions 

These permissions are required to run spend inquiries: 

Application 
Activities/Lists 
Permissions 

Spend Management 
Spend Inquiry 
Run 

If your user account doesn’t have the permissions shown above, then ask your System 

Administrator for assistance. If you have administrator privileges, you can assign permissions for a 

new feature to a user or to a role. See Roles and Permissions (on page 604) for a description of 

how to review a user’s permissions. 

---



##### Performing a Spend Inquiry
*Source: `RP Financial Suite Spend Management User Guide.pdf`, Page 461*



##### Managing Spend Inquiry Views
*Source: `RP Financial Suite Spend Management User Guide.pdf`, Page 461*

Chapter 10: Periodic Tasks 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage® Financial Suite Spend Management User Guide 

Performing a Spend Inquiry 

To perform a spend inquiry: 

1. 
Either use filters to set up a view or apply a pre-made view. 

2. 
Review and organize the results in the list. 

3. 
Export the results to Excel (on page 450) for use in reports. 

Applying a View 

If you have a view for the spend inquiry you want to perform, select the view you want to use 

from the Apply View drop-down list. The table loads with the transactions filtered and sorted for 

the applied view. 

Applying Filters 

If you have not set up a view for the spend inquiry you want to perform: 

1. 
Filter for a transaction type: 

• 
A/P Invoice: This option filters results for A/P invoices. 

• 
Purchase Order This option filters results for purchase orders. 

• 
Service Contract: This option filters results for service contracts. 

• 
Subcontract: This option filters results for subcontracts. 

2. 
Select any of the criteria in the top section of the workbench to filter for the transactions 

you want to find. See Filters in Fields (on page 450) for more information. 

3. 
Click the Apply button. The table loads with transactions that meet the filter criteria. 

4. 
Sort and move columns as preferred. 

5. 
Click the Export to Excel button to save the results to an Excel spreadsheet on your local 

desktop. 

• 
Optionally, click the Save View As button and use the Save view as box to save the 

view. See Managing Spend Inquiry Views (on page 449) for more information. 

Managing Spend Inquiry Views 

Workbench views let you save filtered views of the current workbench page for each access each 

time you load the workbench. 

---

Exporting a Spend Inquiry 

To export spend inquiry results to Excel: 

1. 
Type the file name of the export in the File Name field. 

2. 
Type the name of the worksheet tab in the Sheet Name field. 

3. 
Choose the export type: 

• 
Export Detail: This option exports the full spend inquiry detail. 

• 
Export Summary: This option exports a summary view of the spend inquiry. 

4. 
Click the Export to Excel button. Your browser downloads the Excel file. Open the Excel file 

to view it. 

Depending on the browser you are using, you may have to save the Excel file before 
opening it.

Saved Items List

> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Spend Management > All > Search & Find >

Items`


Use the Saved items list to add and store frequently used items in an offline shopping list for 

purchase orders. When you create a new purchase order, you can select a vendor for the purchase 

order and then open a list of saved items for that vendor. If any items have been stored for that 

vendor, then you can quickly select them from the list and populate them as line entries in the 

purchase order. 

The Saved items list shows items created by all users. It respects any entity restrictions; for 
example, if you are restricted to property A and items are entered for property B, you cannot 
see items for property B. 

When you access the Saved items list from the Purchase order information page, the list 
includes only the items created for the vendor on the purchase order. 

From the Saved items list, you can: 

• 
Select and apply saved items to a purchase order (on page 322). 

• 
Add saved items to the offline shopping list (on page 460). 

• 
View and edit saved items (on page 460). 

• 
Delete saved items (on page 464). 

• 
Import (on page 464) and export (on page 465) saved items. 

Before You Begin 

Access can vary depending on your organization’s subscriptions and your permissions. If you do 

not see the option in the menu, then ask your System Administrator to check your permissions. 

Permissions 

These permissions are required to add and managed saved items for purchase orders.

To add an item to the Saved items list: 

1. 
On the Saved items box, click the Add button.

2. 
If the item is related to a job cost purchase order, then select the Job cost check box. If 

selected, two additional fields appear: Job and Cost code. See Saved Items Information 

Page (on page 462) for more information. 

3. 
In the Vendor drop-down list, select the vendor for which you are saving the item.

• 
In the Job drop-down list, select the job associated with the purchase. 

• 
In the Cost code drop-down list, select the cost code associated with the purchase. 

You must select a job before you can select a job cost code. 

6. 
In the Account drop-down list, select the G/L account to which the item applies. 

7. 
In the Account description field, type a description or memo for the account. 

8.

#### Contracts List
*Source: `RP Financial Suite Spend Management User Guide.pdf`, Page 482*

Bids and Contracts 

RealPage® Financial Suite Spend Management User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Contracts List 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > All > Periodic Tasks > Bids and Contracts > 
Contracts`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > Contracts`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Spend Management > All > Periodic Tasks > Contracts`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Finance Agent > All > Contracts`


Use the Contracts list to view and manage contracts and their associated records.  

The Contracts list can include both of the following record types of contracts: 

• 
Online contracts: When the contract was created in the Bids and Contracts application, then 

the contract is an online contract. These types of records have a check mark in the Online 

column. 

• 
Offline contracts: When you create a contract in the RealPage Financial Suite (using either 

Spend Management or Accounts Payable), then the contract is an offline contract. 

From this list, you can: 

• 
Create a new contract.  

• 
Create a service contract from a contract. After creating a service contract from a contract, 

the Contracts list shows the transaction number and links it to the transaction.  

• 
Create a subcontract from a contract. After creating a subcontract from a contract, the 

Contracts list shows the transaction number and links it to the transaction.  

• 
Create a purchase order from a contract. After creating a purchase order from a contract, 

the Contracts list shows the transaction number and links it to the transaction.  

After creating one of these transactions, if you have the approval workflow turned on, the 
system submits the record for approval. 

• 
View a contract, subcontract, or purchase order from a contract that is associated with it. 

• 
Delete a contract. To delete a transaction that is associated with a contract, go to the Spend 

Management application.  

• 
Export the list of contracts. 

---

When you create a purchase order from a contract, the system completes some of the fields using 

information from the contract, such as Item Description, SKU, Qty, and Price. If taxes and 

shipping are defined in the contract, then they appear as separate line items in the Entries list. 

To create a purchase order associated with a contract: 

1. 
Select the Contracts option. 

2. 
Select the check box of the contract on which to base a new purchase order. 

3. 
Click the Create button, and then select Purchase order. 

4. 
In the Create type section, select the Purchase order option. 

5. 
Click the 
 Calendar button in the Date field, and then select the date of the purchase 

order. 

6. 
Click the 
 Calendar button in the Encumbrance date field, and then select the date of 

the encumbrance. 

7. 
Select a vendor from the Vendor drop-down list. 

If the vendor that you need is not available in the drop-down list, click the Add link and 
then add a new vendor record.  

8. 
Select the Use Company address for bill to check box if you want to use the vendor’s 

company address to send bills to. When you select this option, the Bill to field is not 

available. 

9. 
If you want to select a specific contact to send bills to, select the contact in the Bill to 

drop-down list. If the Bill to list is not available, then clear the Use Company address for bill 

to check box. 

10. 
In the Ship to drop-down list, select the contact record with the address where you want to 

ship goods or deliver services. 

11. 
Click the Saved items link if you want to view an offline shopping list of frequently used 

items for the vendor you entered on the purchase order. Select and apply items from this 

list (on page 322) to quickly populate them as line entries in the purchase order.

page 460) for the future.  

12. 
If this is a blanket purchase order, select the Blanket check box, and then select the 

appropriate option:

•

the vendor and property on the purchase order.

For standard line entries, refer to Standard Line Entry list in Fields (on page 322).

Working with Attachments 

If your Spend Management configuration requires you to add an attachment, attach a document 

to the service contract using one of the following methods. The method that you use depends on 

whether you have scanning enabled in your preferences. 

When you have scanning disabled in your preferences, use the Attachments field to add 

documents to a record. 

When the Attachments field appears, you can attach a file to the record. You can attach a file that 

has already been added to the system or you can upload a file from your computer. You can also 

drag your files from the file explorer into the Attachments box if you are using Firefox, Chrome, 

or Edge web browsers. 

• 
To select a file that is already stored in the system, select the document that you want to 

attach from the Attachments drop-down list. 

• 
To upload a document from your computer, click the Add link in the Attachments 

drop-down list, and then click the Choose Files button. 

• 
Click the Show All/Show unattached link to change the contents of the drop-down list 

between showing all files to showing unattached files. Unattached files are files that are not 

yet attached to any other record in the system. 

• 
To view a document before attaching it, click the document that you want to review, and 

then click the View link. 

• 
To find a document in the system, click the Find link. 

• 
If you are using Firefox, Chrome, or Edge, you can drop your file on the Attachments box to 

attach the file to this record.  

If you have enabled the single scan feature in your preferences, then the Attachments field does 
not appear. Instead, the record has a Documents section where you can attach files. Follow 
method 2 instead. 

Method 2: If you have scanning enabled in your preferences, then you use the Documents section 

to add documents to a record. The Documents section appears in place of the Attachments field 

when you have enabled the single scan feature (on page 641) in your Preferences settings.

Contract Information Page

The content of the Contract information page varies depending on whether the record is a 

service contract, a subcontract, or a purchase order, and whether the contract is online (created in 

Bids and Contracts) or offline (created in RealPage Financial Suite). 

• 
The top section of a record contains information about the contract. 

• 
The Bids and contract attachments section lists the files attached to the contract record 

when the contract is an online contract. 

• 
The Create type section is where you select the type of record that you want to create and 

associate with the open record: a purchase order, service contract, or subcontract. 

• 
The (Date) section reflects the type of record that you chose in the Create type section, a 

service contract, subcontract, or purchase order. 

• 
The Documents or Attachment sections allow you to attach a file to the record. The 

Attachments section and drop-down list appears when you do not have scanning enabled. 

The Documents section appears when scanning is enabled. The scanner setting is available 

in My Preferences (on page 641). 

If the AI contract screening feature is configured, whenever you attach a document to a 

contract record, the system reviews the document for clauses and keywords in the 

document, and then displays the clause information prominently in the contract record. 

• 
When you create a transaction, you can add items in a purchase order, or the job tasks in a 

service contract or subcontract. After you save the transaction, the list does not appear 

when viewing the contract. You must open the transaction to view the list of items. 

After you save the record, additional links appear on the record. The links vary depending on the 

record type and whether your system uses the approval workflow for service contracts, purchase 

orders, and subcontracts:

the link opens the Approval history box so that you can review the record’s progress 

through the approval workflow.

Records that have been matched with A/P invoices have a Matched invoices link. Clicking

Full Service 

Full Service Spend Management integrates RealPage Invoice Processing with RealPage Accounting, allowing you 

to create new invoices in Accounts Payable and Spend Management from scanned invoices without inputting the 

invoices manually. 

To use Full Service Spend Management, you must subscribe to the service. Contact your RealPage representative 

for more information. After enabling and configuring this service, Full Service options appear in both Accounts 

Payable and Spend Management. 

Before You Begin 

After Full Service Spend Management is enabled, you must have the following permissions to view and upload 

invoices via Invoice Processing.

Invoice Processing Upload 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable/Spend Management > All > Invoice Processing Upload`


Use the Invoice Processing Upload page to send invoices into RealPage Invoice Processing from 

your properties. After invoices are uploaded, the system processes them and adds them to your 

workbench. If there are any questions during processing, exceptions appear on the Invoice 

exception queue (on page 492) page. 

Uploading Invoice Processing Invoices 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable/Spend Management > All > Invoice Processing Upload`


For more information about importing a current or historical invoice, see Importing an A/P Invoice 

(on page 256). 

To upload invoices: 

1. 
On the Invoice Processing Upload page, click the Upload link for the property from which 

you want to upload invoices. The OpsInvoice Image Inbox page opens. 

2. 
Click the New button. The Add Image File page opens. 

3. 
Click the Upload link next to the Image field, and then select the file you want to upload. 

Files must be in PDF format for the system to accept them. You can upload only one file, 
but it can contain multiple invoices. 

4. 
Type the number of invoices included in the file in the Invoice Count field. 

5. 
Type notes related to the invoices for processing in the Notes field. 

6. 
Click the Save button. The system uploads the file and adds it to the Invoice Processing 

Upload page with a status of Pending. 

Viewing an Uploaded Invoice Processing Invoice 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable/Spend Management > All > Invoice Processing Upload 
> Upload`


To view an invoice: 

1. 
From the Invoice Processing Upload page, click the link in the OID column for the invoice 

you want to view or edit. The Edit Image File page opens. 

2. 
Click the 
 View File button. Your browser opens the PDF file. 

3. 
Close the PDF file after you finish viewing it.

##### Resolving an Exception Invoice
*Source: `RP Financial Suite Spend Management User Guide.pdf`, Page 504*

Full Service 

RealPage® Financial Suite Spend Management User Guide

Invoice Exception Queue 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable/Spend Management > All > Invoice Exception Queue`


Use the Invoice Exception Queue page to resolve invoice processing issues submitted from the 

RealPage Invoice Processing team. Occasionally, the team requires clarifications on an invoice to 

process it accurately. When this occurs, the team notes the invoice as an exception and sends it to 

the Invoice Exception Queue with a Pending Review status. The 
 Invoice exception button near 

the top of the page appears with a number when there are invoices in the exception queue. 

See Resolving an Exception Invoice (on page 492) for more information on how to comment on 

the exception and send the invoice back to the team. 

Resolving an Exception Invoice 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable/Spend Management > All > Invoice Exception Queue`


When the RealPage Invoice Processing team sends an invoice to the Invoice Exception Queue, the 

 Invoice exception button near the top of the page appears with a number. 

To resolve an exception invoice: 

1. 
Click the 
 Invoice exception button. The Invoice exception queue page opens. 

2. 
Click the link in the Invoice OID field to open the invoice. 

3. 
Update the list of invoice comments and exceptions, and then send the invoice back to the 

team for final processing: 

• 
When you click the comment box, a list of the exception messages appears. You can 

enter part of the exception message to narrow the list, and then make a selection. 

• 
You can also type free-form text as an exception message. 

4. 
After you enter all exception messages that apply, click the Add Comment button. The 

messages are added to the area below the list of invoice exception messages. You see the 

date the message was added, the user ID of the person who added the message, the 

comment for the action, and the description of the message that was selected. 

5. 
Choose an action: 

• 
To save updates and return to the list of invoices, click the Save button. 

• 
If the invoice should be voided, click the Void button, and then click Void again to 

proceed with voiding the invoice. 

• 
If the invoice is ready to go to the team, click the Route to Pending QC button. The 

invoice no longer appears on the Invoice Exception Queue page.

### Reports
*Source: `RP Financial Suite Spend Management User Guide.pdf`, Page 511*

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage® Financial Suite Spend Management User Guide 

Reports 

The Reports feature lets you process and store the following reports: 

• 
A/P ledger: This report provides detailed information on vendors, invoices, and balances for review. 

• 
Budget variance report: This report provides an overview of the budget and open invoices. 

• 
Budget variance with commitments report: This report provides an overview of the budget and open 

invoices, including commitments. 

• 
Purchase orders report: This report provides a list of purchase orders for a given time period. 

• 
Unit cost report: This report provides visibility into unit cost and reviews the highest expenses. 

• 
PO audit: This report provides a view of invoices tied to purchases orders, when each transaction is entered, 

when the final approval occurs, and compliance. 

• 
Spend invoice ledger report: This report provides invoice details such as who submitted the invoice and what 

purchase orders have been matched to the invoice. 

• 
Subcontract report: This report provides a list of subcontracts for a given time period. 

• 
Vendor aging report: This report provides vendor balances from A/P invoices and the lengths of time it took 

to process them through accounts payable. 

• 
Vendor list: This report provides a list of vendors and includes payment terms, tax identification numbers, 

and account numbers. 

This feature also includes options for managing and running reports: 

• 
Memorized reports: Use this feature to save report customizations and schedule recurring reports. 

• 
My stored reports: View your reports on this page.

#### My Stored Reports List
*Source: `RP Financial Suite Spend Management User Guide.pdf`, Page 513*

Chapter 13: Reports 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage® Financial Suite Spend Management User Guide 

My Stored Reports List 

See the How to Get Here topic for a list of ways to access this list. 

Reports are added to the My stored reports list when you process them offline or schedule them 

to run at a later date. 

• 
Processing and storing reports: You have the option to process a report in the background 

and store it in the system. This option is particularly useful for reports containing amounts 

of data that are too large for the system to run in real time. You can also use this feature to 

take and store periodic snapshots automatically for future reference. 

• 
Scheduling reports: You have the option to store reports and set them up on a schedule to 

run periodically. After the system runs a scheduled report on the date you selected, the 

report is available in the menu of the application that you ran it from. 

About the My Stored Reports List 

The My stored reports list is available in any application that has reports.  

• 
When you access the list from an individual application, it will display only the reports that 

you scheduled or processed in that application. For example, if you open the My stored 

reports list in Accounts Payable, then you will see only Accounts Payable reports. 

• 
When you access the list from the Reports application, it will be centralized—that is, you will 

see all of your stored reports regardless of which application it came from. 

From the My stored reports list, you can: 

• 
Sort and filter the list of reports. 

• 
Save reports as a PDF file. 

• 
Open a report’s data in Excel. 

• 
Download the report data as a CSV file.  

• 
Export the list of stored reports. 

• 
View an error log for failed reports. 

About Stored Reports 

Note the following behavior of stored reports: 

• 
The data in stored reports does not reflect any changes beyond the report’s As of date. 

However, if you click any links in the report that open other pages, you will be accessing the 

latest data on those pages. 

• 
By default, the location ID and location name are appended to the end of the report name 

to easily identify the property for which the report was run. If you ran the report on a 

location group and did not choose to run it as an individual report, then the location group 

ID and location group name appears at the end of the report name instead.

##### Before You Begin

##### Memorizing a Report or Chart
*Source: `RP Financial Suite Spend Management User Guide.pdf`, Page 526*

Reports 

RealPage® Financial Suite Spend Management User Guide

Memorized Reports 

Use the Memorized reports page to run custom reports and to edit report customizations. 

Before You Begin 

Access can vary depending on your organization’s subscriptions and your permissions. If you do 

not see the option in the menu, then ask your System Administrator to check your permissions. 

Memorizing a report requires that you have the permissions to do so. You must have permissions 

to access and run a report in order to memorize it. Permissions for users, groups, or roles are 

configured in the Company setup. 

If your user account doesn’t have the permissions shown above, then ask your System 

Administrator for assistance. If you have administrator privileges, you can assign permissions for a 

new feature to a user or to a role. See Roles and Permissions (on page 604) for a description of 

how to review a user’s permissions. 

Memorizing a Report or Chart 

To memorize a report or chart: 

1. 
Set up a report or chart with the filters and parameters that you want to save. 

2. 
Click the Memorize button. The Memorize report parameters box opens. 

3. 
In the Name field, type a name for the report or chart. 

If you plan to make the report or chart public, give it a name that is easily identifiable to 
others. 

4. 
Select the Public check box to make the report or chart available to other users in their 

Memorized reports list. Clear the check box to keep it private. Private reports and charts are 

visible only to the person who created them (owners), and administrators. 

5. 
Click OK. 

---



#### Memorized Reports List
*Source: `RP Financial Suite Spend Management User Guide.pdf`, Page 527*



##### Editing a Memorized Report
*Source: `RP Financial Suite Spend Management User Guide.pdf`, Page 527*

Chapter 13: Reports 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage® Financial Suite Spend Management User Guide 

Memorized Reports List 

See the How to Get Here topic for a list of ways to access memorized reports. 

Use the Memorized reports list to view and manage reports that you saved in an application or 

that other users saved and then made public. From this list, you can: 

• 
Run memorized reports. 

• 
Edit memorized reports that you created. 

• 
Process large reports in the background and store them in the My stored reports list. 

• 
Schedule reports so that they run at a future date. 

• 
Delete memorized reports. 

• 
Export the list of memorized reports. 

Memorized reports are also accessible from the Reports center. 

Editing a Memorized Report 

See the How to Get Here topic for a list of ways to access memorized reports. 

You can edit a memorized report or chart only if you are the owner or a system administrator, 

even if the report or chart was made public. As the owner, you can change any parameter, 

including who owns it. The only field you cannot change is the report type.  

To edit a memorized report or chart: 

1. 
In the Memorized reports list, click the Edit link next to the report or chart that you want to 

change. The Edit memorized report page opens. The fields on this page correspond with 

the report’s type.  

2. 
Update the fields in the General information section as needed: 

• 
In the Report name and Report description fields, type a new name and description 

for the report, respectively. 

---

##### Scheduling a Memorized Report or Chart
*Source: `RP Financial Suite Spend Management User Guide.pdf`, Page 528*

• 
In the Report owner drop-down list, select a different user to be the owner of the 

report. If you change the report’s owner, then you will no longer be able to edit this 

memorized report after you save the changes. However, you can continue to run the 

report if it’s still public.  

• 
Select the Public check box to make the report available to other users in their 

Memorized reports list. Clear the check box to make the report private; that is, 

available only to yourself and system administrators. 

Others can see private memorized reports by selecting the Include private check box 
in their Memorized reports list. 

3. 
Modify the other settings as needed. 

4. 
Click Save. 

Running a Memorized Report 

To run a memorized report: 

1. 
From the Memorized reports page, click the Run link next to the memorized report that you 

want to run. A box opens. 

2. 
Select the type of report to run from the Select report type drop-down list. 

3. 
Click the OK button. The system runs the report. Depending on your selection, the system 

either opens the report in the browser or exports the report as a download. 

Scheduling a Memorized Report or Chart 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Reports > All > Reports Center > Memorized > More Actions > Edit 
Schedule`


See the How to Get Here topic for a list of ways to access memorized reports. 

Use the Schedule memorized report page to schedule a memorized report or chart to run 

automatically and routinely. 

Accessing the Schedule Memorized Report Page  

You can schedule a report or chart from either the Reports application or the application where it 

was originally memorized. 

To schedule a report from the Reports application: 

1. 
Open the Reports menu, and then click the Reports center option. The Reports center page 

opens.  

2. 
Select the Memorized tab. 

3. 
In the (View) drop-down list, select the application associated with the report, or select All 

applications. 

---


<!-- Page 529 -->
Chapter 13: Reports 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage® Financial Suite Spend Management User Guide 

4. 
Find the report or chart you want to schedule, and then click More actions. 

5. 
Select the Edit schedule option. The Schedule memorized report (on page 521) page 

opens. 

To schedule a report from another application: 

1. 
In the Applications menu, select the application where the memorized report is located, and 

then select the All tab. 

2. 
In the Reports section, click the Memorized reports option. 

3. 
Find the report or chart you want to schedule, and then click the Schedule link. The 

Schedule memorized report (on page 521) page opens. 

Filtering the Report 

1. 
In the Department/group and Location/group drop-down lists, select a specific department 

or location (or group of departments or locations) by which to filter the report. If you leave 

the filters blank, then the report will run for all departments and locations. 

2. 
If you are scheduling a financial report and the report is set to prompt for G/L account 

groups, then the G/L account group selection box appears. Select one or more G/L account 

groups to filter the report by. 

3. 
In the As of date field, type or select the date from which the scheduled report should 

display data. Leave this field blank to use the current date. If you enter an As of date, that 

date will always be used regardless of when the schedule is run. 

Type “p” in a date field to automatically insert the last day of the prior month. See 

Specifying Dates in Getting Started for a full list of shortcut keys related to entering dates. If 

you enabled reporting account labels in the General Ledger, then you have the option to 

substitute the account labels in the report with the reporting account set’s labels: 

• 
To enable reporting account labels, select the Substitute with reporting accounts 

labels check box. The Reporting account set drop-down list appears. 

• 
In the Reporting account set drop-down list, select the reporting account set whose 

labels you want to use. 

Scheduling the Report 

1. 
In the Start date field, type or select the date on which to start running the report.  

Typically, the Start date is a date in the future. If you select a date in the past, then the 
report executes immediately after you save it. The Start date also determines the date 
that the system schedules the report to run in future occurrences; for example, if you are 
scheduling the report to run weekly and the Start date is on a Monday, then the system 
will run the report every Monday. 

---


<!-- Page 530 -->
Reports 

RealPage® Financial Suite Spend Management User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Type “p” in a date field to automatically insert the last day of the prior month. See 

Specifying Dates in Getting Started for a full list of shortcut keys related to entering dates.  

2. 
In the Ending on field, select when to stop running the report:  

• 
Never: Run the report indefinitely. 

• 
Number of occurrences: Stop running the report after a specific number of 

occurrences.  

• 
In the End after field, type the number of occurrences after which to stop running 

the report; for example, type “5” to stop after five occurrences. 

• 
End date: Stop running the report on a specific date.  

• 
In the End on field, type or select the date on which to stop running the report. 

3. 
In the Recurrence drop-down list, select an option: 

• 
None: Run the report once on the scheduled date. 

• 
Days: Run the report once every X days. 

• 
Weeks: Run the report once every X weeks. 

• 
Months: Run the report once every X months.  

• 
Select the End of month check box to disregard the start date and run the report 

on the last day of the month. 

• 
Years: Run the report once a year. 

4. 
If you selected Days, Weeks, Months, or Years, type the number of times to run the report 

in the Every field.  

5. 
In the Email results to field, type the email address where you want the system to send the 

report results. 

• 
Click Save. 

Storing and Delivering the Report 

1. 
Select one or more delivery options for the report: 

• 
Email: Sends the report in an email. 

• 
Store report: Stores the report in the My stored reports list. 

• 
Store in cloud: Stores the report in a cloud-storage target. 

• 
Store in Reporting Portal: Stores the report in the selected owner portal(s). 

2. 
Fill in the fields corresponding with each section. 

Email 

1. 
In the To field, type the email address to which you want to send the report. 

2. 
Select the CC me check box if you want the system to send a copy of the email message to 

your inbox. 

---

In the Subject field, type the subject of the email message. 

4. 
In the Report type drop-down list, select a report format: 

• 
HTML: Sends the report as an HTML file. 

• 
Printable: Sends the report as a printable PDF file. 

• 
CSV: Sends the report in a comma-separated values (CSV) file. 

• 
Excel: Sends the report in an Excel file. 

•

Store Report

In the Report description field, type a description of the report to help you remember its

appears in the My stored reports list in the Title column. 

2. 
In the Report type drop-down list, select a report format: 

•

Printable: Saves the report as a printable PDF file. 

• 
CSV: Saves the report in a comma-separated values (CSV) file.

Excel: Saves the report in an Excel file.

Deleting a Memorized Report or Chart 

See the How to Get Here topic for a list of ways to access memorized reports and charts. 

Deleting a memorized report or chart removes it from the Memorized reports list and also 

removes the report or chart from any dashboard on which it appears.  

You must be either the report or chart owner or an administrator to delete it. 

To delete a memorized report: 

1. 
Open the Memorized reports list. 

2. 
Find the report or chart that you want to delete, and then click the Delete link. A 

confirmation box opens. 

3. 
Click OK.

Customizing and Running the Vendor Aging Report 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > All > Reports > Vendors Reports > Vendor Aging`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Spend Management > All > Reports > Vendor Reports > Vendor Aging`


The Vendor Aging report is a standard report. If you are looking for information on financial 
reports, see Creating a Financial Report. 

To customize and run the Vendor aging report: 

• 
From the Vendor Aging Report page, fill in the Reporting Currency section. This section 

appears only when you are working in a multi-currency system. 

• 
In the Reporting currency drop-down list, select the currency to use for the report. 

• 
In the Convert currency from section, select whether to convert the currency using the 

entity’s Base currency or the currency that was used in the transaction, Transaction 

currency. 

Filling In the Time Period Section 

Define the time period for the report. 

1. 
From the Aging periods drop-down list, select the aging period to include in the report. 

Aging periods are user-defined. For information, see Configuring A/P aging periods. 

2. 
In the Report as of section, select Today to report vendor aging as of today. Select Selected 

date and then type a date or click 
 Calendar and select a date. 

Type “p” in a date field to automatically insert the last day of the prior month. See 
Specifying Dates in Getting Started for a full list of shortcut keys related to entering dates.  

3. 
In the Date to use section, select the date type for which you want to see invoices. 

• 
A/P Invoice date: Show invoices that have the specified A/P invoice date. 

• 
Due date: Show invoices that have the specified due date. 

---


<!-- Page 542 -->
Reports 

RealPage® Financial Suite Spend Management User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

• 
G/L posting date: Show invoices that posted to the general ledger on the specified 

date. 

4. 
In the Based on section, select the date type to determine how the report is aged. 

• 
A/P invoice date: Base the aging on the date of the vendor invoice. 

• 
Due date: Base the aging on the invoice’s due date. 

• 
G/L posting date: Base the aging on the date the invoice posted to the general ledger. 

Filling In the Filters Section 

Set up a filter as needed. Using filters is optional. 

1. 
To filter the report by A/P accounts, click the Select button to open the multi-select box, 

and then select the desired A/P accounts. 

If you have already selected items, in place of the Select button, a box appears that shows a 

list of the selected items.  

2. 
Use the From vendor and To vendor drop-down lists to select the beginning and ending 

vendor in a range to include a range of vendors (suppliers) in the report. 

• 
From the From vendor drop-down list, select the first vendor in a range of vendors to 

include in the report. The system fills in the To vendor box with the same vendor, 

setting it up in case you want to include only one vendor in the report. 

• 
From the To vendor drop-down list, select the last vendor in a range of vendors. 

3. 
From the Vendor type drop-down list, if you want to limit the report to a certain vendor 

type, select the type here. 

The next two drop-down lists appear only if your company is multi-currency enabled. 

4. 
From the Transaction currency drop-down list, if you want to filter for a specific transaction 

currency, select the currency to filter for. 

5. 
From the Exchange rate types drop-down list, select the desired exchange rate type to filter 

for. 

6. 
From the Location drop-down list, to limit the report to a specific location, select the 

location. 

• 
Select the Individual report check box to create a separate report for each selected 

location. 

---


<!-- Page 543 -->
Chapter 13: Reports 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage® Financial Suite Spend Management User Guide 

• 
Select the Prompt on run check box to have the system prompt you for a location 

when it is about to run the report. 

7. 
From the Department drop-down list, to limit the report to a specific department, select the 

department here. 

• 
Select the Individual report check box to create a separate report for each selected 

department. 

• 
Select the Prompt on run check box to have the system prompt you for a department 

when it is about to run the report. 

8. 
From the Show for drop-down list, select one of the following options: 

• 
All locations: Include vendor aging data for all locations. 

• 
This location: Include vendor aging data for the selected location only. 

• 
Child locations: Include vendor aging data for the additional locations (buildings) on a 

property. 

9. 
From the Job drop-down list, select the job to filter by. 

If you want to filter by job and the Job drop-down list does not appear below the Show for 
(locations) section, go to the Format section of the page, and select the Include G/L detail 
check box, and then return to the Filters section. 

Filling In the Format Section 

Use this section to specify the type of report you want to create. 

1. 
From the Sort by drop-down list, select how you want to sort the report. You can sort by 

Vendor ID, Vendor name, Amount, Amount (descending order), G/L posting date, or G/L 

posting date (descending order). 

The abbreviation “desc” after an option means “Descending order”—in this case, reverse 
alphabetical or reverse numerical order. The default sort order and number of options 
changes depending on whether you want a summary report or a detail report. Vendor ID 
is the default sort order. 

2. 
Use the Group by drop-down list to arrange related data together by group according to 

the option you specify. To arrange related data together by group, click the Group by 

drop-down box and click on these options: 

• 
None 

• 
Vendor ID 

• 
Vendor name 

• 
Vendor type 

• 
Payment priority 

---


<!-- Page 544 -->

• 
Due date 

• 
G/L posting date 

• 
A/P account 

• 
Property with vendor 

• 
Property 

For example, to see all of the items grouped by the name of the vendor, select Vendor 

name. You can then sort the items by due date. 

3. 
In the Report type section, select Summary or Detail. 

• 
The Summary report type condenses all account details to a single line. 

• 
The Detail report type displays one line per customer per account. It also includes 

additional columns of information. 

4. 
Select the Include G/L detail check box to include invoice details in the report. The 

additional details include G/L account, location, memo, department, job, and unit for each 

line item. This option is available only when you select the Detail report type. 

5. 
Select the Include aged payable invoices check box to include aged payable invoices in the 

report.  

6. 
Select the Include job check box to include invoices associated with job records. This option 

is selectable only when the Include G/L detail check box is selected. 

This option is available only when your company subscribes to the Job Cost application. 

7. 
Select the Include retention check box to include the Retention held column in the report. 

This option cannot be combined with an A/P account filter. If you filter for an A/P account, 
then the Retention Held column does not appear.  

This option is available only when your company subscribes to the Job Cost application. 

8. 
Select the Include invoices pending approval check box to include any invoices that are 

pending approval in the Vendor Aging report. 

Invoices that are pending approval do not reconcile in the General Ledger. 

9. 
In the Show vendors with zero balance section: 

• 
Click Yes to include vendors with a zero balance or click No to exclude them from this 

report. No is the default option. 

10. 
In the Page orientation section, select Portrait or Landscape.

Vendor List

Use the Vendor list page to set up and run a Vendor List report. This report provides a list of 

vendors and includes payment terms, tax identification numbers, and account numbers. Use this 

report for tracking vendors, making decisions on future purchasing and contracts, and for 

flagging vendors who are on hold or exceed the established credit limit. 

The Vendor List report is a standard report. If you are looking for information on financial 
reports, see Creating a Financial Report. 

Before You Begin 

Access can vary depending on your organization’s subscriptions and your permissions. If you do 

not see the option in the menu, then ask your System Administrator to check your permissions. 

Permissions 

No additional permissions are required to run the Vendor List report. 

If your user account doesn’t have the permissions shown above, then ask your System 

Administrator for assistance. If you have administrator privileges, you can assign permissions for a 

new feature to a user or to a role. See Roles and Permissions (on page 604) for a description of 

how to review a user’s permissions. 

How to Get Here 

These are the most direct options for accessing the Vendor list page. You may have additional 

options based on your permissions.

Select the All tab. 

3. 
Under the Reports section, then Vendor Reports section, select Vendor List. 


> **Navigation Path:** `Spend Management Home Page > Reports > Vendors > Vendor List`

##### Customizing and Running the Vendor List Report
*Source: `RP Financial Suite Spend Management User Guide.pdf`, Page 552*

Customizing and Running the Vendor List Report 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > All > Reports > Vendor Reports > Vendor List`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Spend Management > All > Reports > Vendor Reports > Vendor List`


The Vendor List report is a standard report. If you are looking for information on financial 
reports, see Creating a Financial Report. 

To customize and run the Vendor List report: 

1. 
In the Filters section, set up filters to define the data that you want to see in the report. 

2. 
To limit the report to a vendor type, select the vendor type from the Vendor type 

drop-down list. 

3. 
Use the From vendor and To vendor drop-down lists to select the beginning and ending 

vendor in a range to include a range of vendors in the report. 

In the From vendor drop-down list, select the first vendor in a range of vendors to include 

in the report. The system fills in the To vendor field with the same vendor, setting it up in 

case you want to include only one vendor in the report. 

In the To vendor drop-down list, select the last vendor in a range of vendors. 

4. 
To limit the report to vendors that work with a specific location, select a location from the 

Location drop-down list. 

• 
Select the Individual report check box to create a separate report for each selected 

location. 

• 
Select the Prompt on run check box to have the system prompt you for a location 

when it is about to run the report. 

5. 
To limit the report to vendors that work with a specific department, select a department 

from the Department drop-down list. 

• 
Select the Individual report check box to create a separate report for each selected 

department. 

• 
Select the Prompt on run check box to have the system prompt you for a department 

before it runs the report. 

6. 
In the Show for drop-down list, select: 

• 
All locations: Include vendors for all locations. 

• 
This location: Include vendors for the selected location only. 

• 
Child locations: Include vendors for the additional locations (buildings) on a property. 

7. 
To list only vendors with which your company has exceeded the credit limit, select the Show 

only vendors exceeding credit limit check box. 

---

RealPage® Financial Suite Spend Management User Guide

To list only vendors that are on hold, select the Show only vendors on hold check box.

box. 

Filling In the Format Section 

1. 
Select the check box for each category of data to display in your report. The report fetches 

this information from the information you provided on the Vendor Information page of the 

Accounts Payable application.  

Select as many check boxes as you want. If you do not select any check boxes, the report 

displays only the vendor ID, vendor name, term, tax ID, account number, and the date that 

the DE542 form was sent.

In the Sort by drop-down list, select the category to sort by. You can sort the results by: 

Vendor ID, Vendor Name, Vendor Type, Term, Tax ID, Credit Limit, Credit Limit Desc, 

Balance, Balance Desc, Status, or On Hold. 

The abbreviation “desc” after an option means “descending order”—in this case, reverse 
alphabetical or reverse numerical order. By default, the system sorts this report by Vendor

You may want to examine the list to check for low credit limits, in which case you would 
choose Credit Limit. 

4. 
In the Line format drop-down list, set the report to display the filtered information in a 

single line format or a multi-line format. 

• 
The single line format displays all of your filtered information on a single line. This 

produces a much wider report that may extend past a single page, even in landscape 

mode. This format is useful for exporting vendor data to a CSV file. 

• 
The multi-line format displays each category of your filtered information on its own 

line. This may result in a much longer report, but when you print the report, it will fit 

within the width of a page. Multi-line produces a vertical report with the vendor 

information organized below each vendor name.

A/P Ledger 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Spend Management > All > AP Ledger`


Use the A/P ledger page to set up and run an A/P Ledger report. This report provides detailed 

information on vendors, invoices, and balances for review. Use this report for information 

purposes and for auditing and balancing accounts payable. 

The AP Ledger report is a standard report. If you are looking for information on financial reports, 
see Creating a Financial Report. 

Before You Begin 

Access can vary depending on your organization’s subscriptions and your permissions. If you do 

not see the option in the menu, then ask your System Administrator to check your permissions.

If your user account doesn’t have the permissions shown above, then ask your System 

Administrator for assistance. If you have administrator privileges, you can assign permissions for a 

new feature to a user or to a role. See Roles and Permissions (on page 604) for a description of 

how to review a user’s permissions. 

How to Get Here 

These are the most direct options for accessing the A/P ledger page. You may have additional 

options based on your permissions. 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Spend Management > All > Reports > Vendor Reports > A/P Ledger`


1. 
From the Applications menu, select Spend Management. 

2. 
Select the All tab. 

3. 
Under the Reports section, then Vendor Reports section, select A/P Ledger.

##### Customizing and Running the A/P Ledger Report
*Source: `RP Financial Suite Spend Management User Guide.pdf`, Page 560*

Reports 

RealPage® Financial Suite Spend Management User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.


> **Navigation Path:** `Spend Management Home Page > Reports > Vendors > A/P Ledger`


1. 
From the Spend Management home page, under the Reports section, select Vendors. 

2. 
Select A/P Ledger from the drop-down list. 

Customizing and Running the A/P Ledger Report 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > All > Reports > Vendors Reports > A/P Ledger`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Spend Management > All > Reports > Vendor Reports > A/P Ledger`


The AP Ledger report is a standard report. If you are looking for information on financial reports, 
see Creating a Financial Report. 

To customize and run the A/P Ledger report: 

1. 
On the A/P Ledger page, use the Time Period section to define the time period you want 

the report to cover. You can specify either the reporting period or the start and end dates, 

but not both. Do one of the following: 

• 
Select the Reporting period and then specify an As of date. You can either type a date 

or click 
 Calendar, and then select the date from the calendar. Select the Prompt 

on run check box when you want the system to prompt you when you run the report 

to ask for the reporting period. 

• 
Specify the starting and ending dates to identify the report’s coverage period. Set a 

specific Start date and End date. You can either type the dates or click 
 Calendar 

and select the date from the calendar. Select the Prompt on run check box to have the 

system prompt you when you run the report to ask for the date range. 

Type “p” in a date field to automatically insert the last day of the prior month. See 
Specifying Dates in Getting Started for a full list of shortcut keys related to entering dates.  

Filling In the Filters Section 

1. 
In the Vendor type drop-down list, to limit the report to one vendor type, select the vendor 

type from the Vendor type drop-down list. 

2. 
To limit the report to transactions in a summary, in the Summary drop-down list, select the 

desired summary. 

3. 
Use the From vendor and To vendor drop-down lists to select the beginning and ending 

vendor in a range to include a range of vendors in the report. 

In From vendor, select the first vendor in a range of vendors to include in the report. The 

system fills in the To vendor box with the same vendor, setting it up in case you want to 

include just one vendor in the report. 

In To vendor, select the last vendor in a range of vendors. 

---


<!-- Page 561 -->
Chapter 13: Reports 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage® Financial Suite Spend Management User Guide 

4. 
Select the Transaction currency to assign the base currency the report should use. This 

option appears only for companies that have multiple entities and that use multiple 

currencies. 

5. 
In the Location drop-down list, select a location to limit the scope of the A/P Ledger report 

to one location or location group. This option appears only for companies that have 

multiple entities and that use multiple currencies. Location is a required field. 

Select the Individual report check box to have the system generate one report per location. 

If you select the Individual Report option, you must click the Process & Store button when 
you have finished customizing the report. 

Select the Prompt on run check box to have the system ask the user to select a location 

before it will run the report. 

6. 
In the Unit drop-down list, select a unit to limit the scope of the report to only one unit. 

7. 
In the Department drop-down list, select a department or department group to limit the 

scope of the A/P Invoice Register report to one department or department group. This 

option appears only for companies that have multiple entities and that use multiple 

currencies. 

Select the Individual report check box to have the system generate one report per 

department. 

You must click the Process & Store button at the end if you select the Individual Report 
option. 

Select the Prompt on run check box to have the system ask the user to select a department 

before it will run the report. 

8. 
Find Show one-time vendors and select one of the following: 

• 
Exclude: Select this option if you don’t want to include one-time vendors in your 

report. 

• 
Include: Select this option if you want the report to include vendors who you use 

occasionally (or “one-time”). 

• 
Grouped: Select this option to include one-time vendors as a stand-alone group. 

9. 
Find Based on, and then select the Document date to base your report on the date that its 

corresponding document was created. Select G/L posting date to base your report on when 

the transaction posted to the G/L. 

10. 
Select the Include all vendors check box to include transactions to and from all vendors in 

your report. 

11. 
Select the Include zero balance vendors with activity check box to include accounts with 

zero balances. 

---


<!-- Page 562 -->
Reports 

RealPage® Financial Suite Spend Management User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

12. 
In the Show for drop-down list, select the desired locations to include. This selection applies 

regardless of the location selected in the Location drop-down list. 

All Locations: Display the data of the location/entity you selected and its children. 

This Location: Only display the data of the location/entity you selected and not of its 

children. 

Child Locations: Only display the data of the children of the location/entity you selected. 

Filling In the Format Section 

1. 
In the Sort by drop-down list, select the field by which to sort the report: Vendor ID or 

Vendor Name. Vendor ID is the default sort order. 

2. 
In the Page orientation area, to set the page layout of the report, select either Portrait or 

Landscape. 

Filling In the Titles Section and Running the Report 

Use this section to add a title, subtitle, and footer to your report. Titles, subtitles, and footers 

apply only to the .PDF version of this report. (Click Print to get the .PDF version). 

The system completes the Report Title 1 field with the system-assigned report name. This title 

displays in large type at the top of the page directly below your company name. 

1. 
You can leave the title as the default or change it by typing over the default name in Report 

Title 1. 

2. 
In Report title 2, enter the text that you want to appear under the title of the report. This 

subtitle displays in smaller type, directly beneath the main title. 

3. 
In Footer text, type the text that you want to appear in the footer of the report. Footer text 

displays at the bottom center of the report. 

You can use up to 80 characters, including spaces, in each title, subtitle, and footer. 

4. 
Click the View button to run the report. Use trial and error to get the precise results you 

want. To refine the report further, click Customize to return to the report setup page. 

Repeat this process until you’re satisfied. 

The report loads with the following options depending on your configuration: 

• 
To print the report, click the Print button. The report loads in the browser in a 

printer-friendly format. 

• 
To process and store the report in My stored reports, click the Process & store button. 

Use the Storage Options (on page 503) box to select options for processing and 

storing the report.  

• 
To add the report to the Dashboard, click the Add to dashboard button. Use the Add 

to Dashboard Parameters box to select Dashboard options.  

---

To save the report’s customizations, click the Memorize button. The Memorize Report

memorized report. For reports that you plan to run regularly, memorize the report 

when you are done setting it up. The next time you are ready to run the report, select 

the Memorized reports option on the menu, and then select Run. 

• 
To export the report, click the Export button, and then select the format in which you 

want to export it.

reports, see Creating a Financial Report.

how to review a user’s permissions.

Budget Variance with Commitments Report 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Spend Management > All > Budget Variance with Commitments`


Use the Budget variance with commitments report page to set up and run a Budget Variance 

with Commitments report. This report provides an overview of the budget and open invoices, 

including commitments. For the purposes of this report, commitments are open orders such as 

purchase orders, service contracts, and subcontracts. Use this report to compare your actual 

expenses with your budgeted expenses by month and year. To run a budget variance report 

without commitments, see Budget Variance Report (on page 555). 

If January is not the first fiscal month of an entity, the Budget Variance with Commitments 
report takes the defined month into consideration when the report is run. 

The Budget Variance with commitments report is a standard report. If you are looking for 
information on financial reports, see Creating a Financial Report. 

You can access additional information by clicking the active (blue) links in the report. 

Before You Begin 

Access can vary depending on your organization’s subscriptions and your permissions. If you do 

not see the option in the menu, then ask your System Administrator to check your permissions. 

Permissions 

These permissions are required to run and store a Budget Variance with Commitments Report in 

Spend Management:

Run

how to review a user’s permissions.
