To run a purchase orders report: 

1. 
From the Purchase orders report page, select a time period: 

• 
Use the calendar in the Start date field to select the start date. 

• 
Use the calendar in the End date field to select the end date. 

Type “p” in a date field to automatically insert the last day of the prior month. See 
Specifying Dates in Getting Started for a full list of shortcut keys related to entering 
dates.  

2. 
Select a property from the Location drop-down list. 

3. 
Optionally, to filter purchase orders for specific statuses, click the Select button, and then 

use the menu to select one or more statuses. 

4. 
Select the Include Service Orders check box when running the report to see any matching 

invoices. 

5. 
Select the report format from the Report type drop-down list: 

• 
Summary: This format lists the purchase orders without listing individual line items. 

• 
Detail: This format lists line items for each purchase order. 

6. 
In the Page orientation field, select either Portrait or Landscape. 

7. 
Type the title of the report in the Report title 1 field. 

8. 
Optionally, type the subtitle of the report in the Report title 2 field. 

9. 
Optionally, type the report footer in the Footer text field. 

10. 
Click the View button to view the report. The report loads, and depending upon your 

configuration, you may have the following options: 

• 
To print the report, click the Print button. The report loads in the browser in a 

printer-friendly format. 

• 
To process and store the report in My stored reports, click the Process & store button. 

Use the Storage options box to select options for processing and storing the report. 

See Processing and Storing a New Report for more information. 

• 
To save the report’s customizations, click the Memorize button. The Memorize report 

parameters box opens, and you can use this box to save the customizations. See 

Saving Customizations for a Memorized Report for more information. 

• 
To export the report, click the Export button, and then select the format in which you 

want to export it.

Customizing and Running the Unit Cost Report 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > All > Reports > A/P Invoices & Registers > Unit Cost`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Spend Management > All > Reports > Vendor Reports > Unit Cost`


The Unit Cost report is a standard report. If you are looking for information on financial reports, 
see Creating a Financial Report. 

To customize and run the Unit Cost report: 

1. 
Open the Accounts Payable menu. 

2. 
In the A/P Invoices and Registers section, select Unit Cost. 

Filling In the Time Period Section 

You can use one of the predefined reporting periods available from the Reporting Period and As 

of Date fields or create your own reporting period using the Start Date and End Date boxes. You 

can specify either the reporting period or the start and end dates, but not both. 

Type “p” in a date field to automatically insert the last day of the prior month. See Specifying 
Dates in Getting Started for a full list of shortcut keys related to entering dates.  

In the Time Period section, do one of the following: 

• 
Use the Reporting period drop-down list to select the desired reporting period and then 

either type a date in the As of Date field or use the calendar to select a date. These periods 

are relative to the As of Date. All periods begin on the first day of the period—that is, the 

first day of the month/quarter/year you select. For example, select Prior month as the 

reporting period, and then select a vendor to limit the report to a list of payments to that 

vendor. 

• 
Type a specific Start date and/or a specific End date or use the calendar in each field to 

select the desired date(s). 

Type “p” in a date field to automatically insert the last day of the prior month. See 
Specifying Dates in Getting Started for a full list of shortcut keys related to entering dates.  

• 
Select Prompt on run to have the system prompt you for this information at run time. 

---


<!-- Page 596 -->
Reports 

RealPage® Financial Suite Spend Management User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

If you don’t specify a reporting period and you don’t select Prompt on run, the generated 
report uses the current month to date. 

Filling In the Filters Section 

Set the Filters to get the specific data you want. You can include specific types of data, such as 

specific vendors, accounts, location, and unit. 

To get fewer and more precise results in your report, set more filters. 

1. 
Use the From Vendor and To Vendor fields to choose one vendor, a range of vendors, or all 

vendors. Leave the fields blank to include all vendors in the report. 

2. 
Use the Account from and Account to fields to choose one account or a range of accounts. 

Leave the fields blank to include all accounts in the report. 

3. 
In the Account group drop-down list, choose an account group to filter the report by. 

4. 
In the Location drop-down list, select a location to limit the scope of the Unit Cost report to 

one location or location group. 

Select the Individual report check box to have the system generate one report per location. 

You must click the Process & Store button at the end if you select the Individual Report 
option. 

Select the Prompt on run check box to have the system ask the user to select a location 

before it will run the report. 

5. 
In the Unit drop-down list, select a unit to limit the scope of the report to the unit cost for 

one unit. 

Filling In the Format Section 

• 
In the Report type drop-down list, choose the format the report, Summary or Detail. 

Filling In the Titles Section and Run the Report 

Use this section to add a title, subtitle, and footer to your report. Titles, subtitles, and footers 

apply only to the PDF version of this report. (Click Print to get the PDF version). 

The system completes the Report title 1 field with the system-assigned report name. This title 

displays in large type at the top of the page directly below your company name. 

1. 
In Report title 1, you can leave the title as the default, or change it by typing over the 

default name. 

2. 
In Report title 2, enter the text that you want to appear under the title of the report. This 

subtitle displays in smaller type, directly beneath the main title. 

3. 
In Footer text, type the text that you want to appear in the footer of the report. Footer text 

displays at the bottom center of the report. 

---

4. 
Click the View button to run the report. 

View, process, memorize, export, or customize the report by clicking one of the buttons at 
the top of the page. You can use trial and error to get the precise results you want. Fill in 
the desired fields and then click the View button to see the report. To refine the report 
further, click Customize to return to the report setup page. Repeat this process until 
you’re satisfied. Also, for complex financial reports you plan to run regularly, save the 
report when you are done setting it up. The next time you are ready to run the report, 
change only the As of date before running the report.

The detailed Unit Cost report contains the following columns:

Status 
This is the status of the cost, Posted or Paid. 

Qty 
This is the quantity of the item purchased. 

UOM 
This is the unit of measure (UOM) associated with the quantity (Qty) 

field. 

Price 
This is the price of one item.

#### RealPage Financial Suite
*Source: `RP Financial Suite Spend Management User Guide.pdf`, Page 612*

Appendices 

RealPage® Financial Suite Spend Management User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

The RealPage Financial Suite integrates a traditional back-office accounting system with general 

ledger, cash management, accounts receivable, and accounts payable applications with new and 

updated applications that let you save valuable time by streamlining and automating your daily 

processes and workflow. Some applications described in the documentation are optional and can 

be purchased through RealPage sales. RealPage Financial Suite is composed of RealPage 

Accounting core applications, optional applications, and add-on applications.  

The RealPage Accounting suite contains these core accounting applications: 

• 
Accounts Payable: Use the Accounts Payable application to manage vendor records, pay 

vendors, create custom terms, adjust accounts with credit and debit memos, and create and 

print A/P reports. 

• 
Accounts Receivable: Use the Accounts Receivable application to manage the full A/R cycle, 

manage customer records, receivables transactions, and generate reports, create and send 

invoices, apply penalties and adjust accounts, make deposits, and deliver statements. 

• 
Company: Use the Company application to manage your company setup and to set up user 

accounts. Administrators can define security and global settings, grant permissions to users, 

and manage subscriptions to applications and services. 

• 
Dashboard: Use Dashboards to get real-time snapshots of information. 

• 
General Ledger: Use the General Ledger application to post journal entries, design and run 

reports, create budgets, and more. The General Ledger is the central ledger for the 

company. 

• 
Cash Management: Use the Cash Management application to manage your cash accounts, 

including checking accounts, savings institutions, and credit cards. 

• 
Reporting Portal: Use the Reporting Portal application to set up owner portals for owners 

and investors so you can upload financial reports and other documents for them in a central 

location. 

• 
Reports: Use customizable reports to get real-time snapshots of information. 

• 
Platform (Customization) Services: Administrators use the Platform Services (or 

Customization Services) application to customize and extend the RealPage Accounting 

system. 

• 
Multi-entity: Administrators use the Multi-entity application to set up and run multi-entity 

shared companies. 

• 
Forecasting & Planning: Use this application to create and refine budgets, and to associate 

properties with a budget when publishing it. 

These applications are part of RealPage Accounting core applications, but are optional as not all 

of our clients need them: 

• 
Global Consolidations: This application is used by multi-currency companies. 

---


<!-- Page 613 -->
Chapter 13: Appendices 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage® Financial Suite Spend Management User Guide 

• 
Taxes: This application is used by companies who are required to collect and report value 

added taxes (VAT) to the United Kingdom’s tax authority, HM Revenue & Customs. 

The RealPage Financial Suite contains RealPage Accounting applications, plus additional 

applications that you can purchase to extend and enhance the functionality of the suite. 

• 
Job Cost and Reserves: Use this application to manage costs for property improvements 

and new developments. 

If your company does not subscribe to Job Cost, then use the standalone Replacement 

Reserves application to track replacement and repair expenses and request 
reimbursements from lenders. 

• 
Spend Management: Use this application to set up a budget and bring visibility to 

spending, to analyze the impact of sourcing strategies, assess business savings, and review 

compliance with preferred suppliers and contracts. 

• 
Commercial Property Management: Use this application to set up your properties, 

locations, floors, and units and then configure and manage billing, including straight line 

rent billing, and percentage rent billing. Manage the billing and payment cycle, including 

inter-entity billing, collecting fees, and recovering expenses. 

• 
Condo and Co-op: Use this application to set up condominiums and co-operatives and then 

manage owners, bill dues and other charges, and manage unit maintenance.  

• 
Financial Close Management: Use this application to simplify your month-end and year-end 

close processes by reconciling work papers into one package that you can download and 

open in Excel. 

• 
Fixed Assets: Use this application to manage your assets, including depreciation and asset 

disposal.  

• 
Investor Tracking: Use this application to track contributions from and distributions to 

investors. Using this application, you can invoice contributions, calculate and pay out 

distributions, and run reports of these activities.  

• 
Procore Integration: Integrate Job Cost with the Procore construction management 

platform to synchronize job information, job budgets, and cost totals between the two 

systems.  

To purchase any of the add-ons, contact your RealPage Account Representative.

#### Roles and Permissions
*Source: `RP Financial Suite Spend Management User Guide.pdf`, Page 616*

Appendices 

RealPage® Financial Suite Spend Management User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Roles and Permissions 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > Setup > Users/Roles`


Permissions determine the specific features and activities that a user can access and the reports 

that the user can run. 

User-Based Permissions 

If you have not enabled roles in your company, then your company employs user-based 

permissions. With this permissions model, each user or user group has its own set of permissions. 

When you assign permissions to a particular user, your selections expand or limit what that user 

can see and do. 

Role-Based Permissions 

If your company enabled roles, then you use role-based permissions in your system. Using this 

permissions model, you can define a set of roles, and then assign the roles to users or user 

groups. For example, you can define an A/P Clerk role that includes permissions to enter and pay 

A/P invoices. 

Reviewing a User’s Permissions 

To review a user’s actual permissions: 

1. 
Open the Company menu, and then click the Setup tab. 

2. 
Select Users. 

3. 
Find the user, and then click the View permissions & roles link. The system opens the 

Permissions & roles report page. 

4. 
Review the user’s permissions. Optionally, click Print, and then use your printer’s dialog box 

to print the report. 

5. 
When you are finished viewing the user’s permissions report, click the Close button.

#### List Features and Controls
*Source: `RP Financial Suite Spend Management User Guide.pdf`, Page 622*

Appendices 

RealPage® Financial Suite Spend Management User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

List Features and Controls 

This section describes how to use each of the features and controls that let you manage lists. 

List pages provide a means of viewing all of the objects of a particular type such as invoices or 

posted payments. All lists have a set of columns that are sorted alphanumerically, usually based 

on the most important field in the list. 

The system provides searches and filters that you can use to customize a list so that it displays 

exactly the records that you want. You can save the sort and filter customizations as a View. 

These are the most commonly used list features and controls: 

Sorts 
You can sort on most columns in a list. Learn about Sorting Lists. 

Filters 
Each column in a list has a filter field above it. Type a letter, word, or phrase 
to limit the list to records with that letter, word, or phrase in the column. 

You can also filter columns that contain check boxes. Type True to find all 
items with the check box selected or type False to exclude all records that 
have the check box selected. Learn more about List Filters (on page 613). 

Drop-down lists During the setup phase, you add the items to drop-down lists that others 

use when working with the system’s lists and forms. 

Drop-down list 
options 

Many drop-down lists offer three options to allow you to add a new item to 
the list, find an item in the list, and view the record of a selected item in the 
list. Learn about field level controls in drop-down lists. 

Views 
You can configure lists when they have these controls at the top: 

• 
All drop-down list (It either displays All or the name of the currently 
selected view) 

• 
Manage views drop-down 

• 
Advanced filters 

• 
Clear all filters 

When they are configured, you can save the settings so that you can 
re-apply the view settings later. Learn more about Views. 

Include Private 
Select this check box to include records that users created at the entity level 
in addition to records created at the top level. To exclude records created for 
a specific entity, clear the Include Private check box. 

Include Inactive 
Select this check box to include records with a status of inactive. 

Searches 
Type text in any box that appears at the top of a column to search for 
records with matching text in that column. 

---



#### Managing Lists
*Source: `RP Financial Suite Spend Management User Guide.pdf`, Page 623*

Appendix C: Appendices 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage® Financial Suite Spend Management User Guide 

Managing Lists 

Lists provide access to like records. After you create a record, you can access it from its list. Most 

lists allow you to add, edit, view, and delete the records in it. You can also export the list to an 

XML file or a PDF file. After exporting a list, you can import the list into an external application like 

Excel, and then print the list from that application. 

Some lists allow you to access related information. For example, from the customers list, you can 

also access the customers A/R ledger and view a breakdown of the total amount that the 

customer owes. 

Since the list page is where you perform most of your work, the system provides several features 

to let you filter and sort lists and create and manage custom views of your data. 

• 
Sorting (on page 612): Sort the list alphabetically by the data in the desired column. 

• 
Filtering (on page 613): Filter lists so that you see only the data that you need. 

• 
Views: Create a custom view to determine which columns appear in your lists, and apply a 

filter so that the list appears just the way you want it. 

Lists and Links 

Each list is unique and can offer links to let you navigate into an associated record to see more 

detailed data. For example, some invoice lists have a Preview link that, when clicked, opens the 

invoice in PDF format in a browser window. Another type of list may have a link to the customer 

record or the vendor record. 

Many reports present figures as links that, when clicked, open the associated record. This example 

shows links in the Debit and Credit columns of a journal entry. When you click a link, the system 

navigates to more information, allowing you to delve into the details. 

---



##### Sorting Lists
*Source: `RP Financial Suite Spend Management User Guide.pdf`, Page 624*

Appendices 

RealPage® Financial Suite Spend Management User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Sorting Lists 

You can display a list by a column’s ascending or descending values by clicking the column name. 

An arrow to the right of the column name indicates the sort direction. The arrow points 
 up for 

ascending order and 
 down for descending order. Only one column can control the list’s sort 

order at a time. 

In this example, the system sorts the list by the data in the Entity ID column. The sort arrow 

appears on the column that the system is sorting on. 

To reverse the sort order, click the column name again. The sort order reverses, and the arrow 

flips direction to indicate that the sort is reversed. 

---



##### Filtering Lists
*Source: `RP Financial Suite Spend Management User Guide.pdf`, Page 625*

Appendix C: Appendices 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage® Financial Suite Spend Management User Guide 

To sort on a different column, click the desired column name. 

Filtering Lists 

Using Column Filters 

Column filters are text boxes that appear at the top of each column. Filters let you find items in a 

list that match the text that you enter. 

To apply a column filter: 

• 
Type the text that you want to find in the column filter, and then press ENTER. 

The system searches for matches, and then displays the matches in the list. 

If a text box does not appear at the top of a column, the column is not searchable. 

Using the Wild Card Character 

• 
Use the % symbol as a wild card or placeholder. For example, typing “san%” in the City 

column’s filter would find both San Francisco and Santa Diego. 

• 
Placing the % in front of text tells the system to find these letters in the middle of text in a 

field. 

• 
Placing % at the end of a word tells the system to find the word and any letters that follow 

the word. 

• 
Use % to filter text columns only. The % symbol does not work on non-text columns such as 

date columns or amount columns. 

• 
For best success, anticipate differences and adapt your filter to account for them. 

To find records that contain a specific value: 

• 
Type the first part of the value. 

---


<!-- Page 626 -->
Appendices 

RealPage® Financial Suite Spend Management User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

If you are looking for a contact in a city that starts with “San,” then you can filter the Contact 

list by typing “san” in the City filter field, then and pressing ENTER. The system searches for 

contacts with a city that begins with San, such as San Jose, San Francisco, and Santa Fe. 

• 
If you know only part of the text that you want to find, type “%” and then type the text that 

you have. 

For example, if you are looking for a contact with the letters “Will” in the name, but you do 

not have the full, correct name of the business, type “%will%” in the Contact name filter of 

the Contacts list, and then press ENTER. The system searches for matches, retrieving all 

contacts that contain the letters “will” in the Contact name field. 

Example 

Your company uses this standard format for naming invoice summaries: Invoices: Month Year. 

When you want to find all June summaries, type “%June” in the filter above the Summary column, 

and then press ENTER to apply the filter. Placing the % in front of June tells the system that the 

word “June” appears in the middle of the text string. Placing % at the end of the word “June” tells 

the system to find the word June and any word with letters that follow the word “June,” such as 

“Juneteenth.” 

Searches for Units 

You can search for a unit by entering any part of the unit ID. The system will find matches for any 

part of the unit ID string. For example, if the units in your property are configured with an 

alphanumeric pattern such as A-10, A-11, A12, B-20, B-21, B-22, then you can enter any part of 

the string, such as “22,” and the system will find B-22.  

The string does not have to start with the entered value to match. Typing “A” finds a list of units 

on the A floor as in our example or all units that have “A” in the unit ID. 

Displaying One-Time Items 

Some quick-entry records are set for one-time use. For example, you may have a seasonal 

customer, such as a Halloween supply store, or customers who pay only once and are not likely to 

purchase again. 

Create the customer record so that you can record the cash receipt, but because you don’t need 

to see that customer in your customer list regularly, flag the customer as Exclude from the 

---


<!-- Page 627 -->
Appendix C: Appendices 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage® Financial Suite Spend Management User Guide 

company contact list. One-time customers aren’t included in the list unless you specify them to be 

included. 

To include one-time items in the list, select the Include One-Time check box. The system displays 

the one-time items along with regular items and adds a One-Time column to show which items 

are one-time records. 

Example 

You may have a customer who purchases from you only once a year, and you do not want to see 

the customer’s name in the list all the time. You still need to create a Customer record so that you 

can record the cash receipt, but since you do not need to see the customer in your Customers list 

regularly, edit the Customer record, and select the One-Time Use check box. 

Including Inactive Records in Search Results 

Almost every kind of record in the system has a Status field with choices of Active and Inactive. 

The Include Inactive check box appears at the top of many lists and allows the system to include 

the inactive records in search results. 

• 
Select the Include Inactive check box to include items set to a status of Inactive in the 

search. The system refreshes the list and adds a Status column to indicate which items are 

active and which are inactive. 

• 
Clear the Include Inactive check box to prevent inactive items from appearing in the list. 

A list can contain items that are inactive but still present because they link to transaction data. For 

example, you may have a vendor who no longer carries items you need to purchase. In the vendor 

record, you flag the vendor as Inactive. Inactive vendors aren’t included in the list unless you 

select Include Inactive.

Include Private 

Customer records created prior to June 2020 could be created at the entity level. Records created 

at the entity level are private. Customer records that you create today can be created only at the 

top level. The Include Private check box controls whether entity level customer records appear in 

the Customers list. The Include Private check box is selected by default so that all records appear 

in the Customers list. 

• 
Clear the Include Private check box to display only public records (records that are set up at 

the top level). 

• 
Select the Include Private check box to show all customer records in the list, regardless of 

where they were created. When the Include Private check box is selected, the list includes 

the Entity column, identifying the entity to which the private item belongs.

check box appears above the list. 

• 
Select the Display Hierarchy check box to illustrate the relationships between the records. 

• 
Clear the check box to flatten the list so that no relationship information appears in the list.

Advanced Filters 

Use advanced filters to apply standard operators to a list’s columns so that you can view only the 

records you want. You can do this using the simple column filter boxes, but advanced filters offer 

many more operators. Click the Advanced filters link to open the filtering box. 

The Advanced filters section has three fields per filter row. 

a) Column name field: The first field is a drop-down list where you select the column that you 

want to filter. 

b) Operator field: The second field is where you select the operator that evaluates each record. 

In the example, the starts with operator evaluates whether the vendor name starts with the 

letters Ch. For a list of operators and what they do, see Operator definitions (on page 618). 

c) Search field: The third field is where you type that foe which you want to search. 

d) Filter row: One row is called a filter row. You can add additional filter rows by clicking the 

Add filter link. To remove the last filter row, click the Delete last filter link. 

Filtering by Check Box Status 

In some lists, you can search for records by the status of a check box. To search for records with 

unselected check boxes, type “false.” To search for selected check boxes, type “true.”

##### Operator Definitions
*Source: `RP Financial Suite Spend Management User Guide.pdf`, Page 630*

Appendices 

RealPage® Financial Suite Spend Management User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

This example shows how to search for items that are not flagged as at risk or holdover. 

Clearing Filters 

Click the Clear all filters link to remove all filter conditions from the list. Clear the filters before 

beginning a new search, or when you want to restore all of the data to the list. 

Operator Definitions 

The following operators are available for use when filtering: 

• 
Equals: Displays all records in which the data in the chosen column matches the text or 

number in the Value field. 

• 
Less than: Displays all records in which the value of the number in the chosen column is less 

than the number in the Value field. 

• 
Greater than: Displays all records in which the value of the number in the chosen column is 

greater than the number in the Value field. 

• 
Less or equal: Displays all records in which the value of the number in the chosen column is 

less than or equal to the number in the Value field. 

• 
Greater or equal: Displays all records in which the value of the number in the chosen 

column is greater than or equal to the number in the Value field. 

• 
Not equal to: Displays all records in which the data in the chosen column does not match 

the text or number in the Value field. 

• 
Contains: Displays all records in which a character or group of characters in the chosen 

column matches the character or group of characters in the Value field. The characters must 

match in the same order. For example, “ox” typed in the Value field may return records for 

Oxygen Inc., Boxing Agency, and Clorox, if those were values in the chosen column. 

• 
Does not contain: Displays all records in which no character or group of characters in the 

chosen column matches the character or group of characters in the Value field. 

• 
Starts with: Displays all records in which the first character or group of characters in the 

chosen column matches the character or group of characters in the Value field. The 

characters must match in the same order. For example, if you have an item ID scheme that 

uses initial letters to identify the product type, you can select the item ID column and set the 

Value field to these letters to display all records for that product type.

##### Displaying a Hierarchical View
*Source: `RP Financial Suite Spend Management User Guide.pdf`, Page 631*

Appendix C: Appendices 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage® Financial Suite Spend Management User Guide 

• 
Ends with: Displays all records in which the last character or group of characters in the 

chosen column matches the character or group of characters in the Value field. The 

characters must match in the same order. For example, if you tag the end of the item ID for 

all custom order items with the letters “CO,” you can select the item ID column and set the 

value to CO to display all records for custom order items. 

• 
Includes: Displays all records that match items in a comma delimited list in the Value field. 

• 
Excludes: Displays all records that do not match items in a comma delimited list in the 

Value field. 

• 
Field equals null: Displays all records that have a null or empty field. 

• 
Field not equals null: Displays all records that do not have a null or empty field. 

Using Wildcards 

Use the % character as a wildcard to match zero or more characters in text columns. 

Examples: 

bank% will display all vendors that have “bank” at the beginning of the name, like Bank of 

Metropolis. 

%bank or %bank% will display all vendors that have “bank” anywhere in the name, like Bank 

of Metropolis, Metropolis Bank, and MetroBank. 

% bank will display all vendors that end with the word “bank,” like Metropolis Bank. 

Displaying a Hierarchical View 

Some lists, such as the Locations list, can display a hierarchical structure of parent-child 

relationships using icons and indentations. 

Use the Display Hierarchy check box to view the list to help you identify locations that are 

subsidiaries of parent records. 

Parent records can have up to five levels of child records, allowing you to view and act on the 

records as needed. You can still sort and search for records as you would in any view. 

If the parent record is not visible because of permission restrictions, or if you filtered the list in a 

way that the parent is not visible, the system still shows the child as indented and colored to 

indicate that it is a child in a relationship. 

To toggle between flat view and hierarchical view of a list: 

• 
To switch to a flat view, clear the Display hierarchy check box on the white bar above the 

list. Clearing the check box causes all items to be displayed by their unique ID, whether they 

have relationships to other items. 

• 
To return to the hierarchical view, select the Display hierarchy check box.

Exporting from Lists 

You can export most lists to several available file formats and then import the data into an 

external application, such as Microsoft Word or Microsoft Excel. 

Although you can export up to 25,000 rows, if you want to save time and effort, we recommend 

that you filter your list to pinpoint only the information you need to export by creating a custom 

view. That way, when you export the list, you’ll have a spreadsheet tailored to the information you 

need. You can export any view of this list for use on your local computer. 

Use column filters, advanced filters, and views to filter the data. For instructions, refer to 

Managing Lists. 

If you have a sorted and filtered list that you use consistently, you can create and save it as a 

custom report for convenience. With a custom report, you need to set the filtering and 

parameters only once to enable you to generate the report as needed after that. 

To export a list of records from the system: 

1. 
Select the Include inactive check box to include items with an Inactive status in the data 

export results or clear the Include inactive check box to exclude inactive items. 

Some lists do not offer an option to filter by active/inactive status. 

2. 
Select the Include private check box to include items that are associated with an entity or 

clear the Include private check box to exclude these items. 

Some lists do not offer an option to include and exclude private items. 

3. 
Click the Export button. 

4. 
Select the format to which you want to export the list. 

• 
CSV: Select this format if you plan to move the data from one program to another. 

You can use files that you save in CSV format with any spreadsheet program. 

• 
Word: When you select this option, the system exports the list in Word format. If a list 

of conversion formats displays, select HTML document. 

• 
Excel: When you select this option, the system exports the list in XLS format. If you see 

an error message about file type and extension type incompatibility, you can disregard 

the message and select Yes. 

• 
PDF: Select this option if you plan to print or share the list. When you select this 

option, the system exports the list and tries to open the file in the browser. If 

prompted, select Yes to allow the PDF to open. 

• 
CSV for import: Select this option if you want to export data, change it, or add to it, 

and then import it into the system again.

Finding Transactions in a Specific State 

List views of transactions provide a hub for viewing and accessing all transactions of a specific 

type, for example, bills or invoices. 

There are two ways to locate transactions in a specific state: 

• 
Filter for the transaction state on the fly: In the transaction list view, type the state in the 

State column, then click Go. The list displays only those transactions in that state. 

• 
Create a permanent custom view that filters for the transaction state: Create the view and 

set the filter to State = <state>, where <state> equals the state you are seeking, such as 

Draft, Posted, Paid, Reversed, and so forth. This custom view is always available from the 

transaction list.

Finding an Item in a Drop-down List 

The field-level Find command lets you search for a value in a drop-down list.

find an item in a long list that you want to add to a drop-down list.

Each search form is unique to the type of information that you want to find, but all search 

forms have these common commands. 

• 
Clear all filters: Remove all text from the search fields from previous searches. Clearing 

a search returns all of the items of this type. 

• 
Cancel: Exit the search form without adding a new value to the drop-down list or text 

box. 

• 
Select: Add the item to the drop-down list.

appear in rows below the form.

Audit Trails 

Each action you take can impact your financial statements, so both internal and external 

stakeholders need to know how things have changed and who made those changes. The system 

audit trail keeps track of the changes so that you know who made changes to a particular record 

and when they made the changes. The View audit trail command is available on most records. 

Viewing Audit Trails 

You can access the audit trail of a record. The method of accessing the audit trail varies based on 

the record type. 

Accessing the Audit Trail  

1. 
Open the record that you want to examine. 

2. 
Click the More actions button, and then select the View audit trail option.  

Instead of the More Actions button, some records have a View Audit Trail button. 

The Audit trail list opens with a list of changes that users have made.  

Buttons 

Audit Trail Box/Audit Trail Page 

Done 
Saves any changes and opens the previous page 

Help 
Opens the Online Help page 

More actions 
Opens a drop-down list with the following options: 

• 
Export to CSV: Downloads the report as a CSV file 

• 
Export to Excel: Downloads the report as an XLS file 

• 
Export to PDF: Downloads the report as a PDF file 

• 
Table size: Allows you to select the number of rows you want to 

display per application page

Attachments Appendix 

This appendix contains supplementary material about adding attachments. 

Adding an Attachment to the System 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > Storage > 
 Attachments`


You can create an attachment record in the Attachments list to upload one or more files into a 

single attachment and store it in RealPage Financial Suite. Any attachment records you create will 

be available in Attachment drop-down lists throughout RealPage Financial Suite; for example, 

when you are entering a new transaction or record and you want to attach supporting 

documents. 

To add an attachment, you need at least one attachment folder in which to store the attachment. 

Your company may have created an initial folder for you. If no folder currently exists, you can 

quickly create one while you are adding an attachment.  

To add a new attachment record in the system: 

1. 
In the Attachments list, click the Add button. 

The Select attachments page opens. 

2. 
Type a unique ID for the attachment record. If your company is configured to auto-number, 

then the system automatically displays an ID for the attachment. 

3. 
Type a Name that identifies your attachment. If you leave this field blank, the system 

automatically adds a Name for the attachment based on the first file that you upload. You 

can change this name as needed. 

Since an attachment record may contain more than one file, choose a name that describes 

all of the files in your attachment. For example, if you attached 20 scanned invoices to 

support 20 invoices, then you could name the attachment “Invoice Scans - 20 Files.” 

4. 
Select the Folder where you want to store your attachment in the system. If you have the 

appropriate Attachment permissions, you can create a folder:  

• 
Click the down arrow beside the Folder field, and then click Add. 

• 
Type a Name for the folder. 

5. 
Optionally, type a Description of the attachment. 

6. 
In the Attach files section: 

• 
Click the Choose files button, select the file(s) you want to attach, and then click the 

Open button. Alternatively, you can drag and drop files directly from your file explorer 

into the browser window. 

A P P E N D I X E

Scanning Documents with a Scanner 

Use a personal scanning device to scan a document and automatically attach it to an A/P invoice, 

purchase order, or service contract. 

Before you can use the scanning device, complete these required steps: 

1. 
Set up a scanning device through your local IT department. 

2. 
Download the scanning software (on page 641). 

3. 
Enable device scanning (on page 641). 

Enabling the Device Scanning Feature 

To enable device scanning: 

1. 
Click your sign-in name at the top of any page and select My preferences. 

2. 
In the Display section, find the Personalize interactive behavior section. 

3. 
Select the Enable single scan upload check box to enable it.  

Clear the check box to disable the feature. 

4. 
Click the Save button. 

Downloading the Scanning Software 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts Payable > All > 
 A/P Invoices`


You can scan and attach documents to several types of records in the RealPage Financial Suite, 

including A/P invoices, purchase orders, service contracts, and vendor records. You can also use 

the scanner in Spend Management Site Experience. 

To download the scanning software: 

1. 
Open the Accounts Payable menu. 

2. 
Select 
 A/P invoices. The A/P invoice page opens. If your computer has scanning 

enabled but does not have the scanning service installed, a box appears that allows you to 

install the scanning software.

If the Dynamsoft single scan application is already installed, a prompt to install the newest 
version appears when you add an A/P invoice, a purchase order, a service contract, or a 
vendor from a core Accounting product, scan a document into the document dashboard, 
or scanning in the Spend Management Site Experience product. There is no need to 
uninstall the previous version of the software, just download the newest version. 

3. 
Click Download (for user). 

4. 
Find the downloaded file in your browser’s default download location. 

5. 
Double-click the file to open the download. 

6.

wizard launches. 

7. 
Click Next to step through the wizard, as needed. 

8. 
Click Close when the wizard has completed.

After installation, restart the browser. 

Naming Scanned A/P Invoices 

The file number for a single scan is a combination of the A/P invoice number and the date. The 

file number for multiple scans is a combination of the A/P invoice number and the date, plus a 

version number appended to the end. For example: 

• 
First scan: 846566-09-26-17 

• 
Second scan: 846566-09-26-17-1 

• 
Third scan: 846566-09-26-17-2

Appendix H: Appendices 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Vendor Information Page 

Use this box to add vendor records. A vendor record has six tabs: 

• 
Vendor: The Vendor tab has two sections: the summary section and the Primary contact 
section. Use this tab to record all of the contact details for the primary contact of this 
vendor. 

If the vendor is an online vendor with a Storefront Supplier Code, when Vendor 
Credentialing attempts to update the vendor status to Inactive, the RealPage Accounting 
system checks the Storefront supplier code field and, if populated, will mark it as Don’t 
Pay instead of Inactive. 

• 
Additional information: This tab has four sections: Vendor details, Billing details, Vendor 
merge, and CA DE 542. Use this tab to record additional details about this vendor. 

• 
Contact list: This tab has two sections: Pay to/Return to and Contact list. Use this tab to 
define the contact to whom to direct payments and to list all contacts associated with this 
vendor. 

• 
Payment information: This tab has three sections: Payment details, Payment services, and 
Vendor account number. Use this tab to define how and when to pay this vendor.  

• 
Restrictions: This tab has one section. Use this tab to restrict access to this vendor. 

• 
Insurance/License: This tab has three sections for three insurance policies and licenses. Use 
this tab to maintain details about insurance and licenses that cover this vendor.

Fields 

Vendor Information – Vendor Tab – Vendor Section 

ID 
The system provides two mutually exclusive ways to add vendor IDs. You 
can type your own unique ID. 

This ID cannot be overwritten after the vendor is created. 

Best Practices for Creating Identifiers 

An ID enables your company to keep track of a specific type of 
information, such as G/L account, department, location, item, project, 
class, transaction, vendor, and customer. You can create IDs by adding 
them on the fly or by having the system automatically add them from a 
preset numbering scheme. 

Whichever method you choose, we recommend against using leading 
zeros as part of an ID. IDs with leading zeros can cause errors when you 
import information into your company from Excel because Excel 
removes the leading zeros. 

Best practice: Use a character as a prefix to your ID; for example, C0001 
for a customer ID. 

Workaround: if you must use leading zeros in IDs, then convert the 
column of ID numbers to text format in Excel before importing the file 
content. Excel will not remove the leading zeros when you save the file. 
Remember to do this every time you use a template to import 
information that requires IDs. 

Name 
The name of the vendor as it will appear in lists and menus across your 

company. 

One-time use 
This check box designates the vendor as a one-time or occasional use 

vendor that you don’t want to include in your standard vendor lists. 

Corporate vendor 
Select the Corporate vendor check box when you want to prevent 

invoices for the vendor from appearing in the Site Experience. Also, 

corporate vendors do not appear in the Site Experience. 

This vendor is an 

investor 

Select this check box if the vendor invests in the company. When you 

select this option, the Investor Information tab appears on the vendor’s 

record. 

Status 
Options: Active and Inactive. Active vendors can have A/P invoices 

entered and payments issued. Inactive vendors cannot.

or Edge web browsers.

adjustment that includes this vendor. You can override the A/P account by selecting a

This drop-down list appears only when you’ve enabled the feature. The system fills in the

 You can override the account later on the A/P invoices page.

• 
In the Contact tax group drop-down list, select a contact tax group. Assigning a

The contact tax group must exist before being added to this vendor. 

4. 
In the Credit limit field, type the amount of credit extended to you by the vendor. 

5. 
To put a vendor on credit hold, select the On hold check box. This status prevents users 

from entering A/P invoices into the system for the vendor. 

6. 
Select the Don’t pay check box to stop payments to the vendor from the system. Users can 

add A/P invoices with the vendor, but the system prevents payment until someone clears 

this check box.  

The Don’t pay check box can be used as a temporary measure when your company is 

waiting for supporting documentation from the vendor such as proof of insurance or 

licenses. 

The Don’t pay check box is also useful when your company determines that it will no longer 

do business with a particular vendor and does not intend to make any further payments to 

that vendor. This decision could be due to various reasons such as poor quality of goods or 

services, unresolved disputes, or the vendor going out of business.

in this field, as other users can see these comments.

The US government offers set-asides for businesses with special designations. The designations 

include women-owned businesses, veteran-owned businesses, HUBZone businesses (businesses 

that are located in a traditionally underutilized business area), and 8(a) businesses owned by 

socially and economically disadvantaged people. You can flag a vendor’s business with one of

Payment Details Section

You can override the vendor’s default preferred payment method on both these pages.

Setting Up Automatic Payment Notifications 

You can have the system notify vendors that they have been paid. As part of the setup process for 

automatic payment notifications:

1.

notifying them of the payment. If a credit was applied to the payment in full, then the 

system sends an email with a list of invoices to which the credits were applied. 

2. 
On the Contacts list tab for the vendor, verify the vendor’s name and email address. 

• 
The system sends the payment notification to the email address listed in the Pay to 

contact, and the uses the vendor’s Print as name (from the Vendor tab) in the email 

greeting line. 

• 
If the vendor’s Pay to contact is “Same as Vendor,” the system uses the “Print as” name 

and email address from the Vendor tab.

2. 
In the Vendor insurance type list, select the appropriate option to indicate the type of 

insurance or license that you want to maintain for this vendor, such as Liability or Worker’s 

Compensation. 

3. 
In the Expiration date list, type the date on which the insurance policy or the license expires. 

4. 
In the Carrier name field, type the name of the insurance carrier. 

5. 
In the Policy number field, type the insurance policy number of the license identification 

number. 

6. 
Repeat these steps for up to three insurance policies or licenses. 

7. 
Click the Save button to save the vendor record.

#### Contacts
*Source: `RP Financial Suite Spend Management User Guide.pdf`, Page 690*

Appendices 

RealPage® Financial Suite Spend Management User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Contacts 

Contact records hold all of the information you need to contact an individual or business, 

including the name, email address, phone number, mailing address, and more. These contacts are 

associated with one or more records across many applications. The system uses contact 

information to: 

• 
Send event notifications 

• 
Determine the ship-to/bill-to addresses in Order Entry and Purchasing transactions 

• 
Determine the pay-to/return-to addresses in Order Entry and Purchasing transactions 

• 
Determine the tax on transactions 

Contacts are not dimensions like Vendors, Employees, or Customers. Instead, think of your 

contacts as a common, shared address book used across your company by many people for a 

variety of purposes. 

The Contacts feature lets you manage your contact information. Using the Contacts feature, you 

can view, edit, duplicate, and print existing contact and mailing information.

#### Contact Field Definitions
*Source: `RP Financial Suite Spend Management User Guide.pdf`, Page 693*

Contact Field Definitions 

Contact Prefixes 

When uploading a vendor list, you must indicate a primary vendor contact. However, you may 

also assign optional return-to and pay-to contacts. The difference between these designations is a 

contact prefix. In this instance, the return-to contact fields have an R_ prefix and the pay-to 

contact fields have a P_ prefix. 

Primary Contact: None 

Vendor Pay to Contact: P_ 

Vendor Return to Contact: R_ 

Customer Bill to Contact: B_ 

Customer Shipto Contact: S_ 

If either the return-to and/or pay-to contact fields are not included, the primary contact 
information is used instead. 

For example, the COMPANY_NAME field when used for the return-to contact would be 

R_COMPANY_NAME, and the pay-to contact would be P_COMPANY_NAME.

uploads: 

Vendor upload — field example

Adding a New Contact 

To add a new contact: 

1. 
From a drop-down list that features contacts (such as a Bill to or Ship to list), click the Add 

link. The Contact Information box opens. 

2. 
Complete the fields in the Contact information tab: 

• 
Type the contact’s last name in the Last name field. 

• 
Type the contact’s first name in the First name field. 

• 
Type the contact’s middle name in the Middle name field. 

• 
Type the contact’s title in the Mr./Ms./Mrs. field. 

• 
Type the contact’s email address in the Primary email address field. 

• 
Type the contact’s primary phone number in the Primary phone field. 

• 
Type the company associated with the contact in the Company name field. 

• 
Type a unique name for the contact in the Suggested contact name field. 

This field cannot be changed after you create the contact record. 

• 
Type the contact name for printing in the Print as field. 

• 
Select Active from the Status drop-down list. 

---


<!-- Page 701 -->
Appendix I: Appendices 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage® Financial Suite Spend Management User Guide 

3. 
Go to the Mailing information tab, and then add the mailing information for the contact: 

• 
Type the contact’s address in the Address line 1 field. 

• 
Type the second line of the address for the contact in the Address line 2 field. 

• 
Type the contact’s address city in the City field. 

• 
Type the contact’s address state in the State/Province field. 

• 
Type the contact’s ZIP Code in the ZIP Code field. 

• 
Select the contact’s country from the Country code drop-down list. 

4. 
Go to the Additional information tab, and then add additional information for the contact: 

• 
Type the contact’s secondary phone number in the Secondary phone field. 

• 
Type the contact’s cell phone number in the Mobile field. 

• 
Type the contact’s pager number in the Pager field. 

• 
Type the contact’s fax number in the Fax field. 

• 
Type the contact’s secondary email address in the Secondary email address field. 

• 
Type the contact’s primary web address in the Primary URL field. 

• 
Type the contact’s secondary web address in the Secondary URL field. 

• 
If the contact is taxable, select the Taxable check box. Otherwise, clear the check box. 

• 
If the contact is taxable, type the contact’s Taxpayer Identification Number in the Tax 

ID field. 

• 
If the contact is taxable, select the contact’s tax group from the Contact tax group 

drop-down list. 

5. 
Click the Save button. The system adds the contact.

#### Importing Data into RealPage Accounting
*Source: `RP Financial Suite Spend Management User Guide.pdf`, Page 706*



##### Downloading Import Templates
*Source: `RP Financial Suite Spend Management User Guide.pdf`, Page 706*

Appendices 

RealPage® Financial Suite Spend Management User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Importing Data into RealPage Accounting 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > Setup > Import data`


To import data from an external, non-OneSite source, follow these steps: 

OneSite users can refer to a faster process to import their data. Contact your Customer Support 
Representative for assistance. 

1. 
Download the template (on page 694) 

2. 
Fill in the template (on page 695) 

3. 
Save the template as a CSV file (on page 696) 

4. 
Import the CSV file (on page 696) 

Downloading Import Templates 

Each object has a unique template that you must use for importing data. There are three ways 

you can find a template for your object type: 

• 
Download the template directly from a list. 

• 
Use the Download template link in the Import box. 

• 
Download the template from the Import data page. 

Downloading directly from a list 

• 
In some lists, such as the Working budgets list, the list has a Template button that you can 

click to download the template that you need. 

Downloading from an Import box 

• 
In other lists that have an Import button, click the Import button to open the Import box, 

where a Download template link appears next to the Choose File button. 

Downloading from the Import Data Page 

If you don’t find a download button in the list or a link in the Import box, then you can download 

the template file from the Import data page. See Download a Template from the Import Data 

Page (on page 695). 

---



##### Downloading a Template from the Import Data Page
*Source: `RP Financial Suite Spend Management User Guide.pdf`, Page 707*



##### Filling In an Import Template with Data
*Source: `RP Financial Suite Spend Management User Guide.pdf`, Page 707*

Appendix K: Appendices 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage® Financial Suite Spend Management User Guide 

Downloading a Template from the Import Data Page 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > Import Data`


We recommend downloading a new blank template from the Import data page whenever you 

import information into the system. This is important because:  

• 
Templates are automatically customized based on your company configuration, including 

dimensions and custom fields you created.  

• 
Templates can be updated at any time, especially when a new version of RealPage Financial 

Suite is released. This means that an older template might not work.  

To download a template:  

1. 
Open the Company menu. 

2. 
Select Import data. The Import data page lists the information that you can import.  

3. 
Find the type of data that you want to import.  

4. 
Click the Template link to download the template. You can find the file in your browser’s 

default download location.  

A prompt opens at the bottom of the web page, asking if you want to Open, Save, or 

Cancel. 

• 
Open: Opens the file in Excel. 

• 
Save: Saves the file to your browser’s default download folder. 

• 
Save as: Saves the file under a new name and in a different location. 

• 
Save and Open: Saves the file to your local computer, and then opens the file in Excel. 

5. 
Click Save. 

Save the template to your computer, and then continue downloading templates as needed until 

you have downloaded all of the templates for data that you want to import. 

If you have a database administrator (DBA) of your other system, give the downloaded templates 

to your DBA. Ask the DBA to: 

• 
Export the data from your other system, as specified in the import template spreadsheets. 

• 
Put the applicable data into each spreadsheet. 

• 
Save the spreadsheet as a comma-delimited file (CSV). 

If you do not have a DBA, or if your DBA does not have time to complete the whole task, you can 

complete the tasks. Refer to the following topics for guidance on creating importable data. 

Filling In an Import Template with Data 

Perform the following steps for each item that you want to import: 

---



##### Saving the Template as a CSV File
*Source: `RP Financial Suite Spend Management User Guide.pdf`, Page 708*



##### Importing the CSV File
*Source: `RP Financial Suite Spend Management User Guide.pdf`, Page 708*

Appendices 

RealPage® Financial Suite Spend Management User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

1. 
Open the template in Excel and review the data structure. The information in the template 

file can help you formulate extraction queries. 

2. 
Export the data from your other source. 

3. 
Copy the exported data into the template file for the same kind of object. Take care to 

exactly match the template’s data structure as you do this. 

Avoid using leading zeros in ID fields. If you must use leading zeros in IDs, convert the 
column of ID numbers to text format in Excel before importing the file content. Excel does 
not remove the leading zeros when you save the file. Remember to do this every time you 
use a template to import information that requires IDs. 

4. 
Fill in the required columns. 

5. 
Save the file in CSV format (on page 696). 

Now that you’ve entered your data and looked through it for any of the common issues imports 

can have, you are ready to import your file to your system.  

Saving the Template as a CSV File 

In Excel: 

1. 
Click File, and then select Save As. 

2. 
Click Browse and select where you want to save the file. 

3. 
In File name, type a name that represents the data that the template contains. 

4. 
In Save as type, select CSV (Comma delimited) (*.csv). 

5. 
Click the Save button. 

Some transactions have Import buttons on their lists so that you can import the transactions 
without having to leave the list. You can use this method whenever you have already 
downloaded the template that you need, filled it with the appropriate data, and saved the file in 
CSV format. 

Importing the CSV File 

Now that you’ve entered your data and looked through it for any of the common issues imports 

can have, you are ready to import your file into the system. 

To import your CSV file: 

---


<!-- Page 709 -->
Appendix K: Appendices 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage® Financial Suite Spend Management User Guide 

1. 
Open the Company menu. 

2. 
Select Import data. 

3. 
Find the information type you want to import, and then click the corresponding Import link. 

4. 
Click the Choose file button, and then select the CSV file that you want to import. 

5. 
If the CSV file includes dates that are not in mm/dd/yyyy format, select the date format that 

the data uses in the Date format field. 

The system attempts to import your file using the selected date format. If the system can’t 

import your file with the selected date format, it attempts to discover the date format used 

in your file and import the data using that date format. 

6. 
Leave the File encoding option set to Auto detect unless you’re unable to import your file. 

Depending on your operating system, you may need to select a different type of file 

encoding. 

7. 
If your import box includes a Post to section, select one of the following: 

• 
Select Historical if your data is not active. 

• 
Select General Ledger to post imported invoices to the G/L. 

8. 
If the file that you’re importing is large, consider selecting the Process offline option to 

process the import offline. This will cause the import to run at a later time, when the system 

is less busy. If you prefer to import the data immediately and wait for the results, do not 

select the Process offline check box. 

9. 
Type the email address to which import results and errors should be sent in the Email 

results to this address field. You can enter multiple email addresses, separated by a 

semicolon (;) or comma (,). 

RealPage highly recommends entering an email address. 

10. 
Click the Import button. After an import, the system informs you if the import was 

successful and how many records were imported. 

In a completely successful import, the confirmation page lets you verify that all of the 

records in your original file were successfully imported without having to manually verify 

them. 

---

## Glossary of Terms
*Source: `RP Financial Suite Spend Management User Guide.pdf`, Page 711*

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage® Financial Suite Spend Management User Guide 

A/P batch 

A group of A/P transactions—such as invoices or 

credits—entered and posted together. 

A/P configuration 

The collection of settings that define how A/P 

functions behave, including approval rules, 

numbering formats, tolerances, and posting 

options. 

A/P workflow 

The routing and approval structure that 

determines how invoices move through review 

and approval before posting. 

A/R Batch 

A group of A/R transactions—such as charges, 

receipts, or adjustments—entered and posted 

together. 

Account balance 

The total amount recorded in a G/L account for a 

given period, including beginning balance, 

activity, and ending balance. 

Account grouping 

A structure used in financial reports to organize 

G/L accounts into meaningful categories such as 

assets, liabilities, revenue, and expenses. 

Predefined or custom groupings of G/L accounts 

used for reporting, dashboards, and financial 

analysis. 

Account type 

A classification that determines how an account 

behaves in financial statements (Asset, Liability, 

Equity, Revenue, Expense). 

Accounting period 

Transactions are recorded and separated into 

different reporting periods such as months, 

quarters, and years. The use of reporting periods 

lets you compare past and present performance. 

Accounting reviewer 

A designated role responsible for reviewing and 

approving accounting-related transactions 

before they are posted. 

Accounts 

An account keeps track of what your company 

owns, owes, spends, or receives. Separate 

accounts let you keep separate records for each 

type of asset, liability, equity, revenue, and 

expense. 

Each account can contain several subaccounts, 

which helps organize and manage your finances. 

Each account tracks the activity of its category. 

For example, the Receivables account tracks 

money coming in and the Payables account 

tracks money going out. Each of these accounts 

typically has many subaccounts. For example, the 

Receivables account may have a subaccount for 

each property: 

1201.001 - Accounts Receivable - Fair Haven 

1201.002 - Accounts Receivable - Coconut Grove 

Glossary of Terms

Glossary of Terms 

RealPage® Financial Suite Spend Management User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Each account has a beginning balance. You 

record the increases and decreases for a period, 

and at the end of the period, you have the 

resulting ending balance. 

Accrual accounting 

The accrual method of accounting recognizes 

income in the period earned, and expenses in 

the period incurred. The accrual method is a 

better measure of profit and loss. 

Accrued Expenses report 

A report showing expenses that have been 

incurred but not yet paid, used during close to 

validate balances. 

Accumulated depreciation account 

The G/L account credited when depreciation is 

posted. It offsets the asset’s cost on the balance 

sheet. 

Action card 

A dashboard component that provides quick 

access buttons for common tasks or navigation 

shortcuts. 

Actuals 

Financial results of activity in the general ledger 

and used as the baseline for forecasts and 

budgets. 

Adjustment 

A manual increase or decrease to a customer’s or 

vendor’s balance, used to correct errors or apply 

special credits/charges. 

Adjustment codes 

Predefined codes used to categorize manual 

increases or decreases to a customer’s balance. 

Aging buckets 

Time based categories (e.g., 0–30, 31–60 days) 

used to group outstanding receivables or 

payables for reporting. 

Aging report 

A report that groups outstanding balances (A/P 

or A/R) by how long they have been unpaid (e.g., 

0–30, 31–60 days). 

Allocation 

A process that distributes amounts from one 

account or entity to others based on predefined 

rules or percentages. 

Allocation (Expense Reports) 

A method of distributing an expense across 

multiple projects, tasks, or locations. 

Approval levels 

The hierarchy of users or roles authorized to 

approve invoices based on amount, vendor, or 

other criteria.  

The number of approvers required for a role 

(1–4) when that role is assigned to an approval 

policy. 

Approval policy 

A rule that determines which users or roles are 

authorized to approve a transaction based on 

criteria such as amount, vendor, G/L account, 

job, or payment method.

Glossary of Terms 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage® Financial Suite Spend Management User Guide 

Approval policy manager 

The page in the Company application used to 

create, edit, and organize approval policies. 

Approval queue 

The list of transactions awaiting approval, 

displayed in the Approval Workbench. 

Approval workbench 

An approval workbench is where users review, 

approve, and decline pending transactions. 

Approval workflow 

The routing process that determines who must 

review and approve a transaction before it can 

be posted or paid. A collection of approval 

policies are applied to specific transaction types 

and properties. 

Approver 

An approver is a person responsible for deciding 

to approve or decline a transaction. There are 

three types of approvers: 

• 
General approvers can approve or decline 

only transactions assigned to them or their 

role. 

• 
Unrestricted approvers can approve or 

decline any transaction. 

• 
Delegate approvers can approve or decline 

transactions assigned to another approver. 

Approver permissions 

The system permissions required to create 

approval policies or approve transactions. 

Asset account 

The G/L account representing the asset’s cost. 

Used when posting depreciation and disposal 

entries. 

Asset Activity report 

A report showing additions, disposals, transfers, 

and depreciation activity for selected assets. 

Asset class 

A category of assets that share the same 

depreciation rules and G/L account structure. 

Determines how depreciation is calculated and 

posted. 

Asset Disposal report 

A report showing assets that have been disposed 

of, including gain/loss calculations. 

Asset List report 

A report showing basic asset details such as cost, 

location, class, and placed in service date. 

Asset Reconciliation report 

A report comparing fixed asset balances to G/L 

balances to identify discrepancies. 

Assets 

The tangible and intangible items used in the 

operation of a business. Tangible assets include 

buildings, equipment, and vehicles. Intangible 

assets include the company’s bank account 

balance and A/R invoices representing future 

income from customers. Assets are tracked 

through acquisition, depreciation, transfer, and 

disposal.

Glossary of Terms 

RealPage® Financial Suite Spend Management User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Assumptions 

User defined variables—such as inflation rates, 

occupancy targets, or expense growth—that 

drive forecast calculations. 

Attachments 

An attachment is a bundle of one or more 

supporting documents, such as spreadsheets, 

scanned images, or word processor documents. 

Audit trail 

A system record showing changes made to 

transactions or records, including who made the 

change and when. 

Bank account policy 

An approval policy that routes transactions for 

approval based on the bank account used. 

Bank accounts 

Financial accounts set up in the system for 

issuing payments, recording deposits, 

withdrawals, and performing reconciliations. 

Bank feed 

An automated connection that imports bank 

transactions into reconciliation for matching and 

reconciliation. 

Bank reconciliation 

The process of matching bank activity to general 

ledger transactions to ensure the bank balance 

and book balance agree. 

Bank register 

A chronological list of all transactions recorded 

in a bank account within the system. 

Baseline forecast 

The initial forecast generated from actuals and 

default assumptions before adjustments or 

scenario modeling. 

Batch 

A group of journal entries entered and posted 

together as a single unit. 

Batch report 

A report that displays all transactions included in 

a specific batch, such as A/P invoices or journal 

entries. 

Beginning balance 

The starting balance of a G/L account at the 

beginning of a fiscal period. 

Billable time 

Hours worked on a project that can be invoiced 

to a customer. The Billable Time page allows 

users to generate invoices for approved billable 

hours. 

Book balance 

The balance of a bank account according to the 

general ledger. It can also be the balance from 

the general ledger of a default general ledger 

account set on the bank account. 

Bookmarks / favorites 

User-defined shortcuts to frequently accessed 

pages or modules. 

Books closed 

The state indicating that the accounting period 

has been finalized for a property.

Glossary of Terms 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage® Financial Suite Spend Management User Guide 

Budget 

A financial plan for a future period that outlines 

expected revenue, expenses, and cash flow. In 

Job Cost, a budget is an estimate of expected 

costs for a job. 

Budget version 

A saved iteration of a budget or forecast, 

allowing comparison between drafts, scenarios, 

or approval stages. 

BVA 

Budget Variance Analysis is an analysis of the 

difference between the amount that you 

budgeted for and the actual amount that you 

spent. 

Calculation model 

The logic used to compute forecasted values, 

such as percentage growth, fixed amounts, or 

driver based formulas. 

Cash accounting 

The cash method of accounting recognizes 

revenue in the same reporting period as the cash 

is received, and expenses in the period in which 

cash payments are made. 

Cash flow forecast 

A projection of expected cash inflows and 

outflows over a defined period. 

Certification / skill 

A credential, license, or skill tracked for an 

employee. Users can add, edit, or delete 

certifications and skills in their profile. 

Charge 

A receivable posted to a customer or tenant 

account for rent, fees, utilities, or other billable 

items. 

Charge schedule 

A configuration that defines when recurring 

charges generate, such as monthly rent cycles. 

Chart of accounts (COA) 

The structured list of G/L accounts used to 

categorize financial transactions. 

Check layout 

The format and design used when printing 

checks, including alignment, fields, and MICR line 

settings. 

Check run 

A batch process that selects, reviews, and prints 

multiple vendor payments at once. 

Child location 

In the RealPage Financial Suite, properties are 

called locations. Subproperties are called child 

locations. 

An entity represents the corporate office of one 

or more locations, responsible for locations’ 

taxes. Every location is associated with an entity. 

An entity can be responsible for one location or 

a large group of locations and child locations.  

A company can be composed of one entity or 

multiple entities. See also Multi-entity companies 

(on page 711).

Glossary of Terms 

RealPage® Financial Suite Spend Management User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Cleared transaction 

A payment or deposit that has been matched to 

bank activity during reconciliation. 

Cloned dashboard 

A duplicate of an existing dashboard that can be 

edited independently. 

Close account 

A close account is a G/L account used to track 

job completion. 

Close checklist 

A list of tasks required to complete the financial 

close for a period. Can be generated 

automatically or manually. 

Close console 

A centralized page for managing close activities, 

including generating checklists, opening/closing 

books, and viewing charts. 

Close workbench 

A workspace that displays close tasks, checklists, 

and work paper actions for selected properties. 

Closing period 

The process of finalizing a fiscal period so no 

additional transactions can be posted. 

Coding 

Assigning G/L accounts, properties, entities, and 

other classifications to an invoice or credit. 

Commitment 

A commitment, or purchase order, is an 

agreement to purchase goods or services for a 

fixed amount. 

Component 

An individual element displayed on a dashboard, 

such as a chart, list, report, performance card, 

calendar, or smartlink. 

Component controls 

The actions available on each dashboard 

component, such as edit, delete, expand, 

collapse, or move. 

Component group 

A collection of dashboard components grouped 

together for organization or layout purposes. 

Component permissions 

Permissions required to view the underlying data 

of a dashboard component. Users must have 

access to the data source (e.g., A/P invoices, G/L 

accounts) to see the component. 

Concession 

A concession is a negative charge awarded to 

the customer as a short-term incentive. Examples 

of concessions include waived fees, reduced rent, 

nuisance discounts, and renovation credits.  

Console page 

A dashboard style page showing close status, 

charts, and tools for generating checklists and 

managing books.

Glossary of Terms 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage® Financial Suite Spend Management User Guide 

Consolidation 

Combining financial data from multiple entities 

into a single set of financial statements. 

Contra accounts 

A contra account is an account which offsets and 

reduces or offsets the balance of another 

account. You can have contra accounts for both 

assets and liabilities. 

A contra asset account has a credit balance and 

offsets and decreases the debit balance of the 

related asset account. An example of a 

contra-asset account is Accumulated 

Depreciation Autos & Vehicles account, which 

reduces the Automobiles & Vehicles account to 

arrive at the net value. 

A contra-liability account has a debit balance 

and offsets and decreases the credit balance of 

the related liability account. 

Cost code 

A cost code is a way to track a specific cost 

based on nature or function. 

Cost code policy 

An approval policy that routes transactions for 

approval based on a specific cost code. 

Cost coding 

Cost coding is a method of grouping individual 

costs based on their nature, function, or work 

phase. 

Credit memo 

A credit memo increases the overall amount you 

owe a vendor. It is typically a vendor-issued 

document that reduces the amount owed on an 

invoice. 

Custom field 

A user-defined field added to records or 

transactions to capture additional data not 

included in standard RealPage fields. 

Custom field wizard 

The guided tool used to create new custom 

fields, define field types, and configure visibility. 

Custom report 

A user built report that pulls data from Financial 

Suite records, transactions, and custom fields, 

allowing flexible filtering, grouping, and 

calculations. 

Custom report wizard 

A step-by-step tool for building custom reports, 

including selecting data sources, defining 

columns, adding filters, grouping, and setting 

prompts. 

Custom view 

A personalized list view that displays selected 

columns, filters, and sorting for any application’s 

list pages. 

Customer / tenant ledger 

A detailed record of all charges, payments, 

adjustments, and balances for a specific 

customer or tenant. 

Dashboard 

A workspace where users can pin frequently 

used reports for quick access, and display
