Glossary of Terms 

RealPage® Financial Suite Spend Management User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

business insights using components such as 

charts, KPIs, lists, and reports. 

Dashboard library 

A collection of prebuilt dashboards available for 

installation, typically provided when a company 

is created using a QuickStart template. 

Data import wizard 

A tool used to import data such as vendors, 

customers, G/L accounts, or transactions into the 

Financial Suite. 

Data mapping 

The process of aligning fields in your import file 

with the corresponding fields in the Financial 

Suite so the system knows where each value 

belongs. 

Data source (primary data source) 

The record or transaction type selected as the 

foundation for a report (e.g., Customer, A/P 

Invoice Detail, G/L entry). 

Data template 

A predefined spreadsheet or CSV layout 

provided by RealPage that specifies the required 

columns and formatting for a successful import. 

Debit memo 

A debit memo decreases the overall amount you 

owe that vendor. 

For example, if you receive a credit memo from a 

vendor, enter it as a debit memo to reduce the 

amount you owe that vendor. 

Debits and credits 

In common use, credit generally has positive 

associations; in accounting, credit is associated 

with decreases in asset, expense, and equity 

accounts. 

Debits increase balances in asset and expense 

accounts and decrease balances in liability 

accounts, revenue accounts, and capital 

accounts. 

Credits increase balances in liability, revenue, 

and capital accounts, and decrease balances in 

asset and expense accounts. 

Debit accounts are asset and expense accounts 

that usually have debit balances; the total debits 

usually exceed the total credits in each debit 

account. 

Credit accounts are revenue (income, gains) 

accounts and liability accounts that usually have 

credit balances. 

Declining balance (100/150/200) 

A depreciation method that accelerates 

depreciation by applying a percentage to the 

asset’s remaining book value. 

Default dashboard 

The dashboard automatically displayed when a 

user logs in. 

Default settings 

Predefined values that automatically populate 

fields when creating records, such as default G/L 

accounts or payment terms (A/P), or default 

charge codes or payment application rules (A/R).

Glossary of Terms 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage® Financial Suite Spend Management User Guide 

Delegate 

The approver who assumes your responsibility 

for approving transactions while you are out of 

the office. Any approvals that have been 

delegated while you are out of the office remain 

with your delegate, even if you turn off the 

out-of-office notification before the delegate has 

approved or declined the transaction. 

Deposit 

Funds received and recorded in a bank account, 

often grouped into a deposit batch for posting. 

Deposit batch 

A group of deposits entered and posted 

together. 

Depreciation batch 

A batch of depreciation journal entries generated 

for a period. Can be posted, viewed, or deleted. 

Depreciation expense account 

The G/L account debited when depreciation is 

posted. 

Depreciation journal entry 

The G/L entry created when depreciation is 

posted, debiting expense and crediting 

accumulated depreciation. 

Depreciation schedule 

The system generated schedule showing 

depreciation amounts for each period over the 

asset’s useful life. 

Depreciation schedules (financial vs. 
tax) 

Separate schedules that allow different 

depreciation rules for GAAP and tax reporting. 

Detail data source 

A data source option that includes both header 

and line item information for transactions (e.g., 

A/P Invoice Detail). 

Detail ledger 

A record showing all transactions posted to a 

specific G/L account. 

Detail report 

A report that includes line item or transaction 

level information rather than summarized totals. 

Dimension report structures 

Dimension report structures are named 

structures that you can create for the purpose of 

adding custom analysis to the rows or columns 

of a financial report. You can add dimension 

structures for any dimension that you have in 

your company. 

Disbursement 

Any outgoing cash transaction, such as checks, 

ACH payments, or manual payments. 

Document template 

A customizable Word-based template used for 

printed documents such as invoices, statements, 

sales orders, and purchase orders.

Glossary of Terms 

RealPage® Financial Suite Spend Management User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Document type 

The category of document associated with a 

report, such as invoices, statements, or purchase 

orders. 

Draft asset 

An asset imported from an external system that 

has not yet been activated. 

Draft expense report 

An expense report that has been created but not 

yet submitted for approval. 

Draw 

In Job Cost & Reserves, a draw summarizes 

invoiced costs by combining job activity into 

predetermined categories. After it’s summarized, 

you can provide the draw to the funding sources 

of the job. 

Draw model 

A draw model is an agreement between a lender 

and your company that lists the budgeted items 

approved for funds. 

Driver 

A variable that influences forecasted values (e.g., 

occupancy, rent growth, utility usage). 

Due date 

The date by which a vendor invoice must be 

paid. 

eInvoice 

A system-generated A/P invoice created by 

Spend Management Storefront. 

Entity 

An entity record contains a property’s or 

location’s accounting and legal details, such as 

the business name and address as they should 

appear on A/R invoices, A/P invoices, and tax 

forms. An entity contains the accounting 

information of a location/property or property 

management company. 

In a multi-entity environment, entities are 

distinct—but nearly identical—companies or 

business units that are fully owned by a 

corporate or headquarters entity. Entities can 

represent divisions managed by a common 

entity (central headquarters) using centralized 

payables and receivables and a common chart of 

accounts. 

Exception 

A transaction that does not match bank activity 

during reconciliation and requires review or 

correction. 

Expense report 

A form used to record reimbursable expenses. 

Users can add receipts, allocate expenses, and 

submit for approval. 

FAS 

A final account statement (FAS) is a document 

that provides a detailed record of a transaction’s 

activity. 

Filter 

Criteria applied to limit which records appear in 

a report.

Glossary of Terms 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage® Financial Suite Spend Management User Guide 

Final work paper package 

The completed, approved set of work papers for 

a period, locked after approval. 

Fiscal calendar 

The structure of accounting periods and fiscal 

years used for reporting and posting. 

Forecast 

A forward looking projection of financial 

performance based on actuals, assumptions, and 

drivers. 

Forecast cycle 

The defined period for creating, reviewing, and 

finalizing forecasts (monthly, quarterly, annually). 

Funding source 

A funding source is a lender for a job. 

G/L account (general ledger account) 

A financial account used to categorize 

transactions for reporting and posting. A G/L 

account is associated with each charge or 

payment. 

G/L account group 

A predefined group of G/L accounts that can be 

selected instead of individual account ranges. 

G/L account policy 

An approval policy that routes transactions for 

approval based on a specific G/L account or 

account range. 

G/L group 

A collection of G/L accounts grouped for 

reporting, allocations, or approval routing. 

Global (top level) setup 

Configuration performed at the top level that 

applies to all entities in the portfolio. 

Home page 

The landing page provides quick access to 

dashboards, tasks, and frequently used modules. 

Import log 

A system-generated record that shows which 

rows were imported successfully and which 

failed, including error messages. 

Initial posting date 

Revaluation reports help you manage 

unrecognized gains and losses from the 

fluctuation in exchange rates. Set the initial 

posting date on this report as the end of the 

month. 

Injection (smart rules / smart events) 

A dynamic value inserted into a rule or event 

action, such as a field value, date, or user 

information. 

Interim financing 

Interim financing, or construction loan, is a 

deployment of capital for short-term 

development, such as the acquisition and 

renovation of properties. This capital is typically 

provided by a lender.

Glossary of Terms 

RealPage® Financial Suite Spend Management User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

When the project is complete, owners pay the 

construction loan and replace it with permanent 

financing. 

In-transit item 

A transaction recorded in the system but not yet 

reflected on the bank statement (e.g., 

outstanding checks, deposits in transit). 

Invoice (A/P) 

A vendor’s bill for goods or services received. 

Invoice (A/R) 

A document generated to bill a customer for 

charges owed. In A/R, invoices may be created 

manually or automatically. 

Invoice entry 

The process of entering vendor invoices into the 

A/P module for approval and posting. 

Invoice matching 

The process of comparing an invoice to purchase 

orders, receipts, or expected amounts before 

approval. 

Invoice numbering rules 

Settings that determine how invoice numbers are 

validated, formatted, or restricted. 

Job 

A job is a method of tracking the work and 

expenses related to construction at a property. 

Jobs are used for job costing and approval 

routing. 

Job policy 

An approval policy that routes transactions for 

approval based on a specific job. 

Job type 

A classification of jobs used for approval policies 

and reporting. 

Job type policy 

An approval policy that routes transactions for 

approval based on a job type. 

Journal entry 

A journal entry documents the movement of 

money. When you add a journal entry, you enter 

an accounting transaction into the records. Every 

journal entry must include at least two equal and 

offsetting entries. This is because every 

transaction involves a change in at least two 

places in the accounting records, and the total of 

all debits and credits must balance. 

Key performance indicator (KPI) 

A measurable metric used to evaluate financial 

or operational performance (e.g., NOI, occupancy 

rate). KPIs can be displayed on performance 

cards on a dashboard to show financial or 

operational performance. 

Late fee 

A charge applied when a customer fails to pay by 

the due date, based on configured rules. 

Late fee rules 

Configuration that determines when late fees 

apply, how they are calculated, and which charge 

codes they use.

RealPage® Financial Suite Spend Management User Guide 

Ledger 

The complete set of financial accounts used to 

record all transactions for an entity or portfolio. 

Line item 

An individual revenue or expense entry within a 

transaction such as an invoice, purchase order, 

budget or forecast. 

Loan schedule 

A loan schedule is a list of all payments 

previously paid (historical purposes only) or due 

to the lender for the loan. 

Lookup values 

Reference lists—such as vendors, charge codes, 

or account types—that must exist in the system 

before certain imports can succeed. 

Manual entry 

A bank transaction entered directly into the 

system rather than imported through a bank 

feed or processed by AI. 

Manual journal entry 

A journal entry created directly by a user rather 

than generated by a subsystem such as A/P or 

A/R. 

Matching 

The process of pairing bank activity with 

corresponding G/L transactions during 

reconciliation.  

M-console 

The M-console is the management console used 

by administrators to create and manage multiple 

RealPage Accounting Suite environments. 

M-console access is different from RealPage 

Accounting Suite system access. To access the 

M-console, you must have a separate account in 

the M-console. 

Most implementations of RealPage Accounting 

Suite do not need the M-console. 

Memorized report 

A saved version of a report with preset filters, 

parameters, and formatting for quick reuse. 

Merge field 

A placeholder inserted into a Word document 

template that pulls data from the Financial Suite 

when the document is generated. 

Monthly checklist 

A checklist used for monthly close activities. 

Multi year forecast 

A projection that spans multiple fiscal years, 

often used for long term planning. 

Multi-entity companies 

In the RealPage Financial Suite, a parent property 

is called a location, and a subproperty is called a 

child location. A location must have an entity 

associated with it. The entity handles the 

accounting and tax activities for its location and 

any child locations. 

In a multi-entity shared corporation, entities 

represent a separate tax identification or a 

separately secured, fully balancing set of books. 

Entities typically represent properties, or 

locations, which are managed by a common 

entity (central headquarters) using centralized

Glossary of Terms 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage® Financial Suite Spend Management User Guide 

Performance card 

A dashboard component that displays KPIs, 

trends, or financial metrics in a compact visual 

format. 

Period activity 

The total debits and credits posted to an account 

within a specific accounting period. 

Period close 

The workflow used to review, adjust, and finalize 

financial activity before closing an accounting 

period. 

Periodic tasks 

Recurring A/P activities performed on a regular 

schedule, such as check runs, recurring invoice 

generation, or reconciliation. 

Permission 

The rights required to view and work with data 

and access pages. 

A permission allows you to access a single 

function. When RealPage adds a new feature to a 

product, the feature often comes with new 

permissions that you must enable before users 

can use the new feature. The word “Right” and 

the word “Permission” refer to the same thing. 

When you use the Unified Platform, they are 

referred to as rights. When you set up access to 

functions in the Financial Suite, they are referred 

to as permissions.  

Permit 

A permit is a category that organizes job 

attachments by type or function. 

Placed in service date 

The date the asset begins being used. 

Depreciation starts based on this date. 

PO 

An abbreviation for purchase order (on page 

714). 

Policy type 

The category of rule used to determine approval 

routing (User, Amount, Tiered Amount, Vendor, 

Vendor Type, G/L Account, Job, Job Type, Cost 

Code, Accounting Reviewer, Journal Type, 

Payment Method, Bank Account). 

Positive Pay 

Positive pay is an automated service that the 

bank offers to help detect fraud by matching a 

company’s check with the check presented for 

payment.  

You can use the RealPage Financial Suite Positive 

Pay feature to generate a Positive Pay file and 

transmit the list of checks to the bank for review. 

The bank compares the amount, check number, 

and account number to ensure that they match. 

Non-matching checks are flagged and sent back 

to the check issuer for review. 

You can also configure the system to submit 

Positive Pay files on a schedule. When a schedule 

is configured, the system generates the Positive 

Pay files containing a list of checks on the 

scheduled dates and automatically sends them 

to the bank. 

Posting 

The action that finalizes a transaction and 

records it in the general ledger.

When you post a transaction, you are 

transferring the balance of the transaction from 

its journal to the General Ledger. 

Posting date 

The date assigned to a journal entry that 

determines the accounting period in which it 

appears. 

Posting rules 

Settings that determine how transactions are 

posted to the general ledger, including batch 

behavior and posting dates. 

Pre validation 

A system check that reviews your file for 

formatting or data issues before the actual 

import runs. 

Preliminary work paper package 

The initial version of work papers generated 

before variances are resolved. 

Prepayment 

A payment reflecting an invoice that is not yet 

billed. The customer’s account balance is zero. 

Project

entries and expenses. Projects must be created 

before they can be used in timesheets. 

Project type 

A classification used to group projects for 

reporting and setup. 

Prompts 

User input fields added to a custom report to 

allow filtering at runtime. 

Properties (entities) 

Individual business units or properties whose 

financial activity is tracked separately. 

PTO (paid time off) 

Time away from work that can be requested and 

approved through the Time & Resources 

application. 

PTO approvals 

The list where approvers review and approve or 

decline PTO requests. 

PTO request 

A request submitted by an employee for paid 

time off. 

PTO types 

Administrator-defined categories of PTO, such as 

vacation, sick leave, or personal time. 

Punchout vendor 

Punchout refers to a digital system in which a 

vendor allows customers to browse his product 

catalogs online and then purchase goods or 

services within the client’s e-procurement 

system. 

Purchase order 

A purchase order, or commitment, is an 

agreement to purchase goods or services for a 

fixed amount.

automatic document numbering feature used to 

assign unique identifiers to new records. This 

helps ensure consistency and avoids duplication.

sequencing, is available only for select 

transactions and records in RealPage 

Accounting. Document sequencing uses 

pre-defined numbering plans to assign 

sequential identifiers to new records or 

transactions, such as customer records or A/R 

invoices. Document sequencing is a two-step 

process. First, you configure the numbering 

scheme, then you assign the scheme to the type 

of record or transaction.

adjust the book balance.

Glossary of Terms 

RealPage® Financial Suite Spend Management User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Subledger 

A subledger is a ledger containing all of one kind 

of transaction. For example, a subledger may 

contain all accounts receivable transactions, or 

accounts payable transactions, or fixed asset 

transactions. All transactions in all subledgers roll 

up into the general ledger. 

Submitted (timesheet status) 

Indicates that a timesheet has been submitted 

and is awaiting approval. 

Sum of years digits (SYD) 

An accelerated depreciation method that applies 

a decreasing fraction of the asset’s cost each 

year. 

Summary 

Summaries are collections of the same type of 

transactions, grouped together for processing. 

Until you or the system creates a new summary, 

no line items appear in the Summaries list. 

Summaries can be either open or closed. When 

summaries are open in Accounts Receivable, you 

can add invoices, adjustments, and deposits. In 

designing an accounts receivable process, the 

system administrator can give access to the 

pages involved with managing invoices but not 

opening or closing summaries. 

Summary report 

A high level report that aggregates data without 

showing line item detail. 

Suspense account 

A temporary account used to hold transactions 

that require review or correction. 

System journal 

A system journal is a journal that is used by the 

system. Users can designate a journal as a 

system journal. Users cannot add journal entries 

to system journals, and system journals are 

excluded from appearing in manual journals 

drop-down lists. 

Target (budgeting) 

A predefined financial goal used to guide 

budgeting or forecasting (e.g., NOI target, 

expense cap). 

Task (Financial Close Management) 

An individual close activity, such as reconciling a 

subledger or reviewing a report. 

Task (Time & Resources application) 

A specific activity within a project. Tasks must be 

created before they can be selected on 

timesheets. 

Template version (importing) 

The specific RealPage-approved layout for an 

import file. Using an outdated version can cause 

errors. 

Tenant / customer 

The individual or organization responsible for 

paying charges recorded in A/R. 

Three-way tie 

A reconciliation requirement ensuring that the 

bank balance, book balance, and cleared balance 

all match.

Glossary of Terms 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage® Financial Suite Spend Management User Guide 

Tiered amount policy 

An approval policy that routes transactions 

through multiple approval tiers based on 

increasing amount ranges. 

TIH 

Trust Interest Holder 

Time approvals 

The list where approvers review and approve or 

decline submitted timesheets. 

Timesheet 

A weekly record of hours worked on projects and 

tasks. Users can add comments, submit for 

approval, and track status. 

Timesheet periods 

Defined weekly or biweekly periods used for 

time entry. Administrators open and close 

periods as needed. 

Tolerance percentage 

The allowable variance between an invoice and 

the expected amount before manual approval is 

required. 

Transaction date 

The date the A/R activity occurred, which 

determines how it appears in aging and 

reporting. 

Transaction detail 

Line-level information associated with a 

transaction, such as invoice items or journal 

entry lines. 

Transaction type 

The category of transaction, such as invoices, 

journal entries, or payments. 

Transactions 

A transaction represents money flowing from 

one account to another. Whenever you spend or 

receive money, or transfer money from one 

account to another, it is represented as a 

transaction. 

In double-entry accounting, transactions always 

involve at least two accounts—a source account 

and a destination account. 

Transfer 

A movement of funds between two bank 

accounts within the system. 

Transfer (asset transfer) 

Moving an asset from one location, entity, or 

department to another. 

Trial balance 

A report showing all G/L accounts with 

beginning balances, period activity, and ending 

balances. 

Unapplied payment 

A payment that has been received but not yet 

applied to specific charges. 

Unapplied payment handling 

Rules that determine how payments are stored 

when they cannot be matched to specific 

charges. 

---

Glossary of Terms 

RealPage® Financial Suite Spend Management User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Unapproving (Expense report) 

The action of reversing an approval so the report 

can be edited. 

Unapproving (Expense report) 

The action of reversing an approval so the report 

can be edited. 

Uncleared transaction 

A transaction recorded in the system that has 

not yet been matched to bank activity. 

Unit 

A unit is a rentable space on a property. 

Unposted batch 

A batch of journal entries that has been created 

but not yet posted to the general ledger. 

Unrestricted user 

A user who can do a task, such as approve work 

papers on behalf of others, regardless of 

property restrictions. 

An unrestricted user can see all transactions that 

are waiting to be approved. Unrestricted users 

can act on these transactions even when the 

approvals are not assigned to them. 

Useful life (periods) 

The number of periods over which the asset will 

depreciate. 

User 

An individual system account assigned roles, 

permissions, and approval responsibilities. 

Variance (Financial Close 
Management) 

A difference between expected and actual 

balances in work papers, requiring review and 

resolution. 

Variance (Forecasting and Budgeting) 

The difference between actual results and 

budgeted or forecasted values. 

Vendor 

A supplier of goods or services who receives 

payment through the A/P process. 

Vendor categories / vendor types 

Classifications used to group vendors for 

reporting, workflow, or payment processing. 

Vendor defaults 

Preset values applied automatically when 

creating invoices for a vendor, such as G/L 

accounts or payment terms. 

Vendor import 

A file upload that creates or updates vendor 

records, including addresses, payment terms, 

and tax information. 

Vendor policy 

An approval policy that routes transactions for 

approval based on a specific vendor or vendor 

range. 

Vendor type 

A classification of vendors used for approval 

routing or reporting.

Glossary of Terms 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage® Financial Suite Spend Management User Guide 

Vendor type policy 

An approval policy that routes transactions for 

approval based on the vendor’s classification. 

Version control (budgeting) 

The system of tracking changes across multiple 

budget or forecast versions. 

Views (manage views) 

Saved list configurations that define which 

columns appear and how data is sorted or 

filtered. 

WHFIT 

Widely Held Fixed Investment Trust 

WIP account 

A WIP account, or work in process account, is a 

G/L account used to track jobs that are in active 

development. 

Work breakdown structure (WBS) 

A work breakdown structure (WBS) is a system 

that organizes a large project into manageable 

sections. In Job Cost, a job, or project, is 

separated into cost codes that help organize the 

job and track progress. 

Work in process account 

A work in process account, or WIP account, is a 

G/L account used to track jobs that are in active 

development. 

Work paper 

A work paper is an accounting document that 

reconciles all subaccounts of an accounting 

category for auditing purposes. Work papers can 

also be used for preparing financial statements. 

Work paper package 

A compiled set of work papers, attachments, and 

supporting documents for a period.

Spend Management Quick Steps 

RealPage® Financial Suite Spend Management Quick Steps 
Doc ID [195754] 
9/13/2024 

About Spend Management 

Spend Management enables the delivery of enterprise 
spending visibility to ensure compliance and control. Use 
Spend Management to analyze the impact of sourcing 
strategies on key categories, assess business savings, and 
review compliance with preferred suppliers and contracts. 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Spend Management`


Configuring Spend Management 

Use the Configure Spend Management page to enable 
tolerance rules for A/P invoices, enable the logging of the 
receipt of goods to a journal, allow change orders to be 
performed, require attachments from site users, enable the 
Storefront feature, set up journals for logging the receipt of 
goods, choose the account for retainage on contracts, and 
set up prefixes for document numbers for orders, service 
contracts, and subcontracts. 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Spend Management > Setup > Configuration`


To access the configuration page: 

1. From the Applications menu, select Spend 
management, and then select the Configuration 
option on the Setup tab. The Configuration spend 
management page opens. 
2. In the Thresholds section, select the Enable tolerance 
rules check box. Additional options for setting a range 
for the variance appear. 
3. Choose whether to set the threshold at a certain 
Percentage or a fixed Dollar Amount. 
• If you select Percentage, in the Percentage field, 
enter a percentage amount. 
4. To skip any invoice approval requirements if the 
purchase order amount is within tolerance, select the 
Bypass invoice approval if within PO/SO tolerance 
check box. Additional approval requirement settings 
appear. 
5. In the Enable Functionality section, select any (or none) 
of the available options. 

Some features, when enabled, cannot be disabled. 

6. In the Journals section, select the journal where the 
system logs goods received and a liability account. 

This section appears if you enable the receipt of goods 
in the Enable Functionality section. 

7. In the G/L Accounts section, select a G/L account to 
use for retainage on contracts from the Job Cost 
retention account drop-down list. 
8. In the Document Sequencing section, select the prefix 
numbering for order, service contract, or subcontract 
numbering. 

Document sequencing is fully customizable. You can 
add and modify document sequence options. 

9. In the Enable Functionality for Custom PO section, 
select the Enable Custom PO check box. The 
Additional verbiage field appears. 
10. In the Additional verbiage field, enter custom text you 
want to include. 
11. Select the Include Workflow History check box to 
include the approval workflow history. 
12. Click the Save button. 

Spend Management Workbenches 

The Workbench feature puts all of your spend activities 
into one location. Spend Management features two 
workbenches: the Spend management workbench and 
the Approval workbench. 
To add, find, manage, and approve transactions: 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Spend Management > All > Workbench`


• 
Edit: Edit the transaction. 
• 
View: View the transaction. 
• 
Delete: Delete the transaction. 
• 
: View the transaction attachment(s). 
• 
Close: Close the transaction. 
• 
CO: Create a change order. 
• 
Receive: Update the order with received goods. 
• 
Create invoice: Create an invoice for the order. 
• 
Detail: View the transaction details. 
• 
Cancel: Cancel the transaction. 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Spend Management > All > Approval 
Workbench`


• 
Edit: Edit the transaction. 
• 
View: View the transaction. 
• 
Approve: Approve the transaction. 
• 
Decline: Decline the transaction. 
• 
: View the transaction attachment(s). 
• 
$: View the available budget for the transaction. 
• 
Add approver: Add an additional approver. 
• 
Send back: Send the transaction to the last approver. 

Adding a New A/P Invoice 

Use the A/P invoice information page to add a new 
invoice. 
To add a new A/P invoice without a matching purchase 
order: 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Spend Management > All > Daily Tasks>`


Create a AP Invoice 

1. From the Spend management application menu, in the 
Daily Tasks section on the All tab, select Create a AP 
invoice. 
2. At a minimum, complete these required fields: 
• Date: Select the invoice date. 
• Total invoice amount: Type the invoice amount. 
• Vendor: Select the vendor. 
• Invoice number: Type the invoice number on the 
invoice. 
• Due date: Select the due date on the invoice. 
3. Choose a line entry type: Standard, Job cost, or Both. 
4. Add any attachments if needed. 
5. Complete the Invoice Entries table. 
• At a minimum, complete these required fields: 
• 
QTY: Type the amount of the item listed in the 
invoice. 
• 
Price: Type the price of a single unit of the 
item. 
• 
Amount: Verify that the total amount that is 
calculated and populated is QTY times Price. 
6. Save the invoice as a draft or submit it for processing: 
• Draft: Click the 
 Expand button next to Draft & 
new, and then select Draft. 
• Submit: Click the 
 Expand button next to 
Submit & new, and then select Submit. 

Creating an A/P Invoice Package 

Use the Package invoices button when you want to bundle 
a set of invoices. 
To create an A/P invoice package from a bundle of 
invoices: 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Spend Management > All > Workbench > 
Package Invoices`


1. From the Spend management application menu, in the 
Daily Tasks section on the All tab, select Workbench. 
2. Select the AP Invoice view option. 
3. Click the Package invoices button. The page name 
changes to Package AP invoices. 
4. Filter the list to display the invoices you want to 
package. 
5. Select the invoices to include in the package. 
• After one invoice is selected, check boxes appear 
next to the Edit link with three options: 

• 
Show only selected invoices: Select to 
removed unselected A/P invoices from the list. 
• 
Generate package: Select to open the 
Generate Invoice Package box to finalize the

Adding a New Purchase Order 

Use the Purchase order information page to add a new 
purchase order.  
To add a new purchase order for new purchases: 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Spend Management > All > Daily Tasks > 
Create a Purchase Order`


1. From the Spend management application menu, in the 
Daily Tasks section on the All tab, select Create a 
Purchase order. 
2. At a minimum, complete these required fields: 
• Date: Select the purchase order date. 
• Encumbrance date: Select the encumbrance date. 
• Vendor: Select the vendor. 
• Bill to: Select the location to bill. 
3. Choose a line entry type: Standard or Job cost. 
4. Complete the line entry table. 
• At a minimum, complete these required fields: 
• 
Location: Select the location from the 
drop-down list of the item. 
• 
Account: Select the account from the 
drop-down list of the item. 
• 
Item Desc: Type a short item description of 
the item. 
• 
QTY: Type the amount of the item. 
• 
Price: Type the price of a single unit of the 
item. 
5. Save the purchase order as a draft or submit it for 
processing: 
• Draft: Click the Draft button. 
• Submit: Click the Submit button. 

Adding a New Service Contract 

Use the Service contract information page to add a new 
service contract. 
To create a new service contract: 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Spend Management > All > Daily Tasks >`


Service Contract 

1. From the Spend management application menu, in the 
Daily Tasks section on the All tab, select Service 
contract. 
2. At a minimum, complete these required fields: 
• Start date: Select the contract start date. 
• End date: Select the contract end date. 
• Vendor: Select the vendor. 
• Bill to: Select the location to bill. 
• Contract amount: Type the total contract amount. 
3. Complete the Service Entries table. 
• At a minimum, complete these required fields: 
• 
Location: Select the location from the 
drop-down list of the item. 
• 
Account: Select the account from the 
drop-down list of the item. 
• 
Service: Select the service from the 
drop-down list of the item. 
• 
Amount: Verify that the total amount that is 
calculated 
4. Click the Submit button. The page reloads. 
5. Click the Schedule button above the line entry table. 
The Service Contract: Bulk Schedule box opens. 
6. Complete the following in the Schedules section: 
• Start date: Select the service start date. 
• Scheduling repeat by: Select a frequency option 
from the drop-down list. 
• Complete the additional scheduling fields that 
appear based on the frequency option. 
7. Click the Save button. 
8. Review the Preview Orders section, and then add or

9. Click Generate orders to generate the service orders. 
10. Click the Save & Done button to close the box.

Accessing a Service Order (QS) 

Use the Service Order Information page to view, 
duplicate, print, and email service orders. 
To view a service order: 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Spend Management > All > Workbench > 
Service Contract > Transaction Type > Service Order`


1. From the Spend management workbench page, in 
the Transaction type field, select Service order from 
the drop-down list. 
2. Click the Apply button. The page refreshes with a 
results list of only service orders. 
3. Select one of the following actions: 

• View: Click to open the Service order information 
page of the service order. 
• Create invoice: Click to open the A/P invoice page 
of the service order. 
• Close: Click to return to the Spend management 
workbench page of the service order. 
To duplicate, print, or email a service order: 

1. From the Service order information page, click the 
Print/Email button. 
2. Click the Apply button. The page refreshes with a 
results list of only service orders. 
3. Select one of the following options: 
• Duplicate: Click to make a complete copy of the 
current service order. 
• Print: Click to print the Service order information 
page of the service order. 
• Email: Click to email the Service order information 
page of the service order. 
4. Click the Proceed button. The system opens a PDF file 
of the service order for printing. 
5. Print the service order, and then close the PDF file.

subcontract. 
To create a new subcontract: 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Spend Management > All > Daily Tasks > 
Create a Subcontract`

Daily Tasks section on the All tab, select Subcontract. 
2. At a minimum, complete required fields: 
• Date: Select the contract start date. 
• Expiration date: Select the contract end date. 
• Contractor: Select the contractor. 
• Bill to: Select the location to bill. 
3. Complete the line entry table. 
• At a minimum, complete these required fields: 
• 
Location: Select the location from the 
drop-down list for the item. 
• 
Job: Select the job from the drop-down list for 
the item. 
• 
Cost code: Select the cost code from the 
drop-down list for the item. 
• 
Item Desc: Type a short item description of 
the item. 
• 
Schedule value: Type the scheduled value for 
the item.

Spend Management Periodic Tasks (QS) 

The Periodic Tasks section includes various features of the 
Spend Management application. 
To view the periodic tasks: 

Spend Management > All > Periodic Tasks 

• 
Open purchase orders: View only open purchase 
orders. 
• 
Spend Inquiry: Create custom inquiries into company 
and property expenditures by reporting period. 
• 
Site view: Access the Spend Management Site 
Experience from the core Spend Management 
application. 
• 
Spend management views: Review a list of custom 
views created in Spend Management, including view 
created for the Spend management workbench, 
Approval workbench, and Spend inquiry pages. 
• 
Vendor property accounts: View vendors associated 
with your Spend Management implementation. 
• 
 Saved items: Add and store frequently used items 
in an offline shopping list for purchase orders. 
• 
 Contracts: View available contracts when your 
system is integrated with the Bids and Contracts 
product. 

Running and Exporting a Spend Inquiry 

Use the Spend inquiry page to perform spend inquiries on 
A/P invoices, purchase orders, service contracts, and 
subcontract transactions. 
To create custom inquiries by reporting period: 

Spend Management > All > Periodic Tasks > Spend Inquiry 

1. Apply a view or use filters to set up a new view. 
2. Review and organize the results in the table. 
3. Type the file name of the export in the File name field. 
4. Type the name of the worksheet table in the Sheet 
name field. 
5. Select either Export Detail or Export Summary for the 
report. 
6. Click the Export to Excel button to save the results to 
an Excel spreadsheet. 
• Alternatively, click the Save View As button to save 
the field selections as the default view. 

Using Full Service Invoice Processing Upload (QS) 

Use the Invoice Processing Upload page to create new 

invoices in Spend Management from scanned invoices 
without inputting the invoices manually. 
To upload an invoice: 

Spend Management > All > Full Service > Invoice 
Processing Upload 

1. From the Spend management application menu, in the 
Full Service section on the All tab, select Invoice 
Processing Upload. The Invoice processing upload 
page opens. 
2. Click the Upload link next to the location you want to 
view invoices for. The OpsInvoice image inbox page 
opens. 
3. Click the New button. The Add Image File page opens. 
4. Click the Upload link next to the Image field, and then 
select the file you want to upload. 
5. Type the number of invoices included in the file in the 
Invoice Count field. 
6. Type notes related to the invoices for processing in the 
Notes field. 
7. Click the Save button. The system uploads the file and 
adds it to the Invoice processing upload page with a 
status of Pending. 
To view an uploaded invoice: 

1. From the Invoice processing upload page, click the 
Upload link next to the location you want to view 
invoices for. The OpsInvoice image inbox page 
opens. 
2. Click the link in the OID column for the invoice you want 
to view or edit. The Edit Image File page opens. 
3. Click the 
 View button next to the Image field, and 
then select the file you want to upload. 
4. Close the PDF file after you finish viewing it. 

Using the Full Service Invoice Exception Queue (QS) 

Use the Invoice Exception Queue page to resolve invoice 
processing issues. The 
 Invoice exception button near 
the top of the page appears with a number when there are 
invoices in the exception queue. 
To resolve an exception invoice: 

Spend Management > All > Full Service > Invoice 
Exception Queue 

1. From the Spend management application menu, in the 
Full Service section on the All tab, select Invoice 
Exception Queue. The Invoice exception queue 
page opens. 
2. Click the 
 Invoice exception button. The Invoice 
exception queue page opens. 
3. Click the link in the Invoice OID column to open the 
invoice. 
4. Update the list of invoice comments and exceptions, 
and then send the invoice back to the team for final 

processing: 
5. After all exception messages are entered, click the Add 
Comment button. The messages are added below the 
list of invoice exception messages including the date 
the message was added, the user ID of the person who 
added the message, the comment for the action, and 
the description of the message that was selected. 
6. Select a line item, and then click the Action button. 
• To save updates and return to the list of invoices, 
click the Save button. 
• If the invoice should be voided, click the Void 
button, and then click Void again to proceed with 
voiding the invoice. 
• If the invoice is ready to go to the team, click the 
Route to Pending QC button. The invoice no longer 
appears on the Invoice Exception Queue page. 

Running Reports 

The Reports feature lets you process and store the 
following reports. 
To process, review, and store reports: 


> **Navigation Path:** `Spend Management > All > Reports`


1. From the Spend management application menu, in the 
Reports section on the All tab, select a report to run 
from the list. 
2. Complete each report section: 
• Time period: Specify the time period. 
• Filters: Select filtering criteria. 
• Format: Choose the report format. 
• Titles: Name the report. 
3. Click the View button to view the report in the browser 
window. 
4. Click the Customize button after running the report to 
refine and rerun the report. 
5. Click the Add to dashboard button to add the report to 
the dashboard. 
6. Click the Memorize button to save the report 
parameters. 
7. Click these buttons to save and share the report: 
• Print: Download and print the report. 
• Export: Select a format for exporting the report. 
• Email: Share the report via email. 
8. Click Process & Store to save the report in the Spend 
Management application.

## AI Finance Agent
*Source: `RP Financial Suite AI Finance Agent User Guide.pdf`, Page 9*

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Financial Suite AI Finance Agent User Guide 

AI Finance Agent 

The AI Finance Agent streamlines accounting operations by automating key tasks and reducing manual effort. It 

helps identify missing expenses, records monthly accruals, approves invoices within set criteria, and processes 

payments automatically. The agent also reads and codes invoices, identifies critical information in contracts, and 

handles bank reconciliations with minimal intervention.  

Use the Finance Agent application to view and manage all AI-related activities in the Financial Suite in one 

centralized location.

### Finance Agent Introduction
*Source: `RP Financial Suite AI Finance Agent User Guide.pdf`, Page 12*

Welcome to the Finance Agent 

RealPage Financial Suite AI Finance Agent User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Finance Agent Introduction 

The Finance Agent is your smart assistant for handling financial tasks with ease. Whether you’re 

tracking expenses, generating invoices, or running reports, it helps you stay organized and 

efficient. With real-time insights, it simplifies your workflow, reduces errors, and supports 

confident, data-driven decisions—so you can focus on what matters most. 

The Finance Agent is composed of several high-powered AI subagents.  

• 
A/P Invoices: The AI finance agent reads in invoices that you email, scan in, or upload and 

then turns them into invoice records. When approvals are enabled, the system automatically 

approves invoices from your standard vendors when they meet your set tolerances.  

• 
Contracts: With AI contract scanning, the AI finance agent reads the text of new contract 

attachments and uses the configured clause names and keywords to find and highlight the 

information that your company most cares about. 

• 
Bank reconciliation: The AI finance agent automatically completes bank reconciliations, and 

when approvals are enabled, sends reconciliations for approval. 

• 
Automated Actions: The AI finance agent automatically inactivates vendors when they meet 

your set criteria. The agent can also recognize and set a standard vendor’s default expense 

account, and begin the escheatment process automatically.  

• 
Standard Vendor Types: The AI finance agent checks for invoices from standard vendors, 

and if invoices have not been received within two months, the agent notifies you that 

invoices may be missing. When approvals are enabled, the system also automatically 

approves invoices from standard vendors. 

• 
Bank Statements: You can upload bank statements and have the AI finance agent turn the 

line items on the bank statement into transactions in a bank feed record. 

• 
Automated Accruals: The AI finance agent creates accrual templates and automatically 

posts accruals when timely invoices are not received. 

• 
Automated Payments: The AI finance agent makes regularly scheduled payments 

automatically. 

• 
Financial Close: The AI finance agent runs jobs that automatically close books for the 

subledgers that you choose, and generates work paper packages automatically. 

Each of these functions requires configuration. Refer to the Setting Up the Finance Agent (on 

page 15) section for configuration instructions.

### Finance Agent Menu, Setup Tab
*Source: `RP Financial Suite AI Finance Agent User Guide.pdf`, Page 16*

Welcome to the Finance Agent 

RealPage Financial Suite AI Finance Agent User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Finance Agent Menu, Setup Tab 

Before AI agents can operate within your system, each AI-enabled task must be configured to 

match your workflow preferences. These are the options on the Setup tab of the Finance Agent 

menu: 

• 
AI Configuration (on page 25): Use this menu option to configure AI invoice scanning, 

contract screening, bank reconciliation, automatic invoice approvals when the invoice comes 

from a standard vendor type, and several additional automated actions. 

Close Configuration 

• 
Work Paper Configuration (on page 54): Use this menu option to create work paper 

configurations so that you can generate the work paper packages that meet your business 

needs. 

• 
Tasks (on page 70): Use this menu option to view, add, and edit tasks. Before you can 

generate a work paper package, you must set up tasks to be performed during the work 

paper configuration. 

• 
Close Checklist (on page 76): Use this menu option to assign monthly tasks to accountants 

and track the progress for month-end close across entities or locations. 

• 
Monthly Checklist (on page 92): Use this menu option to assign tasks to users to complete 

over the course of the month.

### Finance Agent Action Cards
*Source: `RP Financial Suite AI Finance Agent User Guide.pdf`, Page 17*

Chapter 1: Welcome to the Finance Agent 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Financial Suite AI Finance Agent User Guide 

Finance Agent Action Cards 

The AI Finance Agent offers additional action cards that you can add to the Financial Suite Home 

Page. These action cards provide a snapshot of tasks that the Finance Agent has completed and 

that now require your action. These are the Finance Agent action cards: 

• 
Bank Reconciliation 

• 
AI Invoice Queue Count 

• 
Missing Expenses - Current Month 

• 
Missing Expenses - Prior Month 

• 
Automated Accruals - Current Month 

• 
Automated Accruals - Prior Month 

Prerequisites 

Before the Finance Agent action cards can appear on the Home page, you must have the 

following: 

• 
Your company must subscribe to the AI Finance Agent application. 

• 
You must have permissions to view each type of data. For example, to view the AI invoice 

queue count, you must have the View permission for A/P invoices and the Run permission 

for the AI Invoice Queue. 

AI Finance Agent Action Cards 

Clicking a number in an action card opens the task list associated with the action. 

AI Invoice Queue Count: This card displays the number of invoices that have been AI-processed 

and that are in queue.  

• 
Click the number to open the AI-Invoice Queue list where you can view, edit, review, and 

archive AI-processed invoices. You can also upload and scan invoices from this list. 

---


<!-- Page 18 -->
Welcome to the Finance Agent 

RealPage Financial Suite AI Finance Agent User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Bank Reconciliation: This card displays the number of open and automatically completed 

reconciliations, and the number of reconciliations that are pending approval. 

• 
Click the Open number to open the Pending Bank Reconciliations list. 

• 
Click the Pending approval number to open the Approve Bank Reconciliations list where 

you can view and approve or decline reconciliations. 

Missing Expenses - Current Month: The categories that appear on this action card are 

determined by the four vendor types that have the most missing expenses for the current month. 

The rest of the categories are combined in the Other category.  

• 
Click a number to open the Missing Expenses list, filtered for the current month and vendor 

type that you clicked. For example, if you clicked 5 for Landscaping, the Missing Expenses 

list opens filtered for Landscaping vendors. 

Missing Expenses - Prior Month: The categories that appear on this action card are determined 

by the four vendor types that have the most missing expenses. The rest are combined in the 

Other category.  

• 
Click a number to open the Missing Expenses list, filtered for the previous month and the 

vendor type that you clicked.

To Do List on the Financial Suite Home Page 

The To Do list on the Financial Suite Home page shows tasks that the AI Finance Agent has 

started and that are waiting for you to complete the final steps. Clicking the View button opens a 

corresponding list of transactions that have been processed by AI. 

Prerequisites 

• 
Your company must subscribe to the AI Finance Agent. 

• 
The tasks that appear depend on your permissions. 

AI Finance Agent Tasks 

Tasks that may appear in the To Do List include:  

• 
Pending Reconciliation - Bank Rec: This task appears when a bank reconciliation is pending 

your approval. Select the View button to open the Approve Reconciliations list. 

• 
Approval Needed - Invoice Approvals: This task appears when invoices require your 

approval. Select the View button to open the Approval workbench. 

• 
Invoice Entry - AI Invoice: This task appears when the AI agent has received and processed 

invoices and place them in the queue. Click the View button to open the AI-Invoice Queue 

list. 

• 
Review Needed - Missing Expenses: This task appears when the AI agent has identified 

missing expenses and has placed them in the list for your review. Select the View button to 

open the Missing Expenses list. 

• 
Review Needed - Accruals: This task appears when the AI agent has calculated accruals that 

need your review. Click the View button to open the Accruals workbench. 

• 
*Check Printing - Payment: This task appears when printed check payment requests need 

to be confirmed. Click the View button to open the Print Checks page. 

• 
*ACH Creation - Payment: This task appears when the AI agent has selected an ACH 

payment request for payment. Select the View button to open the ACH Payment File list.

Subscribing to the Finance Agent 

The Finance Agent is a powerful tool designed to make your financial tasks easier and more 

efficient. To access the Finance Agent, you’ll need an active subscription with a small additional 

fee.  

To subscribe to the Finance Agent: 

1. 
Open the Company menu. 

2. 
Click the Setup tab of the menu. 

3. 
Click Subscriptions. 

4. 
In the Applications tab, find the Finance Agent application. 

5. 
Click the toggle to subscribe. The Finance Agent box opens.  

6. 
Click the Subscribe button. The system displays the configuration page for the Finance 

Agent. 

7. 
Configure the Finance Agent (on page 24). 

8. 
Click Save.  

You are now subscribed to the Finance Agent. The next time you sign in, the Finance Agent 

appears in the list of applications.

Enabling Finance Agent Permissions 

After your company has subscribed to the Finance Agent application, you must grant permissions 

to use the application’s features.  

Financial Suite environments are set up to be either roles-based or user-based.  

• 
If your system is role-based, you can create a custom role or you can add Finance Agent 

permissions to existing roles. To add the permissions to an existing role, follow the 

instructions in the Role-based Permissions section. 

• 
If your system is user-based, then follow the instructions in the User based permissions 

section. 

Role-based Permissions 

To add Finance Agent permissions to an existing role: 

1. 
Open the Company menu. 

2. 
Click the Setup tab of the menu. 

3. 
Select the Roles menu option. 

4. 
Find the role that you want to add the permissions to, and then click the Subscriptions link.  

5. 
In the Roles Subscriptions page, find the Finance Agent application, and then click the 

check box next to Finance Agent.  

6. 
Click the Permissions link on the Finance Agent row. The Finance Agent Permissions page 

opens. 

7. 
Select the permissions that you want to grant to the role. 

8. 
Click the Save button on the Finance Agent Permissions page. 

9. 
Click the Save button on the Roles subscriptions page. 

10. 
Click the Done button to close the list.

Finance Agent Roles 

Roles are used in the Finance Agent to determine who receives emails from the system when the 

AI agent completes a task.  

• 
Assign the Finance Agent - Automated Accrual Notifications role to users who should 

receive an email every time the AI agent completes processing automated accruals. 

• 
Assign the Finance Agent – Automated Payment Notifications role to users who should 

receive an email every time the AI agent completes the processing of automated payments. 

Access to AI Finance Agent functionality is controlled through permission assignments. Each 

permission defines the level of access and the specific actions a user can perform within the 

Finance Agent. 

You can create a custom role and assign it only specific permissions as needed. For example, if 

you want to limit a user to the AI Finance Agent payments, then you would create a new role and 

assign the Agent payments permissions to the role. To create a new role, see Adding a Role. 

Finance Agent – Automated Accrual Notifications 

No permissions are associated with this role. 

Assign this role to a user who should receive email notifications when the Finance Agent 

completes an accrual task. 

Finance Agent – Automated Payment Notifications 

No permissions are associated with this role. 

Assign this role to a user who should receive email notifications when the Finance Agent 

completes a payment.

AI Configuration Powered by Lumina Page 

This page is composed of seven sections: 

• 
AI Invoice Scanning (on page 26): Enable AI scanning of incoming invoices, and set up how 

you want the system to handle due dates, itemization, and automatic posting.  

• 
AI Contract Screening (on page 29): Define the clauses and keywords that you want the 

system to display in a contract record. 

• 
Bank Reconciliation (on page 32): Allow the system to automatically complete bank 

reconciliations or send for approval, and then set up keywords to book journal entries for 

charges, interest, or other entries. 

• 
Automated Actions (on page 34): Allow the system to inactivate vendors, automatically set 

vendors’ default expense accounts, begin escheatment for uncleared checks and aging 

unpaid invoices, and set up notifications for missing expenses. 

• 
Standard Vendor Types (on page 37): Set up standard vendor types, select standard 

vendors, and enable  automatic approval of invoices for standard vendors. 

• 
Automated Accruals (on page 43): Set up automated accruals which allows the system to 

create accrual templates.  

• 
Automated Payments (on page 47): Set up automated payments for regularly scheduled 

invoices.

### AI-Invoice Scanning
*Source: `RP Financial Suite AI Finance Agent User Guide.pdf`, Page 36*

Setting Up the Finance Agent 

RealPage Financial Suite AI Finance Agent User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

AI-Invoice Scanning 

The AI-Invoice feature automates the process of bringing A/P invoices into the system, creating 

A/P invoice records by reading and extracting key information from the invoice document.  

How It Works 

The AI agent receives invoices when you scan, upload, or email invoices to the system. You can 

scan or upload invoices directly into the Financial Suite or set up an email address for vendors 

and employees to send invoices for AI processing. 

The AI agent scans the document and extracts all relevant information, including the invoice 

number, date, amount, vendor, property, and line-item descriptions.  

To find a vendor in the system that matches the vendor on the invoice, the agent first looks for a 

vendor record with a matching Vendor name. If it doesn’t find a match, then it will look for a 

matching Print as name instead. If it still doesn’t find a match, it will check for a matching vendor 

address. 

After the AI agent processes an invoice, the result is an A/P invoice record. You can view the 

invoice records that the agent created in the AI-invoice queue list. 

Configuration 

Before you can use the AI-Invoice Scanning agent, you must enable the AI-Invoice Scanning 

function and configure its settings. See Configuring AI-Invoice Scanning (on page 27) for more 

information. 

Agent Processing Results 

After configuring AI-invoice scanning, use the following pages to track the progress of invoices 

that have been processed by the AI-Invoice scanning agent: 

• 
AI-Invoice Queue: (on page 113) This page displays a list of all invoices successfully 

processed by the AI-Invoice feature.  

• 
AI-Invoice Upload Audit (on page 139): This page provides an additional view for 

administrators to monitor which email addresses the invoices are submitted from, what time 

they’re submitted, and who submitted them. 

To monitor the scanned invoice progress, you can add an action card to your Home page for AI 

invoice queue count. To add an action card, see Adding a Finance Agent Action Card to the 

Home Page (on page 10). 

When the AI Agent Fails to Match an Invoice to a Property 

When an invoice is sent into the AI-Invoice queue and the AI Finance Agent cannot identify the 

property, the AI agent creates invoice but does not assign a property to it. The AI agent places the 

invoice in the AI-Invoice Queue list where the submitter can access it.

AI Contract Scanning 

The AI contract scanning feature allows you to define keywords that the AI agent uses to 

automatically identify and extract contract clauses—such as management agreements and vendor 

contracts—so that you don’t have to read through the full document to find the information.  

Configuration 

By configuring keywords on the AI Configuration page, you enable the system to scan uploaded 

contracts and pull out any clauses that contain those terms. This streamlines clause management 

by ensuring that key sections of a contract are captured without manual review. 

After configuring this feature, the extracted data is available in the Contract record, and in the 

Contract Activity report. All information that the AI agent extracted can be edited. 

To use this feature, the contract must be uploaded as a PDF attachment to the contract 
record. 

How It Works 

After you define the keywords, you upload a PDF of a contract into the system. The AI agent 

analyzes the document, locates matching clauses, and extracts them into the system for further 

review or processing.

Bank Reconciliation 

The Bank Reconciliation feature in the Finance Agent application automates the process of 

reconciliation.  

Configuration 

Before the process can be automated, you must define the transaction types to create manual 

journal entries for each month, such as bank fees and interest. In addition, specifying a G/L 

account and whether the transaction would be a debit or credit completes the definition of each 

transaction type’s reconciliation process. 

This feature offers a companion action card. To enable the bank reconciliation action card, see 

Adding a Finance Agent Action Card to the Home Page (on page 10). 

How It Works 

The system reconciles transactions of the defined transaction types, and books journal entries for 

you automatically. 

Configuring Bank Reconciliation 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Finance Agent > Setup > AI Configuration > Bank Reconciliation`


You can configure the system to: 

• 
Mark the reconciliation as reconciled--or submit it for approval--when the amount to 

reconcile is zero. 

• 
Book journal entries for charges, interest, or other entities based on keywords that you 

configure. 

To configure bank reconciliation: 

1. 
Open the Finance Agent menu, and then click the Setup tab of the menu. 

2. 
Click the AI Configuration menu option. The AI Configuration Powered by Lumina page 

opens. 

3. 
Find the Bank Reconciliation section. 

4. 
Select the Auto complete bank reconciliations or send for approval, if enabled check box 

to have the AI agent mark the reconciliation as reconciled or submit it for approval when 

the amount to reconcile is zero. 

5. 
To allow the system to book transactions based on the keywords, define the transactions 

and the keywords to associate with them: 

• 
In the Transaction type column, select the transaction type to configure for 

reconciliation.

### Automated Actions
*Source: `RP Financial Suite AI Finance Agent User Guide.pdf`, Page 44*

Setting Up the Finance Agent 

RealPage Financial Suite AI Finance Agent User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Automated Actions 

Use the Automated Actions section of the AI Configuration page to have the system take action 

when specific situations arise.  

Inactivating Vendor Records Automatically 

You can inactivate vendor records. Inactivating a vendor record doesn’t delete the vendor, it 

marks them as inactive, preserving their history while keeping your system lean. 

• 
Inactive vendors who haven’t been paid in months or years can clutter your vendor list, 

making it harder to find active ones. Inactivating them streamlines searches and reports. 

• 
Inactive vendors can skew reports if not properly managed. Marking them as inactive 

ensures cleaner data for audits, budgeting, and forecasting. 

• 
Auditors often look for signs of good data hygiene. Inactivating unused vendors shows that 

your organization maintains accurate and up-to-date records. 

• 
In large systems, reducing the number of active records can improve performance and 

reduce processing time for tasks like batch payments or vendor analysis. 

Triggering Automatic Escheatment 

You can trigger escheatment based on time. Starting the escheatment process based on time 

thresholds helps you stay compliant, reduce liability, and maintain clean financial records. 

• 
Legal compliance: States require businesses to report and remit unclaimed property after a 

set period (often 1–5 years). Starting the escheatment process early ensures you meet 

deadlines and avoid penalties or audits. 

• 
Risk management: Uncleared checks and unpaid invoices represent contingent liabilities. If 

left unresolved, they can distort your financial statements and expose your business to fraud 

or errors. 

• 
Operational efficiency: Automating escheatment helps clean up stale records and reduces 

manual tracking of dormant transactions. It also improves reconciliation and frees up 

resources for active accounts. 

• 
Customer protection: Escheatment ensures that funds eventually reach the rightful 

owner—even if they forgot or lost track of the payment. It’s a safeguard against 

permanently losing access to owed money. 

---

### Standard Vendor Types
*Source: `RP Financial Suite AI Finance Agent User Guide.pdf`, Page 47*

Chapter 2: Setting Up the Finance Agent 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Financial Suite AI Finance Agent User Guide 

Standard Vendor Types 

Standard vendors are vendors that send you an invoice regularly, such as utilities vendors. 

Standard vendor types are used in the system to: 

• 
Identify missing expenses and create accruals.  

The AI agent creates accruals when it detects missing expenses from standard vendors.  

• 
Automatically approve invoices from standard vendors. 

When an invoice from a standard vendor is received, the AI agent compares the amount on 

the invoice with the typical amount for the vendor. If the amount is within the configured 

tolerance level, it automatically approves the invoice. 

Configuring Standard Vendors 

Use the Standard Vendor Types section of the AI Configuration page to: 

• 
Identify your standard vendor types. 

• 
Choose whether you want to have the AI agent automatically approve invoices for the 

standard vendors when the invoice amounts fall within a tolerance percentage. 

Example 

Standard vendor types: 

• 
Utilities – Water  

• 
Utilities – Electricity  

When you select Utilities - Water and Utilities - Electricity in the Standard Vendor Types list, and 

then click the Set Standard Vendors button, the AI agent searches your system for all vendors 

marked as Utilities – Water and Utilities – Electricity. It detects which of these vendors have had 

one invoice each month for the last six months, and then sets them as standard vendors.  

The AI agent analyzes the vendors’ relationship with each entity individually.  

• 
If vendor A has sent only one invoice in the last six months for entity Coconut Cove, then 

vendor A would not be set as a standard vendor for Coconut Cove. 

• 
If vendor A has sent one invoice each month for the last six months for entity Villa Verano, 

then vendor A would be set as a standard vendor for Villa Verano. 

The first time that this process runs, the system processes the vendors for every entity. After the 

first time, the system finds the new vendors and sets only the new vendors. The AI agent will not 

remove any existing standard vendors. 

The system does not process TEMP or REIM vendors.

Enabling Automatic Approval of Invoices for Standard Vendors 


> **Navigation Path:** `Finance Agent > Setup > AI Configuration > Standard Vendor Types > Agent Invoice 
Approval`


You can have the AI agent automatically approve invoices when the invoices are from standard 

vendors of an entity. Before the AI agent can approve invoices, it checks to make sure that the 

invoice amount falls within a reasonable range and is not for an unusual amount. To set this up, 

you set a tolerance percentage. This tells the AI agent how much the invoice amount may vary 

from the usual invoices from the vendor. For example, if you set the tolerance percentage at 10% 

and you receive an invoice that is 15% higher than usual, then the AI agent will not automatically 

approve the invoice. You can approve invoices that fall outside of the tolerance percentage 

manually from the Approval workbench in Accounts Payable.  

Before you begin, you must have defined standard vendors (on page 38) for your entities. 

To set up automatic invoice approval for invoices from standard vendors: 

1. 
Open the Finance Agent menu. 

2. 
Click the Setup tab of the menu. 

3. 
Click AI Configuration. 

4. 
Find the Standard Vendor Types section of the page.  

5. 
Below the list of standard vendor types, find the Agent Invoice Approval section.  

6. 
Select the check box next to Auto approve invoices for standard vendors within tolerance. 

7. 
In the Tolerance percentage field, type the percentage that represents the variance limit for 

automatic approvals. 

8. 
Click Save.

### Automated Accruals
*Source: `RP Financial Suite AI Finance Agent User Guide.pdf`, Page 53*

Chapter 2: Setting Up the Finance Agent 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Financial Suite AI Finance Agent User Guide 

Automated Accruals 

Use the AI agent accruals feature to have the system assist in ensuring that income and expenses 

are recorded in the period they actually occur, not just when cash changes hands.  

Configuration 

You set up automated accruals by defining how and when the AI agent calculates accruals. 

In the Automated Accruals section of the AI Configuration page, you select the following to set 

up automated accruals: 

• 
A standard vendor type, like utilities 

• 
The debit and credit accounts 

• 
The day of the month that you want to run the accruals 

• 
Which period to calculate the accrual for, the current period or the previous period.  

You also choose whether to post the accrual or not.  

How It Works 

After setting up an automatic accrual, the system creates an accrual template. You can find the 

template in the Agent Accruals list (on page 211). When the AI agent processes an accrual, the 

system sends an email to notify you. To receive an email about accruals, you must be assigned to 

the Finance Agent - Automated Accrual Notification role. See Enabling Finance Agent 

Permissions (on page 19). 

Changing Automated Accruals 

You can change any automatically saved accrual in the Automated Accruals section of the AI 

Configuration page or use the Agent Accruals menu option on the Finance Agent menu. There, 

you can open the accrual template and change many of the details such as the journal, 

description, reference number, and segments.  

Action Card 

You can add action cards to your Home page for automated accruals for the current month and 

for the prior month. To add these action cards, see Adding a Finance Agent Action Card to the 

Home Page (on page 10). 

---

Automated Payments 

The automated payments feature uses the Ai agent to make payments for standard expenses.  

Configuration 

Before you can use the automated payments feature, you must configure payment schedules for 

each standard vendor type that you want to pay automatically. For each standard vendor type, 

you specify the payment method to use, the bank account to draw money from, the date to start 

the automatic payments, and how often to pay them.   

How It Works 

The Ai agent creates a payment based on the schedule that you configure, and then notifies the 

user whose email address that you included.  

Changing Automatic Payment Schedules 

Payment schedules can only be created from the AI Configuration page, but you can view and 

update the schedules from either the Agent Payments list or the AI Configuration page.

The Work paper configuration list page lets you view, add, and edit work paper configurations. 

Before you can generate a work paper package, you must set up a work paper configuration. For 

example, if you want to perform a regular month-end close for a specific property or group of 

properties, set up a monthly work paper configuration that pulls the work papers you want from 

those properties. 

Accessing the Work Paper Configuration List Page 

Use one of these methods to access the Work paper configuration list page: 

• 
From the Home page, click the Applications menu, select Financial close management, and 

then click Work paper configuration on the Setup tab. 

• 
From the Financial close management home page, click the Work paper configuration 

button in the Data section. 

•

configuration menu option in the Close Configuration section of the menu.

a) Edit: This link allows you to edit a work paper configuration (on page 63). You also have the 

option to duplicate the configuration instead of editing it. 

b) View: This link allows you to view and preview a work paper configuration (on page 56).

1.

Click the Preview button. Your browser downloads an Excel file.

Work Paper Configuration (on page 64) for more information. 

Viewing or Exporting the Audit Trail for this Configuration 

The system keeps track of all changes that you and other users make to each record. To view the 

audit trail for this work paper configuration, click More actions, and then select Audit trail. The 

Audit Trail box opens with a list of changes that users have made recently. See Viewing Audit

Editing a Work Paper Configuration 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Financial Close Management > Setup > Configuration > Work Paper 
Configuration > Edit`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Finance Agent > Setup > Close Configuration > Work Paper 
Configuration > Edit`


You can edit any of the features of a work paper configuration. For example, you can make 

changes to subledger sources for work papers, add or remove properties, and update designated 

approvers. 

For instance, if there is a new designated approver, you can edit a work paper configuration to 

replace the approver with the new person. All work paper packages that are generated after the 

edit will be sent to the new approver when it is their turn in the approval process. 

Any edits you make to work paper configurations affect work paper packages that are generated 

after the edits are saved. They do not affect the appearance of previously generated work papers. 

However, if you regenerate work papers after changing their configuration, the changes appear 

with the regenerated work papers. 

To edit a work paper configuration: 

1. 
Open the Financial Close Management or Finance Agent menu, and then click the Setup 

tab. 

2. 
Select the Work paper configuration option. 

3. 
On the Work paper configuration list page, click the Edit link next to the work paper 

configuration you want to edit. The Work Paper Configuration information page loads. 

4. 
To update the name of the work paper configuration, type the new name in the Name field. 

5. 
From the Type drop-down list, select Monthly or Annual. 

If you want to create an Annual work paper configuration based on a Monthly work paper 
configuration (or vice versa), click the Duplicate button. See Duplicating a Work Paper 
Configuration (on page 64 ) for more information. 

6. 
To update the approver, select the approver from the Approver drop-down list. 

7. 
To update the reviewer, select the reviewer from the Reviewer drop-down list. 

The roles of Approver and Reviewer can be a user or group of users. After the Approver has 
completed the task of approving the work paper, the work paper will continue to the next 
step and user, if different, in the workflow. 

8. 
To update the status from active to inactive (or vice versa), select Active or Inactive from the 

Status drop-down list.

Duplicating a Work Paper Configuration 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Financial Close Management > Setup > Configuration > Work Paper 
Configuration > Edit/View`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Finance Agent > Setup > Close Configuration > Work Paper 
Configuration > Edit/View`


Duplicating a work paper configuration lets you create a new work paper configuration based on 

an existing work paper configuration, eliminating the need to start over each time you want to 

create a new configuration. 

For example, to generate year-end work papers using the same (or similar) criteria as your 

monthly work papers, duplicate the monthly work paper configuration to add a new annual work 

paper configuration based on the monthly configuration. Add “Annual” to the name, change the 

type to Annual, make any other necessary edits, and then click the Save button. As a result, you 

have both a monthly and an annual configuration for the same setup. 

To create a new work paper configuration based on an existing work paper configuration: 

1. 
Open the Financial Close Management or Finance Agent menu, and then click the Setup 

tab. 

2. 
Select the Work paper configuration option. 

3. 
On the Work paper configuration list page, click either the Edit or View link next to the 

work paper configuration you want to use. The Work Paper Configuration information page 

loads. 

4. 
Click the Duplicate button. The screen refreshes with a form for adding a new work paper 

configuration, and the configuration settings match that of the configuration you 

duplicated. 

---

> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Finance Agent > Setup > Close Configuration > Tasks > Edit`


To edit a new task: 

1. 
Open the Financial Close Management or Finance Agent menu, and then click the Setup 

tab. 

2. 
Select the Tasks option. The Tasks details page opens. 

3. 
Click the Edit button next to a task. The Tasks detail page opens. 

4. 
In the Task field, the name of the task cannot be changed. 

5. 
In the Description field, change the short description. 

6. 
Click Save to submit the updated task and return to the Tasks list page. 

• 
Click Cancel to return to the Tasks list page without saving any changes made. 

• 
Click Duplicate to create a duplicate of the task. 

• 
Click Print to to view and download the task as a PDF file or an XML file. 

• 
Click More Actions to either save the changes and open a new Tasks information page 

or change the table size settings.

Adding a Close Checklist 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Financial Close Management > Setup > Configuration > Close Checklist 
> Add`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Finance Agent > Setup > Close Configuration > Close Checklist > Add`


To add a new close checklist: 

1. 
Open the Financial Close Management or Finance Agent menu. 

2. 
Click the Setup tab, and then click Close checklist.  

3. 
Click Add. The Close checklist page opens. 

• 
Alternatively, you can click the 
 New button next to the Close checklist option to 

access this form. 

4. 
In the Close checklist name field, type the name of the close checklist. 

5. 
From the Status drop-down list, select Active or Inactive. 

6. 
From the Tasks drop-down list, select a task to be performed. 

• 
If you are unable to find a task in the list, click the Find link. The Select Tasks box 

opens. See Select Tasks Box (on page 84) for more information. 

7. 
From the Generate after task drop-down list, select a task to generate after the previous 

task is completed. 

You can choose to generate tasks after ones in the same checklist as well as another 
checklist, including monthly and close checklists. 

---
