#### Troubleshooting Reconciliations
*Source: `RP Financial Suite AI Finance Agent User Guide.pdf`, Page 316*

Using the Finance Agent 

RealPage Financial Suite AI Finance Agent User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Troubleshooting Reconciliations 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Cash Management > All > Reconciliation > Bank > Continue`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Finance Agent > All > Cash Management > Bank Reconciliation > 
Continue`


Reconciliation differences must be resolved before you can finalize the reconciliation. 

The following procedures walk you through resolving common reconciliation issues. 

Amount to Reconcile Field Is Not Zero 

A non-zero value in the Amount to reconcile field indicates an error made in the reconciliation 

process. 

There are uncleared checks or deposits. 

If there are uncleared checks or deposits for bank or check reconciliation, or uncleared charges 

and payments for credit card reconciliation: 

1. 
Make sure all transactions that have cleared the bank are marked as cleared. 

2. 
Make sure that you entered all manual checks and that their amounts in the system are the 

same on the statement. 

An item was accidentally cleared. 

Cause: 

You accidentally cleared an item that didn’t clear the bank yet. 

Solution: 

Only check off items that you are sure have cleared. Uncheck the item that was inadvertently 

cleared. Uncheck items that have not cleared the bank. 

Transactions were entered in a previously reconciled period. 

If there are transactions entered in a previously reconciled period: 

• 
If the transaction is in the correct period, reopen the reconciliation and reconcile again. 

• 
If the transaction is not in the correct period, edit the transaction to fall in an open period or 

the correct period. 

Other reasons the Amount to Reconcile field might not be zero. 

1. 
Verify that you entered the statement ending balance correctly. 

2. 
For first-time reconciliations, make sure that you entered the initial open items correctly and 

that you cleared the compensating initial open items entry. 

---


<!-- Page 317 -->
Chapter 3: Using the Finance Agent 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Financial Suite AI Finance Agent User Guide 

3. 
Make sure that you entered all miscellaneous charges that appear on your statement, such 

as service charges and interest earned for bank reconciliations, or finance charges and other 

fees for credit card reconciliations. 

4. 
Verify that you selected the Clear check boxes for all of the checks, deposits, charges, 

payments, or adjustments that have cleared the bank. 

If the balance is still not zero 

If the balance is still not zero, perform the following steps: 

1. 
If you can divide the difference by nine, resulting in a whole number, go back and examine 

each item by comparing it to the amount shown on the bank statement. You can correct 

any error by making an adjustment in the G/L. 

2. 
Reopen the last reconciliation and examine a snapshot of your last reconciliation to check 

for errors in transposing two items that look similar, such as two $100 checks. 

If you still cannot find the difference, you can make an adjusting entry by clicking the Add interest 

& charges link and entering a debit or credit with the description “Reconciliation Adjustment 
Entry. ” However, RealPage does not recommend this action. 

Incorrect Reconciliation Ending Date or Balance 

Perform the following steps if you accidentally entered the wrong statement ending date or 

statement ending balance for the previous reconciliation. 

1. 
In the Applications menu, select the Cash Management application, and then select the All 

tab. 

2. 
In the Reconciliation section, select View reconciliation histories.  

3. 
Find the previous reconciliation, and then click the Reopen link.  

The Reopen reconciliation confirmation box opens. 

RealPage recommends that you save a record of your cleared and open items before 
reopening a reconciliation. On the Reconciliation histories page, use the links to generate a 
Reconciliation report, an Outstanding Items report, and an Adjusted Items report. 

4. 
Click Yes to reopen the reconciliation. 

When you reopen a reconciliation for a period prior to the last reconciliation, the system 
reopens all reconciliations from that point forward. For example, say your last 
reconciliation was on 5/30, and you had previously reconciled on 4/30 and 3/30. If you 
reopen the 3/30 reconciliation, then the system will also reopen the 4/30 and 5/30 
reconciliations at the same time.  

5. 
Update the incorrect statement ending date or statement ending balance.

this number changes. It also changes according to whether you are 

clearing checks or deposits.

Pending Reconciliations 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Finance Agent > All > Cash Management > Pending Reconciliations`


Use the Pending Reconciliations option to view the list of pending bank reconciliations. 

Pending Bank Reconciliations List 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Cash Management > All > Periodic Tasks > Reconciliation > Pending 
Reconciliations`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Finance Agent > All > Cash Management > Pending Reconciliations`


The Pending bank reconciliations list displays a list of any open bank reconciliations. These are 

bank accounts for which the reconciliation process has been initiated but not finalized. 

From this list, you can: 

• 
View a bank account’s ending balance, amount to reconcile, and number of unmatched G/L 

transactions. 

• 
Open the Reconcile bank account page for a bank account. 

• 
Generate a Pending Reconciliation report for a bank account. 

• 
Export the list of open bank reconciliations to a CSV, Excel, Word, or PDF file. 

Reconciliations can be finalized after all bank statement transactions have been matched to G/L 
ledger entries in RealPage Financial Suite and the Amount to reconcile field is zero.

If you have the Submit permission (on page 324) for bank reconciliations, then you can submit 

bank reconciliations for approval. 

To submit a bank reconciliation: 

1. 
On the Reconcile bank account page, when you’ve matched your transactions and the 

Amount to reconcile is zero ($0.00), click the Submit button. 

2. 
After you submit the reconciliation, the system: 

• 
Adds the reconciliation to the Approve bank reconciliations list. 

• 
Sends an email to any users who have the Approve permission, respective of entity 

restrictions. 

• 
Locks the reconciliation to anyone who does not have the Approve permission.  

As the user who submitted the transaction, you can still view the reconciliation, but 
the Save button will no longer be available on the 
Reconcile bank account page. 

---



#### Approving and Declining Bank Reconciliations
*Source: `RP Financial Suite AI Finance Agent User Guide.pdf`, Page 336*

Using the Finance Agent 

RealPage Financial Suite AI Finance Agent User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Approving and Declining Bank Reconciliations 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Cash Management > All > Periodic Tasks > Reconciliation > Approve 
Reconciliations`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Finance Agent > All  > Cash Management > Approve Reconciliation`


If you have the Approve permission (on page 324) for bank reconciliations, then you can approve 

or decline bank reconciliations that have been submitted for approval. 

Approving Bank Reconciliations 

To approve bank reconciliations: 

1. 
In the Approve bank reconciliations list, select one or more bank reconciliations. 

2. 
Click the Approve button. 

The system validates whether the amount to reconcile on the account is zero ($0.00). 

• 
If the amount is zero, then the account is automatically reconciled. The reconciliation is 

removed from the Approve bank reconciliations list and a new entry is added to the 

Reconciliation histories list. The system also sends an email (on page 328) to each 

submitter notifying them that their reconciliation has been approved. 

• 
If the amount is not zero, then you will receive the error message “You cannot approve 

the bank reconciliation because the amount to reconcile is not zero.”  

Declining Bank Reconciliations 

To decline bank reconciliations: 

1. 
In the Approve bank reconciliations list, select one or more bank reconciliations. 

2. 
Click the Decline button. 

The Decline comments box opens. 

3. 
Type the Reason for declining the reconciliation(s). 

4. 
Click Done. 

The system sends an email (on page 328) to each submitter notifying them that their 

reconciliation has been declined. The reconciliation is removed from the Approve bank 

reconciliations list. 

---

Opting Out of Approval Notifications for Bank Reconciliations 

By default, the system sends email notifications related to bank reconciliation approvals: 

• 
If you have permission to Submit bank reconciliations, then you will receive an email 

notification if your reconciliation has been declined. 

• 
If you have permission to Approve bank reconciliations, then you will receive a single, 

consolidated email at the end of each day with a list of bank reconciliations you need to 

review. 

If you don’t want to receive these notifications, then you can opt out of them in your user 

preferences: 

1. 
Click your user name in the upper-right corner, and then select the My preferences option 

from the drop-down list. 

The Preferences page opens. 

2. 
In the Email notifications section, select the Exclude from bank reconciliation approval 

notifications check box. 

3. 
Click Save. You will no longer receive email notifications for bank reconciliation approvals.

The Reconciliation histories page displays a list of previous reconciliations and reconciliation 

events for a particular account. From this page, you can: 

• 
Attach files to the financial record. 

• 
Generate a reconciliation report with a summary of items that were reconciled in the 

reconciliation period. 

• 
Generate an outstanding items report with a summary of items that were not reconciled in 

the reconciliation period. 

• 
Generate an adjusted items report with a summary of adjustments that were made to a 

bank reconciliation. 

• 
Reopen a prior reconciliation report. 

• 
Download a reconciliation report. 

• 
Pull multiple bank reconciliations into a package with reports and attachments. 

Newer reconciliations appear at the top of the list. You can filter the list by bank account, which 

displays the reconciliation periods in descending order. 

Before You Begin 

Access can vary depending on your organization’s subscriptions and your permissions. If you do 

not see the option in the menu, then ask your System Administrator to check your permissions.

Reopening and Adjusting a Closed Reconciliation 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Cash Management > All > Periodic Tasks > Reconciliation > View 
Reconciliation Histories > Reopen`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Finance Agent > All > Cash Management > Reconciliation History > 
Reopen`


You can reopen a closed reconciliation and make adjustments to it. The system retains any 

documents or bank statements that you attached to the original reconciliation, so you don’t need 

to re-upload them. 

Before You Begin 

• 
Download the Reconciliation Report so that you have a history of what was originally 

matched and reconciled. 

• 
Make the appropriate corrections inside your company. For example, you might have 

written a check to a vendor but forgot to create the record in the system. 

Adjusting a Closed Reconciliation 

To make an adjustment to a closed reconciliation: 

1. 
In the Reconciliation histories list, find the desired reconciliation period, and then click the 

Reopen link. 

A confirmation box opens with the number of reconciliations that will be reopened. 

2. 
Click Yes to reopen the reconciliation. This action can’t be undone. 

3. 
In the Account to reconcile drop-down list, select the account that you want to reconcile, 

and then click Continue. 

The Reconcile bank account page appears. You can now re-reconcile the account for that 

period and for all subsequent periods that were reopened. For example, if you’re currently in 

the month of August and reopen the reconciliation from June, you need to re-reconcile for 

June and July. 

---

> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Cash Management > All > Periodic Tasks > Reconciliation > View 
Reconciliation Histories > Package Reconciliation History`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Finance Agent > All > Cash Management > Reconciliation History > 
Package Reconciliation History`


You can generate a PDF package that contains multiple bank reconciliation histories. Packages 

can include the Reconciliation report, Outstanding Items report, Adjusted Items report, and the 

bank statement. 

To generate a package of bank reconciliations: 

1. 
Open the Cash Management or Finance Agent menu.  

• 
In Cash Management, select the View reconciliation histories menu option in the 

Periodic tasks section, below Reconciliation. 

• 
In Finance Agent, select the Reconciliation History menu option in the Cash 

Management section. 

2. 
Click the Package reconciliation history button. 

3. 
Select the check box next to each reconciliation history that you want to include in the 

package. 

4. 
Click the Generate package button. 

The Generate reconciliation history package box opens. 

5. 
Type a name for the package. 

6. 
Select the components that you want to include in the package. 

• 
Cover page: Click the Browse button to select a custom cover page from your local 

drive. 

• 
Summary: Include a summary page with a list of reconciled bank accounts that are 

included in the package. 

• 
Attachments: Include the bank statement attached to the reconciliation record. 

• 
Reconciliation report: Include a copy of the Reconciliation report for each 

reconciliation history. 

• 
Outstanding items report: Include a copy of the Outstanding Items report for each 

reconciliation history. 

• 
Adjusted items report: Include a copy of the Adjusted Items report for each 

reconciliation history. 

7. 
Click the Build package button to generate the PDF file.

Customizing and Running the Finance Agent Activities Report 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Finance Agent > All > Reports > Finance Agent Activity`


To customize and run the Finance Agent Activity report: 

1. 
Open the Finance Agent menu. 

2. 
In the Reports column, select Finance Agent Activity. 

Filling In the Time Period Section 

Define the time period for the report.  

• 
Enter dates in the Start date and End date fields to define the scope of the report. 

Filling In the Filters Section 

Set up filters to define the data that you want to see in the report. Using filters is optional. 

1. 
To narrow the report so that it shows only specific Finance Agent actions, click the Select 

button under Action, and then choose the desired action or actions to show in the report: 

• 
Bank Reconciliation 

• 
Accrual - Missing Expense 

• 
Selected for Payment - Standard Vendor 

• 
Standard Vendor - Approve Invoice 

• 
Created Aged Payable 

• 
Inactivated Vendor 

• 
Set Vendor’s Default Expense Account 

• 
Added Contract Clause 

• 
Job Agent 

2. 
To narrow the report so that it shows actions only for specific properties, click the Select 

button under Property and then choose the desired property or properties. 

Filling In the Titles Section and Run the Report 

1. 
In the Report title 1 field, type the text that you want to appear as the main title of the 

report. 

This title displays in large type at the top of the page, directly under your company name. 

You can type over any default name that appeared automatically in this box. 

---


<!-- Page 355 -->
Chapter 4: Finance Agent Reports 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Financial Suite AI Finance Agent User Guide 

2. 
In the Report title 2 field, enter the text that you want to appear under the title of the 

report. 

The subtitle displays in smaller type, directly beneath the main title. 

3. 
Type the footer text in the Footer text box. 

Footer text displays at the bottom center of the report. 

You can use up to 80 characters, including spaces, in each title, subtitle, and footer. 

4. 
Click the View button to create the report. 

What’s Next?  

After running the report, you can: 

• 
Customize: Click the Customize button to return to the main report page and refine the 

report further. 

You can use trial-and-error to get the precise results you want by filling in the desired fields 

and then clicking View to see the report. If after viewing the results you want to refine the 

report further, click Customize to return to the report setup page. Repeat this process until 

you’re satisfied.  

• 
Print: Click the Print button to display the report in printable PDF format so you can print it 

or save it on your computer. 

• 
Process & Store: Click the Process & Store button to generate the report and store it.  

• 
Add to Dashboard: Click the Add to Dashboard button to add the report to a dashboard. 

• 
Memorize: Click the Memorize button to save the report so that you can refer to it later, or 

modify and re-run it. 

• 
Export: Click the Export button to save the report in a different format so that you can 

distribute it or save it on your computer.

Buttons 

Customize 
Opens the report’s customization page to change filters and time periods 

and to exclude specific types of data. 

The Customize button appears only after viewing a report or ledger. 

View 
Opens the report in your browser. 

Print 
Displays the report in printable PDF format so you can print it or save it on 

your computer. 

Process & store 
Generates the report and stores it for later access. 

Available formats include HTML, printable (PDF), Excel, CSV 

(comma-separated value), and Text. You can store reports in the system, 

and then access them with the My stored reports option in the menu.  

Email

and then fill in the To field with the recipient’s email address. 

This button is not available for all reports. 

Add to dashboard 
Adds the report to a dashboard. 

Select the dashboard that you want to add it to, type a name for the 

report, and then type a description of the report.  

Select the Public check box to make the report available on a dashboard. 

This option is not available for all reports.  

Memorize 
Memorizes (that is, saves) the report in the system so you can refer to it 

later or modify and re-run it. 

Reports that you memorize can be scheduled to run on a recurring basis 
and can be automatically emailed.

### Vendor Activity Report
*Source: `RP Financial Suite AI Finance Agent User Guide.pdf`, Page 374*



#### Before You Begin
*Source: `RP Financial Suite AI Finance Agent User Guide.pdf`, Page 374*

Finance Agent Reports 

RealPage Financial Suite AI Finance Agent User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Vendor Activity Report 

Company > All > Import Data > Set Up A/P Master List, Open Invoices and 
Adjustments > Standard Vendors > Activity Report 

This report provides visibility into standard vendor activity across properties and is available only 

when the Finance Agent subscription is enabled. It is designed to help users quickly identify 

standard vendors—those that are used frequently and consistently across the organization. 

Purpose of the Report 

The report analyzes standard vendor activity over the past 180 days and highlights which vendors 

are actively generating invoices. By showing how often each vendor is used, the report helps 

users: 

• 
Identify vendors that are part of routine, recurring operations. 

• 
Spot unusual or low-activity vendors that may require review. 

• 
Support vendor standardization efforts across properties. 

What the Report Shows 

For each vendor and property combination, the report displays: 

• 
Vendor Name 

• 
Property 

• 
Invoice Count (last 180 days) 

This allows users to compare vendor usage across locations and understand where vendor 

relationships are most active. 

How It Helps 

The report supports financial oversight and purchasing consistency by: 

• 
Highlighting vendors with high invoice volume. 

• 
Helping users validate whether vendors should be considered “standard.” 

• 
Providing a quick way to review vendor activity without navigating individual invoices. 

Before You Begin 

Your company must be subscribed to the Finance Agent to run this report. 

---

The Cash & Cash Equivalents report details the liquid assets on a company’s balance sheet. Cash 

includes currency and demand deposits, while cash equivalents are short-term, highly liquid 

investments. Government bonds, money market funds, and commercial paper are common types 

of cash equivalents. 

Before You Begin 

Access can vary depending on your organization’s subscriptions and your permissions. If you do 

not see the option in the menu, then ask your System Administrator to check your permissions.

Customizing and Running the Cash & Cash Equivalents Report 


> **Navigation Path:** `Application > Financial Close Management > All > Reports > Cash & Cash Equivalents 
Report`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Finance Agent > All > Financial Close Reports > Cash & Cash Equivalents

To run the Cash & Cash Equivalents report: 

1. 
Open the menu of the desired application, Financial Close Management or Finance Agent. 

2. 
In the Reports column, select Cash & Cash Equivalents. The report customization page 

opens. 

Setting Up the Time Period 

Set up the time period for the data that you want to capture in the report. 

1. 
Enter the opening balance date. 

2. 
Enter the closing balance date. 

Setting Up the Filters 

You can filter the report results by account group and by location. Both of these filters are 

required. 

1. 
Select an account group from the Account group drop-down list. 

2. 
To filter the report for a single location, select the location from the Location drop-down 

list. 

Filling In the Titles Section and Running the Report 

1. 
In the Report title 1 field, type the text that you want to appear as the main title of the 

report. 

This title displays in large type at the top of the page, directly under your company name. 

You can type over any default name that appeared automatically in this box. 

2. 
In the Report title 2 field, enter the text that you want to appear under the title of the 

report. 

The subtitle displays in smaller type, directly beneath the main title. 

3. 
Type the footer text in the Footer text box. 

Footer text displays at the bottom center of the report. 

You can use up to 80 characters, including spaces, in each title, subtitle, and footer. 

---

Finance Agent Reports 

RealPage Financial Suite AI Finance Agent User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

4. 
Click the View button to run the report. 

Optionally, you can also click the Export button to select the Excel report output link. The 

report is generated and a Save As dialog box opens. Enter a unique name for the report and 

click Save. Otherwise, click the Cancel button to discard any changes and return to the Cash 

& Cash Equivalents report page. 

What’s Next?  

After running the report, you can: 

• 
Customize: Click the Customize button to return to the main report page and refine the 

report further. 

You can use trial-and-error to get the precise results you want by filling in the desired fields 

and then clicking View to see the report. If after viewing the results you want to refine the 

report further, click Customize to return to the report setup page. Repeat this process until 

you’re satisfied.  

• 
Export: Click the Export button to save the report in Excel format so that you can distribute 

it or save it on your computer.

•

• 
Property: This is the property ID and name that the report covers. 

• 
Period: This is the period that the report covers. 

Cash & Cash Equivalents Report: [Property] 

• 
Acct#: This column displays the unique number of the account. 

• 
Account Description: This column displays a description of the account. 

• 
Amount per TB: This is the amount that is delinquent or prepaid per Trial Balance (TB). 

• 
Statement Balance: This column will be blank as we do not pull any information. 

This column is designed for the client to manually add in the balance shown on their bank 
statement for their cash account once they have run the report for comparison purposes. 

• 
Variance: This is the variance between the Amount per TB and Statement Balance columns. 

• 
Variance Explanation: This column displays the explanation for the variance. 

• 
Total: This is the total amounts for columns Amount per TB, Statement Balance, and 

Variance.

##### Accounts Payable Report Columns
*Source: `RP Financial Suite AI Finance Agent User Guide.pdf`, Page 386*

Finance Agent Reports 

RealPage Financial Suite AI Finance Agent User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Accounts Payable Report Columns 

Accounts Payable Summary Reconciliation 

This section analyzes the vendor aging balance from the general ledger balance. The goal of this 

process is to ensure that both sets of records agree, providing an accurate picture of the 

company’s liabilities and identifying any discrepancies, errors, or potential fraud. If they do not, 

the report shows the amount of variance with a column for you to enter the reason for the 

variance after the report runs. 

Accounts Payable Detail Aging for Location 

This section lists all unpaid vendor invoices, broken down by vendor, invoice, and the number of 

days the debt is past due. This report helps businesses manage their cash flow by showing what is 

owed, to whom, and when payments are due, and can often be filtered to a specific location if the 

accounting system tracks expenses by location. 

By default, the Accounts Payable report contains the following columns: 

Summary Section 

• 
Report Name: This is the name of the report, Accounts Payable report. 

• 
GL Account Group: This is the account group used for this report. 

• 
Property: This is the property ID and name that the report covers. 

• 
Period: This is the period that the report covers. 

Accounts Payable Summary Reconciliation: [Property] 

• 
Acct#: This column displays the unique number of the account. 

• 
Account Description: This column displays a description of the account. 

• 
Amount per TB: This is the amount that is delinquent or prepaid per Trial Balance (TB). 

• 
Subledger Report: This is the total amount for the account, as recorded per the vendor 

aging report. 

• 
Variance: This is the difference between Amount per TB and Subledger Report columns. 

• 
Variance Explanation: This column displays the explanation for the variance. 

• 
0 - 30 days: This is the amount you owe to your vendor that is up to 30 days past due. 

• 
31 - 60 days: This is the prepaid and delinquent amount that is at least 30 days old. 

• 
61 - 90 days: This is the prepaid and delinquent amount that is at least 60 days old. 

• 
> 91 days: This is the prepaid and delinquent amount that is 90 days old or over. 

• 
Grand Total: This is the total amounts for columns Amount per TB, Subledger Report, 

Variance, .0 - 30 days, 31 - 60 days, 61 - 90 days, and > 91 days.

A/R - Multifamily Report Columns 

Delinquent and Prepaid Tie-out 

This section analyzes the delinquent and prepaid amounts in RealPage Accounting and Leasing & 

Rents, and shows when the totals agree (tie out). When they do not, the report shows the amount 

of variance with a column for you to enter the reason for the variance after the report runs. 

Summary by Charge Code 

This section summarizes prepaid and delinquent activity by transaction code. It prints only if you 

chose to include it on the report options page. Each column is totaled, with the exception of the 

first two columns. The totals consist of transaction code level balances and may not equal the 

beginning/ending prepaid or delinquent balances in the Resident Summary Balances report, which 

totals transactions by subjournal. 

Summary by General Ledger Account 

This section summarizes prepaid and delinquent activity by G/L account. It prints only if you chose 

to include it on the report options page.

0-30 days

Delinquent and Prepaid Details: [Property] 

Unit 
This is the identifier of the unit described in the row. 

Name 
This is the tenant name and contact information. 

• 
If you have started eviction proceedings on the tenant, an 

asterisk (*) appears beside the name. 

• 
If this is a business or corporation, an asterisk (*) or caret (^) 

appears beside the name, depending on the placeholder that 

was entered as the first name of the business. 

• 
If the business is also under eviction, the system flags the 

account with an asterisk; therefore, you may see “**” or “^*” 

beside the name of a business that is under eviction. 

Status 
This is the occupancy status, such as current tenant or applicant. 

Move-in/Out 
This is the date the tenant moved in or is scheduled to move in. If this is 

a former tenant, this is the move-out date. 

Charge code 
This is the charge code description. 

If a payment is allocated to a future charge and you chose to show 

prepaids as allocated, the code has “Future:” as a prefix. 

If there are multiple transactions, a Subtotals row appears below the 

last transaction. Separate totals are calculated for prepaid, delinquent, 

net balance, and aged amounts. 

Account 
This is the account number associated with the unit. 

Total prepaid 
This is the total amount of all open payments or credits associated with 

this charge code as of the current property date. 

---


<!-- Page 394 -->
Finance Agent Reports 

RealPage Financial Suite AI Finance Agent User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Total delinquent 
This is the total of all open (or unpaid) transactions associated with this 

code as of the current property date. If a dagger symbol (†) appears 

beside an amount, the charge is delinquent due to NSF activity on the 

ledger. If a double dagger symbol (‡) appears, the charge is 120+ days 

past due. 

Net balance 
This is the net ledger balance as of the current property date. A negative 

amount is a prepaid balance; a positive amount is a delinquent balance. 

If the household has multiple transactions, the net balance prints in the 

Subtotals row and the total is: 

Total Prepaid (Subtotals) + Total Delinquent (Subtotals) 

If the subtotal has both a prepaid and delinquent balance resulting in a 
net balance of zero, the manual cash application feature is enabled in 
A/R settings, so credits (the prepaid balance) are not automatically 
applied to charges (the delinquent balance). 

0-30  
This is the prepaid or delinquent amount for this code during the 

current period. The current period is the current “Calendar” month or 

current “Fiscal” period, based on the Aging columns parameter. If aged 

by: 

• 
Calendar month, open transactions posted during the current 

calendar month are included in the total. 

• 
Fiscal period, open transactions posted in the current fiscal 

period are included in the total. 

The age is based on the original transaction date, not the date the 

amount became delinquent or prepaid. 

31-60  
This amount is at least 30 days prepaid or delinquent for this code. If 

aged by: 

• 
Calendar month, an open transaction posted during the 

previous month is included in this total. 

• 
Fiscal period, an open transaction posted in the previous fiscal 

period is included in this total. 

---


<!-- Page 395 -->
Chapter 4: Finance Agent Reports 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Financial Suite AI Finance Agent User Guide 

61-90  
This amount is at least 60 days prepaid or delinquent for this code. If 

aged by: 

• 
Calendar month, an open transaction posted in the calendar 

month that is two months prior to the current property date 

month is included. 

• 
Fiscal period, an open transaction posted in the fiscal period that 

is two periods prior to the current fiscal period is included. 

The age is based on the original transaction date and not the date the 

amount became delinquent or prepaid. 

Over 90  
This amount is at least 90 days prepaid or delinquent for this code. If 

aged by: 

• 
Calendar month, an open transaction posted in the calendar 

month that is at least three months prior to the current property 

date month is included. 

• 
Fiscal period, an open transaction posted in the fiscal period that 

is at least three periods prior to the current fiscal period is 

included. 

The age is based on the original transaction date and not the date the 

amount became delinquent or prepaid. 

Total due 
This is the total amount due. 

Prorate credits 
If the tenant is moving out or transferring in the middle of the month, 

this is the prorated credit for this code. (A separate line item appears for 

the proration that covers the exact number of days the unit is occupied 

during the billing period.) 

Deposits held 
This is the total paid deposits. 

Outstanding deposit 
This is the total unpaid deposits (required deposits less deposits held). 

#Late/#NSF 
This is the number of times the tenant paid late, and the number of 

times checks were returned due to non-sufficient funds. For example, 

3/0 means the tenant paid late three times and has no NSF checks. 

Grand Totals 
This row calculates property totals. Each column from Total Prepaid 

through Deposits Held is totaled.

This is the transaction code.

This is the G/L account of the delinquent or prepaid transaction.

footnote. 

Beginning

G/L accounts will equal the grand total beginning balance for the

The A/R - Multifamily (No Variance) report displays the accounts receivables of a multifamily

To customize and run the A/R Multifamily (no variance) report: 

1. 
Open the menu of the desired application, Financial Close Management or Finance Agent. 

2. 
In the Reports column, select AR Multifamily (No Variance). The report customization page 

opens. 

Setting Up the Time Period

1.

2.

<!-- Page 400 -->
Finance Agent Reports 

RealPage Financial Suite AI Finance Agent User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Setting Up the Filters 

You can filter the report results by account group and by location. Both of these filters are 

required. 

1. 
Select an account group from the Account group drop-down list. 

2. 
To filter the report for a single location, select the location from the Location drop-down 

list. 

Filling In the Titles Section and Running the Report 

1. 
In the Report title 1 field, type the text that you want to appear as the main title of the 

report. 

This title displays in large type at the top of the page, directly under your company name. 

You can type over any default name that appeared automatically in this box. 

2. 
In the Report title 2 field, enter the text that you want to appear under the title of the 

report. 

The subtitle displays in smaller type, directly beneath the main title. 

3. 
Type the footer text in the Footer text box. 

Footer text displays at the bottom center of the report. 

You can use up to 80 characters, including spaces, in each title, subtitle, and footer. 

4. 
Click the View button to run the report. 

Optionally, you can also click the Export button to select the Excel report output link. The 

report is generated and a Save As dialog box opens. Enter a unique name for the report and 

click Save. Otherwise, click the Cancel button to discard any changes and return to the Cash 

& Cash Equivalents report page. 

What’s Next?  

After running the report, you can: 

• 
Customize: Click the Customize button to return to the main report page and refine the 

report further. 

You can use trial-and-error to get the precise results you want by filling in the desired fields 

and then clicking View to see the report. If after viewing the results you want to refine the 

report further, click Customize to return to the report setup page. Repeat this process until 

you’re satisfied.  

• 
Export: Click the Export button to save the report in Excel format so that you can distribute 

it or save it on your computer.

Delinquent and Prepaid Details 

This section analyzes the delinquent and prepaid amounts in RealPage Accounting and Leasing & 

Rents, and shows the total details. 

Summary by Charge Code 

This section summarizes prepaid and delinquent activity by transaction code. It prints only if you 

chose to include it on the report options page. Each column is totaled, with the exception of the 

first two columns. The totals consist of transaction code level balances and may not equal the 

beginning/ending prepaid or delinquent balances in the Resident Summary Balances report, which 

totals transactions by subjournal. 

Summary by General Ledger Account 

This section summarizes prepaid and delinquent activity by G/L account. It prints only if you chose 

to include it on the report options page. 

Click any link to navigate into the details. The default Accounts Receivable - Multifamily report 

contains the following columns: 

(Summary Section): [Property] 

Report name 
This is the name of the multifamily report, Accounts Receivable - 

Multifamily report. 

Property 
This is the property ID and name that the report covers. 

Period 
This is the period that the report covers. 

Delinquent and Prepaid Details: [Property] 

Unit 
This is the identifier of the unit described in the row. 

Name 
This is the tenant name and contact information. 

• 
If you have started eviction proceedings on the tenant, an 

asterisk (*) appears beside the name. 

• 
If this is a business or corporation, an asterisk (*) or caret (^) 

appears beside the name, depending on the placeholder that 

was entered as the first name of the business. 

• 
If the business is also under eviction, the system flags the 

account with an asterisk; therefore, you may see “**” or “^*” 

beside the name of a business that is under eviction. 

Status 
This is the occupancy status, such as current tenant or applicant.

RealPage Financial Suite AI Finance Agent User Guide

Move-in/Out 
This is the date the tenant moved in or is scheduled to move in. If this is 

a former tenant, this is the move-out date. 

Charge code 
This is the charge code description. 

If a payment is allocated to a future charge and you chose to show 

prepaids as allocated, the code has “Future:” as a prefix. 

If there are multiple transactions, a Subtotals row appears below the 

last transaction. Separate totals are calculated for prepaid, delinquent, 

net balance, and aged amounts. 

Account 
This is the account number associated with the unit. 

Total prepaid 
This is the total amount of all open payments or credits associated with 

this charge code as of the current property date. 

Total delinquent 
This is the total of all open (or unpaid) transactions associated with this 

code as of the current property date. If a dagger symbol (†) appears 

beside an amount, the charge is delinquent due to NSF activity on the 

ledger. If a double dagger symbol (‡) appears, the charge is 120+ days 

past due. 

Net balance 
This is the net ledger balance as of the current property date. A negative 

amount is a prepaid balance; a positive amount is a delinquent balance. 

If the household has multiple transactions, the net balance prints in the 

Subtotals row and the total is: 

Total Prepaid (Subtotals) + Total Delinquent (Subtotals) 

If the subtotal has both a prepaid and delinquent balance resulting in a 
net balance of zero, the manual cash application feature is enabled in 
A/R settings, so credits (the prepaid balance) are not automatically 
applied to charges (the delinquent balance).

0-30 
This is the prepaid or delinquent amount for this code during the 

current period. The current period is the current “Calendar” month or 

current “Fiscal” period, based on the Aging columns parameter. If aged 

by: 

• 
Calendar month, open transactions posted during the current 

calendar month are included in the total. 

• 
Fiscal period, open transactions posted in the current fiscal 

period are included in the total. 

The age is based on the original transaction date, not the date the 

amount became delinquent or prepaid. 

31-60 
This amount is at least 30 days prepaid or delinquent for this code. If 

aged by: 

• 
Calendar month, an open transaction posted during the 

previous month is included in this total. 

• 
Fiscal period, an open transaction posted in the previous fiscal 

period is included in this total. 

61-90 
This amount is at least 60 days prepaid or delinquent for this code. If 

aged by: 

• 
Calendar month, an open transaction posted in the calendar 

month that is two months prior to the current property date 

month is included. 

• 
Fiscal period, an open transaction posted in the fiscal period that 

is two periods prior to the current fiscal period is included. 

The age is based on the original transaction date and not the date the 

amount became delinquent or prepaid. 

Over 90 
This amount is at least 90 days prepaid or delinquent for this code. If 

aged by: 

• 
Calendar month, an open transaction posted in the calendar 

month that is at least three months prior to the current property 

date month is included. 

• 
Fiscal period, an open transaction posted in the fiscal period that 

is at least three periods prior to the current fiscal period is 

included. 

The age is based on the original transaction date and not the date the 

amount became delinquent or prepaid. 

Total due 
This is the total amount due.

Allowance for Doubtful Accounts Report Columns 

Aging per Subledger Report 

This section analyzes outstanding debts (like accounts receivable or payable) by how long they 

have been past due, categorized into time “buckets” such as 0–30 days, 31–60 days, 61–90 days, 

and over 90 days. 

Calculated Allowance 

This section calculates the allowance using either the percentage of sales method or the accounts 

receivable aging method. The percentage of sales method estimates bad debt based on a 

percentage of total credit sales, while the aging method categorizes receivables by how long 

they’ve been outstanding and applies a different uncollectible percentage to each category. 

By default, the Allowance for Doubtful Accounts report contains the following columns: 

Summary Section 

• 
Report Name: This is the name of the report, Allowance for Doubtful Accounts report. 

• 
GL Account Group: This is the account group used for this report. 

• 
Property: This is the property ID and name that the report covers. 

• 
Period: This is the period that the report covers. 

Allowance for Doubtful Accounts - Aging per Subledger Report 

• 
Property: This is the name of the property for the report. 

• 
Current: This column displays the current total of the Subledger Report for the time period. 

• 
30 days: This is the outstanding debt amount within the last 30 days.

A/R - Commercial Report Columns 

Accounts Receivable Summary Reconciliation 

This section analyzes the subledger and general ledger balances comparing the customer aging 

report in commercial to the General Ledger. The goal of this process is to ensure that both sets of 

records agree, providing an accurate picture of the company’s liabilities and identifying any 

discrepancies, errors, or potential fraud. When they do not, the report shows the amount of 

variance with an explanation. 

Accounts Receivable Detail Aging for Location 

This section lists all unpaid vendor invoices, broken down by vendor, invoice, and the number of 

days the debt is past due. This report helps businesses manage their cash flow by showing what is 

owed, to whom, and when payments are due, and can often be filtered to a specific location if the 

accounting system tracks expenses by location. 

By default, the A/R - Commercial report contains the following columns: 

Summary Section 

• 
Report Name: This is the name of the commercial report, A/R - Commercial report. 

• 
GL Account Group: This is the account group used for this report. 

• 
Property: This is the property ID and name that the report covers. 

• 
Period: This is the period that the report covers. 

Accounts Receivable Summary Reconciliation: [Property] 

•

A/R - Other Report 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Financial Close Management > All > Reports > A/R - Other`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Finance Agent > All > Financial Close Reports > A/R - Other`


The A/R - Other report displays the accounts receivables from the customer aging in Accounts 

Receivable. This report provides a detailed breakdown of outstanding balances beyond simple 

sales invoices to help manage cash flow, assess credit risk, and track financial health. The system 

uses data from the Delinquency and Prepaid report in OneSite for this report. 

Before You Begin 

Access can vary depending on your organization’s subscriptions and your permissions. If you do 

not see the option in the menu, then ask your System Administrator to check your permissions. 

Permissions 

These permissions are required to work with the A/R-Other report: 

Application 
Reports 
Permissions 

Financial Close 

Management 

A/R-Other 
Run 

If your user account doesn’t have the permissions shown above, then ask your System 

Administrator for assistance. If you have administrator privileges, you can assign permissions for a 

new feature to a user or to a role. See Roles and Permissions for a description of how to review a 

user’s permissions.

#### Customizing and Running the A/R - Other Report
*Source: `RP Financial Suite AI Finance Agent User Guide.pdf`, Page 417*

Chapter 4: Finance Agent Reports 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Financial Suite AI Finance Agent User Guide 

Customizing and Running the A/R - Other Report 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Finance Agent > All> Financial Close Reports > A/R - Other`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Financial Close Management > All > Reports > A/R - Other`


To customize and run the A/R - Other report: 

1. 
Open the menu of the desired application, Financial Close Management or Finance Agent. 

2. 
In the Reports column, select A/R - Other. 

Filling In the Time Period Section 

Define the time period for the report.  

• 
Enter the date for which you want to run the report. The report will reflect data as of the 

selected date. 

Setting Up the Filters 

You can filter the report results by account group and by location. Both of these filters are 

required. 

1. 
In the Account group drop-down list, select the account group to filter the report by. 

2. 
In the Location drop-down list, select the location to filter the report by. 

Filling In the Titles Section and Running the Report 

1. 
In the Report title 1 field, type the text that you want to appear as the main title of the 

report. 

This title displays in large type at the top of the page, directly under your company name. 

You can type over any default name that appeared automatically in this box. 

2. 
In the Report title 2 field, enter the text that you want to appear under the title of the 

report. 

The subtitle displays in smaller type, directly beneath the main title. 

3. 
Type the footer text in the Footer text box. 

Footer text displays at the bottom center of the report. 

You can use up to 80 characters, including spaces, in each title, subtitle, and footer. 

4. 
Click the View button to run the report. 

Optionally, you can also click the Export button to select the Excel report output link. The 

report is generated and a Save As dialog box opens. Enter a unique name for the report and 

click Save. Otherwise, click the Cancel button to discard any changes and return to the Cash 

& Cash Equivalents report page.

Security Deposits - Multifamily Report Columns 

Security Deposits Report (Multifamily) 

This section analyzes the delinquent and prepaid amounts in RealPage Accounting and Leasing & 

Rents, and shows when the totals agree (tie out). When they do not, the report shows the amount 

of variance with a column for you to enter the reason for the variance after the report runs. 

Security Deposits for Location 

This section summarizes prepaid and delinquent activity by transaction code. It prints only if you 

chose to include it on the report options page. Each column is totaled, with the exception of the 

first two columns. The totals consist of transaction code level balances and may not equal the 

beginning/ending prepaid or delinquent balances in the Resident Summary Balances report, which 

totals transactions by subjournal. 

Click any link to navigate into the details. The default Security Deposits - Multifamily report 

contains the following columns:

report.

Property: This is the property ID and name that the report covers. 

• 
Period: This is the period that the report covers.

### Security Deposits - Commercial Report
*Source: `RP Financial Suite AI Finance Agent User Guide.pdf`, Page 431*



#### Before You Begin
*Source: `RP Financial Suite AI Finance Agent User Guide.pdf`, Page 431*

Chapter 4: Finance Agent Reports 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Financial Suite AI Finance Agent User Guide 

Security Deposits - Commercial Report 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Financial Close Management > All > Reports > Security Deposits - 
Commercial`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Finance Agent > All > Financial Close Reports > Security Deposits - 
Commercial`


The Security Deposits - Commercial report reviews the security deposit status of a commercial 

property. Security deposits protect the property owner by covering any damage to the property 

beyond ordinary wear and tear, loss, or non-payment of rent. Security deposits earn interest. 

Some states require the landlord to pay the interest earned on the deposit to the tenant. 

Before You Begin 

Access can vary depending on your organization’s subscriptions and your permissions. If you do

page opens. 

Setting Up the Time Period 

Set up the time period for the data that you want to capture in the report. 

1. 
Enter the opening balance date.

Enter the closing balance date. 

Setting Up the Filters 

You can filter the report results by account group and by location. Both of these filters are 

required. 

1. 
Select an account group from the Account group drop-down list.

1. 
In the Report title 1 field, type the text that you want to appear as the main title of the 

report.

2.

report. 

The subtitle displays in smaller type, directly beneath the main title. 

3. 
Type the footer text in the Footer text box.

You can use up to 80 characters, including spaces, in each title, subtitle, and footer. 

4. 
Click the View button to run the report.

Security Deposits Report (Commercial)

Security Deposits for Location]

totals transactions by subjournal.

The Notes Payable report details the breakdown of a company’s formal debt obligations, which 

are based on written promissory notes with specific terms like interest rates and maturity dates. 

This report provides insight into a company’s financial structure by showing how much is owed to 

lenders, the repayment schedule, and how these debts will affect cash flow and profitability.

Prepaid Expense Report Columns 

Prepaid Expenses Report 

This section summarizes the costs a company has paid in advance for goods or services it will 

receive in the future, such as insurance or rent. 

The default Prepaid Expenses report contains the following columns: 

Summary Section 

• 
Report Name: This is the name of the report, Prepaid Expenses report. 

• 
GL Account Group: This is the account group used for this report. 

• 
Property: This is the property ID and name that the report covers. 

• 
Period: This is the period that the report covers. 

Prepaid Expenses Report: [Property] 

The report allows for multiple expenses to be listed individually, including all payment due 
details. 

• 
Vendor/Type: This is the vendor or account group type represented in this report. 

• 
Coverage Period: This is the specific length of time during which an insurance policy is 

active and provides protection. 

• 
# of Months Coverage: This is the number of months the coverage is for. 

• 
Amount Paid: This is the amount paid for the coverage. 

• 
# of Months Remaining: This is the number of months remaining until the coverage end 

date. 

• 
# Remaining Balance: This is the amount left to cover the remaining coverage. 

• 
Total: This is the total amount of the # Remaining Balance column. 

• 
Variance: This is the difference between the previous period and the reported period 

• 
Grand Total: This is the total amount of all the prepaid expenses for the reporting period. 

Fields 

Time Period Fields 

Opening balance date This field is the earliest date in the date range for the report. 

Closing balance date 
This field is the latest date in the date range for the report. 

Filters Section 

Account group 
This field is the account group associated with the report. 

Location 
This field is the property associated with the report.

Fixed Expenses Report 

This section summarizes the expenses a company can plan for and are likely already factored into

Summary Section 

• 
Report Name: This is the name of the report, Fixed Expenses report. 

• 
GL Account Group: This is the General Ledger account group used for this report. 

• 
Property: This is the property ID and name that the report covers. 

• 
Period: This is the period that the report covers. 

Fixed Expenses Report for Location: [Property] 

• 
Date: This is the date of the fixed asset in this report. 

• 
Vendor: This is the name of the vendor associated with the fixed asset in the report. 

• 
Transaction ID This is the transaction identification for the fixed asset in the report. 

• 
GL Account Description: This is the description of the general ledger account for the fixed 

asset in the report. 

• 
GL Account#: This is the number of the General Ledger account.

the GL Account Group selected in the Summary section.

Beginning Fixed Assets Total: This is the grand total of all the fixed assets for the report. 

•

• 
Total Ending Fixed Assets: This is the date the expense is incurred. 

• 
Balance per TB This is the General Ledger account code or account used to automatically 

find the balancing account for a transaction. 

• 
Variance: This is the difference of the fixed asset listed.

Property Tax Report Columns 

Property Tax Report 

This section summarizes the costs a company has paid in advance for goods or services it will 

receive in the future, such as insurance or rent. 

The default Property Tax report contains the following columns: 

Summary Section 

• 
Report Name: This is the name of the report, Property Tax report. 

• 
GL Account Group: This is the account group used for this report. 

• 
Property: This is the property ID and name that the report covers. 

• 
Period: This is the period that the report covers. 

Property Tax Report 

The report allows for multiple properties to be listed individually, including all payment due 
details. 

• 
Property: This is the property (such as land and buildings) represented in this report. 

• 
Vendor: This is the taxing authority associated with the property in the report. 

• 
Parcel ID: This is a unique numerical identifier assigned by local government authorities to a 

specific piece of real estate for the property in the report. 

• 
Tax: This is the amount of property tax expense, which is a local government levy on 

physical property (such as land and buildings) that businesses record as an operating 

expense in in the report. 

• 
Date Paid: This is the specific date when the tax liability was settled. 

---


<!-- Page 472 -->
Finance Agent Reports 

RealPage Financial Suite AI Finance Agent User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

• 
Start Period: This is the date of appraisal for the property, which is often January 1st in 

many jurisdictions. However, the actual reporting period can be tied to a company’s fiscal 

year, which might differ.  

• 
End Period: This is the date when the appraisal for the property ends, depending on the 

entity’s annual accounting period or fiscal year-end, as property taxes are generally accrued 

and expensed over the period for which they are levied. The specific date depends on 

whether the entity uses a calendar year or a fiscal year, and the relevant jurisdiction’s 

property tax calendar. 

• 
Term in Months: This is the property tax year or fiscal year that the specific tax bill covers, 

which is a 12-month period. 

• 
Current Period in Months: This is the current period’s property tax year or fiscal year that 

the specific tax bill covers, which is a 12-month period. 

• 
Monthly Amortization: This is the systematic expensing of the property cost to recognize 

one-twelfth of the annual property tax expense each month. 

• 
Total Accrued: This is the total property tax expense that has been incurred by the property 

owner up to a specific date but has not yet been paid. 

• 
GL Account: This is the specific category within the general ledger that tracks all property 

tax transactions, showing debits/credits, dates, and amounts to reflect costs and obligations. 

• 
Balance per GL [Account Code]: This is the current running total of the property tax-related 

transactions recorded in the company’s General Ledger system. 

• 
Variance (should be zero): This is the difference between the actual property tax expense 

incurred and the amount that was budgeted or forecasted for the same period. 

• 
Grand Total: This is the total amount of the property tax obligation.

#### Customizing and Running the Rent Roll Report
*Source: `RP Financial Suite AI Finance Agent User Guide.pdf`, Page 475*

Chapter 4: Finance Agent Reports 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Financial Suite AI Finance Agent User Guide 

Customizing and Running the Rent Roll Report 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Financial Close Management > All > Reports > Rent Roll`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Finance Agent > All > Financial Close Reports > Rent Roll`


To customize and run the Rent Roll report: 

1. 
Open the menu of the desired application, Financial Close Management or Finance Agent. 

2. 
In the Reports column, select Rent Roll. 

Filling In the Time Period Section 

Define the time period for the report.  

• 
Enter the date for which you want to run the report. The report will reflect data as of the 

selected date. 

Setting Up the Filters 

You can filter the report results by account group and by location. Both of these filters are 

required. 

1. 
In the Account group drop-down list, select the account group to filter the report by. 

2. 
In the Location drop-down list, select the location to filter the report by. 

Filling In the Titles Section and Running the Report 

1. 
In the Report title 1 field, type the text that you want to appear as the main title of the 

report. 

This title displays in large type at the top of the page, directly under your company name. 

You can type over any default name that appeared automatically in this box. 

2. 
In the Report title 2 field, enter the text that you want to appear under the title of the 

report. 

The subtitle displays in smaller type, directly beneath the main title. 

3. 
Type the footer text in the Footer text box. 

Footer text displays at the bottom center of the report. 

You can use up to 80 characters, including spaces, in each title, subtitle, and footer. 

4. 
Click the View button to run the report. 

Optionally, you can also click the Export button to select the Excel report output link. The 

report is generated and a Save As dialog box opens. Enter a unique name for the report and 

click Save. Otherwise, click the Cancel button to discard any changes and return to the Cash 

& Cash Equivalents report page.

What’s Next?  

After running the report, you can:

You can use trial-and-error to get the precise results you want by filling in the desired fields 

and then clicking View to see the report. If after viewing the results you want to refine the 

report further, click Customize to return to the report setup page. Repeat this process until 

you’re satisfied.  

•

it or save it on your computer. 

Rent Roll Report Columns 

Rent Roll Report 

This section summarizes all rental income for a property, listing each unit, tenant, lease terms 

(start/end dates, rent amount, security deposit), payment status (paid, balance due, past due), and 

property/unit specifics, crucial for investors, managers, and lenders to assess financial health and 

potential. It focuses solely on income, unlike expense-tracking ledgers, showing gross revenue 

and potential issues like vacancies or delinquencies. 

The default Rent Roll report contains the following columns: 

Summary Section 

• 
Report Name: This is the name of the report, Rent Roll report. 

• 
Property: This is the property ID and name that the report covers. 

• 
Period: This is the period that the report covers. 

Rent Roll Report (Multifamily: [Property]) 

• 
Resh ID: This is the system-assigned resident ID. 

• 
Lease ID: This is the system-assigned lease ID. 

• 
Bldg/Unit: This is the building (if applicable) and unit number. 

• 
Floor Plan: This is the floor plan code. 

• 
Unit Designation: This is the unit designation type on the Lease information page. 

• 
SqFt: This is the unit rentable square footage. 

• 
Unit/Lease Status: This is the unit status as of the report date. 

• 
Occupied 

• 
Vacant 

• 
Admin/Down 

• 
Name: This is the head of household name. This column is blank if you activated the Hide 

All PII Data? switch in the report parameters when you generated the report. 

---


<!-- Page 477 -->
Chapter 4: Finance Agent Reports 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Financial Suite AI Finance Agent User Guide 

• 
Move-In: This is the move-in date for current residents and the scheduled move-in date for 

applicants. This column is blank for vacant units. 

• 
Move-Out: This is the move-out date for former residents and the scheduled move-out date 

for pending move-outs. 

• 
Lease Start: This is the lease start date. 

• 
Lease End: This is the lease end date. 

• 
Market +Addl: This is market rent plus the total of non-CA type transactions scheduled for 

the floor plan or unit, and the transactions are not grouped in the effective rent transaction 

code group. 

• 
Sub Journal: This is the subjournal name (if applicable); otherwise, the system posts all 

billings to the default resident journal, and the report excludes this column. 

• 
Required Deposit: This is the required unit deposit amount. The report considers only the 

required deposits that have the DEPOSIT transaction code. 

• 
Dep on Hand: This is total paid deposits (includes pet, unit, and all other deposit receipts). 

• 
Balance: This is the resident’s current ledger balance. 

• 
Lease Rent: This is the rent amount in scheduled billing. For vacant units, this is 0.00. 

• 
RENT: The column is the amount of rent for the unit. 

• 
HAP: This is the amount of Housing Assistance Payments, primarily from HUD’s Section 8 

program, representing the government’s direct payment to landlords for a portion of a 

low-income tenant’s rent, 

• 
RENTCONC: This is the rent concession discount or incentive provided by the landlord to 

the tenant, which impacts the total rental income. 

• 
Total Billing: This is the resident’s total scheduled billing. The report excludes asterisked 

amounts from totals. 

• 
Grand Totals: This is the total amount for the Market +Addl, Required Deposit, Dep on 

Hand, Balance, Lease Rent, RENT, HAP, RENTCONC, and Total Billing columns.

### Roles and Rights
*Source: `RP Financial Suite AI Finance Agent User Guide.pdf`, Page 481*

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Financial Suite AI Finance Agent User Guide 

Roles and Rights 

This appendix describes roles and permissions, and lists the permissions in the Finance Agent 

application. 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > Setup > Users/Roles`


Permissions determine the specific features and activities that a user can access and the reports 

that the user can run. 

User-Based Permissions 

If you have not enabled roles in your company, then your company employs user-based 

permissions. With this permissions model, each user or user group has its own set of permissions. 

When you assign permissions to a particular user, your selections expand or limit what that user 

can see and do. 

Role-Based Permissions 

If your company enabled roles, then you use role-based permissions in your system. Using this 

permissions model, you can define a set of roles, and then assign the roles to users or user 

groups. For example, you can define an A/P Clerk role that includes permissions to enter and pay 

A/P invoices. 

Reviewing a User’s Permissions 

To review a user’s actual permissions: 

1. 
Open the Company menu, and then click the Setup tab. 

2. 
Select Users. 

3. 
Find the user, and then click the View permissions & roles link. The system opens the 

Permissions & roles report page. 

4. 
Review the user’s permissions. Optionally, click Print, and then use your printer’s dialog box 

to print the report. 

5. 
When you are finished viewing the user’s permissions report, click the Close button. 

A P P E N D I X A

#### Importing Standard Vendors
*Source: `RP Financial Suite AI Finance Agent User Guide.pdf`, Page 494*

Importing Standard Vendors 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > Import Data > Set Up AP Master List, Open Invoices 
and Adjustments > Standard Vendors > Template/Import`


You can import standard vendor data by uploading a CSV file with the standard vendor data in it. 

Download the Standard Vendors Import Template 

1. 
Open the Company menu. 

2. 
Select Import data. 

3. 
In the Set Up AP Master List, Open Invoices and Adjustments section, find Standard vendors, 

and then click the Template link. The system downloads the Standard Vendors.xls file to 

your browser’s default download location. 

Fill the File with Your Data 

By default, the file opens in Excel.  

1. 
Fill in the required columns for each vendor that you want to import: 

• 
VENDOR_ID: Type a unique identifier of the vendor. 

• 
ENTITY_ID: Type a unique identifier of the entity associated with the vendor. 

2. 
Add any other optional data to the additional columns in the import template. 

• 
VENDOR_NAME: Type the name of the vendor. 

• 
ENTITY_NAME: Type the name of the entity associated with the vendor.  

3. 
Save the import template file as comma delimited (CSV). 

Importing the Standard Vendor Data 

1. 
Open the Company menu. 

2. 
Select Import data. 

3. 
In the Set Up AP Master List, Open Invoices and Adjustments section, find Standard Vendors, 

and then click the Import link. 

4. 
Click the Choose file button and browse for the CSV file. 

5. 
Select the CSV file to import and click Open. 

6. 
Click Import.

approvals based on predefined business rules. 

Bank Feed 

A direct data connection that imports bank 

transactions into the Financial Suite for 

reconciliation. 

Match Confidence Score 

A system generated score indicating how likely it 

is that two transactions or records are a correct 

match. 

Variance Threshold 

A rule defining how much difference is allowed 

between two amounts before the system flags 

an exception. 

Glossary of Terms

*Source: `RP Financial Suite AI Finance Agent Getting Started Guide.pdf`, Page 5*

Getting Started with the AI Finance Agent 

Welcome to the RealPage Financial Suite AI Finance Agent—your smart assistant for managing 

financial tasks with greater speed, accuracy, and confidence. Whether you’re reviewing invoices, 

tracking expenses, reconciling bank activity, or closing the books, the Finance Agent helps you stay 

organized and ahead of schedule. 

This guide gives you a quick tour of what the Finance Agent can do and where to find its key features 

so you can start working more efficiently right away.

### What the AI Finance Agent Does For You
*Source: `RP Financial Suite AI Finance Agent Getting Started Guide.pdf`, Page 6*

Getting Started with the AI Finance Agent 

RealPage Financial Suite AI Finance Agent Getting Started Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

What the AI Finance Agent Does For You 

The AI Finance Agent brings together several powerful AI-driven tools that automate routine work 

and surface the information you need most. It reads invoices and contracts, helps reconcile bank 

activity, suggests and posts accruals, selects payments, and surfaces tasks that need attention—all 

with role-based controls and audit trails. 

Here’s a quick look at what it can help you with: 

• 
A/P Invoices: Reads uploaded, scanned, or emailed invoices and creates invoice records 

automatically. When approvals are enabled, invoices from standard vendors can be 

auto-approved based on your tolerances. 

• 
Contracts: Scans new contract attachments, identifies key clauses, and highlights the 

information your organization cares about. 

• 
Bank Reconciliation: Matches transactions, completes reconciliations, and—when 

enabled—routes them for approval. 

• 
Automated Actions: Inactivates vendors based on your criteria, identifies default expense 

accounts, and initiates escheatment steps automatically. 

• 
Standard Vendor Types: Monitors expected invoices and alerts you when they appear to be 

missing. 

• 
Bank Statements: Converts uploaded bank statements into bank feed transactions. 

• 
Automated Accruals: Creates accrual templates and posts accruals when invoices haven’t 

been received on time. 

• 
Automated Payments: Selects and processes recurring payments automatically. 

• 
Financial Close: Runs close jobs, generates work papers, and keeps your close process 

moving.

### AI Invoicing: Faster, Smarter Invoice Processing
*Source: `RP Financial Suite AI Finance Agent Getting Started Guide.pdf`, Page 10*

Getting Started with the AI Finance Agent 

RealPage Financial Suite AI Finance Agent Getting Started Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

AI Invoicing: Faster, Smarter Invoice Processing 

You can load a file containing invoice data to have the system use AI to analyze the file and turn it 

into an invoice record.  

Loading the Invoice Data 

When you load a file with invoice information, the system uses AI to analyze the file and create a 

new invoice using the data from the uploaded file. When the file has multiple pages with separate 

invoices on each page, the pages are separated and an invoice is created for each page.  

You can load the invoice file using three methods: 

• 
Scanning: Scan an invoice with a scanning device to add it to the queue. 

• 
Emailing: Send invoice files to the email address that your company defined during 

configuration. It is the address that ends with @ap.realpage.com. 

• 
Importing: Import an invoice file from your computer. 

When the auto post option is enabled and the loaded invoice contains all of the required data, 

the system automatically submits the invoices for review and approval. If approvals are not 

enabled, then the system posts the invoices. 

If the required fields are incomplete, then the system creates the invoice records and saves them 

as drafts in the Ai Invoice Queue list, where you can open the invoices and fill in any missing 

information.  

The AI Finance Agent offers two lists for working with AI-processed invoices: 

• 
AI Invoice Queue (on page 11) 

• 
AI Invoice Upload Audit (on page 13) 

Use the AI Invoice Queue list to: 

• 
Review and complete invoice details 

• 
Submit or save invoices 

• 
Archive or delete items 

• 
Upload new invoices 

For a quick way to access the AI Invoice queue list, click the Globe button. The number of 

invoices in the queue appears on the Globe button at the upper right corner of the page. 

If an invoice fails to upload, use the AI Invoice Upload Audit list to troubleshoot and retry the 

upload. Only administrators have access to the AI Invoice Upload Audit list.

Work Paper 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Finance Agent > All > Activities > Work Paper`


A work paper is any supporting document used to justify, explain, or validate a balance during the 

close process. A work paper package is a collection of these individual work papers. 

The Work papers page allows you to download work paper packages and submit final work paper 

packages for approval. Reviewers and approvers use this page to download and approve work 

paper packages.  

Tabs are the individual worksheets inside an Excel work paper file that the system generates. Each 

work paper is typically an Excel workbook, and the tabs are the separate sheets within that 

workbook. 

You can use this page to upload additional tabs to final work paper packages or upload 

replacement work paper packages for the ones generated by the system. For example, if you add 

several tabs throughout a work paper package to mark sections, upload the entire package rather 

than several tabs. 

a) Filters: Use either the Filter by drop-down list or a column filter to refine the list of work 

papers to the ones you want to work with. 

b) Status: When the status is Pending Review or Completed, click the link to view the work 

paper approval history. 

c) Lock/Unlock: If an Unlock link appears in this column, the work papers can be edited. Final 

work papers in Completed status are locked and cannot be edited. 

d) Common Tasks: Several links can appear to the right of the Lock/Unlock column: 

• 
Download: Saves the final work papers in Excel format. 

• 
Generate: Creates the final work papers for download. 

• 
Re-generate: Generate any of the final work papers again for download in Excel 

format. 

• 
Upload: Add attachments to a work paper. 

• 
History: View the revision history of a work paper. 

• 
Re-set: Regenerate the final work papers.

### Missing Expenses
*Source: `RP Financial Suite AI Finance Agent Getting Started Guide.pdf`, Page 22*

Getting Started with the AI Finance Agent 

RealPage Financial Suite AI Finance Agent Getting Started Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Missing Expenses 

Missing expenses are unrecorded costs due to timing delays, typically because the invoice hasn’t 

arrived. Without accruals, missing expenses would cause understated liabilities and overstated 

profits. Accruals correct this by recognizing the expense in the correct period—even if the cash 

hasn’t left the account yet.  

Prerequisites 

• 
The missing expenses feature uses standard vendors set on an entity. See Set your standard 

vendors for instructions. 

• 
To receive accrual emails, you must be assigned to the Finance Agent - Automated Accrual 

Notifications role. 

How It Works 

• 
The AI agent continuously searches for missing expenses and when found, adds them to the 

Missing Expenses list.  

• 
You select the missing expenses in the list that you want the AI agent to accrue, set the 

posting date and email address, and click Post Accruals. 

• 
The AI agent runs an offline process to calculate the accruals and post them. The system 

then sends an email to notify you when the posting is complete. 

• 
The accrual entries reverse automatically on the first of the next month, and the system 

sends an email when the reversal is completed.

Agent Accruals helps simplify the accrual process by using AI to identify missing expenses and 

create accruals. The AI agent accrues missing expenses for standard vendors, those that you 

receive bills from regularly such as utilities or telecom providers.  

Before you can use this feature, you must define your standard vendors and then associate the 

vendors with the appropriate entities. Additional configuration is required to define how and 

when accruals are calculated. When you complete the configuration, the AI agent creates an 

accrual template that it uses to accrue missing expenses from the standard vendors. After the AI 

agent processes accruals of missing expenses from standard vendors, you can review and edit 

them in the Agent Accruals list. 

a) Edit: Change an accrual. 

b) View: Review an accrual’s details. 

c) Delete: Delete an accrual template. 

d) Done: Close the list and return to the Finance Agent Home page. 

e) Export: Save the list of accruals as a CSV or Excel file.

Accrual Workbench

The Accrual workbench contains accrual information based on accrual templates. 

Use the Accrual workbench to filter and search for calculated accruals. You can view the 

suggested accruals, select what you want to accrue, and then post the accruals. After an accrual is 

posted, the system creates a reversing entry. The reversal date defaults to the first day of the next 

month. You can change the reversal date in the Reversal Date field.  

Using the Accrual Workbench with the AI Finance Agent 

If your company subscribes to the AI Finance Agent, the workbench contains accrual information 

based on accrual templates that the AI Finance Agent creates in addition to any accrual templates 

that you created manually. Note that only the Accrual workbench in the Finance Agent application 

includes both regular and AI agent-processed accruals. 

Use the Accrual workbench to find accruals that the AI agent has calculated.  

• 
Use the filters for Property, Accrual for (month), or an Accrual ID and then click Apply to find 

the calculated accruals.  

• 
Click the Amount in the list to view the missing expenses for the vendor.  

• 
After you validate the accrual, you can post it here by selecting the accrual, and then clicking 

the Post button. The system posts an accrual entry based on the accrual template and then 

reverses it on the first day of the next month. 

• 
Use the Accrual Activity report to check which missing expenses that the AI agent calculated 

or posted, and the date it occurred. 

You can receive an email from the system when accruals are calculated or posted when you are 
assigned to the Finance Agent - Automated Accrual Notifications role.

The Accrual workbench is divided into two sections: Filters and the list.

want to work with.

Calculate, Post, Unpost, and Delete buttons act on the selected expenses in the list. The 

Refresh button updates the list with any new expenses that match your filters. 

c) List of expenses to accrue: After you click the Apply button, the list of expenses that fall 

within your filter settings appear in the bottom section. Use this section to select the 

expenses that you want to act on (Calculate, Post, Unpost, or Delete).  

d) Save View As: When you have the filters set to retrieve accruals that you want to use again 

later, save the settings in a view.  

e) Export: Exports the list of expenses that appear in the list in the selected file format.  

f) 
Done: Closes the workbench and returns to the application’s home page.

Click the number in the Journal Entry column to open the journal entries associated 

with the accrual.
