### Cash Management Tools
*Source: `RP Financial Suite AI Finance Agent Getting Started Guide.pdf`, Page 32*

Getting Started with the AI Finance Agent 

RealPage Financial Suite AI Finance Agent Getting Started Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Cash Management Tools 

Use Finance Agent to automate and streamline the bank reconciliation process.  

To get started, upload your bank statements into the system. From there, the AI Finance Agent 

automatically takes care of the following: 

• 
Sets the statement ending date and ending balance. 

• 
Creates corresponding bank transactions. 

• 
Generates journal entries for additional statement activity, such as bank fees and interest. 

• 
Automatically matches bank transactions to General Ledger (G/L) transactions. 

After the process is initiated, the system automatically begins reconciliation. If reconciliation 

completes successfully and the remaining amount to reconcile is zero, you can choose to have the 

reconciliation submitted automatically. 

The Finance Agent offers these tools to help with the bank reconciliation process: 

• 
Upload Bank Statement 

• 
Bank Reconciliation 

• 
Pending Reconciliations 

• 
Reconciling Items 

• 
Approve Reconciliation 

• 
Reconciliation History 

Together, these tools streamline your cash management workflow from upload to approval.

Filters 

By default, the Reconcile bank account page displays all transactions for the bank account—both 

matched and unmatched—regardless of the transaction type.  

You can filter the list by state (matched or unmatched), transaction type, bank amount, check or 

document number, and more. See Filtering and Sorting Transactions for more information. 

RealPage vs. Bank Transactions 

The Reconcile bank account page contains two lists of transactions: 

•

Financial Suite directly. 

•

file. It appears only when you have imported transactions. 

Click the Match link to open the Find match page so you can match imported transactions with 

transactions in the system. 

Click the Action link to perform one of the following actions: 

• 
Create JE: Create a journal entry when a matching transaction does not exist. 

• 
Exclude: Exclude the transaction from the reconciliation. 

• 
Reconciling: Mark a transaction as a reconciling item. 

After you reconcile a bank, you can view reconciling items in the Reconciling items list (on page 

38). 

More Actions

during reconciliation:

Adding a manual payment

Adding a receipt

Making a deposit 

• 
Transferring funds

Paying A/P invoices

Applying payments

Adding bank transactions

need your review. Click the View button to open the Accruals workbench.

to be confirmed. Click the View button to open the Print Checks page.

AI Agent Chat Box 

Located in the right-side panel, the AI Finance Agent chat box provides a conversational interface 

where you can ask finance questions, receive guided assistance, and launch suggested actions. It 

is designed to improve efficiency by surfacing relevant answers and shortcuts in context. 

Key Features 

• 
Conversational assistance for finance-related questions 

• 
Suggested prompts to help you get started quickly 

• 
Contextual support without navigating away from the current page 

• 
Quick access panel for interacting with the agent alongside normal workflow 

Example Use Cases 

You can interact with the chat box to ask questions such as: 

• 
What are my Expenses vs. Budget? 

• 
What invoices are past due? 

These prompts help you retrieve insights faster and reduce the need to manually search through 

finance screens and reports. 

About the Chat Box 

The panel includes: 

• 
A header identifying the active agent 

• 
A welcome message personalized to the user 

• 
Suggested starter questions 

• 
A text input box for free-form questions 

• 
Action controls for sending messages and interacting with the assistant 

Using the Finance Agent Chat Box 

1. 
Click the Lumina Finance Agent button to open the chat panel. 

2. 
Select a suggested prompt or type your own question in the message field. 

3. 
Review the response provided by the agent. 

4. 
Continue the conversation for follow-up questions or related finance tasks.

The system automatically accrues an expense.

> **Navigation Path:** `Company > Setup > Users > Edit > Role Information`

Finance Agent - Automated Payment Notification

• 
AI invoice scanning 

• 
AI contract screening 

• 
Bank reconciliation 

• 
Enable any desired automated actions: 

• 
Inactivate one-time vendors after they’ve been paid. 

• 
Inactivate dormant vendors. 

•

• 
Begin escheatment process when checks have not been cleared or invoices not 

paid.

Notify when there are missing expenses for two months.

## Vendor Aging and Trial Balance Don’t Match
*Source: `Vendor Aging and Trial Balance Quick Help.pdf`, Page 2*



## Step 1: Confirm Your Accounts Payable Configuration for Reversal Transactions
*Source: `Vendor Aging and Trial Balance Quick Help.pdf`, Page 2*



## Step 2: Look for Manual Journal Entries to the A/P Account
*Source: `Vendor Aging and Trial Balance Quick Help.pdf`, Page 2*



## Step 3: Check Payment Dates vs. Invoice Posting Dates
*Source: `Vendor Aging and Trial Balance Quick Help.pdf`, Page 2*

Vendor Aging and Trial Balance Quick Help 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Vendor Aging and Trial Balance Don’t Match 

If your Vendor Aging report balance does not match your Trial Balance, use the checks below to 

identify the cause and understand how to correct it. 

Step 1: Confirm Your Accounts Payable Configuration for Reversal Transactions 

Check that reversals are displayed correctly  


> **Navigation Path:** `1. 
Go to Accounts Payable > Setup > Configuration.`


2. 
Confirm that Display reversals as historical transactions is enabled. 

If this option is not enabled, reversed transactions may appear differently between reports, 

which can cause the Vendor Aging and Trial Balance to be out of sync. 

Step 2: Look for Manual Journal Entries to the A/P Account 

Review the General Ledger for manual journal entries posted directly to the A/P GL account. 

Manual journal entries do not appear on the Vendor Aging report. If they exist in the A/P G/L 

account, the Trial Balance will include them, but the Vendor Aging will not. 

As a best practice, you should avoid posting manual journal entries directly to the AP G/L account. 

How to Prevent This Going Forward 


> **Navigation Path:** `• 
Navigate to General Ledger > Accounts and then edit the A/P G/L account.`


• 
Enable Disallow Direct Posting. 

Step 3: Check Payment Dates vs. Invoice Posting Dates 

Payments made before the invoice posting date may not appear on the Vendor Aging report. This 

typically happens if you run the report for a date range between the payment date and the 

invoice posting date. 

How to Prevent This Going Forward 


> **Navigation Path:** `• 
Navigate to Accounts Payable > Setup > Configuration.`


• 
Enable the Payment dates must be greater than their G/L posting date setting. 

What to Expect 

• 
The Vendor Aging and Trial Balance reports will be out of balance until the invoice posting 

date occurs. 

• 
After the invoice posting date has passed, the balances should align. 

Optional Immediate Fix 

If you need the reports to balance before the posting date: 

• 
Void the payment. 

• 
Reissue it with a payment date after the invoice posting date. 

---



## Step 4: Check for Reversals Posting in the Wrong Period
*Source: `Vendor Aging and Trial Balance Quick Help.pdf`, Page 3*



## Step 5: Review Imported A/P Balances and Imported Historical Invoices
*Source: `Vendor Aging and Trial Balance Quick Help.pdf`, Page 3*



## Additional Items to Check
*Source: `Vendor Aging and Trial Balance Quick Help.pdf`, Page 3*

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
Vendor Aging and Trial Balance Quick Help 

Step 4: Check for Reversals Posting in the Wrong Period 

Review invoices and determine if any invoice posting dates and the reversal dates fall in different 

accounting periods. 

How to Resolve It 

• 
Post a journal entry to remove the reversal from the incorrect period. 

• 
Post a second journal entry to record the reversal in the correct period. 

Step 5: Review Imported A/P Balances and Imported Historical Invoices 

Check whether your beginning A/P balances were imported correctly. 

• 
Review the original balance import for the A/P G/L account. 

• 
Confirm the imported balance matches what you expect based on your historical A/P 

invoices. 

• 
Review historical imported invoices. 

How to Resolve It 

If the balances are incorrect:  

• 
Post an adjusting CONV journal entry for the amount that was missing from the original 

balance import. 

If invoices are missing: 

• 
Use the A/P Invoice Import template to import the missing invoices. 

• 
Be sure to import them as historical invoices. 

Historical invoices will appear on the Vendor Aging report but not on the Trial Balance 

report. 

Additional Items to Check 

If you use an alternate A/P G/L account: 

• 
Verify that invoices are coded to the correct A/P account. 

• 
If not, edit the invoice and update the A/P account accordingly. 

To pinpoint when the issue started: 

• 
Run the Vendor Aging report for prior dates. 

• 
Identify the last date when the Vendor Aging and Trial Balance reports matched and follow 

the steps above to determine the issue. 

---



## Summary
*Source: `Vendor Aging and Trial Balance Quick Help.pdf`, Page 4*

Vendor Aging and Trial Balance Quick Help 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Summary 

Most Vendor Aging and Trial Balance mismatches are caused by: 

• 
Configuration settings 

• 
Manual journal entries to the A/P account 

• 
Payment and invoice timing differences 

• 
Incorrect reversal periods 

• 
Incomplete or inaccurate imported balances 

Following the steps in this document will help you identify the cause of the mismatch and 

determine the appropriate resolution.

## Why can’t I approve an invoice?
*Source: `Approval Workbench Quick Help.pdf`, Page 5*

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
Approval Workbench Quick Help 

Why can’t I approve an invoice? 

Certain configuration rules must be met before an invoice can be approved. 

Common reasons approval may be blocked include: 

• 
One or more invoice lines are coded to the default G/L account while the Do Not Allow 

Posting to Default G/L setting is enabled. The invoice must be re-coded to a valid G/L 

account before approval. 

• 
The vendor requires a Purchase Order, and the invoice has not been matched to a PO. 

You can identify invoices that require a PO directly from the Approval workbench: 

• 
An information icon appears in the Actions column. 

• 
Hovering over the icon indicates that a PO is required. 

---



## What does “Dispute” mean on an eInvoice?
*Source: `Approval Workbench Quick Help.pdf`, Page 6*

Approval Workbench Quick Help 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

What does “Dispute” mean on an eInvoice? 

The Dispute option is available only for electronic invoices (eInvoices). Disputing an invoice allows 

you to notify the vendor of an issue, such as incorrect pricing, missing items, or the need for a 

credit.  

If you need to dispute the invoice with the vendor follow these steps: 

1. 
Select the Dispute option, enter a detailed comment and reason for the dispute. Please 

keep in mind these comments are sent to the vendor directly. 

2. 
After the vendor reviews the dispute, their response will be sent to the user who submitted 

the dispute. 

---



## How do I resolve a disputed eInvoice?
*Source: `Approval Workbench Quick Help.pdf`, Page 7*

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
Approval Workbench Quick Help 

How do I resolve a disputed eInvoice? 

Only invoices that have been disputed show the Resolve option in the Approval workbench. 

To resolve a dispute: 

1. 
Select Resolve. 

2. 
Type a note explaining why the issue has been resolved. 

3. 
If you would like to clear the dispute but not approve this invoice, select the Clear Dispute 

option. This removes the dispute, and the invoice will be available on your Approval 

workbench.  

4. 
If you would like to clear the dispute and approve it at the same time, select the Approve 

check box and then click the Clear Dispute button.

## Approval History
*Source: `Approval History Quick Help.pdf`, Page 2*



## FAQs
*Source: `Approval History Quick Help.pdf`, Page 2*

Approval History Quick Help 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Approval History 

FAQs 

1. How is the default approver set up? 

The default approver is configured in different areas of the system depending on the type of 

transaction. For most transaction types, such as Journal Entries, A/P Invoices, Purchase 

Orders, Subcontracts, Job Cost transactions, and A/P Payments, the default approver is set 

up under Company > Approval Configurations. 

For eInvoice transactions, the default approver is configured under Spend Management > 

Configurations.  


> **Navigation Path:** `For oInvoice transactions, it is set under Accounts Payable > Configurations > Full Service.`


If you need to change the default approver, you must update it in the appropriate 

configuration area shown above. After the default approver is updated, the workflow 

automatically reflects the change. The default approver cannot be changed directly from 

within the workflow itself. 

2. Why did this transaction go to the default approver? 

A transaction is sent to the default approver when the workflow cannot find a valid approver 

for one of its approval steps. This most commonly happens when a workflow policy 

references a user who has been made inactive or a role that does not currently have an 

active user assigned for the transaction’s location. 

You can identify which approval level caused the issue by reviewing the approval history of 

the transaction. For example, if there are three approval levels and the default approver 

appears at level two, then the issue is with the second approval policy. 

To resolve this, update the policy by assigning an active user or by ensuring the required 

role is assigned to an active user at the correct location. 

---


<!-- Page 3 -->
© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
Approval History Quick Help 

3. Why did the transaction auto approve? 

Auto-approval occurs when the same user or role is assigned to multiple approval levels in a 

workflow. After that user approves the transaction at the first required level, the system 

automatically approves the remaining levels assigned to the same user or role. This prevents 

users from having to approve the same transaction multiple times. 

For example, if a user has both the Workflow – Regional Manager and Workflow – Property 

Manager roles, the system requires only one manual approval and will auto-approve the 

remaining levels. 

If you require the same user to approve a transaction multiple times, you can disable 

auto-approval by navigating to Company > Approval Configurations and selecting the 

Disable Auto Approve option.   

4. Why does this approval say it was skipped? 

An approval is marked as Skipped when it has been pending longer than the number of 

days defined in Company > Approval Configurations. If a user does not take action within 

the configured time frame, the system skips that approval step and moves the transaction to 

the next approver. 

The skipped status indicates that no action was taken by the original approver and helps 

explain why the transaction advanced without their approval. 

---


<!-- Page 4 -->
Approval History Quick Help 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

5. Why does it say Submitted and Pending Approval? 

In the Approval History page, Submitted indicates the approval level where the transaction is 

currently waiting for action. Pending Approval shows the future approver who needs to 

approve the transaction after it advances to their level. 

As each approval is completed, the Submitted status moves down the approval history until 

the transaction is fully approved. 

For example, if the transaction is currently in a user’s approval workbench, it shows as 

Submitted to that user. After they approve it, the transaction advances and is submitted to 

the next approver in the workflow.

### Approval Processes Overview
*Source: `RP Accounting Approval Policy Manager User Guide.pdf`, Page 10*

RealPage Accounting Approval Processes 

RealPage Accounting Approval Policy Manager User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Approval Processes Overview 

Organizations that use approval processes benefit in several ways. The use of approval processes 

saves time and maximizes your team’s efficiency. In addition, approving the work of others 

promotes transparency and improves your team’s compliance with your organization’s standards. 

RealPage Accounting offers approval processes for: 

• 
Journal entries 

• 
A/P invoices 

• 
Purchase orders * 

• 
Purchase order change orders * 

• 
Service contracts * 

• 
Subcontracts * 

• 
Job cost transactions * 

• 
Job cost change orders * 

• 
A/P payments 

• 
Vendor records 

• 
Financial close work papers *  

The approval process for financial close work papers is not covered in this document. Refer to 
Work Paper Approval Process in the Financial Close Management
 help section. 

These approval processes are flexible and allow your company to configure approvals of varying 

complexity, from general policies such as approving all new vendor records to specific policies 

such as applying custom conditions to transactions.  

Configuration 

When defining an approval process, ask yourself: 

• 
Who should be the approvers? 

• 
How many approval levels are required? 

• 
Do you want the system to notify approvers when they have items waiting for their 

approval? 

From there, it’s a two-step process: 

1. 
Subscribe to the applications (on page 11) required for your approval policies. 

If you’re an existing RealPage Accounting client and you want to use approval processes for 
the starred (*) items, additional subscriptions are required. 

2. 
Enable approval types and configure their settings (on page 12). 

---



#### Subscribing to Approval Workflow Applications
*Source: `RP Accounting Approval Policy Manager User Guide.pdf`, Page 11*

Subscribing to Approval Workflow Applications 

The first step in configuring approval workflows is to make sure that you are subscribed to the 

needed applications. 

Vendor Approvals 

Vendor records are associated with the Accounts Payable application. You must be subscribed to 

the Accounts Payable application to use the approval process for vendors. 

To subscribe to the Accounts Payable application: 

1. 
From the Applications menu, select Company, and then select the Setup tab. 

2. 
Select Subscriptions. 

The Subscriptions page opens. 

3. 
On the Applications tab, click the switch next to Accounts Payable to subscribe to the 

application. 

4. 
Click the Configure link. 

5. 
To enable vendor record approvals, find the Vendor approval settings section, and then 

select the Enable vendor approval check box. 

6. 
Click the Save button. 

Job Cost Transactions, Job Cost Change Orders, Service Contracts, and Subcontract 
Approvals 

Job cost transactions, job cost change orders, service contracts, and subcontracts are associated 

with the Job Cost & Reserves application. You must be subscribed to the Job Cost & Reserves 

application to use the job cost change order approval process. 

To subscribe to the Job Cost & Reserves application: 

1. 
From the Applications menu, select Company, and then select the Setup tab. 

2. 
Select Subscriptions. 

The Subscriptions page opens. 

3. 
On the Applications tab, click on the switch next to Job Cost & Reserves to subscribe to the 

application. 

---

Approvers’ Processes 

This section describes how to participate in an approval workflow as an approver. If you are an 

approver, follow these quick steps to get started approving: 

Approving Transactions 

To approve transactions: 

1. 
Open the Company menu. 

2. 
Select the Approval workbench link.  

The Approval workbench - My approvals page opens. 

3. 
Select the transaction type you want to approve. 

The approval queue at the bottom of the page displays any pending transactions of this 

type that are assigned to you. 

4. 
Approve or decline transactions as needed. 

Approving Vendors 

To approve vendors: 

1. 
Open the Accounts payable menu. 

2. 
Select the Approve vendors link. The Approve vendors list opens. 

3. 
Approve or decline vendors as needed.

#### Setting Up Delegates for Approvals
*Source: `RP Accounting Approval Policy Manager User Guide.pdf`, Page 14*

RealPage Accounting Approval Processes 

RealPage Accounting Approval Policy Manager User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Setting Up Delegates for Approvals 

<your username> > My Preferences > Approval Delegates 

Things happen and you can’t be available every hour of every day in the year. When you are 

responsible for approvals, but you have to be away, you can delegate approvals to another 

person who is in the system. This user becomes your delegate.  

The Approval delegates section only appears if the configuration for Spend Management is 

enabled for approval delegations and if you have permissions to approve purchasing transactions. 

To delegate your approval role: 

1. 
Click on your login name in the upper-right corner of the window and select the My 

preferences option from the drop-down list.  

The Preferences for <username> page opens. 

2. 
In the Approval delegates section, select the Enable approval policy delegates check box.  

Additional controls appear. 

3. 
In the Delegate drop-down list, select the user who will be responsible for approvals while 

you are out. 

Your delegate is assigned in your organization’s configuration. Contact your system 
administrator for assistance. 

4. 
In the From date field, select or type the date that you want to enable your delegate.  

5. 
In the To date field, select or type the day that you plan to return. 

6. 
Click the Save button. 

The system will start rerouting new approval requests to your assigned delegate on the date 

you supplied in the From date field and will stop rerouting these approval requests on the 

date you supplied in the To date field. 

If you return early, you can log in to the system and change the To date to your actual 

return date. However, any approvals that have already been delegated while you are out of 

the office will remain with your delegate even if you disable delegation before the delegate 

has approved or declined the transaction. 

---

Requesters’ Processes 

Follow these quick steps to check on the status of your approval requests. 

To check the status of a request for an A/P invoice, journal entry, purchase order, service contract, 

subcontract, job cost change order, or A/P payment: 

1. 
Open the Company menu. 

2. 
Select the Approval workbench link. The Approval workbench - My approvals page opens. 

3. 
Click the View all button in the upper-right corner of the page to view a list of all 

transactions in the approval queue. 

4. 
Select the transaction type associated with the approval request to filter the approval queue. 

5. 
Click on the link in the Status column to open the Approval history for a transaction. 

To check the status of a request for a new or changed vendor record: 

1. 
Open the Accounts payable menu. 

2. 
Select the View vendor requests link. The View vendor requests page opens.  

The State column displays the approval status of each vendor record.

### Approval Process Email Notifications

#### Setting Up Email Notification Preferences
*Source: `RP Accounting Approval Policy Manager User Guide.pdf`, Page 16*

RealPage Accounting Approval Processes 

RealPage Accounting Approval Policy Manager User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Approval Process Email Notifications 

This section describes how to configure your personal preferences for approval email notifications 

and system-wide approval email notifications. 

Setting Up Email Notification Preferences 

(User Name) > My Preferences  


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > Configuration > My Preferences`


You can adjust your notification preferences to choose which events you want the system to 

notify you about. 

To set your email notification preferences: 

1. 
On the Preferences page, find the Email notifications section. 

2. 
When you use the Process & store option to store reports, the Stored reports are 

generated and available check box determines whether the system sends you an email 

message with the report as an attachment. If you want to receive stored reports by email, 

then select the Stored reports are generated and available check box. 

3. 
If you want to receive an email when something goes wrong with a regularly scheduled 

transaction, select the Recurring transactions fail check box. This includes all recurring 

transactions. 

To receive this notification, you must have full or limited Admin privileges. 

Intercompany Ticketing 

Use this section to choose your email notification preference for intercompany service tickets. 

When a service ticket is created, the system sends an email to: 

• 
The user who submitted the ticket (to notify them that it was successfully submitted) 

• 
The user or users who are assigned as the reviewer (to notify them that a ticket requires 

their approval) 

• 
The user or users who are assigned to the ticket (to notify them that they are assigned to 

resolve and close the ticket) 

You can select your personal notification preference for these emails: 

• 
None: Do not receive any notifications for service tickets. 

• 
Individual: Receive a separate email each time a service ticket is created. 

• 
Consolidated: Consolidate notifications into a single email for all service tickets created that 

day.

notifications in the Start date/time field, and then specify the time in the adjacent fields.

### Transaction Approval Overview
*Source: `RP Accounting Approval Policy Manager User Guide.pdf`, Page 22*

Transaction Approvals 

RealPage Accounting Approval Policy Manager User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Transaction Approval Overview 

Transaction approvals include A/P invoices, journal entries, purchase orders, purchase order 

change orders, service contracts, subcontracts, job cost transactions, job cost change orders, and 

A/P payments. 

Definitions 

Approval policy: An approval policy is composed of: 

• 
A user or role who you select to approve transactions. 

• 
A definition of the type of transaction that the user can approve. 

After defining an approval policy, assign the approval policy to a workflow.  

Approval workflow: A policy workflow is a collection of policies that apply to a property or group 

of properties.  

Approval workbench: Approvers use the workbench to review pending transactions, and then 

approve or decline them. 

---



### Transaction Approval Configuration
*Source: `RP Accounting Approval Policy Manager User Guide.pdf`, Page 23*

Chapter 2: Transaction Approvals 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Approval Policy Manager User Guide 

Transaction Approval Configuration 

Use these steps to configure approvals for your transactions: 

1. 
Subscribe to any required applications (on page 11). 

2. 
Design the transaction approval process (on page 24). 

3. 
Configure the desired transaction approvals (on page 27). 

4. 
Set up transaction approval permissions (on page 85). 

5. 
Add approval policies (on page 52). 

6. 
Add an approval workflow, add approval policies, and assign properties to the workflow (on 

page 70).

### Transaction Approval Checklist
*Source: `RP Accounting Approval Policy Manager User Guide.pdf`, Page 24*

Transaction Approvals 

RealPage Accounting Approval Policy Manager User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Transaction Approval Checklist 

To use the transaction approval process, your company designs the approval workflow in two 

steps: 

Step 1: Think about the approval policies you need 

Approval policies contain the policy type, approvers, and number of approval levels. Policy types 

determine the reasons that cause transactions to be routed for approval.  

As you configure the approval process, answer the following questions. Use your answers to these 

questions to configure the approval policies that your company needs: 

Users 

• 
Do you want all transactions to go through the approval process? You can assign one 

approver or role to an approval policy and then create conditions in the workflow to sort 

out the transactions that need approval.  

Amounts or Tiered Amounts 

• 
Do you want to flag transactions over a certain amount for approval?  

• 
Can you identify ranges of costs and associate the ranges with specific people or roles who 

can approve transactions in each range? 

Vendors or Vendor Types 

• 
Do you want a certain type of vendor to go through approvals? If so, make sure to create 

vendor types for each kind of vendor that you want to go through the approval process. 

• 
Do you want specific vendors to go through the approval process?  

• 
Who, or what role, would be an appropriate approver of new vendor reds? Changed vendor 

records? 

G/L Accounts 

• 
Do you want to send transactions through the approval process associated with specific 

types of costs, such as Travel and entertainment? 

Jobs, Job Types, or Cost Codes 

• 
Do you want to flag job cost change orders associated with a specific job, job type, or cost 

code for approval?  

Journal Types 

• 
Do you want to send all journal entries associated with a specific journal type through the 

approval process? 

---


<!-- Page 25 -->
Chapter 2: Transaction Approvals 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Approval Policy Manager User Guide 

Payment Methods or Bank Accounts 

• 
Do you want to send all A/P payments associated with a specific payment method or bank 

account through the approval process? 

Step 2: Think about how to group policies and which properties need them 

Workflows contain a collection of approval policies. By associating one or more properties with a 

workflow, the properties are subject to all of the approval policies in the workflow.  

In a workflow, approval policies can be further defined and combined with conditions and 

expressions.

Use the Approval configuration page to configure transaction approval workflow settings for 

journal entries, A/P invoices, purchase orders, service contracts, subcontracts, job cost 

transactions and change orders, and A/P payments. 

This page is divided into the following sections based on the type of transaction: 

• 
Journal entry approvals: This section contains settings for the journal entry approval 

workflow. 

• 
A/P invoice approvals: This section allows you to configure the approval process for A/P 

invoices. 

• 
Purchase orders: This section contains settings for the purchase order approval workflow. 

• 
Service contract: This section contains settings for service contract approvals and 

notifications. 

• 
Subcontract: This section contains settings for subcontract approvals and notifications. 

• 
Job cost: This section contains settings for the job cost transaction approval workflow and 

job cost change order approval workflow. 

• 
Budget check: This section allows you to choose the kind of budget check to use with the 

Spend Management application. 

• 
A/P payments: This section contains settings for A/P payment approvals and notifications. 

Before You Begin

not see the option in the menu, then ask your System Administrator to check your permissions.

#### Configuring Transaction Approvals
*Source: `RP Accounting Approval Policy Manager User Guide.pdf`, Page 27*

Configuring Transaction Approvals 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > Approvals > Approval Configuration`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Spend Management > Setup > Approvals > Approval Configuration`


To configure transaction approvals, fill in the section corresponding with the transaction type. 

Filling In the Journal Entry Approvals Section 

1. 
Select the Enable journal entry approval check box to enable the approval workflow for 

journal entries. Clear the check box to disable journal entry approvals. 

2. 
Select the Ability to delete declined approvals check box if you want the system to delete 

declined transactions. This option is useful when your normal system configuration prohibits 

deleting transactions and you want to override the configuration to allow for deleting 

declined transactions. Clear the check box to retain declined journal entries. 

3. 
Select the Allow deletion of approved journal entries check box to enable deletion of 

journal entries after approval. 

4. 
Select the Email notifications check box to have the system notify approvers when a new 

journal entry requires their attention. Clear the check box to prevent the system from 

sending emails when journal entries are waiting for approval. 

5. 
Select the Advance G/L posting dates when period is closed check box if you want the 

system to automatically change the posting date to the next open date if an entry was 

submitted for approval in a period that is already closed. 

6. 
Select the Allow workflow assignment at journal entry check box to enable workflow type 

and workflow selection when creating a journal entry. 

7. 
In the Unrestricted section, click the Select button, and then choose one or more users to be 

the Unrestricted user. The users you choose can see all journal entries queued for approval. 

Unrestricted users can also act on the transactions even if the approvals are not assigned to 

them. For instructions on using the selection box, see Using the Multi-Select Box. 

8. 
In the Enable journal entry approval against each selected invoice creation type section: 

• 
Select the From CSV import check box to have the system evaluate journal entries that 

were imported from CSV files for approval. Clear the check box to allow imported 

journal entries to post without going through the approval process. 

• 
Select the From recurring journal entry check box to have the system evaluate journal 

entries that are created by recurring transactions for approval. Clear the check box to 

allow recurring journal entries to post without going through the approval process. 

9. 
Select a default approver from the Approver assigned if a user is inactive or a user is not 

present in a role drop-down list. The default approver receives transactions for approval if 

---

there is an inactive user in the role or if there is no user in the role. For more information,

Filling In the A/P Invoice Approvals Section 

Fill in this section to have the system send A/P invoices through the approval process. Otherwise, 

skip to the Purchase Orders section. 

1. 
Select the Enable A/P invoice approval check box to enable the approval workflow for A/P 

invoices. Clear the check box to disable A/P invoice approvals. 

2. 
Select the Ability to delete declined approvals check box if you want the system to delete 

declined transactions. This option is useful when your normal system configuration prohibits 

deleting transactions and you want to override the configuration to allow for deleting 

declined transactions. Clear the check box to retain declined A/P invoices. 

3. 
Select the Email notifications check box to have the system notify approvers when a new 

A/P invoice requires their attention. Clear the check box to prevent the system from sending 

emails when A/P invoices are waiting for their approval. 

4. 
Select the Advance G/L posting dates when period is closed check box if you want the 

system to automatically change the posting date to the next open date if an invoice was 

submitted for approval on a period that is already closed. 

5. 
Select the Allow workflow assignment at A/P entry check box to enable workflow type and 

workflow selection when creating an A/P invoice. 

6. 
Select the Enable preventing or warning a user when adding an A/P invoice that exceeds 

the budget check box if you want to prevent or warn a user from adding an A/P invoice that 

exceeds the available budget. In the Prevent or warn field, select the desired setting: 

• 
Prevent: Select this option to restrict the user from creating an A/P invoice that 

exceeds the budget. 

• 
Warn: Select this option to display a warning message when the user creates an A/P 

invoice that exceeds the budget. The user can choose to proceed anyway. 

This setting also applies to Spend Management Site Experience. 

You can assign permissions to specific users to allow them to bypass these restrictions 
(on page 36 ). When a user has these permissions, they can enter an A/P invoice without 
restriction. 

7. 
Select the Advance to next approver after XX days if the approver has not approved it 

check box if you want to keep the workflow moving when an approver is not available to 

review invoices. Type the number of days to wait before advancing the invoice to the next

review every invoice.

For the payment notification contact, you can choose between: 

• 
Person who selects invoices for payment: Select this option to use the contact 

information of the person who selects the A/P invoices to pay. 

• 
The following contact: Select this option to use the contact information of the person 

you select from the drop-down list. 

Finalizing the Transaction Approval Settings 

Click the Save button to save your transaction approval configuration. 

Defining a Default Approver 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > Approvals > Approval Configuration`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Spend Management > Setup > Approvals > Approval Configuration`


You can define a default approver for any transaction type (journal entries, A/P invoices, purchase 

orders, service contracts, subcontracts, job cost change orders, and A/P payments) if you enable 

approvals for that transaction type on the Approval configuration page. A default approver is a 

user that the system automatically assigns to review and approve a transaction when it detects a 

“gap” in the approval configuration. What constitutes a gap differs depending on the transaction 

type: 

• 
If the transaction is a journal entry, A/P invoice, purchase order, service contract, 

subcontract, or job cost change order, the default approver is automatically assigned if the 

user role that was set up as the approver is not assigned to any users, if there is an inactive 

user in the role, or if no one with that role has access to the transaction’s entity. 

• 
If the transaction is an A/P payment, the default approver is automatically assigned if a 

location is not assigned to a workflow for the payment method(s) selected from the 

Payment method drop-down list. 

How It Works 

The process for default approvers works as follows: 

1. 
A new transaction is submitted for approval. 

2. 
The system checks if there is a gap at any point in the workflow. 

3. 
If a gap is detected, a warning message appears at the top of the page to alert the person 

submitting the transaction. Warning messages appear in both RealPage Accounting and 

Spend Management Site Experience.

4. 
The system notifies the default approver and routes the transaction to them for approval. If 

you are an admin user, a record of this action appears on the Approval history page.

Contracts, Subcontracts, and Job Cost Change Orders 

To define a default approver for one of these transaction types: 

1. 
On the Approval configuration page, locate the section for the desired transaction type:

•

2.

field appears. 

3.

Make sure the default approver does not have any entity restrictions . 

4. 
Click Save to save this configuration. 

When you save the configuration, the system auto-generates a default policy and a default 

workflow for the transaction type in the Approval policy manager and Approval workflow 

lists. Only admin users with the appropriate right can view default policies and workflows. 

Defining a Default Approver for A/P Payments 

To define a default approver for A/P payments: 

1. 
On the Approval configuration page, locate the A/P payments section.

3.

Make sure the default approver does not have any entity restrictions . 

4. 
Select one or more payment methods from the Payment method drop-down list. 

The default approver receives A/P payments for approval if a location is not assigned to a 

workflow for the selected payment method(s).

### Approval Policies
*Source: `RP Accounting Approval Policy Manager User Guide.pdf`, Page 46*



#### Approval Policy Types
*Source: `RP Accounting Approval Policy Manager User Guide.pdf`, Page 46*

Transaction Approvals 

RealPage Accounting Approval Policy Manager User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Approval Policies 

This section describes how to create transaction approval policies. 

Approval Policy Types 

An approval policy is composed of the policy type, policy name, approvers, and number of 

approval levels.  

The system offers 13 types of approval policies. Each policy type requires configuration. The 

settings tell the system how to determine whether or not a transaction requires approval.  

User: Use this policy type to send all transactions to a specific user or role. You can combine 

this policy with one or more other policies that are based on other criteria in the approval 

workflow. 

Amount: Use this policy type to have the system check for transactions that are based on 

the amount of the transaction or change order. The system sends transactions of the 

amount you enter (or higher) to the selected approvers. Amount policies recognize the 

approver level of the person submitting the transaction or entering the change order; the 

system auto-approves (on page 63) transactions up to the submitter’s level in the approval 

hierarchy. 

Tiered amount: Use this policy type to have the system check for transactions that are 

based on the amount of the transaction or change order. Each approver has a limit to the 

amount he or she can approve. When a transaction or change order comes in that is over an 

approver’s limit, each approver must approve it to move the transaction to the next level. 

Tiered amount policies recognize the approver level of the person submitting the 

transaction or entering the change order; the system auto-approves (on page 63) 

transactions up to the submitter’s level in the approval hierarchy. 

Vendor: Use this policy type to have the system check for transactions that include a specific 

vendor. The system sends all transactions for the selected vendor to the designated 

approver or approvers. 

Vendor type: Use this policy type to have the system check for transactions that include a 

specific vendor type. The system sends all transactions for the selected vendor type to the 

designated approver or approvers. 

G/L account: Use this policy type to have the system check for transactions associated with 

a specific G/L account, such as Travel and Entertainment. The system sends all transactions 

tagged with a G/L account or G/L account range to the selected approver or approvers. 

Job: Use this policy type to have the system check for transactions associated with a specific 

job. 

Job type: Use this policy type to have the system check for transactions associated with a 

specific job type. 

---


<!-- Page 47 -->
Chapter 2: Transaction Approvals 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Approval Policy Manager User Guide 

If you do not see Job and Job type policy types, your company may not have enabled the Job 

Cost application. 

Cost code: Use this policy type to have the system check for transactions with a specific cost 

code. 

Accounting reviewer: Use this policy type to collect all A/P invoices and put them in an A/P 

invoice approval queue. The invoices must be approved before they can be posted. After 

creating this policy type, apply the policy to a workflow, and then assign the workflow to the 

desired properties. 

Journal type: Use this policy type to collect all journal entries for a journal, and then put 

them in a journal entry approval queue. The journal entries must be approved before they 

can post to the General Ledger. After creating this policy type, apply the policy to a 

workflow, and then assign the workflow to the desired properties. 

Payment method: Use this policy type to have the system check for A/P payments made 

through a specific payment method. The system sends all payments for the selected 

payment method to the designated approver or approvers. 

Bank account: Use this policy type to have the system check for transactions that are 

associated with a specific bank account. The system sends all transactions for the selected 

bank account to the designated approver or approvers.

#### Approvers
*Source: `RP Accounting Approval Policy Manager User Guide.pdf`, Page 48*

Transaction Approvals 

RealPage Accounting Approval Policy Manager User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Approvers 

Approvers are users who are responsible for deciding on whether to approve or decline a 

transaction. You can also designate a role to be an approver role. Everyone who is assigned that 

role is responsible for approving transactions. 

There are four kinds of approvers: 

• 
General approvers: These are users who are assigned to specific approval policies. Your 

company may have one approver who is assigned to transactions over a certain amount, 

and another person who is responsible for evaluating the A/P invoices of a new employee. 

• 
Unrestricted approvers: These are users who are assigned an unlimited ability to review and 

approve a type of transaction, even when they were not selected as the approver for the 

specific approval policy. You can assign unrestricted users on the Approval configuration 

(on page 26) page. 

• 
Default approvers: These are users who are automatically assigned to review and approve a 

transaction if there is an inactive user in the role or if there is no user in the role. You can 

assign default approvers on the Approval configuration (on page 26) page. 

For A/P payment approvals, the default approver receives transactions for approval if a 
location is not assigned to a workflow for the payment method(s) selected from the 

Payment method drop-down list. 

• 
Delegates: When an approver plans to be away or is unable to access the Approval 

workbench, they can enable approval policy delegates to temporarily assess transactions in 

their place. See Setting Up Delegates for Approvals (on page 14) for more information. 

---



#### Approval Levels
*Source: `RP Accounting Approval Policy Manager User Guide.pdf`, Page 49*

Chapter 2: Transaction Approvals 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Approval Policy Manager User Guide 

Approval Levels 

Approval levels reflect your company’s processes and organizational structure. 

Tiered Approvals 

Many companies use approval levels to monitor transactions of increasing amounts, requiring 

higher managerial levels to approve the higher amounts. Using the Tiered amount policy type, 

transactions progress through multiple levels of authority.  

When a transaction amount requires the highest level of authority to approve it, the transaction 

must progress through each lower level approver before it reaches the highest level’s approval 

queue. 

Tiered amount policies recognize the approver level of the person submitting the transaction; 
the system auto-approves (on page 63 ) transactions up to the submitter ’s level in the approval 
hierarchy. 

Example 

This example is based on the settings in the following image. 

When a transaction for $5101.00 enters the approval workflow, it must be approved by the 

Property Manager first. While the transaction waits for approval, it is not queued for the higher 

approvers; it waits to be approved by the Property Manager. Only when the Property Manager 

approves it does the transaction move to the next level, appearing in the Regional Manager’s 

approval workbench.  

If either of the lower approvers declines the transaction, then the CFO never sees the transaction 

to act on it.

Transaction Approvals

Vendor Approvals 

For vendor approvals, approval levels are built into permissions. If you are responsible for 

approving vendor records, your user account is assigned an approval role with permissions 

enabled for your approval level. Vendor approvals have up to three levels. For information, see 

Configuring permissions for vendor approvals (on page 155). 

If email notifications are enabled for your company, then approvers receive one email for every 
level to which they are assigned. As a best practice, assign users to one level or as few levels as 
possible.

Approval Policy Manager List

> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Spend Management > Setup > Approvals > Approval Policy Manager`


The Approval policy manager list is a central location where you can manage your system’s 

approval policies. When new transactions are entered, the system compares them against the 

policies to determine the approval’s route. If the details of the transaction (amount, vendor, G/L 

account, etc.) match a policy, then the system assigns the approver(s) set in that policy. You can 

apply approval policies to journal entries, A/P invoices, purchase orders, service contracts, 

subcontracts, job cost change orders, A/P payments, and purchase order change orders.  

Use this list to view and manage the existing approval policies. From this list, you can: 

• 
Add new approval policies. 

• 
Edit existing approval policy details. 

• 
View existing approval policy details. 

• 
Export the list of approval policies. 

• 
Use the list controls to sort, search, and create custom views of the list. 

When you enable approvals for a transaction type, RealPage Accounting auto-generates a 
default policy and a default workflow for routing transactions of this type to the user (or role) 
you have set as the default approver. Default policies and workflows are visible only to admin 
users. The system uses these default policies and workflows only under certain conditions; see 
Defining a default approver (on page 34 ) for more information.

To add an approval policy: 

1. 
In the Policy type drop-down list, select the approval policy type. The available types 

include: 

User: Use this policy type to send all transactions to a specific user or role. You can combine 

this policy with one or more other policies that are based on other criteria in the approval 

workflow. 

Amount: Use this policy type to have the system check for transactions that are based on 

the amount of the transaction or change order. The system sends transactions of the 

amount you enter (or higher) to the selected approvers. Amount policies recognize the 

approver level of the person submitting the transaction or entering the change order; the 

system auto-approves (on page 63) transactions up to the submitter’s level in the approval 

hierarchy. 

Tiered amount: Use this policy type to have the system check for transactions that are 

based on the amount of the transaction or change order. Each approver has a limit to the 

amount he or she can approve. When a transaction or change order comes in that is over an 

approver’s limit, each approver must approve it to move the transaction to the next level. 

Tiered amount policies recognize the approver level of the person submitting the 

transaction or entering the change order; the system auto-approves (on page 63) 

transactions up to the submitter’s level in the approval hierarchy. 

Vendor: Use this policy type to have the system check for transactions that include a specific 

vendor. The system sends all transactions for the selected vendor to the designated 

approver or approvers. 

Vendor type: Use this policy type to have the system check for transactions that include a 

specific vendor type. The system sends all transactions for the selected vendor type to the 

designated approver or approvers. 

G/L account: Use this policy type to have the system check for transactions associated with 

a specific G/L account, such as Travel and Entertainment. The system sends all transactions 

tagged with a G/L account or G/L account range to the selected approver or approvers. 

Job: Use this policy type to have the system check for transactions associated with a specific 

job. 

Job type: Use this policy type to have the system check for transactions associated with a 

specific job type.

#### Auto-Approving Transaction Amounts Through the Submitter Level
*Source: `RP Accounting Approval Policy Manager User Guide.pdf`, Page 63*

Chapter 2: Transaction Approvals 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Approval Policy Manager User Guide 

Auto-Approving Transaction Amounts Through the Submitter Level 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > Approvals > Approval Policy Manager`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Spend Management > Setup > Approvals > Approval Policy Manager`


If an approval policy is based on the amount of a transaction (the policy type is set to Amount or 

Tiered amount), then RealPage Accounting will automatically approve transactions up to the 

submitter’s level of approval. This means that if the user who submitted the transaction is higher 

in the approval hierarchy, the system auto-approves the lower levels. For example, a CFO who 

enters a transaction in a multi-level approval workflow does not need approval from approvers at 

lower levels, such as a Property Manager or Regional Manager. 

Example 1: Amount Policy 

XYZ Company has set up an Amount policy to require approval for transactions over $500.00. The 

policy designates four (4) levels of approval—Property Manager, Regional Manager, Asset 

Manager, and CFO—for four (4) different amount ranges. The image below illustrates this policy. 

A user with the Regional Manager role is entering a new A/P invoice. The system can 

auto-approve invoices up to the Regional Manager’s amount range. For example: 

• 
If the Regional Manager enters an invoice for $600.00, then the system auto-approves the 

invoice instead of routing it to the Property Manager because the Regional Manager is 

higher in the approval hierarchy than the Property Manager. 

• 
If the Regional Manager enters an invoice for $2,000.00, then the system auto-approves the 

invoice instead of routing it to the Regional Manager role because the Regional Manager is 

the one who submitted the transaction. 

---



##### What’s Next?
*Source: `RP Accounting Approval Policy Manager User Guide.pdf`, Page 64*

Transaction Approvals 

RealPage Accounting Approval Policy Manager User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

• 
If the Regional Manager enters an invoice for $3,000.00, then the Asset Manager must 

approve the invoice because the amount is above the Regional Manager’s approval limit. 

Example 2: Tiered Amount Policy 

In an alternate scenario, XYZ Company has set up a Tiered amount policy to require approval for 

transactions over $500.00. The policy designates four (4) levels of approval—Property Manager, 

Regional Manager, Asset Manager, and CFO—for four (4) different amount ranges. Unlike the 

Amount policy, the Tiered amount policy does not route transactions directly to the approver 

assigned to the amount range. Instead, the transaction must be approved in tiers, starting from 

the lowest level and progressing to the highest level required for the transaction amount. 

A user with the Regional Manager role is entering a new A/P invoice. The system can 

auto-approve invoices up to the Regional Manager’s amount range. For example: 

• 
If the Regional Manager enters an invoice for $600.00, then the system auto-approves the 

invoice for the Property Manager tier because the Regional Manager is higher in the 

approval hierarchy than the Property Manager. 

• 
If the Regional Manager enters an invoice for $2,000.00, then the system auto-approves the 

invoice for both the Property Manager and Regional Manager tiers. 

• 
If the Regional Manager enters an invoice for $3,000.00, then the system auto-approves the 

invoice for the Property Manager and Regional Manager tiers; however, the Asset Manager 

must still approve the invoice. 

What’s Next? 

To apply an approval policy to one or more entities, you must set up an approval workflow. For 

more information, see Approval Workflow (on page 68).

Approval Workflows 

This section describes how to set up transaction approval workflows. 

Thus far, you have created the approval policies that you want your company to use. Approval 

workflows bring together the approval policies with the properties that you want to follow the 

policies. 

To configure an approval workflow, the following steps walk you through the process: 

1. 
Create an approval workflow. 

2. 
Add the approval policies that you created. 

3. 
Choose the properties to use these approval policies.

Distribution (D): This option appears only if the Investor Tracking application is 

enabled and A/P invoice approvals are enabled. If selected, then invoices created from 

a distribution will go through the approval workflow before being posted. 

• 
Petty cash reimbursement (PCR): This option appears only if Debit cards for petty 

cash is enabled and A/P invoice approvals are enabled. If selected, then invoices 

created from a card transaction will go through the approval workflow before being 

posted.

#### Submitter Conditions in Approval Workflows
*Source: `RP Accounting Approval Policy Manager User Guide.pdf`, Page 80*

Submitter Conditions in Approval Workflows 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > Approvals > 
 Approval Workflow`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Spend Management > Setup > Approvals > 
 Approval Workflow`


You can set up submitter conditions for approval workflows based on the user (or user role) who 

submitted the transaction. These conditions can be used to: 

• 
Apply the workflow only when a specific user or user role—such as a President or 

CFO—enters a transaction.  

• 
Apply the workflow to every user except a specific user or group of users. 

To define submitter conditions, set the Policy type of the condition (on page 77 ) to “Submitter ” 
or “Submitter role ”. 

Example 1 

The approval workflow should apply only when Kim Johnson enters a transaction. 

Set up the condition as follows: 

• 
Policy type: Submitter 

• 
Operator: Equal to (IN) 

• 
From: Kim Johnson 

• 
To: Kim Johnson 

If you are specifying a single user, make sure to set the From and To fields to the same user.

RealPage Accounting Approval Policy Manager User Guide 

Example 2 

The approval workflow should apply only when Kim Johnson or Alex Garcia enters a transaction. 

Set up the condition as follows: 

Row 1 

• 
Policy type: Submitter 

• 
Operator: Equal to (IN) 

• 
From: Kim Johnson 

• 
To: Kim Johnson 

Row 2 

• 
Policy type: Submitter 

• 
Operator: Equal to (IN) 

• 
From: Alex Garcia 

• 
To: Alex Garcia 

If you are specifying multiple users or roles, make sure to set the Filter condition to “Any (OR).” 
This tells the system that the condition is met if Kim Johnson or Alex Garcia enter a 
transaction.

#### Bypassing the Approval Workflow
*Source: `RP Accounting Approval Policy Manager User Guide.pdf`, Page 87*

Chapter 2: Transaction Approvals 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Approval Policy Manager User Guide 

Bypassing the Approval Workflow 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > Setup > Roles > Subscriptions > (Company) > Permissions`


The system offers three ways to bypass the approval workflow.  

Option 1: Create Manual Checks 

Manual checks always bypass the approval workflow because the system creates the A/P invoice 

and the payment at the same time. 

Option 2: Bypass Approvals Based on Creation Method (A/P Invoices Only) 

A/P invoices can bypass the approval workflow based on how the A/P invoices are created.  

1. 
Open the Company menu. 

2. 
In the Approvals section, select the Approval configuration menu option. 

The Approval configuration page opens. 

3. 
In the A/P invoice approvals section, clear one or more of the following check boxes: 

• 
From CSV import: Clear this check box to bypass approvals when A/P invoices are 

imported using a CSV file. 

• 
From recurring invoice: Clear this check box to bypass the approval workflow when 

the system creates A/P invoices based on a recurring transaction. 

• 
From bill back templates: Clear this check box to bypass the approval workflow when 

the system automatically creates A/P invoices resulting from the bill back feature. 

---


<!-- Page 88 -->
Transaction Approvals 

RealPage Accounting Approval Policy Manager User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Option 3: Assign Bypass Permissions 

Assign one or more bypass permissions to a user or a role. With these permissions, whenever the 

user creates the selected transaction type, the system allows the transactions to bypass the 

approval workflow. 

These permissions are required to bypass the approval workflow:

for subcontracts.

For information about permissions and roles, see Roles and Permissions. If you don’t have

### Transaction Approval Process
*Source: `RP Accounting Approval Policy Manager User Guide.pdf`, Page 89*

Chapter 2: Transaction Approvals 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Approval Policy Manager User Guide 

Transaction Approval Process 

1. 
A user creates a transaction and submits it. (When an approval process is configured, 

transactions are Submitted to the approval process rather than Posted).  

2. 
The system evaluates the transaction to see if it requires approval based on the policies that 

your company configured. 

3. 
When a transaction requires approval (because it matches an approval requirement), the 

system puts the transaction into the approval workflow. When it does not require approval, 

the system bypasses the approval process and posts the transaction. 

4. 
The system sends email notifications to approvers (if your company chose to enable 

approval notifications), and then tracks the progress of the transaction through the approval 

workflow.  

5. 
The transaction enters the Approval workbench where it waits to be approved. 

6. 
Approvers use the Approval workbench (on page 93) to review the transactions that are 

moving through the approval process.  

The system stores the history of approval events for auditing purposes.  

When an eInvoice is created in Accounting, goes through approvals, and then gets posted, 
RealPage Accounting sends an update to OpsMerchant to change the partner status from 

Pending to Approved. This ensures that the vendor is aware of the current status of the 
invoice. We also send updates to OpsMerchant when the eInvoice is paid or voided, along 
with the payment details. 

---

can click the link in the Status column to review the transaction’s approval history.

process with purchase orders, service contracts, and subcontracts. 

• 
General Ledger: Subscribe to the General Ledger application to use the approval process 

with journal entries. 

• 
Job Cost & Reserves: Subscribe to the Job Cost & Reserves application to use the approval 

process with job cost change orders.

> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Spend Management > All > Approval Workbench`

Open the Spend Management menu.

Workbench Features 

The workbench is a central location where you can monitor and manage transactions. The 

workbench offers controls that allow you to: 

• 
View all columns available in Accounting 

• 
Use SmartGrid technology to: 

• 
Rearrange the columns 

• 
Customize and save which columns you see by default 

• 
Group and ungroup transactions based on different fields, like vendor or property 

• 
Apply operators to columns 

• 
Multi-select different filters for the following: 

• 
Property 

• 
Transaction type 

• 
Status 

• 
Submitted by 

• 
Next approver 

• 
Units 

• 
Save filter settings as a view and then reapply the view any time that you return to the 

workbench 

• 
Retain filters when switching between transaction types to alleviate selecting and applying 

the same filters again on both Approval and Spend Management Workbenches 

• 
Select the option to include future orders 

• 
Export the data in the workbench to an Excel file

Using the Columns Tab

#### Applying Mathematical Operators to Column Values
*Source: `RP Accounting Approval Policy Manager User Guide.pdf`, Page 101*

Chapter 2: Transaction Approvals 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Approval Policy Manager User Guide 

To discard the row grouping or value operator, click the 
 Close button. 

Applying Mathematical Operators to Column Values 

Use the Values box to apply mathematical operators to the values in a column. The most 

common use of this feature is to sum the Amount column. 

1. 
Drag the desired column by its dots and drop it in the Values box. 

---


<!-- Page 102 -->
Transaction Approvals 

RealPage Accounting Approval Policy Manager User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

The Amount column defaults to the sum ([column name]) operator: 

Click 
 Close to discard the value operator. 

2. 
Click the item to open the operator menu so that you can change the operator if needed. 

Available operators include: 

• 
Avg: Calculates the average of the numbers in a column. 

• 
Count: Counts the number of items in the column, or the number of elements in the 

collection. 

• 
First: Finds the first element in the column. 

• 
Last: Finds the last element in the column. 

• 
Max: Finds the largest number in the column. 

• 
Min: Finds the smallest number in the column. 

• 
Sum: Add the values in the column. The field can be a currency field or a numeric field.

#### Exporting from a Workbench
*Source: `RP Accounting Approval Policy Manager User Guide.pdf`, Page 103*

Chapter 2: Transaction Approvals 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Approval Policy Manager User Guide 

Exporting from a Workbench 

To export from a workbench: 

1. 
Right-click any data in the workbench to display the export controls menu. 

2. 
Click the Export button, and then select the file format that you want the system to use to 

export the data. 

• 
CSV Export: This format makes it easy to move the data from one program to another. 

You can use files that you save in the CSV format with any spreadsheet program. After 

selecting this option, the system exports the list as a CSV file. 

• 
Excel Export (.xlsx): After selecting this option, the system exports the list in Excel’s 

native format. 

• 
Excel Export (.xml): After selecting this option, the system exports the list in XML 

format. 

The location of the exported file depends on your browser’s default download functionality. 

All three of these export formats export the entire list, including these links: 

• 
Actions: Exports the HTML code for editing, viewing, approving, and declining the 

transaction. 

• 
Add approver: Click to add another approver for the transaction. 

• 
Send back: Send the transaction back to the requester. 

• 
Status: Click to view the transaction’s approval history. 

Additional Menu Items 

• 
Select Copy to copy the data in the selected cell to the clipboard. You can paste the copied 

data into a text file or another application. 

• 
Select Copy with headers to copy the data in the selected cell and the cell’s column header 

to the clipboard. 

The Paste command is not for use in the Workbench at this time.

Filtering Transactions in the Approval Workbench

The filter options on the Approval workbench page change depending on the transaction type 

you select. 

To filter the approval queue: 

1. 
Select the transaction type: 

• 
A/P invoice 

• 
Purchase order 

• 
Service contract 

• 
Subcontract 

• 
Job cost change order 

• 
Journal entry 

• 
A/P payment 

• 
Expense report 

2. 
Select additional filter criteria as needed. See the section below that corresponds with your 

transaction type for a list of available filter options. 

3. 
If you want to hide declined transactions from the list so you can edit and resubmit them, 

select the Included declined check box.  

By default, declined transactions are not included in the workbench. If you want to include 
them by default, then create a custom workbench view with the Include declined option 
selected and save it as the Default view. 

4. 
Click the Apply button. 

The approval queue refreshes with a list of transactions that meet the selected criteria. 

The system retains your filter selections even if you switch to a different transaction type 
in the workbench. To clear and reset filters, click the Clear button.

*Source: `RP Accounting Approval Policy Manager User Guide.pdf`, Page 109*

Approving and Declining Transactions 

See the How to Get Here (on page 93) topic for a list of ways to access the Approval workbench.  

This page has two views, View All and My Approvals. You must be in the Approval Workbench - 

My Approvals view to approve and decline transactions. If you are on the Approvals Workbench 

- View All view, click the My Approvals button to change to the My Approvals view.  

From the My Approvals view, you can approve or decline transactions individually or in bulk. If 

you are reviewing A/P invoices, then you can use the Review and approve button to quickly 

approve or decline invoices back-to-back (on page 147). 

When you approve a transaction, the system looks up the next approver. If the next approver 
previously approved the transaction, then the system sets the status of the transaction to 
Approved. 

Approving One Transaction 

To approve one transaction: 

1. 
Click the Approve link. 

The Approve [transaction type] box opens. 

2. 
Optionally, in the Comments box, type a comment. 

3. 
Click the Approve button. 

---


<!-- Page 110 -->
Transaction Approvals 

RealPage Accounting Approval Policy Manager User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Approving Multiple Transactions 

This method does not allow you to enter a comment about why you are approving these 
transactions. 

To approve multiple transactions: 

• 
From the Approval Workbench - My Approvals page, select the check box for each 

transaction that you want to approve, and then click the Approve button. 

Declining One Transaction 

To decline one transaction: 

1. 
Click the Decline link. 

The Decline [transaction name] box opens. 

2. 
In the Reason box, type an explanation for why you declined the transaction. 

3. 
Click the Decline button. 

---

Declining Multiple Transactions

You can export transaction data from the Approval workbench or Spend management 

workbench to an Excel file. The data included in the file depends on the columns that you have 

enabled in the workbench. 

To export data using the Export to Excel button: 

1. 
Click the Export to Excel button in the upper-right corner of the approval queue. 

The Excel file downloads with any column data configured in the workbench. 

2. 
In the Save as box, name the Excel file, and determine a file location for the exported file. 

3. 
Click Save. 

Adding an Approver to a Transaction 

See the How to Get Here (on page 93) topic for a list of ways to access the Approval workbench. 

As an approver, you can add another approver to a transaction in the Approval workbench. 

To add an approver to a transaction: 

1. 
Click the Add approver link next to the transaction. 

The Add approver box opens. 

2. 
Type any comments explaining why you are adding the approver. 

You can drag the lower-right corner of the Comments text box to resize it as needed. 

3. 
In the Additional approver drop-down list, select the user that you want to add to the 

transaction, and then click the Done button. 

All users in the drop-down list have access to the transaction ’s location.

#### Sending a Transaction Back to the Previous Approver
*Source: `RP Accounting Approval Policy Manager User Guide.pdf`, Page 114*

Transaction Approvals 

RealPage Accounting Approval Policy Manager User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Sending a Transaction Back to the Previous Approver 

See the How to Get Here (on page 93) topic for a list of ways to access the Approval workbench. 

Some transactions require approvals from multiple levels. If a transaction pending your approval 

was approved by someone else, you can send the transaction back to that approver instead of 

declining the transaction outright. 

To send a transaction back to the previous approver: 

1. 
On the Approval workbench - My approvals page, click the Send back link in the Send 

back column next to the transaction. 

The Send back box opens. 

2. 
Type your reason for sending back the transaction in the Comments field. 

3. 
Click the Send back button. 

The system loads the Approval workbench - My approvals page, and the transaction no 

longer appears in your queue. 

Sending Back Multiple Transactions 

To send back multiple transactions to the previous approver: 

1. 
From the Approval workbench - My approvals page, select the check box next to each 

transaction that you want to send back to the previous approver. 

2. 
Click the Send back link in the Send back column next to any of the transactions that you 

selected. 

The Send back box opens. 

3. 
Type your reason for sending back the transaction in the Comments field. 

4. 
Select the additional approver from the Additional approver drop-down list. 

5. 
Click the Send back button. 

The system loads the Approval workbench - My approvals page, and the transactions no 

longer appear in your queue.

This page opens when you click the Spend control button on an A/P invoice, purchase order, or 

subcontract. 

The tabs on the Available budget page change depending on the Line entry type that you 

selected in the transaction:  

• 
Standard 

• 
Job Cost 

• 
Both 

Standard Line Items 

If you selected Standard as the Line entry type of an A/P invoice or purchase order, then the 

Available budget page includes three tabs, (Month, Year to date, and Current Year), that show 

the monthly, year-to-date, and current-year spending for a property and account. 

Use the Current year tab to view the full-year budget and current activity and compare it to the 

planned activity for the remainder of the year. 

---


<!-- Page 118 -->
Transaction Approvals 

RealPage Accounting Approval Policy Manager User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Job Cost Line Items 

If you selected Include Job cost as the Line entry type on an A/P invoice or purchase order—or if 

the transaction is a subcontract—then the Available budget page shows only job cost budget 

amounts. You can view the amount budgeted, the actual amount spent, and the budget 

remaining for the job cost code. 

Standard and Job Cost Line Items 

If you selected Both as the Line entry type for an A/P invoice, then the Available budget page 

includes an additional tab labeled Job cost. The tab shows the amount budgeted, the actual 

amount spent, and the budget remaining for the job cost code.

### Approval History List
*Source: `RP Accounting Approval Policy Manager User Guide.pdf`, Page 122*

Transaction Approvals 

RealPage Accounting Approval Policy Manager User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Approval History List 

See the How to Get Here topic for a list of ways to access this area. 

Use this page to review a transaction’s approval history. This page displays when you click a status 

in the Approval workbench. 

When you enable approvals for a transaction type, RealPage Accounting auto-generates a 
default policy and a default workflow for routing transactions of this type to the user (or role) 
you have set as the default approver (on page 34 ). Default policies and workflows are visible only 
to admin users, including any events or actions logged in the approval history. 

Columns 

• 
Policy type: This column shows the policy type that the system used to approve the item. 

• 
Policy name: This column shows the policy name that the system used to approve the item. 

Click the link to view policy details. 

• 
Workflow name: This column shows the name of the workflow that the system used in the 

transaction. Click the link to view workflow details. 

• 
Approver role/user: This column contains a link to information about the person who 

decided on the approval. Click to view the role assignment details. You can find out who is 

assigned to a particular role with this link. 

• 
Approved/Declined by: This column contains the user name of the person who made the 

approval decisions. 

• 
Event date: This column contains the date that the transaction last underwent an approval 

event. (It was submitted for approval or partially approved.) 

• 
Comments: This column contains the comments the approver made along with his decision. 

• 
State: This column contains the status of the approval. 

• 
Action type: This column contains the approval status of the transaction. 

• 
Action comments: This column contains the comments associated with the action in the 

state. 

• 
Submitted by: This column contains the name of the user who submitted the transaction. 

“Console member” appears when the user accesses RealPage Accounting through the 
console rather than by logging in directly.
