#### Viewing Approval Policy Details from Approval History
*Source: `RP Accounting Approval Policy Manager User Guide.pdf`, Page 123*



#### Viewing Workflow Details from Approval History
*Source: `RP Accounting Approval Policy Manager User Guide.pdf`, Page 123*

Chapter 2: Transaction Approvals 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Approval Policy Manager User Guide 

Viewing Approval Policy Details from Approval History 

See the How to Get Here topic for a list of ways to access this area. 

You can view the details of an approval policy that was used to decide on a transaction. 

1. 
Apply filters (on page 104) to the workbench so that the desired transaction appears in the 

list. 

2. 
If needed, click the View all button to show all transactions (not just the transactions in your 

approval queue). 

3. 
Find the desired transaction in the approval queue. 

4. 
Click the link in the Status column. 

The Approval history list opens. See Approval History List (on page 122) for more 

information. 

5. 
Click the text in the Policy name column to open the Approval policy manager, allowing 

you to review the policy details. 

6. 
Click the Close button to return to the Approval history box. You can also click Print to 

print the approval policy details. 

Viewing Workflow Details from Approval History 

See the How to Get Here topic for a list of ways to access this area. 

You can view the details of an approval workflow that was used to route a transaction. 

1. 
Apply filters (on page 104) to the workbench so that the desired transaction appears in the 

list. 

2. 
If needed, click the View all button to show all transactions (not just the transactions in your 

approval queue). 

3. 
Find the desired transaction in the approval queue. 

4. 
Click the link in the Status column. 

The Approval history list opens. See Approval history list (on page 122) for more 

information. 

5. 
Click the link in the Workflow name column to display the Approval workflow details. 

6. 
Click Close to return to the Approval history box. You can also click Print to print the 

approval workflow details. 

---

### Review and Approve Process for A/P Invoices
*Source: `RP Accounting Approval Policy Manager User Guide.pdf`, Page 144*

Transaction Approvals 

RealPage Accounting Approval Policy Manager User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Review and Approve Process for A/P Invoices 

The Review and approve process allows you to evaluate A/P invoices quickly. Instead of opening 

each A/P invoice individually, the Review and approve process moves to the next A/P invoice in 

queue instead of returning you to the workbench to select the next item to evaluate.  

The Review and approve process is available only for A/P invoices. Before you can use this 
process, you must configure the system. 

Configuration Process 

1. 
Add an approval policy that uses the accounting reviewer policy type. See Creating a 

Reviewer Policy Type (on page 146). 

2. 
Apply the policy to a workflow, and then assign a property to the workflow. See Adding a 

Reviewer Policy to a Workflow (on page 146). 

This feature works well with the image viewer. When you open an A/P invoice with an 
attachment, the attached document opens in a separate window. You can enable the image 
viewer in your preferences. See Enabling the Image Viewer (on page 145 ). 

Reviewing and Approving Process 

• 
Someone creates A/P invoices for the property to which the reviewer policy is assigned. 

When the user submits the A/P invoice for approval, it appears in the Approval workbench. 

• 
The approver opens the Approval workbench and clicks the Review & approve button to 

begin reviewing A/P invoices. See Reviewing and Approving A/P Invoices (on page 147).

#### Reviewing and Approving A/P Invoices
*Source: `RP Accounting Approval Policy Manager User Guide.pdf`, Page 147*

RealPage Accounting Approval Policy Manager User Guide 

Reviewing and Approving A/P Invoices 

See the How to Get Here (on page 93) topic for a list of ways to access this area. 

When the Approval workbench is filtered by A/P invoices, an additional button appears in the 

upper-right corner labeled Review & approve. This button allows you to quickly open and review 

invoices in the order they appear in the approval queue.  

To review and approve A/P invoices: 

1. 
From the Applications menu, select Company, and then select the All tab. 

2. 
Select Approval workbench. 

3. 
Select the A/P invoice option. Set any other filters as needed. 

4. 
Click the Apply button. The system filters the list so that it shows only A/P invoices. 

5. 
Click the Review & approve button. The A/P invoice page opens. If the A/P invoice has an 

attachment and you have enabled the image viewer, the attachment displays in a separate 

window. If not, the invoice image will show on the same page as the invoice. 

If the Review & approve button does not appear, there are no A/P invoices in queue to 
approve. 

6. 
Review the A/P invoice. You can also edit the invoice at the same time. 

7. 
Click one of the buttons: 

• 
Approve & next: Approve the current A/P invoice, and then have the system display 

the next A/P invoice to evaluate. If you made any changes to the invoice, your changes 

are saved and the invoice is routed to the next person for approval. 

• 
Approve & next > Next: Skip the current A/P invoice and display the next A/P invoice 

in your queue. Any changes you made to the invoice will not be saved. 

• 
Decline & next: Decline the A/P invoice, and then display the next A/P invoice to 

evaluate. Any changes you made to the invoice will not be saved. 

• 
Add approver: Add someone who you think should approve the A/P invoice. Any 

changes you made to the invoice will not be saved. 

• 
Send back: Send the invoice back to the previous approver. Any changes you made to 

the invoice will not be saved. 

• 
Done: Close the approval queue. 

8. 
Click the Done button to exit the review and approval process. 

When an eInvoice is created in Accounting, goes through approvals, and then gets posted, 
RealPage Accounting sends an update to OpsMerchant to change the partner status from 

Pending to Approved. This ensures that the vendor is aware of the current status of the

### Vendor Approval Types
*Source: `RP Accounting Approval Policy Manager User Guide.pdf`, Page 150*

Vendor Approvals 

RealPage Accounting Approval Policy Manager User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Vendor Approval Types 

Vendor record approval can help with oversight of the vendors added to the system and helps 

prevent duplicate vendors. 

The system offers two types of vendor approval processes: 

1. 
You can configure the system to send new vendor records and updated vendor records 

through the approval process. To configure vendor approvals, see Vendor Record Approval 

Workflow (on page 151). 

2. 
You can configure the system to send transactions associated with a specific vendor or 

vendor type through the approval process. To do this: 

• 
Create vendor types and then assign the types to your vendors. See Adding a Vendor 

Type. 

• 
Configure transaction approval processes. See Transaction Approval Configuration 

Process (on page 23).  

• 
Configure an approval policy using use the Vendor or Vendor type policy type. See 

Adding Approval Policies (on page 52). 

Follow the steps in the Vendor Record Approval Configuration Workflow (on page 151) to 

configure the vendor record approval process. 

---



### Vendor Record Approval Workflow
*Source: `RP Accounting Approval Policy Manager User Guide.pdf`, Page 151*

Chapter 3: Vendor Approvals 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Approval Policy Manager User Guide 

Vendor Record Approval Workflow 

These are the steps required to configure the vendor record approval feature: 

Step 1: Design the approval process (on page 153). 

Step 2: Enable and configure vendor approval process (on page 154). 

Step 3: Configure permissions of approvers (on page 155). 

What’s Next? 

• 
Once configured, when a user creates or updates a vendor record, the system checks to see 

whether vendor record approval policy is enabled.  

• 
If so, the system next checks to see whether approvals are required for new vendor records 

or updated vendor records, or both. 

• 
If so, the system queues the vendor record for approval. 

• 
If your company selected to notify approvers when a vendor record is waiting for approval, 

the system sends emails to the designated approvers. The email contains a convenient link 

to the vendor approval page. 

• 
The requester (the user who created the vendor record) can see his vendor record while it is 

in queue for approval. The requester selects View vendor requests. 

• 
Approvers select Approve vendors to approve or decline vendor records. 

• 
When the approver approves the vendor, the system changes the status of the Vendor 

record, allowing it to appear in the Vendors list. All eligible users can then see the vendor 

record in the list of vendors. 

---

### Designing Your Vendor Record Approval Process
*Source: `RP Accounting Approval Policy Manager User Guide.pdf`, Page 153*

Chapter 3: Vendor Approvals 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Approval Policy Manager User Guide 

Designing Your Vendor Record Approval Process 

Before you configure the vendor approval process, answer the following questions. Use your 

answers to these questions to configure the vendor approval feature. 

Vendors 

• 
How many approval levels should be required for new vendors? (1-4) 

• 
How many approval levels should be required for vendor updates? (1-4) 

Approvers 

• 
Who will be the approvers? Make a list of users.  

• 
Who should be assigned to level 1 approvals? This person will receive the most approvals. 

• 
Who should be assigned to level 2?  

• 
Who should be assigned to level 3?  

• 
Who should be assigned to level 4?  

Level 0 means approval is not required. 

Notifications 

• 
Do you want every approver to be notified with an email every time their approval is 

required? 

• 
Do you want the system to send emails to approvers only for new vendors? 

• 
Do you want the system to send emails to approvers for vendor updates? 

Best Practices 

• 
Create a role for each vendor record approval level with permissions just for the associated 

vendor approval level. Then, assign the users who have authority and knowledge to approve 

new and updated vendor records to the appropriate role. 

• 
Make sure each role is assigned to more than one user. Approvers cannot approve their 

own vendor requests, so if an approver adds or edits a vendor and they are the only person 

with permission to approve that vendor, the vendor request will get stuck in the approval 

queue.  

---



#### Enabling the Vendor Approval Process
*Source: `RP Accounting Approval Policy Manager User Guide.pdf`, Page 154*

Vendor Approvals 

RealPage Accounting Approval Policy Manager User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Enabling the Vendor Approval Process 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Accounts payable > Setup > Configuration`


Step 1: Enable the vendor approval feature 

To enable the vendor approval feature: 

1. 
Click the Applications menu, select Accounts payable, and then select the Setup tab. 

2. 
Select Configuration. The Configure accounts payable page is displayed. 

3. 
Find the Vendor approval settings section. 

4. 
Select the Enable vendor approval check box. The Approval values list appears. 

5. 
In the Approval values list New vendor row, select the approval level for when someone 

adds a new vendor. 

Approval Levels 
0 = No approval is required 
1 = Approvers with Level 1 approval must approve 
2 = Approvers with Level 2 approval must approve 
3 = Approvers with Level 3 approval must approve 

6. 
Select the Notify approvers check box to have the system send an email to all approvers. 

The email contains a link to the Approve vendors page. 

If you select level 0, the system does not offer the Notify approvers check box because level 

0 vendors do not require approvals. 

7. 
In the Update vendor row, set up the approval level and notification preference for when 

someone changes a vendor record. 

8. 
Select Notify approvers if you selected level 1, 2, or 3 to have the system send emails to 

approvers.

*Source: `RP Accounting Approval Policy Manager User Guide.pdf`, Page 155*

Configuring Permissions for Vendor Approvers 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > Setup > Roles > Subscriptions`


As a best practice, create a new role for each level of vendor approver and then assign the role to 

the appropriate users. 

Make sure each role is assigned to more than one user. Approvers cannot approve their own 
vendor requests, so if an approver adds or edits a vendor and they are the only person with 
permission to approve that vendor, the vendor request will get stuck in the approval queue.

approvers 1. 

If you name all vendor approver roles consistently, it will pay off when you assign the roles 
later. 

4. 
In the Description, describe the purpose of level one approvers: First level approves all 

vendors and then click the Save button.  

The Vendor approvers 1 - Roles subscriptions page is displayed.

### Vendor Record Approval Process
*Source: `RP Accounting Approval Policy Manager User Guide.pdf`, Page 158*

Vendor Approvals 

RealPage Accounting Approval Policy Manager User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Vendor Record Approval Process 

This section describes how to participate in the vendor record approval process. 

1. 
A user (“the requester”) creates a new vendor record (on page 160). 

2. 
The system checks the vendor record approval policy to see if it requires approval for new 

and updated vendor records.  

• 
If it does, the system adds the vendor record to the approval queue.  

• 
If it does not, the system adds the vendor record to the Vendors list and this is the end 

of the process. 

The user who adds or edits the vendor record cannot be the person who approves the 
vendor request. If no one else has permission to approve vendors, then an administrator 
will need to assign that permission (on page 155 ) to at least one other user. Otherwise, 
the vendor request will be stuck in the approval queue. 

3. 
The requester can view the status of the vendor record he created or updated (the “vendor 

request”) using the View vendor requests (on page 164) option. 

4. 
The system notifies approvers that a record is pending approval. 

5. 
Approvers can click a link in the email notification (on page 166) to open the system to 

where the vendor record is waiting for approval. 

6. 
The approver reviews the vendor record in the Approve vendors list. 

7. 
The approver approves or declines the vendor record (on page 164). 

• 
If approved, the system moves approved vendor records to the vendors list.  

• 
If declined, the system deactivates declined vendor records.  

8. 
The requester checks with the approver to find out why the vendor was declined and then 

resolves the problem. 

---


<!-- Page 159 -->
Chapter 3: Vendor Approvals 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Approval Policy Manager User Guide 

9. 
The requester recreates the vendor record, and the approval process begins from step 1.

Adding Vendor (Supplier) Records 

See the How to Get Here topic for a list of ways to access the Vendors list. 

Adding Vendor Records 

Add vendor records when you want to pay A/P invoices.  

When you add a vendor, you can type key descriptive information about that vendor and select 

the payment method that the vendor prefers, such as by check, credit card, or ACH (electronic 

payment). 

If you enabled the Single Scan Upload feature in your preferences and have previously 
downloaded the Dynamsoft scanning software, you may be prompted to update the software 
when you add a new scannable record such as an A/P invoice, vendor, purchase order, service 
contract, or document. When this occurs, download the new software; there is no need to 
uninstall the previous version. 

To add a basic vendor record: 

1. 
In the ID field, type a unique identifier for the vendor record. 

Use a character as a prefix to your ID; for example, V0001 for a vendor ID. 

When you save the record, the system converts the vendor ID to all uppercase to prevent 

duplication. You can prevent this conversion by clearing the Set IDs to uppercase check 

box. For information, see Disabling Vendor ID Capitalization. 

After creating a vendor ID, you can only change it with the Customer Utility Tool. Most users 

do not have access to the tool as it requires administrator privileges. Contact your system 

administrator if you need to change a vendor ID. 

2. 
In the Name field, type the vendor’s name. The system completes the Print as field in the 

Primary Contact section. 

3. 
Select the One-time use check box to designate the vendor as a one-time or occasional use 

vendor that you don’t want to include in your standard vendor lists. An example of a 

one-time use of a vendor record is when you issue a customer’s deposit refund. 

These vendors won’t appear in the Vendors (Suppliers) list unless you select the Include 

one-time option at the top of the list. 

4. 
Select the Corporate vendor check box as needed. When you add an invoice for a corporate 

vendor, the system marks the invoice as a corporate invoice and prevents it from appearing 

in Site Experience. Also, corporate vendors do not appear in Site Experience. 

5. 
Select the This vendor is an owner check box when the vendor is also the owner of the 

company.

being entered and payment issued. 

You can inactivate multiple vendors at a time using the Customer Utility Tool’s Inactivate 

Vendors option.

Select the appropriate Storefront supplier code. This code is the vendor’s code for use with

### Why Is My Invoice Stuck in the Approval Workflow?
*Source: `RP Accounting Approval Policy Manager User Guide.pdf`, Page 168*

Approval FAQs 

RealPage Accounting Approval Policy Manager User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Why Is My Invoice Stuck in the Approval Workflow? 

This topic explains why an item may remain in the Approval workbench without advancing to the 

next step. It also outlines common causes and how to resolve them. 

Symptoms 

• 
The invoice shows a status of Pending Approval for an extended period. 

• 
The item does not move to the next approver. 

• 
No approver is displayed, or the wrong approver is shown. 

• 
The user cannot take action on the item. 

Possible Causes 

• 
The approval workflow is not configured correctly. 

• 
An approver is inactive or unavailable. 

• 
Approval thresholds do not match the transaction amount. 

• 
Required vendor or transaction data is missing. 

• 
The user does not have the correct permissions. 

Resolution 

1. 
Verify the current approval status of the item. 

2. 
Review the assigned approver and approval path. 

3. 
Confirm the transaction amount matches the configured approval threshold. 

4. 
Check whether all required fields and vendor records are complete. 

5. 
Confirm the approver has the correct role and permissions and is an active user. 

6. 
Resubmit or re-route the item if your process allows it. 

Additional Information 

• 
Approval routing may vary by transaction type, amount, entity, or property. 

• 
Some approval delays are caused by upstream setup issues rather than system errors. 

• 
Roles and permissions may affect both visibility and approval actions. 

---



### Why Can’t I Approve an Invoice or Transaction?
*Source: `RP Accounting Approval Policy Manager User Guide.pdf`, Page 169*

Chapter 4: Approval FAQs

RealPage Accounting Approval Policy Manager User Guide 

Why Can’t I Approve an Invoice or Transaction? 

This topic explains common reasons you may be unable to approve an invoice or transaction in 

the Approval workbench. It also provides steps to identify issues that may prevent approval, such 

as access, workflow, or setup issues. 

Symptoms 

• 
The Approve option is missing. 

• 
You can view the invoice or transaction but cannot approve it. 

• 
The item does not appear in your My Approvals workbench view. 

• 
The item appears to be assigned to another approver. 

Possible Causes 

• 
You are not the current assigned approver. 

• 
You may not have View or Edit permission for this transaction type.  

• 
The transaction is not assigned to you for approval. 

• 
The approval workflow routed the item to a different user or role. 

• 
The item is waiting on a previous approval step. 

• 
Your user account is inactive, restricted, or not fully set up for the required approval role. 

Resolution 

• 
Confirm the item is assigned to you 

Review the approval details to verify whether you are the current approver. If the item is 

assigned to another user or role, you will not be able to approve it until it reaches your step. 

• 
Check the current approval step 

Determine whether the item is still pending an earlier approver. If approval is sequential, 

you may not be able to act until prior approvals are complete. 

• 
Validate your approval authority 

Confirm that your approval level matches the invoice or transaction amount and any 

applicable approval thresholds. 

• 
Confirm your user account is active 

Check that your account is active and correctly associated to the necessary role, entity, 

property, or approval group. 

• 
Review workflow routing configuration 

If the item should have routed to you but did not, review the approval workflow setup for 

the transaction type, amount, and approval conditions. 

• 
Refresh and reopen the item 

---


<!-- Page 170 -->
Approval FAQs 

RealPage Accounting Approval Policy Manager User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

In some cases, recent updates to assignment, permissions, or workflow setup may require 

the item or queue to be refreshed before the action becomes available. 

• 
Contact your administrator if reassignment is needed 

If the invoice or transaction is assigned incorrectly, an administrator may need to update the 

workflow, permissions, or reassignment based on your organization’s process. Confirm the 

item is assigned to you 

Additional Information 

• 
Approval rights may vary by transaction type, amount, entity, property, or role. 

• 
If the item is part of a multi-step approval chain, only the current approver can take action.

### How Do I Find Who Is Currently Assigned to an Approval?
*Source: `RP Accounting Approval Policy Manager User Guide.pdf`, Page 171*

Chapter 4: Approval FAQs 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Approval Policy Manager User Guide 

How Do I Find Who Is Currently Assigned to an Approval? 

This topic explains how to identify the user or role currently responsible for an item in the 

Approval workbench. It also outlines common reasons that the assigned approver may not be 

obvious. 

Symptoms 

• 
An invoice or transaction is pending approval, but it is unclear who needs to act next. 

• 
The item has not moved forward, and you need to know where it is in the workflow. 

• 
The approval queue does not clearly show the current approver. 

• 
Users are unsure whether the item is assigned to a person, a role, or a previous approval 

step. 

Possible Causes 

• 
The item is currently assigned to another user. 

• 
The approval is waiting on an earlier step in a sequential workflow. 

• 
The workflow displays a role or approval group instead of an individual user. 

• 
The workflow configuration routed the item differently than expected. 

Resolution 

1. 
Open the item in the Approval workbench or A/P invoices list. 

Locate the invoice or transaction and open its approval details, if available. If it is not 

available, it is not assigned to you for approval. You can view all transactions for approval 

only when you click the View All button at the top right side of the page.  

2. 
Review the current approval status by clicking on the status or on the Approval History of 

the transaction. 

Check the item status to confirm whether it is pending approval, awaiting review, or held at 

another workflow stage. 

3. 
Look for the current Approver Role/User field in the Approval History  

Identify whether the item shows a current approver, assigned user, approval group, or 

workflow step owner. 

4. 
Review the approval path or history 

If available, check the approval history to see completed steps and determine which step is 

currently active. 

5. 
Confirm whether approval is person-based or role-based 

In some workflows, the item may be assigned to a role, team, or approval group rather than 

a specific named user. 

6. 
Check whether a prior approval step is still pending 

---


<!-- Page 172 -->
Approval FAQs 

RealPage Accounting Approval Policy Manager User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

If the process is sequential, the next approver may not appear until the earlier step is 

completed. 

7. 
Verify workflow routing if the assignment looks incorrect 

If the item appears to be assigned to the wrong user or group, review the workflow setup 

and approval conditions. 

8. 
Contact your administrator if assignment details are not visible 

If the Approval workbench does not display enough detail, an administrator may need to 

review workflow routing or user roles and permission assignments. 

Additional Information 

• 
The current assignee may be an individual user, a role, or an approval group. 

In a workflow with multiple approvers, only the active approver can approve the transaction. 

The other approvers must wait their turn. 

• 
Approval history can help determine whether the item is delayed at the current step or still 

waiting on an earlier approver. 

See Also

### Why Was My Approval Request Not Routed to the Correct Approver?
*Source: `RP Accounting Approval Policy Manager User Guide.pdf`, Page 173*

Chapter 4: Approval FAQs 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Approval Policy Manager User Guide 

Why Was My Approval Request Not Routed to the Correct 
Approver? 

This topic explains common reasons an invoice or transaction may not be routed to the expected 

approver in the Approval workbench. It also provides steps to review workflow setup, approval 

conditions, and assignment logic. 

Symptoms 

• 
The invoice or transaction was routed to the wrong user or group. 

• 
The expected approver did not receive the item. 

• 
The item skipped an approver or approval level. 

• 
The approval request appears in an unexpected queue. 

• 
The routing path does not match the organization’s approval process. 

Possible Causes 

• 
The approval workflow is configured incorrectly. 

• 
Approval thresholds do not match the transaction amount. 

• 
The workflow uses a different approver based on entity, property, department, or 

transaction type. 

• 
The assigned approver in setup is inactive or unavailable. 

• 
Required transaction or vendor data is missing or incorrect. 

• 
The item was routed based on role or group logic rather than an individual user. 

Resolution 

1. 
Review the item details 

Confirm the transaction type, amount, entity, property, department, vendor, and any other 

values that may affect approval routing. 

2. 
Check the approval path or current assignment 

Review the routing outcome to identify who received the item and whether it was assigned 

to a user, role, or approval group. 

3. 
Validate approval thresholds 

Confirm that the transaction amount falls within the expected approval range and did not 

trigger a different approval level. 

4. 
Review workflow conditions 

Check whether routing rules depend on transaction type, amount, organizational structure, 

vendor setup, or other approval criteria. 

5. 
Verify approver setup 

---


<!-- Page 174 -->
Approval FAQs 

RealPage Accounting Approval Policy Manager User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Confirm the expected approver is active, properly assigned, and included in the correct 

workflow step or approval group. 

6. 
Check for missing or incorrect data 

Review the transaction and related records for missing fields or incorrect values that may 

have affected routing. 

7. 
Confirm whether routing is role-based 

In some cases, workflow rules route to a role, team, or group instead of a specific individual. 

Make sure the routing logic matches the intended process. 

8. 
Update workflow setup if needed 

If routing rules are incorrect, an administrator may need to revise the workflow 

configuration so future items route properly. 

Additional Information 

• 
Approval routing may vary based on amount, entity, property, department, vendor, or 

transaction type. 

• 
Items may route differently when workflow rules use approval groups or role-based logic. 

• 
Incorrect master data or incomplete transaction details can affect routing outcomes. 

• 
Reviewing both the item data and the workflow configuration is often necessary to identify 

the cause.

### How Do Approval Thresholds Affect Routing?
*Source: `RP Accounting Approval Policy Manager User Guide.pdf`, Page 175*

Chapter 4: Approval FAQs 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Approval Policy Manager User Guide 

How Do Approval Thresholds Affect Routing? 

This topic explains how approval thresholds influence routing in the Approval workbench. It also 

describes how transaction amounts can determine which approver, approval level, or workflow 

path is used. 

Symptoms 

• 
An invoice or transaction was routed to a different approver than expected. 

• 
The item triggered an additional approval step. 

• 
The item skipped a lower-level approver and went to a higher-level approver. 

• 
Routing changed after the transaction amount was updated. 

• 
Users are unsure why similar transactions followed different approval paths.

workflow.

Review workflow conditions

routing criteria.

different approval level.

Validate threshold setup

Review the affected transaction details

Check the current approval path

Validate workflow rules and thresholds

Update and retest configuration if needed

The user is troubleshooting workflow behavior. 

• 
The current approval status does not explain what happened earlier in the process. 

• 
An approver, reassignment, rejection, or routing change needs to be confirmed. 

• 
The item’s current location in the approval process is unclear. 

• 
Audit or review activity requires confirmation of prior actions. 

Resolution 

1. 
Open the invoice or transaction record 

Locate the item in the appropriate work area or in the Approval workbench. 

2. 
Navigate to the approval details 

Open the section that displays approval status, workflow activity, or approval actions. 

3. 
Review the approval history entries 

Look for details such as approver names, action dates, approval steps, status changes, and 

comments. 

4. 
Identify the most recent action 

Confirm the latest event in the approval process to understand the item’s current state. 

5. 
Check prior routing and reassignment activity 

Review whether the item was reassigned, returned, rejected, or routed through multiple 

approvers. 

6. 
Compare history to current status 

Make sure the approval history aligns with the item’s present status and assigned approver. 

7. 
Use history to identify workflow issues

If the item appears delayed or misrouted, use the recorded actions to determine where the 

process changed or stopped. 

8. 
Escalate if history is missing or unclear 

If the approval history is incomplete or does not match actual workflow behavior, contact an 

administrator or support team. 

Additional Information 

• 
Approval history may include actions such as submit, approve, reject, reassign, return, or 

complete. 

• 
The amount of detail shown depends on system configuration and user permissions. 

• 
Approval history is often useful for both troubleshooting and audit review. 

• 
Reviewing history can help distinguish between a routing issue, a pending action, and a 

completed workflow step.

### How Do I Identify Approval Bottlenecks?
*Source: `RP Accounting Approval Policy Manager User Guide.pdf`, Page 199*

Chapter 4: Approval FAQs 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Approval Policy Manager User Guide 

How Do I Identify Approval Bottlenecks? 

This topic explains how to identify bottlenecks in the approval process by reviewing approval 

history, current assignment, workflow steps, and timing delays. It also outlines common causes of 

slow-moving approvals. 

Symptoms 

• 
Invoices or transactions remain pending longer than expected. 

• 
Approval items are stuck at the same step for an extended period. 

• 
Certain approvers or workflow levels delay completion. 

• 
Approval timelines vary significantly for similar transactions. 

• 
Users are unsure where the delay is occurring. 

Possible Causes 

• 
A current approver has not taken action. 

• 
The workflow requires multiple approvals before it can continue. 

• 
Sequential approval routing creates delays between steps. 

• 
An approver is inactive, unavailable, or overloaded. 

• 
Missing data, comments, or attachments are delaying progression. 

• 
Workflow design or thresholds create unnecessary approval steps. 

Resolution 

1. 
Review the current approval status 

Confirm where the item is currently pending and whether it is waiting for action. 

2. 
Check the current assignee 

Identify the user, role, or group currently responsible for the next approval action. 

3. 
Review approval history 

Compare action dates and step timing to identify where delays are occurring. 

4. 
Look for repeated delays at the same step 

Determine whether the same approval level, user, or routing condition causes delays across 

multiple items. 

5. 
Evaluate workflow complexity 

Check whether the approval path includes unnecessary steps, duplicate approvers, or strict 

sequential routing. 

6. 
Confirm approver availability 

Verify that assigned approvers are active and able to act on items in a timely manner. 

7. 
Review data or document dependencies 

---


<!-- Page 200 -->
Approval FAQs 

RealPage Accounting Approval Policy Manager User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Make sure required transaction details, comments, or attachments are not preventing 

approvals from moving forward. 

8. 
Escalate recurring bottlenecks for workflow review 

If delays happen consistently, an administrator may need to review approver assignments, 

thresholds, or workflow design. 

Additional Information 

• 
Approval bottlenecks are often caused by a combination of workflow design and approver 

availability. 

• 
Approval history is one of the best tools for identifying where delays occur. 

• 
Repeated delays at the same step may indicate a setup issue rather than a one-time 

processing delay. 

• 
Bottleneck analysis can help improve approval timing and workflow efficiency. 

---



### What Should I Check Before Submitting an Item for Approval?
*Source: `RP Accounting Approval Policy Manager User Guide.pdf`, Page 201*

Chapter 4: Approval FAQs 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Approval Policy Manager User Guide 

What Should I Check Before Submitting an Item for Approval? 

This topic explains what to review before submitting an invoice, expense, or transaction for 

approval. It also outlines common issues that can delay routing, cause rejection, or prevent the 

approval process from starting. 

Symptoms 

• 
An item is rejected shortly after submission. 

• 
The approval request does not route as expected. 

• 
Required approvers are missing from the workflow. 

• 
The transaction cannot be submitted or approved. 

• 
Users want to avoid delays, errors, or rework before submitting an item. 

Possible Causes 

• 
Required fields are missing or incomplete. 

• 
Amounts, coding, or other transaction details are incorrect. 

• 
Vendor, property, department, or account information is invalid. 

• 
Required attachments or supporting documentation are missing. 

• 
The transaction does not meet approval, compliance, or workflow requirements. 

Resolution 

1. 
Review all required fields 

Confirm that all mandatory fields are completed before submission. 

2. 
Validate transaction details 

Check the amount, dates, coding, vendor, property, department, and account information 

for accuracy. 

3. 
Confirm supporting documentation is attached 

Make sure required invoices, receipts, explanations, or other supporting files are included. 

4. 
Verify vendor information 

Confirm that the correct vendor is selected and that the vendor record is active and 

complete. 

5. 
Check compliance-related requirements 

Review any vendor compliance, policy, or documentation requirements that could block 

approval. 

6. 
Review approval-related data 

Confirm that the transaction includes the information needed for workflow routing, 

thresholds, and approver assignment. 

---


<!-- Page 202 -->
Approval FAQs 

RealPage Accounting Approval Policy Manager User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

7. 
Check for validation errors or warnings 

Resolve any system messages shown before submitting the item. 

8. 
Submit only after final review 

Once all information is complete and accurate, submit the item into the approval workflow. 

Additional Information 

• 
Many approval delays are caused by missing or incorrect data at the time of submission. 

• 
Reviewing transaction details before submission can reduce rejections and rerouting. 

• 
Vendor setup, documentation, and workflow conditions can all affect whether an item 

moves smoothly through approval. 

• 
A careful pre-submission review helps prevent avoidable approval issues.

### Why Can’t I Tell Why An Item Was Approved or Declined?
*Source: `RP Accounting Approval Policy Manager User Guide.pdf`, Page 203*

Chapter 4: Approval FAQs 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Approval Policy Manager User Guide 

Why Can’t I Tell Why An Item Was Approved or Declined? 

This topic explains common reasons users may be unable to determine why an item was 

approved or rejected in the Approval History page. It also outlines how to review comments, 

status changes, and workflow details to better understand the decision. 

Symptoms 

• 
Approval History shows that an item was approved or rejected, but the reason is unclear. 

• 
Users cannot find comments or supporting details for the decision. 

• 
The item status changed, but there is no visible explanation. 

• 
Users are unsure whether the decision was based on workflow rules, user action, or missing 

information. 

• 
The approval record does not provide enough context for troubleshooting or follow-up. 

Possible Causes 

• 
The approver did not enter a comment or reason. 

• 
Comments are optional in the approval process. 

• 
Approval History shows the action taken, but not the business reason behind it. 

Resolution 

1. 
Open the item’s approval history 

Review the full approval trail for the invoice, expense, or transaction. 

2. 
Check for comments or notes 

Look for any approver comments, rejection notes, or system-generated messages 

associated with the action. 

3. 
Review the action taken 

Confirm whether the item was approved, rejected, returned, reassigned, or otherwise 

changed in status. 

4. 
Compare the action to the current status 

Make sure the most recent history entry aligns with the item’s present state. 

5. 
Review prior workflow activity 

Check whether earlier routing steps, missing information, or reassignment activity may help 

explain the final decision. 

6. 
Confirm whether comments are required in your process 

Determine whether your organization requires approvers to document approval or rejection 

reasons. 

7. 
Check user visibility and permissions 

---


<!-- Page 204 -->
Approval FAQs 

RealPage Accounting Approval Policy Manager User Guide 
© 2026 RealPage, Inc.

Verify whether your role allows access to the full approval history, including comments and 

related workflow details. 

8. 
Escalate if the decision still lacks context 

If no explanation is available, contact the approver, workflow administrator, or support team 

for clarification. 

Additional Information 

• 
Approval History may record what action occurred without explaining why the user chose 

that action. 

• 
Some approval processes do not require approvers to enter comments. 

• 
Limited visibility can make approval decisions appear incomplete or unclear. 

• 
Workflow logic and business rules may affect outcomes even when a clear narrative is not 

shown in history. 

---

Customizing and Running the Report

location. 

•

#### Approval Aging Report Columns
*Source: `RP Accounting Approval Policy Manager User Guide.pdf`, Page 209*

Chapter 5: Reports 

© 2026 RealPage, Inc. 
RealPage Accounting Approval Policy Manager User Guide 

Approval Aging Report Columns 


> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Company > All > Approvals > Approval Aging Report`



> **Navigation Path:** `Applications > Spend Management > Setup > Approvals > Approval Aging Report`


You can click any link to navigate into details. 

Depending on your report configuration, the Approval Aging report may contain the following 

columns: 

• 
Vendor: The name of the vendor on the transaction 

• 
Order no: The transaction’s order number, such as the purchase order number 

• 
PO created date: The date that the purchase order was created 

• 
Employee: The name of the employee who submitted the expense report 

• 
Expense report name: The name of the expense report 

• 
Date filed: The date that the employee submitted the expense report for approval 

• 
Current state: The status of the approval, whether “Submitted,” “Declined,” or “Partially 

approved” 

• 
Next approver: The next approver in line to approve the transaction 

• 
Days aged: The number of days since the transaction entered the approval workflow 

• 
0-7: The amount of money waiting for approval from transactions that are between zero 

and seven days old 

• 
8-14: The amount of money waiting for approval from transactions that are between eight 

and 14 days old 

• 
15-21: The amount of money waiting for approval from transactions that are between 15 

and 21 days old 

• 
22-28: The amount of money waiting for approval from transactions that are between 22 

and 28 days old 

• 
29-: The amount of money waiting for approval from transactions that are older than 29 

days old 

• 
Total: The total amount of money owed to the vendor based on the purchase order or other 

transaction. Click the link to open the Purchase order information page, A/P invoice page, 

or Job cost change order page. 

• 
Grand totals: Each column is totaled at the bottom. The grand total at the far right is the 

total amount waiting for approval for all transactions and vendors.

About the Approval Policy Manager

Use the Approval policy manager page in the Company
application to create approval policies and organize them into
workflows. To do this, you must have Approver permissions,
and you must enable approvals for the transaction type on the
Approval configuration page.

Adding an Approval Policy by User

Set up an approval policy where all transactions go to a specific
user or role for approval.

1. In the Company menu, select the All tab.

2. Click 
 next to Approval policy manager.
3. Select User from the Policy type drop-down list.
4. Type a Policy name for the policy.
5. Select the Role/user to whom all transactions must be routed
for approval.
6. If you selected a role, then select the number of people with that
role who are required to approve transactions (1-4).

7. Optionally, add more roles and users. Click 
 Add to add
another role or user and then repeat steps 5 and 6.
8. Click Save.

Adding an Approval Policy Based on Amount

Set up an approval policy for all transactions that meet the
amount threshold.

1. In the Company menu, select the All tab.

2. Click 
 next to Approval policy manager.
3. Select Amount from the Policy type drop-down list.
4. Type a Policy name for the policy.
5. Select the Role/user that you want to approve all transactions
that meet the amount threshold.
6. In the Amount from field, type the lowest amount that requires
transactions to be approved.
7. In the Amount to field, type the highest amount that these
approvers are authorized to approve.
8. If you selected a role, select the highest level of approval
required for these transactions from the Require approvers
drop-down list, up to four.

9. Optionally, add more roles and users. Click 
 Add to add
another role or user and then repeat steps 5 through 8.
10. Click Save.

Adding an Approval Policy for Tiered Amounts

Set up an approval policy for transactions that meet the amount
threshold, passing the transactions through tiers of approvers
based on the amount.

1. In the Company menu, select the All tab.

2. Click 
 next to Approval policy manager.
3. Select Tiered amount from the Policy type drop-down list.
4. Type a Policy name for the policy.
5. Select the Role/user responsible for approving the amount tier.
6. In the Amount to and Amount from fields, type the dollar
range for which the role or user is responsible.
7. If you selected a role, select the highest level of approval
required for these transactions from the Require approvers
drop-down list, up to four.
8. Continue adding rows for additional tiers of approval.

For the last row, leave Amount to blank.

9. Click Save.

Adding an Approval Policy for a Specific Vendor

Set up an approval policy for all transactions from a specific
vendor or range of vendors.

1. In the Company menu, select the All tab.

2. Click 
 next to Approval policy manager.
3. Select Vendor from the Policy type drop-down list.
4. Type a Policy name for the policy.
5. Select the Role/user responsible for approving transactions
related to these vendors.
6. In the Vendor from and Vendor to fields, select the starting and
ending vendor in an alphabetical list of vendors for whom the
approvers are responsible.
7. If you selected a role, select the highest level of approval
required for these transactions from the Require approvers
drop-down list, up to four.
8. Continue adding roles and the vendors they are responsible for
approving as needed.
9. Click Save.

Adding an Approval Policy for a Vendor Type

Set up an approval policy for all transactions of a specific
vendor type.

1. In the Company menu, select the All tab.

2. Click 
 next to Approval policy manager.
3. Select Vendor type from the Policy type drop-down list.
4. Type a Policy name for the policy.
5. Select the Role/user responsible for approving transactions of a
specific vendor type.
6. Select the type of vendor that must go through the approval
process from the Vendor type drop-down list.

7. If you selected a role, select the highest level of approval
required for these transactions from the Require approvers
drop-down list, up to four.
8. Continue adding roles and vendor types as needed.
9. Click Save.

Adding an Approval Policy for a G/L Account

Set up an approval policy for transactions that contain
expenses set to a specific G/L account (such as Travel and
Entertainment).

1. In the Company menu, select the All tab.

2. Click 
 next to Approval policy manager.
3. Select G/L account from the Policy type drop-down list.
4. Type a Policy name for the policy.
5. Select the Role/user responsible for approving transactions
associated with a specific G/L account or account range.
6. In the G/L account from field, select the starting account in a
range of accounts.
7. In the G/L account to field, select the ending account in a
range of accounts.

If your system has a G/L account group defined for sets of G/L
accounts, such as a group for All Investors, select the G/L
account group from the G/L account group drop-down list
instead.

8. If you selected a role, select the highest level of approval
required for these transactions from the Require approvers
drop-down list, up to four.
9. Click Save.

Adding an Approval Policy for a Job

Set up an approval policy for all transactions from a specific
job.

1. In the Company menu, select the All tab.

2. Click 
 next to Approval policy manager.
3. Select Job from the Policy type drop-down list.
4. Type a Policy name for the policy.
5. Select the Role/user responsible for approving transactions
related to this job.
6. Select the job that requires approval from the Job drop-down
list.
7. If you selected a role, select the highest level of approval
required for these transactions from the Require approvers
drop-down list, up to four.
8. Continue adding roles and the jobs they are responsible for
approving as needed.
9. Click Save.

Adding Approval Workflows

 next to Approval workflow.
3. Type a Name for the new workflow.
4. Select the transaction type(s) to which the workflow applies.
5. In the Policies section, select a policy from the Policy name
drop-down list.
The Policy type populates based on your selection.
6. In the Properties section, select the properties to which the
approval workflow should apply.
7. Optionally, in the Conditions section, select the Enable
conditions check box to apply additional criteria to determine
whether the system should apply a workflow to a property.
8. Click Save.

Approving and Declining Transactions

1. In the Company menu, select the All tab.
2. Select the Approval workbench option.
3. Select the desired transaction type to filter the approval queue.
4. To view your pending approvals, click the My approvals button.
To view all pending approvals, click the View all button.
5. Review the transactions in the approval queue. You can click
the Edit or View link to open the transaction details.
6. Click the Approve or Decline link to approve or decline a single
transaction, or select check boxes for multiple transactions and
then click the Approve or Decline button to approve or decline
them in bulk.
